reviews.comment: Professor Demarest was one of the toughest Professors I had. It was very hard to study for because it was very unclear on what was needed to know from the test. He  gave a great lecture but it was hard to feel the same confidence when it came to the test because of how he worded it. The final was the worse test of my life, and he does not curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Demarest is an amazing person, he gives a really good and interesting lecture. He is not really clear on whats gonna be on the exams, or how to study for them. So its not really helpful. I didn't really enjoy the class after the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Demarest is one of the best professors in the science department. Great at making concepts easy to understand, and clearly demonstrates what information you'll need to know. Most of the class is online learning but going to class is still beneficial. If you've made it through Bio 1 this class shouldn't be a problem. He's also a great person

Bio is always hard so it's not an easy class, but Demarest does make the lectures as enjoyable as possible. I'm not a fan of his teaching style - learn everything your self and then go over it in class because I feel like I could just study instead of going to class and do better BUT participation counts. Be ready for a lot of online homework

Prof. Demarest is a great and solid professor. He teaches Intro Bio with a passion and is great at explaining concepts in an easily understandable way. Tests come almost completely from his slides. As long as you make an effort, it's not at all hard to get an A or a B.

Seriously one of the nicest and most sincere guy around. Always eager to help and genuinely wants you to understand the material rather than just spit random facts out. The tests are more about understanding the material than straight up facts so they can be a little tricky

Nice guy and good teacher overall, but tests can be challenging. still probably the easiest of the general biology professors on campus. online power points are 90% of the tests, with a few things from the lecture. weekly online quizzes that can be taken 5x, and iclicker points

There was no curve!! so if you expect a curve for your science courses, don't take this one!! But he is a great teacher, hilarious lecture commentary, and a very nice person! He is a great teacher and is always willing to help!! but beware, biology is really tough course so you need to prepare! Also, do not buy the book, he gives you a free code.
Amazing professor. Doesn't make you memorize all the little details and tests are challenging but extremely straightforward. Show up to class and study and you're set for a good grade!

His class mainly composes of  the online works (lectures in the books) and the in-class lectures, which talk about extension of the online lectures (history of biology,practical application...), so attendance is needed is necessary. Exams consist of 50 questions of both of the above. Class grade averages around 70. Best class I've ever taken.

Great Intro Bio prof!! His lectures are interesting and funny, and you can tell he truly cares that we all understand the material even though there's 150 people in the class. 50 MC on tests, and he gets them back within 2-3 days! The tests are "difficult but fair" as he says, expect to really understand the material to get an A.
Be respectful to him and he will help you out.

This class got me to be really interested in anthropology. His class is what I wanted and expected out of college: reading, tests, a fun professor that loves what he teaches, and a few opportunities for extra credit. He is a wonderful human being, I wish I had more professors like him.
Do not take this class if you have other options. Professor goes out of his way to pick on you. The professor took time from class to give me a hard time.
He's actually the worst DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. just lectures, hard grader, hard test
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Dr. Sandell is a nice man and all but this class is terrible. A crazy amount of hard reading that is not interesting whatsoever. His midterms are multiple choice but the questions are based on the most small details in the readings. He goes on tangents in class and does not stay on task and it is hard to get participation.

Dr. Sandell grabs infomation out of thin air. No matter how much you read and how you much study, you will NOT pass his exams. They are the most minute details and random facts. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS - there are other easier cores.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Don't do it if you don't have to. Put way too much time for a core class. He is nice professor himself but his class is not worth your mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's a lot to manage. If you are not sincerely interested in Anthropology, take another professor. I did make an A but it was extremely difficult to handle with the other courses I took this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great person to talk to outside of class. He was super kind and good about meeting you to discuss class assignments or exams. He does assume a few things and that was not my favorite. He grades kinda hard, and you need to pay attention to pass the class. But, he is a good professor just not a good grader.

The reading is a lot but the content is always interesting making it generally easy if you plan accordingly. If you skip the reading you will greatly struggle on the tests. Sandell is caring and his tests are easy if you read and pay attention to his interactive lectures. He makes test expectations clear and easy. Would definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is extremely passionate about anthropology, but hard to follow along in his lectures. You will read A LOT. Generous with extra credit on tests. Go to office hours to build personal connection with him, it will benefit you and your grade. Engage in class as he is a tough professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He uses every class to test you on whether you have read the readings assigned for the week and teaches nothing new. Each week, there's 40 pages of readings (in 12-point font) of convoluted anthropological papers (I'm not kidding) and then 10 pages of your notes on them + answers to his questions. Value your mental health and just don't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take him. He makes up his own criteria for grading papers that will not match anything you learned in high school, AP classes, or from other TCU courses. When you lose points, there will be no explanation as to why. If you want to get your grade up, change your writing style entirely because there is no way of knowing how to improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prepare to be amazed by Dr. Sandell! With his brilliant mind and clever wit, he not only challenges your intellect but also ensures you take responsibility for your academic endeavors. Show up to class, actively participate, and when it comes to your final paper, choose a topic that ignites your passion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Sandell's course was very straightforward and simple.  The course is very easy to get a good grade in, and requires little effort to receive perfect scores on every exam.  There is an average amount of reading required for the class, and the answers to most questions can be sourced directly through the textbooks, along with his lectures.

Dr.Sandell is a solid professor and you can tell he's passionate about the course. The course itself is fairly easy, but requires a decent amount of reading. As long as you keep up with the readings and can formulate a coherent argument in your essays you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you are actually interested in learning and developing academic skills take Dr. Sandell! He pushed me to the best of my abilities throughout the semester and I could not be more grateful! As long as you are engaged in the content you will do fine, don't be intimidated.

David Sandell is a very smart, passionate educator, and I would say his teaching philosophy is rooted in the idea that he wants students to reach new bounds as a reader, test taker, and as a learner. His passion for the subject and his job cannot be understated and is incredibly visible each and every day, which adds to the value of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sandell is one of my favorite professors so far. He is funny and engaging, and really knows what he is talking about. The class is by no means easy, but if you do the readings, pay attention in class, and make a couple of comments each class then you will have no problem getting a good participation grade or doing well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Sandell's class was the highlight of my semester. The subject matter is incredibly fascinating and I really enjoyed all of the readings. Dr. Sandell is funny, kind, and intelligent, and he is one of my favorite teachers I've ever had! The class is not easy but if you stay on top of the readings and pay attention to the lectures, you'll be fine.

Dr. Sandell is an amazing person. He is funny, caring, and passionate about anthropology. If you take his class seriously, you will do well. It is a college-level course so expect college-level work. There are only four exams and a final; the rest of the class is just reading, taking notes, and studying. I highly recommend it, just don't slack off.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I wish I'd looked at Rate My Professor before building my schedule. Professor Sandell is a very nice professor, don't get me wrong, but his class is VERY difficult to earn an A in. If you want an easy core, do not take him, if you interested in anthropology, he's quite interesting. Class is out of 100 points and only 4 exams/1 final/participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sandell is one of the sweetest professors I have had. He is very knowledgeable about anthropology. As long as you read and pay attention in lecture you will do good in his class. Exams are essay responses but as long as you understand the readings you will do fine. I would recommend this class for people who enjoy reading and writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: A lot of reading. Extremely tough grader. He knows his material, but appears to have a hard time explaining it to beginner students. Very high standards when it comes to essay assignments. No sample paper and very little instruction. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't take him unless you have to. Would not have him again, goes on tangents and hard to follow what the meaning of his lectures are. He is flexible with meeting outside of class but does not make any sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: At first I hated him because he assigned so much reading and had stupid pop quizzes. Then he grew on me. Then at the end of the semester, he gave EVERYONE a 70 for participation. I only missed class for medical reasons that I emailed him about and he seemed to be understanding. He told us all we would pass, and we did. Just with bad grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Save yourself by going through all these reviews, the bads outdone the goods for a reason. For an introductory class, he sure converted you to anthropology major.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was so scattered during his lecture, don't take this guy if you want to lose your hair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If I had to describe him, he is too smart for his own good (much to the detriment of the class). He goes on tangents that have nothing to do with the relevant course material and tends to degrade your answer if you dare to participate out loud, stating "you fell into my trap." I personally feel he has created every way possible to see you fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He requires you to purchase 4 books for his class. Every reading was difficult to understand and he does not help at all with explaining it. His lectures do not have any visuals and his hand writing is chaotic and confusing. When he speaks, he does not go through the material smoothly, but decides to jump back and forth between ideas. DO NOT TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes I've taken here at TCU. His grading was completely unclear, I never knew what his expectations were for assignments which is the thing that made the class so difficult. His lectures were completely disorganized and he just seemed incredibly scatterbrained. I struggled my entire way through this class, please save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Class was very content heavy and the exams were very difficult. You will also need to spend lots of time outside of class studying a group of people which takes lots of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Just dont take this class. You think you are doing fine and then he does you dirty on the term paper and drops your whole letter grade. Hardest grader and does not translate well with college students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Too much reading
I loved his class, but there was a lot of writing and reading assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I personally loved this guy. The class was 50 minutes but felt longer for sure, especially when he is lecturing. He is intelligent and experienced in the anthropology world. He has really cool stories but there is a lot of reading, 3 essays and quizzes, and a term paper so it is definitely English heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class is heavy reading and discussion based. There are also assignments and quizzes that have nothing to do with the reading/discussion. My worst professor so far at TCU
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You will read. you will write. you will be confused as hell by what he wants you to do. He is insanely smart but a little all over the place. Work hard and you can get an A. Strict attendance policy. He's tough but fair and passionate about what he does. if you love anthro he can be a blast, if not idk.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Sandell is a great teacher. He is always there for his students and is always willing to help and provide feedback in any way he can. Although he assigns a TON of reading and writing assignments, his class is really worth it, as his lectures are very insightful and engaging. You will definitely come out of it with a new perspective of the world
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Sandell cares a lot and is a very smart man but he just makes no sense. His instructions are never clear and the amount he expects you to read is completely unreasonable. I enjoyed the topics we covered but he overcomplicated everything and talked down to students all the time. Take something else if you can, you'll thank yourself for it.

Most of the grading depends on what your group gives you. This class was different from all of my other ones, but in a good way, very refreshing. You will read a lot, but the reading are very interesting. He cares a lot which goes a long way for me. Great class, you get the grade that you deserved, which is rare in the university.

He is not clear whatsoever on any of his assignments. Tons to read, and his lectures go off in tangents. He grades way too tough, will consider what should be an A paper as an F if he doesn't like one thing. He teaches this course like we're grad students, not as an intro elective course. Do not take him or you'll be miserable the whole time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His lectures were very scatterbrained, half the time I had no idea what he was talking about. He didnt communicate effectively what he wanted from certain projects and assignments, the whole class was constantly confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The course was reading heavy with no clear purpose. The lectures did not connect to the subject matter, and pop quizzes were very specific. I would suggest taking a different anthropology professor on accounts that although Dr. Sandell is very knowledgeable on the subject, he can not express/ teach it to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Sandell is really not that bad. The first month is the absolute worst but Dr. Sandell really does lighten up the course load as the semester goes on. Took this class during my first semester of freshman year. Just do the readings and talk 1x per class and he will reward you with a decent grade. He will learn your name and loves discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: David Sandell is teaching a graduate-level course and for some reason its being passed off as an intro class. There's a staggering amount of reading (he sends postscripts every week with testable material), and the right answer to any question in the class is always what he specifically thinks, not the material. His class sets you up to struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sandell assigns more reading per class than all of my other classes combined. He calls it an "Intro" class, but teaches it like a fourth year course. This is a course that satisfies 2 core credits so that is the only reason I stuck it out, but he sure made it hard. 100% do NOT recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You have around 30 pages to read for every week and there are weekly quizzes over reading. Grades on participation. You can't skip class. Not a hard class to pass if you just pay attention to what he says. Not many tests so you have to do well on the ones you do take. I thought it was easy, but there were a lot of people in my class who dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Taking notes from his lecture is nearly impossible. The amount of reading is far more than an intro level course should be. Do not take Intro to C.A. unless you're truly interested in Cultural Anthropology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Don't take this class. You have a participate every class in order to get a good grade for participation. Also there a lot of quizzes and the teacher grades super hard. The tests are very hard and there is a lot of memorization and a lot of reading. The final is a over a whole entire book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Sandell is a brilliant professor who cares about his students. His course consisted of a lot of reading and participation but nonetheless, he catered the class to the students needs ( you were still expected to work for your A though). His test required 7+ hours of studying but if you like non fiction you won't have a problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: One of the best classes I have taken. He posited questions and allowed the students to engage in discussions to figure out the answer. Great listener and offers writing workshops that are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If you like theory and discussion Sandell is great, but if you are trying to learn about the topic, good luck. You are required to read a lot, and analyze the articles. If you don't know how to analyze the articles to his liking don't expect him to teach you how. He also likes to hear himself talk. Recommend you don't disagree with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Makes you read- and read, and read some more. Likes to have class discussions and gives participation grades. Attendance is huge since you are getting participation grades and weekly quizzes! Overall he was a nice guy and brought donuts to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sandell is an awesome Professor! His intro class was super great cause its super discussion based. All you have to do is just contribute to the conversation and give your opinion. It is a lot of reading but its not super difficult, mainly a lot of stories. An easy class if you just do what your suppose to.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Teaches differently than most teachers, wants the students to learn skills instead of actual material. May seem hard at first but one of the best teachers I had at TCU . He cares about the students future which is different than most teachers. There is alot reading but if you do the work , you will most likely get a B or above in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You have to read 100+ pages every week for in class discussions and quizzes. You have to attend every class basically or you won't pass. He never teaches, your peers in the class teach, and yourself. WAY too much work for a class that is an elective. Tests are somewhat easy though. 6-8 page paper for the final (interview).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: None of those tags apply to this teacher. He says he wants participation but really wants you to watch him participate in his own discussion about himself, his ideas, and what he thinks about his ideas. Your thoughts don't matter if they don't line up with his. If you are a person of color, be prepared for him to patronize you. Don't take him.

He is a very smart professor, but he cannot relay his info to the class. He is very scatter brained, and very unorganized. He also is not clear on his directions and what he expects for tests and the class. He acted like he wanted to help, very nice and acted that it was going to make a difference but it didn't. Definitely would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: i took intro to anthro. he cares about his students a lot; he assigns a lot of reading each week but you don't really have to read it all because he gives you the test questions (short essay/paragraph response questions) before each test so you just have to find what you need to answer them. participate in class & do study questions & its an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I took Sandell for Intro to Anthro, and this was seriously the hardest class i've taken at TCU. You need to be at all the lectures or else you'll miss information you need to answer the test questions. He gives you possible test questions every week which is helpful, but grades tests really hard. I got a B and had to work so hard to even get that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: CULTURAL ANTHRO: Sandell is a very tough grader. He has years of anthro experience and expects you to think like him. TONS of reading, but if you do the readings and answer the study questions you can pass. A's on tests are possible if you do study q's each week. No final, just a paper. Class is easy--just open discussions, but lots of homework.

Sandell pretty much just wanted to hear his own opinions repeated. He also was political but failed to hide which party he favors, which isn't bad since the research paper at the end of the semester should be written in the opinion of Sandell's political views.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Ok so basically Sandell gives study questions which he then picks two or three to be on the tests (3 tests, 1 final). He has lectures every period that are supposed to be group discussions but he goes off on weird tangents and analysis that leaves everyone scratching their head. Not impossible but requires alot of BS and tolerance. Gives ex. credit

This class is basically taking a philosophy class because Sandell goes off into long, long lectures EVERY single class about the "hidden, true meaning" behind things (which doesn't even sound legit). Participation is supposed to be everyday but he talks so much that it's hard which makes it hard for you to get credit for that. Boring, wouldn't take

This class was the worst experience of my entire academic career. I was very excited to take his Intro class but I wish that I had stabbed myself repeatedly in the eyeballs instead. That would have been a far more enjoyable experience. Although his tests appear simple, he is an extremely harsh grader and does not give any basis of what to study.

If you aren't willing to rise to the challenge,don't bother taking Dr Sandell. He assigns the same amount of reading as the other Anth profs, but you are expected to actually critically read the text and discuss. He's not going to baby lazy people,he is going to train you to think and write critically. Your grade reflects your willingness to do so.

David Sandell is an interesting character... To say the least. His class is difficult to pay close attention to, he is "funny" I suppose, but doesn't keep me awake very well. I cannot wait for this class to end.

Took him for Cultural Anth and Lang&Culture. Can be a bit dry, but overall a great professor. Willing to help. People most interested in the material are ANTH majors, so if you're not prepare to be a bit out of your element. Lots of reading, not excessive. Easy short exams.You can pull an A if you keep up with the reading and weekly study questions

Sandell's Intro to Anthro class was literally AWFUL! Please safe yourself and do not have him as a professor. All he does is lecture about things completely irrelevant to the test of study guide topics. If you ask him for clarification he goes off on a rando tangents about nothing you asked. Got an A b/c I taught myself, don't expect him to.

I took Anthropology of Violence course. Although it was a higher level course, it was nearly incomprehensible. His "teaching method" is supposed to be in class discussion, but all you do is listen to his disconnected opinion filled thoughts only sometimes connected to the readings. EXTREMELY SUBJECTIVE GRADER

After taking his Language and culture class twice, I can truthfully say Dr. Sandell is an excellent professor. Yes the material can be dense but however once you learn the lingo of an anthropologist the course really begins to take off. Work toward learning the material and not a grade. Do this and the only way to fail is to not apply yourself.
I was so excited about anthro before I had him. The discussion based class was pointless to the hmwrk or tests. Easy A, but you have to teach yourself.

took intro to anthropology, used to be pretty excited about taking it but by the end it was one of the most absurd classes ive ever taken. The rest of the poor comments say it all except I'm pretty sure i have NEVER EVER been let out on time in that class. So if you your into that sort of thing id avoid him

I took Intro to Anthro with him, and I think he's a generally good teacher.  Most of the class is just class discussion about the readings, but Sandell is passionate about his work.  As long as you do the readings, it's not hard.  I'd recommend!
The class is very easy. All you have to do is keep up with readings and particpate in discussion. If you like to get by just skimming the reading and complaining, its not for you.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF. for any class! All he does it talk forever and you learn nothing. His classes have no structure and he assigns excessive amounts of reading that don't apply to anything he talks about. Absolutely pointless.
useless professor who is not willing to help and will decide on a random grade. AVOIDE AT ALL COSTS (EVEN IF YOU ARE A MAJOR)
Dr. Sandell is lenient and very willing to help. I recommend him to all.
He is extremely helpful, the class is interesting, stay on top of the readings and you will be fine. He has interesting experience and views, great professor.

If you want an easy class don't take this class. Then again if you're in college and expect to take easy classes then you should probably feel pretty bad about yourself. The material is easy to grasp, but you have to stay on top of it. Also Sandell is easily the most helpful prof. on campus.

This class was awesome, a lot of hands on work that really illuminate the lecture, Sandell is great and really cares about his students, he brought us a ton of treats and will do whatever he can to help. The class required effort but if you put it forth you are golden.

He assigns obscene amounts of reading and multiple essay questions each week. You have to memorize all of those essay questions to answer only one or two on the exam. He never clarifies info from the reading and has students present their thoughts on the reading instead of teaching but then butts in anyway yet never explains the topics we read.

As all the others have noted Dr. Sandell is a very nice, personable man, but he is practically useless in explaining topics, and tends to repeat his sayings rather than explain them. In addition, be prepared to hear why capitalism and "whites" are to blame for all the evils of our world. Very heavy on Marxist philosophy, and would not recommend him

Really is a nice guy! There is way to much reading to keep up with and is nearly impossible to retain the amount of detail needed for on the tests. There is only a midterm and a final of which you must choose two of four topics to write on. the topics that come from the weekly study questions through out the semester (4-5 a week) Its too much

He's a very nice person, but not exactly the best teacher for an intro class. He assigns massive amounts of reading that are difficult to get through because he wants you to retain every detail. He is very opinionated and wants you to see his point of view. Doesn't explain the complex ideas very well. Tests are all essay and subjectively graded.

Dr. Sandell is a nice person, but his Language & Culture class is nearly incomprehensible unless you already have a tons of prior knowledge. The readings might as well be in Greek for all the sense they make, and he often just doesn't understand why people are confused about a complex topic. The class is really not worth the agony.

Most students that give bad ratings come across as idiots, but please think this rating through before you consider his class. Though Sandell is kind, he lacks the ability to make a dense subject comprehensible: he assigns ridiculously long readings that while interesting, are not well explained in class, & he's very subjective when grading. Beware

While I found the class interesting, he taught a 2000 level class like a graduate course and expected us to have prior in-depth knowledge before the class began.  Though he is smart, he lacks the ability to bring a complex topic down to size.  Would not recommend because in the end, I still had to fight with him for my grade (B+).  Rough class.
Dr. S is a great prof...he's kinda tough, but you'll come out better for it.  Reading can be lil' dense, bu not too bad. Definitely worth taking

Dr. Sandell is an exemplary professor who will challenge you to become both a better student and a better person. His dedication is rare among professors; indeed, he will spend hours outside of class with you to help you build your writing skills. If you are looking for an authentic intellectual experience at TCU, look no further than Dr. Sandell.
Horrible teacher. Lectures are all over the place & don't relate to anything. Not helpful at all. Makes you feel dumb. Talks down to students when meeting 1 on 1 & even during class time.
writing a paper in this class is impossible. his criticism is so harsh  and unfair that it is so hard to get a descent grade on a paper. never have hated a teacher so much in my life.
Polish your writing and analytical skills before you ever set foot in his class.
I took him for into to Antho.. and we had to do so much reading, which was actually interesting, but I did not learn anything from thic class from Sandell. Waist of time.
this professor is an idiot...Not structured at all!!! He's really random and makes no connections to his lectures and the readings.

Not very good at the beginning of the semester, but definately improved.  Lots of reading, but I never did it.  I still BS'ed the quizzes pretty well and made A's and B's.  His tests are pretty hard and long for such a short time, but still doable.  Lots of writing.

Over half of the class dropped. And please be reminded his classes are introductory, but he makes it like a graduate class. He practices favoritism. He barely teaches, always depends on the talkative students to contribute. His paper requires us to deliver world class grammar & writing skill, not contents...

I wouldn't even recommend this class to my worst enemy, that's how horrible this teacher is. His lectures are boring and esoteric and he has no concept of a well structured class. There is a tremendous amount of reading and the tests and quizzes are all in essay form. This class is nearly impossible to pass and is a complete waste of anyone's time.
No Comments
No Comments
Class was fun. My favorite this semester-- a break from big lectures.

Professor is super nice and super passionate about Shakespeare. The class is boring but easy as long as you participate. Grade is mostly based on 7 “pop quizzes” but he'll actually tell you when they are. These are generally after you've read the first act of a play and mostly ask about the characters all multiple choice. No technology allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I didn't think I'd like poetry, but the teacher made it so interesting. Each class he projects a poem on the screen and has students read it out loud and talk about it. I got so much better at reading and understanding. Class had a fun vibe.
This was the most fun class I had this semester. I loved listening to everybody's ideas and watching the scene videos. The readings made sense after the classes.
I loved the discussions. He made super hard texts make sense.
This was a freshman composition class. He made the writing assignments fun because they were relevant to student's lives. I liked attending the class.
Great teacher. Made class fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher overall, we did the same thing every class (analyze poetry). My only problem was with how few assignments went on our grade, there were just two analyses and three tests. The tests were not difficult if you studied and understood the material. The analyses were entirely subjective though.

He is really engaging and nice!! His lectures are amazing and not boring at all. I'm not a person who really into writing but end up this is the class I like most in this semester. Take his class and you won't regret.

Lectures are boring and he “cold calls” to read poems/share your thoughts. He's monotone so it's hard to stay engaged and if you don't like poetry the content is uninteresting. Your grade is only based on 3 exams and 2 analyses. The exams are subjective and the analyses are hard to understand. If you don't need to take this class, please don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't think I'd like this class but it turned out to be great.
He was really nice. Class was fun. He lets us get writing homework done during class.
I loved this class-- films were fun and it was interesting to hear other students opinions.
I liked the films and discussion on Fridays. The films helped me understand the plays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Gil knows what he is talking about. However, you are only graded by three assignments which are tests. Attendance is mandatory and you only have 3-4 skips which he factors in at the end of the semester. Lots of reading for class but if you take notes you will do well on the tests. He is straightforward in the answers he is looking for.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is fine, lectures are boring. During finals week my grade dropped nearly 4% after he went back and changed grades from months ago, he provided zero explanation to why this is happened to a lot of us. Now my grade went from an A to an A-. Thanks.

Professor Gil was pretty good up until the end of the year. 2 days before the final Professor Gil went into the grade books and started to change percentages on assignments that had been completed and graded months prior. My grade dropped 4% 2 days before the final adding unnecessary stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly if you took AP Lit an did well in the class, Shakespeare will be easy for you. Has a clear schedule for when each act will be read, quizzes are 5 questions each but easy if you know the general plot and names of characters and places. The essays are easy if you took ap lit or lang cause they're the same thing and he grades easy.

This class was pretty easy (if you're a decent essay writer). I barely read the plays and was able to get A's on all the exams because they're just essays based of the themes of the plays. If you review his slides posted on D2L and have a general idea of the play's plot/it's main themes you'll be fine. Recommend if you're interested in Shakespeare!

Nice guy, but the Shakespeare class wasn't easy or enjoyable. If you don't write something that he wants to see in your essay, you won't get a good grade. Entire grade is also based off 6 essays. 2 of them being in class ones. He's a repetitive lecturer (most classes are lectures) but he knows his stuff. If you can handle a hard class, go for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took this class online and it was more interesting than expected. Beware he will call on you randomly with questions, so make sure to have the reading done by class time. All exams are essay based questions.

He is the most boring guy trying to teach a class. He constantly repeats himself throughout his lectures. He gives you two super complicated analysis papers with no instruction on how to do it, so your grade suffers because you don't know how to follow the exact structure he wants. Highly recommend taking a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Gil is really great if you already love Shakespeare, and a good intro to it if you don't. You can tell he really loves what he teaches. However, he tends to repeat himself/talk himself in circles a lot. Can get annoying. Do your reading and you'll be fine. There are lots of surprise quizzes, but they're easy to predict and not hard if you read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took Gil for Intro to Shakespeare because I heard it was an easy class. The class itself is pretty easy and the test are pretty straight forward from the readings and the things he mentions during class. For the reading quizzes if you don't read you won't pass. I recommend reading the book and No Fear Shakespeare to get a better understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Gil is one of the nicest professors I've had at TCU! However, his lectures can be rather monotonous, he likes to repeat himself. Always do the reading because you never know when a quiz may come. Only two tests that are essentially just in class essays. If you do the work he will help with your final grade if you're on the line.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Gil is VERY knowledgable! This class IS NOT HARD, but people make it hard for themselves. If you read thoroughly you will get 100% on all the quizzes and just participate, its not hard. Highly recommend this class if you are interested in Shakespeare

He knows what he's talking about. You can tell he's passionate, but he repeats the same information a lot within the same lecture. He will also ask a question in such a long-winded way that you will forget what he asked when he points at you to answer. Quizzes are easy if you read, and reading is not difficult to complete at all.

Dr. Gil is a fantastic professor. His lectures are extremely enjoyable and he's a nice guy to be around. This class was a lot of reading, but I'm pretty sure it's his last time teaching the class. Also, he was fair on the two essays we wrote and reading quizzes were very easy if you read.

He's very nice and helpful. He'd try everything to help you out with your essays during office hours. He's clear about what he expects from your essay and gives helpful feedback on essays. Pop quizzes are very predictable if you notice the pattern of when he's gonna give a pop quiz. Go see him during office hours, read the books and you'll be fine.

he is awesome and enthusiastic with his lectures. those are sometimes pretty boring, anw, you can know and learn so many interesting aspects about early ideology of civilization. I hate lit best but this class just makes me so involved and interested. requires averagely 3 chapters for each class, but no readings do not harm much so far :)

Not a hard class just extremely boring. There's reading almost every night and weekly quizzes that aren't too bad as long as you do the reading. you have to do the reading or you'll be lost and fall behind quickly. his lectures are repetitive but that makes it easier cause you know exactly what the essays on the tests will be on. easy A if you try

Only take if you are obsessed with Shakespeare. He is extremely repetitive during lectures...anything he lectures on for 50 minuets could be summed up in about 5 which makes for an extremely boring class. Quizzes are easy if you read, but I don't even think it's worth it because of having to sit through lectures.

Honestly I haven't had an English class this easy since 7th grade. Lectures are so repetitive and inconsequential its mind numbing- if you listen for 5 minutes total scattered throughout the period you'll pick up everything he's trying to explain. I don't recommend taking him if you want to keep your sanity.

I am currently taking Intro to Shakespeare and was never really interested in the class... Honestly, all you have to do is sparknotes prior to read, read the book, participate in class and act like you are semi interested. He loves when you give your opinion. He asks a lot of questions and its an interactive class, but it's a manageable core class!

Great professor, fair grader. I found his lectures and our class discussions insightful and interesting most of the time...but you have to read the material before class to follow along. He encourages class participation, and never demeans you if you're not quite on topic. Four essays, one in-class.

I was initially very excited about this class and the material covered, but the focus often drited in the student led discussions and overall the class was bland. It was difficult to determine your grade throughout the semester but Gil attaches letters to essays which helps. Gil's a great professor, it just was not an interested group of students.

Class was terribly boring, unless you are really into Shakespeare. The class isn't hard, but there are daily reading quizzes that are difficult even if you read. He is very knowledgeable about the subject, but I think he is just an alright teacher.

Dr. Gil is a really cool guy. The source material could be kind of confusing at times but he really likes to discuss it and always does his best to understand a point you're may be trying to make. Grade was made up of 4 papers and he is a really fair and quick grader. Recommend to anyone.

Very nice guy, very fair grader, not the most interesting class I ever took but I managed to sit through all of them (except for one, overslept that day. :P). If you need an Honors English credit, you can do worse than Literature and Civilizations with Dr. Gil.

Professor Gil was very hard to understand at times, he says "um" every other word.  There is a lot of reading for this class, but I don't think anyone actually did read.  There are also e-college assignments, which he grades easily on, but the 2 exams throughout the semester are very hard.  You kinda have to be interested in Shakespeare...
Nice guy, but I was so bored in his class! Reading about Homer and other ancient literature made me want to go to sleep. Yet another disappointing honors class at TCU.

Intro to shakespeare.  Great teacher!  Really knows what he's talking about.  Only a Midterm and a Final with some monotonous e-college assignments and a memorization for grades.  Definitely need to go to class for the information.  Read about an Act a day for most plays.
Gil is the best english prof I have ever had!  Class is fun and his lectures are wonderful.  There is never a dull moment in his class.

I took Intro to Shakespeare and loved it. While he didn't go too in depth with the subject material, it was very interesting and enjoyable. He says "um" A LOT but you get used to it. He's an EXTREMELY nice guy and easy grader. Just wants students to be interested in the topic and discuss.

Personally I liked Dr. Gil a lot, he is always willing to help you with your papers and takes an interest in getting to know you.  The class however was not what I was expecting, not too challenging and his lecture style is a little boring and uninforming.

This was basically a discussion class...got rather boring on some days.  Towards the end of the semester, i even stopped reading the material, but it's easy enough to bs.  He likes for you to participat, so do so, even when you don't really know what you're talking about.  He's a nice guy.  Not too clear on what he wants on essays..but easy grader.

I actually looked forward to this class--it was the only one I didn't skip. Dr. Gil is a great professor.  He's very kind.  You don't have to worry about the class being difficult.  You will understand the material after he's gone through it with you, and he's a generous grader.  I'd recommend him to anyone.
Extremely lenient when it comes to turning in essays.  The class structure is very loose and discussion is interesting.  He's a cool professor and a nice guy.
Lots of exam periods but at the end of the semester, there's a day where you can retake any exam you did bad on. Very caring and answers any question no matter. Super helpful overall!

Gives lots and lots of resources and practices for students to use and bases his exams on these practice problems. Very straight forward math class, with homework, quizzes, group work, and tests. Final exam grade can replace lowest exam grade. Likes to put a few tricky problems on the exams, but attainable A.

Dr. Tomlin is great. His class was pretty difficult but he is more than willing to help during his office hours, and responds quickly and thoroughly to all email questions during the week. The exams were difficult but he gives lots of partial credit. He genuinely cares about his students, and students that say he is mean are just soft.

his class is very hard and fast compared to any other classes, take him if you are already good at math. very accessible outside class, very supportive during office hours, reasonable exams, lots of hw but flexible with deadlines. great lectures but if there is anyone else easier than him just take them! still one of my best professors ever!

Do not take this class unless you are ready to teach yourself outside of class. Rarely helps and yells at students for being on their phones for a split second. Only teaches through videos outside of class and will embarrass you in front of everyone for asking a question.

His precalc class was SO hard. He did not teach, he instead put us in groups every week to teach eachother. Mandatory to be in every class, as every day something was graded. He would get annoyed when we would ask questions even through we werent even being taught. I think he does mean well but just has a very unique "teaching" style.

Worst teacher I've ever had, take someone else if you can. Idk how these ratings are so good because he makes this class way harder than it needed to be.I studied at least 8 hrs for the tests to barely pass them and 13 hrs for final which I think I failed. He grades so specifically & takes off points if you do not answer exactly how he wants.
His pre-calc class was all group learning. He did not teach at all, and would get upset if you asked any questions. Not a good teacher if you can't learn from teaching yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This professor is probably among the best professors I have ever had, his teaching style was engaging, and his assignments were easy to follow. The way to succeed in this class is to practice practice practice even if it means going to YouTube for help. His office hours were great and walks through things you may not understand. Would take again!!

This professor is the best! Guided notes in class, works through problems and answers questions thoroughly! HW is due night before exam (ask for extensions if need - very understanding), exams on paper, quizzes each week on paper. Math was always a bit easier for me, but I think he is very helpful during office hours and wants to see all succeed!

Easily the best professor and teacher I have ever had. I had no experience with math other than PEMDAS, and he guided me through doing quite well. It is hard to put into words how amazing he truly is. I wish I could take him for every math course in my future with TCU. He has absolutely changed how I view math and life for the better. Thank you DrT

Honestly one of the best teachers/professors I've ever had in my life. ALWAYS willing to help and wants to see you succeed, want homework extended, done, have question about work, answered. Tests are reasonable. He explains so well and writes all the notes needed & posts to D2L. Attendance is needed. A lot of homework and tests.

Tomlin's teaching is mainly done online through the textbook and videos outside of class, but practice problems are done in class with him.  Every student goes at their own pace and you have multiple chances if you fail a quiz.  It is a little confusing sometimes but overall a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Tomlin is definitely the best professor, I've had at TCU. He is very easy to reach, has easy enough lectures, and is very understanding. Exams may be a little tough, but he lets students take an index cards to them, so its not bad at all. Incredible professor, would definitely take again.

Dr.Tomlin was a great professor and i learned so much from him. His grading is a bit confusing but allows you to retake modules if you dont get the grade you want. He was always so great about answering emails and he truly wants you to succeed and do well in his class. His office hours are so helpful and he guides you through any questions you have

He was an ok professor. His exam style is super weird and unfair. 0-6, 6 only being 1 answer wrong and after that it immediately drops to a 5 which is equal to an 80. Highly recommend office hours, it does help but he almost makes passive aggressive comments that make you feel like an idiot at times.

Class: Elementary Stats. Dr. Tomlin is a very good professor, especially for people who aren't necessarily math-inclined. He gives extensions on homework, no-questions-asked and is always willing to talk outside of class. However, for people who are more math-inclined, I'd warn that his lectures could be really slow.

Dr. Tomlin is one of the best professors I have had. His course outline is clear and simple. He gives you 3 opportunities to take a module. This allows you to practice and fully understand the concepts. He delivers his lectures well and is always there to help his students. He is flexible and understanding if you need more help and an extension.

Would 100% recommend him!! He's very understanding and cares about his students and their success. It is an overall self-taught and self-paced class, but he is there to help and is extremely helpful when you need it.

Really nice teacher. Dr. Tomlin makes calculus not boring somehow, but he isn't the best teacher. You have to teach most of the information to yourself. His tests are hard too. Good guy, but not a great teacher
Best Math Teacher I have had
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Tomlin is such a great professor. His lectures are easy to follow and he will answer any questions you have. He grants homework extensions without question and really cares for his students. Math is definitely not my strongest subject but his class was a breeze. Go to class, pay attention, and do test reviews and you will do great in his class!
Amazing teacher , Cares a lot about his students. Go to Office hours ! Take him for both percalc and calc you won't regret it.
not bad, very self taught and all at your own pace. hes quite the character.

He is very accessible to his students and if you make an effort in this class you will do well. He cares about his students and learned everyone is my lecture of at least 50 students' names which was thoughtful and shows he cares.

Dr.Tomlin really cares about his student and wants them to do well. He is very accessible outside of class and is easy to approach with questions.His lectures are very enthusiastic which can be really helpful for those who have his class early in the morning.Doing the assigned homework and reviews will help you make sure you are ready for the test.

Dr. Tomlin is one of the best stats teacher at TCU. My only issue within the class was that all exams were taken without calculator. His lectures however were extremely helpful and he is always there to help.
He is really comprehensive pretty chill. You need to go to class but he knows the material
Really cares about his students; the tests are kinda of hard but as long as you show up everyday and pay attention you will be fine

super nice teacher and wants you to succeed in math. is also always there if you need help in the class room and out side of the class room. in class he gives easy point for his little daily assignments he does at the end. study guides are very clear and so are exams.

Professor Tomlin is the best to take for stats! He wants his students to succeed and is such a good teacher. He explains the material so you understand it clearly and posts his notes from class in case you were absent. Exams have a study guide that prepares you so much. If you pay attention you will do well. Take him for stats!!!

Overall just a very good prof. Test reviews that show everything you need to know, enough homework to understand information but not an excessive amount, and very accessible if you have any questions. I would definitely take him again if I needed another math class.

Professor Tomlin cares so much for his students! I was nervous about this class because his teaching style was difficult to adjust to but once I did it all went great. Tomlin replied to emails, is flexible, and genuinely wants his students to understand and do well. You are able to retake quizzes at least twice for a 100! I got an A!

Dr. Tomlin is one of the best professors I have ever had. He has office hours 4 days a week and will respond to emails as soon as possible. He wants all of his student to succeed and really had a passion for math.

Dr. Tomlin is really enthusiastic about teaching. He has a lot of office hours available and is really willing to help so take full use of that. I take Discrete Mathematics I with him and now I want to major in Mathematics. His exam is quite long and require a bit of thinking, but he gives 10 percent extra credit opportunity after every exam.

He is very helpful during office hours and during class. If you need help, he is extremely willing to answer any questions, explain problems, and go over the material again. He can be a little frantic and he goes through material quickly in class but if you attend office hours, he will help in any way he can. He wants you to succeed. I recommend.

Dr. Iba is one of the most genuinely caring professors I've encountered in my academic career. I took her for Communication and Third Places and she made every lecture feel fresh and distinct. No two classes felt the same. As long as you have a solid grasp of the key terms the exams are very manageable.

Dr. Iba is the ideal professor. She is kind, engaging, and incredibly intelligent. Her class is not attendance mandatory at all, you can fade whenever you want but her classes are also enjoyable enough to where I enjoy going. Tests are easy essays based off a list of vocab you need to know and are open book. Definitely recommend any of her classes.
Very nice professor and works with you with whatever you need. Gives good feedback and only wants the best for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Iba is nice and caring; I loved having her as my prof. She is not very accessible through email outside of class, and her lectures are interesting to an extent. She pulls from in-class discussions and textbooks for the exams. Her exams aren't hard, but can be confusing in the way she asks her questions. Can be nit-picky for an opinion class.

Dr.Iba is a fairly easy grader and very eager to help her students, but it is impossible to pay attention during lectures. Listening to her lecture is like a lullaby. Tests are medium hard, mostly multiple choice. Nonetheless, she wants the best for her students and loves her job.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Iba is a great professor. Yes, sometimes the lectures do get boring, but she does a great job of keeping people engaged. She's a pretty easy grader when it comes to assignments and presentations. The tests are difficult, but they are worth little to none of your grade.

This class was the most boring class I have ever taken. The lectures are nonsense, a bunch of rambling. The tests are insane, it's over stuff we have never learned. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. She is chill but her class makes zero sense. I will never use this information ever again. The tests are like we are in graduate school. Class is a GPA tanker.

Dr. Iba is an awesome person and she makes the class environment pretty light. My only real issue with her is how she lectures. She almost never gives a straight answer to any question, and she goes on unbearable tangents that don't relate to the topic. Her lectures are almost no help for her exams. But otherwise, it wasn't a bad class.

Dr. Iba is amazing! For Food Comm, we did a semester-long project building a website, and she was so involved in everyone's projects and wanted everyone to succeed. Her tests are HARD, but they aren't worth a ton compared to presentations. She cares so much about her job, her students, and our futures. I always looked forward to coming to class!

Good teacher. Easy to get along with - if you respect her and show her you are interested she will reciprocate. Tests are hard I averaged around a 70-75% for both exam 1&2. Quizzes were ok - you just had to be familiar with textbook and class information. Learn a lot but a lot of work is required to succeed in this class.
Food comm is much more doable than her other classes

Teaches her political opinion and tests you on that. She insults the president in her exam questions. Unreal. Its like she is purposefully triggering anyone who disagrees with her. As a man in this class, I feel personally insulted, I feel uncomfortable in her class each time I have gone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Iba's class is challenging but very rewarding. I learned A LOT and was inspired to be more proactive in my personal life. The tests are challenging. Make sure and know your notes inside and out! Class is incredibly interesting and relevant to today. Iba encourages and prepares you to apply the material outside the classroom!

Very sweet lady and easy to communicate with in and out of class. The lectures are extremely boring, and the tests questions are very confusing. Interesting class, but wouldn't recommend if you aren't a good test taker. Also there are 6 tests but you get to drop one so it's nice.

Do not take. Yes you learn, but she is INCREDIBLY boring. Its only a 3000 level class, and she creates her test as if we are in Graduate school. Hardest tests I've ever taken and I'm a senior. Every single MC question has answers like "c) both a & b" and "none of the above". She doesn't post her powerpoints/notes online either. GPA dropper class!!!

This woman is a literally angel. You will walk out of her class feeling much smarter and confident as a student. Make sure to do the reading and youll be good. Shes funny and such a boss I honestly wish she could teach every comm class
Great teacher highly recommend. Tests aren't that hard and she grades everything pretty easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Iba must have changed a lot since she was last reviewed on here because this class was not easy. The content of nonverbal itself is not difficult, but her exams are very tricky. I would have my notes memorized backwards and I still struggled to get even a high B. Presence isn't mandatory but she doesn't put her lectures up online.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She has definitely gotten a lot harder since others rated her, but she is nevertheless a great professor. (I am a straight-A student & barely got an A.) Take good notes, ask questions, & memorize the material backwards & forwards. I found flashcards helped me. Her tests are tricky and she wants you to know the material well! Interesting class.

I've taken ALL of Dr. Iba's classes. She is my favorite professor at TCU. She teaches group discussion & nonverbal comm- highly recommend both! Exams are multiple choice. Don't buy book. Highly recommend her classes for both comm majors & non-comm majors! Her classes are fun, interesting, & the material is applicable to every day life.

Professor Iba is great! She's helpful, funny, nice, and uses real life examples. You have the ability to do very well in her class and to learn a lot. Group discussion teaches you good skills about how to work in groups that translate into the working world and other school group projects!! If no other reason, take it for that!

I've had Iba for group discussion and nonverbal. She is amazing! She is one of the best teachers in the comm department. Tests are multiple choice. You do not need to buy the book. Easy A & youll learn a lot! Take Iba!
great teacher

Group discussion was such an easy class. She tells you everything you need for the tests, and grades all projects/assignments very easily. Just do the work, and you will be great! She is a very fun and caring person.
really helpful, clear, and easy
She is such a great teacher!! easy A if you study what she asks. EASY EASY EASY!!!!!!!!

Iba is the best teacher at TCU...you can tell she really loves her students and her job.  She makes class interesting and she is willing to help you anyway she can.  I highly recommend her, if you see her teaching a class you need hurry and sign you.  SHE IS AWESOME.. Not hard...not too easy you have to study..
She really is the best at TCU!
Incredibly patient teacher who in my opinion is underappreciated. The material is common sense, but the work definately can keep you busy.
Best teacher at TCU...she lets you take your test in groups...need i say more?!?!?
A-mazing.
the goat fr
BEST teacher. she makes class fun and likes to have personal relationships with her students. best accounting teacher by far. TAKE HER IF YOU CAN!!!!! you wont regret it

Ms. Davis is a decent professor. She tries hard but still sometimes has difficulties explaining concepts  to students. Her tests are tricky but she curves. Participation matters and you are expected to be completely professional in the classroom. Read the book, make sure you understand the material, do the problems many times and you should do fine
My favorite Professor at TCU by far. She is one of the reasons I became an accounting major. I was dreading my first accounting class, and ended up loving it and learning a lot.

Professor Davis has been one of my favorite teachers so far. Account in general is not easy but with her you will learned a lot. She made the class interesting and she was very helpful throughout the whole semester. If you can I recommend you to take her! Her tests are hard but if you know your material and study you will get a good grade.
She is the best professor I've taken at TCU. She actually cares about her students and wants you to succeed. She's the reason I am an accounting major.
Ms. Beaver was one of the best teachers I've had in Neeley. She's an expert on the material and makes accounting fun. Take her!

She makes accounting easy to understand and takes the time to learn every one of her student's name. Accounting isn't an easy class, but she's very willing to take time out to help out her students. Also responds to email in a timely manner. I would recommend taking her class.
Beaver is awesome! I cant say enough good things about her. She wants you to do well and she wants to be your friend. She does a lot of work out problems and is always clear. TAKE HER!
Ms. Beaver is super nice and connects with her students; she even took the time to learn every single student's name. Tries to make accounting fun and relatable. Definitely take her for accounting!!

This is Ms. Beaver's first semester to teach at TCU. I was nervous to take her class at first because she was new, but she seems really helpful and enthusiastic and does her best to present the material in an understandable way. If you like accounting OR don't like accounting - either way -take her class.

Lots of work. If you forget to do peer review you get 20 points off major assignments you spent lots of time on. Class is boring. Grades hard. Don't recommend taking her for this class but maybe shes better for a different class. She was very helpful when you go in and ask for help during office hours though. She is very nice and wants to help.

There are 3 projects and 2 tests. The projects are not explained well and her feedback is not the best. She is the best option for research and it is jsut a hard class in general, but I would be on top of your work and ask for clear instruction
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No rubrics whatsoever for huge assignments. Very misleading grading. Nice in general, but not an adequate professor. Not helpful with questions/feedback. Take the other research prof!

Nice lady, but she takes pride in making her class hard to succeed in. The content is so easy. Literally review of other classes, but she makes it so difficult to get an A in the class. She has extremely high expectations, but doesn't give clear instructions. Lectures are super boring. 2 exams, not hard if you study and 3 parts to a sem group proj.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Does not give clear directions for ANYTHING. No rubrics for massive research papers, making it impossible to get an A on big assignments (which is basically your whole grade). Test reviews are only two days before the test—study a TON if you at least want a B & if you can't present without referring to the slides even a little, she'll fail you.

She is really a sweet person, but her grading is extremely unclear. There were test review days but what was gone over wasn't even on any of the tests. Kind of just unclear what she wants from students and attendance is mandatory.

Very caring Professor. 2 difficult tests throughout the semester with a study guide if you study you can do well. The group project descriptions throughout the semester can be confusing but if you ask questions and pay attention in class you will do well. Lots of grades in the gradebook can make up for bad test grades. Attendance heavy but 3 skips
I would not take her.

Her grading and assignments are very unclear. She is a nice woman and cares about her students. Her grading never makes sense and she is strict on attendance. I wouldn't take her again for the sake of my GPA but she is a nice person.

Kwon is the worst. She does not care about your success and can be rude about it. She has very unclear directions a lot of the time. Her lectures contradict the text book and it can be very confusing. For tests, she gives a study guide but then tells you just to read the whole text book, which is very overwhelming and unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her courses are structured with an emphasis on lectures, supplemented by occasional quizzes, in-class activities and group projects. Dr. Kwon's teaching style might be challenging but it is equally rewarding. She balances academic strictness with personal warmth, making her an invaluable educator and mentor.Getting to know her can be deeply helpful

Kwon is super sweet and the class is straightforward. The lectures can drag but she tries to make them interesting. Prepare early for exams and STUDY THE TEXTBOOK. Group projects can boost low test grades. The content is interesting and you will learn a lot that can apply to future STCO classes.

Professor Kwon is a very nice person, but a tough grader. Tests are closed note and pretty difficult even attending class everyday. Everyday is full lecture and homework is reading and quizzes. There are a few projects with presentations throughout the semester that will help your grade if you put in the work on them.

Professor Kwon's assignments are applicable in the digital media industry and I gained a digital media marketing certification from this course. Her teaching style is lecture-heavy, but study the class slides/notes and you'll do fine on exams.

Holy crap. DO NOT TAKE PROF KWON. I cannot even start to explain how hard this class was. She specifically told us to NOT reach for an A in her class... I'm sorry what? She would read off the slides and if you ever had a question she never knew how to properly answer it and would respond with "ill get back to you on that". unacceptable!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Kwon did not have the best lectures but she does try to engage everyone. i did have a situation with her where she tried to give me a B+ instead of an A- due to attendance (although i literally emailed her a valid excuse which she never responded to) although she isnt the nicest, her class was not super hard and i loved what we learned!!

A pain waking up at 9:30 and listening to her read off slides. Would ruin my entire day actually. I really love advertising but this class was something I would never look forward to. Tests are just not what she would teach in class at all. Never again.
Literally all lectures and so boring. I thought I was going to love this course but sadly she centers class around lecture and barely any group work or interesting assignments. Not that hard though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, the lectures are the worst part. You have to sit in there and watch her read off of the slides. I could have skipped every class and had gotten the same grade.

I had Kwon for advertising. She is a sweet woman but the worst teacher I have ever had at TCU I finished with a B in the class and it was the class I worked hardest for. I am usually a straight A student but Kwon completely made them impossible for this class. Do not take her.

Dr. Kwon is the worst professor. She means well and probably is a nice person, but she is very difficult to understand and her tests are confusing and really hard to study for. Most people barely pass her class. She just reads off of the powerpoint but tests on material that she's never taught. 100% take advertising with another professor.

She is a sweet person, but a terrible professor. Never made an A on any assignment in that class and I'm barely passing(usually I'm an all A's student but have a high C). This class is unnecessarily hard and she is a strict grader. Her exams are the worst and don't make sense at times, even if you study a lot. Don't recommend this professor.

I took notes by pulling out my textbook & highlighting what was on the slides, bc they were word for word from the book. Her tests are too difficult or got caught up in definitions, bc I did very average on the tests after thorough studying. I did great on projects, so I clearly understood the material. She is well-meaning but not a good prof.

She is really terrible. Her lectures have no flow and don't really make any sense. The book is equally as bad. Her tests are on large chunks of material but ask super specific questions. She grades projects harshly and they are all group projects.
One of the worst classes I've ever taken. She is a nice lady but was difficult to understand at times and would contradict herself a lot. The tests were way too hard for what this class is.

Do not take this teacher! She is a left-wing narcissist who pushes her agenda onto her students. Furthermore, she will negatively impact your grade if you do not follow the propaganda of the left and use your brain to think critically. Avoid this teacher at all costs to save your sanity.
Hated this class. Condescending, rude professor. Random discussion and no value added by professor. Avoid at all costs.

Do not take this professor or this course. Pushes her own agenda and opinions. Incredibly condescending if asked questions or for clarification. Has student lead lectures every week, and is extremely critical of personal reading comprehensions. Much of the semester long project is busy work as well. Overall very rude, and has elitist values.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor is terrible. She pushes her agenda and often pushes her opinions as facts. Avoid!

Dr.Farris is a fantastic professor and her lectures are very interesting. She really cares about you as a person and is willing to work with you through your issues. The homework is just a reading assignment, and the tests are not hard. If you study you will do great and make a B to an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Attendance is rarely taken. Lots of reading, but it will help prepare you for participation in class and the exam. She's nice, and she's easily accessible via email or office hours. She did provide extra credit. You will have a few group projects in her class, but she tries not to weigh them at an unreasonable percentage.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Farris is one of the best professors at TCU. She doesn't try to push her agenda and isn't interested in getting you to like one political party. Always willing to help students in office hours. Hard work and effort is something she notices! She loves class discussion as well. Overall, great professor! Would take her again.
Dr. Farris is a really hard grader. The democracy labs are very hard to get a 100 percent on and she is very picky. Her exams are also sort of difficult on the essay questions.

Dr. Farris was awesome. She delivers really thoughtful lectures and if I could take another of her classes I would. She almost convinced me to switch to a Political Science major. Her classes require you to do the reading but she's fair and definitely cares about the material. Take her if you can!
She let me wear a mask even after TCU lifted the mandate

If you can avoid this professor, I would suggest it. The content is not hard. However, the professor is very annoying; she has an elitist mindset and makes her political opinions obvious in class, ridiculing students who do not align with her beliefs. She is also a frustrating grader, often taking 1 point off on an assignment to avoid giving a 100.

I absolutely loved the class I took from Professor Farris. She is amazing at telling what kids are putting a lot of work in and helps those kids get a fair grade for the work they do. She is also amazing at keeping her political opinion silent and just teaches facts. I highly recommend her class.

Dr. Farris is one of the best professors I've ever had. She rewards students who are engaged and show effort. If you don't care, she won't care.
