She has a lot of office hours, but come with questions. Don't expect her to help without any. It can be a pretty difficult class, but still doable.
Be prepared to have wayyyy too many slides and basically remember everything on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I understand that with COVID, classes are crazy, but I, along with many classmates, feel we were left in the dust, and nobody cared or wanted to help us. reviews.comment: Dr. Fry is a sweet person but a tough teacher. She breezes through the slideshows and expects you to know a lot of material that wasn't covered in high school.

reviews.comment: Fry doesn't teach and class is spent doing practice problems in break out rooms over content we were supposed to have taught ourselves using her prerecorded lecture videos before class. reviews.comment: She is a very nice lady and qualified for her job. However, Dr. Fry was not meant to be a teacher. You basically must teach yourself and make yourself practice the material in order to do mediocre. Even then, she is not clear what will be on quizzes/tests. There are too many students for her alone to teach, not very accessible in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She grades lab reports pretty generously. There is a fair amount of busy work, especially considering how this is an upper-level course, but they are generally easy As. Be prepared to write a lot, but overall, the course is not difficult to do well in.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Chemistry at TCU in general sucks. If you have to take gen chem, make sure you get Dr. Fry. She is very accessible to students in office hours and via email. She will try her best to help you learn and pass the class, but the class itself is very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is going to be a hard class no matter who you take it with and Dr. Fry is no exception, but I 100% recommend her over any of the other GenChem professors. She is tough and expects a lot but is very clear about her expectations and genuinely cares about her students. Her tests and quizzes pull heavily from her powerpoints so study those.

Dr. Fry's class is super hard, however she is one of the best, sweetest, caring professors ever! Her material is difficult, but she is a fair grader (gives partial credit) on her quizzes/exams. She is super accessible outside of class in OH/emailing questions. She truly cares about you doing well and will work with you if you have any issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Fry's General Chemistry I is a weed out for pre-meds. If you haven't taken AP Chemistry, good luck surviving. Demanding class that requires hours of practice a day. Dr. Fry is willing to help you but looks at you stupidly when you don't know chemistry concepts you have never been taught. AP Chem is better to know beforehand.

Dr. Fry is the best professor I have ever had. She is a very hard grader but she explains concepts so well. If you prepare and pay attention during class the next part is doing the practice problems which takes a lot of time.

Chem can be hard, but taking her will make Chem much easier. She explains the concepts in great details, provides lots of practice exercises to help you prepared for quizzes and exams (Practice Practice Practice is her usual saying), and even specify what will be tested. Do the exercises, and ask for help during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Fry cares about her students so much! She's AMAZING! People who don't like her are people who don't try or put in the work. Chem is super hard, but she is available outside of class to help. She is SO smart and knows what she is doing. You just really have to study and prepare. She's an actual teacher not just someone who gives you the answers
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Fry is a nice person but a terrible professor. The lectures are the most confusing thing you will ever listen to, so it helps to have background info

reviews.comment: Dr. Fry is good in quant, although when you ask her questions in the lab she will not answer them, even if it's about improving your technique. reviews.comment: Dr. Fry is an amazing person. She makes time for her students outside of class and is so patient. The class is very difficult, but Dr. Fry makes it bearable, for she is kind and helpful. Some say she can be scatter-brained, but I didn't find that to be a problem.
Absolutely terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: JULIE FRY IS A FABULOUS PERSON. She couldn't be more helpful and caring. The weekly quizzes are actually helpful in preparing for the exams, so give adequate time to them. The final is a grade booster if you study enough. Don't be afraid to set up meetings with her or go to office hours, she really cares about helping students.

Dr. Fry is a nice professor. Expect weekly quizzes and a test about every month. Do the suggested practice problems and you will be set. Go to office hours and get to know her because she is helpful one on one. You have to do lots of work outside of the lecture to get the concepts but she will help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Fry is a wonderful person, but not a good teacher. She has a clear understanding and passion for Chemistry, but cannot give clear and concise lectures. Thankfully, her office hours and willingness to teach devoted students allowed me to pass. I would not recommend her as your first Chem teacher. Very hard if you've never taken AP Chem.

Started the first day washing glassware and it was the most stressful thing I've ever done. It gets better... actually you just get used to the stress. It's not hard to make an A but quant will consume all of your time. Lectures are very hard to follow. Memorize procedures, equations and slides for exams. Sometimes I think I still smell ammonia...

Take Dr. Fry over Dr. Bob! I have had both and I performed way better with Fry. Focus on her powerpoints and do those problems and work old exams for practice. I used the book for reinforcement, especially for titrations.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Quant was definitely fun and prepares you for future labs, but it is not a walk in the park. Make sure you know each lab inside out and titration techniques well bc accuracy is a large chunk of your lab grade. (she does drop the lowest one) Tests cover more info from lecture and the labs than the book. Quant is a lot of work, but totally worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: PRACTICE PRACTICE PRACTICE. This is the key to doing well in chemistry. She provides PLENTY of sources of practice and is EXTREMELY accessible outside of class. She can be tough to follow in lecture and can sometimes go off on tangents. Take advantage of office hours as she will take her time to explain there. She is usually very nice and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Fry is polite and professional, but she is incredibly difficult. She is so scatterbrained. It is hard to follow her train of thought. She lectures off of her slides and doesn't do a lot of teaching, just reading. You have to teach yourself everything. If you are not good at chemistry before taking this introductory class. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Julie Fry is a monster of a woman who won't teach you anything. You will have to teach yourself almost everything beyond the most basic chemistry information. Chemistry does take work as you just have to practice the application of concepts learned in class. She constantly contradicts herself which forces you to spend extra time teaching yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr Fry is just an amazing person in general, very very caring. Quant puts pressure on labs by having accuracy points, but the large majority of students get an A or B (currently 81%). It does get quite stressful at times, and it requires effort, but the  point is to prepare students for the future labs. A must-take for chem majors.

Love Dr. Fry! Quant Lab is definitely difficult but I LOVE the class. Great class for pre-med majors. Definitely not an easy class but she is super helpful in office hours! Labs are stressful because you are graded on accuracy but if you like lab then its fun in a way! Just be organized!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While Gen Chem I and II itself aren't that hard, Prof. Fry makes it so. Her lectures are difficult to follow purely because she seems so directionless and scatterbrained when she speaks. 90% of the time, I ignored her in class and simply studied on my own, both from her slides and the textbook. She isn't terrible, but definitely is not helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. Very caring. Practice her past exams and you shall pass. Learn your dimensional analysis well. Don't memorize answers. Go to lectures and practice MasteringChemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dont bash the teacher,  Chem is just one of the toughest at TCU. Yes, she could have graded easier, but she does curve about 6% at the end of the course. Don't need to show up except for clicker points. I thought myself everything, didn't need lectures. online portion  easy. Quiz on Wednesdays  study 1/2hours. 3 Exams  each needs an all nighter!

Dr. Fry is very scatter-brained, and it was hard to keep up with the lessons. The examples she works in class don't help with that problems on the tests. However, if you go to her office hours she's sure to give you extra credit.

A lot of people don't like Dr. Fry but honestly she was the best professor I had 1st semester. I really wasn't putting in the work, or bothering to learn, but she never made me feel bad about it she just kept encouraging me and giving me advice and even though I bombed the 1st 2 tests I'm coming out with a C-. Do the work, and get committed or else

Dr. Fry is the worst teacher I have had. Her lectures are scattered, her homework and practice problem level do not match with test and quizzes, she will say something is not important for the exam and then its worth 50% of the points.  She also expects at least 15 hours a week studying. If you have options stay away from her class.

I had Dr. Bob 1st semester and Fry 2nd.  I'd say Bob is probably a little better as a teacher, but Fry is easier.  She still felt super hard while I was taking the class, but I ended up getting a B (instead of the C I got in Bob's).  So I'd say take her. Even though they're both terrible I think you can get a better grade with Fry

Dr. Fry comes off as a sweet caring mother-like figure, however that does not mean her tests are easy, they are very tough. Lectures are all over the place and often rushed through. Don't plan on making an A, unless you took AP chem in high school. EVERYONE will have to STUDY HARD AND LONG if they want to even pass this class.

Dr. Fry is without a doubt one of my favorite professors at TCU. Dr. Fry wants her students to actually understand chemistry concepts. If you listen to her and understand the math, you will ace her tests. Go to office hours: she gives those students more partial credit. She always posts a worksheet for each chapter online that is similar to test.

I don't even know where to begin. Extremely scatter-brained. Expects you to know everything and is horrible at explaining anything. Her office hours didn't help much either. Practice problems are always way easier than test problems. Very boring. Went to class just to get the 4% for iClicker. I'm usually an A student and this class killed my GPA.

Nothing about her teaching or homework was helpful. She suggests the homework & her practice problems for prep, but once it comes to test time, everything is 1000x harder than what you practiced. Also, terrible at concepts and flies through info. I've had to teach myself everything. Usually I'm an A student, best at math & science, and I have a C-

She is a very confusing lecturer, very scatter-brained and ditsy at times. Tests are hard and graded harder. I leave class and office hours more confused than when i first got there. I do the home work and extra practice problems and go to the office hours and I am struggling to even pass. Only take if it is your last option. Or wait till next year

Tough class if you don't have a strong chemistry background. I took AP chem and got a 95% first semester, so it's definitely doable. My suggestion-- study details of her powerpoints. Do quizzesexams from previous years. And use the book to clarify certain concepts. I found it helpful to ask kids in the AED pre-health office questions.

Fry will help you if you ask for it, but as far as the lectures go I was pretty much teaching myself. She rambles on a lot and expects you to know most of the information before you come to class as she moves very quickly through examples and the lecture. Google will be your best friend in this class. On the bright side she is really nice.

I really didn't like Julie (I don't think she deserves a title) as a teacher. She doesn't explain things well, she rambles a lot, and she gives poor examples. If you don't read the text book, you will die; God forbid she actually teaches you something in class! I would take Dr. Bob. Yes, he's harder, but at least he teaches and explains things well

Quant was actually a really cool & helpful lab to be a part of because of the TAs; but, her control over grading & her discussion portion ruined everything. She can't even solve her own practicetest problems & when you go into her office hours she belittles you and makes you feel dumb instead of helping you (because she doesn't know how to help)

Definitely choose your chemistry professor based on your major. I would say if you needed this course as req for a major such as Kinesiology or Engineering, pick Frye. But Pre-Med should go with Dr. Bob because he preps you for O-Chem. Frye was a pretty decent teacher overall. Go to her office hours and practice workbook q's if you want to do well!

Yes, General Chem is VERY hard and that makes Dr. Fry's class very difficult. However, Fry is an AMAZING teacher if you actually work hard and go to her for help. She is very understanding and truly wants you to do well in her class, you just have to make an effort (and let her know you're making an effort).
By far the WORST teacher I've ever had. She makes everything impossible to understand and you are forced to teach yourself everything. I definitely recommend taking a different class!

She doesn't teach in class. She MAY go over two problems max in class and then you'll never see them again. Her exams aren't anything like her in class problems and hardly ever similar to the homework. Utilize her TA but wouldn't recommend going to her office hours. Her TA helped me a ton, but I still go a low C in the class and I'm a science major

She is a good teacher, but the class is very hard.(Office hours saved me) she will bump you up a point or two if you or borderline. She prepares you for Organic very well by giving test that force you to study to do well. I recommend her to see if you can handle Pre-Med

Very nice lady, and helpful if you go to office hours. Didn't learn anything from class- had to teach it to myself using the book. Tests and quizzes are really difficult and she will put problems ont here that she knows you can't get full credit for. Also asks a lot of concept questions. You have to know about scientists, dates, and experiments.

Her quizzes and tests are killer. To be successful you need to read the chapter before class, take notes during class, read the chapter again, do all of the homework problems, and do the practice quizzes and tests. She is actually very very helpful in office hours and I wish I had been able to go more often. For our grading scale, an 84 was an A.

Worst professor I've had at TCU. Does not thoroughly explain or teach concepts. She will rapidly skip through powerpoint slides, saying "you should already know this." Ridiculous considering this is first semester gen chem. Then she will put that info she didn't teach on the test. Tests and quizzes are hard. Everything I learned was from my tutor.

Mrs. Fry is a nice person, but assumes you already know everything in the class. Isn't the purpose of taking the class to learn it? I always got low test scores, and its really discouraging. Chemistry is hard no matter who you take, but Mrs. Fry isn't very good at making concepts simple.
Tough!
She has easier tests, but she doesn't teach the material, you have to teach yourself everything outside of class.

I took Fry for Gen Chem my freshman year and she was AWFUL. After making a 4 on the AP Chem test in high school, I felt pretty prepared for her class, but she makes things so complicated and explains nothing that I started to hate chemistry. She even gave us a quiz with a question that she couldn't even solve. Don't take her unless you have to.

She's a very caring professor! It's not an easy A but she pays attention if you're making effort and she becomes more flexible in grading. A very sweet personality. It's a lit class but there isn't a lot of readings and some weeks we had no readings at all. Yes, attendance matters in her class.

She is one of the best professors I've ever had! Yes, she can be a little tough but she gives you multiple opportunities to improve your grade. She gave us a mental health day and decreased the number of pop quiz questions when we asked her in the class. She's passionate about the course and she doesn't give readings longer than 15 pages.

Attendance is mandatory and can really affect your grade. Her lectures are thorough but can be very confusing. She is a really harsh grader and will find any way to mark you down. Her assignments are very though and she gives you very little time to complete them. There are also pop quiz's on the lectures and assigned readings that are difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I love her at first because I think she is pretty caring. However, mad tough grading on assignments. Yes there were detailed feedbacks, but on each assignments she will find something to grade you down. There were pop quizzes and they are crazy. Extra credit for not using phone but only 3 credits for that. High expectations for our assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She has crazy expectations for assignments that are due the next week. Gives pop quizzes. You do get 5 free absences but if you miss a day, you will probably miss a lot of info. Uses an ai detector that is not accurate at all and if it's not below a certain percentage she will just send it back or give you a zero. Take someone else.

Mrs.Ferdos can give you detail feedbacks on your writing. pop quizzes. Tough grader, attendance matters. no phone for extra credits. if you want to improve your writing and learn more ab literature, take her. if you just want a chill core class, i would go for the others. I had been working a lot just to get an A- in her class (95 is A)😭😭
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Never (Never!) take this man for lecture. His lectures make no sense, there are no practical/scaffolding problems. He is condescending and mean. The grades are all exams, and they are extremely difficult.. He also takes forever to return your grades back. The only redeeming part of this class is that the exams are heavily curved.

One of the worst teachers I have ever had in my education, when it comes to the lecture side of this class. His whole class is based on the tests, which are AP test style and extremely hard. He also provides very minimal study material, making most of the studying up to figuring it out on your own. AVOID!!!

Dr. Funkhouser's lectures are LONG and confusing. Even the TA tends to be confused by his instructions for the lab. If you are lucky enough to be able to select a lab time on a Friday afternoon, any evening, or when he is teaching something else, DO IT! He never attends those times. Labs go by much faster and smoother when he isn't there.

He is not good at lecturing and is very confusing. Doesn't explain much and just writes down equations, saying to use them. Tests are very hard and the only thing graded in the class. 5 tests during the semester. Avoid taking him if you have the option

I think all labs are entirely taught by TAs. That being said, there is a lot of grace being given. You don't get to pick your TA, but mine went step by step to help us. Class often went over time, and honestly I don't think I could tell you a single relationship I learned from lab. I got a lot of Bs on minor labs, major labs is where it counts!

Not a very good lecturer, lectures generally end up leaving you confused while also being way too theoretical and not actually ever explaining formulas. Exams are generally nothing like the homework he assigns, only redeeming factor is heavy curves on tests which are needed as otherwise there would be a forty average.

Physics 1 and 2 labs are mainly taught by TAs, with Jeff popping in from time to time.10 labs each, 2 are major labs.Reports are 3 parts, procedure, data, and conclusion & you split up each part in your group. TAs are super helpful, willing to check work before turn in. Don't miss a lab or your grade will drop by a letter. Overall not bad.

He generally explains the lab well but its mostly the TAs who work with students so take the ratings here with a grain of salt. He allows you to drop at most one lab. Grading criteria are not always clear so ask the TA to clarify as much as you need (or you will be deducted points for the most trivial errors.)

The lab makes physics bearable! He does lecture for a while, but it's helpful stuff especially if you engage. He and the TA (who is very nice) are super helpful, and make it clear what stuff to include to get full credit.
He is nice and labs aren't hard, but he talks and talks so labs take way longer than they should.

Makes a 2 hour lab go by really fast. Really fun and not difficult experiments. He helps you do the experiments when you are stuck, really willing to help you and help you learn skills. He does sometimes talk and explain too long and then you don't have enough time to complete experiments.

Ms Abigayle is incredible. I have never had a professor who loves their job and their students as much as she does. Class feels more like a conversation than a boring lecture, so it's easy to want to show up. She is a genius so you will definitely learn the material. She also bakes for us and brings her dog a couple of times and she's gorgeous

Miss Abigayle is such a caring and fun professor. She clearly cares about student success and I never dread going to her class. It is a 30000 level course but totally doable as a freshman. Class almost always involves a fun activity and I always felt like I was learning and making connections. Definitely take her if you can!!

THE BEST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD. she is so amazing and cares about you so much (and she brings her golden retriever to class!). The class is super doable and fun! lots of group work but this was one of the only classes that I actually met people and the entire class talks so its super engaging.

Take this class! There are lots of reading assignments, but they are very easy. You get 2 absences and grades are mostly based on reading evidence and group work. 3 very short writing assignments and an easy final presentation. If you're looking for an easy A this is it. I finished with a 99 and didn't always stay caught up on readings. Fun class!
This is a woman who loves to teach and genuinely loves her students. That's really all you need to know. Even if you don't like the class subject, you'll like Ms. Abigayle's class.

BEST PROF EVER!!!!!! She is genuinely so kind and cares about every single one of her students. For this class we did have to read, but they are all books that adolescents read, so it wasn't very time-consuming. I don't love reading but she made this class so enjoyable and we had very little work outside of class other than some reading. I love her

Abigayle is SO nice. I took this class as an elective. It was a manageable workload and Abigayle did a great job making the content relevant. You can tell she really likes her job and loves interacting with students. One of the nicest professors I've had!
So nice. So easy. So light.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The most caring professor I've ever had at TCU. She loves her students and is passionate about her work. Class is fun and interesting, she even brought her dog one time!

Abigayle Farrier has been my favorite professor so far at TCU. She is genuinely so kind and is always willing to help with any homework or projects. I have never had a professor like her. She even has brought her dog to class. There are two quizzes and a few writing assignments. Everything has been fairly easy. I LOVE LOVE LOVE HER.

I was not looking forward to taking Writing and Editing, but Dr. Farrier made it a positive experience. She is a super nice and funny professor, and it's obvious she cares a lot about her students. The best part was how willing she was to look at articles outside of class. She always gave helpful feedback and it allowed me to improve as a writer.
AMAZING!!!! She truly cares about her students and makes the lectures fun yet educational. She is the best professor, definitely take a class with her!

I loved her!! I don't really like reading but she made it very easy to succeed in this class and easy to understand what we were reading. Very few assignments. She would also bring her dog to class on exam review days. She loves to talk about her pets and just her life in general which always makes a professor seem more personable. 10/10 recommend

Very interesting class, as long as you come prepared each day and do the readings you will do fine on your exams. She loves to talk about her pets and even brings her golden retriever into class who is super cute.
Great teacher, you can tell she enjoys her job. She cares for her students and she seems to put a lot of energy into the students. If there is anything that you need help with shes gonna be there.
Professor Farrier is amazing. She is clear with assignments and they are super manageable. She always has great stories and cares for her students. I wish she would teach more classes in STCO!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: kindest professor I've had at TCU. The class it actually pretty interesting because she runs discussions very well. She's easy to talk to and makes it easy to get a good grade. I think everyone would love her and her class even if you don't like literature.

Dr. Farrier is the best professor I've had so far in my college career. Not only is her class structured so that it is easy to succeed as long as you are putting in a fair amount of effort, she is also a very kind person and genuinely cares for her students. I would 100% recommend taking a class of hers if you can!

Dr. Farrier is the best English professor I've had. Extremely understanding, caring, and personable. Brings in her dog for review todays and likes to bake for students. Would absolutely take a course of hers if you can.

I wasn't expecting to like this class but Ms. Abigayle made the literature interesting. She's super nice and the class is honestly not that hard if you just do the work. There's extra credit and she brings her dog to class on review days. Definitely the best English professor I've had!

Ms. Abigayle was terrific! Her class should be an easy 4.0 for anyone that participates and actively tries. She assigns short readings, discussion board questions, and small essays for the multiple-choice tests. She's a professor that wants to see you succeed, and she's very accessible out of class if you need help! I recommend her 10/10!
Great at everything!

Professor Farrier is one of the kindest professors I have had at TCU. She truly wants to see everyone succeed and if you reach out she will be there to support you. You do definitely have to go to her class or you will not do well, but overall it was. a great course. She made it very enjoyable.

I love Ms Abigayle!!! She really cares about us and it shows. She's the best professor I've had at college and always goes out of her way to help everyone. I don't like reading but she made literature fun. She bakes for class and the food is so good! Ask for her pumpkin muffin recipe :) It's not hard to get a good grade if you come to class.

She is seriously one of the best professors here. So kind and wants you to do good. The class is very doable and an easy literature class. She is very understanding and hardly assigns outside work. You will get an A if you show up and do your work. Take her if you can!! She is the BEST.

Ms Abigayle is the best. If you can take her at TCU, do it!! She's so nice and really funny. And she always brings dessert to class! It's easy to get an A if you do the assignments and show up. She just wants to see that you're making an effort. Love her! (:

Ms. Abigayle is by far the best teacher I have had at TCU. Her classes normally have a theme (mine was criminal minds). She reads over drafts and final papers before you submit them and is constantly giving feedback on your work. Easy A and class time is great. She gives you time in class to work on upcoming essays!! TAKE HER CLASS
She's the best!

Ms Abigayle is the best professor I've had so far in college. She made English class fun and was always willing to read drafts before we submitted them. She's the most caring professor and is genuinely interested in students lives. She also makes the best desserts ever and brings them to class every week! Try and take her class if you can!!

Abigayle Farrier is an amazing teacher. She is understanding, organized, and timely. I took her English class first semester of freshman year and it was by far my favorite class. Farrier made sure to clearly explain each assignment and concept. When I was sick one week, she helped me get caught up. It also helped that she brought food to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Abigayle is seriously the nicest professor ever. This class wasnt hard and as long as you do the work its pretty easy to get a good grade. She gives lots of extra credit and lets you fix things if you ask. Go to her office hours! Shes really good about helping with papers if you ask her. Class is always fun and shes gorgeous too!

Abigayle is the best professor ever!! She bakes for us and is so caring. Attendance is not "mandatory" in class but she is very understanding if you need to miss classes. She also gives out so much extra credit and you can fix your essays. The class is a breeze as long as you put in the effort that is all she wants to see.

Professor Abigayle is one of the best professors out there, period! Shes caring, and makes sure you get the material and offers her help at all times! Shes also very funny and loves to hear and engage with her students. She always encourages student feedback and caters her class to student needs. The best professor ever!!

Abigayle really makes an effort to help you outside of class, and is willing to read drafts and give you feedback before you turn in major assignments. She was good about asking the class for input on how everything was going, and valued our opinions on the class. The readings were better than I was expecting and the class was fun. Would recommend!
The material covered in class is completely different from the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a great lecturer and really nice professor who is available outside of class to answer any questions. Attendance is not mandatory, but you should try and attend class because the test reference specific details from the lectures a lot. The tests are specific to the readings which makes it difficult to study and do well even though it's online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a very good guy. Has great energy and is a true Texan. His class does get boring and lecture heavy. Ask us to read a lot and has extras credit over the readings. Did some fun things but class is pretty dependent on the test. I never read and was able to get around an 80 on each. They're take home test on a lockdown browser.
Super great guy and funny but the tests are awful. Doesn't matter how much you study the questions are so specific and hard to answer.

Awesome dude, super engaging lectures. Grading is based off of a few tests so do well on those. Some pop quizzes here and there along with other extra credit opportunities. Great group project half-way through the year.

Dr. Ferguson is super sweet but he makes his tests very difficult. I have been a straight A student for the past 3 years and his class was the first I have ever gotten a B in. He is very caring and offers a ton of extra credit, but unless you do not write down everything he says in class, the test is going to be super hard.

If you're struggling in the class, he will help you if you ask.Homework was always watching movies and TV episodes (most of which you had to rent on streaming services) and reading articles. Only 2 exams (together are 53% of your grade). Tests are very difficult. He offers extra credit occasionally. Projects are easy if you follow directions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take Dr. Ferguson if you enjoy gambling! Dr. Ferguson gambles with your grades, literally. Want extra credit? Pick a number between 1 and 20. Your team won a debate? Only one of your teammates gets credit for it. How do you pick? No worries, he'll roll a dice for you. If you don't care about passing a class, this one is for you.
Group project was a pain honestly and his test were really hard Nd didn't match the lectures. I would take only if really interested in the subject and contents

Prof. Ferguson is super friendly! BUT- his class is so ridiculously hard. Considering that this is an entry level political science class that most students take just to fulfill their requirements, it is way to difficult and time consuming. There is is heavy amount of outside reading, and there are only 4 exams that make up your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ferguson is genuinely the nicest professor!! He cares about his students and brings so much energy to class. The class has a good amount of reading but it is completely manageable. All exams are about 30 mcq and online. If you go to class, pay attention to lectures, and keep up on readings you will do great. He also gives tons of in class EC!!

Professor Ferguson is a super nice guy but he is a very hard teacher. The class itself is easy and the only homework is reading articles every night and pop quizzes but the test are so hard. I studied long hours, took great notes and still did poorly on the test. There are 3 tests and a final and that is the only thing that makes up your grade.

Very excellent professor. Very nice person, responds to emails quickly, very friendly with the class. There are no assignments, but one group paper, 3 midterms, and one final. The tests require you to draw from being present in the class, some guest lectures, and lots of reading before hand. Not required but reading quizzes are worth bonus points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is very difficult. I would not recommend this class if you were just taking it to fulfill a CORE requirement. Dr. Ferguson is a really nice guy who is really passionate about what he teaches but the test is very hard, and 3 tests and a paper is what goes into the gradebook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy.... but I'm trying so hard in his class and can barely manage a C. I loved Gov in high school and had some familiarity in it and I still STRUGGLED. I had no clue what to study for the tests and they are soooo hard. It's only graded by 5 assignments, 4 exams which are actually impossible. The essay is actually ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You'll probably have a hard time doing well in this class if you dont attend his lectures. There are lots of questions on his tests that come from lectures. Great professor, super funny! Make sure to do readings often because the extra credit quizzes (which are on random days) can be extremely beneficial for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ferguson is a great professor who cares about his students.  I appreciate that he is never biased politically.  Tests, however, are really hard, even though I did all of the readings and studied with plenty of time in advance.  There are many extra credit opportunities, though, and so definitely do those!  There also is one group paper.

Great guy, great lectures but tests are some of the hardest I've ever taken. This class is a good way to double dip but definetely not an easy A. Roughly 30 mins - 1 hour of reading every night and roughly half the tests are made up of reading material.

Dr. Ferguson is the freaking man. Took this course twice and failed when I was a freshman, but got an A when I retook. Do the readings and participate and he will help you out, great place to get your feet wet in poli sci.

Although he is a very kind professor, his tests are AWFUL. Even with studying, he tricks you and doesn't prepare his students well enough. Like I said - GREAT guy. He's so nice. But beware of tests. You take 4 tests and have one big group project, that's all for grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ferguson is awesome! His exams are hard and require a lot of studying. One large group project and 4 exams is all that is required. Attendance is not required but missing a class might hurt your grade.

Literally 3 grades in the class: 2 exams and a fat paper. If you mess up one your absolutely screwed and he doesnt care at all. Luckily got a B but he doesnt care about how his students do because our first exam our average was a 55, IDK how he has good ratings but dont take this class it is not an introductory level class that is the biggest lie.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Such a funny guy who genuinely cares about his students.He tells awesome stories and makes lecture super interesting.There are occasional pop quizzes that are always easy if you do the reading, and they only count for extra credit.There's one paper and about 4 exams and that's all you're graded on, so make sure you do well on those.Definitely take!

He is really nice and cares about his students! He is very passionate about politics and tends to tell a lot of random stories. He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities, but there aren't many assignments. Your grade is mainly made up of just exans. Overall, he was pretty cool and relaxed.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ferguson his a great guy and a great professor. He told us on the first day of class that his tests are hard and he has high expectations - which is definitely true. You have one big group paper that you have to complete. Attendance is not mandatory, but if you miss lectures, you won't do well on tests. Prepare to take notes and study A LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No small assignments, only tests. Attendance isn't mandatory but you will be confused if you miss one class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Doctor Ferguson is a great guy who really cares about his students! However, if you are looking for an easy A this class is not it. There are weekly readings that aren't for a grade but are on the exams. The exams are very difficult and you NEED to study. There is one group paper that is a major part of your grade. Very interesting class but hard.

Dr. Ferguson is a great guy and truly cares about his students. His class is very lecture heavy, but the way he teaches it makes sense and is very clear! One of my favorite teachers at TCU! I highlight recommend taking his class!

Political psychology is a VERY interesting class; however, his tests are timed and are all application questions (usually 25-35 questions). Tests were online and cannot use notes. He does provide tons of extra credit but they are only worth .25 or .5. Material is on the lectures provided but be ready to apply the material quickly on the test!

Dr. Ferguson is by far one of the best professors at TCU. For what could be a very biased class, he does a great job of remaining unbiased and showing all sides of the political spectrum. He is also super helpful and easy to reach for questions and if you need help with anything he is there to help. Plus, he's an all around friendly guy.

Fantastic Professor! Knows so much and is so fair and unbiased in teaching the material. You will be relatively unaware of where he stands on the political spectrum. His lectures are great and he gets so excited about the material it's hard not to smile. Mostly graded off of tests so definitely study or you will get in a hole. Can't recommendenough
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ferguson is one of the best prof Ive had This is NOT a easy class lots of readings few assignments and cumulative final. Overall if u put in the work u can pass the class. Big tip is that your class better engage during class to make it fun BUT Ferguson is very respectful and knows his stuff and my fav. KEEP up with readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: "Howdy Y'all" is the first thing you'll hear every single class. Overall, he is a really sincere guy and nice, but the class had very few assignments that are graded, with 3 tests being 80% of your grade. These tests are some of the hardest tests I have ever taken, but he does make it up with the group assignments, which aren't too bad.

Professor Ferguson is one of the happiest professors I've ever had, simply adores his job. I took his Am./TX Gov. intro class and it was much more difficult than expected (no easy A), but I did learn a lot here, and he's a fantastic professor. I'm also not a POSC major, but do recommend it for any non-majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: If you don't care about your GPA and want to enjoy class take this. TESTS ARE INSANELY HARD. I am a relatively smart student and I received two grades in the 70's. Ferguson is a GREAT guy and makes class enjoyable, but the tests are ridiculous. He also uses a hard A/B/C/D scale so if you're at an 88 you're out of luck and you're getting a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Ferguson is an amazing poli sci professor. I absolutely loved his class and would strongly recommend taking his courses. Prof. Ferguson clearly cares a lot about his students and their wellbeing outside of class. There is a lot of reading in this class which I recommend doing because it comes up in exams.

Professor Ferguson is a great lecturer, and he really cares about his students. He is respectful to all political viewpoints and teaches from an un-bias view. There are only 3 exams and 2 group projects, so you have to do well on them. The exams are HARD, and he asks very specific and tricky questions over all the material (2 books, textbook, etc).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ferguson is a great professor. Keeps the class rolling, his lectures don't get boring and he even brought two guests to talk to us. With that being said, his tests are very hard, as he tricks you and asks weird questions. Reading the materials is a must to do well on the tests. Manageable class, but be prepared to earn the grade
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class was American & Texas Government and Im from Texas, so admittedly I had a major advantage over other people in the class. Even though it wasnt A difficult class for me, he is a very interesting, caring, intelligent, and funny professor. He gives a lot of extra credit as well. If you need an extra Social Science credit take Dr. Grant!

A lot of reading and he tries his best to test you on all the readings. He truly cares about his students and wants the best for them. Final will be cumulative but he will give you a grade he thinks you deserved in the class he does not try to fail anyone. Also he does not do the plus/minus system. You should for sure take him but be ready to read.
Dr. Ferguson is a very personable Professor. He gives interesting lectures and an absurd amount of extra credit. I would definitely take Dr. Ferguson again, hes a great professor.

Treats introductory level course as a 3000/4000 level. 4 exams. Tests on SPECIFICS on multiple articles & textbooks & notes. Exams 30 questions only & difficult. Extra credit consists of .25 pts and .5 pts here or there. Memorize terminology (he tricks ya.) Great guy but not a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Ferguson is one of the best. He really cares about his students and is more than willing to help you. Tests arent bad if you put in a little effort. Attendance isnt mandatory but I wouldnt recommend skipping frequently. Overall Id definitely take him again, great prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I LOVE THIS MAN! Seriously cares so much about his students and is willing to help you get to where you want to be. Tests are hard, but LOTS of extra credit and an 89.5 is an A. His lectures are engaging and you can tell he is super passionate about everything he talks about.

Dr. Ferguson brings his A-game to every single lecture and is great at engaging his students. He provides plenty of extra credit, does not plus/minus grades, and an 89.5 is an A. Was always available to talk and help you figure out what you can improve on if you are not doing as well as you would like. One of the TCU poli sci department's bests.

"HOWDY Y'ALL" get ready to hear that at the beginning of every class along with amazing outfits. Ferguson is an amazing professor who is truly passionate about what he does. He is SO caring and really wants you to succeed. Not much work but read the articles and readings because they will be on the test! LOTS of extra credit!! - Honors Amer. Poli
really hard exams, DONT TAKE HIM
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Love this professor! You can tell he genuinely cares about his students. He is very engaging and never boring. Make sure you do all the reading though because it will show up on the test. If you study you can easily get an A in the class. Also, he gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit that can really boost your grade.

Great person, not such a great professor-- He basically just explains/reads whatever the book says-- he CAN'T connect the dots and his lectures are kind of boring and mainly useless because you can't really understand what he's trying to say and you're like trying to write down whatever is on the board since he doesn't share the powerpoints

Ferguson rocks! I'm not into politics, but he made the class interesting and the grading criteria was clear. If you put some effort into the class, you can probably skip the final. The paper is easy as long as your follow the instructions, basically everyone gets an A on it but this is an enjoyable class!

Dr. Ferguson is awesome. Intro to American politics was super fun and super easy. Make sure you do the readings and come to class. Super funny and entertaining class. I recommend to all of my friends, even ones who aren't political science majors!

Ferguson is a great guy and you can tell he loves teaching. Make sure you go to class because he doesn't send out the lecture slides and a majority of the test comes from the lecture slides. Also make sure you read the articles and book before the test because he puts stuff from those on there too. Would definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is an incredible human and I have never met someone so happy to teach. His tests have very few questions so if you answer only a few wrong you get a bad grade. Only one paper.

Great guy. he is really funny and his lectures are fun for the most part. there is a lot of extra credit to earn. test aren't easy but they are definitely  doable. I have taken two classes with him and hope to take a third

Dr. Ferguson is one of the nicest professors I know he will literally go out of his way to help a student. The only downside is his tests are oddly worded and many people complained about it so I imagine he will do his best to fix that knowing him. Take him he's passionate and cares greatly. (Campaign and Elections)
Ferg is a great teacher who cares about the well being of his students! I would recommend taking from him. Tests are very difficult and require a lot of detailed studying.
Always willing to answer questions in class. Gives several opportunities for extra credit. His tests definitely cover the material in class and in the textbook.

Dr. Ferguson is a really nice guy. American Politics with him was a blast and you can really tell he has a passion for politics. Lots of reading, but tests are fairly simple with questions coming from lecture and the readings.
Awesome guy that is very nice. More than willing to help with any questions you have and you can easily make an A if you study the lecture notes and the assigned readings.

He is a very nice man but it not very helpful when telling you what to study. It is essential to do the readings outside of class for the exams. 30-40% of the exam is based on the readings. He will take very specific details from lecturesreadings and use those as questions on the exam. Hard A, Moderate B, Not hard C, Easy D.

You don't have to go to class, but there are questions on the test that you'll only get if you do. There are only 3 tests and a final, but they are HARD and about 25 questions each. It is a lot of material, and you have to study all of it and READ THE READINGS. Readings are made into a few very specific test questions. Offers in class extra credit
Great professor and easy A if you do your work. I took the 3-hour night class, and the lectures took up the entire time most classes. Great class and would recommend.

Prof. Gray is a great professor. His lectures can drag on a bit, but he'll make sure to let you know what's important to know. Not really about him, but the class itself is pretty much a semester-long group project, and you'd better pray you get half decent teammates. Test aren't bad at all if you pay attention.

Gray is the best BIS professor! He makes the class super managable and is willing to work with you. Weekly discussion posts, 3 exams, and semester long group project. The exams are an easy A if you study a little and he is super helpful if you need it. Also a little lecture heavy but it's worth it. Take him!!!
Terry the goat

Best BIS professor you could get. However, it is a night class and he does not let out early actually ever. He lectures most of the time, but if you actually listen he explains the concepts really well and makes it semi interesting. He is very laid back. His exams are not super easy but not bad, I always got an A but had to study. He is great

I have heard bad things about this class, but Gray made it as straightforward as possible. His class is lecture-heavy, but super manageable as long as you take notes and study a little for his tests. There is a semester-long group project, but he is super helpful and accommodating. Overall, would recommend!
I felt that his lectures were really hard to follow which isn't great for a lecture based class. Class is only based on the group you have so I wouldn't recommend taking this class.

You spend the whole semester in a group. Class is a little boring really lecture heavy especially late at night. You do SQL which he is very helpful on. Class isn't bad or too difficult, unless you get a bad group.
He is the goat. rounded my grade up, helped me so much with sql. however the tests can be somewhat difficult.

Though I would give a worse review of Terry Gray, the fact is that there are no good BIS professors at TCU. I was enrolled in his Monday night class. His lectures were very boring and full of rambling, always lasting at least two hours and sometimes the full two hours and thirty minutes. His grading relies heavily on exams, with one final project.

TAKE HIM! I have heard horror stories of other BIS professors, but Professor Gray makes this class simple. Study the slides for the exams and you'll be fine. Mini presentation and final presentation are easy. Only downfall is the long lectures, but it's def worth it to take him. I was able to learn a lot in this class without it being difficult.

Awesome guy who made a class I was dreading enjoyable. For the project, I had a group from Hell. Terry was very accommodating and tried to get me on another team before allowing me to complete it on my own. Taught SQL extremely well and provided practice problems & solutions. Consistent class schedule and a fair grader. Happy to have had him!

Best professor for this class. Dark sense of humor, down to earth. 
Saved my dog from a burning building. 
Rescued my grandmother from drowning.
Saved my uncle from the mafia.
Got my brother out of a hostage situation.
Convinced my parents not to put me up for adoption, but most importantly taught me how to use SQL. You will learn best from him.

Lectures are pretty excruciating - most read off slides. That being said, Gray is a nice & reasonable guy. Usually get out of class 30 min early. Make sure you get a good group for the project. Probably the best BIS professor.

Gray is great for BIS. While lectures can get a bit long at times, it is just the nature for a 3-hour lecture. Homework is an easy 100, and exams are very easy. The final project is graded slightly harder but will not be impossible. Very funny and relatable guy, knows what he is talking about and is a great choice for BIS.
Good BIS professor. Nice guy, classes can get boring when lectures are long. Big semester-long group project which is the meat of the class. 3 tests, the last one is just SQL.

Such a great teacher, grades homework 100% every time, and everyone got 100% on their mini-presentations. Tests are very easy if you take notes during lecture. Night class is a little dull because he and the students are both tired, but he cares a lot about his students.

Best professor for this class!! Tests are overall pretty easy if you study. Graded by 3 tests and a group project. The last test is SQL and was really easy - most got 100s. Group project is kind of long but it is split up throughout the semester and he grades it easy. Exams are straight from the PowerPoints. Take him over any professor!!!!
Take him for your BIS class. Such an understanding guy. He tries to give good grades to the students as much as possible.
He is such a fun guy, i really like him. His lectures are very heavy and his exams are not open notes anymore and not easy. If you study you will do well. I would take him again.

There are no better options for BIS than Terry Gray himself! He is very easygoing and understands students very well. His lectures are boring as he speaks in a monotone, but it's all good because he makes the class way easier than it should be. 3 easy exams, group project, and Microsoft Teams stuff.
Take him!! Potentially I should be getting an A in this class, the exams are easy from lecture slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The other reviews pretty much covered everything but I will just add some more. Despite his lectures being boring, exams are pretty easy and focused much on the slides and weekly homework discussion posts. There's a semester long group project and communicate with your teammates! Use Writing Center and PDC to prepare for the group assignments.

Long, boring lectures, but he cares a lot about his students and considers us as his friends. Very accommodating, I had a big personal event happen 2 days before an exam and he gave me an extension to take it whenever I wanted. Group project throughout the semester but the rubric is "suggested," so he just gives an A if he thinks it's good. Easy A

Great professor! He only teaches night class which is never fun anyways, but taking his class is worth it. I really came around at the end of the semester and started to enjoy BIS because he is so nice and cares about his students. It was graded based on 3 exams and a group project, but he gives you very clear expectations so you can do very well.

He is a boring lecturer. Does not give feedback at all. Even if he was a good teacher this would be a boring subject but he is terrible at telling you information that is essential in the course. Would not take again with him. Every student is confused about what he wants for projects.

I love Terry Gray but his lectures are kinda boring. He's pretty clear about grading and what to expect before class, but it isn't enjoyable going to his night classes at all. I think he is the best option for BIS though.
Terry Gray is awesome. He really cares about his students and you will do well if you study. We had 3 exams and we had a group project that was almost half of our grade. Would take again

Prof Gray is by far the best BIS prof at TCU. Although his lectures are somewhat boring, he is one of the most caring professors I have ever met. He truly does make the BIS class tolerable, as the BIS curriculum in Neeley is one of the hardest. One thing you will have to do is teach yourself SQL as it is not really taught and it's 1 of your exams.

He' a good guy, the tests are pretty straight forward. However, sometimes his instructions for the semester long project can be really confusing. If you study for the test you'll get at least a B+. He is pretty fair and easy going. He cares about his students a lot.

Prof Gray is a solid choice (he only teaches night class tho) class is fairly easy with 3 exams (straight from PPT/lecture notes) and discussions every week. If you are just familiar with the material you should get an A. The project, however, needed a lot more explaining. Really struggled towards the end with this. Def take him over other profs

I took Professor Gray in Spring 2021. I have to say that he has been my favorite professor at TCU so far. The class is absolutely manageable and if you participate and do your assignments, you will pass his class no problem. Professor Gray is my favorite professor because of how caring he is! He responds to emails fast and is genuinely a great guy!
BIS is a hard class at TCU but Terry is a laid back guy and fair grader. His lectures can sometimes be boring but he makes the class easy to understand so students can succeed. I would recommend.

I took Prof Gray's BIS class. This class involves one major group project no matter who you take. Aside from that project, most of your grade is from the online "Learn Smart" quizzes and exams, not lectures. Prof Gray does well in leading you through your assignments and preparing you on how to study for the exam. Nice guy, can be funny.

Dr. Greensword is a great professor who genuinely cares about her students. People that have had issues with her must just not want to be in college. As long as you take very basic notes or do some of the hundreds of extra credit opportunities you'll be given, you should CRUISE to an A. It's a good time being in her class and it's not that hard.

Dr. Greensword is amazing; you should take her if you get the chance. Such a fun and generous professor. I took Black Panther: Culture, Literature, and Adaptations, and even though the concepts are not always easy, we learned them in a super accessible way. Additionally, there is so much extra credit that the in-class grades can be minimized.
She's very straight forward and offers many extra credit opportunities. Her lectures are very interesting and she makes the class super fun. It's basically impossible to fail the class
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Truly the easiest class you will ever take as TCU. She offers so much extra credit that you can basically fail a bunch (like the quizzes because they are difficult for no reason) and still get a high A. There's a lot of papers to do, but they aren't that bad at all. She is somewhat of a tough grader until you figure out what she wants. Easy A!

Everybody that has any problem with this class is just lazy. Show up and take OCCASIONAL notes, and do some extra credit. It's a pretty easy A if you aren't completely ignoring the class. She's not good at telling people when things are due, but she genuinely cares and her class is not that hard.

If you get anything below an A, you should not be in school. So much extra credit its impossible to fail unless you dont submit things. Response papers: you do 4. Do the FIRST 4 offered = forget abt it for rest of sem. Makes life easier. Quizzes? so difficult for no reason, you will always do bad, don't fret. Just summarize readings on Chat.

I really enjoyed Professor Greensword; she is very nice and truly cares about what she teaches. The deadlines for assignments do tend to change. She is accessible outside of class and is very understanding. She is willing to accept late work, but some points will be deducted. There is lots of extra credit.

attendance not mandatory but have to be in class to get notes. so many readings, didn't do any of them was fine. took her hunger games class, LIBERAL you'll study gender roles and racism. hated doing her random in class group assignments. disorganized and hard to find stuff on d2l
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment:
Literally you could have earned like a 150% in this class given all the bonus
at first, it did seem like she was harsh with grading
She was very inspiring and fun. Absolutely Loved when she would randomly drop a smart joke
Professor really feels like a 4.5, but closer to a 5
I would SO take her again. Liked her more as semester went along
She's super nice and you get SO many opportunities for extra credit you have to go to lecture everyclass to get the information but most of the time class is half movie and half lecture

Dr. Greensword is super chill. Attendance is technically mandatory, but one kid in our class missed 2/3 of our classes and still got an A-. There are 30+ extra credit opportunities, so getting an A is super easy. Only 2 things that were negative, she is pretty disorganized with her assignments and she is very liberal (she doesn't push it too hard).

I love Dr. Greensword! I have taken her both semesters and have an A in both classes. Her quizzes are very hard, and you have to write 4 papers over the semester. However, if you do badly on that, she offers like 30 different extra credit opportunities. She can be a little iffy with timelines, but it works in the end.

I took this class when it was based on the Hunger Games books/movies. I don't think the teacher is a hard grader as long as you know what she is looking for, but she will try to push you out of your comfort zone by talking about topics like ecofeminism, racism, family/gender roles.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She gives over 30 extra credit opportunities but she is a really hard grader. I had to attend a lot of extra credit to keep an A in what I thought was going to be a super easy class. Im not the biggest fan of the way that she teaches because she has a weird way of organization. The due dates were never really reminded which I was not a fan of.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's is the best! She gave over 20 extra credit opportunities. Also, we were able to go on a fully funded dinner and trip to the symphony!! Really cares about students and facilitates a welcoming and fun classroom environment. Her class content, vocab words, and projects WILL be useful to any major! Trust me don't miss this unique opportunity!

I've taken both Africa through Film and the Black Panther class with her. She is an amazing professor that gives so many extra credit opportunities. She is very kind and generous when it comes to grading and is a good person. I don't understand why people don't like her, it is so easy do well in this class because of how much extra credit is given.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took the Black Panther version of this class. The teacher does not always give due dates in advance because she believes this method is in the best interest of the students. It was also not always clear what the contents of the quizzes would be. The final project is a lot of work but gets graded very quickly. It's possible to do well, but tricky.

She is very caring and wants to help, so do not be afraid to go to office hours. Assignments are manageable, and she provides so many extra credit opportunities. If you need strict structure and directions, take another teacher because she gives students a lot of leeway on papers and changes due dates a fair amount.
Please take another class if you appreciate your sanity. She is so disorganized and is unclear with her grading. I wish I dropped this class every day.

It's not that she's a bad person, she's actually really nice, but she doesn't post notes or have clear grading criteria, most papers are due 2 days after they're assigned, and other deadlines/tests seem to appear whenever she decides. You have to pay attention to deadlines because they could change at anytime/do not follow a strict schedule.

She doesn't have a very organized structure for the class, so be aware of random deadlines that pop up. There are a lot of response papers, and it takes some time to get used to her VERY specific grading. Once you get the hang of it, though, the class gets easier. She is sweet and you can tell she wants you to learn, but she can be sporadic.

The best way I could describe this class is just unnecessarily difficult. The content itself isn't that hard but the quizzes are meant to trick you, I study for them a lot and usually get B's. If you do extra credit you can get an A, but it is overall a class that is just a lot of work. Attendance isn't mandatory, but nothing is posted on D2L.

If you are not interested in Black Panther or Marvel, do not take this class. Assignments, due dates, and quiz/test dates are not posted online. Even if you attend class, read assigned homework, and study, the quizzes are very difficult, and the questions have tricky/unclear wording. She is a hard grader and is unclear about the grading criteria.

Grades very tough. There are response papers, quizzes, presentations, readings, and other assignments that absolutely tank your grade. Extra credit is helpful but also super time consuming. This class was my worst grade at TCU thus far. The final project is terrible and time consuming when I have other classes for my major that I need to focus on.

Greensword's my least favorite Honors Professor, she overcomplicates the class. She rarely uses D2L(not posting slides or deadlines). Left guessing when things are due. Most grades are "response papers" to readings where you must use 6-10 key words from slides(that aren't posted). She doesn't respond to emails at all. I would not recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is the worst class ever. You need to write 4 response papers throughout the semester using 6-10 key words on slides that she doesn't post on D2L. For your final, you have to connect Black Panther to your major and write a 6-page essay along with a physical presentation, which is completely unrealistic. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was impossible. She is so unclear and does not explain any of the assignments. The slides that she shows in class are not given to you and you must use her "key words" on all response papers. But she refuses to give out the slides after class or on d2l. I would not take this class because you will be confused the entire semester.

This class is the worst class I have taken. She will purposely try and trick you on quizzes. Also, puts all the "keywords" on a PowerPoint and won't share it with her students. If you are sick/have accommodations, she won't care and will not share the PowerPoint.

The class has two exams, a midterm and a comprehensive final which he gave study guides for. Also has a problem set due every other week (45% of the grade). For attendance he has you do problems in class but they're graded on participation. It wasn't a difficult class as long as you pay attention and take notes. Very lecture heavy, but chill guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: There are a lot of equations that aren't complicated, but you would think they were in a different language the way he explains them. He does not know how to explain things simply. He is not helpful during office hours because he can never just give you a simple answer.
I don't even know what to say. Just avoid this class and this professor. He has two test the whole semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He lectures the whole time and he talks so fast you can't even take notes. I had to take this class for one of my credits and I had to withdrawal. I went to his office hours and spent so much time trying to study his notes. He explains everything so bad and talks so fast. I can't even understand him. Very awkward guy too. No help outside of class.

I have seen and heard that Gordeev isn't a great professor, but I would disagree. Macro isn't the easiest class to begin with, and Gordeev doesn't have the best lectures. But if you do the homework and then review it for the tests, you'll do just fine. The tests are pretty simple, and luckily, the final is easier than the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is one of the worst professors at TCU. He is not helpful and is tough with grading. No professor is as cruel as him. Avoid him at all costs

There are no readings and there is HW every other week, midterm and final are the only exams, so the workload is manageable. He lectures so fast and overcomplicates everything he teaches, he won't explain anything in a way that is simple and logical, even when the content is actually not that hard. He also does not stop to let people ask questions.

He's a nice guy, but his lectures are incredibly boring and way overcomplicated. There's an optional textbook that I feel taught me better than he did. He's a generous grader, but if I could go back I would not choose to take him again, because I feel like I learned nothing that wasn't self-taught or remnants from AP Macro in high school.
He just talked at us. We only had 2 exams before the final. Hw every other week. The way he phrased his hw and tests was impossible to follow. Good guy. Not the best professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I will say intermediate macro is not an easy class and his lectures are the most boring thing ever he goes way too much in to depth when the homework and exams are so much more simplified, which i will say is nice but they are still difficult . The class consist of 6 home works a mid term and final. He is also a light grader which is nice.
worst teacher ever dont take
You have 2 tests and only a few homeowners but they are your entire grade. He was not good at teaching this class I had to learn everything myself and I was still lost.

Poor teaching style stay away from Gordeev lacks the ability to teach the information on a base level of understanding does not slow down to check if class understands topics and gives horrible lecture notes

He is very passionate about what he does and explains stuff in class clearly. There are 4 tests that I think were pretty difficult, and I studied a lot. The tests are comprised of 10 MCQs and 3 "problems and explanations" questions. There isn't any homework but I would suggest reviewing after every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring at times but he is really passionate about what hes teaching. Goes off of what students are saying and tries to adapt to make the class easier for us. Exams are easy if you pay attention and study a bit out of class.
Makes learning very fun and wants all his students to succeed.

I have taken 2 of Robs classes, and I love anything he teaches. He makes every class fun to attend even if the subject is a bit boring. The test are relatively easy, just make sure you attend every class. If you need any Econ electives make sure to take any of his classes if they are available!

Dr. Garnett is a very kind instructor, albeit he is a little all over the place sometimes. History of economic thought is centered around reading. You have to read the material for every class and you will get by fine. The class is not very exciting though, and it can be very repetitive.

Garnett is an amazing professor. He really cares about his students and makes it fun to be in class and learn about relevant topics. I couldn't recommend Garnett enough. If you are majoring in Econ, you need to take him!

Prof Garnett is the best! He's very invested in making sure his students succeed. His Contending Econ class was so interesting. There's a decent amount of reading and in class quizzes basically every day, but as long as you actually read and listen in class, you'll do great. I actually feel like I learned something in this class that I'll remember.
Dr. Garnett is the absolute best! TAKE HIM! Show up to class, listen/engage, and the class is a breeze.

History of Economics is an interesting class overall and not over the top difficult. The class feels more like a combination of poli sci/econ so if you're into both you'll love this class. Although there is an in class quiz every day, it's really more of a participation point than anything that helps reduce the importance of the few tests.

Professor Garnett makes this class engaging and manageable. Readings are interesting, not just textbook material. Use Unstuck ai and stay on top of work - you'll do great with this fair, helpful prof.

He's literally my favorite professor I've had so far. He's so nice and so caring and is just overall amazing. As long as you read and go to class you will do well. He makes the concepts so clear and doesn't try to trick you on exams and quizzes. He puts so much effort into this class and it's clear. I love him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Great prof at TCU. Easy reads compared to other profs. Try not to miss lecture! If you do, he's very understanding and willing to help out students.

Dr. Garnett is one of my favorite professors at TCU. His Cont. Perspectives class is very engaging. He wants all of his students to succeed, and he chooses interesting articles and chapters to read in class. He is very approachable and happy to discuss topics outside of the class.  He is very passionate about what he teaches and makes class fun.

TAKE HIM!! Especially for Cont. Pres, such a great professor. If you put in the work, you will truly enjoy the class, and reap the benefits. Daily quizzes, but very doable if you do the reading. Highly recommended.

Contending Perspectives has been one of my favorite classes at TCU. Dr. Garnett is a fantastic professor who keeps the class both interesting and engaging, and he makes himself readily available to students for any questions or struggles they have. The class is very manageable if you keep up with the reading. Would definitely recommend.
Dr. Garnett is my favorite Econimcs Professor at TCU. He is so helpful and actually emails you back (in a reasonable amount of time)! Very clear lectures and manageable work load.

Dr. Garnett is one of the best professors at TCU. I have never had a teacher put forth so much effort on behalf of their students.  He continually goes out of his way to help students succeed. He even allowed us to design our final paper so that we could apply our economic learning to something we actually cared about. Will take again if possible.

Class time is super involved. One of those classes where you won't be bored. Dr. Garnett is super cool and keeps class interesting. As long as you keep up with the readings which are actually interesting, not just taken out of some textbook, you'll do great. I recommend to anyone.

Best Econ class I've taken at TCU. Dr. G's lectures are interesting and easy to understand. The class was very organized. Only homework were typically short readings, and there were no surprises on the tests. Dr. G is a very fair grader and very helpful outside of the classroom. I strongly recommend taking any Econ class with Dr. Garnett.

Dr. Garnett is a very intelligent and thoughtful professor. He clearly cares about the quality of his classes and works to keep students engaged.
