reviews.comment: He's a good guy, but he is an extremely hard grader, tests require hours upon hours of studying to do well, and he is very, very unclear about deadlines and what is expected for assignments, for which he has no grace for mistakes. Most of the material for tests is solely talked about in discussions during lectures, so missing class screws you up.

Great guy, just very unorganized. Extremely detailed lectures. Different documents and handouts scattered throughout his D2L and weekly emails. If you are enrolled for this class, Chat is enough to help you speed through the readings and I recommend keeping track of all the notes/handouts on your own separately. Also use his preview guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't get me wrong, this is a HARD class over the Bible, but if you're willing to put in the work by reading, studying for at least 5 hours for exams, and participating in this class, it IS possible to get a good grade. He grades harshly and exams are all based on lectures, but he pushes you to be a better student and Christian knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy. Lectures are insane, never know the difference between important material and rants. Got an A but spent excessive office hours time with him. Lost half the class in the first few weeks. Mandatory reading quizzes on lockdown. Be prepared to work just for a passing grade. Impossible to please on writing assignments. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is not a great professor to take if you have a busy semester. The class is not impossible to do well in, but a very heavy time (much more than the typical 2 hours per credit hour) commitment is needed to get an A. Assignments are vague but not graded too harshly. There is a LOT of reading for this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't know who these people who rated Dr. Miles a 4.0 are, but they are wrong. Dr. Miles is very uninteresting to listen to, which is bad because he lectures for the whole class every day. His tests are unpassable. You can study for hours, know all the information on the study guide and still get a bad score. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Study guides for every exam with everything you need to know. Keeps the lectures engaging and is someone I respect. As long as you are present in class (need to be, can only have a handful of absences) you will be fine. Couple of assignments that he didn't give much heads up about but as long as you are responsible you'll be just fine. Great guy!

Great person and gives very informative lectures. No late work, takes attendance, the way he grades may baffle you at times, gives vague instructions for assignments: he expects the best interpretation from you. Exams aren't that hard, but I would advise to take note of EVERYTHING he says; his "tangents" are often actually exam-worthy material!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He was a caring professor. However, I feel like he expects a lot from his students. He provides study guides for the exam, but you could fail his class even if you study for hours. He assigns short readings each class period, but in order to do well in his class you need to take thorough lecture notes. He offers extra credit. He takes attendance.

This professor does not let you know why you made specific grades on tests. The tests are long, but I will say that the study guides go hand in hand with the test. The teacher is understanding if you communicate with him, but that does not mean he will help you with your concern.

I usually give the benefit of the doubt but Prof. Miles created a very uncomfortable atmosphere in class and was often extremely condescending. He was unclear with his explanations especially with his rubrics, and I really did not appreciate his lack of transparency and accessibility (he works as an adjunct/part time). TAKE ANOTHER PROF!!!

Do not listen to the other reviews on here! I am typically a good student, but taking this class was the hardest thing I have ever done. Miles was extremely impartial and assignments were not clear (especially finding them). Take another 8 AM to spare your time, or just do not take it at TCU. Definitely a waste of my time and money!
Very unclear when giving criteria for assignments. Feels like he is out to get you and doesn't want you to do well. Do not take. Take another teacher at 8am if you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this professor. I ended up having to pass/no credit his class and still stressed about passing. He grades extremely unfairly and doesn't care about his students. The tests are very hard so doing the study guide is a must and take good notes during class.

DO. NOT. TAKE. Extremely unreasonable grader. Gives unclear instructions regarding assignments and projects. Despite studying for hours you can still bomb his tests. Unwilling to work with students. Is not understanding. Sometimes made rude comments. If not taking his class means taking a Friday 8am take the 8am. It's the lesser of the two evils:)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Miles is a great professor. He is one of the few professors that go out of their way to get to know you. His class definitely is not the easiest ESPECIALLY if you are not somewhat familiar with the Bible, but it is manageable. Lecture Heavy! Attendance and staying on top of the assigned readings is the key to success.

Really nice guy and genuinely cares about his students, but that won't help you in the class at all. Defiantly go meet with him outside of class and ask how he thinks you should study to do well. Super difficult class but good extra credit opportunities. Even if you prepare and study a lot, you will probably still fail the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Literally the worst class I've ever taken. I really didn't expect religion to be this hard. Don't think that this class will be easier bc you've been a Christian your whole life. Tough grader for no reason and just don't take this class. Take a religion class at a community college or something. TCC sounds like a good option. Take my word for it.

If you can come to class, take notes and listen, you will be perfectly fine. He tries to be a funny guy and actually cares. He gives quite a bit of extra credit which is nice. He gives exam reviews and if you take notes in class they are easy to fill out and once you know the review, the tests are a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible. No compassion towards students at all. Tests are extremely difficult. You can study for hours and still fail. Extremely boring lectures. Just terrible.

This was the worst class I have ever taken. I have never gotten a C in my life, but this class changed that. I worked really hard and even went in to ask for help. He was not nice and did not care about my grade. I didn't know a religion class could be this hard but trust me, any other religion class is better than this one.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Miles is a fun guy but this class is very hard especially for an intro class. He is lecture heavy and talks really fast and it is hard to keep up with him. The tests are very difficult and are nothing like the study guide he gives out before the tests. Tests also make up of 65% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I honestly wouldn't recommend Dr. Miles. His lectures go by fast and my classmates & I were always lost. He assigns various work and projects and would often never tell the class about it. He isn't clear about assignments either. His tests are difficult, even if you study the study guide. I've never done so bad in a religion class until now.

The class is lecture heavy and he moves entirely too fast when speaking. When questions were asked in class he would get an attitude with students as if it was a problem. Also directions on assignments are very unclear and when asked he acts as if he doesn't know about it. He also assigned a group project and was not going to tell my class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Whatever you do don't take Johnny Miles. I don't care if you have to take a night class or an 8 am to get out of taking him, trust me on this one. He is disrespectful and makes rude comments to his students during office hours and before class starts. He is a tricky test taker and does not care about students grades. Overall, not a good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take this class or Prof under any circumstances!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I was not expecting this class to have so many pointless assignments. A religious site visit is required. There are online quizzes about once a week. Everything that is on the test is from what he says during lecture. The study guides are SO long and not the most helpful. I would definitely recommend taking a different religion. Used my pass/fail

He is willing to help and wants you to pass his class. He does not assign a lot of homework and the reading you do need to do is really just from the Bible because you have a quizzes or focus questions. However, if you read both of these assignments are easy. The study guides are very helpful and a really good indication of what is on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Miles is awesome. His class is easy and he really cares about his students. If you have a basic understanding of the Bible, you'll do fine. If not, I would suggest taking another course. Class is confusing sometimes but his tests are easy and the material you learn is very interesting.

Dr. Miles is a great guy, he is funny and caring but I really did not enjoy his Bible class. I found it really difficult and all he does is just talk in class so it is hard to pay attention. I found the material really boring and not what expected the Bible class to be like. I wouldn't recommend taking this class, take another type of Religion!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He can sometimes be hard to understand with his accent and his feedback during homework or in class work isn't the best, but you can tell he enjoys teaching this class. It is test heavy, they are every 3-4 week and theres a decent amount of homework and other assignments that you do in class.

Dr. Ryu is probably the least approachable teacher I have had at TCU so far. My friend had excuses sent from the dean to him, and he still did not excuse her. If you have questions, he is not a great asset to ask. He does not like re explaining himself. 
The lectures are very long and I do not feel like I learned much in this class at all.
He's not very easy to understand because he doesn't speak English very well but he's an easy grader. Just go to class, do the assignments, and study for exams - which are not very hard at all.

He is really hard to understand since he has such a thick accent. He gets frustrated very easily when students ask a lot of questions. he lets you use whatever you want, except asking friends, when taking skill assessments. It is a really easy class, just not the best prof.

He is a good teacher. Yes there is a bit of a language barrier and he is teaching graphic design which he even admits to not knowing much about.. But he was assigned the class which is not his fault. He does the best with what he was given and I came in with no prior design knowledge and got a 100. Just go to class, and ask him for help. EASY A

Dr. Ryu is really hard to understand. He's really smart but he doesn't explain things very well for students so be ready to read the textbook a lot to figure out what's going on. His power points are pretty helpful. If you go to class, take notes and read the textbook you should be find. Tests are pretty hard and you can't cram the night before.

He Literally does not even speak english.. and his instructions have errors that he takes points off from your projects because of.. don't listen to him at all he barely knows what he is doing and makes you relearn what he makes you learn outside of class.  Got a A- because he took off 20 pnts for something tiny on my final project, class is a joke
He's very hard to understand but gives you a sheet with instructions so if you follow them it's an easy A. There is really no use for him in the class at all, I didn't listen to him once.

Hard to understand him so his instructions can be confusing sometimes. He uses a website to teach so it's basically all online. Only makes you go to class once a week, but it is mandatory to pass the class. He gives in-class tests and assignments then.  Its basically a "teach yourself" class so put in the effort.  An A isn't hard to get if you try.

Very amazing lecturer, I would take this course again just to sit in on his teaching. He obviously cares greatly about Astronomy and is also well versed in all aspects of it. He gets carried away in very interesting tangents that, while not necessary for the course, are very fun to listen to. A lot of info to memorize but just put in a good effort
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: his class is very memorization heavy, which works for some and is terrible for others. for me, this was one of the easier classes this semester and I really didn't put too much work into it beyond what is required to pass. as long as you do the hw and study a bit before the tests, I feel like it's really not too hard to pass. can be a tough grader
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: expects you to come to class reading the material and ATTEMPTING problems before. would have gotten a much higher grade by doing all the homework and practicing. you have to be on it, but with 6 exams (10% each) before the final you have so many chances to improve. plus everyone gets almost all 200 points from lab  (huge boost)

He seems to think that his class is the most important class that every student he teaches has on their schedule. He will assign you 3+ hours of reading a week; he doesn't teach concepts in class, he goes over study guide questions based on a 60-question module that you are expected to do on your own. This process restarts every 2 weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests were easy if you study and do your homework. He's super nice and will help you with your homework.

His class was set up to where we had 5 modules and each module we would take a test. However, each module there would be about 60 questions that we would have to learn and memorize. Only 8 would be on the exam. I also went to his officers hours one time to talk to him and he completely shut me down and was not helpful. It's just to much to remember
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had him for lab and it was one of the easiest labs I have ever taken. There were plenty of makeup labs if you couldn't make it and I finished the class 3 weeks early because of the supplemental labs. He's smart and gives great help. The lab never takes the entire time.

While there were a few homework assignments, he always went over pretty much all questions in class and the homework is easily found in the readings or videos that he assigns. The homework is also the questions on the test, and if you actually do the reading it gives you a good study foundation and makes it easier to memorize for tests later.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's okay as a professor. Lectures can be boring and the class is straightforward, but problem is you have to put an egregious amount of memorization for an A. He claims that he doesn't grade strictly on exams but he does. I probably studied more for this class than my actual major classes. Every other astronomy professor is just way better anyway.

Prof. Ingram's class requires consistent effort, but the structure helps you succeed. Use the study guide and Unstuckstudy to prepare - it saved me time. Labs were fun, and he's willing to clarify any questions. Definitely take this class if you're up for the work.

The most fair professor there is. Tests are easy if you understand all of the practice problems from class, he pulls questions you have already see before. He is always willing to meet or answer questions over email if you need extra help. Only professor you should take for physics
If you have accommodations be ready to fight him to have him follow those accommodations. I have never been so disrespected by a professor. DO NOT TAKE!

This professor single-handedly gave me the worst advice of my college career, which will cost me THOUSANDS. If you are pre-med, BEWARE! I would not take this class with other prerequisites because he has quizzes every week and tests every other week.

Dr. Ingram is such a great professor for physics, he goes over concepts but mostly does problems in class which is so helpful. We have six exams with four questions each, but they're taken from worksheets and homework and you have access to previous exams and quizzes. He gives a lot of credit just for doing the work correctly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good Professor over all, test is hard but if you study the questions he post it is a easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class involved a lot of outside readings and videos in order to prepare for exams. Six exams with eight free response questions from the 60 provided every few weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Ingram shows how to solve specific problems in class when starting a chapter then goes over any questions people have in the class afterwards up until the quiz. Grading includes 6 exams and in my case 13 quizzes. He is accessible outside of class and is a funny professor. He may offer an extra credit opportunity.

The most frustrating thing about this class to me was how you could work for hours to memorize the 60 study guide questions only to get a low grade because you had memorized an incorrect answer. The classroom is flipped so you spend hours each week outside of class reading materials. I would not take this class, especially not for a core credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DONT TAKE THIS CLASS! he changed his way of teaching from the earlier reviews, he makes this intro science class so unnecessarily hard. had to P/NC it because it was so time consuming and difficult. The exams are any 8 of the 60 short answers that you have to find all the answers to outside of class and need to know all of them bc they r random.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ingram is a nice guy but just makes an intro class way too time-consuming. Unless you are good at memorizing 60 short answer questions for a test don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 5 tests, each unit you have 60 potential questions from the readings & lectures that could be on exam. Exam is 7-8 questions, so hope you get ones you remember. Some questions you can only check in class, others you can email and he will look them over. If you can memorize 60 multiple sentence and diagram answers per unit, you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you want to get a good grade you have to consistently go to class, but if you go to class getting a good grade is not too hard. He gives you a study guide of 35-40 questions for each module and 6 of those questions are the test - short answer. There are no surprises. You have to put in the work but he will go over any of the questions you have.

Dr. Ingram is a great teacher. He wants students to succeed, but you have to do the work, but if you do it, he will happily review it and guide you in the right direction. Although online learning can be a challenge, he adapted the course and made it a great one, definitely take him for core classes.
Dr Ingram is a great guy, he is easy to talk to and pretty funny. Labs were always enjoyable

Dr. Ingram actually works problems in class, which is how you learn physics. I wish I had him for physics 1 and physics 2 because physics 1 would not have been so horrible if he was my professor. Please take physics with him: he is very helpful and wants you to understand physics. Also, physics is not his favorite subject, but he will make it fun

He is, by far, one of the best professors that I have had at TCU! Has a clear grading scale, gives you the needed materials, and is always accessible. Lectures were engaging, and the material was excellent. Offers FUN supplemental labs including planetarium visits, sky tours outside at night, and a star party at lake Mineral Wells. Best class ever!

Professor Ingram always said how important it was to come to lecture despite not taking attendance, but every day it felt like we would cover 10 minutes worth of material and the rest was spent telling stories. Lab grade is easy and boosts your overall grade, lecture requires a lot of effort to do well. He always seems to be in a bad mood too.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FOR CORE. Youre only graded on 3 tests that have 8 questions but you are given study guides, however, they have over 60 questions on each study guide. In order to do well, you have to memorize the study guides and guess which ones will be on the exams. LOTS OF WORK and there are easier NSC courses to take instead.
Tests are over study guides that are given so you have the test in front of you before you go in. No curve balls. 3 tests, lab grade, that's it! Easy!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Ingram is a good professor. For some reason he seems annoyed most of the time, but he gives good lectures and is clear about what you need to study for his tests. He provides study guides he can check for you. Theres a lot of material in this class but its doable and is pretty interesting.

Doug rocks- I took Physics II with him. Definitely need to study outside of class and do all the videos and past tests to do well. He understands its a hard class and treats everyone with respect. Clear, concise lectures. DO NOT SKIP!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor, very funny. Only 3 tests, final, and lab grade (each 1/5). Study guides given for each test but you have to answer the questions and then get them checked, and he's very helpful with checking. Have to study these extensively as there is no extra credit. Lab is very very easy to ace.

Dr. Ingra is very knowledgeable and funny. He provides a study guide, update throughout the term, that lists the questions he could put on the test. He will look at your answers before the exams to verify correct answers. So, it is pretty easy to get an A as long as you attend class and have him check your answers to the study guide questions.

Dr. Ingram is a bit nerdy but in the best way! He has been one of my favorite professors so far and I wouldn't hesitate to take another class of his. Physics is tough material, but he does a really great job explaining it. He is so helpful outside of class - I've emailed him several times late at night and he always responds within an hour!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: the class is hard, It won't really matter how good you think you are, his exams are just way much harder than the rest of what the reviews here say. If you don't want to feel bad abt yourself then take another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Lot of work and memorization but Ingram is a good lecturer and cracks professor jokes that are funny.

Intro to Astronomy is not about stars!!!! It's a class about physics and chemistry!!! If you want a fun class I hear Archeo Astronomy or Astrology are the ones to take. At the end of the semester Ingram gives you 5 grades in your grade book: 3 tests, your lab, and your final. The tests are so dang hard so get ready to live in the library.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I don't like study guides, but there is no other choice for Dr Ingram to handle the class since it is huge (>70 students). Lectures are good, and he is passionate about the subject. Sometimes he can come across as aloof or condescending, but he is not here to please whiny lazy students, so that's ok to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He gives a lot of homework and a lot of materials to learn on your own, however if you don't know the material in the first place you'll find yourself trying to understand it on your own. His teaching skills are not that great and if you learn from others explaining to you, then DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER. Otherwise, take him
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a good professor. 3 tests and a final. Before each test, he gives you 50 questions you answer them, (and check them with him!!!) and he will ask 8 of those questions on the test. Make sure you get your questions checked by him, and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: TAKE HIM! He is the only professor in the department that can teach Physics, believe me. Lectures are inspiring and clear-cut. Tests are just modified version of the homework, though you really need to work to get the grade you want. Barely need textbook. Easy A. He even exempts you from finals if you have at least 96% expected grade.

Ingram is a gem. He is super passionate about astronomy and spends the first 20 min of class just talking about a constellation. If you show up and do the study guide each week it's an easy A. He'll check your work during office hours or by email to guarantee success.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Although he makes this class sound easy, it's not. He gives you a study guide of 50-60 questions and picks 8 for exams. Keep in mind that to get full credit on most questions you will need a detailed paragraph response and a well-labeled diagram. Way too much to ask students to know that for 50-60 questions and then chose only 8. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Ingram is very blunt about what you need to do to succeed in his class. If you put in a lot of effort you will do well. In my class, you can prepare for every short answer on the test ahead of time.

Dr. Ingram makes sure that you understand the material before the test. He also is pretty funny and makes the class go by pretty fast. If you need a science credit this is a course I would recommend. I knew nothing about the material going in and was still able to get an A with a little effort

Take this class if you need a science credit also doubles as GA. Overall the course was pretty easy if you show up and pay attention you will have no problem with this course. I took it in the spring but have heard the summer portion is easier.
Regardless of the course, Doug Ingram is the most rude and arrogant professor I have encountered at TCU. When I had questions, he would not help; his condescending attitude is sure to bring you down!

I went into this class expecting to hate it but actually found it to be a lot of fun. I thought professor ingram was a great teacher. If you show up and pay attention there is no reason you shouldnt get an A

Ingram is a great professor. Most of the bad reviews are pretty old and I think that may be the reason. I took him in the summer of 15 and was amazed at how fun the class was. While you will need to put in some work the class seems like a good GPA booster.

This class is not an easy A, but he provides a study guide and his tests are literally the same. The study guide is hard and time-consuming, but if you study it you will get an A in the class. Best part is there are a ton of extra credit labs so you don't actually have to go to the weekly labs. He is really nice and I would recommend this class!

Take thorough notes during the lecture, and do all of the studyguide. His exams are straight from the studyguide; literally just memorize it. He grades kind of hard, but get your studyguide checked with him beforehand and you'll be fine. Not an easy A, but if you do the work, you'll be fine. For honors, all you do is write an extra easy essay.
Made an A.  Doug kills off students with his grading. Stellar students were killed off due to his arrogant expectations in an introductory class. Shame on him. Garbage.

Doug needs work... His test are not that hard if you have good memory. It is his TOUGH SUBJECTIVE GRADING that takes you down. Shame on him. I would not take this class again. PERIOD. I made a B that took blood, sweat, and tears to reach. Take as a Pass/No Credit option or do not even bother. Still a nice guy though.

The tests are extremely tough. All test questions are essay/short answer responses that are detail oriented and very hard to memorize. I would never take this class again and if you do PASS/NO PASS the class. I made the mistake of not making it  P/NP and made a D in the class even though I went to every lecture.

Ingram speaks kind of fast, so if you miss something don't be afraid to ask because he's very willing to go over it again or slow down. It helps a lot that he makes study guide questions, and also you can get your answers checked by him. However, don't wait too late to study because each study guide has about an average of 50 questions.

Must do assignments before class to be able to answer the quiz questions.  Tests are kind of hard but is made up of assignment questions.  He always provides formulas so you can use your math skills to figure out the answers.

he is such a character. very funny for such a smart man and his lectures are not as boring as people say. the study guide is a pain though but at least you know exactly what's on the test. its hard to memorize them even if you look at them for a while so if you're not good at memorizing i wouldnt take this class. otherwise all good!

My favorite teacher! His arrogance is to fight off the ignorance of the people around him because he knows so much! Come to class preparing to have your mind blown because he simply knows so much! He teaches things plain and simple. He answers the  study guide questions at the beginning of class, I just fill in answers to the study guide as he goes

Ingram is awesome. If you keep up with the study guide, you'll do well. You always know what the questions on the test will be, because they're all straight from the study guide. It's a very intelligent way to let students know what's important to study, but it is  a lot of information if you're trying to cram at the last minute.
This class was a cluster. I consistently asked for help to no avail. His tests were such a mess. I studied for weeks and barely passed.
He skips around in lectures. MUST MEMORIZE the study guide to make a good grade. Most study guides are on quizlet

HARD CLASS. You have to put in the work.   No away around it. Each study guide he gives are at least 50 short answer questions. He is a nice man, but hard teacher. He is quick to take off points on test. You have to play by his rules. If you do then you will be ok. Check your study guide answers with him.  Do well on labs, it really helps ur grade

Don't take this class unless you can memorize 60-80 short answer study guide questions for an 8 question short answer test. Took this class thinking it would be easy and it took more time out of my day than any other class. I did the entire study guide and emailed in my answers and barely got a B.
WARNING: DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!!!!!

Dr. Ingram is one of the most unpleasant people I have ever encountered. He is a decent professor when it comes to knowdledge, but his personal intercommunication skills are TERRIBLE...at best. I have never experienced such rudness in my life and I would not wish it upon anyone else. Stay away from him if character matters to you.

For me, Dr. Ingram took some getting used to but by the end of the semester I liked his class. After you get the hang of it, his class is easy, you just have to keep up with the work. He talks really fast but you can always ask him questions through email or office hours. If you keep up w/ the study guide and check answers with him, you'll do fine.

Dr. Ingram is a great teacher. The reason why people struggle is because they dont pay attention in class. Its only 30 minutes of notes because the first 20 he spends going over constellations that you dont have to know. Gives you questions online that are on the test. As long as you take notes and do the readings and study guide Q's you'll do well
Hes awful. He is no help and not friendly. If you go to his office hours he barely explains. In class he flat out told a kid I don't want to review this question. I don't like him!

Dr. Ingram is a solid guy with a good knowledge of the material.  He dabbles a lot with both the textbook, his personal lectures, and online articles.  Be sure to email him about the exam questions, it is the only way to study.  You gotta try pretty hard to fail one of his exams, they are straightforward.  Final exam exemption with a 96 or higher!

The teacher is very good at explaining things to where you actuallyunderstand them. He uses visual aids and tells you excatly what will be on the Exams. If you learn, and dont just read, you will get a good grade on all the tests. My fav class I took this semester.

Dr. Ingram was not a helpful teacher to me at all! I did everything: came to class, took good notes, did the study guide questions, yet I still found his class difficult. The test is only 8 questions while the study guides are 40. If you do not answer with the wording he likes, he will take major points off! Disliked this class!

Dr. Ingram's archaeoastronomy course is incredibly easy if you just answer the study guide questions and check the answers with him. There is no reason anyone should ever get below a B in this course... Unless of course you just don't show up...

If you do the study guides you'll do fine on the tests. Some of the study guide questions are on lectures so go!! He's really helpful on answering any questions and you tell he really loves astronomy.

Wonderful professor. He's nice and slightly geeky, but in a charming way. He loves the material and makes you want to love it too. If you keep up with the study guide, it makes the exams a lot easier. Gives out exemptions for the final if you're pulling a high A (94 or higher). Takes attendance and will give you extra credit if you don't miss class

Yes he checks the study guides, but he adds 6-10 questions every class period! There all essay & it takes him close to a week to get back to you. The tests are only 12 questions from the study guide, so you do 70 questions to answer 12 on the test. And the tests are also short answer. Stay on top of the study guides! Pass/fail the class if you can!

Dr. Ingram was the best professor I had this semester. I highly recommend his class! It is not difficult if you keep up with the study guide and take advantage of the supplemental lab opportunities. He is extremely knowledgeable on the subject and sparked me to have further interest in astronomy. Overall very good because he loves to teach!!

I really struggled in this class, but I don't have a good head for science. I stayed on top of the workload, sent him all of my study guide questions, consistently went to class, and still made a 75 on the first test. He tries to be helpful, but his arrogance gets in the way.

I do not recommend Ingram if you plan on just wanting to know about the interesting facts of space and planets. He wants you to know about EVERYTHING before you even start that mid-semester. A lot of the work is on your own and while the labs are easy, the tests destroy some kids. They're 100% essay and he counts off for little mistakes. Good luck.

Great professor. Funny. Keeps you interested. Tests are very difficult though, so do everything you can to study or be prepared to fail. Lab will save or kill your grade, so go to lab. Your entire grade rests on 3 tests and lab grade. STUDY!

Good teacher with condescending tone and elitist attitude, good lectures, will help if you ask and will check your answers to reviews if you email them. If you do not prepare his tests will destroy you so be warned.

Holy crap this class was hard. I had to pass/fail it and then just stopped going. Don't take over the summer because I don't think it would have been nearly as hard if I would have taken it during a regular semester. 3 labs a week sucks!

Dr. Ingram is a really awesome teacher. He seems a little arrogant, but that's mostly because he has a huge amount of knowledge about astronomy. If you do the study guide, memorize the answers, and can duplicate them on the test then you will ace this class. Also, instead of going to his normal labs, do the supplemental ones. They're fairly fun.
So much easier than I anticipated!! I took his Intro to Astronomy. Fill out the study guide, send it to him. If it gets the ok, memorize the answers. I guarantee 100% in the class if you stick to it!

Difficult class but you learn so much.  Ingram is a genius and explains everything so well really cares about how his students perform.  Do the study guide as he covers the material in class and email him your answers for him to check and you should be fine.  Definitely recommend.

Doug is the man. He is a great teacher, is excited about what he teaches and is always willing to help students. I took the intro to astronomy class and learned a lot, even though I never have really understood any of that stuff before. Easy A if you go to class at least every other day and send him your study guide answers!
BEST TEACHER AT TCU

You have to go to class to do well, but he keeps it very interesting. The study guide he gives us is the test. Going to class helps you do the study guide and doing the study guide helps you on the test. Information is difficult and this is not a blow off class.

the class is hard only because of the amount of work, but he practically GIVES you all the answers in the beginning of class. he teaches by the study guide and repeats the answers at least twice. recording the lectures helps tremendously cuz you sometimes cant catch it all. the guy has an amazing nerd sense of humor making the class very enjoyable

Funny dude but hard class.  I was looking forward to learning about planets, but in the spring he teaches stellar astronomy.  The subject matter is hard and you have to go to class and take good notes.  I make pretty good grades, so Im not an idiot, and I failed the class.  The labs are miserable.  You have to do the study guides, which take foreve

This class was so hard. I studied more than I have for anything and I still never made above C on my tests. If your willing to make astronomy your life, go for it. Good teacher, but such a hard class.

Great great great professor. I got a C in the class and it was still one of my favorites to attend. He doesn't take role but attendance is pretty much mandatory if you want to pass. Every lecture is interesting and he's a pretty funny teacher. Would recommend to anyone looking to satisfy a science credit or just take a good class.

Best prof I had at TCU - hands down. Crystal clear - many demos to make things stick in your head. It's just interesting stuff. Its all about understanding why something happens - never will he ask you some ABCD/vocab question. If you want a relevant science class that is NOT just a blow off waste of time - take Ingram!

Great teacher, not hard to make an A. Buy a voice recorder, arrive on time to class, and he will give the answers to the previous day's study questions in the first 5 min. but record it cuz he talks fast.

IT IS ESSENTIAL TO DO THE STUDY GUIDES.  There are 40+ questions on the study guides but only 6 on each exam - if you blank out on one question you just failed. A boring lecturer but you have to come and take notes. Also if you're not into environmentalism you might not want to take this class because he spends several weeks talking about it.

Loved this class. LOVES Dr. INGRAM! DON'T BUY THE BOOK. All test info is given in the lecture. TAKE EXTENSIVE NOTES! He lets you email your study guide answers to make sure you have it right. All study guide questions are potential test questions so he's basically giving you the test in advance. STUDY and you can do well.

This class was not my favorite. I didn't feel like the things he taught were very interesting. I also though it was pretty hard. Be wiling to put a lot of work into the study guides. He gives you like 60 questions to answer and learn and then tests you on 6. Hes a really nice guy, and willing to check all your study guide questions.

DONT BUY THE BOOK.. all of the test questions come from lecture. he gives you study guides and the tests come straight from the study guide. If your willing to put in a few hours studying the study guide before the test its an easy A. By far my favorite class this semester and I'm a business major

prof ingram is really considerate when it comes to help in the class and extra credit. the labs are SUPER easy but you HAVE to attend class if you want to pass. the final is SUPER easy and the class is definitely an easy B but you really have to work and memorize the study guide if you want an A. I thought the class was pretty fun and interesting
Dr. Ingram is an awesom professor. lecutres are very interesting. give study guides after every class. rarely uses the book. if you keep up with your study guide which is easy, you will do very well

He is one of the best profs at TCU. Go to class, take notes, do the study guide and you'll be fine. The tests are exactly like the study guide. And you're required to do 10 labs which are so simple! He also gives plenty oppurtunities for extra credit and he is extremely helpful if you don't understand any of the material.

He's really funny and a good teacher. The only down side is that if you don't go to class every day, it's really easy to get lost. You also have to do the homework. Your entire grade is based on 10 tests, 10 homeworks and the lab. The lab TAs don't speak english well, so that makes it hard.

Dr. Ingram really tries to be reasonable in what he requires of students. His lectures were very clear and understandable, although some people might not like his emphasis on solving problems in class. It is very easy to study for tests, since he posts a lot of old exams and worked-out solutions online.

Pretty much just keep up with the study guide questions and email him your answers because he'll let you know whether they are correct or not. Then, you study those answers and you are golden for the exam. I personally thought the class was very easy and interesting!

Very boring class. He's a smart man, but doesn't really teach concepts and just shows the class lots of examples. I didn't really learn anything in his class. Gives lots of tests with no opportunity to make up bad grades. Gives different versions of test with increasing difficulty and picks who he gives each one to.

One of the best teachers I've ever had. I could rave all day. He explains things well, never thinks a question is stupid, and is always happy to help. If you go to class, pay attention, take notes, and do the homework (before he answers questions on it in class) you will do fine. A great guy through and through.

Wow, a great teacher, the most helpful i've ever had and even though the class wasnt mandatory it was still enjoyable most of the time.  I recomend you go to class as much as possible and do the study guide questions and you will do good.
loved this class!! go to class, take good notes and do the study guide (you can email your answers to him and he will check them).  the tests are ?s straight from the study guide.  hes awesome!

Show up for class, take good notes, do the study guide (and do not procrastinate in doing so), and check your work with him via e-mail. He tells you exactly what you need to do, and if you don't do it - you're in big trouble. He's a good teacher, loves what he does, and is respectful, but either be prepared to do the work or don't take the class.

Great teacher.  He tells you exactly what will be on the test with the study guides and really cares about his students.  He's always there for questions and help, especially through email.  He is always looking for recommendations to improve the course.  Highly recommended if you put in the effort to do the study guides!

Not sure if this is a new trend or a fluke, but gave our class nearly 200 study guide questions in the 5 week term, quite a few more than from his older study guides, summer session or not.  Nice guy though, highly intelligent and loves what he teaches.  Seems to be a sci-fi geek; he even mentioned dilithium crystals one day!
I worked hard and ended the semester with over a 100 average. I didn't have to take the final.

STUDY...do the study guides...I can't stress that enough.  Just pay attention in class, take good notes, and you'll do alright--he'll help you out if you need it...but don't fall behind.  I got a B just because I procrastinate and didn't do those study guides.  Otherwise, you're fine.

Nice man, interesting teacher, everyone says keep up with the study guide and you'll be good- but the SG is hard as hell. It's 6-8 questions per class and they all require intense research- at least an hour and a half a day of outside study. THis is a "non-science major" course but it sure wasn't treated like one.

Loved him!  This was one of my favorite classes in undergrad!  I liked him so much I took astronomy with him, just because he's so awesome!  He's probably the best teacher I had in all four years of undergrad and 2 of grad at TCU

Ingram is cool as hell, he gives you M&Ms for asking good questions, but his class is rediculously hard.  If you dont go to class you are screwed and you cant find the study questions in the book so dont take this class.

Loved this class and I'm not even a science person. Keep up with the study guide questions and submit them to him to check before tests and you will do great. You are required to complete 10 labs, do 7 consecutively and 3 supplementals and you'll be done with them before spring break. He really loves his subject and is a very dedicated teacher!

AMAZING teacher. Made the class enjoyable and clear. He tells you EXACTLY whats test material and what is not, and he doesnt waste your time with what is not test material. He DOES give you extra material if you are interested. Going into the lab I was teaching people basic things because they had the other Intro Astro teachers. E-mail to reach him

great prof.  material is really interesting.  he tells you exactly what will be on the test through the study guide questions.. which is great... but you do have to really study the study guide if you want a good grade... he loves what he teaches and knows a lot about it.  i loved the class and you really do learn a ton
He's a nice guy, but don't be fooled. His class is pretty tough but if you keep up with the study guides, you should be fine.

You really have to screw up to fail or get below a C or B. You can exempt your final exam and all he does is take off 6 points if you don't take it or at worst takes off 6 if you just bomb it. Go to every class and do the study guide and you should be fine. There is also almost no math involved and the little there is in lab is idiot proof.

This class was my favorite learning wise. he has a study guide that if you do the questions and submit them, he'll tell you if they are right, and they are the only questions allowed on the test. he's a science geek, but a nice one. GREAT TEACHER!!!
Hard tests but good professor
He is very fun and he loves to teach, he is also very clear on what he wants you to study for the tests. He makes the labs fun too. I highly recommend him.
Very passionate, loves to teach.  He's very clear about what he wants from you.  You have to go to class, but if you take notes you'll do well in the class.  A pain-free science credit.

I liked this class. It's tough but if you show up and do your stuff, you'll be fine. He's extremely clear on what he wants and his nerdy enough to make you smile and have a great time in class. A must take at TCU

The best professor i have had since i have been at TCU. Truly passionate about his teaching, cool, down to earth and interesting.  If you don't do well in your class then you are either not attending class, or not doing the reviews.  He literally personifies what every student wishes their professor would be like!  awesome, i definitely reccomend!!
Really cares about teaching. If you make the effort in the class he is very willing to help you out in anyway.  Best way to contact him is by email.
Not an easy class, but very clear lectures. He perfectly explains what he wants for the tests. And also if you get 96 as an average before the final - no final for you. That is cool though hard.
he is really fun! if you do the problems every class you will get an A, guaranteed. He gives the same questions on the exams.

4 star prof! Teaches things really well. You have to keep up with the study guide or you will get in a hole. If you keep up with the study guide, have him check it, and study it on a regular basis, you are garunteed an A.
Tougher class than I thought. If you do the study guide as you go and go to class everyday, you should be allright. Funny guy too.

Last semster i failed the first test but then got my act together and made A's on the rest and ended up placing out of the final. This semster I have an A.  Do the study guide, make note cards, and MEMORIZE them word for word.  He's a great guy and attempts to make astronomy super interesting.

He makes it so interesting! Hard, detailed test questions that you have to have memorized to get an A on the essay tests (which is every test, by the way). But I can't think of a better intro science class to take!

Very amazing smart person and professor. Class was VERY difficult, but he puts it in understanding terms. Cares about what you learn. Funny, cool, highly recommended. Always do the extra suggested problems, and you'll be ok on exams.

Very good teacher! All science classes seems to be hard, but he tells you eveything on the tests. Do the study guides, and HAVE HIM CHECK THEM and you're golden! Very understanding and cares about his kids

fascinating class, but if you're not a scientific thinker, you'll have a really hard time.  just because you do the study guide doesn't guarantee an A, like i heard. i had to really study hard, but he is very helpful by putting past exams as examples online. takes up a lot of outside class time...

Hes an awesome teacher! He makes hard concepts easy to understand & he's funny too. There is a study guide, but its not graded, and the test comes directly from it. Plus, you can email him the answers and he will tell you what concepts need work.  If you need a PSL, DEFINETELY TAKE THIS CLASS!

Ingram was really cool. He is down to earth and does not believe in making a student do pointless work. He explains things, that most find difficult, very clearly. As long as you complete the study guide and study moderately you are almost promised a "B," but if you put forth a little more effort--A

requires a ton of outside work for the study guides but if you do them and have him check them you'll be fine. explains stuff very well and is more than willing to help but if you can put in the extra hours then definitely dont take.

a science class, so its hard.  but he does his best to make it as easy as possible.  if you do the study guides, you're guarenteed 100%. the study guides are hard though, so its actually not an automatic A.
Great teacher... I am NOT a science person and he definitely explains things and keeps things clear and concise.  Great for a PSL credit that you are afraid to take!
he look good, nice hair
He is GREAT!!!
It's not as easy as you hear.  It requires significant amounts of work, and there is tons of material to study.  Slip up a bit and you will get that C you don't need.
cool class, learn some interesting things about our solar system.  do the study guides, all the questions on the tests are off them.  if you do the study guides smooth sailing

The best teacher and class i've had yet!! The class isn't the easiest i've had, but 100% worth your time.The labs are easy and it's a great class to take if you're an honors student because there are a few more easy assignments to cushion your grade!
Awesome Professor! He is extremely helpful and offers lots of extra credit to boost your grade.
He offers extra credit and wants students to get an A in lab. I was a few points short of an A and he rounded it up!

He is a great teacher!!!!! keep up with the study guide and you will be okay.  he doesn't trick you, if it's not on the guide it won't be on the test.  He was very enjoyable, my favorite prof yet!!!!!
Very hard class, but great teacher.  Its a lot of work for a freshman class but I loved it (the class not the work).

i probably should have gone to his office for help like he kept asking us to do.  tests are reasonable and he grades fairly.  when i had him he gave extra credit for going to tutoring.  show up on time!  he gives quizzes over the reading at the beginning.

BEST class I've had at TCU(And it's not even my major!) Got a D in the 1st exam for slackin off, but I worked harder and ended up with an A at the end. Ingram is the best damn teacher EVER, plus he's friggin hilarious!
Yeah, Ingram is a HARD teacher, but if you just keep up with the study guide, you can get a B.  Seriously, gotta keep up...slacking in his class will murder you.

Bill Gates, I mean, Ingram, is easy if you just. keep. up. with the Study Guide.  I kinda did, and I got a B, but not without some effort at answering more the day before the final.  I recommend the look-alike.
This is the worst class ever.  Unless you are majoring in Astronomy, DO NOT TAKE INGRAM. If you are he knows what hes talking about, but if your just looking for a science. Look elsewhere.
I Loved this class. You have to review and study for the tests but if you keep up with the study guide it really is not that difficult. This was by far my favorite class this semester.
I didn't think the class was too bad.  You can def. get an A.  You may have to actually sit down and study for the tests though...there's a thought.
No Comments

1st, i'm a "science person", so this class comes easy to me as far as learning goes, but if you dont study, you will fail. must go to class and keep up with the study guide (daily/weekly). my favorite teacher of all time in his teaching style.
The guy is really rude outside of class.  He is tougher than other astronomy teachers.
he is a really nice teacher but his tests are kind of hard but he is really really nice
His class is usually entertaining, between the stories and sarcastic comments it's always good for a laugh. He is also very willing to help you with any problem you might have!

Whoever gave Ingram a positive rating is crazy.  This guy is terrible.  Yeah he knows what he's talking about, but he makes it so confusing.  I studied so hard and could never get a good grade on the test.  DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!
Greatest professor in the world!  His Astronomy class is a blast.  Take it.
Dr. Ingram is one of my favorites that I had at TCU.  I had him for Physics and took him again for astronomy because I liked him so much!  He makes science fun and makes it understandable.

Always willing to help. Do the study guide and go to class and you'll do fine (don't buy the book, get it from a friend!). His tests take some studying but the guide helps a ton. The labs are pretty easy, and so is the honors supplement.

I am not a science person. Lectures are, at times, vague, and lacking in neccissary explanation. Although, do the study guide everyday and eamil it to him religiously and you will get through it. He means well, tests hard, attendance a must.
Go to class and do the study guide and you will do fine.  Dr. Ingram is one of my favorite teachers here.  He is funny, and makes a tough subject easy to understand and interesting.
teaches you to hate tests! Bookwork is good, quizzes fair but damn those tests are insane!!
I don't know what everyone else is talking about, Ingram was terrible.  After three hours a weak of his pompous whining, I was ready to drown myself in Frog Fountain.

I'm not great with science but I earned a B in this class without alot of effort.His career intention is to teach-he makes that obvious by his availability to his students.Know the study guide like the back of your hand and you'll get an A.

Knows what he's talking about and makes it clear... don't bother with reading the chapters, just answer study guide questions, which he lets you send through email so he can check them for you. Very willing to help -- study guide is essential!
Don't read book. Do study guide. Straightforward, but you've got to go to class.
Manages large class well, do the study guide.

Prof Ren's Zoom class was a walk in the park. Excellent at walking you through the test material. Drops lowest online quiz and HW grades. What I appreciate is she doesn't gatekeep her PowerPoints; she'll post them along with how to calculate answers and/or what formula to use. Attendance isn't graded whatsoever. We didn't even meet half the time.

I took the Maymester with her, and it was definitely worth it; the workload was very manageable, and I would highly recommend this course. There are a few homework assignments and quizzes that are just like the homework, midterms, finals, and a very easy project on Excel.  No class on days that your homework and quizzes are due and the last week.
Pretty easy concepts. You get a formula sheet on all tests. Let us out 20 minutes early every single class

She's great, teaches well, cares a lot, and she rounded everyone's letter grades up when the midterm avg was below her expectations. Only bad thing is that two tests and the final make up 75% of the total grade. Test 2 covers weeks 3 through 14, so basically the entire course. That's why it's so hard. The first test and final are pretty easy.

This class was alright, lectures were short and to the point. She's a quiet lady who explains the material well. The exams were straightforward with no surprises, but they make a big chunk of your grade and have 10-15 MCQs, so there's very little room for error.

Your grade is mainly determined by the three exams: 2 midterms and final (35%). She keeps lectures succinct and provides lots of practice problems. Most stressful part of class is the exams, and you get a cheat sheet for both. The first exam was 15 questions, and second one was 10, which makes keeping an A hard. Lets class out early every day.

Sweet lady who's a great professor. I found the material interesting and she explained all concepts well. She provided ample practice material for all exams and was very straightforward in telling us what to study for. One knock is that the final is worth 35%, so even though I had perfect performance throughout the semester the end was stressful.

Took her for a Maymester class and it was a super manageable course. Class never went the full time. Homework and exams were manageable. She is always happy to help explain concepts and problems. I would not recommend the May class to a finance major though.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Significantly enhanced my learning experience. Unique way of breaking down complex concepts. The PPs are very helpful! She provided us with multiple opportunities to practice the material (helps a lot). Available to provide additional help & responds to emails. Small language barrier but TAKE HER she is easy to follow along!
She thoroughly explains each topic in class. Does many practice problems in class. Very nice. Gets let out early most classes.

She teaches a little slow and unclearly sometimes, but she will walk around to make sure you understand. Further, she is very caring if you ask to meet with her regarding homework or tests. An MBA student offers tutoring on Fridays, which is helpful. However, I would say I taught myself most of the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Participation 50 (free points)
Quizzes 50 (free points)
Project 100 (free points)
1st Midterm 250 (hard)
2nd Midterm 250 (pretty hard)
Final Exam 300 (hard)

I hated this class. I am not sure if these other reviews got her in a smaller class, but I had her in a big lecture hall and could barely hear her. She barely explained her math. Class is all lecture and exams are super hard.

She is a great , amazing professor, and makes the class fun. You do not need the book at all as everything you need is on her PowerPoints and she does share them. Participation is clutch to get a good grade, but overall very straight forward class if you pay attention and understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Reading the powerpoint and her lecture will be enough to understand the chapters and pass the exam. She is nice and willing to help her students outside the class. The homework and exams except final are taken online, and she will give extra credit if you are the first one to write answers of one of the practice questions from handouts on the board
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I was a little worried at first that I wouldn't be able to understand her, but her lectures are easily understood. She gives out homework once a week. Her lectures are so informative that you don't need to read the book. Which is good because that book is confusing. You won't be disappointed if you take her class.

Quesada was clear on what she wanted from her students in order for them to excel in the class, and she gave useful feedback on all assignments. Participation is important and you need to do the readings, but it is not an insane amount of work and she is always happy to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Don't have to participate in class. She is super nice and caring. She grades really hard, so I would go to all of the extra credit opportunities because she does give you some, and they are easy to do. easy weekly work but hard tests. the review may help, but not as much as it should. She loves it if you are involved in the class or ask questions.

Cold calls. A lot. She gives lots of extra credit, but it's because YOU NEED IT. As someone who's ending with an A, this class was unreasonably confusing. Expects you to be a biblical scholar on the tests because a ton of it isn't on the review. She's very caring, but gets really frustrated in class, and it's annoying. Feels like high school

She is overly criticized. Lots of freshmen take this course, who just think it's hard (it's not). She gives a crazy amount of extra credit opps (got my midterm up 15 points after she curved it 5). Might seem rude, but she just wants you to participate since nobody does. 0 hw. 4 at-home quizzes. Easy A with all the XC and a very passionate teacher!

She is very passionate about what she teaches. Her lectures are sometimes hard to follow and she gets frustrated when people don't know the answer. She will cold call on you if she thinks you are someone that knows the answer. There are 2 essays and 2 tests so study for the tests and turn your essays in on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's passionate about what she teaches but overall it's hard to know what she expects us to know for the 2 exams. Some of the lectures can be hard to follow especially if your reading comprehension is not the best. Heavily class discussion-based, and if you don't understand the textbook well, exams will be hard. Chunk of your grade is attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is probably the worst ive taken at tcu. all paper class, expect for pop quizzes online. Very tough grader and will cold call people who are quiet in the class. no phones, computers, anything. Really confuses me why she cares so much about that stuff. wouldn't recommend. if u fail midterm then u will have a U automatically
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Overall, a fine class, teacher treats you like your 15. Cold calls, no technology, arbitrary grading, pop quizzes that are not in the syllabus, and only gives you 5 minutes for the reading quizzes. In terms of religion classes, it is probably not super difficult but expect to be super bored and be taught by someone with a strong religious bias.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had in a long time! Didn't even think I would like the class since I'm not religious but ended up being my favorite of the semester. She is engaging, funny, and thoughtful. Stay off your laptop in class and take notes and you will do fine.

Least favorite class and professor i've had during college and im going into senior year, shes always in a bad mood, and takes it out on the class. She's very passionate about this class but doesn't understand that everyone in the class is only taking it to fulfill a requirement. Lectures are boring and she's very opinionated.

The actual class is easy, you just have to show up and do the work. Its really annoying because in her syllabus it says every exam is online, however, she decided to make it in person. We did get a cheat sheet tho. She is quite literally always in a bad mood. She treats you like a highschooler, constantly cold calls, and is overall miserable.

Low ratings seem to be from people who don't like being called out for scrolling and general disrespect. Really caring professor. I had a couple personal situations that she was super understanding about. Interesting perspectives. Clear expectations. I would 10/10 recommend Dr. Quesada and this class. Do me a favor and participate. She deserves it!

OVER RATED. I dread this class more than anything. This was the first year where the tests aren't online, but she does allow a cheat sheet. The class isn't hard, but all she does is lecture and it's painful. She doesn't like computers. She has major attitude when she realizes no one is paying attention, then she cold call ppl she doesn't like.

I took this fall of 24. She is so sweet and cares about her students. As long as you read and participate in this class you will be fine. Some classes the lectures are boring, but you get in what you put in. I would take this class if you need a religion credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Quesada was a degrading and misleading professor. No iPhones or computers allowed, but that's not the issue. If she felt you weren't paying attention, she would call you out and belittle your participation. She is a very harsh grader but does not specify what she is looking for, the lectures were the most boring thing to listen to as well
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I personally think Dr Quesada is overrated. She is pretty condescending and calls out people if she doesn't think you are paying attention. Every class you miss takes a percent off your final so beware of that. Nice lady at heart all in all.

I would recommend taking professor Quesada for a religion credit. She cares about student success and was accessible outside of class. She is understanding and will especially help out students who participate in class. The class is very lecture and reading heavy so you do need to go and take notes since most assessments are open notes.

Quesada is a sweet person and prof! She knows most students are taking the class for credit, so showing her effort and respect is all she really wants. The class was VERY reading & participation heavy. I participated, READ, and still didn't always do the best on the exams, which was really annoying. If you show up for her, she'll show up for you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class feels like the students are treated as high-schoolers, which wasn't the best. Lots of reading, but assignments are super easy. The final is the only slightly tricky part of the class. Attendance is needed for a good grade. Do some of the readings and do good enough work on assignments and you'll be fine. Easyish religion credit.

This class feels as if it is run a bit more as a high school class, and the professor treats kids as high school students. It was not exactly my favorite, but I did learn a lot. Most of the class is online and easy, but the final is a little tricky. Keep up with readings and assignments are super easy.

For the most part, she is great. Very nice and caring and wants you to do well. However, she assigns a lot of reading, though she claimed she would dial it down in the future. Tests and quizzes aren't too hard but you definitely need to show up to every class if possible. Also, no phones out whatsoever.

Professor Quesada is one of the kindest and most engaging instructors I've had. While the class involves a lot of reading, the assignments are manageable. Quizzes are easy, and attendance is key. unstuckstudy was a lifesaver for study prep.

Only homework is to read the Bible. We have quizzes every two to three weeks but they are open note. She gets upset when people are staring at their screens but overall she is easy. Definitely take her for a religion credit.

Very lecture heavy so attendance is mandatory, or you will miss out on vital information. Class will be very easy if you take notes and do the reading. Professor Quesada is very caring and wants you to do well in the class, I would highly recommend her to any first level college student.

Very caring. Attendance is mandatory, your grade takes a hit if you skip class. Lots of reading, she gets upset if no one does it. Otherwise, her expectations are very clear, she's an easy grader. Lectures cover interesting topics, but sometimes it's hard to pay attention and a bit boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Quesada is a very professional professor who make her expectations clear from day one. The class is easy to succeed in as long as you pay attention and show up to class. Attendance is mandatory, and your grade will be affected if you miss a certain amount of class sessions.

Dr Quesada is a great professor! She has a great heart, you can tell she truly cares for her students. Note that there are no devices allowed in the classroom. For assignments, we have discussion posts and essays. For exams/quizzes, there is a midterm & a final (both taken online) and weekly quizzes. Really like being able to complete work at home.

Dr. Quesada is one of the best teachers I have had. Her lectures are very easy to follow along with and she is always open to questions. The readings for the class are very manageable, along with the quizzes. If you get the chance to take her class you should.

Overall, the class isn't difficult and Quesada is very kind and easy to talk to. One of the nicest professors I've ever had and engages with students well. Beware of lots of reading, but the reading tends to be pretty short. She also will give you credit for the assignments if you are present in class which is a huge bonus. Quizzes are easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very kind woman, easy class, but long reading assignments for every class. If no one participates, she gets angry. There are a few quizzes, discussion boards, etc. but she's an easy grader. Participation is mandatory: 1% taken off your grade for every absence. Absolutely no technology allowed. A little boring, but easy religion credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Quesada is an easy grader, but she does not allow technology and if she sees it she will call you out in front of the entire class. U cant use the restroom, and cannot talk to your peers during the lecture. She lectures the ENTIRE class with very boring Powerpoints it is hard to stay awake. Environment is borderline unbearable.

This professor hates technology- that's fine. She treads carefully when discussing religion. The books provided have an overarching, screaming left-leaning political bias. It is not at all addressed by her. She treads carefully.
Dr. Quesada is the sweetest teacher and always engages with what you say and discuss in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Quesada is such an amazing professor. She is really passionate and cares about you. You do have to go to class every day and participate, but overall the class is really easy. She does a no tech policy but if you want an easy A, take her.

Dr. Quesada is the best! I have never felt more appreciated by a professor before. She really cares about her students and how class goes. She likes no technology, so get a journal or paper notes. shes super sweet and truly cares. AND it is such an interesting and necessary class to take.

I highly recoomend people take dr. quesada. She grades fairly and exams aren't hard (she allows notecards) lots of reading every week, and so much information to retain on all worldly religions. 

1 midterm exam, 1 midterm essay, 1 group project, 1 final exam.
She is such a wonderful professor! Would totally recommend

She's a nice woman, but she plays favorites- if you know a lot about religion and participate and do all the reading, she likes you. It's not too hard, the test and quizzes are taken home but every now and then there's a hard assignment that knocks your grade- especially the writing portion of the midterm. Relatively boring class- lecture heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: She banned technology this semester, only allows one absence, and is honestly rude. Expects way too much from students not majoring in religion and gets angry when we don't lead class for her. It's painful sitting through her classes.
Class is easy and she is the sweetest teacher! Loved having her class this semester.

Dr. Quesada is a really nice woman, but she wants you to do a LOT of reading at home, then just discuss the readings in class. I took an intro class, but the quantity of reading was greater than what the class was worth. You CAN scrape by if you don't read, as long as you take really good notes in class, but she'll be upset. Easy class overall.

Professor Quesada was an amazing teacher. I took her 8 am class and she brought energy even when the students were tired. Her test and quizzes were easy if you pay attention in her class. There is reading but if you stay on top of it you will get an A in the class. I would 100% recommend this class because of how nice and caring she is.

A lot of reading and quizzes , but I mean a lot. She will ask you the most specific questions to make sure you actually read for her quizzes. Ive heard of easier classes , definitely take another religion class that is easier and not as demanding. But be prepared to read almost all of the Bible and still feel unprepared for her quizzes/exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You just have to attend class but all tests are open notes and the final is as well. The readings are interesting.

I absolutely love Professor Quesada, just participate, and listen to lectures and you will be totally fine! If you forgot a reading or two, she will 100% explain it in class! Super sweet and made me love the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Dr. Quesada's Understanding Religion class. Tests and quizzes are easy as long as you do the reading and study guides. Her lectures were pretty similar to the readings. She gives great feedback and is overall a very understanding professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Such a sweet lady who explains things very well. Weekly assignments, but only keeps 10 highest grades at the end of the semester. Midterm and final that aren't hard. One group presentation, relatively easy grader. Take this as your religion with her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I have had. She is amazing and cares about you. Easiest religion class at TCU take it if you need a religion you will love her.

She's such a sweet lady, and is accessible outside of class and is so accommodating. She's very lecture heavy and expects you to do the reading in the discussion-based class, and the reading can be a lot. Politics sometimes show up but nothing major. Take her for understanding religion: texts and ideas: the Bible if you can!
I had Quesada for Interfaith Studies and she was great. She is super passionate about everything she teaches. The quizzes and tests can be hard, however, they are open note, so take good notes.

This professor knows what she's talking about. However, she frequently allows her left-leaning politics to influence the class material and it makes the class VERY hard to sit and listen to without speaking up. The class itself is easy. If you have a heartbeat you'll probably get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy
