His test reviews are very similar to his tests, and he does not try to trick you on tests. He is a very good teacher, calculus is a hard class but he explains things well and simplifies the material.
Genuinely wants every student to succeed! Tests are graded very kindly and are very similar to the review guide

He was so caring and genuinely wanted us to pass the class. If you study and learn each process, you can easily ace the tests. He creates study guides similar to the tests to better prepare you. Would take again.
test heavy. 4 exams plus a final.
good professor, not to hard if you study before the test, he gives good material to study.
Highly recommend this class, Dr.Webb is very carrying and makes her class super easy and a great GPA boost class. there's only a few assignments but they're not difficult at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Only 8 week course, so super fast. Only had two in-person classes. Literally the easiest thing ever if you just do the assignments on time, and there're not many, and they're super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Super easy, most classes are on zoom. She is super caring you just have to go to class.

LOVED Dr. Webb she is genuinely the kindest professor ever and you can tell she genuinely cares about the content she teaches. For Intro to Kines just don't procrastinate on assignments because sometimes they take a lot longer than you may anticipate but never that difficult.

Dr. Webb is amazing! This class prepares you to look at your future in kinesiology. Her weekly assignments were not difficult and were great practice for things you will have to do in the future. The guest speakers were so helpful and this class was overall extremely enjoyable.

Ridiculously easy class. Never payed attention and got an A and she's a  sweet lady. You are graded off of labs and tests. The labs are super easy-taking a mindfulness walk around campus and working out in the gym. The tests are kinda common sense and no lock down browser...she doesnt even walk around the room. TAKE HER CLASSS!!!!

I love Dr Webb. She is so caring and inspirational and genuinely wants everyone to succeed. The class is lecture heavy and the exams are based off of the slides, so you know what you are getting into for the exams. They are usually only around 40 questions. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her, please do it. She is amazing!

Dr. Webb is very kind and genuinely wants her students to get an A. She is lecture heavy and there is a quiz or assignment due almost every class. I would love to take her again, but for one of her other classes that may be more challenging.

very chill teacher. slightly annoying how she doesn't put rubrics and stuff on d2l but instead makes you take pictures of the rubrics. if you follow the rubrics and do everything, she tells you you'll do good in the class. can be slightly passive aggressive. but overall, a good teacher and wants you to succeed in the real world.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: As long as you go to class and read a bit beforehand, you'll get an A. There are a couple of presentations, some short (60s) and some longer group projects. Class gets out early a decent amount as well. good fine arts option.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is a nice lady and getting an A is very attainable. Make sure you show up, only complaint is she doesn't post slideshows or grading rubrics and her directions are very vague. But she is not a hard grader so it is not a big deal. Great option for fine arts credit.

Professor Lindsay is very kind in her feedback and is a fair grader. The class is participation heavy with many assigned readings but they are not too heavy. She is very accommodating and gave me some grace for turning an assignment in slightly late. Class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is participation-based and attendance is mandatory. As long as you go to class and take notes you should do well. A lot of assigned readings that are not important. Better classes to take for the credit but not the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She grades very tough for an intro class. She assigns A TON of readings, and only like 5% of them end up actually being relevant to the class. The entire class performed poorly on the midterm and she blamed us even though there was a lot of content that was not discussed/barely discussed in class on the midterm. Wont accept late work.
Makes the class harder than it actually is but is a nice person and has good intentions. Class is graded on mainly the tests so if you get one bad grade expect to finish with a low grade
Rough class. Lectures are boring tests are difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have never reviewed a teacher on here before since even the bad reviews for good teachers are normally bias. This is the toughest class I have ever taken at TCU as a Finance and Management major. The tests are only 20 questions, 10 math based and 10 vocab. 30% of the questions are never deeply explained besides her speeding through slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: very nice professor, fair grading and lots of chances to succeed

Professor K was an amazing person and an even better teacher. She does not deserve the poor reviews here. I struggle with math bad. She saw that I was trying, and was a very generous grader, and gave me so much of her time to help me. 

She is extremely kind and is always willing to help. My classmates that disliked her gave zero effort in class.

I have never written a review but honestly I read her reviews before the semester and was really nervous. Just wrapped up the semester and it ended up being a great class. She really appreciates if you participate and if you show up to all (most) of the classes you will do totally fine.

Had her for Fin Man, she's okay. Her lectures are long, boring, and confusing. But she gives review questions before the exam and they weren't hard. She gives you a notecard or cheat sheet. Her lectures are just such a pain to sit through, she way over complicates everything but she is nice and cares about her students.

She lectures too fast and covers too much to follow. The review barely matches the test, and she adds random multiple choice questions that are impossible to prepare for. She only flashes long equations on the board without teaching or explaining them, and we never actually practice the ones that show up on the test. Do not take, you will be lost.

Take her. She is one of the kindest professors I have had at TCU. My attendance was not great and I did not study until 1 hour before the exams and ended up with an A. The class is easy and you get notecards for exams. If you study more than I do, it should be a walk in the park.

I took this class for fun in my senior year. I'm not a finance major. She is very nice and caring. Her lecture is boring and hard to understand, but the material for Investment 1 is also very heavy. Her exams are a little tricky, but she curves it A LOT. Just put effort into it, do the review questions, and it is manageable to get an A

We are graded by very few homework assignments and only tests. The assignments are easy, tests are tough but get curved; so it's not too hard to get an alright grade in this class. However, you will feel so lost the entire semester, you will know nothing that is going on. She explains things in the most complicated ways and only reads off slides.

I felt throughout this entire course that 95% of what we learn in class is not what we are assessed on. I am a very good student and work extremely hard, however, when you don't know what to expect and almost all of your notes from class and the textbook do nothing there is little trust in my knowledge or lack there of.

Trust me, the stuff is hard, and there will be times you will have no idea what is going on in class. However it is doable. You just need to study more and pay attention in class. She is friendly, and if you don't understand the stuff, she is willing to explain it to you. The exam stuff can be a little different, so be ready to start studying early

Honest rating: She is an incredible person that means well and genuinely cares about students. Her class is very hard for Investments 1 but she curves grades very heavily. People giving bad professor scores probably got a bad grade on an exam and are just salty. The class is hard but managable, and you will have to study a bit outside class

Worst teacher I have had, including high school. Be prepared to listen to broken English for complex investment terminology, unclear deadlines, and no homework (but 20-question MC tests covering 6 chapters). Get ready to teach yourself everything. She also never discloses the curve or the uncurved average, if that says anything about her exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a very nice professor. The tests are hard but aren't weighted as much as most classes. If you do well on the homework, take-home quizzes, and participation you will do well. Very easy B and decent effort for an A.

I took her in her 1st semester at TCU. You have to teach yourself the material because she follows the long slides Neeley makes. It feels impossible until you get the practice problems leading up the test and then its alright. Definitely not impossible to get an A if you work hard. A lot of the test questions were from the quizzes and homework.

By far the WORST teacher I have ever had at TCU. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Zero structure to her class and no one ever knows what is going on. Impossible to understand and even hear when she is lecturing. Makes you buy so many course packs and simulations in addition to the textbook. Save your money and frustration.

Don't take this professor, she is definitely the most difficult professor I've had at Neeley and I've taken much harder classes with more difficult material. She is just very lazy and only reads off of slides. The exams are timed to an hour and she puts between 20-30 questions on every exam, you will be lucky to finish them. def the worst for gpa
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Terrible professor who reads PowerPoint slides instead of teaching. Zero original homework, quizzes, or tests. Doesn't grade anything herself. Nice person, but completely disengaged from actual teaching. Students get no educational value. Avoid this course and save your money. Find a professor who actually cares about students and isn't lazy.

I feel bad because she is a nice person, however she is not a good professor. All she does is read the slides from the textbook. The practice problems she gives are nothing like the exam. I will most likely receive a B in the class after hours put into it each week. If you are fine with teaching yourself the material, then you will be fine.

I think she is a really nice and great person. Approachable outside of class and is open to help students. Review sessions before the test offered. She goes over an 100+ slide deck almost every class. She only works problems right before the test. You must teach yourself the material. Overall nice professor but you will not learn much in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: PLEASE DO NOT TAKE! She is the absolute worst professor I have ever had. She does not explain anything well. Financial management is a tough class, but it is not that tough. She is impossible to understand. Nothing she says in class is on the exam. Class average for exam 2 was 65 AFTER the curve. Save yourself.
Boring class, homework is infrequent, tests are similar to quizzes and in-class worksheets. Lots of people complain about the material but it is very learnable.

I rarely actually know what's going on in class. She reads directly from the 100+ slide deck and doesn't explain the concepts at all. Homework takes forever and usually looks nothing like the exams. She is a very sweet lady but avoid her class if you can.

First year teaching a class, doesn't really understand how to answer questions students ask she just repeats what she previously read off of slides from the textbook. She doesn't make test based off of what is taught in class, instead she just uses the test given straight from Pearson textbook. Nice lady though.

She is a nice professor and does in class packets that help with the material but all of the tests are on Pearson and are 1000 times harder than any of the homework or quizzes. The homework and quizzes are very time consuming, she asks after they are due if they were hard like she had no clue what was on it. Take as last resort. Need to go to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You basically have to teach yourself all the material. She reads off the book slides which are 100+ slides every class which most people learn nothing from. The quizzes and homework are different than what she teaches. She is smart and nice but has no idea how to teach a class. This has been my worst experience in a class by far in Neeley. Avoid.

Lectures are very difficult to understand. She doesn't explain concepts well and lectures are based on 100+ slide powerpoints. The homework and quizzes are online and they do not relate to what she teaches in class. Basically have to learn everything on my own. Do not take.
Avoid her.

She is definitely smart but does not know how to explain things clearly in English. You will not understand the WHY of what you are taught. You are supposed to come to class and thats how she does attendance. Everything is through Pearson and many of the questions in the homework have nothing to do with what we are learning in class. Dont take her!

Class structure is not set up to help students succeed. TCU really needs to change how this course is graded. The simulation is not helpful what so ever. My group did fine but if you have a bad group, you are SCREWED. Take someone else who has does not have absurd exams. Layton is a good professor and good man, but take someone else.

Take anyone else if you can. Tries to make everyone a supply chain major because he is the head of the department. Exams are extremely tough compared to other teachers. Provides little to zero help with the simulation
just dont. dont.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: test were actually so hard and about the most specific random things. the simulations was hard with the group I had because they didnt know anything about how to use it. did not get a good grade in the class. also he barely helps with the sim

Nice at first. So unhelpful with simulation, if you get a bad group your whole semester grade is messed with. He has no idea what hes doing with the simulation, and anytime we met with him we did worse. He's a nice guy, just so unhelpful. No one should be doing the simulation. Also his tests are just ridiculous and average is like a 70

Layton was great. He is extremely passionate about his information and is very helpful when teaching. The tests are pretty difficult and have really low averages. If you use the 3 pages front and back of the cheat sheets the right way, you will do fine. Not sure why he has such a low score here.

Should have listened to the reviews. If he is your only option, I would wait a semester to get a different professor. He had a whole lecture at the beginning of the semester explaining why our GPA doesn't matter and why he will only give 4/35 of us an A. He does not understand that most people are not supply chain majors. If you got him, good luck!

DO NOT TAKE if you are trying to get an A. Test averages were between 70 and 79 and nobody got an 100. He does not curve at all. The simulation is hard and he does not explain it unless you meet him outside of class. There is no grace for anything, especially a bad team member. Grading criteria is clear but set up for failure. I normally get As.

Professor Layton made this class more bearable. The class is hard, exams weren't too bad but the simulation is horrible if you're stuck with a bad group. I will say, his lectures were good and he is very knowledgeable about the field. I liked him as a professor, just didn't like how the class was structured with the simulation.

I should have listened to the reviews. This class is impossible if your team is not good. He does not explain the simulation at all and expects you to do well. Exam was way harder than he made it sound, most failed and he didn't curve. He takes pride in only giving a few kids an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Layton is a fantastic puzzle solver! Him and Luke were able to solve the mystery of the Elysian Box. I would highly recommend the IGN guide for some of his assignments as they can be difficult even if the game is PEGI 7!

I went into his class with low expectations, but he ended up being one of my favorite professors. The group simulation is tough, but you don't have to finish 1st to get an A, just focus on doing well on the exams, he allows a 6-page note. He is very knowledgeable and gives some of the best lectures. Don't let the ratings here scare you off

Professor Layton is an expert in his field, he is very knowledgeable and his lectures are very informative. He is a hard grader and has a philosophy that he is doing everybody a favor by not giving out A's but to 10% or so of the class. Your grade might not be the best, but you will have the strongest grasp on material out of any teacher.

Layton's class isn't as hard as other say. The class is very dependent on the simulation, but I had a bad group and still did pretty well. The exams are tricky but not as hard as they sound (6 pages of cheat sheets). He is kind and super accessible. Maybe not the easiest class but all SC classes are pretty difficult.

Very hard to do well in this class. Attendance isn't mandatory and you really don't learn much in class anyway. The SIM is a huge part of your grade and its very difficult to know what's going on. 6 page cheat sheet is allowed for tests but even then 70s are the test average (not curved). Super nice guy but way too hard for a business core class.

he's really nice but oh my gosh it is impossible to do well in this class. the past two exam averages were in the low 70s and he didn't curve them. exams are not anything like he says and they're impossible to study for. the grading for the SIM is ABSURD and so unfair - makes grades drop a lot, thinks we're all SCM majors and understand everything

Extremely hard grader for everything. Not many opportunities to earn good grade. For the sim, he's gonna grade you based on how much better and the rank you get after each round. If you make higher ROI, but not much & drop a rank, he's gonna give you a B. Tests are way too hard even with 6 pages cheat sheets. People barely get 70,80s.

Layton makes this class extremely difficult to pass. There are 8 different categories that you are graded on and our test averages weren't above 73% and he didn't curve. He says he "gives a lot of extra credit" but its 30 points in a 1000-point class. The simulation is impossible and he doesn't help. He expects everyone to be a SCM major.
Wow this guys awful! Took him last spring and the worst experience I've had in a neely class. Zero help or support during group projects. Avoid at ALL COSTS.

Probably the worst prof I've had at this school. It's absurd how many things he requires you to sign up for outside of class. We all take other classes and it's a junior / senior year class - the time you need to be spending finding jobs. Horrible and would never take again. Avoid at all costs.

Nothing good to say about this guy. he gives zero direction on the simulation other than “communicate with your groups.” Tests have nothing to do w lectures and he prides himself on a “gotcha” at every turn. absolutely no respect for the fact that students take other classes and have other things going on (like applying for jobs).

One of the worst professors at TCU. His exams are extremely hard, with no forgiveness. His simulation is horrible and he has no clue how to run a class. Other sections with other professors seem to actually enjoy their class. I think Layton forgets none of us are supply chain majors or care about supply chain. It's an intro supply chain core class.

Layton is a nice guy - but my god Neeley needs to change their core curriculum. Supply chain was revamped a few semesters ago and now feels like a intermediate/upper level supply chain course. If you have a brain you will get a B in his course - but you will be spending your entire semester learning about pallets and truckloads if you want an A.

Your entire grade is basically based on a simulation and 2 tests. The simulation is graded so harsh and if you don't increase by like 3% ROI each time, you'll be getting Cs or Bs in that round. My team was top 3 at the end and the last round we got a B-, makes no sense. Tests are extremely hard and not even over anything covered in class.

Professor Layton is a great guy with lost of experience and always accessible when you need him. However, his class is graded very hard. There is a group project simulation that is graded very heavily. The two exams are difficult but you get notes pages which help tremendously.

RUN! Take anyone else just not him! He does not even know what is wrong with the stimulation. Lots of groups followed his instructions and their ROI was destroyed. Unreasonable grading, ridiculously low points for the game itself. No curves for exams

Extremely hard simulation game that solely depends on your group and how much your ROI increases/decreases each week. The group presentations are also graded extremely hard and the 2 exams in the class are very specific and difficult! If you don't want to be left guessing each week about a juice game, don't take him!!

Professor Layton is a nice guy and the lectures are interesting. The simulation however is ridiculously hard and completely depends on your group. Also, the tests are VERY HARD. Extremely specific questions about the simulation and lots of hard multi-select. His class isn't bad but there are definitely easier professors.

I know this class used to be terrible so I'm glad I waited to take it. The test was very fair, not nearly as hard as people used to say. The worst part of the class is the simulation that no one understands. The simulation has far too much information to comprehend and leaves us guessing each week lol. I would recommend prof layton for the class!
The simulation is hard and dependent on your group. I would not recommend taking him, lots of easier supply chain teachers out there. If you are doing the simulation, use inflatable PET bottles

Nice guy that is very experienced in the industry and knowledgeable. They completely changed the course from previous years this semester and introduced a semester-long simulation game that is a big part of the grade but it is easy to get decent scores on. The exams are still difficult but easier than in previous years. He is the best for the class

Honestly, Professor Layton is a great guy... he is super knowledgeable & is very passionate about what he is teaching. The class goes by very fast imo, and I supply chain definitely is not my favorite, but Prof. Layton makes it interesting. The only thing that brought my grade down were his EXTREMELY HARD tests. Everything else was great.

Professor Layton is a nice guy and to me the lectures were interesting, but the tests are unbelievably difficult. You have chances to do well in other aspects like excel workshops, capstone projects, etc. But the tests brought down my grade a decent bit. Extremely knowledgeable about the Supply Chain and passionate about it.

Layton's class is very interesting! He's very personable and VERY approachable. His exams are tough. However, even with a low testing avg you can still earn a good grade as there are many other easier points. 3 tests & comprehensive final, one large group project, 3 excel sets, and 3 discussion posts make up most of grade. Highly recommend!

Supply Chain is a very difficult class no matter who you take. Prof Layton is awesome and is a great teacher. He has started many businesses and is very successful. He makes the concepts easy to understand and will respond to your text at any hour of the day. Don't get me wrong, the exams are tough, but he is a great guy. Highly reccomend.

Everyone on here who gives negative reviews of Layton is wrong. He is a great professor, incredibly knowledgeable, and fair. Yes, his tests are really hard but if you study, you'll pass. He helped start numerous businesses and works in consulting, VERY experienced.

Professor Layton is a tough professor. Ive texted him questions at all hours of the night and he always answers. Very approachable. He is passionate in what he teaches about and has tons of experience in the industry. The content can be difficult, but as long as you do the homework, pay attention in class, and do his assignments, youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Overall, I thought Professor Layton was a great professor. His class is definitely hard but I have learned a lot of useful information. Overall, I would recommend him for Supply Chain!

Supply chain should not be a difficult class but Layton manages to do just that. The majority of the questions on quizzes and tests are trick questions or not very clear and when you ask him about the questions he always responds with "Well, I didn't write the question so I can't really help" Worst prof I've had in a long time, makes me not like SC
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The exams are loaded with trick questions. DO NOT take this class. Im surprised that TCU even employs him as a professor. Absolutely awful.
Awful class, you can study all day and night for his tests and will still fail. Group projects are decent but lectures are boring. Do not recommend if you want a life outside of this class.

This class frustrating, simply put. The content of the class itself is not too difficult and the concepts are relatively easy, HOWEVER Prof. Layton manages to make this class one of the hardest I've every taken. The way his quizzes/exams/projects are structured are extremely arduous and force a low grade. Do not take if you value your GPA!
He is a great professor but the class is super difficult. He is really willing to help so do not ask for help last minute!

Not sure if the supply chain class is like this for every professor but Layton assigns a LOT of work for an intro level supply chain class - multiple case studies, 3 tests plus a comprehensive final, project at the end of the semester, multiple Excel exercises (that you have to figure out on your own), online quizzes. Don't take if not supply major

This is by far the hardest class I have taken at TCU. The amount of assignments that we have to do in this class usually leave students scrambling to just try and finish them rather than actually retain any information. The tests are impossible regardless of how much you study. He does not allocate enough time for each chapter. DO NOT TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His tests were very difficult and lectures are very fast paced. Lots of group work/ time demand outside of class but offers extra credit credit opportunities to make up for bad grades. He is a nice guy & has a hard class but if you work hard you can do well.

A lot of work to do during the semester. Always says he grades the group case from the view of the real world without telling what he expects from the paper. Tests are open book and open notes, but there is no time for you to actually search for answers, especially the last two tests.

I took his Supply Chain Management course at TCU. The material the class covers isn't extremely hard, the only complaint I really have is the way he graded some things. Every group case study we did got the same grade, and we tried several different methods but could not get a 100. Feedback on the grading wasn't super clear either.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not nice. Very unorganized as he gives zero directions. Takes off points based on his personal preferences. Had to buy expensive textbooks to use them all twice. Me and multiple students got 10 whole points off for spelling one thing wrong which I find incredibly wrong. This class is a lot of work I would take the other professor. I hated this clas

Digital storytelling was a much easier and more fun class compared to Design. You had to get through that tough class to get to this fun, creative one. Levering is super chill and wants to see you succeed. Highly recommend this one for your STCO elective.
He is a very sweet and caring teacher, however the class is hard. You really need to know how to do everything for every single test as he will refuse to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Levering is a nice teacher, but his grading is based on personal preference. He gives barely any instruction when giving assignments, and spends random class doing "Photoshop Fun Days" where we do random stuff on our computers instead of learning anything about what we are being assigned. He takes a lot of points off for tiny mistakes.

There wasn't another option for design teachers, so I didn't have a choice, but I had heard good things going in. He could be helpful at times but chose when to be. His grading felt entirely based on personal taste, and it seemed like he had something against certain students, consistently grading their strong designs poorly for no clear reason.

Cancels class a lot. He expects attendance but not included in grade. Class is made up of 7 projects and 3 tests. He grades tough and it's all his opinion if your design is good or not. To do well on projects you need to ask so many questions. Tests are medium difficulty. He can sometimes be very helpful but chooses when not to be helpful.

Levering is great! Such a sweet guy and really cares about his students. He has clear expectations for exams and projects and expects them to be fulfilled, so take lots of care with the details. It can be hard to be creative and precise with the timelines given for assignments, but IT IS POSSIBLE TO DO WELL!!!! You will learn so much!
he is a fun professor and will let u out of class early sometimes, but exams are kinda difficult and there's barely enough time to finish them.
Highly recommend taking one of his classes. He is a great professor and is fun to be around. He lets you out early most of the time and is available to meet frequently.

Levering is a really tough grader and takes a lot of points of for small mistakes so be sure to double check over work. Other than that its a pretty chill class as long as you stay on top of work since there is a good amount of projects.

Professor Levering is interesting and pretty chill for the most part, but can be a tough grader. The class is paced well throughout the first half of the semester, but speeds up quite a bit in the end with 5 or so projects due and all spaced only a week apart. Overall not too hard of a class, just don't procrastinate too much.

levering is really chill but a tough grader. if you show up to class and actually try, you'll do well. only had one written type of exam (we were online though) and i've heard other design profs have a lottt- so definitely recommend levering.

Had him for design, not the easiest class if you don't pay attention or put in some effort to understand photoshop. He's a real nice guy though and cares about graphic design. Few projects at the end of the year and one exam.

Professor Lewis is the absolute best! I have taken both his classes now and wish I could take more. Both were night classes but he never kept us longer than an hour and a half. He is very understanding, caring, and entertaining. Tests are online not in class and there are weekly writing assignments but is a very fair grader and they are not hard.

He is the absolute best! I have taken two of is classes now and I wish I could take more. Both have been night classes but he never keeps us longer than an hour and a half. He is very understanding, kind, and entertaining. Tests are online not taken in class and there are weekly writing assignments but he is a very fair grader and they're not hard.

The best. The kindest teacher ever; if I could fit him into my schedule next semester, I would. Lectures are great, super interesting since he is in the field himself. One writing assignment a week, if that, and it is super chill and fun to write. Tests are online, you can use notes. Going to end with an A+ (most likely), and I learned so much!!!
Dr. Lewis is great and started a spark for my future career path!!! Absolutely recommend taking him. He is one of those professors you will never forget about.

Professor Lewis is amazing. 
His classes are both extremely interesting - especially because he has a lot of personal stories to share.
The workload is fair and he tells you exactly what he expects.
He also truly cares about his students - he just wrote me a letter of rec. for law school.
10/10, 100% suggest his class.

Loved Professor Lewis. I took both White Collar and Courts. If you can take him 100% do it for both. He is a fair professor with a well-laid out class. Class is not boring and he doesn't keep you there longer than you need to be. You also get some cool personal stories from his time as a prosecutor. Awesome professor.

Professor Lewis was an awesome professor! He is very clear about what you have to do. He doesn't mess around, all of his lectures are straight to the point and so is every assignment. He is always available when you contact him. He has interesting stories to tell and is just all around an amazing professor.110% recommend for courts and white collar

I took both the classes that he teaches at once and it was fine. Courts is very easy but White Collar Crime requires a lot more work. While it is a lot of work, I feel very prepared for the future and very much appreciate that. He is a funny guy and I like the way he teaches.

Gives you all powerpoints before class to have and use. His lectures are captivating and engaging. As a WEM class, you will do weekly writing homework, however as long as you pay attention in class, these are easy points. Exams are easy, small portion of MC and 1 writing section per exam. Attendance optional but recommended.

I took Professor Lewis' White Collar Crime class. The class is easy, with clear and concise lectures. Grades are made up of 1. Exams (2) 2. Weekly Writings (10) 3. Final Paper (1). There is a textbook for this course, but Professor Lewis says you can pass the class without it. He is caring and understanding. He works as a federal prosecutor too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class made me go back to therapy.

guys please do not take Unity class for your first semester at TCU. I was super depressed the whole semester for this course. It was super hard. lecture are super heavy, but the exams are different. Dr. Luque is smart, but really hard to follow if you are not really good at Biol. grades mostly depend on tests. be prepared to cry and study.

She is sometimes very hard to follow in her lectures and many times the lectures and even practice problems can be nothing like the exams/quizzes. Pre and Post Lecture assignments are due every day online and the grading is based almost entirely on the few exams and a small amount on the weekly quizzes. One of the most difficult classes.

For both Unity and her Intro Lab she is extremely hard to follow. She is so intelligent in the field of Biology that unless you already have a good biology foundation and also love biology it will be very hard to learn anything from her. When you ask a question she is highly condescending or will laugh at you and then give a useless response.

She made the class really hard and was condescending to any student who was confused. Do NOT take Unity in your first semester. The tests are nothing like the material in class, and prepare to spend weeks studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Test questions are overall complicated for no reason, even if you study and know the curriculum you may fail the exam. Get ready for lots of busy work outside of class with short completion windows.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her quizzes are very difficult. Homework is every day of the week, a connect assignment before and after the lecture. She goes over topics like it is just a review for her, and is very condescending when asking her questions. She makes you feel stupid when you get something wrong. I would not take her again!

Dr. Luque was amazing and made my first semester at TCU genuinely enjoyable. Her office hours fill up quickly, but if you send her an email, she's very flexible and will work with you to find another time to meet. My only complaint is that grading can take a while, but aside from that, she's awesome, funny, and incredibly knowledgeable.

Luque only did the lecture portion, but most of this class is in a lab with a TA. The class is structured oddly, with the lecture being on a Friday, even though it makes more sense for it to be on Monday. Lecture knowledge is important, but she isn't very entertaining, and it's hard to stay focused during them. Exams are tricky but are online.

DO NOT take Unity your first semester. It's very chemistry-heavy, and without a strong foundation, you'll struggle. Take Diversity (book heavy but easier) and Chem 1 first to build study skills and a chem foundation. She is very sassy when answering questions, and the tests are extremely difficult. You will have to study like you never have before.

Even though Dr. Luque's class was really tough, she was an amazing professor who knew how to explain things in a way that made sense. She pushed me to do my best and helped me improve my study skills, which made a big difference in how I approach school now.

Although Dr.Luque is very knowledgeable, She is very condescending in and out of class, laughs at students questions, and is not very kind or patient to students who were sick/had an emergency and had to miss class. Her class is hard but Im sure helpful on pre-med track - I HIGHLY suggest taking a different professor.

Dr. Luque's class is challenging, but going to office hours and using tools like Unstuck ai can make a big difference. The exams are tough, so consistent studying is key. With effort, you can succeed in this class.

Dr. Luque is one of a kind. She is very smart but also extremely difficult. She is not very accessible outside of class, aside from her 2 hour office hours (so it really stinks if you can't make those). Luckily this class was graded on a curve so I was able to pull a B by making C's on every exam including the final. Good luck !!!!!
I wish Dr. Luque had her own style of teaching plans for cell but instead it was a copy and paste of Dr. Lakoduk's unit plans.

This summer  class for STEM Scholars has daily quizzes, and weekly exams, which require very IN-DEPTH and THOROUGH answers. The key to excelling in this class is to practice writing each key concept on the exam with at least 4-5 sentences, with even the simplest definition being 2-3 sentences. Put in the work, leave the rest to God, you'll be ok!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The tests are hard but lecture isn't mandatory. I made d on all three exam including the final and finished with an a from lab work. Lab attendance is mandatory

She is very condescending and answers your question with a question or says "you should know that".  She words questions a little tricky and half of the exam is Demarest (lab) which are easier. Overall not the worst class I've taken but could be better.

It is obvious that Dr. Luque is passionate about what she teaches, and I have a lot of respect for her. However, she is extremely condescending towards students and makes it hard to want to ask questions in class. She is great in office hours, but not in a lecture setting. Not a big fan of her teaching style, but se is very intelligent.Good luck...

Dr. Luque is an excellent lecturer. Her learning/time-management material on D2L is liquid gold! Her major downfall is her attitude/emotional instability/superiority complex, which ruins the course. She can be dry/condescending in class/over email and is a ticking time bomb over literally any accidental irritant. Life is too short to stay so angry.

Dr. Luque is an amazing professor, most freshman struggle with her course because they might expect an easy way to navigate biology instead of truly knowing what is expected as a pre-health student. Her exams are difficult and tricky but each student needs to find their own strengths and weakness. Listen to all her recorded lectures after class!
Good luck. That is all I have to say

I have a lot of respect for Dr. Luque, she is very smart and caring towards her students. That doesn't mean she can't be condescending at times, but she truly cares. I was struggling at first in her Unity course, but going to her office hours made the most change in my grade. Don't be discouraged and don't compare yourself to others, don't give up!

GO TO OFFICE HOURS. She can be very intimidating, but her class is interesting and makes you learn. She cares about students but will not put up with bs. Study constantly and you will feel like you learned something, even if youre grade isn't the highest. Don't be upset by low test scores, her tests are designed to challenge you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Luque is a bit of a tough love professor but she is nice and tells you what you need to know for exams. Her class is difficult but it is all memorization so it comes down to how much effort you are willing to put in. She also drops the lowest assignments of each category which tremendously helps grades.

Unfortunately, you need this course to continue with the pre-med track. She was very condescending in the classroom and during office hours. During office hours, she rushed explanations. I've seen many students change their major, cry because of her class or just her attitude towards them, and even go as far as withdrawing from the university.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Some say that Luque is mean but those people haven't spoken to her for help. She is so sweet. Luque is so smart and breaks down very hard topics that require LOTS OF STUDYING. Her tests will test your knowledge but it's only preparing you for what is to come. You can't want to be pre-med and then complain about a weed out like duh it'll hard.

I think a lot of the negative reviews come from angry freshmen who didn't do well in her intro bio class. Luque teaches an extremely difficult class that will be a shock to a lot of people going into the pre-med track. This is why it's a weed out--not everyone can be great. However, she is so insanely smart and helpful. Just go to office hours!

Luques unity and cells was very hard. Exams had very detailed questions and were worded to trick you. Attending lectures is a must if you want to do good. There were a lot of mindtap assignments and quizzes but she gave a good amount of drops. Her class made me rethink my career many times but she is a great professor that wants to see you succeed.

Hardest class I've taken. Dr. Luque's lectures are good, but you will question your existence during the exams--they are EXTREMELY difficult. If you think you know something well, you don't. Definitely go to office hours, even if you think you know what you're doing (because you most likely don't). Class was only curved by a whopping 0.5 points..

Dr. Luque's Unity and Cells class was VERY difficult and time-consuming. I changed my major because of this class. Dr. Luque is very knowledgeable and a great teacher, but she can be condescending sometimes. If you are taking this class, be prepared to read and study every day and attend office hours. Exams are worth 85% of your grade. Good luck!
Words her tests so weird that no matter what you study you will do bad. Avoid! And she is so mean during lectures like for what
Make sure you pay attention and take notes on the lectures. Her tests are based off of the stuff she teaches in class and less on the textbook.

Professor Luque started out nice but after the first test she started being super annoyed with students. she isnt nice over email, her tests are WAY harder than anything else she gives you. i personally will not take her again but i also have heard lots of people love her.
She is tough, but you will learn the material. The tests are on another level of difficult, so fair warning. She has a great accent haha!

Dr. Luque, although a challenging professor, ultimately pushes you to learn biology extremely in-depth. The course requires alot of outside practice and work, however, if you put in the work you will understand the subject in much greater detail. She sets you up for success, however, is challenging.

In this class be prepared to work your butt off, if you aren't the best at biology. Dr. Luque can be super rude but also can be nice, you just need to respect her and ask her questions if you have them. Good luck
Professor Luque is so harsh at times. If an emergency happens, she gets upset with you and makes you feel dumb for asking for help.

Dr. Luque is very degrading. She will cut you off when asking questions. If we do not remember something from the lecture before,cshe sits there and says "You should know this. we just talked about it." The class is very time-consuming we have an assignment every day except for Saturdays and for me personally, I have to relisten to her lectures.

Dr Luque explains complex topics well and has weekly quizzes to keep you up to date with content. She is easily accessible outside of class, so I highly recommend going because hearing the answers to both your questions as well as those of others boosts your content knowledge. Her exams are extremely in depth compared to her quizzes so be ready.

The lectures may seem simple enough to understand, but always read the textbook as she will ask specific questions on quizzes and tests that won't always come from the PowerPoints. And make sure your phone is silent and away, because she WILL call you out on it in lectures. Overall this is a weed-out course so be prepared to work for your major.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take her class in your first semester of college because you will struggle and need to learn how to study. As a person, she is super sweet, but make sure never to take pictures in her class or she will get furious. Her exams are very difficult and she expects you to know every detail. If you don't sleep next to your textbook you won't pass.

This is 100% a weed-out course. If you don't live, eat, and breathe biology you are going to fail. The quizzes aren't horrible but the tests are BRUTAL and makeup 85% of your grade. Dr. Luque is extremely intelligent and if you aren't on the same level as her you will feel incredibly stupid for asking any questions. SOS avoid at all costs!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I withdrew from this class...I even changed my major! Though it wasn't because of the class. This class is difficult. Be prepared to read. Please pay attention to lectures and DON'T AVOID office hours!!! A big portion of the class are exams, then follow quizzes, homework, and participation. Dr. Luque is nice, but sometimes would give smart remarks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Weed out class, switched my major after this, don't ask questions in this class...

Dr. Luque is obnoxiously challenging. She will smash your confidence into a million pieces, which is awful since she teaches a beginner biology course. Her exams and quizzes are multiple online choices, and you can only see one question at a time without going back. I was failing her class, dropped and will be taking it elsewhere over the summer.

If you cant does multiple-choice, that's all her course is. I failed the first 2 exams and decided to drop out from taking 3 stem courses. Taking this class elsewhere. If you don't know the material perfectly memorized, you won't succeed. I went to office hrs every time offered and still got bad grades, she is rude if you call her out on anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Expects you to learn everything the day of and if you ask a question she will ask you the same question or if you get it wrong she makes you feel dumb and embarrassed. Exams and quizzes are very wordy and are meant to throw you off guard. She is great at teaching the class but teaches at a very fast pace.

I took Luque my 1st semester and its 100% a weedout class. I had to drop this class bc I had a low F by the drop date. If youre taking both Chem and Bio at the same time DROP BIO! I was advised to drop Chem and stay in Bioso I didonly to drop Bio too bc I was failing. Advisors DONT help one bit! Taking her class somewhere else. DONT GIVE UP!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Confidence shredder

Dr. Luque is an amazing professor who gives students a challenge but also gives them all tools for success. If you are prepared before lectures, her lectures are extremely helpful and you will learn a lot over the semester. This class is very difficult, but so is the entire pre-med track; Dr. Luque will teach you so much and you'll learn fast.

Is a good prof but expects a lot. 5 exams (20 ?s total mixed with 1 essay, a few fill in black & rest multi )&12 quizzes (both lockdown & webcam) 1 research paper final is cumulative. If u follow along in class & take good notes u will succeed. At end of each PP she ask can u do this & has 5-10 ?s about that lecture which is used for the exam

I never write reviews for professors but Dr. Luque does not deserve to be a professor. She deserves to be fired. She tells you to ask questions but does not answer them and calls you stupid for not understanding. She refused to follow accommodations. TCU needs to fire her or they will lose students! She is one scary professor and doesn’t care!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class will push you to your limits. The amount of learning is insane however Dr. Luque will help you through every step as long as you ask. Tutoring and office hours should be used weekly so you stay on top of material and never fall behind. This is a weeding course and Bio 2 will be way easier.

This class is a weed out class, so it may seem harder than most. Dr. Luque in lecture can be very intimidating, but she is very nice and approachable during office hours. She doesn't have many office hours, so do take advantage of them. She expects you to ask questions in lecture, so even if its clarifying something, DO IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I transferred here with a 4.0 and her class completely crushed my GPA. She makes it difficult to get any accommodations and is extremely rude about personal situations. Her goal is to make sure you're dropping her class and she brags about how poorly her students do. If you don't eat, breathe, and sleep biology you're not going to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you have any confidence, she will crush it. I never asked a single question because she is terrifying, after observing her responses to others and how she made them look stupid. I studied so hard for her exams but they are extremely hard. If youre a bio major dont give up on bio because of her class.

I have never felt so defeated until taking this class. I am quite literally TERRIFIED to ask questions in class and don't even get me started on answering her questions. almost 100% of your grade is based off of the 5 tests which are stupid hard. I have put more hours into this class and consistently do not see any progress. SOS AVOID HER!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Luque teaches a VERY tough class. That being said she is incredibly kind and truly cares about her students. She makes her rules and expectations clear in the syllabus, don't try to challenge them. Try to NEVER miss class and going to office hours and asking questions will be your best friend. She is very intimidating the first week but is amazing
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is a weed out class. Don't take endless you're 100% committed to study, read, ask questions, and apply the learning. You will be pushed. Dr. Luque is very serious about retaining the information and applying it to every quiz and exam. She can be very harsh and will make you feel like you are inadequate, but ultimately wants you to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Have a question during lecture? Don't ask. She will just try to make you look stupid in front of the class by asking you another question instead of answering your original question.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Luque has been the worst professor I have ever had. Her questions on tests and exams are not only confusing and have grammar issues, but the questions are meant to trick and confuse you. She thinks you'll understand something after she says it only one time and gives you attitude if you ask a question during lecture. She is absolutely horrible.

You've never studied hard until you've taken this class, it truly makes you feel like you know nothing. Extremely intimidating person but is really nice at her office hours, her tests and quizzes are insanely detailed and if you don't put in the work super early on in the course, you will not be able to recover. Go to class and ASK QUESTIONS!!

Dr. Luque cares about her students but expects the most. This was my second time taking the class and still never studied more in my life. Took it after ochem which helped. Don't take it with any other hard classes as studying and memorization is a lot. She does drop a lot of the lowest things, but staying above average on exams is most important.

This is now my second time taking Bio I, and I still hate it. RE-LISTEN TO LECTURES TO STUDY! The class is incredibly hard and the test questions are meant to trick you. If you go to her office hours she will love you. Don't ask obvious questions during lecture or she will roast you. She is extremely unforgiving and is often malicious in email.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Luque truly cares about her students and is willing to help. She is very intimidating in lecture, but much nicer in office hours. The class content was extremely hard, and I got an A in AP Bio. The class content was killer, and only graded of 4 tests given during the semester. If you're a bio major, take Luque because she be great help
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class was the hardest thing ever when I first took it. I had to drop it and retake, but I ended up getting an A. It was the most useful class I've taken thus far, because it made me learn how to study and it worked. Study early (like right after lecture) and keep reviewing. If you're a freshman pre-med, don't give up. Keep trying!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Okay listen any incoming pre med that is serious about being a doctor you will have to put in more work than the vast majority of other college students. Im convinced anybody is capable of getting an A in this class IF you are willing to truly work for it (and i mean really work). Listen to the recorded lectures after class and know them by heart

Dr. Luque may come off as harsh, but she is actually an amazing person who really cares about her students. Put forth the effort and she'll put in the time to help you. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. They'll help you learn material you didn't realize you didn't know and get to know her better. Her tests are definitely hard, so find your way to study early!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best Professor I have ever had. By attending office hours she will not only go out of her way to help you understand the material discussed in lecture but she will learn your name immediately and constantly give advice on how to study more effectively. Don't get me wrong she makes the class very challenging which isn't a bad thing. Study everyday.

So basically if your looking for any type of social life this is not the class for you. I went in full force while also wanting to have a good experience in college and unless you have time to study for this class for 2-3 hours every day and also be able to manage other classes, you will not get upwards of a B. If you do take it, GO TO OFFICE HOURS
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: definitely a weed out class for pre-med kids! very sarcastic with her answers but very willing to answer any question and help as much as she can. lectures are recorded and posted online but attendance is mandatory for daily grades! book is not used, everything you need to know is in her lectures. biggest tip:STUDY THE MATERIAL AFTER EVER LECTURE
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I got a 3 on AP Bio and an A in this class, so the two aren't related. Don't read the book, study her lectures (recorded) WORD FOR WORD. Understand every part of what she says and why, be able to write it out for yourself from memory. This class is a test of how committed you are to remembering the little details not how smart you are.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I was a straight a student in high school with all AP credits and I barely passed her class. I'd wanted to be a doctor for years until her class. I studied at least 10 hours for each exam and 40 hours for the final. Sweet person but she also killed my dreams. Premed kids: take more than 13 hrs even though you get told differently at orientation.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Luque has been one of the best professors I have ever taken, She will go out of her way to make sure you understand the material as long as you are putting effort on it. make sure you read her syllabus! Your attendance matters, if you skip a class you will fall behind. She cares about her students, would totally take her again!

Something I wish I would have known: don't waste time reading the textbook. Go over the slides MULTIPLE TIMES before each test and pay attention in lecture. Also, go to the free tutoring that is offered!!! Luque is a great person, but her course is very challenging. It is a weed out course, so beware.

This class is hard, but not as impossible as people make it out to be. Don't study the textbook for the tests because all of the content comes from lecture. If you know the content covered in the lectures backwards and forwards you should do fine. Your grade is almost entirely dependent on your test grades so make sure to study.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Luque can be strict but she really cares for her students. I thought she was a great teacher but this class was HARD. I studied for weeks for the tests and normally got in the B range. Beware of the 2nd Metabolism test- it killed my grade. 3 point curve.

The exams are extremely difficult. I would always go in feeling prepared, but the exam questions are confusing and it is hard to make an A. She does not mention the curve until the very end of the semester. She is kind in office hours. Get ready to study a TON and do not expect an A.
The most unfair class I have ever taken. She doesn't even make her own exam questions. Clearly a weed-out class. All I can say is good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I like luque, she clearly cares about her students but this class is truly insane. It is so clearly a class meant to push pre med kids out of the program. If you take Bio 1 with her you will spend your whole first semester in tears and not enjoying TCU one bit. Never miss one day of studying. It will set you back more than you can believe.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Luque is so sweet, and she really cares about her student's success. Biology is a difficult class, but if you go to class, and don't study the night before a test, you can definitely be successful. I never really used my book, but you need to purchase an online access code for the online text book because there are many activities done online.

Dr. Luque is one of the most personable professor's I have ever had, but she also teaches one of the hardest subjects I've ever taken. That being said, she expects a lot out of her students. She is a weed out professor and that isn't a bad thing; she is helping figure out if you are actually passionate about the path you are pursuing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Luque is such a sweet professor and extremely knowledgeable and helpful! Intro Bio is incredibly difficult by design at TCU, so be prepared to study like crazy. I purchased a second textbook from a different publisher/author to make sure I hit the material from a different angle. I would take her again in a heartbeat (for another class!)

Very difficult class and you must study a ridiculous amount for every test. Re-listen to all lectures because every question is talked about in class, but don't bother reading. Go to the review sessions and be prepared for all-nighters before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Luque is not mean, but very strict. She serves as a weed-out teacher to see which students can handle the work-load of Pre-Med, and is very good at it! She has informative lectures, and requires lots of reading. For first-year Bio/Chem/Biochem students, she is a requirement. Get to know her in office hours, and she will help you!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: nice professor, but you will cry in this class
Go to office hours! Pay attention during class, she'll call you out if you're on your phone the whole time. Be prepared to get an F on at least one test.

She is not as hard as everyone makes it sound like. No need to read every chapter but do read if you're not understanding what she's talking about. Go into her office hours and have specific questions ready to ask because she doesn't explain things just because. She usually curves at least 4 but don't depend on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tons of material and tests are tough- it's her confusing wording and answers that make it so difficult. She can seem condescending in lecture but is pretty nice outside of class. She says don't memorize but you'll have to memorize a ton for tests. It's hard but definitely possible to make a good grade w/ LOTS of studying and good testing skills.

My biggest complaint is that her office hours are very limited. She is a very knowledgable, although she can be sassy sometimes, she is usually very nice and helpful in office hours. Tests are rather tricky but are not impossible. Don't obsess over reading and MindTap (only read for further clarification); study the past quizzes and her lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Luque is a great person. She is really nice and really wants her students to do well. That being said, this class is by no means easy. Do not be deceived by the time between exams. Study often and daily because the lectures are heavy in content. Second exam on Metabolism is the hardest. Use office hours, especially before the exam.

This class is extremely difficult. It requires constant studying, even if there isn't a test coming up. Despite what some say, I think Dr. Luque is a brilliant professor. With the right mindset, I think passing is more than possible. If you struggle, try taking it your sophomore year.

I would study for hours every night, listen to every lecture and read every chapter in the book and always go in for tutoring. It didn't help at all. People smarter than I am did worse and unless you are prepared for a lot of all nighters then don't even bother taking this class because it will suck the life out of you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Luque has VERY hard exams, even if you study. 4th exam easiest. 3rd exam hardest. MindTap is a joke, literally all you need the book for. All based on lecture and notes but you have clicker points so you have to attend. Her exams are hell and very abstract. Don't take this if you're not a science major...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures were relevant to the tests and interesting. I recommend getting Campbell Biology regardless of what the syllabus states. I think she is more comfortable drawing from Campbell material and her quizzes reflect that. Answers questions, emails, seems caring. Also intimidating and demands respect. Great professor in my opinion. Study!!!!

If you have to take her, here are my tips. Sit at the front and pay attention. Do not, for the love of good, let your phone or computer make a noise. Tests are lecture based, textbook is good for reiterating information. Make an appointment with her before the test to ask questions, she is very kind 1 on 1. Study EVERY day. And, you'll get a C...

She is literally the worst professor at TCU. I was able to pass every other science class except hers which makes no sense. Her test are so hard no matter how much you study. The answer choices are basically all the same but one is slightly better than the other. Avoid her, her class, take bio somewhere else until TCU lets her go

reviews.comment: I love this woman. She helped me get into med school and so much more in life. She's incredibly smart, and determined to help her students. Not clear during lecture, barely accessible outside the classroom, kind of rude/condescending when you ask her questions. I had an A in cell bio (first A in a biology class) until her second test. reviews.comment: Unless you've taken lots of Bio, you'll have to put a lot of effort in to do well. Her tests are mostly application problems of what's being taught so you must know it well. reviews.comment: Luque is very smart and engaging and her lectures are helpful.  But,  I recommend not taking it unless you have to due to the fact that her tests are incredibly difficult. reviews.comment: Difficult class but doable if you actually study. Homework every single night, weekly quizzes, tests are difficult. She expects you to know things.
