She has random pop quizzes so attendance matters, but if you do the reading they're very easy! Definitely recommend taking this class!!

One of my favorite professors. She does give pop quizzes but they are really easy and based only on a loose understanding of the reading. This class was one of my favorite classes and I learned so much and actually had fun in class.

Vartabedian is an awesome teacher; she's fun and intelligent. The class is mostly discussions and some powerpoints. We get study guides before the midterm and final and it isn't hard to do well if you read the readings and go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at TCU thus far! Her class was so engaging, and it is clear that she is passionate and knowledgable about what she is teaching. 2 tests (midterm and final) that she gives study guides and an in class review for. Group project at the end, but she grades clearly and pretty easy. An A is easily attainable. Would take again!

Difficult to get a hold of, I sent emails that he took several days to reply to, course ended and he still hasn't replied to one I sent before, feels like he didn't care much. His feedback felt very copy and paste, lacks compassion.

Mr. Vogel is a very nice man but is not organized. One good thing is he is a very easy grader and the quizzes are questions you will see on the test. He is not very clear about when things are due and the lectures are very boring, most of the time I find myself not knowing how to do projects or when they are due. But, it is easy to get an A.

really boring class, but quizzes every so often. they are done in a group or open note. everyone thinks it is a blow off class but you need to study for his tests. projects are a waste of time but can change your grade tremendously. funny guy.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Vogel is very kind and is a pretty easy grader. However, he does not keep you updated on when things are due. The quizzes are usually done in groups but when you get to the tests and projects, everyone is confused because we feel like we haven't learned anything.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I wouldnt say best class ever. Interesting guy and  online discussions are easy, only two tests, but he had a paper. Talked about dropping the paper in the next class, so maybe it will not be a factor but i had to work on mine for about 10 hours.  I will probably get an A.

Daniel Vogel is a very gentle mannered teacher and is very helpful. While I do agree that the online work is busy work, it prevents you from writing an 11 page paper at the end of the semester. He is very understanding, tests are simple, comprising of questions from daily quizzes. DEFINITELY take for a history credit.

Vogel's class is strange. The first test is ridiculously hard and results in low scoring for most students. The second test is take-home, so it's easier. Online discussions are busy-work, but easy grade boosters. However, he does not answer emails...he can be frustrating to work with. A good option, but probably better professors out there.
Nice guy, I learned a lot. Online crap was dumb, but overall in class he was funny and knowledgeable. I bugged him a ton after class, he probably hates me but I got an A.
Class is super easy. Barely paid attention. Study vocab and the questions for the test and its cake.

Professor Vogel is awesome. He is a really nice guy and he knows a lot about history. His class can be a bit boring at times and there is a lot of homework but in the end it's worth it because he grades pretty easily and he really is a very lenient professor who wants everyone to do well. I highly suggest taking him if you need the credit.

I took this thinking it would be an easy A but boy was I wrong. There are two kinds of test,  a map test and then your four exams. Once you figure out how to study for map tests they're a breeze but the exams are what get you. I studied extremely hard for the exams and still got a C on every single one. Had to use one of my P/NC for this class.

I really liked his class. The map quizzes can be a little challenging, but if you study, they're definitely manageable. The tests are easier if you pay attention during lectures. I'd also recommend studying the vocab terms heavily before tests. He also offers a good amount of extra credit.
Map tests are HARD, and so are exams. If you're looking for an easy credit, look away. Its possible to get a good grade but lots of effort needs to be put in for an elective.

if you take this class get ready to STUDY STUDY STUDY...I took this as a core and hated every second of it...it wasn't THAT hard but I dedicated so much time to studying/memorizing. Professor Tillman thinks everyone is a geographer major and can devote hours to his class but he's nice ig.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was a class I took only to satisfy a core requirement, but compared to my other classes that semester, it was on the easier side. If you connect the dots between the key terms, lecture study guides and the book, you'll do fine. With that being said, I didn't do that and ended up with a B. Do not buy the map test packet. It's all online on D2L
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: LOVE HIM! He was so passionate about geography, always started class with a dad joke, and offered so much extra credit. We had 1 in class essay, 5 map quizzes, and 4 tests. It is very straightforward and he gives you so many tools to succeed. The final is not cumulative, just test #4. ppl complaining abt him are prob COMM majors, it was not hard

He is very nice, but it's way too much for a class that most people take as an elective, the department complains that they have very few geography majors and then there is Tillman making everyone think geography requires more effort than stem, you will be expected to know every country and capital as well as rivers, lakes, of the whole world.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Avoid at all cost. Hardest core class I've taken at TCU. Not worth your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am a geography minor and am taking an upper level geography class at the same time where i have over 100%, and i have a 87 in this bums class. there is absolutely no structure, his powerpoints are terrible, his exams are worded ambiguously and impossible to understand. nice guy but extremely unhelpful and needs to find a new profession.

If you think this will be an easy A where you just pull up to class and take the quiz and test your wrong. This class is stupid hard for no reason. The test material is completely different from what is presented in class. Don't take.
Oh my goodness... He is a great guy but this is WAAAAAAY too much work for a core class. Put more time into this class than any of my others. Still ended up with a dang C.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Boring lectures. 4 Exams and 5 Map tests that are very content-heavy.

Nice guy, interesting lectures, but expects way too much for a core class. Map tests are pretty straight forward, but exams require lots of preparation and include questions on the most minor details. If you really apply yourself and put the work in you'll probably be fine, but not the easiest A out there.

Dr. Tillman is a really nice guy who has a very clear love for what he teaches. The map quizzes are a lot to memorize, and the exams do require some studying beforehand, but as long as you put effort into the class you should be ok. Definitely some easier core credits out there if you're looking for an easy credit.

Tillman is a great guy BUT its way too much work for a core. The content itself isn't hard, but you have to take both map tests and regular tests that have tons of information on it and you have to memorize all of the stuff at least 5 days in advance. Also, his "extra credit" for each test takes hours to complete but is only worth 3 points.

Such a cool dude, but map tests are so much memorizing and exams don't relate to majority of his lectures. Don't take this class with him unless you want to spend your whole life studying geography. It's possible to get an A, but if you have a life you will get a C.

He is a very nice professor and is very helpful and gives clear directions. He does map tests which are a lot of memorization and information at one time. The tests are very difficult and it mostly covers all of his lectures so must take good notes to pass. One essay that is very easy if you know what its over. Lots of extra credit opportunities!!

Professor Tillman is a great professor. He keeps lectures very interesting but it is mandatory to pay attention and follow along. He also provides great study guides which help a lot when it comes to studying for exams. Overall, take him! He will always be more than happy to help during office hours and replies to emails relatively quickly.

Excellent professor! Offers extra credit for map tests and exams that will boost your grade by a full letter. Doing the extra credit will also prepare you for these exams, free points for studying! They will take time, but it will be worth it. Lectures are interesting, and Dr. Tillman is very kind! Loved having him for my first semester.

Tillman is a professor I would definitely take again! His lectures are entertaining and you can tell that he knows his stuff. He is always available to help his students no matter what. Definitely don't skip class because he doesn't post all of the lecture notes. His map test are difficult if you don't study way in advance, its a lot of memorizing.

Such a nice prof! He is so kind & genuinely cares about his students, as a professor i adore him BUT the class is unreasonably hard. The content on the tests is very difficult/confusing & timed (65 qs in 60 min). I was the only one in my class to get an A, and that was after hours and hours a week of studying & going through every single thing

Dr. Tillman is a very nice person. Come to class and he will explain what you will have on the test. Do the EC, it will boost your grade by a letter, also will prep you for test and map tests. You can buy one book for a group of friends, because it will only be useful for the extra credit (questions from which will be on the test).

Dr. Tillman is an awesome guy. GEOG 10003 was an absolute blast. I learned a lot of things about the world and he opens up a lot of interesting dialogues. Would take again for more geography courses but sadly I am graduating.

Tillman's a nice guy, but runs an ill-managed class. Runs off into tangents often during lectures, forcing you to the book for the specifics you'll need for the tests. There's a lot of useless writing assignments including a book review, all of which are graded by a TA. Not hard, but not fun or very thought provoking. Fair amount of busy work.

Tillman is a super nice prof and he wants you to do well. His class isnt that hard, lots of extra credit. Lectures are interesting but do not underestimate his tests. They arent super hard but they arent super easy either, definitely do the study guide. If you put in the effort you can get an A. Map test can really help your grade, easy 100.

Yeah don't take Tillman as a core requirement. I'm a junior finance major with a 4.0 throughout my first three years and this man singlehandedly messed that up. You have to be laser focused in his lectures because his powerpoints are uninformative, and he asked test questions over the dumbest small details. you have 9 total tests, so that sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof Tillman wants you to succeed in his class! He will always answer questions when you have them and his tests/quizzes are very straight forward. He is a goofy prof in the best way possible. His lectures are very helpful so I would try to make it to class when you can. One of the best profs I've had by far.

I'm in his world regional geography class. Tests are hard most of it is in textbook. A lot of extra credit opportunities + the map tests are easy if you put in the work. You will def get a B if you do all the extra credit, get mid to high C's on the exams and 100s on map test. Doesn't take attendance.

Tillman is a very nice guy and tells jokes before every class. If you study and fill out the study guides, you'll get a good grade. It's a relatively easy class and you won't fall behind if you miss class because he posts all lectures online. Overall, it's an easy class for core credit.

This course consists of 5 map tests worth 30 points, 3 exams worth 130 points, an in-class essay worth 50 points, and the final worth 160 points. He practically rewards you for studying because the completed maps and key terms are your extra credit which is 45 points. DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE HIS TEST. He is very nice, but his test are challenging.
Good teacher and very enthusiastic. Geography covers a lot of material so there is a good bit of studying to do but there are lots of opportunities for extra credit! Test are tough.

Much harder than I thought it would be. I heard other geography teachers are easier. Map quizzes are easy but the exams are very hard. It took a lot of reading and studying. He was helpful during office hours.

Overall an average class. Felt like he didn't do enough to prepare you for the tests that would ask oddly specific questions. Make sure you attend and pay attention to his lectures, its where a lot of information comes from. Offers a lot of extra credit. Study had for map tests, easy 100 if you know them well. Extra credit is easy and worth it.

Lectures are strictly powerpoints that he uploads onto eCollege. Kind of boring. You should take notes and follow along with powerpoint. 4 exams (multiple choice), 5 easy map tests (multiple choice), 1 short in-class essay. Doesn't take attendance. If you work for it, you will get an A.

Dr. Tillman is very approachable and helpful. If you go to his office hours, he will take the time to explain anything. Grades are based off map quizzes and tests. For each map you can label a couple of maps and it will count towards extra credit. The extra credit for the tests (MC), is longer but really helpful to study. PowerPs with each lecture.
Studied for 4 days for the exam and finally got a C

The only grades you will have are for exams, map tests, and one in-class essay, but you are given the opportunity to get so much extra credit, and the extra credit is basically just doing a study guide. Professor Tillman is so nice, and seems kind of like a funny older uncle. You just kind of have to love him. He is easily accessible for help.

Had him for world regional geography. Such an easy class! Lots of tests but they're pretty easy if you study some. Every test has extra credit you can turn in with it for 3 or 4 extra points. Lectures are boring but you don't have to pay much attention to them.
Tillman is really nice. His exams & tests require lots of studying. If you don't study you're not going to do well.
I felt that this should be an exciting class and it was not. It was also a writing emphasis and I felt it did not improve my writing. Tillman is kind, but needs to readjust this class.

Not great. Tillman is very unclear and the tests are needlessly tedious. If you aren't good at memorizing a lot of terms and places, you won't do well. Expect to spend more time than feasible trying to study. Would've taken a different class with a different professor if I could go back. Tillman is a good guy but the class is needlessly difficult.
Dr. Tillman is awesome! Lots of extra credit opportunities. Study guides are available on the first week of class for all exams during the semester. Very consistent. Great class.

A needlessly tedious class in terms of map tests. Thankfully, I can memorize things relatively easily. You will have to memorize a geographic region every 2-3 weeks and be tested on only a portion of it. Tests consist of some notes from lectures and random facts from the book. I could have taken something else and received an A.
Tillman is genuine, nice and easy to relate to. My favorite professor of all time, very understanding and laid back.

Dr. Tillman is an excellent professor. He was generally friendly and open to questions. The class itself was fairly easy -- I never actually studied besides doing the extra credit and got an A. By all means do the extra credit, it not only provides a few extra points it also prepares you for the exams.
Dr. Tillman is a wonderful educator. He is passionate about Geography and its contagious! Great class but you will need to keep up with the readings and go to class to do well.
Lots of chances for extra credit, lots of quizzes and tests. Gives a study guide before each exam and map quizzes are pure memorization. Cool guy, laid-back class. Highly recommend.

Tillman is awesome!! He's such a laid back prof and taught in a really interesting way that helped me learn. There are a lot of grades for the class and it's not difficult to get an A if you keep up and study hard. He's a really nice and helpful guy, I would definitely recommend him!
Dr. Tillman is awesome! His class is difficult but I learned a lot. Tests are a bit tricky but an A is possible with lots of studying.

I love Dr. Tillman- he is so funny. His class is pretty easy and he gives lots of extra credit opportunities. The tests can be a little tricky- so study for them! But if you put in the effort I think it is a fairly easy A. Take him!

Easy assignments, fun class, dorky teacher, yet you may take it for granted that you can make an A and NOT study and then you would have let a great opportunity go. No extra credit, but the assignments are fun and you put extra effort in you should make an easy A. Go to class, because he announces things you need to know. Fun, interesting class.

Very enthusiastic guy, I learned a lot.  Lots of extra credit -- do it all, it's just to prepare for the tests, it's better for you anyway.  If you pay any attention, take notes, and do the extra credit, you're golden.  Pretty straightforward. ;)  Tests are pretty simple, one question's answer option was "Islands don't have sides!"  See, humor!
fun teacher, alot of reading, and test.  he gives you study guides and extra credit...do not take in 3 week mini...too much stuff to know, but regular symester he is probably an easy "B"

Great easy UCR!  Very easy if you pay ANY attention.  All multiple choice tests.  Map tests a little harder b/c maps are unclear sometimes, but not that bad.  Lots of extra credit.  Only complaint-the regions he doesn't care much about he kind of skims over (i.e. everywhere outside the Western world and Latin America), but overall, great class!!!

Map tests are easy if you study but the tests can get kinda tricky. Plenty of extra credit, do all of it! He tells stupid jokes and is a little overenthusiastic about geography, but its not awful. He teaches in a variety of ways, helps students of all learning types!
Nice guy, but if you are not good at multiple choice tests then don't take this class.

This is an easy class as long as you pay attention and do the key terms. Map tests can be a little time consuming to prepare for but aren't hard by any means. Offers lots of extra credit and if you do it the class is an easy A. Dr. Tillman is a little crazy but overall a good guy =D
I think his teaching methods are kind of boring, but he's a great guy. The class is fairly easy. If you study the study guides, you'll do well on the tests. Plus, lots of extra credit opportunities.

"It's a great day for geography!"  Tillman is awesome. Class isn't boring at all, even at 9am. Maps are only on quizzes and aren't on the tests. You can tell what parts of lecture will be on the test but everything he talks about is interesting. Final is not comprehensive. Reccomended to my friend

This guy is a great teacher! Interesting, upbeat, and will not give you tons of work. Study for the tests, though. They're not as easy as you would think. Take notes, make flashcards, go to class.. you'll be fine!

Dr. Tillman is a really nice professor. I wouldn't say his class is really easy, you definitely have to study, but it is possible to make an A without too much effort. His tests are somewhat difficult, but he offers alot of extra credit points!
was really really nice and helpful

An absolutely awesome teacher. His only goal is to help you learn!!!  Not on any kind of power trip like most professors. His class was a complete joy and if he wasn't my professor ,I know he would be a great friend!!!!!
very cool professor, nice guy, doesnt overload you, but you learn a lot...not a jerk which seems to be a rarity sometimes at TCU
do not recommend

It is hard to keep up with the pace of his lectures. He does not engage the class and treats questions like unnecessary interruptions. He assigned way too much work without helpful feedback. He was a lenient grader though. I made an A because I'm good at math, but I am not sure if I really learned from this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Mihov lecturers in a way that terrifies the entire class. He really wants students to participate in class so do not make eye contact unless you want to be cold called on. I went into his office hours and came out more confused than before. Other professors at TCU are easier for Financial Management.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The Wednesday before finals he assigned a group project final presentation due in one week. Obviously it is extremely difficult to coordinate plans to do the project and practice presenting when people have other finals. Overall, he talks in broad concepts and scoffs at questions from students. If you can take anyone else, do it.

If you love finance, and I mean love finance -- you will do just fine in this class. If you do not, I can see why this class is hard. Mihov is very nice and caring, but he does not sugarcoat things. You have to participate and practice problems in the book to have a firm understanding. Overall, I enjoyed this class and Mihov. NPV!
Professor Mihov is a nice guy, but he assigned an insane amount of homework (all difficult and took hours to complete) and is difficult to understand with his accent.

I don't understand why they keep this professor around. He grades participation at complete random. And his class lectures are completely irrelevant to the tests. Do not take him if you have the choice.

This guy has no idea how to teach undergrads. He mainly teaches grad students and even said, "I failed my grad students as a teacher because the average on their first exam was a 60, but it'll be much easier for you guys." The average was a 66. Don't take him until he learns how to teach bc no one understood any of his lectures. Nice guy though.

He only talks of lofty ideas and not the basics that you should be taught in a intro class. You really have to teach yourself the material. Also, he makes you pay for a lot of the case studies you go over in class rather than using the cases in the textbook. He is a great guy, but he has trouble translating finance to people who do not know it.

Mihov normally teaches MBA students, so he has a hard time communicating simple ideas to intro finance students. He assumes we should all know things that we don't know and gets mad when people are confused. However, he is a nice guy.
Hard as can be. way too smart for his own good. Not very helpful with questions. However, very kind and goofy guy.
Helpful, good, smart, encouraging, funny

Generally, if you are a finance major you will be fine with the class; if you are not, you will be confused. Everyone does fine (We had mostly As, some Bs) He's challenging, only 2 exams.  Take the time to do well on homework projects and participate a little in class and you will be fine. Final is harder so do well on the midterm which is easier.
A really nice guy and willing to help as long as you show up for most of his classes. Participate, and try to answer his questions in class and you'll be fine.
Rude, obnoxious and condescending.  He always seemed highly annoyed to get questions from students.  Very disappointing as I had hoped to get alot from the class!!!

Class is okay, a little boring and tough to keep up.  I got the feeling that he was more interested in proving how smart he was than teaching us.  Spent way too much time on theory and not enough on application.  He is very smart, but a poor prof - especially for a class this crucial.  Study the old exams that he gives you and you should do well.

Rating below that says class was to hard should not be at TCU. This class was a joke.  If you actually want to learn something avoid this class at all cost. I covered the entire book in undergrad, Vassil only covered 50% in graduate school.
No Comments
Relates well to students and works hard to help students understand.
He tries to be a good teacher, but he forgets that he is teaching undergraduates and not graduates!

I love Dr. Vanbeber. She is very easygoing, little no homework, take home quizzes, and I believe there was 3 exams. She is funny and makes class  interesting and straightforward. I really enjoy her class.

Dr. V is amazing and cares a lot. If you have a question she doesn't know, she will say so and get back to you with an answer. Sometimes, she gets a bit off track or disorganized during lectures, but she gets everything necessary done. Do the D2L review questions before exams and you'll be fine. The final exam is much harder than the rest of them.

I love Dr. V. Her lectures and labs are engaging and her passion for the material makes it so easy to follow along. Sometimes she rambles on and can be a little unorganized, but it didn't affect my grade, so I can't complain lol!
Dr V is easily my favorite professor at TCU! She cares about each and every student and will talk to you about anything you need. Do your lab reports and study for the test and you will make an A.
This class is easy, just a few exams and 2 reading assignments. The tests are not difficult but they do require studying for them.

I have had Dr. V for so many classes. She truly is an amazing person and professor. Dr. V is very caring and if you are ever struggling she will help you. I am not currently in this class but I had to leave her a review because she is awesome. Get ready to cook in her labs!

I truly can not express how amazing Dr. V is as a professor and an advisor! I took Food Prep with her and absolutely loved it. Attendance is mandatory, but there was never a time where I hated being in class. She is so sweet and caring! She is a stickler for due dates but that's the worst of it, I learned so much from her. 10/10 would recommend!
One of the nicest and caring professors ever. She is hilarious and has a lot of good stories. This class has a lab which is super fun but make sure you turn your lab in on time.

Dr. Vanbeber is amazing! Take her for every class you can! I took her last semester for Food & Culture and am taking her again this semester. She does take attendance daily and deducts from your final grade if you miss more than one class. You do eat A LOT in the class and just have to turn in sensory evaluations the next class period.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. V is the sweetest professor I had at TCU. Really cares about her students and she will try hard to make sure you pass her class. Plus all the food helps.

This class is super interesting and fun. You get to do tastings from food all around the world. Tests aren't hard and the only assignments are tasting responses. Definitely take this class. VanBeber is passionate and wants you to do well.
She is one of the best professors at this school so take her if you can
My favorite professor at TCU! She is extremely passionate about nutrition. I've taken several classes with her and she was great in each one.
She's nice and helpful. She is understanding and a fun person to sit and talk to. Her class can become a little boring at times, but its quite easy and straight forward. Highly recommend her.
No Comments

Labs are fun and there's so much yummy food! It was a big feast every time we had lab. Science concepts can be a little difficult to grasp, but not impossible. 3 exams, 12 lab reports, & 6 'pop' lab quizzes (w/lowest grade dropped). Lab reports & lab quizzes really help the overall grade. Nice teacher; wants you to do well in lecture and lab.
A totally fun class that I would recommend to anyone who has an interest in cooking!
very intelligent, but kind of a hard-ass when it comes to grading. other than that she's nice and wants students to do well/learn as much as they can.

Not only was this class amazing (so much good food)! VanBeber is a wonderful and loving teacher. She really taught us a lot of relevant information about cooking that will be very helpful in the future. This class is only for seniors.
very very good

Amazing professor overall! She is so caring, understanding, and kind to all her students. Just do the homework and practice exam reviews + past in-class problems to do good on exams. The second exam was the most difficult for most people I know (including me since I didn't even know how to answer the last question) so don't be discouraged by it.

If you're good at Finance, this class will be very easy with Traweek. If you struggle with finance, she will be very helpful outside of class for you. Very nice lady. Straightforward class. Probably the best professor you can take for Fin Man.

Traweek is a great professor. She clearly explains the material and is accessible outside of class. She makes a hard class manageable and wants her students to do well.  She is funny and smart. The grading criteria is clear, she is a fair grader and she does a great job of preparing you for the tests. I would take her again without question.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super caring professor who really wants you to do well. Go to class and you will be perfectly fine. She's also really good at letting you know what you need to study for the exam. Take her for Fin Man!!
Super chill and accessible. Study well and you will do fine. She is a great teacher.

Dr. Traweek makes finance understandable for people with little financial background. If you put a decent (not crazy) amount of effort, you will ace it. She welcomes questions and is very available beyond class. I probably won't take finance again cuz it's really not for me, but if I do, I'd take it with Dr. Traweek!
This is one of the best professors I have had at Neely. She explains material well and tells you what you need to study for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She doesn't take time explaining enough, goes really fast over the material and we have to constantly tell her to slow down. Needs to find balance between the time spent telling funny stories and actually taking the time to expand on the class material.
Will always help you
Good professor overall. She is fair enough, too
Best Professor in neeley and at tcu take her
She was awesome, she will do everything in her power to help you. Take Her !
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easily the best finance professor. Kind and caring, great at giving feedback. Class is hard but that how finance is no matter the professor, and she does everything she can to help her students learn the material. I mean she has a higher rate my professor than Matthew McConaughey for a reason.

She is easily one of the best professors in Neeley. I know that a lot of professors say that they care about your grade and well-being but I can tell she genuinely does. I would highly recommend for FinMan.
Take her she is fabulous!!!!

amazing professor! she gives a lot of partial credit on exams and prepares you well for them by telling you what you need to study. She tries to make the class engaging and overall would definitely recommend.
Professor Traweek is the best for this course!! She gives so much partial credit on exams and a review that provides clear expectations. She cares so much and truly wants her students to succeed.
Take this professor for Finanacial Managment!! She is hands down the best professor for this course and I would 100% take her class again.

She cares so much about her students and wants everyone to do well! She will provide you with everything you need to exams and she writes them all herself. The class isn't a super interesting one but she does her best to keep everyone engaged. Definitely take her if you can.
She is a great teacher and super knowledgeable. You get a formula sheet on every exam front and back which makes it easier.

One of the best professors I have had at TCU! Professor Traweek is so helpful and is always there to help students. She clearly outlines what is going to be on the exams and you allowed a full page of notes front and back for each exam.

Professor Traweek is one of my favorite professors! She is always available to help me when I am struggling in class and is very good at teaching. She also tries to make respectful relationships with her students and I love this! She also did a very VERY good job working with my accommodations!!

Not many assignments just one quiz every week about readings (open note) and a midterm plus final which is all open note. One group presentation which is really straight forward. Dr. Vargas is lecture heavy so most classes is just her talking but if you want an easy religion class this is a good option.

I cannot recommend taking this class because of how boring it is. Vargas is a little easier than other religion professors but is probably the most uninteresting professor in the entire religion department. Very little is actually taught in this class that you can walk away with. I genuinely don't know what she is trying to leave her students with.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Vargas is great ! Group journals and quizzes have clear instructions. She tells you what to look for in the readings to prepare you for quizzes and class discussions. Just listen during lecture and do the reading questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I liked Professor Vargas, the class was super easy. Everything is open note, but still read the readings just so you know what's going on in class. I will say though that her lectures are super duper boring. Like  literally I would be doing something else or the same with other people like sleeping or other hw, but if you want an easy A, take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Professor Vargas and her class thoroughly. The class is very reading and lecture heavy with a quiz on the reading every Monday. There is a group presentation but you are allowed to read the slides off the screen and have notecards as well. There is a group journal once a week due on Sunday over the reading and the final is open note!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Vargas is a really nice person outside of the classroom but her class seems like it would be easy. There are not tests and all the readings are provided on D2L but she is very nitpicky in her grading. We asked her to look over one of our group assignments and she said it looked great but then still gave us points off.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Vargas is a great Professor that cares and grades easily as long as you participate. However the class is somewhat uninteresting and it is hard to stay involved in the class if you are not interested. Be prepared to do some legwork when it comes to reading every week
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Shes a good professor, weekly quizzes but there open-note. She is really strict on attendance but if youre sick she allows you to join on zoom. One midterm essay. One open note final (final is hard but if you do the study guide youre fine)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Vargas is a great professor! There was a weekly reading quiz and group entry, a small written midterm assignment, one wellbeing entry, and one cumulative (open-note) final. I enjoyed the different cultural perspectives she presented in class and that she presented information in an unbiased manner. I recommend taking this class with Dr. Vargas!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: The professor is very nice and understanding. You have 3 absents allowed and after that, it comes out of your grade. All quizzes are open note and there is one exam that is open note too. Definitely recommend this class and is a super easy religion credit.
Dr Vargas is a very kind and approachable professor, that being said this class was a slog. Lots of reading every week and then a quiz over it. Lectures are long and tedious.
Super easy, does not require attendence, exams are take home online and open note. This Man needs a raise.

Professor McGinney does a great job of explaining the material while also assigning just the right amount of work for a core class. The class was fun and entertaining, and he made everything so easy. I would totally take his class again!
love this guy, can't say enough good things.

honestly one of the easiest classes, barely had to do anything. most people never show up to class, and all tests were done outside of class (no lockdown, no recording). very lecture heavy, but honestly they were pretty interesting to me. if you're going to take any survey and don't care specifically what it is, take this class!

He really cares about the class, but it is one of those big, easy, lecture classes that you just can sit through mindlessly. Make sure to sign in to class, but he posts all slides online. Tests are take home, but he takes forever to grade anything.
Dr. McGinney was fine. I was in his Western Music History 1 class this semester. Lectures would really drag on and it was hard to pay attention, rather easy class though. Much better than Watkins.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally the freest class at TCU. He says attendance is mandatory, but I don't show up half the time and haven't gotten a deduction. However, when I am in class, you listen to music and notice his awesome hairstyle. He really loves music and will actually play some songs you will add to your playlist. Great guy and fun course, would 100% recommend

great guy, but lectures are just him talking at you so you have to be able to pay attention; cool class but not my favorite, he is a very caring prof but lectures are so messy and feel like they drag on a bit

Survey of Rock is super easy but all Professor McGinney does is lecture and his lectures can be really boring. The tests are all open note and you don't need the textbook. He didn't grade until grades were due which was annoying but overall the class was fine. He gives two skips and says attendance affects your grade but it doesn't.

Survey of Film Music is a breeze if you go to class and talk every now and then in class. The answers to quizzes and exams can be found on the internet, and all exams are take home too. The lectures can be boring sometimes, but Professor McGinney is nice and actually knew everyones names by the 3rd class. Only bad thing is he takes long to grade.

Professor McGinney's class was worth it! If you need a fine arts credit I highly recommend this class! All tests are open note outside of class, and there are a few short essays about a specific subject that are extremely easy. Overall this class was fun to go to, and it was not hard at all!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a nice professor, just boring lectures and takes FOREVER to grade even though he has a TA and the online tests are graded automatically. It is too difficult and too much work for a 100 level music class that everyone takes for a fine arts credit.

The class is very lecture heavy and the tests are surprisingly difficult. Twice the professor has done "pop quizzes" when not many people show up to class, even though we are allowed skips. Just a few essays and tests throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is a breeze, get the work done and you'll get an A. Attendance isn't mandatory but he gives all the quiz answers in class so it's worth going.
Unless you need this class for your major dont take it. She gives too much work for the small credit it gives.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: One of the nicest professors I have had at TCU as she really cares about the students. She is very passionate about the material and is corny sometimes and the lectures and documentaries can be boring. You have a reading quiz once every three classes with a not too hard midterm and final exam with a fairly easy interview project with a partner.

Dr.V teaches in a way that she wants your discussion to mimic her own thoughts. There is not much room for differing views from her own and you will feel like an outcast or like you are being penalized for your thoughts. Participation is very important in her course grading, so make sure to stay on her good side to get called on and be grade fairly
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. V is caring and respectful, and handles our more difficult discussions with grace. Cultural Anthropology has lots of different kinds of assignments to suit different students, including quizzes, an interview project, and an essay. Clear guiding criteria throughout and she is willing to answer questions and provide feedback. Would recommend!

I took this class for the double-dipping credit, but it was not worth it. This is one of the most difficult classes I have taken, which I was not expecting. The midterm and finals were extremely difficult and required a ton of studying. If anthropology is something you're passionate about, take this class. But don't take it just for core.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This was my most annoying class. The professor has good intentions, but she overcomplicated all her test questions, gives lots of homework, and lectures are long and tedious. There is a big group project that is extremely time-consuming at the busiest point in the semester. VERY detail-oriented and LOTS of material to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. V is so kind and considerate! There is a lot of reading, writing, and discussion involved but the content is enjoyable. I would 100% suggest taking a class from her if you enjoy this type of work, and she is flexible about due dates if you are upfront with her.

If you are a non-anthropology major or graduating senior looking for a blowoff class, RUN!!!! This class is the most reading-intensive class I have ever taken. Professor is a wonderful lady, probably the sweetest I've had, but the class is impossibly hard to keep up with. 40-50 pages of reading per night, tons of pop quizzes, difficult tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lisa purposely talks down to you and uses language that makes it so hard to learn. She also teaches from the point of view that she is teaching truth. and its not. she also expects you so absolutely love anthropology. I took this class because i thought it would be interesting and sort of easy. exact opposite.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This is a reading heavy class and requires a lot of writing. IT IS A WEM CLASS. The professor is very sweet and outside of class gives tons of feedback and help. She is very nice and respectful. I love her class because there is interesting material however newer material could be nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. V doesn't give constructive criticism on assignments, which makes it difficult to improve your grade. The class also only utilizes one or two sources from this century, which is odd for a class titled Mass Media and Culture. The class is also very repetitive in content and theme.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I owe my mental health to this woman. She gave me the inspiration to develop genuine care about cultural and social issues and prompted me to make changes in my personal life. It was a lot a work, but very do-able when managed right. I loved learning something new every single class and I cannot be more thankful for that feeling! Dr. V, you rock!

I love this woman. Every time I go to her class I feel like I'm getting on the magic school bus, b/c she reminds me of Ms. Frizzle. She makes the class so interesting. All you have to do is read the text book (which is really not that bad) to do well on the quizzes. The tests are straight from the readings and her lecture. 10/10 would recommend!!!!

Excellent professor!! The class was really engaging. Dr. V really knows how to make every part of the class interesting. You really need to read and take notes on the textbook, because you definitely have to work hard for a decent grade. Grades participation so make sure to speak up during discussion!

Best professor at TCU. She loves her job and her class is great. It's entertaining, not too hard, and she is incredibly helpful. I would recommend Vanderlinden to anyone interested in Anthropology or just taking it to get core reqs.
SHE IS AMAZING.. she made a class that would have been so boring with any other professor SO interesting. I looked forward to her class and would take it again instantly even though i got a C.

Awesome teacher! Challenges students to look at the world in a new way. Really invested in her classes and goes the extra mile expecting students to do so in return. My favorite class and teacher at TCU thus far!
Very nice, knowledgable, fun, interesting teacher. Very hard grading though. You have to work to get a B. Saying that, I would still take her if you can

She is so tough. Lots of reading and awful exams and quizes. She made an interesting class a boring one. Overall the way she taught was helpul, but the way she graded was too bad! Yet she is nice and I think individual meetings will help people who really want to get an A. Goodluck

Lisa is one of the few professors who reminds you that you aren't just in school to get a degree. I've learned so much in her class and would recommend her to anyone. She's passionate about her job and she truly cares about her students.
Love. Her. You will work hard for her, lots of reading and writing. So worth it. I would recommend this class to everyone.

Dr. Vanderlinden is an extremely interesting and intelligent person.  I had her for Sex, Gender, and Culture and the class was absolutely amazing. I learned about very important issues occurring in the world today.  She keeps class interesting and there is alot of discussion.  You will have to work fairly hard for an "A" but take the class anyways!

I had Dr. V for Intro to Cultural Anthropology and I really enjoyed the class. You will learn so much from her and she is a lovely and interesting person.  You will have to work VERY hard for an "A".  LOTS of reading and class discussion is required!!!  The tests are tricky,  but the quizzes are easy if you read.  The interview project is fun!

Dr. V is very passionate about anthropology and teaching. Engaging class with interesting materials-she is very smart and articulate.  Participation is expected, so you need to attend class and discuss. High expectations (hard quizzes!), but she is helpful and really nice.  Great class if you want to learn something.  You can make an A with work.

Dr. V is fantastic!  She is intelligent, enthusiastic, and will get you thinking about the world from a different perspective.  She is one of those profs who just loves to teach and she wants everyone involved.  You will have to  work hard, but it is worth it.

Dr. Vanderlinden is my favorite professor at TCU- and I'm not even an Anthro major.  Shes got to be one of the most intelligent, articulate, and kind people Ive ever met.  Intro and Mass Media are both very fun and stimulating- be ready to discuss! Plenty of reading, but its interesting so you'll NEVER be bored in her class!

Lisa is the strict yet nice teacher who keeps class interesting. Her quizes and tests are hard, but she gives reviews for the two tests. If you are an A or B student, it is possible to make the grade. Don't miss class because you'll miss a lot of important material. She's a very sweet lady.
If you do the reading it's pretty easy, she is so nice and helpful and I really enjoyed this class. I definately would take her again if I could!

Extremely articulate and intelligent woman--one of the best profs I've ever had here.  The class is discussion-based, so there's no tests to stress over.  Take this class and you'll never look at mass media the same way again.

Lisa is energetic and loves what she teaches.  READ READ READ, because shes tough on quiz grades.  Tests arent too bad, you only have a mid-term and final, and the stuff is interesting/unique so you should be able to recall lectures and films.

Class was good. She won an award for her teaching excellence. Very polite. Prob is her quizes are near impossible. I read and didn't read for those and there was no difference for the grades. She is very clear overall. Good experience.
i didn't like the class at all but she is a very sweet person.  She made things seems just a little more interesting
Extreemly interesting class. I loved going and learned all that I could. That wasnt reflected in my grade however cuz she's maniacle when it comes to that...and being fair.
interesting class. good professor. HARD TESTS. LOTS OF READING.
A lot of reading...some interesting and some mind-numbingly boring.  She's a good person but grades extremely hard on the interview project.  I got a unfair grade on mine for minor details.
tests were awful and there are only 2 and one very involved project worth 25% of ur grade.  usually weekly quizzes on readings.  I found it interesting and very hard and im an anthro major

awesome interesting class! shes very enthusiastic. there are teachers who just teach, and some like her who enjoy it. Prof V is super fun, even though the material may be tedious at times. half the readings are cool stories, just keep up. easy B-take it!

Lisa grades hard, and is unforgiving when differences of opinion arise. She'll ask for your opinion, but she really only wants to hear you parrot back what she thinks. If you don't think Freud is the end-all/be-all, don't bother.
There is lots of reading, but she's a good professor and you'll learn a lot about other cultures...it's much more interesting than I thought it would be
TOOOOOOO MUCH READING ASSIGNMENT BUT INTERESTING CLASS
She was extremely nice and i liked her a lot.  The class was very interesting and although a lot of reading, it was pretty easy and interesting.  Her tests were awful though!
Wonderful professor!  She is very nice and understanding.  The class is very interesting and not hard at all if you can keep up with the readings.

You have to read a chapter (or two, or three) each night, and it's thick reading.  She gives lots of pop quizzes, and the pop quizzes account for 20% of the grade.  Her tests aren't too bad, but you'll need to study and need to read...A LOT.

Do not take. If you do the homework and study 15 hours you would think it would be similar but it is NOT. She asks harder questions on exam then homework, and there are no reviews for the exam. She will show one problem during class and then expect you to know how to do it, and work the rest of class by yourself. Excel project took hours.

Sweet teacher and available to call at anytime on her days off. Exams are hard, but she had plenty of assignments to buff it out. She's relatable and understanding. Best professor I had this semester. Recommend.

Professor doesn't lecture, but works on practice problems during all classes. If you're fine on those, you won't be fine on the exams, because it is what we do in class * 100. You also don't have an exam or any grades until a month and a half into class, so no seeing how you do the first few weeks and then dropping and getting some kind of refund.
Never had a worse teacher at Neeley. Take someone else if possible

Was excited for this course, but was quite disappointed. Hard to reach outside of class and was not welcoming. Wood gives OK lectures and posts her slides.The personal stories were interesting, but often very little of the class was spent learning material or preparing for exams. TCU should have other professors available for Audit

Wood is a great teacher. Accounting is boring and not fun so its not a fun class but its easy enough. She is very adhd but I liked it because she goes off topic talking about her family and gives us a break from accounting.

At first I hated this class and felt it was disorganized, but halfway through the semester you get used to it. The test questions were way easier than the in class questions and accounting test prep practice, idk what people are on about. The first excel project sucks though.
Her exams are tough if you don't put in the work. She often spends most of class talking on topics other than the material. Hardly teaches and blows through slides extremely quick.

Honestly avoid her if possible. Nice lady (sometimes), loves to tell stories, but honestly a pretty terrible teacher. Class is like nails on a chalkboard and she's super passive aggresive and rude sometimes. Never gives a clear answer when you ask questions. The tests are pretty easy if you go to class and study the packet but hated every second.
She's a nice lady, but doesn't really teach the information. A lot of learning on your own for the tests
Took my review down lol. audit is hard w her, unorganized and test questions r so hard even if u study the study guide she gives.

Wood is such a nice lady, loves to tell stories. No required homework, just study the packets she gives in class for exams and quizzes. Tests are pretty simple but sometimes the wording throws you off, multiple choice q's sometimes come out of nowhere. Go to class, pay attention and study and you'll do fine.

Professor Wood is amazing!! She provides all of the materials and is super straight forward about what will be on the exams! She is very helpful and will let you attend different sections if it better suits your schedule. My only "negative" was her reliance on AccountingTestPrep which I did not find particularly helpful.
Prof Wood is one of the best professors I have had. She is great at teaching the material, cares about her students, provides extra credit for participation, etc. You should absolutely take her!

Dr. Woods is a great option for FR1. The first half of the class is just a review of fundamental ACCT. Knows every student by name. Class is not the easiest but FR1 is not easy. Most HW is optional. Just learn the packets you do in class and you will do good. Attendance required.

I LOVE Professor Wood. She is truly an amazing human. FR1 is a hard class and Professor Wood is aware of this, so she makes participation extra credit. You can get up to 25 points (3-4% of your grade). Her class takes studying, but if you do your homework before class and come in with a decent understanding, its bad. She is a great pick for FR1!!!

For audit she is pretty good. You do a memo/paper but she helps you prepare for the writing style she wants. She gives lots of handouts. The tests are some workout/short answer and some multiple choice CPA practice questions. There's a lot of assigned practice questions so do some each week so that its not overwhelming when you study for the tests.

I love prof wood! TBH im surprised her score is not a 5/5 because everyone loves her. Definitely recommend her class, I think the tests are fair and she gives out packets to study from which I love. No powerpoints all hands on work!

Professor Wood is very caring for her students! She knows her material and truly cares if her students learn. The course itself is hard but she makes a concerted effort to make it easier. Homework is not graded. Grades come from tests, quizzes and projects. She says prays for every student by name every night - and I believe it. Highly recommend!

She is the nicest lady in the world. If your good with getting on a teachers good sideand communicating with her you may be able to get an inside scoop on what will be tested and quizzed. She gets a bad rep but for FR1 take someone else. Stay away if you want weekly HW to help stay on top of the work. Reccomend someone else but she is really nice.

Gotta grind to do good like any FR1 class. Shes an awesome sweet person, but just isn't really a good teacher. Lot of packets that you work through for "HW" which she never checks (if you like 0 HW) but it was kinda tough to keep up with the work with packets you have 0 clue how to do. In fundamentals there was pearson to check work

I was able to do well in FR1 and I think Professor Wood is very caring, but I don't think that the lecture material was clearly conveyed well. The explanations given during the lecture didn't exactly help me. A vast majority of the learning in the class is using the accounting test prep and reviewing the homework packets.

one of very few professors where i felt like i could ask a question without feeling dumb. FR1 is not easy so a lot falls on the student to study, but I feel like her lectures could've been structured better to learn more in class. Lots of note taking and paper work

Laurie is a very nice lady. But shes scatterbrained and frequently made errors in her lectures which made the content more confusing than it needed to be. Tests are tricky but if you prepare properly they arent bad. If you come to class and participate the participation grade will raise you up if you have a bad test. Not bad but not great either.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: LOVE her class so much. Content is pretty confusing but she does a good job giving tests and quizzes based on the examples she provides in class. such a sweet person and never condescending when I asked dumb questions. no homework grade, but some quizzes and participation to soften the tests if you don't do as well.

Professor wood is one of the nicest teachers by far. If you pay attention, study, and ask for help you should be fine. Unless you're a natural accounting genius you will need to practice and study hard for the tests if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Laurie Wood is the best professor at TCU and is one of the kindest people I have ever met.

Mrs. Wood is a very sweet and caring professor. Shes a good choice to take for FR1, her tests can be a little tricky, but if you study well you will be rewarded. She does offer some extra credit so take advantage of it. Overall, good choice for Intermediate I.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Wood is extremely nice and fair. This class was lecture heavy and the grades consisted mostly of 3 quizzes and 2 tests (called mid terms) and a final. She was very willing to help me after class and wanted to help me succeed. The only problem I have is she is a bit unorganized. Overall this class is not super fun but she was a good option
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: By far one of the worst teachers I have ever had. You will only do well if you are able to teach yourself all of the information. She does NOT teach you.  Pointless stories of her home life is distracting and not helpful especially if you are struggling with the material. The online homework is very different compared to her Exams.

I loved Wood for accounting. I learned a lot and exams were in the same format as problems worked in class so you know what to expect. Some parts of her exams can be tricky but if you study and pay attention in class an A is achievable. She sometimes tells stories of her kids which adds a nice little break from focuses on so much accounting.

Tests are tough; if you don't study hard, you won't do well. Ms. Wood is very sweet and helpful, but you have to badger her via email to receive responses. Homework and tests can be tricky because Ms. Wood teaches differently than the textbook sometimes.

Literally the most useless teacher I've ever had. She's never once given a straight answer to a question. This is a problem because the wording on her testsassignments is so messed up that nobody is ever exactly sure what she is expecting. If you don't want to be frustrated on a daily basis, I would recommend taking just about any other professor.

She's a super nice and lovely lady. Her personality is very interesting, which also make the class kinda strange in a good way, which makes the class super interesting. Lectures are very clear and straightforward. Tests are based on what she covers in class and are pretty easy.

Ms. Wood's Accounting class is in a great format and is easy to understand. There is homework most nights, but it is helpful and she goes over it in class. She is always willing to help. Lowest test grade gets replaced with final grade if you score better.
Extremely helpful

Take her! There are homework assignments almost every class but if you do them they end up being grade boosters and really help you keep up with material. Tests are kind of hard but she provides plenty of practice probs. She is also really willing to help you and her stories are funny too

Course materials are too expensive. Already paying 20K a semester for tuition YET have to pay another couple hundred for access to online materials that aren't helpful! Too much material crammed into a semester. We didn't get our exams back after tests. How can you prepare for a cumulative final without prior tests? Class was a HUGE disappointment!

One of the absolute best professors I've had at TCU. Yes, you have to keep up with the work, but if you do, the tests are manageable. Ms. Wood is really helpful and sets the class up in the most interesting/manageable way given that most people don't like accounting. If you have to take accounting, take it with Ms. Wood.

Mrs. Wood is a great teacher! She is very helpful and uses examples that are easy to relate to in order to help students understand. She walks through problems with you before sending you off to do homework. Some homework is mandatory, however if you want to do well on tests and quizes (quizes are given randomly) then doing all the hw will help

Too much material for a class focused on minors. Very little time on each subject and extremely easy to get left behind. I feel like Mrs. Wood did her best with what was given though, she is the only one in the department who teaches 120+ students and makes time for you, IF you ask for it. Bad intro for business school. Tests are impossibly hard.

Really bothersome that they make so much $$ (use Cobb's txtbk AND website) off of us for materials that are NOT helpful. Poorly constructed. Random material will pop up that you haven't heard of and will be expected to know. Sweet teacher but terrible class.

Mrs. Wood is very sweet,but I had serious qualms with this class. The course materials are inconsistent! The book is teacher-made & is not helpful. The book does not follow a logical order & is confusing to use for studying. Also, you have to spend $ on an equally confusing website. Most of class you go over hmwk rather than learn next material.
Nicest lady I've met. It really is hard to stay awake because it is accounting, but she really tries hard to make class enjoyable. Her tests are very difficult, and there is a lot of homework.

I loved this class. I took accounting for fun (it was part of my minor and then I dropped the minor). She is so sweet and fun. She makes accounting very interesting and always tells good stories and brings neat stuff to class. Lots of extra credit. Do your homework and you can make an A easily. TAKE HER. Favorite professor of the semester.

Mrs. Wood is a very nice and caring professor. Accounting is not easy, but she tries her best for her students to understand. If you do the homework, the tests are alike. She will sometimes make them confusing which is my only complaint.

This class is hard for many people just because it is accounting, not because of the teacher. Wood will help you outside of class, even gives out her cell phone number. She gives lots of homework, and if you actually do it you won't have to study for the tests much. However you can copy the answers from online if you want.

Accounting for Minors. Class is challenging and you must go to class to do well, but Mrs. Woods is very helpful if you ask her for help. She tells you exactly what will be on the test. Plan on having homework almost every night.
The comment below is obviously Wood...
I thought I would hate accounting but because of the way ms wood taught, I liked it!

Seriously, people! Yes, accounting isn't the easiest, but its just formulas. You have to take this class, so suck it up and deal. At first, you think she's going to be terrible, but turns out she's not a meanie. LOTS of homework and checks it randomly. REALLY wants her students to do well.  Has a good heart, but won't bend the rules for anyone.

prepare to spend a lot of money.  website is a pain, especially if you have a mac. managerial section of website only works with internet explorer and that's if it actually is working (rarely does). tests suck so study as much as you can. she seems like a good accountant, just not able to communicate those skills well.

I had Mrs. Wood last semester for Financial Accounting and have her again this semester in Managerial because I absolutely love her!! She really is a helpful teacher and will do anything to help you make an A, she even says so! The class is really expensive however, you need all of the practice you can get from the website,etc. Highly recommend!!

prepare to spend a huge ammount of money. 2 learn books, online account (3 diff. payments) she doesnt teach so youll have to teach urself but the class isnt hard. you need to come to class and do online assignments. and A is possible but shes a bad teacher.

Dr. Wood does a good job teaching for an extremely tough subject. She cares about your success and is willing to help you outside of class. She'll sometimes tell jokes or stories in class to lighten the mood. Tests are difficult but accounting is a difficult subject. Go to class, study the material, and you should be able to pull a B.
Professor Wood doesn't really teach the material. If you are an accounting major, she doesn't help in preparing you for what is to come. Avoid if possible.

Laurie Wood is a good teacher. She cares about her students and does whatever she can to help them out. I didn't read unless she hinted that there would be a quiz next class. Just do practice problems until you understand what you're doing and get the right answers. I just studied the night before and received an A-.

Accounting is hard in general but Laurie Wood makes it miserable.  She does not "teach". She makes you buy a cheap paper back book that her best friend (Cobb) made and lets you teach yourself.  She also lets you pay to use Cobbs website which contradicts the book! Avoid

First off, Accounting is not an easy subject, it is down right challenging. Second, Wood is actually makes this class easier than most. People complain b/c they want to do nothing and make an A. If you want to learn the material and do the work, you have nothing to worry about. Wood is genuinely nice and helpful.

OK, all these criticism's are unfair. Accounting is a horrible subject, whoever the teacher may be. Mrs. Wood is a nice and accessible lady outside of class and will help you out if you put in the effort. DO THE HOMEWORK, keep up with the reading and use the website and you will be fine.

Laurie Wood is not a teacher....she is a small white woman who merely shows up everyday and speaks in an annoying, whiney voice.  She calls herself "LAW" and seems to think that she is the filter between those who deserve to get into the business school and those who don't.  Horrible class, do not take her or Cobb.

This lady ruined a lot of Thursday nights with her Friday quizzes & tests along with dead days with her overly comprehensive final. I have taken a break from studying to help prevent others from the misery that comes with this class. Stay away from laurie wood.

Ok, if you take Wood you have to be prepared for a shafting. This class and teacher are really that bad; they're ridiculous. She is an awful teacher; so even if youre an acct major be prepared for extreme aggravation. She is a terrible lady and won't help you. Study hard and still have no success.

I would rather eat glass then endure laurie wood. I made an A in Financial Acct and have a Cost Acct internship, but struggle to teach myself the material since she is no help, none. I have so many angry feelings that I can't express with 350 characters.

Ok, if you take Wood you have to be prepared to study.This class and this teacher aren't bad; they're just tough. She is a tough teacher; so if accoutning is not your subject you just have to be prepared to do alot of studying. She is a nice lady though and she will help you; but you have to do your part too. If you don't, you will fail the class.

She is awesome.  Attendance is extremely important though, and so is doing your homework.  She picks up the homework randomly, so do it.  The homework counts as a quiz grade so they are really important.  The book is kind of confusing, so pay attention in class and show up.  If you can do that she is easy.

Quit crying. She is a great teacher and teaches what you need to know. If you actually read the material and do homework then you will be fine. People over complicate everything. Truly some people can't cut it. You can not just breeze your way through, this is college.

Dropped her course a few weeks in when I realized how difficult she was going to make things. Her book and website seem questionable at best and her teaching style is horrid. Not to mention her voice is like nails against a chalkboard. Do not recommend.

Laurie Wood is the first professor that has truly made a class miserable for me in college. Her lectures consist of her reading word for word from an incomprehensible text book like is was story time. Homework is sporadically taken for a grade and problems are explained by simply putting the teachers edition on the overhead. Do not take her, ever.

I would hate to overexaggerate; however, it might actually be considered an understatement to rate this woman as useless. She is unwilling to listen to any and every complaint unless it is done formally regarding her ridiculous textbook and website which is absolutely plagued with errors. I would advise this teacher to no person in any circumstance

Where to begin this woman. Tests are ridiculous because she always puts them in different formats and tries to fool those who study for days on the website. Went for help numerous times and its like talking to a child with downs syndrome. Studied balls to get a C. quizzes are gay. the website is $40 and its full of errors. avoid at all costs

Spend way too much time studying just to make a C or B on the tests and quizzes. Homework problems and the website she created DO NOT help for the test. Test questions are nothing like what she teaches you. Attendance is mandatory even though you learn nothing in class.

Tests are Unessecarily hard ... there is no real way to review for tests. Book is a joke website is even worse and she co wrote both of them. Never take this teacher ... Study for hours for a low B. Class avg was a 73 after 3rd test and final average was a 65 for the class. Shes a real C U Next Tuesday

tests are unnecessarily hard and are extremely difficult to study for as the questions are completely different than the practice ones. intentionally tries to trick you and the tests are way too long for an hour class. studied for HOURS to get a mid C on each test. avoiddddd

Wonderful teacher! Best one I have had at TCU. Go to class, read the sections, and do the HW she assigns. The test are like the online problems, which no one does and is a big reason why they feel like they have never seen the problems. TAKE HER!!!

LAW really is a great teacher. She teaches you the stuff you need to know, however her tests are really hard. She gives a review, and partial credit for the tests. Her tests are nothing like the home work problems, so make sure you know the material all the way through.
No Comments
Super sweet, only four tests & a project for your entire grade, but they're pretty easy. She's great and doesn't want this class to take your time away from other things.
such a sweet and amazing professor who truly wants her students to succeed. will take her again!

She's super sweet, helpful, and knowledgeable. Attendance not required and she posts the slides, but there's often in class extra credit. Get the textbook to study from, but don't bother reading before lecture. Tests are on paper and multiple choice. Easy A studying only the night before. One project but don't have to present it and four tests.
Literally such a sweet person and caring teacher. Grades are super chill and tests are super easy. 100000% would recommend.

If you want a VERY easy A, TAKE HER CLASS!! I went to class only 6 times the entire semester, and ended with a high A. The only grades are tests, but the tests are pretty much just common sense. Just look at the review she posts and you will be fine.

I cannot recommend this class enough. She is so sweet. The final is not cumulative and is just the 4th test. We have one project aside from the 4 tests, and she gave us two extra credit opportunities.

LOVE HER!!! She's so sweet and you can tell she cares about all of her students. I'm trying to take another class with her next semester! Tests don't require a ton of studying and she always does a review day the class before.

This was a great class. Bodine made it fun and I learned a lot. The attendance is not mandatory at all and you are graded by 4 exams and 1 final project. These are the only grades so there is no wiggle room if you don't do well on an exam. Although they are all online and open note.

She is by far the best professor I have had. She respects our time and lets us out of class early every day. All of our tests are online and straight from the power points. She makes the class relatable to real life. I highly recommend taking this class by her.
She is the best professor! She is very straight forward and interesting to listen too. She works in the health care field so she is a great source for advice! Loved her class!

The material is easy, but his explanations can be really confusing. He keeps us past class time almost every class, and sometimes will give a quiz with 5 minutes remaining of class. He is nice but can be condescending.

Honestly a super easy class if you just show up and pay attention. It can be a bit boring, but is otherwise a free A. You are allowed a formula/cheat sheet on exams which is helpful, and the quiz/exam content is exactly as he says it will be. The slight accent can be difficult at first, but isn't bad when you get used to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Problems from exams/quizzes almost identical to practice. Helps you during quizzes and sometimes tests. Lenient with make-up exams and accessible for office hours. Goes over problems a lot during lectures and tries hard to help you understand. Allows note cards on exams. Can be hard to understand b/c of his accent. PAY ATTENTION and you'll do well

Due to a language barrier/thick accent, this class was a bit difficult. He was not patient with students and became very irritated/angry if class questions weren't answered. Weekly quizzes and homework, frequent exams. If you're good at math, you can do well as long as you stick to the notes. He answered emails well. Use the allowed cheat sheet!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lots of homework and VERY lecture heavy. If you want to do good in the class you have to pay attention, take good notes, and do lots of time outside of class. He is a very strict grader and has a strong accent that is difficult to understand at times. He had to drop our worst test grade so that kids could pass the class. Would not recommend.

Took Stats in HS and got an A, so I expected an easy credit- def wasn't. Homework was SO forgettable and not helpful, lectures were dry, and most kids bombed the first test. He dropped lowest test so we could pass. Stats is tough, but it could've been taught way better. Final was a cumulative test + group project. I recommend avoiding this teacher.

not really sure how I got an A. YOU NEED TO STUDY. He dropped 2 lowest exams which was very helpful. Xie is a great teacher and people who say he's hard understand are being rude. He is completely understandable so I don't really know where that came from. Anyways take this for an A for NS.

I would 100% take this class again. Easiest class to earn the credits needed. Professor Xie is very accessible and overall, a great professor. Although class isn't mandatory, I highly recommend you attend because he does not announce when quizzes are and they are mostly given after lectures, but not worth much.

Prof Xie is amazing, and really cares about what hes teaching about. There are pop quizzes in class, so you do have to attend, although its not mandatory. The class is very test heavy, but they arent too difficult as long as you review the lecture slides. We had online exams after most people flunked the first one, but theyre still very easy.

Long, boring lectures where he for whatever reason does not look at the students, but at a wall.
