The class total points is out of 700 points so as we go into our final in a couple days, nobody has any clue what their grade is in the class. She takes forever. DO Not Take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst class I've taken at TCU. So unorganized.Class based on a group project with a real company but she throws in 2 random exams on info we barely talked about...the class average was a D on the exam 1.Know how to use SPSS prior to class-- we had to figure it out ourselves, she barely knew what she was doing. Her exams don't make sense. Dont take!

She's the most disorganized professor ever, but her grading is really easy, especially when you can make a case for yourself. She gave 100 on almost every group assignment done because she was confused about her own curriculum. Honestly if you want to learn don't take her (if you have a choice), but if you just want to pass the class then take her.

I love her teaching style, very collaborative and straightforward with the students. But be warned, she doesn't use D2l, you submit everything via email. She grades late, she uses PowerPoint slides that seem outdated, and she's disorganized. But she is open to student's suggestions and there is no homework aside from working in your teams.

The way she graded our exams and assignments was pitiful. She clearly didn't read the assignments/essay answers in full. Always said she was "confused." Very disorganized. Wasn't hard, just frustrating with a teacher who doesn't seem to care or get what's going on. Took forever to grade, didn't even grade everything when we got our final grades.

You can learn a lot in her class/lectures are interesting but she's very unorganized and SLOW at grading (that's why Im not sure what's my grade and still have 3 weeks left). The projects instructions are unclear and her exams are easy but she has essay questions about specific examples during her class. Hard grading unless you're SUPER specific.

The class is an easy A. Do not expect to learn anything though. The group project that her students are required to do is abysmal. For my group's first assignment, there were no instructions for it and when we talked to her about why we received a 42/50 she said it was all formatting, saying our mini paragraphs are too lengthy. No instructions too

Dr. Bhagwat is extremely knowledgeable in the field of marketing and her lectures are very informative and interesting, the class is basically a group discussion. My issue with her is she is unreachable over email and she is very unorganized and slow at grading. That being said, I definitely learnt a lot in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Pretty much every class is just a big discussion about current events happening in the marketing world. class is pretty enjoyable but you have to be willing to talk to get those participation points because only written grades are the project and tests. a likable, young professor and it isn't too hard to do well - tests right from in class material
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: A really interesting class and a cool professor, but she doesn't answer emails or post grades. She never put our final grades, participation grades, or our big project grade in so we don't know what we got which is annoying. The class itself is super laid back and its mainly a big conversation about whats going on in the business world. Easy tests
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: AVOID! First year teaching class, and he just copied and pasted Gagne's syllabus, and it felt like he was learning along with us. I learned nothing from his lectures, and random assignments would randomly just pop up. Half of the stuff is graded by a TA who grades so harshly. Dreaded going to this class.
Shouldn't be teaching in Neeley. Worst Bis teacher in the program. Dosent give students  a rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: no rubric at all but the professor will take off a huge chunk of your grade for every smallest detail. obsessed with framework. don't even think about asking for technical feedback, all you would receive is "this is good, but have you applied this framework to your project?".

This professor is obsessed with frameworks and whether you match his instructions word-for-word. Technical knowledge is almost nonexistent here. Ask a technical question, and you'll be redirected to another framework which our actual client couldn't care less. If you're expecting this class to teach you technical skills, think again.

Unfortunately, if you are a BIS student, you will have to take a class with Ali. Get ready for the most nitpicky-micro-manager teacher of your life. No rubric. No clear instructions. If you don't know it, that's on you, because apparently, he's never wrong. The grade for every assignment is going to be based on his personal preferences. Good luck.

Not every BIS major wants to go into coding or super technical fields, and this class respected that. It built on prior technical knowledge from other BIS classes we took over three years and focused on applying it through strategy and teamwork. The professor's vast experience in consulting made the course incredibly valuable for me

As someone not super technical, this class was a huge relief. this class is a great intro to real-world project management and consulting. It's about teamwork, strategy, and communication. The professor shared clear expectations, industry insight, and mentored students throughout.

Amazing class with a professor who genuinely cares about your success. He answers emails promptly, gives clear direction in lectures, and always helps if you're confused. His examples, feedback, and approach to teaching made every assignment feel connected to real-life work. This course gave me practical tools I'll actually use in my career.

The course was structured around collaboration and real project management. Teams were intentionally built with diverse skill sets, just like in the real world. The professor always explained his expectations in class, provided examples, and posted helpful resources on D2L. The assignments helped develop critical thinking. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the most rewarding classes I've taken at TCU. The professor is extremely supportive and he truly goes above and beyond to help you succeed, not just academically but also professionally. I gained valuable skills in teamwork, and project management that align directly with real world expectations. His mentorship truly made a lasting impact.

Professor Ali is one of the most dedicated and caring professors at TCU. He always makes time for students, even outside office hours, and breaks down complex material in a way that's easy to grasp. Capstone was tough, but he made it manageable. It taught me real-world skills in teamwork, time management, and client-focused problem solving.

The professor and the class are absolutely horrendous. I really don't know why he got hired in the first place in the BIS department. He was the most non-technical person I have ever met as a professor, and I would really recommend he take some time to sit in some BIS courses such as AI or BIS dev from Professor Kelly Slaughter.

A big philosophy of this prof is no rubrics. He expects us to ask "clarifying questions" for EVERY SINGLE DETAIL and then grades so hard on those seemingly unnecessary things. His obsessions for "titles and subtitles," "title slide with dates," are just a few examples. Don't fall for "I thought you did a great job" - the grades don't reflect it.

Having a non-technical professor leading a Capstone class is frustrating. He doesn't even know what an API is, and when we secured a sponsor for the project, he spent the money on T-shirts instead of covering the cost of our OpenAI API key. Quizzes are random and all he talks is non-sense. Would not recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ali can be a challenging instructor to work with. His expectations are often unclear, and he gives surprise quizzes on readings with only three minutes to complete them. He is unresponsive to emails, making it necessary to ask questions in person during class. Avoid due to his lack of consideration for students time and grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is mainly graded on three exams, a few small quizzes, and a final project. He gives an exam review which is very helpful and a formula sheet for the exam. The slides have a lot of information and he is always happy to answer questions. I recommend as far as Investment 2 professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at TCU. I took him for Investments 1 and 2. He seems to have a true enjoyment for what he teaches, which is very refreshing. He is extremely smart, and is able to answer any question you will have. You can have a double sided cheat sheet for tests, so tests are not too hard.

Dr. Zheng's first semester at TCU was impressive. He might be slightly hard to understand in class due to his accent (at no fault to him), but his PowerPoints are very clear and act as a great reference for the tests. He allows a note sheet for the tests, which are fairly straightforward. I would recommend Dr. Zheng for Investments I.

It was Dr. Zheng's 1st semester and I enjoyed him. Investments is a hard class no matter who you take. He has a thick Chinese accent that can be hard to understand but he's extremely smart. Read ppts before class and you'll do well. Lets you have a double-sided cheat sheet for 3 exams and 2 group projects make up the course. easy quizzes for points

Ok, she is a good person but one of the worst professors I've ever had. I barely knew what was going on half of the time and the exams were difficult to get through. If you work hard, you'll do well but do not depend on her.

Her class is a bit fast paces and she is quite loud when she lectures but her class is super interactive and really interesting. Her assignments are group assignments and super easy.  I don't think there were any individual assignments at all. Take her!

She can get annoying but she's so passionate and SO easy. The final exam was word for word from the review, no homework, just a bunch of in class assignments you do with your group. the only thing is she makes you scan in for attendance and she will never cancel class, but besides that she is so easy and it is not hard to get an A.

TAKE HER! She may scream into a microphone the whole class, but she is such a sweet and actually good professor. She teaches exactly what is on the exams. You get into groups at the beginning of the semester and have weekly in-class assignments, but they are super easy!

Zadeh is the best professor to have for this course. His main job is not at TCU so it makes him way more interesting. Minimal homework, projects, and expectations which made me want to do even better. Awesome guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is AWESOME! Take him!!!!

Professor Zadeh was a great professor; he has real world experience and tells "war story's" known has story's he's experienced within business law. The tests are open everything and are written responses. Each person does an individual presentation and a group, but it is super chill. I love him and would recommend him to everyone!

TAKE HIM! This was one of the best classes I have taken at TCU! His lectures are super engaging always connects the law to his job and never went the full time. Even though it was an 8am it was so worth it to go. Only 2 exams and final project not a hard grader. Not hard to get an A-.

Professor Zadeh is an amazing professor! I would 100% take it again. Even though he teaches 8 am, his lectures are so interesting and he is very engaging with his students. He was by far the best professor I have had at TCU. The tests are open note and theres one group project at the end of the semester. No homework. Take him!

I really liked this class. He cares a lot about students and is interested/passionate about the material. Workload is very light, but there is a group project at the end. There are very few grades so you don't have much room for error if you want an A but he is a very fair grader.

I love prof Zadeh! At first wasn't able to get into his class, but requested a permission code and he let me in! Super chill. You're graded on few things so you have to do well on the exams. 2 Exams. 1 individual case study presentation and final group presentation. Exams are open note/resource but free response. No HW. Short lectures in class.

2 tests online (google doc) on powerpoints & he encourages using AI. 1 Indiv pres (can use AI) & group project, NO FINAL. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to get a good grade. Never goes full 1:20. Has his own firm & has cool stories which makes class interesting. Easy grader, no hw, no textbook, cool guy. TAKE HIM

Even though this class is only offered at 8 am, it is so worth it to take. There is very minimal work and tests are all open note. The group project at the end of the semester will come up fast but it is not difficult. Just make sure you understand in depth his concepts before the test and you will be fine.
I would 100% recommend taking his class. His test are open note, and he is a very fair grader. Although it is an 8am, his class is much easier than the other BLAW classes. No quizzes or homework!

Jim's lectures were super engaging, especially for a 1.5hr 8 am class. While not expecting us to be pre-law students, he pushed us to learn how to apply the law to business, stay within the bounds of the law, and use it to our advantage. I enjoyed listening to his "war stories" about cases he worked on in the past.

I had Professor Zadeh for his first-ever class at TCU. Take this class if you want a well-respected teacher. Yes, it is easy, but his lectures are also fantastic and engaging, and for an 8 am, it is great! I don't write reviews much, but he deserves more recognition for his teaching style. Everything is open note as he says, "That's how life is."

I had a TA for my communicating effectively class, but it was by far the best class I have ever taken. Shoutout Ms. Van Hare who is the best teacher on campus. Not only did I learn a lot from the class, I genuinely looked forward to going to class. If you put in effort and do your assignments it's an easy A.
Overall a really nice class I guess it depends on the TA you get but my TA was really fun and overall its just giving speeches probably one of the easiest course I've taken at TCU.

I didn't actually have Professor Frohlich and had one of his TA's. The course structure was great ! Three big speeches and midterm and some homework. I'm not big on public speaking but the class environment makes it easier because you all are doing the same thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Frohlich was such a great professor who really cared about us as students and gave great feedback. 2 major speeches and final was situationional depending on grade. really chill class and hardly any homework

PSA: Don't expect Frohlich to be teaching in fall or spring semesters! Me and my friend were surprised when we both ended up having TAs. However, they all follow Frohlich's curriculum and rubrics, so it really depends on who you end up with. I loved mine and the class was super light. Easy A even for people who hate public speaking (including me).
Loved Frohlic! He was awesome he was an awesome teacher! He was super friendly and encouraging! I really looked forward to going to his class everyday!
I have one of his TA's and its super easy and hard not to do well
By luck of the draw if you get Arganbright, ur set, goated.

Amazing professor to take for communication! It was a class I was always happy to attend even though it was at 8 am. You have 2 practice speeches that get you used to presenting, then 2 speeches that are graded more harshly but as long as you do everything on the rubric you should end with a high grade. Few group projects, and not a lot of hw.

My class was taught by Sarah Stacy his TA and she was super nice!! Just show up to class and she always makes it interesting and is super caring and nice and is always there for you. It's super chill, but you have to put in effort for the presentations but they can be interesting and aren't bad and that's all classes.

Signed up for Frohlich and my class was taught entirely by a TA but she was extremely nice! The guidelines are super clear and you know exactly how you will be graded. Grade is made up of mostly speeches and a few other assignments. As long as you show up and follow the rubrics you will easily make an A.

I'm not sure if something changed this semester but it's entirely taught by the TA. She grades hard and will take off points/ give zeros if you're not present for group activities or miss out on speech days. She's nice for the most part, it just would've been better to know this course was going to be taught solely by her instead of the prof.

I enjoyed taking Frohlich for the intro communications class. He is a generous grader when it comes to the 5 speeches you have to give. He makes you feel comfortable and welcome if you have speech anxiety. Just follow his speech outlines and you should have no problems. There was a midterm & final exam. The final was open book/note too

CLEAR GRADING CRITERIA. You know exactly what your going to be graded on, you know exactly what to do to succeed. If a speech is 60 points,,, there will be 60 free points: i.e: "body of speech" "draft" "written outline" "visual aid" which is all a free 100%. Im sure there are actually easy A alternatives with like a TA but frohlich is def a easy A

Public speaking is public speaking. Your either chilling or your going to be very anxious before the speech. If you get anxious, gotta prepare and practice because the speeches arent long (2-4 min) and there about topic you choose so no excuse to BOMB them. Everyone in my class did great, allowed paper outline, or notecards  Exams r easy.

Professor Frohlich was a great teacher. This class requires some public speaking but he made the criteria and the process of the assignment clear. He also offered to meet with students outside of class if they were super nervous about giving the speech. He is an overall kind and supportive professor.

I absolutely loved Professor Frohlich. I hate public speaking but he made an environment that made everyone feel comfortable. He is fun and funny and explains everything very well. Wish I could take him again !

Only had to do two major speeches, one of which is a group speech. The two exams have some information thats only from the textbook so keep that in mind. I really enjoyed having him as my professor because his expectations were clear and his grading was relatively lenient. He gives really good feedback that really helps everyone grow in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: By far one of the sweetest professors ever. You can tell she is passionate about sociology which made lectures interesting and worthwhile. Exams are taken on paper in class and the final is not an exam. You should do good if you attend class and study. I couldn't recommend her enough, she wants to help and is so kind!!!
kind always respectful of others

By far my favorite professor at TCU. It's obvious that she cares about the material she is teaching and the students she is teaching it to. Although her readings can be a little lengthy, they are intriguing and completely relevant to class discussions. I've had her for several classes and she's truly an inspirational human and amazing professor.

dr. Zarrugh was the best! She was very easy to listen to and talk to, and she made sociology really interesting. people talking about her "leanings" are dramatic, it's a fun class to take and not too hard! you have to be present for activities and the exams are not easy, taken in class on paper. She cares about her students and I def recommend.
Very politically swayed a certain direction, felt like I was getting indoctrinated and not taught. It's hard to get an A in her class and it's not super interesting. I wouldn't recommend.

Dr. Zarrugh is the most caring professor I have ever had. She is very accessible out of class, and willing to work with you on anything. Her tests used to be open book, online at home, but now they are in person on paper (closed book). She does not take attendance but does not post the slides, so you need to go to class. Tests are not easy.

She is a very inspirational and caring professor and makes her lectures interesting. The tests are exact things from her powerpoint so take notes in class. Rarely any homework other than discussion questions and studying for the exams. No final, just a final project.

Great Professor! Her class was super easy. As long as you go to the lectures and take notes you will pass the class. She made sociology very interesting for me. There's a textbook but there was rarely anything on the tests that she didn't go over in lecture. Do the readings and take notes and you'll be fine.

Prof. Zarrugh is a great professor. She has a way of lecturing that can keep you interested. She provides a presentation during lectures for notes. There aren't very many grades, so the tests are a really big part of your grade. A good class, just prepare for studying.
nicest lady and a pretty easy class, my only complaint is the lack of grades so every grade matters. overall i would reccomend it
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Zarrugh's class, she made sociology super interesting for me. Although she's very lecture based, the lectures are engaging. This is because it's based more on actual studies and statistics, rather than just definitions/terms being shoved down your throat. This in the long run really helped me remember all the information for exams.

Dr Zarrugh was a very kind professor. She gave clear descriptive lectures, and told us what we need to know. She would post a review sheet to help study for exams. For the maymester you are graded by few things, but the final is not cumulative. She recommended the textbook reading, but not much of it was on the exams. I definitely recommend her

Dr Zarrugh is a very kind professor who gives clear lectures, and offers help to those who need it. She would always give clear answers to questions. Her study guides helped prep for exams. I would recommend answering questions in class as it makes her respect and remember you well. Definitely take her

One of the kindest professors I have ever taken a class with at TCU. She goes out of her way to interact with her students and make sure that they do well in the class. The material is not difficult to comprehend, regardless of whether or not you are invested in the field. If you just need to take the class for a credit, you won't be disappointed.

Absolutely love her, she truly cares about you learning the material! Her political sociology class was Monday lectures, and Wednesdays are discussions. You are only a discussion leader once a semester and present along with one or two others, so you're not alone. Attendance is not mandatory but your grade will drop if you don't go.

Professor Zarrugh is the sweetest and most amazing person you'll ever meet. She is caring and passionate about what she teaches. I had her course for 3 hours long but time went by so fast because she made her lectures so interesting and worth listening to. Her assignments are simple and there is no final exam, just a simple project. She's worth it!

One of my favorite professors at TCU so far. Dr. Zarrugh does not post lecture slides so you have to go to class to get the material. The class is very engaging as she asks a lot of questions and talks about interesting topics. She makes an effort to learn students' names and is extremely fair when it comes to her expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Zarrugh is a literal angle. I had to take intro to sociology for core, as many TCU students do, and I found the subject SO interesting! Her lectures are really informative and engaging. As long as you participate, take good notes, and actively engage with her in class, you'll be set up for success. I 100% recommend taking her class! Love her!

Good professor, my main complaint is that the lectures get a bit repetitive. Readings are a bit long, but doable if you don't wait till the last second like me. She does the discussion post plus replies, which gets redundant after a while. Overall decent class and professor, easy enough to pass, just a bit dull.
An absolute angel. Such a nice woman who really cares about sociology. She gives great lectures. All tests are open note and nothing is a surprise. Definitely recommend!

Prof Zarrugh is so kind and really cares about her students. Her lectures are really interesting, and really encourages participation. Not many assignments, just discussion posts. A decent amount of outside articles to read, which do come up on exams. I loved her class, and I really recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is the sweetest lady you will meet and gives great feedback and encouragement! She adapted really well to lecturing online- I was in the once a week LONG class and she allowed the class to agree upon their style of lecture to make it through such a long class. Be sure to read the readings each week they're discussed in class and on the test!!

Professor Zarrugh is very interesting to listen to and give very clear information. There is quite a bit of reading in her class however, it is interesting and she goes over everything before the test. She wants her students to do good and she makes sure that everyone has everything they need to succeed. Take Professor Zarrugh!!!
Intelligent, caring, and insightful. Lots of reading, reflections, and discussions because she wants to make sure you're actually understanding and applying the material--so be ready to read.
Best teacher I've ever had! She loves her students, and she interacts with everyone. She gives breaks during class, and she makes class fun.

do yourself a favor and take Dr. Zarrugh! She is 100% incredible. Class was 3 hours long and I was never bored for a minute. She makes everything super applicable and very interesting (also pre-med kids she teaches you EVERYTHING in the sociology section of the MCAT!). Take this class!!

I absolutely loved this professor, and I would greatly recommend her. She is caring, interesting to listen to, and understanding. I never dreaded going to class, and reading is fairly easy. I loved this class.

Dr. Zarrugh is probably my favorite professors at TCU. I've taken several of her classes, I like her so much. She is encouraging, helpful in and out of class, gives amazing lectures, and sincerely wants her students to learn and succeed. Her classes are not the easiest sociology classes you could take, but you learn so much that it's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I am an A student. I took this class thinking it would be fairly easy, and I was completely wrong. I worked extremely hard to get a good grade in this class and I got a low C. She is a very awful and subjective grader. She makes an intro class way more difficult than it needs to be. I do not recommend this class, most P/NC. Take Witworth's class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class has been my absolute favorite class to take. Dr. Zarrugh was always well-prepared and did a phenomenal job engaging the class. Her discussion-based class time was intimidating, but it grew and stretched me in so many ways. I would take this class again if I could. She is by far, the best sociology professor at TCU.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved having Amina as a professor, especially in sociology. She is very careful about making sure that everyone gets a chance to participate in class discussion and she very obviously values each and every one of her students as an individual. Her lectures are insightful, her expectations are reasonable, and she is overall awesome.

Dr. Schiffer is super passionate about what he teaches and it really comes across. Just show up and pay attention and you should be okay grade-wise. He really appreciates when people are active in class and engage with him. He's not going to slow down for people who are struggling, but if you show up and do the work, it's not a very hard grade.
Such an awesome professor who actually cares. Do the practice tests and go to his office hours before the exams and you are sure to get an A.

Dr. Schiffer is great! Read and pay attention during class and you will be fine. The whole class was so fun and we learned a lot without it feeling too difficult. There are 3 exams and 3 papers but you have the tools to be successful for all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Schiffer is great! He keeps everyone engaged in lectures. If you listen to his lectures, take good notes, and pay attention in class, you're fine. I found the exams very easy with preparation. The labs are ridiculous and take forever, but the main class is good enough to overcome that.

Dr. Schiffer is easily my favorite prof and Scope & Methods might be my favorite class at TCU. It can be hard, but Dr. Schiffer wants his students to succeed. Don't miss class, write down EVERYTHING, and DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS (very similar to the exams)! He's hilarious and the exams truly reflect who he is as a person (big bird guy). TAKE HIM!!!!!!

I took scope with Dr. Schiffer this past semester. This class in very difficult, easily the hardest class I've ever taken. Going into it, I didn't know there was a coding portion of the class but it was my best grade in the end. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!! If you try your best in this class you will be ok, but take it serious from day 1!

Dr. Schiffer gives great lectures and I was never bored in this class. You will not need the book at all if you go to class, everything on tests is covered in lecture and book won't help much when studying.

I took scope and methods with Dr. Schiffer. This class is notoriously difficult, and I was sure I was going to fail. Dr. Schiffer was very clear in his lectures. The only thing I do not like is that he does not post his slides, so make sure you have a friend in class that you can get the notes from. His exams are hard but he gives you the old ones
Dr. Schiffer really cares about the material and his lectures are interesting. Take him if you can

I really enjoyed this class and I feel that his lectures were so interesting and he was very passionate with what he was teaching. However, I would say that attendance (although) not graded is mandatory and to do well on the exams you have to go to class. The exams are not hard but they are application based so studying is slightly difficult.

Prof. Schiffer is a great professor and super knowledgable. Attendance is not graded but you need to be in class to succeed. There are four tests and up to 5 optional assignments you can do based on how heavily you want each test weighted, which makes it easy to achieve an A. Tests are difficult and a mix of lecture material and textbook terms.

Dr Schiffer is a good teacher, but this is a hard class. He let us know on the first day that a few students were in the class for the third time. 75% of the grade is 3 tests and 25% is in lab, which is not difficult at all. You need to go to class and pay attention and take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I went into Scope and Methods knowing this class would be difficult. However, previously taking elementary statistics the first 2 units were not difficult. Attend every class, do the labs, go over the practice test/study guide with friends and go into his office hours for things you don't understand. Not a hard class as long as you make the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr. Schiffer is the nicest guy and tries his best to make lectures entertaining. His class is really lecture-heavy, and what he lectures is different from the book, so you need to go to class. Mr. Schiffer is a pretty hard grader, but I've learned a lot from his class and genuinely look forward to going to his class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is an introductory class on american politics and I found it to be fairly easy. We were graded on 4 tests, with the lowest score being weighted less. The tests were primarily multiple choice and based on both the readings and lectures. Attendance is optional, but I would recommend attending most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took Intro to American Politics with Professor Schiffer because I thought it would be cool, and it was. Half the class was the exact same material from AP Gov in high school, so I never read the textbook and got an A. If you liked Gov. in high school take it, if not, just prepare to read outside of class. Schiffer is a cool guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His class is extremely test and lecture heavy, so be ready to take notes. He is passionate about politics, so it keeps the class interesting. It's difficult to know what to expect on tests, and there are only 4 of them. I would suggest actually reading the textbook and understanding the key terms, as well as taking detailed notes/taping lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Schiffer is the ultimate example of "if you put in the work you'll do fine" lectures are great and Schiffer always jokes and keeps you interested tests are hard but not impossible just study the practice tests he gives you
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Countless nights were spent preparing for his tests, which were not too hard, but worth the MAJORITY of your grade - the rest comes from labs. He does not care much for his students - literally told kids to drop the class after performing poor on the FIRST test. He is an arrogant, and plays with his pet parrot in his free time. DO NOT TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Quite possibly the worst professor that I have had at TCU. He's a very "here's the information. Figure it out for yourself" type of guy. Lectures did not make sense and I found myself attempting to try and teach this myself since he was absolutely no help in office hours. Take someone else for Scope and Methods if you value passing.

Dr. Schiffer puts a lot of effort into his lectures. I have taken him both online and in-person and both were phenomenal. He is a difficult grader but gives you every opportunity to improve throughout the semester. I found that I truly learned a lot from him and his classes. One of my favorite poli-sci professors at TCU.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I was diagnosed with a viral infection. Asked all my other professors for a P/NC which all accepted because of my illness except him. I have communicated beforehand about my situation. It was not like where I had sprung this up onto him. I now have been rejected from Neeley because of this and I have to retake the calls this semster.

He will give you all of the opportunities you need to succeed in the class, but you must read the textbook, take good notes, and show up to class to do well on the tests. He is a very entertaining lecturer so that helps a ton!
Professor Schiffer is the best! This class is super fun and he definitely wants to make sure all his students get an A. If you try your best, you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Schiffer is extremely arrogant, says he's willing to help in office hours but just makes you feel insecure and leaving still knowing nothing. Tests are fine, just be prepared to entirely teach yourself. I left every class extremely confused, he seems to forget that we don't have PhD's in this field like he does. Don't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You will not pass this class if you don't go. Schiffer is the funniest professor ever and really keeps your attention to lecture. This is NOT an easy class, but he gives past tests as study guides. You will not pass the tests if you don't do these The labs are moderately hard but he is more than willing to help you. He knows really knows his stuff.

Lectures are very interesting... He's the kind of presenter we all wish we could be! He has an awesome ability to tie stuff to everyday events. Also takes time to explain his arguments so you end up really respecting him, even if you disagree (although he convinced me to change my mind more than once!) Engaging, cool, actually useful class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures are so interesting... He's the kind of presenter we all wish we could be! He has an awesome ability to tie stuff to everyday events. Also takes time to explain his arguments so you end up really respecting him, even if you disagree (although he convinced me to change my mind more than once!) Engaging, cool, actually useful class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Schiffer is a great professor... his lectures are so interesting and he is a hilarious professor. The papers and tests aren't too tough at all and he's always helpful if you email. Great guy; cares about his students and the quality of his courses SO MUCH. You won't regret taking Media and Politics with him.

Great professor. This is the second time I have taken Dr. Schiffer and I plan on taking him again. He is funny and always makes you laugh. Smart guy who is great at keeping his political beliefs aside and being neutral. Wants you to learn  and get something out of the class. Take one of his classes while you're at TCU! He is an amazing professor!!!

Schiffer is a different person that's why some don't like him. He has an awkward personality, but you just have to find the humor in that. He will tell jokes and cuss in class which is funny. Not as hard as everyone make him out to be. He seems disrespectful at times, but don't take it personally he's like that to everyone. Study decent get a B.

If you study, read the textbook, and put effort into the papers it's an easy A. He organizes the class so that you choose from a selection which papers you want to do which is really helpful. The class can be dull at times but he's very passionate and definitely knows his stuff.

Dr. Schiffer you either hate him or love him. He has a very dry personality and difficult to talk to on a one on one basis. If you are scared to take him for Scope and Methods... Don't be. Show up to the lab work with partners and do different questions to get out of there. Study with a group and you can easily make a good grade.

The class material isn't incredibly interesting, but Dr. Schiffer makes it as humorous and attention grabbing as possible. He's an extremely funny dude and is cute in the nerdiest way. If you skip a bunch of classes you won't do well, and you lose 50% on each lab you don't attend, even if you do it and turn it in. I would definitely recommend him.

Scope & Methods isn't a fun or easy class, but Dr. Schiffer makes it fun & manageable. He doesn't take attendance, but nearly all of the material on the exams comes from class lectures. Labs are on the computer and are actually enjoyable- and can boost your grade. You have to study for the exams, but you can get an A if you put time into it.

Funny guy. He's really great, but at times found lectures hard to follow and a little boring. Read the book, study vocab and lecture and you will do fine. Take advantage of the extra paper! Test are an odd creative version he makes up of MC, TF, and 5-10 short answer essays. But good guy and interesting class. He does take attendance randomly!

Schiffer was a great Intro to American Politics teacher. First test is hard every year, since you don't know what to expect. But the two tests after, I got A's on. He also lets you write an optional essay to boost your grade. The class is super interesting, Im always pumped to go! He says the F word a lot, so you know he's funny :)

He is very intelligent, and he likes to make that known. That being said, he is a great prof. The key to doing well is following his directions exactly as he says them. If he says pay attention to this part of the book, pay attention. If you do this, and listen during lectures, you will be fine.

There is a textbook for this class, but I never needed to use it. Attendance for labs is part of your grade, but a lot of the land are completion and help boost your grade. I just copied down all the notes from his power point lectures and was able to get an A- with very little effort. Lectures were easy to follow and somewhat funny.

Prof Schiffer is one of the nicest teachers I have had, lectures are not the most interesting but even I was not bored. He worked with me in office hours and never once felt like he was arrogant, one of the best!

Easy class. His tests are just like the practice tests he sends out. You need to come to class, but no homework or outside work.  Minimal studying if you understand basic statistics well. He is a tad arrogant but nice enough and willing to help if you approach him.

Dr. Schiifer keeps his class very interesting and engaging. Nerdy, but in a way that keeps the class attentive. Read the book. Most of the vocab is from the books and although attendance in class in not mandatory, his lecutres are what he test over. Two outside papers, but he lets you choose between four topic and sumbit three, taking the highest 2

Dr. Schiffer's a cool guy. Very liberal, and sometimes shows it in his lecture, but who doesn't these days. Three exams: MC (usually over vocab from book) and short answer (theories that he'll lecture but aren't in the book). It'd prob help to read the textbook, but I didn't and got by with a high B. Two outside papers that are fairly easy.

adorably nerdy. good at throwing humor into his lectures to keep you interested. no quizzes or HW. reading outside of class for test only. two fair papers. very frank w/his words if you make a mistake on the tests or papers. test format is 10 m/c & 10 short answer(2-3 sentences). highly recommend-learned more in 1 semseter than in 2 years of HS gov
Ok class, reading is important, I got an A and put forth sufficent effort. However, not helpful in office hours, and actually a bit rude and arrogant. I wouldn't take him again

For all of those who say that the class is hard, I believe they are lazy. I hardly ever read the book, I tended to daze every now and then and received a B with no effort. Went over any unclear ideas and was always so COMPLETELY willing to help! I love his nerdyness and his goofy animation. I wanted to laugh at him (not with him) alot. Great Asset!

Dr. Schiffer is a great professor!  He is very honest and passionate about teaching poli sci.  He makes class interesting and relevant.  His class takes effort,but they are worth it.  I would highly recommend him.  He is one of the best professors at TCU!

Great teacher, nerdy but pretty funny. Wants everyone to do well. Helps with labs, questions on tests. Doesnt require attendance but it helps alot by going to class. Really interesting guy, knows alot about pop culture. If you have any questions, he tries his best to help you with it.

Dr. Schiffer really likes to help! If you get to know him and talk to him once or twice in his office he'll go out of his way for you. I completely forgot to turn in a paper and he let me turn it in late and said he'd take a letter grade off but didn't. His classes are always interesting. Yeah he's a little nerdy but still has a fun class.

He's very smart and interested in the subject, however he had a very difficult time explaining the material to the class. I got an F on the first test, then an A on the second, and somehow by the grace of god squeezed out a B in the class. BUY THE BOOK and teach yourself, if you do that then you can easily get a B, and go see him in the office.

It is very possible to get an A in this class, just take good notes and dont let the reading pile up on you. Dr Schiffer is a really cool guy. He's very funny and very smart. I really recomend taking this class if you need it, its really interesting.

tests are hard, but class is interesting. obvioulsy really likes his subject. nerdy guy, but thats what makes him so cool. take him in summer school - a lot of reading but def enjoyable if you go to class.
BORING.  and i always felt like he had no idea what he was talking about.  the class was a waste of time and money.
Great Professor!!!!  For a UCR Course, this was a great class! I don't know what is up with everyone else but he is not that hard and he makes the class INTERESTING.
Dude, this guy sucks! Worst teacher in the entire department. Very opinionated and arrogant. Didn't learn a damn thing. My worst grade in all of college. Do NOT take!

Refreshing liberal attitude which is hard to find at this school.  Very intelligent, knows his stuff, but can be a little unapproachable.  Tests aren't too bad, just take good notes and read but don't kill yourself over the reading. An asset for the PoliSci Department.

Very frustrating.  I think he really tries but it's almost like he thinks on a different level.  The way he explains stuff didn't help me.  You think you know the material and you do bad anyway.  It's also hard to stay focused in class (easy to daydream).  Maybe he could spice up the lectures a bit.
I liked the class.  His test were pretty much from the book if you make notecards you do just fine.  I think he is very helpful and very accomodating.
easiest posc class at tcu. tests are a joke. just know the basic concepts and it's a breeze. class is most definately optional. easy A.
not bad! Test are difficult...but really just need to get the basic concepts..and no vocab...not to hard!!

He is a very knowledgable teacher.  His tests are all essay with some fill in the blank that always killed me.  I got a B in the class, which isn't that hard to do.  Just go to class and pay attention and you will do ok.

VERY HARD!  Not too helpful at all.  Don't bother studying, you will just do worse!  Very smart prof, but not very clear in his expectations.  Nice guy, but damn hard tests.  Perfect attendance might get you a point on the final!
Even if you know all the material covered- you will still fail his class.  He takes pleasure in our failures.  You can't talk to him either- he is very hard headed and irrogant.

HORRIBLE CLASS!! i dreaded going there everyday. i wanted to shoot myself from boredom. he thinks he's smarter than everyone so he tries to prove himself all the time. tests are hard as anything. don't take his class!!

We referred to his class as the "hell-whole."  Not only was he unfriendly but he was also a horrible teacher.  He could lot explain the material and constantly tried to prove that he was smarter than us- obvisously!

HORRIBLE teacher!!! He does NOT prepare you for his tests. I pulled an ALL nighter the night before the final and could spit any information back at you....too bad I failed. This is how you know the proffessor is the problem. Wont answer questions either!

The tests in this class are horrible. It wouldnt be that bad, but he doesnt tell you what he wants you to know. so no matter how hard you study you will never have it all. I think his goal in the class is to make himself feel smarter than the whole world.

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.  He is very picky and not willing to help anyone out.  He constantly would fight with an old man in the front of the class, too.  A B is hard to get even with effort.  For example, he put rhyming couplets on the test.
He's one of my favorite professors so far.  He encourages discussion.  An A is tough but a B is very attainable.

Do not take this guy. His test are extremely hard, the test comes after pass/fail can be selected, and he is not clear as to what is going to be on the tests.  Two essays on test and no matching.  A B is the highest grade I see possible.
good organization is a must!! He is not nitpicky on details, but know the concepts.  He is not an easy teacher... a B comes with effort.

This class felt like a fever dream. The content is incredibly easy but she is not a good teacher so be ready to teach yourself. Thick accent and she is pretty aggressive if you do something she doesn't like. Nice lady other than that, pretty funny too, but I would not take her again. All exams open note, weekly quizzes are not.

Ms Ada is a good person but she is not a good professor. She just writes a whole bunch of nonsense and makes math harder than it already is. She over complicates things and the method of each problem online is different than whatever she does in class. Exams are open notes but the reviews she does she teaches them wrong!

Ada McArthy Pratt was a disappointment; I took her college algebra course for the summer of 2024, and it had so many problems. The course was poorly structured, especially with her syllabus, which was misaligned. She was completely disorganized, and she didn't even reply to emails since day 1. Don't waste your time sitting through her lectures.

If you are a busy student and need clarity on what is expected in order to keep your life in order do NOT take this course. You won't be able to understand what she wants EVER. She is incredibly difficult to understand both in person and over email, you're constantly guessing if homework is due, and having to teach yourself material on your own.

easy concepts but taught in a confusing way. It is easy to teach yourself. There is about 8 homework assignments which are a bit more difficult than what you do in class but not essential to pass. One quiz most weeks but is one or two problems. Tests are open note but be sure to attend review days because she tells you what is on the test.

She's a nice woman. Can be a bit sassy at points and doesn't lecture super well. The content is easy and she's understanding. If you laugh at her jokes and get along with her and participate you will do well.
Work and class were easy, but she just doesn't make any sense. I didn't understand half of the lecture, but if you study on your own, you'll be okay. Just don't expect to learn much from her.

I took this professor my freshman year and she is not my favorite. The class she teaches is easy, which is why the ratings are so high. It is impossible to fail. However, if you genuinely need guidance, she is not thorough while explaining and honestly, she makes it more confusing. She definitely is a good person but not the best professor.

I am genuinely awful at math and even lazier when it comes to doing the work to understand it. I did the absolute bare minimum as bare minimum gets and still managed to do decent in the class. She is a little hard to understand sometimes but she is way too kind when it comes to grading and letting stuff slide.

She is one of the sweetest people, but she isn't the best teacher. I'm not great at math and she was hard to understand most of the time but was always willing to help. You definitely should not get below a B in this class.

While the good reviews have truth to them, everything in the bad review is true.  Be prepared to never miss a class & be prepared to have your GPA destroyed with a +/- grading system.  Unless you pretty much make 100s on all the quizzes & exams, then expect nothing higher than an A- in the course, which calculates out to a 3.67 for GPA purposes.

Ms. Ada was by far one of my most favorite professors during my time at TCU.  She is extremely helpful inside and outside the classroom and truly cares about her students.  As long as you show up to class, listen to what she's saying, and do homework, you'll get an A.

This class is super easy, my suggestion would be to take organized notes since all the tests are open note your notes are what you rely on. As well, there are quizzes every week so keep up with the material. Make sure to go to class, attendance will be taken but not every single time.

This class is very easy but that doesn't dismiss the fact that she doesn't know how to correctly teach. She will just put the answer on the board without working through it with you and expects you to understand it all. She also goes very fast so you cannot doze off here. Lots of quizzes so be prepared.

Professor Ada gives quizzes that are not open note, so study! she does give out homework from the textbook, if you get any wrong you can correct them and the tests are open note, so very easy class to get a A!
Ms.Ada is an amazing professor! As long as you attend lecture and the notes you should pass the class. The exams are open note so make sure to use a journal. Super easy to get an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easiest class on the face of the earth. She's hilarious and gives you the world if you simply come to class and do the homework. Tests are open note and reviews make it so clear what is on it. SO SO EASYYYY

I really enjoyed having Ms. Ada. She made math very bearable. She gives weekly quizzes, but also provides help. Her tests are open note, so if you take good notes and show up to class you will have no problems. She gives really good reviews that are important to go to. Ms. Ada was a great teacher and I would definitely take her class again.

If you want an easy math class take her! As long as you show up to class consistently and stay on top of work it should be very easy. She truly cares about her students but you also need to show mutual effort. easy A

Professor Pratt is very helpful and tries to make sure that everyone understands the material. The tests are exactly like the reviews and open note. She is easy to asks questions to and grades relatively easy as long as you put in the effort. Showing up to class will almost ensure you an A in the class.

Ms.Ada is one of sweetest professors I have ever had. She truly cares about all of her students. Tests are open note, so not much studying is required. She is also is very accessible outside of class, she wants all of her students to do well. If you need this class, TAKE HER she's the best!

Literally the easiest math class I've taken since 6th grade. She actually is so good at explaining and wants you to understand the material. Exams are open note and quizzes are 1-2 easy questions. Homework is also easy and she's lenient at grading if you show your work. Attendance is required but literally I've never missed a class. TAKE HER

The Professor truly cares about making sure students have As in the course. Sometimes there are homework or Quizzes; however, it may be only 2-3 questions. When checking quizzes before grading, she helps you out. Make sure you attend, do homework, tests, and you will make an A.
Homework is straight out of textbooks-just a few problems a week. Quizzes are 2 questions each. Tests are open note and she does a review before the test

Professor Pratt cares a lot about the success of her students. She covers everything you need to know in her lectures, gives thorough test reviews, and the tests were open note. The only thing to keep in mind is that the homework is assigned verbally in class and is not listed on the syllabus, so make sure you pay attention during her lectures!
Professor Pratt was always available for help. She gave great review sessions for every test and all of the tests were open note.
She is really sweet. It can be hard to follow her sometimes, but if you pay attention you will be fine. The material is really easy.

I didn't miss a class but I'm pretty sure I didn't learn anything. Probably the worst teacher I've had in all of my education. If had the teacher's book I truly believe I could've taught the class better myself. She is not very helpful and will count correct answers incorrectly on tests. She makes the easiest class difficult. She has an accent.

Ms. Pratt was really nice and easy to talk to, but rather disorganized. Her curriculum was not well prepared. No quiz or exam dates on the syllabus, misplaced homework and quizzes, confused on the schedule... She's kind and genuinely cares, but is a poor teacher in my opinion. Class is extremely easy however, so you'll have no problem passing.

Professor Ada is a very funny and straight-to-the-point person! She explains things thoroughly and makes sure we all understand the material. Her reviews are like the tests so that makes it easier on studying it. Theres a good chunk of homework but nothing absurd, and the in class lectures are tiring but worthwhile. A real good professor.
Great professor. Give great feedback on essays. Lots of reading. Takes attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 10 journals and 3 essays determine your grade. Easy grader as long as you include everything on the rubric, he is very specific in what he wants. Allowed to skip 3 classes without penalty.

Mr. Gellings is a great professor! You have weekly discussion posts that are mainly opinionated and are graded super easy. Three big essays determine your grade, but he's really helpful with them and even lets you do corrections at the end of the year if you don't like your grade. He's also a great guy i enjoyed going to his class.

I loved Professor Gellings! Attendance is mandatory, but you can have 3 unexcused absences throughout the semester. If you complete the weekly assignment as well as the discussion board posts, you will be fine!!  Definitely my favorite class and I do not enjoy english at all so if that says something about the class, there you go!

Great teacher who cares about his students. Grade is determined by 3 essays, but he gives you plenty of time to write them and ensures that every student understands what is expected from the essay. He is very available and willing to help students with whatever they need.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! The class has 3 essays, however he helps you with any questions you have. He is very caring and understanding with his students. I would HIGHLY recommend you take his class when needing a LIT credit!

Best professor ever. He is so sweet and his class is enjoyable. Can easily do whatever you want during lectures (as long as you maintain a good grade which is easy). You have like one "journal" reflection a week- about 200 words. We only had 2 essays and 1 annotated bibliography about texts/movies of choice. Ended with a 100 along with many others.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: not a nice professor,

Professor was very nice and understanding... in his intro class. As soon as you start taking advanced classes with him, he becomes far more strict and tends to single people out.  He tends to stifle creativity for upper level students and has a hard time understanding boundaries and "netiquette".
I came to class 20 minutes late once and he was very cool about it. He is chill and flexible about deadlines and if you're having any issues with assignments, he is happy to help and give advice.

Amazing painting professor. So good at actually teaching, rather than just letting students paint without feedback. I loved this class. I put in a lot of work outside of class, but I'm really happy with how (almost) all my projects turned out. Great balance of structure vs flexibility. Super happy to be in that class. 100% will take again.

Adam is very helpful and cares about his students a lot. He makes a great effort to learn about everyone and make sure everyone is comfortable. He is very understanding of students time and allows you to work at your own pace-he offers guidance only when you ask and sees value in all his students artwork.
Adam is very knowledgable in his field and really cares about his students. He is always willing to lend a helping hand and I would highly recommend taking a class from him if you get the chance!

Dr. Babineau gives a clear view of what is required in her class. The quizzes are easy and she puts everything you need to know for her tests on her reviews. She does a great job of presenting her slides in class while not losing her audience. Taking her class has many benefits, including knowledge on psychology and an easy class to make an A.

This has been one of my favorite professors at TCU. You can tell she is passionate about what she teaches and does a good job of explaining things. I am excited to be taking another course from her coming up. Her exam reviews are EXTREMELY helpful and if you have questions she explains them thoroughly. She gives a good amount of extra credit.

Prof. Babineau was an okay teacher. She flies through her lectures and it was hard to grasp any information if you didn't study. The final paper was easy so you can definitely rake up points on that. DO THE EXAM REVIEWS! She always answered emails efficiently and was always kind enough to help out! Weekly homework (easy) and pop quizzes.

He's the most condescending person. He will absolutely degrade u and compare u to his family, BUT his class is engaging and pretty manageable. Just make sure u have patience and thick skin w him. Lots of textbook assignments, group projects, and his tests are so subjective. There absolutely are easier options, but if u have to take him its ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Whitworth is a super nice guy, but if you want an easy A, do not take this. He assigns weekly homework, attendance is mandatory, and his lectures are very boring. His tests are on the textbook and notes you fill out during class, but he is always very unclear about what specifically will be on the test, and they're hard to do well on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took his introduction to sociology class, and it was very test-heavy. You need to read the textbook, and class is mandatory. He is a sweet person, but I wouldn't recommend him if you want an easy core.
Very sweet, but harder applied testing curves, but overall very well and good class

Such a good, involved teacher. He wrote the textbook, but you really just need to study the notes he gives you in class to be prepared for the exams. The exams are not easy, but you get a review day before each exam. I enjoyed this class so much that I am now working towards my sociology minor.

Keith was a good professor in many ways but he just didn't care about the individual student. You could tell his tests are geared towards the holy bell curve which made the intro class my hardest class to get an A in. If you are taking this class to have a fun time learning something new but you don't want to have to work to hard don't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall good class, however, the tests were extremely difficult and entirely subjective. I studied multiple hours before an exame, just to find out that they were mostly true or false questions that were extremely subjective to a persons point of view. I do not recommend this class unless you're planning on a mediocre grade.

Dr. Whitworth is so kind and caring! It is clear that he genuinely wants to get to know his students. But, HIS EXAMS ARE SO HARD. They are in person and are all subjective and over information not always talked about during lectures.

Professor Whitworth's class is well-structured with engaging lectures and fair assessments. The online textbook is helpful, and using unstuckstudy AI alongside the readings makes studying straightforward. Attendance is mandatory, but the exams are manageable with proper preparation.

5 exams on your computer, 3/5 were open textbook (not note). Lectures-super boring but we played Monopoly once. No quizzes. Textbook completion. One Cultural Awareness assignment at the end where you have to depict how 12ish sociological factors are a part of your life in 150-250 words each but able to use chat gpt on this. Easier class but boring.

Dr. Whitworth is one of the sweetest professors and I always loved going to his class. He wrote the ebook you use and it is completely online. There are readings and quizzes every week but they're all in the textbook. If you do the readings the exams are straightforward. You have one paper and it's split up into two parts which he gives feedback on

You can simply attend class, listen, and pass. Attendance is taken. If you do the work which is very easy work, take good notes, and do the assigned textbook work you will get an A. He is willing to work with you and your schedule and offers SO MANY extra credit opportunities. It's an easy A and he's a good professor.

Dr. Whitworth is very kind and clearly wants his students to do well. Exams are very easy with most of them being open book, and there are many extra credit opportunities. The lectures are very interesting as well. The SociologicalYou textbook is very well written and easy to study. The class is a very easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Keith is literally my favorite teacher of this semester. He is hilarious and his class is very simple and easy to get an A in! His exams are pretty easy as long as you go over your notes and read the textbook (4 exams were open note). Hes very passionate about sociology and wants you to leave this class having a basic understanding! Loved him 10/10
He's genuinely a great guy and wants you to succeed. If you actually listen to the lectures you will do well in the class. He keeps content interesting too. Lots of extra credit, but exam heavy.

Amazing professor, really good personality. A lot of his tests are open book, they can be kind of difficult. Provides 5 bonuses that altogether boost your grade by 2%, only allows you to complete 2 the last 2 weeks of school. It might not seem worth it but trust me it is, you'll want all 5. Uses notes as attendance with an attendance sheet.

Notes have to be submitted for attendance daily, chapter certificates about weekly (can miss 2), 5 exams (some open note), & 1 writing assignment. Easy just pay attention. He's absolutely wonderful. You do learn and have a good time.

Dr. Whitworth was an amazing teacher! He is very intelligent when it comes to sociology and cares a lot about teaching. The class is easy as long as you keep up with the reading. You have 4 free absences, use them wisely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Really easy going guy and cares a lot about sociology. As long as you keep up with weekly work the entire class is really quite easy.

He is a great professor who I would take again. Attendance is mandatory but as long as you show up and take class notes you will be good. Tests are pretty neutral and he let 3/5 of them be open note. The final papers are manageable and he will even help you edit them if you turn them in early.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor! Reading the textbook and study guides extensively will make or break your grade! Give yourself at least two days of studying and you will ace the exams (3/5 were open book for our class). Two 500-word essays with plenty of time given; he also offered to read rough drafts early and provided feedback. Happy to have had him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is set up so that you read and submit a chapter certificate for the textbook as homework maybe once a week to be prepared for classes which are just lectures over the material, there's two papers due for the whole semester, and 5 exams (our class had 3 open note). He's a very kind and respectable person as well.

One of my favorite professors and I feel bad because people would use their phones during class. His assignments are pretty easy and make sure to take advantage of the bonus opportunities because it can really boost your grade. I will say his feedback on assignments was not that helpful, but the criteria were clear. Overall, dedicated professor.

Dr.Whitworth is by far the best professor you can take at TCU! He truly cares about what he's teaching and makes sure to provide current examples in his lectures. This year, he gave 5 exams and the exams are pretty easy in my opinion and it's possible to score a 100. Definitely take him if you want a professor who is accessible.
Take him you'll love him!!

Dr. Whitworth is a really great professor, who cares a lot about his students and is very understanding. His course is designed to really educate students and help them succeed. He offers bonuses throughout the semester that can help boost your grade.

Dr. Whitworth really cares about his students and the subjects he teaches. You have weekly homework, but its all completion and can be done quickly. 3/5 of his tests were open book(including final), and he gives clear and fantastic resources to study for the ones that aren't. You just have to prepare when it's needed and you'll get a good grade.

Whitworth is so nice and none of his assignments/tests were overwhelming. There is frequent HW but it's easy. Tests were open-book for us all semester when I had him, but I have heard students from the most recent semester say he didn't do this for all of their exams. If you do the work you'll get an A and none of it is too hard.
favorite professor. really takes the time to get to know everyone. He wrote his own textbook, so exams are all in there. Take him if you get the opportunity for intro to sociology!!!!

Dr. Whitworth is a really great professor. There are 5 exams throughout the semester and the last one is the final so it's not cumulative. Exams are both open and closed book. You have to complete certificates and worksheets but they aren't hard at all. Make sure to study for exams, but he also offers 2% extra credit to your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Whitworth is a nice guy and wants his students to succeed. However, for intro sociology, this class was too hard. You basically have to teach yourself which I did, and it did not help me do better on exams. He never goes over everything that will be on the test so you have to read the book thoroughly. Anyway, nice guy but would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ignore every past review of him, because his class is completely different now. Attendance is required and graded, and tests are all closed book now. His teaching is also biased and leans left. I don't have a problem when someone is left-leaning, but he teaches it in a condescending way as though he's the only correct one.

Dr. Whitworth is a great teacher, who cares about his students and is very understanding. he loves participation and when students ask questions. He offers many bonuses, so if you need an extra grade bump those will help. All in all an amazing teacher that I highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Whitworth is one of the sweetest professors at TCU and his class is super easy. Every week you have easy textbook assignments, which are practically completion. Tests are pretty easy and open book. If you don't show up to class he won't penalize you and he truly cares about his students.

He is kind of professor you can talk to about anything. He is so kind and cares so much about his students. I emailed him one day and told him I would miss class due to personal reasons and he met with me outside of class, and just talked about how I was doing. As for his class, you read the textbook and fill out a worksheet and take the test. Easy

This class is not hard at all if you read the textbook. All of the homework was online in the textbook. The textbook also gives you study guides that are similar to tests. Do homework and study for tests for an easy A. Also Whitworth is a very caring guy.

His class is very easy as long as you read the the book. Everything from the book is on the test and 4 out of the 5 tests we were allowed to use the book. You really only spend an hour doing work in his class for the whole week. Super easy class I would recommend everyone take it for an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Whitworth is an amazing teacher! He cares about his students and provides a safe and engaging learning space. We have open note (and sometimes open book) exams and quizzes. We also have a few writing assignments scattered throughout the semester, but these are very easy.

He is a sweet guy. You have to buy the textbook since he wrote it. He gives lots of extra credit, I am just too lazy to do it. You have to read the book, 1 quiz for every 1,5 weeks, and an exam for every 2 chapters. This class makes you work for it, and I learned a lot after this class. He is so caring

Dr. Whitworth is a very caring professor who is flexible with students if need be. There is a lot of textbook reading and the tests could sometimes be difficult, but if you study you'll be fine. He also allowed a lot of extra credit opportunities and gives many small daily/quiz grades to boost your grade.

Dr. Whitworth is very kind and lays out his expectations clearly, but I learned next to nothing in this class because he never gives a lecture of his own (he always brings in semi-relevant guest speakers or just lectures straight from the book) and goes off on tons of tangents. Most of the people in class didn't try.

Whitworth is a nice guy but his lectures don't make any sense. I literally taught myself everything from the textbook and still wouldn't get good grades because his tests are too specific. He also treats you like you're in middle school by giving you assigned seats and tokens when you're late. This class isn't worth the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's super friendly and cares about his students. Tests can be hard and extra credit is busy work, but the content is interesting. You only get a combined 5 absences and tardies so good luck

reviews.comment: Dr. Whitworth is literally one of the funniest Sociology professors at TCU. Attendance is mandatory but you'll enjoy the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Whitworth cares a lot about his students. He goes out of his way to make sure the learning is enjoyable and that everyone gets the most out of his class. Does not round. You must show up to get an A. Can be politically biased and teaches his opinion as fact.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Whitworth is so cool. You don't have to work super hard for Sociology but if you do, you'll get an A. He really cares about his student's mental health, and he is pretty funny. His lectures are really interesting, I got a lot out of this class.

Easy A as long as you show up and do the work outside of class. There are 8 tests (no cumulative final). The tests are annoying as they're all true/false or "select all that apply," but if you read the textbook, you'll get above an 85 % on every one. You can get up to 2% extra credit too. He's a good guy and cares a lot about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Whitworth is very specific about how he wants things done. There are eight tests and all of the questions were either true/false or "select all that apply". good i loved that
He is too hard and never test over what he taught

His tests can be difficult, but overall an A is achievable. Everything is based on the book, so you don't really have to listen to lectures because ALL YOU HAVE TO DO is study the book for the exams. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is pretty straightforward. There is homework every other day, but it is easy and the tests are simple enough as long as you read the chapters online. Dr. Whitworth is literally the best professor I have had at TCU. His class was so easy and fun. He really cares about each one of his students. Even a year after I took his class he still says hi to me if I see him. Would definitely take.

This class was definitely challenging but if you work for it & do the extra credit, you can get an A. READ THE BOOK. He wrote it so the most of the test questions come straight from it. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is an overall good teacher. The tests are overall pretty easy. Class notes are picked up after every class. There is homework every other day. He does give a lot of extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Whitworth is one of my favorite professors ever. He has an extensive knowledge about everything and shares so much with you. His tests can be tricky but if you do his reviews and take good notes in class you'll be fine. Hilarious teacher and his lectures are very interesting. 5 skips and you get 10% off your grade so go. Great sociology class!

reviews.comment: I didnt care for Dr. Whitworth at first, but after a couple weeks I learned to love him. He is a witty guy and hilarious once you get to know his humor. The only reason you have to show up is because he takes attendance, read the textbook and you'll do fine on tests. Nice guy, he'll respond to your emails and help if you go to his office.

The class is significantly harder than you would expect an intro to sociology class to be. The tests are all choose all that apply and true/false.
