Professor Anglin has been my favorite at TCU so far. His lectures are short and interesting. He is charismatic in class but also very kind and thoughtful one on one. He is helpful on projects and clearly cares about his students. He can be hard to please on projects so be prepared for that, but it is because he wants you to get better.

Anglin is a great professor who wants everyone to succeed. He is helpful at providing feedback and answering questions for the project. His lectures can be boring and he knows it (he tries to make them as quick and painless as possible). He is fun yet serious and cares about his students.

Lots of reading/hw/quizzes, as there is lots of material to cover. Much interesting insight on the Hebrew Bible, but can sometimes derail the lecture by going in-depth answering questions or opening them to classroom discussion. Would be helpful to organize whiteboard notes better, but his writing is legible! Personable, approachable, good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He was a very kind man and I learned a lot from this class considering I knew just about nothing in regard to the Bible. You definitely have to read in order to pass because he gives a pop quiz every week. There were only two tests but they are pretty tough but as long as you study you should get at least a B. The final project was not my favorite.

Great instructor.  Quizzes are from the reading assignments for that day.  Doesn't grade them too hard, just wants to know you are reading.  Tests are tough, but there are only two.  Extensive group project, but you have the entire semester to do it.  Can only miss 3 days of class.  No homework, just reading the textbook.  Overall a great teacher.

Coming into the class, I really wasn't interested in the Bible, but Dr. Serino made it interesting. He did give 10 pop quizzes throughout the year but he didn't grade them hard at all. The two tests were meh, I paid attention and did fine. The end of the year project left everyone kind of directionless, but we worked through it.

My favorite part is the fact she doesn't believe in buying textbooks, she will always find a free pdf or text to read. The reading load is a lot but it's not hard and for essays she always gives the chance to redo or fix your grade if you aren't satisfied. She is probably the best professor I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 5 books in the semester and one quiz per book, a midterm and the final. TBH I didn't read a single one of the books. To get an A in this class you MUST show up. Take very detailed notes (literally write down everything she says) write down the page numbers she talks about and you will be fine. Get ther online version of the book to command F

Dt. Abunasser is a great professor! She is very intelligent and her lectures are very good. She grades very leniently. The only homework is to read, which isn't 100% necessary, but definitely encouraged. There are not many grades, but enough to give some wiggle room. Attendance is for a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: dr. abunasser is amazing! attendance isnt required but if you dont read the books AND dont go to class you will not be successful. her lectures are very insightful! she is so knowledgeable about literature! quizzes every week over reading but they are short and easy. 3 major tests in the semester. she is seriously so sweet! take her class!!

Dr. Abunasser is a wonderful, sweet woman and an amazing teacher. She is one of the few professors I have who actually checks in with her students before every class and truly cares. In her lectures, she is so eloquent in speech and really connects the literature we read to the real world. I will definitely miss her class!

This woman is so well educated and so kind. She would cancel several of our classes and cancel some quizzes when we were stressed out. All you really have to do for this class is read, but that isn't even really necessary. As long as you know a little bit about the books you will be fine.

Dr. Abunasser is amazing! I looked forward to her class every week. The books she gives are interesting and discussion/class goes quickly. There is a good amount of reading and writing involved but you are going to get that with any English class, especially an Honors one. She is very caring and the class is engaging. I would definitely recommend!

Intimidated by this class at first, but ended up getting a lot out of it. Definitely lots of reading but books aren't bad. Class is discussion based so participation is key. Cares about her students and is willing to work with them. Clearly very knowledgeable, but still easy to follow. Not much work besides the readings, fair grader on assignments.

Dr. Abunasser is an amazing lecturer, and if you pay attention, you will 100% learn something new, even if you don't expect to. However, if you aren't down to write short papers or hate lectures (why are you in college?) you might have a difficult time. Otherwise, she is fun, the readings are EXCELLENT, and the quizzes are really easy if you read
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: SHE IS AMAZING! Ignore the other people commenting negatively on her. This class is easy, and those who say it was hard CLEARLY DID NOT READ!!! You are in college for gods sake!! Learn to follow the syllabus and learn to read the assigned pages. If one cannot read 60 pages, then how are you going to survive the real world with a real job?!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Did not like her at all. The class was boring and does not respond to emails. Grades hard, either she likes you or she doesn't ! do NOT take professor Abbunnaser whatever her name is BOOKS ARE SO BORING. Chose books that had magical powers, curses, etc I reported her to the department for not responding to emails
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Amazing class and even more amazing prof! 5 pretty interesting books and the class is all discussion based. Grades are from participation (discussion), 3 exams, a group presentation, and 5 pop quizzes (1 per book). As long as you read and show up you'll be fine! Reading is about 50 pages per class, sometimes shorter, rarely longer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took this class because I heard it was easy, def not easy. You have to read around 60+ pages every night. Doesn't respond to emails. GRADES HARD. Takes points off for every little thing. The class was just not interesting unless you like reading about magical powers and African Literature.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I learned so much from Dr. Abunasser and I sincerely enjoyed her class! There are five books that you read throughout the semester, and expect a pop quiz over the previous night's reading once for each book. But they're not hard and neither are her 3 exams. Highly recommend her class! She is super nice and very educated on so many cool topics!

Dr. Abunasser is one of the best professors I have ever had. She leads discussions on difficult topics with grace and skill, and makes tough ethical issues accessible to students who might come into her class prepared to feel defensive or dismissive of the subject matter. Do your reading, come prepared to ask questions, and you will do well.

She is a very involved professor and while attendance can impact your grade, she is very understanding about missing. It is a very laidback class and she is a really easy grader. She has pop quizzes and they are based on just the most recent reading. She makes the class fun and interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Abunasser for Global Women's Literature. There is a lot of reading, but the books are all good reads. There are pop quizzes almost every week, but as long as you read you will be fine. She offers extra credit opportunities and she is super nice if you come to her office hours for help. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Abunasser is an incredible professor. She is hilarious and makes you feel comfortable during class discussion. Her class is discussion-based and it is focused on the readings she assigns for each class, which is about 50 pages, but she asks interesting questions and adds insightful commentary. Would highly recommend!
Take her, take her, take her! Dr. Abunasser is awesome. You will enjoy her class, fall in love with the books, and laugh with her good sense of humor. Definitely recommend this professor.

I LOVED HAVING ABUNASSER! She's funny, sweet, and provides very interesting novels for the class. She is very passionate and knowledgable about the course so thats a plus. As long as you read and study, you will do great. Also went to her office hours and she was so sweet and helpful! TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved this teacher. Not a big fan of reading/ English and she made is very interesting. If you go to class and put in effort you will do well. She is understanding and so sweet and wants her student to do well. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved this class. There's a good amount of reading, but it's all very interesting. I loved this class and I would highly recommend that you take her. You just have to keep up with the readings and listen in class. If you take notes and pay attention, tests are fairly easy.

By far one of my favorite professors ever. She is intelligent, funny, and makes the class enjoyable. I have had her for two english classes now and am upset I can't take any more before I graduate. Not taking a class from Dr. Abunasser would be a mistake. She is extremely helpful and wants everyone to succeed. Brilliant professor.

Best professor I have had at TCU. The books & in-class discussions are so interesting you will fall IN LOVE with reading. She has a great sense of humor and keeps you engaged. The class is a lot of reading but go in for office hours and she will help you SO MUCH.

Dr. Abunasser is AMAZING. If you love reading, this is the professor for you. Even if you don't, she picks such interesting books, you'll probably still love it. She does random pop quizzes, but they're easy if you read. The essays are where a lot of people have trouble, but as long as you're clear and understand the concepts, you'll be okay.

I had Dr. Abunasser for Honors Global Women's Lit. She is one of the best professors I've had at TCU! No tests or quizzes - all discussion so participation is important. One big project and final essay, but she grades pretty easily. Most students didn't read all the novels and still got A's. So inspirational and her lectures are eye-opening!

Loved her Global Women's Lit class! There's a lot of reading, but the books are pretty interesting. She gives random pop quizzes, but as long as you do the reading you're fine. Plus she drops one at the end of the semester and offers tons of EC opportunities. She's hilarious and an amazing professor. Would 100% recommend taking one of her classes!

Her class is freaking easy as long as you go. Her essay prompts on test will be exactly the same as questions she asked and answered in class so as long as you take a few notes on the questions she thinks is important than you will be fine. I got an A and put in minimal effort, everyone can get an a.

She is a great teacher, passionate about her job and the subject. As long as you keep up you'll be fine. She's not a harsh grader and gives very useful criticism. Defiantly recommend taking her if you're looking for a Lit core class. Interesting readings are chosen
As long as you do your work, come to class and complete your readings you will be fine.  She is an amazing teacher.

Dr. Abunasser is a great professor. She requires alot of readings but they are interesting. She does random pop quizzes so you must read to pass. She is very helpful and will try to help you the best way she can.
Great Professor, have had her a couple of times and her classes are great.  If you are a able take SATIRE with her it is the best class at TCU.
Easy easy class, got a 100 or above one every test, reading is required and random in class pop quizzes kinda suck

LOTS of reading, but if you can keep up with it, then you'll do well in the class.  Fall behind just one day, and it will hurt you.  She gives pop reading quizzes.  Her discussions are SUPER helpful when it comes to the exams which are all open book online.  The most difficult part of the course is the paper you have to write over a movie.

Great Professor. You have to put in the time and effort, but she rewards it.  People who say she's hard pass/failed the class and thats why their grades are low.  She is very rewarding towards those who show legitimate interest in the class.  A is very achievable and B is near given with effort.

Dr. Abunasser is a good but tough professor. You have to read multiple books (with usually 50-70 pgs assigned each day). She gives quizzes throughout the semester so you have to go to class. She presents the information very clearly in class but is a tough grader when it comes to the tests and the paper you have to write. Hard work but interesting.

VERY DIFFICULT CLASS especially when English and writing are not your thing. 50-75 pages assigned reading each class... quizzes on material so reading is mandatory and essential for your grade. Test are essays but she is very hard grader. Do not recommend if you are not willing to put into A LOT of time.

English has never been my favorite subject but she made it really interesting.  There is a lot of work and reading, but she does a good job at picking a good variety to appeal to everyone.  No tests, just papers and she grades tough, but gives you the opportunity to rewrite.  She is always available for extra help and I enjoyed going to class.

Oh Rima is the bomb.com, class is interesting and there were 4 papers/projects instead of tests. She really like class participation which makes class a lot more interesting. I was borderline and she was nice enough to bump me since I hdnt mssd class

Class was very interesting.  I actually enjoyed going.  Abunasser is really great teacher and nice person. There is a heavy amount of reading but if you miss a reading or two and come to class for the lecture, you will be fine.

She is one of the BEST professors I've had at TCU!  I took her last semester for Major British Writers and looked forward to her class every TR.  She's SO smart and I love the way she holds class and how she organizes it.  Her tests were really hard, but if you studied and read and really took interest in it, you got an A!  Taking her again (:

MY FAVORITE CLASS AT TCU SO FAR! I took her for soph comp. arab women's lit..she is so incredibly knowledgeable and makes class so interesting. I loved it! Go to class and read the assigned reading and you are good to go :) Also participate in class discussions but DEFINITELY TAKE THIS PROF! I LEARNED SO MUCH AND HAD SO MUCH FUN!

This is my 2nd semester taking her,& I will again. Read if you want A. There are quizzes to see if you did your reading assignment, but never on poetry or subjective material. She's VERY clear on what she expects & happy to help her students. I've learned a LOT from her & LOVED this class.  Found the material HIGHLY useful. TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!

Intro to Fiction; Simply FANTASTIC. She is very passionate about the subject, and highly knowledgeable. Do your readings and show up to class, and you will receive your A. She is a great professor, and I recommend her to EVERYONE. Very fair grader as well. All around the best class of my fall semester. GREAT GREAT Professor.

This was a short 8 week class, so the classes were long at 3 hours each, but the professor was extremely knowledgeable about the subject and was fair about grading.  If you came to class and read the texts you got an A.

I had him in 2004,he gave me a C and not a D because I was so heartbroken for this reason:  my friend died in Iraq that year and out of all of the professors, he was the only one who lent me a gracious hand in understanding; he even cried.  i will always remember Dr. Ledek.  Thank you.

Kind of goofy.  Definitely a Christian as tried to make it not obvious in the last section, but was very obvious to me. Read the book and you will be fine.... last test is the only hard one, and huge, easy extra credit opportunity.  Easy A if you study and read a little before each test and that's all you do!
Stfu!  Dr. Ledek gave me a C when I had a low D in his course.  Don't diss the white bearded professor!
This class was very easy if you paid attention in class. Reading wasn't all that important. The notes you take in class are the most important and the tests are all easy.

This class is so confusing. I make great grades but I just couldn't get a grasp on this. He tries to be funny, but class feels like it's hours long. Don't bother with the book, he teaches his own stuff. If you think abstractly and don't have to have any form of organization - this class is for you.

Critical Thinking Class - He's a great guy. Kinda weird at first but you stick with it, his persona grows on you. His willingness to help exceeds most, but he is not always too clear. Gives a big extra credit opportunity. It's a required class and he's the only one teaching it. What else can ya do?
in my opinion, he is not a very good instructor. he is kind of wierd. all i did was draw, it felt like a waste of time, so i dropped the class.
he is weird. and sometimes nonsensical. class is pointless. read. do extra credit. play crosswords in class. you'll be fine.
Ledek is cool, but I never knew what the hell he was talking about in class.  Do the EC and you'll be fine.
he's kinda weird, but funny, couple of hard tests and do the extra credit. his classes aren't that helpful, and his tests are a little confusing. didnt learn anything out of this class
Great professor, kinda wierd, but very helpful, and easy class as long as you study a little.
if your brain thinks this way, it's not that bad. i need more concrete things, so it was hard for me.. the classes are pretty boring but he tries to be funny. i dont think i learned too much.
One hard test, 2 easy tests. If you do the extra credit you are sure to get an A.
He is very boring and confusing, does not help, but his class is not hard, take good notes, dont buy the book. Do the extra credit.

Hardly any homework, easy open book tests, a couple excused absences a semester, easy grader. Professor John sends you lectures to watch at home and then talks about more interesting, specific stuff in class. Projects were super manageable.

Dr. John was great. She was rudely blunt a few times in class this semester but often apologized after so I think it is something she is working on. She grades a little rough but it is very easy to still turn in A-deserved assignments. Open-note exams and quizzes, interactive lectures, and overall sweet professor, Would take again.

Took Dr. John for Human Behavior and Social Environment. Great class! Dr. John has mastered the structure of an online course. She keeps the class engaged and wants feedback on what is and isn't working for the class. 
Participate, ask questions, and start a class text thread because it is fast-paced. Class topics were super interesting!
Take this class! There is pretty minimal work outside of class and it's not difficult at all. Lectures are kind of boring sometimes, but she tries to make them interactive. Worth it for an easy A!

Dr. John is great! The class can be kind of boring sometimes, but it is not hard. The tests are open note. There are graded activities at least once a week, but they're usually easy. I would recommend her! She is very nice and understanding.

Professor John is great & this class is very easy to navigate. Watch the panoptos, complete in class notes and you will be fine on all quizzes, graded activities & assessments. Everything is open note, open book but you do not actually need to purchase the textbook. She is very sweet, open to opinions, and values her students. I highly recommend!

Dr. John is so kind! She will answer any questions you have. She also is very clear about what she expects from you so there is no confusion. Her classes are fun and she is always willing to make changes if you find something unfair.

Dr. John is great! We had 3 papers, along with 3 exams which were open book/notes. YOU DON'T NEED THE TEXTBOOK! Literally, all material is from the class lectures. The Global Briefs were very fun to do, and she allows for creativity. The case study paper (the final) was pretty straightforward, and she is always open to answering questions. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It was an easy grade, but I found this class to be very frustrating. A lot of the activities are embarrassing and annoying. It felt like a high school class. Had to watch lectures and take notes at home before class, and spend most of class doing an activity. There is no textbook, just do the assignments and get the attendance grade.
I love Dr. John! Her courses do have a lot of work, however, she is a fair grader. Her lectures are worth it too!

Seems like she has a bit of a god complex. Not a very approachable teacher. She takes emails very seriously, In my email I addressed her as Professor instead of Dr. and she replied that she wouldn't answer until I used Dr. VERY STRANGE. It's almost like she's praying on ur downfall. i made an 89.7 and she wouldn't round it.

She isn't a bad teacher but she isn't approachable. Instructions aren't very clear, but if you have questions don't email because she'll never respond. Tough grader on papers - really tough. She marks off random things for projects?? BUT she let's you re-do your papers for partial credit!! & you NEED to go to class

I would not say that she is a bad professor but i would say approach with caution. She does not allow any electronics in class, even if you have your books on a tablet or ipad. Her power points are ok but you NEED to read if you want to pass her test. she does drop 10 of the 30 class activity sheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Chimbel is so funny! He takes some getting used to but once you get going in the class you will love it! There are weekly pop quizzes over the news so make sure you are keeping up with whats going on. There are also weekly reading quizzes that add up.
Professor Chimbel LOVES jokes. He won't get annoyed if you ask him a million questions because he is here to help. And you BETTER know his three things: don't assume, get it right and no cliches.
Cares a lot.

Aaron Chimbel is awesome. As are hard, but possible. He's not one of those teachers that just refuses to give As. He's helped me out even after Multimedia, and is just a great mentor overall when it comes to packages, journalism, or the job search.

Aaron Chimbel is one of the best professors at TCU. He is so invested in students and inspires a love for JOUR. He went completely out of his way for me in enormous ways not once, but TWICE as my advisor. I know he helps students who aren't his advisees if they build a relationship with him. Not an easy A at all, but so worth it. He is the best!

He's a really nice guy that knows what he's talking about. His tests can be tough but if you study you will do just fine. He doesn't provide a lot of help or extra information, but he does provide study guides. Come to class bc news quizzes and reading quizzes count. Overall a good teacher!
Multimedia is a challenging and time consuming class but Chimbel is very helpful and wants to make you a better reporter.
Easy class and a good teacher. If you study for a couple of hours you should make a A or B on the tests. Show up to class because news and reading quizzes(easy) are 20% of final grade
Incredibly nice guy who loves what he's teaching. Completely willing to help you always. Make sure you attend class for clicker quizzes (basically every day). Great guy, easy class.

Prof. Chimbel really knows his stuff.  He uses power points that relate directly to the "Intro. to Journalism" book, and class discussions for the "Elements of Journalism" book.  Read the "Elements" book, because the points from the quizzes really add up! Also, there are news quizzes, so pay attention to the news! I recommend his class.

Like all intro classes, this one covers so much that it's hard to keep track sometimes. Tests were harder than expected. News quizzes and Elements (the book) quizzes can destroy your grade if you don't read or know the news. "No powerpoint" Friday's were so boring.

Chimbel is awesome! This class can be pretty boring at times, but all the ppts are posted to eCollege and the only test is the final.  If you have a question he's extremely helpful.  If you are considering a journalism major, he is a great introductory professor.

The class is pretty boring, but all the lessons are posted to eCollege. He is nice, but some of the classes felt pointless. Doesn't give a clear understanding of what you'll be studying as a Journalism Major. His lessons are very easy and simple. The News quizzes are also easy if you stay informed and he gives bonuses sometimes.

Chimbel is great and the class is pretty fun. There is a midterm, final, and 2 projects. Both the projects are pretty easy and he is very helpful if you ask him questions. Newsquizzes every week so you have to go to class b/c it is worth a good chunk of your grade. I really loved this class. Take it!

Intro to Journalism class was great. There are exams that need to be studied for and current events quizzes keep you on your toes. Chimbel is a great professor and wants you to succeed. One of the younger professors at TCU, but very knowledgeable. Becomes a great friend/ally. Highly recommend.

He's a hottie... Takes attendance every class and gives a news quiz every week. No tests, just a big paper and final project. I think he's a pretty good teacher. And you don't really have to pay attention in class. Easy A if you do extra credit

Good professor, but as others have said, not an easy grader. Means well and is smart, but it won't be a blowoff class. Could stand to teach how to shoot/edit video by example--he kind of explains then pushes you out the door.
Loved him! Hard grader on writing, but learned so much and loved his classes!
So hot, he's SCALDING!!!!
Great instructor, funny and very helpful. At first it seems he is being very critical of your writing but it helps you get better. Everyone did well in the class. Take him!
No Comments
Media Writing & Editing II.  He's a good teacher. He graduated from TCU and works for channel 8. Workload isn't too hard and class never lasts for the full  time. He's helpful with assignments.
LOVE HIM. no notes. he made phonetics so fun

Dr. Campos has a student-centered teaching style. He always makes sure everyone is on the same page before moving to the next material. He is patient and makes sure to answer all the questions that we have.

He is a caring professor, and accessible outside class for any question which I like. I consider him an easy professor this may seem desirable, but this can negatively impact student learning and preparedness especially if you are taking this for your major. If his lectures were designed to challenged us in the major I would feel better off.

I took him for A&P of the speech and hearing mechanisms. It's a lot of busy work and packets, so be prepared. Exams are take-home and open-note. There's a lot of info, but that's just A&P. He's very funny and understanding. Attendance isn't mandatory, but we do labs every class, so missing one can lower your grade.

Dr.Campos is extremely helpful during in-class practice, is willing to answer any questions, and is accessible outside of class. Attendance is not mandatory (you won't get points taken off) but going over the slides in class and practicing with the class helps. Your grades are based on evaluations, but you can re-attempt any skill on future evals.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Campos is great! He wants his students to do well and is super funny. Phonetics is not easy, however, he makes sure everyone understands the material and takes time doing reviews and practice before test days. Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This is by far the hardest course I have ever taken, I do not recommend. This class is only graded based on quizzes and tests. I kept a B average the whole class and one test that was not multiple choice and required you to transcribe words based on his audio files, dropped me to a D.

Attendance is necessary. Mr. Campos is quick to respond via emails, and is willing to meet with students outside of class. Your grade depends on how well you do on the exams. There are no options for extra credit and are no other assignments, but if you study and do the work, you'll pass. Buying a workbook is necessary, and practicing.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class overall is not too difficult, the poetry unit is just extremely confusing. I wouldn't stop that from me taking the class however. Come to class prepared, participate with your opinion, and you will do well.

He is a funny teacher who tries to make class interesting. You have to read before getting to class and the tests are not easy but they are reasonable. He wants you to participate and is okay with mistakes while you are speaking.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Assignments are simple and the class is interesting. Exam guides and project instructions are clear. Can be draining when he goes on a tangent though - the class often ran the full time or over on a 3-hour seminar. My favorite part was the interview project

This class is lectured in all Spanish & you must attend in order to understand what is going on in each unit. Komla assumes that you have all previous knowledge on each conjugation and instead just teaches the difficult exceptions and weird nuances for each tense. You need to have a good grammar background if you are going to do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The entire class he speaks in Spanish, nothing wrong with this just a struggle on occasion to remember or fully understand what he's currently lecturing on. Gives handouts and notes before the test that will help if you do them. puts heavy emphasis on participation in the class which is tough, if your not sure what's going on or struggle with speak

Africa through Film is a perspective-changing class. With his laid-back and heavily discussion-based style of teaching, it's not stressful at all. He's funny, he cares, and he is very good at engaging students in deep discussions about relevant topics. Take him if you can.

best teacher ive ever had for spanish. he is really encouraging. as long as you do every assignment and participate in class  you're basically guaranteed an A. Hes really funny and sweet and open minded. We talk about really relevant topics

Dr. Aggor is very knowledgable on Africa considering this is where he was originally from. A great professor who is always willing to help. This class will teach you a lot about Africa, while it is not stressful because grading is relatively easy. A super nice guy too!

he's a great prof who is always willing to help. my view on the world is so different now after his class. you watch a documentary in each class and the tests are not too bad. reading isn't bad either. he is helpful because he really wants everyone to understand the topics we discuss in class, lots of discussion

Great Prof! He is really funny and makes the class enjoyable. Plus, I think my Spanish really got better in his class. He seems like an all around nice guys and that he really cares about what he's doing. Take him if you have the chance!

Dr. Aggor is so passionate about what he does and it reflects in his teaching. Discussions were always on relevant and current topics like politics or culture and no class was boring. I had reservations in speaking Spanish in front of class without prior preparation, but he's more than helpful with conjugations & never intimidating. TAKE HIS CLASS!

Incredible professor. Very engaging, entertaining, and fun classes. All of the material comes from the lectures and research papers, so attendance is important. He uploads lecture recordings, which are helpful for reviewing material and if you miss class. Exams are both memorization and application, and quizzes over the papers.

This seminar would be once a week where we would go over the documents we had read for the week. We already knew what questions he would bring up so we prepared for class. The book for the semester was long, but very interesting. Had to make a discussion post on it each week as well as new discoveries about cancer. Graded final paper easy. Take him

Biology of cancer is very interesting once a week class. It is a simple discussion over topics read for that week. There is a long book to read over the course of the semester, but it is very interesting. The assignments are discussions on the book as well as new findings on cancer once a week. One presentation is given. Final paper graded easy

Dr. Akkaraju is kind and funny, and he will always help in office hours and after class during q&as. His slides in cell bio were difficult and he didn't always make them available until right before lecture, but overall I'd recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Akkaraju is funny and wants to make sure students understand the material. If you're struggling because of the fast pace of the class, go to office hours and he is super helpful.

Dr. Akkaraju was a great professor. He sometimes was hard to follow because he made mistakes during lectures, often contradicting himself. He also talks very fast so I recommend relistening to the recordings he posts after each lecture. He was helpful in office hours and tries to get to know you as much as possible. You have to work for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Akkaraju really knows his stuff and is pretty helpful in office hours. If you want an A in this class you gotta be next level.. exams are tough for all three profs and Luque's are word terribly so it makes it that much more difficult. Misamore has the easiest section to score well in. B is attainable but tough to get, C is very manageable.
Relisten to lecture and talk to him outside of class. So kind, caring, SO SMART, funny and inspirational. Definitely makes you work for your grade, but you'll be proud of yourself after it all.

Great lectures, he makes a point to know your name and keep the class involved. Test material is mostly from lecture, he pulls some from the readings and questions he asks you to look up outside of class. Not an easy class, but if you put in the effort he will reward you with the same effort in helping you.

Dr. Akkaraju is amazing at taking a complicated concept and explaining it in one sentence. He requires a lot from his students, but if you study and re-listen to the lectures, an A is easily obtainable.

Best teacher for Intro Bio first semester. He simplifies difficult concepts really well. Definitely show up for class and take notes. After each class, relisten to his lecture before the next class and write down details you missed. Study his powerpoints and lecture notes. His tests consists of alot of 'all of the above' choices, so study details

Dr. Akkaraju is an amazing professor. He explains things really well and always  answers questions well. However, because he explains things so much in lecture, if you don't show up your test grade will feel it. He gives a lot of examples that aren't in the notes. I can't stress enough how well he explains things. Also, he's a pretty hilarious guy.

Intro Bio is a team taught class and I thought Akkaraju's section was the easiest. He is very good at making complex concepts simple. He tells his students what will be on the test. The material is difficult, but if you study and get help you should do fine. I highly recommend listening to old lectures and reading the textbook.
Akkaraju is the man! Although he was difficult, he presented the information in a clear way. I learned a lot from him.
Dr. Akkaraju actually made people look forward to coming to class. He is super helpful and funny, but his section was the hardest for me. I would say he was my favorite professor this semester.
He's really funny, great step up from Dr. Hale (who taught the first section) only thing is that the test was extremely hard.

Definitely my favorite of the biology professors! He has a lot of hard material to cover but he presents it in a really clear way that you can understand. He is also funny and makes an extremely long class entertaining. But you do still have to study and show up
I LOVE THIS MAN! He's a great teacher and will stop to clarify anything during class. Everyone looked forward to class. He's hilarious and actually made biology interesting.

One of my favorite teachers at TCU. This Honors Biology class (for pre-med people) is very difficult and is committee taught. Hale, Akkaraju, Hartman are first semester. Horner, Misamore, Chumchal are second semester. No matter who teaches this class, it's extremely difficult. Weed out class. Interesting, lots of studying, but fun.

His two sections of Cell Bio were absolutely ridiculous. He did not test on what he talked about in class and his questions were NOT straight forward. The last exams average was a 65 and the highest was an 84. If that doesn't speak for itself I don't know what will.

Great class. I took AP bio senior year. Heavy specific details. I got a C, but could have gotten a B if I didn't miss 2 quizzes for the lab.  The labs are easy grades except the exams, but if you review the quizzes your fine. I only crammed for 2 nights (total of 14 hours) before each exam and did alright. So study more than that and you'll do fine

He is the easiest of all the five that you will have teaching you.  I took several AP sciences before this class but this is not just an honors science. Don't think that if you have had an AP class or bio that you will walk in and easily make an A or B. You need to know now that you will study an average of 10 hours a week if you want an A or B!!!

The class is tough. If you took an AP Biology in high school you could pull off a B, or an A if you are a really good test taker. For those who haven't had any previous college level prep in bio, Good Luck. Your GPA might suffer from it. But after all, it is one of the hardest freshman classes at TCU. Hartman's test questions are Satin.

I think compared to hartman and misamore, akkaraju is THE BEST! his test questions are much easier and straight forward compared to the other two and explains things really well during class. The class is hard but akkaraju is a great professor and tries not to make it harder then it already is by writing tricky test questions

He is really fun to listen to but makes extremely difficult tests. Make sure you have lots of time to study if you are going to take his honors bio class. Its his class but there are 5 teachers so tests made up by that many people are really strange and difficult to switch from teacher to teacher personalities. Hard to know what to study.
He is very helpful...study from day one...at least an hour every class...rewrite notes & go to EVERY class!  I have a B.
He is really cool but his testing style is SO HARD AND TRICKY. I reccommend NOT taking this class. It was so hard I'm currently failing.

Dr. Akkaraju is THE best. He makes the class interesting and is so funny. The tests are not easy but you can definitely make a good grade if you really strive for it. I thoroughly prefer him over all the other professors that share the class. Definitely go to his office hours, if only to meet him.
easily one of the best professors at TCU! Very approachable, helpful, and has a since of humor! Also, he knows his course is rigorous, and is still encouraging!

He is very helpful...He gives a curve at the end of the course...He is really funny and is always eager to help students. The clss is not an easy A class, but if yu study hard and keep up with the material you can get an A or a B...You have to memorize lots of things!!!
He is the best Prin. of Life Sciences porfessor.  He is very helpful, and despite what some may say, he is very clear and thorough!!
Akkaraju is awesome. He's tough but hes a great prof. I think hes secretly crazy, which makes things more interesting. He was a biohazzard bag for halloween. It was awesome.

He is an excellent professor! His lectures are easy to understand and you can use the book as a supplemental tool. I really slacked off but he helped me bring my grade up from a F to a C!! Go talk to him if you have any problems he is more than happy to help.
No Comments

Extremely nice professor.  He knows what he is talking about.  Notes are essential in order to catch important details on exams.  Reading will definitely help you understand the material even more.  Please don't skip because your grade will be destroyed (trust me, some of my buddies didn't survive...lol).
His questions are hard and complicated, but he's very helpful and speaks perfect English so don't worry about any strong accents.
Dr. Akkaraju can be very helpful if you let him know you need it. I like how he teaches and I think he offers the most interesting classes at TCU, especially upper level bios.
He is very hard for those who find studying doesn't come easy, or who have a life outside the thick textbook. You got to do what you got to do if you want to get into med school.
he's a sweetie

I love Dr. A! He's probably one of my favorite professors at TCU. He is always willing to help and it's quality help. His tests can be tricky but if you study and know the material, you will be fine. The most important thing to do is go to class and ask questions. Not only is he a great professor, he's a really nice guy and is really funny!
He is probably one of my favorite professors ever! He is always willing to help and it's quality help. The class was hard but you learned so much by the end of the semester.
He is so informative and is one of the ONLY bio professors that cares about what you make in the class... I have learned so so much!
I love this class...it's hard but all the professors are really great, especially Dr. Akkaraju!

Dude, it's premed.  Either step up or get out.  It only gets harder after this and Dr. Akk only better prepares you for what's to come.  He's really interested in teaching you everything you want to know about biology and he loves to help anyone who asks, but you have to put forth the effort. PS He's really funny!

His series of professors were unclear on what they were expecting. He did not teach that well but I do agree that he is a nice guy. This class is hard and study a lot. But if you want to party don't take because this class will kill your GPA. Nerds do well, Greeks do well if they study and Party no studying greeks like me bite the dust
HE DOES TO CRZY TEST QUESTIONS (ALL OF THE ABOVE, A AND B ONLY, CAND D ONLY) THOSE ARE NOT FUN :(
His test questions are killer.

His tests killed your GPA? More like your lack of studying killed your GPA. He's doesn't teach art - it's premed Bio. He REALLY cares about us, and tries to answer questions at every turn. The content is tough, and you have to work at it. But I hear from upperclassmen it help down the line (MCAT).

He is a cool guy, and he knows his stuff.  If you talk to him you can tell he really has an interest in his students.  He does a good job of teaching what you need to know, yet keeping the atmosphere light.
awful teacher doesnt help you learn and is unreasonably hard on tests.  tests dont come from lecture and the tiniest print you can find in the book.

Nice guy, but hard to understand and hear him in a big lecture room. His powerpoint is helpful but is way too wordy. Too much material and too little time. His tests are very tricky but not impossible

you have to go to all of the classes to do good in this class, it helped me to read the book before lectures then study the lecture notes for a couple of hours after each class. requires a lot of studying, and make sure and stay on top of it instead of just before an exam or quiz

i enjoyed his lectures.  an extended nap actually caused me to miss one and i was actually disappointed beyond the obvious repercussions. you will be fine in this course if you stay on top of the lectures by studying often rather than just studying before a quiz or exam even if it's like a week.
The class was difficult, but if you study thoroughly, and EVERYTHING, then there's not sweat.  The problems come in when you procrastinate.  Fun class, Good professor.
Great professor!!  Powerpoint lectures but some notes on the side.  Overall, if you go to class and read the powerpoint handouts then you shouldn't have a problem.  This goes for all his classes.
Great teacher!  Extremely clear and structured.  If you can not handle him, he can't handle much else in Biology.
he's funny and makes efforts to help us but his tests will kill you
this guy is a jerk and his tests killed my gpa
He is a very good teacher, but the class is really hard. Study, study, study for the tests. You have to know the material almost as well as he does. Really nice guy though.
Good teacher, he knows how to explain the material in a way that helps you learn and if you are dumb enough to not get it he will take extra time to make sure you.
Very good lecture professor.  Has good explanations!
Honors bio wasnt as hard as expected, you need to study and keep up, be prepared for a lot of all the above or a and b sort of questions from akkaraju's portion of the bio tests
No Comments

His part of the test was so bad.  He really explins a lot in class very well and you feel like you really  understand it and then the test was aweful.  He is a really cool guy and teacher though.  Easy to listen and pay attention to his letures.

Understand his grading criteria at the beginning of the semester and you will be fine! You do not have to take the finals if you have an A in the class before finals season which is not hard to get if you do the work almost every week. Prof Akagi is clear on his expectations and willing to help you. Ask questions, be present, do your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Understanding Science. Attendance is must. Dr. Akagi was clear about the grading criteria. Although the lessons themselves are tough, he creates different types of homework that students can flexibly choose to work on to get credit without having to thoroughly understand the material. A good and understanding professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Akagi creates a respectful environment. The class is reading heavy but in discussion, Dr. Akagi makes sure that everyone is heard by calling on every person in the class and allowing them to explain their thoughts and discussion board posts. He devotes a whole class day to explaining the readings and the grading is mastery based. Great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Understanding Science with Dr. Akagi, and learned some really interesting things along the way. He uses a mastery-based grading system, which took some time to get used to, but I really liked it! You have a lot of flexibility in how you get the grade you want. Some of the readings were dense, but we had some great discussions about them.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Akagi's honors class is set up different than most, as you start at 0 points and pass/fail assignments until you get to the grade you want. The readings provided in his syllabus can sometimes be a doozy to read and you have to stay on top of discussion posts, but he gives you so many opportunities to get an A. I ended the class with a 104%.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy and puts effort into his lectures but the grading system is super weird. The assignments, including the final paper, are all pass or fail. I found it difficult to know what I needed to do to pass assignments, even after asking for help. I felt like I was gambling with my grade. It's possible but difficult to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Akagi is amazing. He grades on a mastery-based scale where you can attempt assignments multiple times to get the grade you want. He's very kind and awesome at answering questions during office hours, after class, and over email. The GOAT.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I found him hard to relate to. I took him for an honors colloquia class expecting to discuss current health and disease topics. It turned out to be a philosophy class where we pondered "what IS disease" for the entire semester. I did not learn in this class and left class frustrated more often than not.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Akagi was an awesome mentor and professor for me in the Science and Philosophy of Social Justice class this Spring!! He is young and very interested in your personal opinions//arguments. I not only learned a ton, but he was reasonable and very insightful and openminded to multiple viewpoints. He is very passionate, which makes class exciting!!
Super sweet and accommodating. There isn't really forced participation, so if you don't actually study for the stuff then you won't acquire the language. Definitely not a hard class!
My grandfather died and she wouldn't excuse my absence even after dean of students approved it. Same thing when I had a fever and note from health center. Took her for Sem III Fren as an adjunct.

Professor Soueid is a great prof for french 1. She did an awesome job at making the material easy to understand and interesting. As long as you come to class and work hard, you will do well. I would definitely take her class again and ngl I wish I could take her class again.

Professor Soueid is very friendly and accessible outside of class. Out of all the professors I've taken at TCU, she is absolutely my most favorite. Very caring and gave extremely helpful feedback as well. The class is pretty easy whether you have previous French knowledge or not. If you are learning French for the first tine, definitely take her!!
Do the study guide, and you will make an 'A'. The tests come straight from the study guide, and you attend lab once a week. Highly recommend this professor!

Only grades you'll have is exams and "pop quizzes" that are given just for participation, and extra credit after every exam. Exams are easy, and very intuition based so as long as you know the basic vocabulary.

I have taken a few classes with Stamatis, and her lectures are VERY hard to listen to. She is a very nice lady, but sometimes she is just talking to herself because it takes her 10 minutes to ramble about one slide. I'm sure her 101 class is great, but if you continue with her just know that her lectures take ten years off your life.
That's homegirl fr! She's super caring and funny, plus the only class assignments we have are short responses on a note card that are due at the nd end of class.

Dr. Stamatis has her class down to a science. Her lectures are interesting, short, and very informative. She basically outlines her test questions in lectures, so if your notes are good you will get an A. 3 Exams, 45 MCQ. Lab was easy but mainly busy work. Easy A for GA and NSC credit. she is very funny and kind, and gives 2 extra credit opps.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are occasionally attendance checks that she does throughout her course they don't take up too much of the grade book. Exams are easy if you study for a decent amount of time. Sometimes does extra credit opportunities for exam points. Do the exam review as she goes on with her lectures because it helps you study and its not much work.

One of the sweetest professors at TCU!! Exams are in person on paper but she gives a study guide that tells you exactly whats going to be on it. Only a few assignments that are short response questions she'll ask at the end of class randomly to check for attendance. Responds quickly to emails and super accommodating and accessible outside of class

The best professor here at TCU who really cares about her students' success as well as what she teaches. I would definitely take her class again. Her tests are easy as long as you review and the lab was always easy if you did the pre lab. Great class overall.

She is a very sweet and caring professor whose lectures are amazing. She clearly understands the class is taken by non-majors and tailors the material well. Lab (taught by a grad student) is difficult initially but gets easy once the process clicks. Highly recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was wonderful, attendance is kinda mandatory with a few in class assignments. Overall sweet lady and tests were not terrible, were in person though.

Amazing prof! Exams are in person on paper, but she gives a study guide that tells you exactly whats going to be on it. No quizzes. She take attendance by giving random questions for you to answer on a note crad at the end of class. She's so sweet and caring! She answer her emails fast, I love her! if you can TAKE HERRRR!

Prof. Stamatis was amazing her class and lab are very easy. She does take attendance every week its random so be in class. 3 exams in total the 3rd one being the final its not cumulative. She post the reviews 2 weeks before the test as long as you study that you will pass the 40 multiple question exams
no hw and weekly test in lab 

Def recommend
W professor holy

Professor Stamatis is really good at what she does, she keeps her lectures engaging and as interesting as environmental studies can be. She cares for her students and their success. If you can take her class you won't regret it.

Take notes in lecture and you will be fine. No homework. Kind and engaging. Gives lots of extra credit. Go to the optional final exam review at the end of the year and she will tell you all of the content covered on it and save you lots of time studying.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lab for this course was very well structured, and the short weekly lab quizzes and lab assignments were so helpful in learning the course material. The lab textbook was also helpful. However, it is very hard to pay attention to her and learn the material in lectures. Most of the grade is based on exams, which makes it hard to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Stamatis is one of the kindest people I have ever met. She is very approachable and understanding if things occur. Also, provides ample extra credit to swing each exam almost a full letter grade. Take this class!

If you need a Natural Science credit, take this class! I took this in combination with Contemporary Issues in Biology and it was a great combo. She is very sweet and there are good extra credit opportunities. Do study for the exams though because they can be a little hard.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Stamatis was AWESOME! I didn't think I could ever be interested in environmental science, but she managed to spark some interest in me. She's very aware of her audience as well (students are taking the class for CORE, not for their major). There are 12 random attendance checks, but 2 are dropped so you have room to skip. I'd take her again!

She gives a lot of extra credit for her tests. They aren't too hard if you study. 12 random check ins for attendance during the lectures. Lab is super easy. Would recommend for a semi easy science credit.

Dr.Stamatis is an amazing person! she understands that her students are here for core credit. However, don't forget to study for exams, or think that they are as easy as she makes them sound, they are quite difficult. If you do bad on one exam, you're not getting an A. We had a weekly lab quiz to study for and the lab exam was SUPER easy.
She really cares about the subject. I would highly recommend for a core credit.

Very clear concise, funny. Best professor I have had so far ever. Test heavy but extra credit and easy studying available. Lectures never feel like a drag and she breaks everything down understandably.

Such a kind professor, really cares about her students. She understands that most people are not taking this class for their major and is considerate regarding the workload. You have to attend class because she occasionally takes attendance for a grade. If you read the slides she posts and listen to lectures you'll be fine for the tests.

Such a kind and caring professor! There are only three exams for the whole course. If you study, it's an easy A. She gives 12 random attendance checks over the semester but drops 2. She even let us have a cheat sheet for the final. I definitely recommend taking Stamatis for an easy natural science course.

We had 3 exams over 11 chapter throughout the whole semester. She does a good job at explaining the topics and she is always encouraging us to go to her office hours if we need to. You obviously need to study for the exams just like for any other college class but if you study efficiently the information isn't hard but may be time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Excellent communicator. Lecture slides are super concise - she makes the content very digestible and her exams are straightforward. Easy A as long as you review the lecture slides before exams.

Definitely one of the most caring professors I've had. Very accessible outside of class. Offers generous extra credit assignments for exam (up to 10 points). There are random in-class assignments that you get an easy 100 on if you're present, so make sure to attend the lectures! You'll be fine on exams as long as you review the lecture slides :)

Professor Stamatis is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is so sweet and very passionate about her job. The tests are not hard as long as you go over the lecture material and she gives a lot of extra credit for every exam.
She is a great teacher and is very clear and goes over everything on the 3 tests in slideshows. If you take good notes this class is so easy. She also gives lots of points back on every quiz.

Probably my most entertaining class, and I have her 8AM. She speaks with pure passion, and she wants her students to be interested. I missed a test once, and she was very helpful when rescheduling. I can not imagine getting a better Prof than her. Class has 3 exams, which are genuinely easy if you show up, pay attention, and take some notes. No HW.

She's a very caring professor. I took her class during her first semester at TCU. Her lectures can get a little too detailed but she's very passionate about the topic. She as given extra credit opportunities and attendance is random and based on a participation assignment. Loved her class
Goated professor, ball knower
Double edged sword. If you just need the easiest A ever, take this class. If you actually want / need to learn a lot about this subject, take a different professor.

If you want to learn anything at all avoid. Probably the worst professor I have taken at TCU, and just has 0 interest in being here. I haven't met someone who cares less about what they're doing. Very unstructured class and just writes definitions on the board. For someone interested in real estate, its a shame I had this professor.
Take him. Don't make the mistake of taking someone else - he gave us pizza on review days.

I took professor Akin's class last semester and can confidently say two things. 1) I learned nothing. 2) He's a rude and demeaning person. He claims attendance is mandatory, which it isn't. He isn't open to any ideas other than his own, and puts down any point that doesn't align with his own opinions. If you don't have to, don't take his course.

Akin is an awesome guy. He is so knowledgeable and gives great advise. Definitely get to know him after class or in office hours. There are 5 exams (including final), a group project, and quizzes, but they are all manageable. Go to class!!!!

He is an amazing person, not an amazing professor. Tests are really hard because they're not based on book or the lecture, just random info. Most of the answers are on Quizlet. Get to know him because he will get you a job or internship if he likes you. Final project worth 30% of grade and no guidance given was awful

he does not write his own test which make the tests very difficult even when lots of preparation goes into them. The group project has very little structure and his outline is very different to what he actually wants, but he will only say that if your group meets with him outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you can help it, don't take Akin. He does not write his own tests, so they are over things not covered in class.  There is a big group project but it is very gray and has little structure.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Akin is funny and laid back for this class. We had it in the big auditorium, so he never really knew if you were present or not. He has lots of slides that go directly to the test, so those are the key to doing well in his class. Huge group project of a marketing tradeshow at the end of the semester that work on often. Fun opportunity.

Akin is by far the worst professor I have ever taken. His lectures are just rambling with countless incorrect facts. He is hard to contact /meet outside of class. There are 4 tests and a group project, but there is little guidance and time given for the project. The project is also graded by random people and Akin isn't even in the room for it.

Class is made up of 4 tests + final + group project. The tests (lockdown with camera) are based on the textbook and lectures - the test is so difficult because he talks about nonsense during class. The project was fun but there should've been fewer tests and more emphasis on the project. Super cool guy but I think there are better professors.

While most people do not attend class, I thought his lectures were super interesting. I think for a class like marketing real life situations and experiences are the best things you can learn from. He does not teach the textbook so you have to do the readings and apply the concepts in order to do well on the tests. The tests were words part.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: In this class there is no homework, just online quizzes, 4 online exams, and a final group presentation. The quizzes are on quizlet and on exam day you can take them any time from 6am-11:59 pm. Exams are lockdown browser but not hard to find help. His lectures don't help with the quizzes or exams he usually just tells stories during class.

Great guy. Terrible professor. Lecture is filled with ramblings about nothing the exams are over. Get ready to teach yourself. Class has no structure, and exams are administered on Fridays, outside of class time. Final project is thrown on to you with no guidance, even though its 30% of your grade. The guy does not care. Talks a storm though.

His lecture is chill and fun, there are 4 exams but it won't be an easy A. You have to understand the concept in the text book to analyze the situation in the exams. The group project is VERY IMPORTANT because there will be a judge (not professor Akin) who will grade your project. So be prepared for that!

Akin is good if you learn best from textbooks. You don't have to go to class - he doesn't teach in class besides going on tangents and skimming through the textbook-provided PowerPoint. 4 tests, many quizzes, and a final project. He offers no guidance on the final project

Professor Akin is a great guy. He has 4 exams and 1 cumulative final. There is also a marketing plan presentation at the end of the semester and quizzes about once a week. Very willing to help with your presentation.

He seems like a cool guy, but isn't a good professor. I haven't learned anything from him, and I teach myself everything. Final project is worth a large portion of the final grade, and isn't during his class time.

Akin is a great guy. So funny and very nice. Although, his teaching isn't much of teaching. If you want an enjoyable class take him but you won't learn anything inside the classroom. you will have to teach yourself through the book. I am a straight A student and was shocked by my first test grade because I don't feel as though he prepared us

Dr. Akin is literally the best professor I have ever had. He truly cares about who you are as a person. He cares more about how real life works than what a textbook says. I don't understand how he doesn't have 5 stars. I wish I could take him again!!!!!

Akin is not a good teacher. I had an A before his group project that he grades very hard on and is worth 30% of your grade. I had to self-teach this entire course to myself and nobody shows up to class. He also doesn't respond to emails and leaves no feedback at all on the tradeshow which is very frustrating.

Akin has great stories and makes class lively and interesting. HOWEVER, he is one of the only marketing professors to have proctored tests. They are based on the textbook, which he does not teach too. For the group project - meet with him multiple times and he'll love you. Expect to do bad on the tests and make up for it on the project.
Attendance is optional, you can legit get an A without showing up to a single class. Very engaging lectures. Only graded by 4 exams, a final, and a group project. Very nice dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would not recommend Professor Akin for Marketing Management. While some students loved him, he was very disorganized and for me it was hard to succeed in class because of it. The syllabus and dates in the class were constantly changing; I never knew when tests were coming up or projects were due.

Dr. Akin is one of the best professors at TCU, hands down! His class is all lectures which gives business world experience while teaching and is very engaging. He does go off topic but you will get good laughs out of his stories. There are 4 exams with a final - all online and group project that is fun and not meant to be serious! Take him!!

If you're a marketing major, I would seriously take him. Yes, he goes off track during lectures, but it's one of my favorite things about his class. He talks about his own experiences and what is going on in the business world. There are 4 tests and a group project. You have to read the book if you want to do well on tests, but it is manageable.

Professor Akin is the best professor I have ever had at TCU. He teaches you about the outside world and has a lot of actual business experience, unlike other professors that have never actually worked in the business world. He brings in guest speakers often that allow you to network with business professionals. I cannot say enough good things!

Akin has been the most capitvating professor i've had at TCU yet. His lectures are very interesting as he uses real world examples to relate the material to actual usage in business. He is a very understanding professor and wants his students to do well. The pop quizzes can be tough, however he lets you use a note card for all tests and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you plan on being a marketing student, TAKE HIM!!! I learned more life skills and made more real-world connections in this class, than my full two other years at TCU. Students often even receive internships after his class because he brings in guest speakers all the time. The tests are based on the textbook, but that's what quizlet is for.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Akin is a cool person. He has so much experience and has a lot of knowledge to share. He doesn't teach to the textbook but that's where all the tests come from. There was very little direction on a huge group project. There were multiple times he gave us tests with material on them we did not cover in class. The class was frustrating.

Dr. Akin is a nice guy but talks a lot about personal stories in class and does not teach the material much but attendance is mandatory. I had to read the text book to teach myself. Tests weren't too though.

Bob Akin is one of the best men I have ever met. He is genuine, kind, and an amazing professor. His tests are hard. I am not going to lie and perhaps I would advise you not to take this class if you are looking for an A. The point is though, he teaches you SO much more than what you need to get an A. He is teaching you about life after graduation.

Take everything he says about the real world with a grain of salt, he said CEOs would rather hire TCU grads over Harvard grads during multiple times throughout the course. Studying was pointless because everything on the test he has never talked about. Convinced he doesn't grade the exams because I received the same grade for all 4 exams.

Terrible Professor and he admits as much to his students. Most of the information he gives in class is wrong and/or outdated. Not only did I not learn anything, but my grade took a hit because Akin makes his tests unnecessarily difficult/confusing while also not covering any of the material in class. Total hypocrite. Do not take.

Akin is a great man, he has a lot of interesting stories. However, these stories are not related to the course material necessarily. He gives lectures on the material but it doesn't help for the tests. Tests are pretty difficult. Pop quizzes. Allows notecards for both quizzes and tests

Akin give you the opportunity to prepare yourself for the real world. He brings in outside professionals that give you insight in the business world. If you go to class, you're fine. If you have a problem in the class, go in and talk to him, as he is very understanding and will help you if you need it. Bad ass speakers in this class too.

Dr. Akin was in the process of getting his second doctorate this semester and that was clearly his first priority.  There was little to no effort put into the class.  He was constantly tired and cranky because he was so invested in his dissertation. Maybe once he is done he will put some effort back in, but this semester was very disappointing.

Akin is the man. All these negative posts below are a little dramatic. He is entertaining, which is a breath of fresh air. He doesn't lecture straight out of the book because a book of information is not going to make you successful. He tells stories because REAL successful people learn thru emulating OTHER successful people, which Akin IS.

Akin is hilarious. He believes that the best thing to teach is experience, not things out of the textbook. That being said, all of his tests come from the textbook, so you're basically teaching yourself. You get a notecard on all exams though, and he will give extra credit and curve the exams like crazy. It's a fun class, just read the book.

Very good lectures and a simple group project. Very enjoyable class and teaches you a lot. 'very specific in project guidelines but will meet with you and tell you exactly what to do.  Only complaint is that tests are tricky. He did give a ten point curve on three of them though.

I like Akin; he's funny and approachable. But as my teacher? Ever since The Great Cheating Scandal of 2014, he hasn't put in much effort. He tells personal stories and jokes during class instead of lecturing. If you're looking for a grown up frat daddy who will be your friend, take Akin. If you want a professor to teach you, look elsewhere.

It's sad how he doesn't lecture about things from the book, just himself. I know more about his life than I do about marketing management. I used to think he wants his students to succeed, but now I really don't think he does. Its sad he has tenure

AVOID AVOID AVOID!!! AVOID AT ALL COSTS! I was very excited about taking this class and although Akin is very hilarious, his class is TERRIBLE! He will promise extra credit and never add it and he will promise a curve on exams and NEVER CURVE! His exams are NEVER what he says they will be! DO NOT TAKE!!!!!!

I don't know why all these people put bad ratings for Akin. Also, he is not biased towards greek life or athletes. He is a great teacher! Class is great and the tests aren't too bad if you read the book and listen in class.
Akin is one of the best business teachers. Class is always fun and you can tell that he loves teaching. Tests aren't that bad if you read the chapters. If you get the chance, take him!

Professor Akin is awesome! Class is always enjoyable and you can tell he loves his job. He is one of my favorite professors at TCU. He is one of those professors that wants to get to know his students and is always available to help. In class he tells stories, talks about real life marketing experiences, and tries to make class fun. Take him!

Worst professor i've ever had. He will manipulate you entirely all semester long. Lectures are completely unrelated to class and book, tests are completely different than he describes, and will claim to give extra credit out purposely knowing he won't. However, if your an athlete or sorority chick, your covered. Take him. If not avoid at all cost.

Professor Akin is hands down my favorite professor at TCU and the mean comments are coming from people who didn't try, were required to take his class, or were looking for a blowoff class. If you actually care about marketing, take him. He may not be the easiest professor, but he genuinely cares about you and wants to be engaged and participate.
Useless professor, never teaches in the classes he doesn't cancel (at least 1/3 of them)and gives rediculously hard tests with info never covered in class. Do not take!

Akin literally went out of his way after submitting final grades to lower 1/2 of the class's grades submitted to the registrar. Is completely misleading all year and then destroys grades at the end. Lectures are so off topic and tests are NOTHING like he promises. Claimed he would provide us with resources for group project, again did not. Avoid.

I'm a girl whose a 3.8 student, take her education very seriously, and was really excited to take this class. While I got an A- in Akin's class, I felt that I needed to warn others about this teacher. This guy lectures the whole class off topic (mostly bragging about himself and talking about beer) and then his tests are not related to lectures.

Lol, obviously that's Professor Akin commenting two posts below giving the only favorable comment on here. Akin finalized the grades and I got a B. Then after tons of kids were emailing him about him not keeping his word for an Extra Credit assignment, he went back and changed an assignment and lowered my grade to a C+ as well as 23 other students.

If you want to fail this class and be tormented all year by a tyrant, then take this class with him. If you are sane, you will avoid him at all cost, and hope he is removed asap. He doesn't help if you "seek" him out, isn't at all approachable, and is genuinely looking to hurt students with lies.

I thought Akin would be a good professor and I'm sad to say I was horribly wrong. He promised extra credit from the 1st test, when he forgot about that he promised to curve our grade, when he didn't do that he added another assignment after grades were due that actually lowered our grades. I am very disappointed there is a prof like him at TCU.

Akin is the most genuine professor at TCU. His class is a great opportunity to learn from a guy that has been there and done it. If you are closed minded and aren't mature enough to cope without structure and a good set of notes then you shouldn't take this class and are not ready to get out of college. Akin truly cares if you engage with him.
If you like being manipulated and lied to by a tenured professor and barely pass the class then take him. Avoid at all cost, or it will ruin your semester.

Haha obviously Akin wrote the post below. Why would a student take the time to correct their teacher's degree. Everything the guy two below said about his haughtiness, ego, and everything else is true. Told us we'd get extra credit or a curve and he never gave us any. Talks about himself all class and tries to look cool. Not a man of his word.

Akin was helpful when I sought him out. His doctorate is in Education (EdD), it is from TCU. Not an on-line program. Two of the 12-12- postings were from the same group, they did not take the class serious. The tests come from the lectures that come out of the book and power points. I made a B.

This teacher lacks integrity entirely. He misinforms students intentionally regarding opportunities for grades. Class time is like comedy hour - completely pointless because he rambles and tells jokes. Nothing on the exams are from lecture. Tests are completely different than what he will describe them as. Take this course with someone else

Reads from powerpoints and strays off topic. Name drops a lot, going to class won't help. Attendance does not affect your grade but there is a sign in sheet each class period. Tests are all application, so memorizing definitions will not do you any good. Grading system is very vague and up to his judgement in the end. Made a B-
