Banos was a great professor! I took him for creative strategy. You have three major projects, reflections over readings, and a final exam! It's all completely doable work but be ready for group work! Would highly recommend this teacher!

He is awesome! He makes the class very similar to what I expect an agency to be. He is so sweet, and is brief and brutally honest, which honestly helps a lot. The group projects are a lot of the class, but he really helps you to go above and beyond. He is super insightful and I learned so much from him!! Not too hard, and I love him!

Best class you will take at TCU!! The projects in his class are very real world and challenging. I actually had a lot of fun! Don't get me wrong, they were time intensive and stressful at times, but SO worth it. He has a lot of real experience that he brings to the class. You need to take his class, seriously. It will change you.

I REALLY enjoyed his class. It's probably my favorite one so far. He has a lot of industry experience which is very refreshing compared to other professors. You will work hard in his class, but he sets VERY realistic deadlines and helps you and your team almost on a one-on-one basis. Great sense of humor. Absolutely recommend him!

He's new to teaching and has a ton of experience in the industry. He expects a lot of you but it's not unreasonable and is good preparation for the real world. I'd say you'll get out of his class what you put in, but he provides so many opportunities for his students to excel. Definitely recommend!

Had him at Collin College for 1350 Systems Analysis and Design. Awesome professor. Doesn't use Cengage but you do have to get the book. He works as a Systems Analyst and knows his stuff and can bring real life examples to class. And he's just nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class is easy. Sometimes assignments can be lengthy, but the textbook has videos to walk you through everything step-by-step. Also, notes are allowed on tests, so just have good, detailed notes and you will be fine. Everyone who got a bad grade did not study or did not prepare notes. He is also accessible outside of class if you need him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He tries to make the Excel class as easy and painless as possible. He takes class time to walk through the assignment that is due for the week so you don't have to do it outside of class. The hardest part of this class is the amount of work but that is set by TCU, not him. He tells you all  topics covered on the quizzes to make it as easy as he can
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He is a really smart guy and if you ask he shows you all the details to get your assignments correct. There's a prepare case every Tuesday, an assessment in every class, 2 easy reflections, 2 quizzes, and 1 easy group project. I always did the prepare cases and assessments weeks before so classes are chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I audited Miller's class and took Baranowski for Excel and figured that no matter who you take it's kinda the same for Excel classes. I would say just do your homework and follow up with assignments and it's easy A. The class itself is pretty straightforward, unless you slack off and forget assignments you should be alright.

Every Monday a Case study assignment was due and every Tuesday there are two Assessments due. Literally it's a 1-hour credit class with triple amount of homework. His quizzes are ridiculous. They cover too many chapters and you just don't have the timeframe to finish it. Take any other professor.

I thought he was a really hard grader, and I don't think i would take him again. His lectures are very interesting, and he is super nice, but it is hard to get a good grade on the tests. Tests are all online. Definitely a reading-heavy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His class is hard bc of the amount of reading you'll be doing. His tests/quizzes pull very heavy from the reading. He goes over all the material in class in a way that's very easy to understand though and he genuinely cares about what he teaches. I'm lucky that I had him but man am I glad it's done now lol
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing at what he does and teaches, it will definitely make a difference in your grade if you read or don't

He is hilarious in his classes and I love his lessons (very informative). However, the reading for this class is HEAVY. I had to read around 9 books for his classes in total.He is very supportive during his office hours. His tests were mad hard, you need to remember everything he said and know your material well. He is tough grader too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's an amazing teacher! His lectures are organized and sometimes goes on a tangent but he relates it back to the topics. You will read a lot but it honestly helps you understand macro and the business world better. I recommend taking him, he's funny and very understanding if you can't attend class.

The most intellectually sound professor at TCU. His lectures are something to be had, incorporating his own insights to the lessons at hand. I thoroughly enjoyed his class, and could listen to his perspectives all day. Tests are the only grades, so read read read. Grades much more generously than others might admit. Absolutely worth it.

Bailiff is an amazing professor. I loved his lectures and always found them interesting. Your grade is based entirely on 6 tests and he drops the lowest test grade. Tests are based on lectures and reading so make sure to read everything. Attendance isn't mandatory but you should attend every lecture. Go to office hours, he provides lots of help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you do not like to read, do not take his class. However, he is the best professor I have ever had. Genuinely loves what he teaches. Tough grader but if you utilize his office hours, the exams get much easier. I won't finish with an A, but it is the most informative class I have taken and I am thankful to have had Bailiff as a professor, he's fun

Best professor ever. I disliked his lectures at first, but looking back on how the class has changed me, I realize I was just a silly, myopic freshman hungry for easy As. I learned the hard way: to read smart, synthesize, and ask questions. He's very passionate; you can tell when he's teaching that it's as if he's preaching. He is the true GOAT.

Bailiff is very smart and definitely knows what he is talking about. I would advise listening to an audiobook when reading and taking notes at the same time. Then, ask chat to summarize the chapters and take notes on that. Review these notes as often as you possibly can. You really have to listen during the lectures and take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bailiff had really great lectures and I agreed with most things he said. I wanted to make his class work and finish with a decent grade but his tests are WAY too dependent on reading long chapters from multiple books. Good professor but do NOT take if you don't want to be reading every night.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bailiff was a nice and funny teacher who kept his class engaged during lectures. The class was composed of 6 tests, one of them being dropped, and some extra credit. If you are consistent with going to class, reading, and reaching out for help you will get a good grade.

Bailiff was a great guy and I truly learned a lot. I took him last semester for micro, and I will admit it was a hard class. We are only graded of 6 exams  so doing well on them is imperative. He does drop our lowest test grade (excluding the midterm and final), which is nice. The worst part about his class is that there is a lot of reading
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Engaging lectures from Prof. Bailiff, but the class requires consistent effort. Attend class, read the textbooks, and use resources like Unstuckstudy for efficient study prep. Grading can be tough, but the material is valuable.

It is a wasted opportunity if you do not take this man for your economics classes. He is funny and knowledgeable about the subject, offering many chances to raise your grade. Yes, the class is difficult, but it is a challenge that you should embrace. I also solved a Rubik's cube for extra credit which I loved. GOAT.

Only take this class if you are prepared to carve out like an hour of time to read every day. There are a ton of books that are hard to understand if you don't know much about economics. There are much easier professors. Bailiff did teach me a lot. Honestly, I am just not interested enough in econ to sacrifice my gpa.

Bailiff is awesome. Yes, the class does require a lot of work and reading, but if you actually lock in during the lectures, which is easy because he's so funny, you'll do well. Don't let your grade on the first exam deter you, he drops the lowest and it gets easier as you learn his question format. Just do the reading and the work. Big Bailiff fan

He's an amazing teacher and I actually loved taking his class. His lectures aren't as important to attend but there is a LOT of reading in this class. You must do your reading to succeed. How it works is his lectures go over everything you need to know, and the reading goes much more in depth about what each of those things are.

Lectures can be funny but also goes on rants and is tough to pay attention in class because under 50% of the time spent in class is about material. Lots of reading and tests are your entire grade which he does not provide feedback. Would try and get another teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a really funny professor. Super understanding guy but if you are dyslexic or have trouble reading longer assignments good luck. This class is all reading and he pulls specific questions from the already confusing reading. If you go to class and take notes on the major topics he discusses and compare it to the book you should ok.

Bailiff is awesome and his lectures always make us laugh. Its important to do the reading for the tests and make sure you are actually learning from the reading not memorizing it. The tests makes you apply your knowledge so just make sure you pay attention in class. For sure recommend taking him for microeconomics.

Lots of reading but doable if you do not wait last minute. He does say unnecessary stuff but he is actually very helpful! attend class and go to office hours and take notes on EVERYTHING he says. Graded on 6 exams where you answer 5-9 questions and he drops the lowest one! You will have to buy a few books but make sure to look for the pdf first
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class isn't easy. It's a ton of reading, and lots of note taking. But if you genuinely work hard, do every reading, and come to class focused, you'll be just fine. He doesn't teach a curriculum, but rather real life economics. Hes absolutely hilarious and incredibly smart. Read a ton, take a ton of notes, GO TO OFFICE HOURS, and you'll kill it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take his class, will not find another class like Bailiff's. Tough, yes, but the material matters and class is never boring.

SO FUNNY! I loved his classes. The exams were easy if you read the books. DO NOT slack off on the reading. Take good notes in class and re-read the sections he talks about in class since those show up on the tests. To be successful go to office hours and listen to what the other kids are asking. Super nice guy  as long as you are not sensitive

Professor Bailiff is who you should take for macroeconomics. He is super engaging and his lectures are clear and to the point(and always entertaining). But you MUST do the readings before each test (and attend class) if you want to do well.

Loved Bailiff so much, learned the most from this guy out of any class taken at TCU so far but the grading is so arbitrary and unclear. Working my ass off to average B's and C's doesn't seem fair and the grading felt very unclear. Worth it to learn a lot about the market and economics, but if you don't want your GPA messed up I don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really good guy and is hilarious. There are 6 tests (take home), one gets dropped. They are all short answer and based off 8 different books that you had to read and understand. First B I have ever received in my life. Genuinely impossible to get a good grade unless you go to lectures, read, and know everything you read. Specific test questions.

You will not find another Professor like Dr. Bailiff at TCU. This man sugarcoats absolutely nothing. Dr. B tells it like it truly is, and if you are afraid to hear the honest truth about something, this class is definitely not for you. He has more common sense than the entire TCU staff combined and it was honor to have him as my professor.

Bailiff is a tough professor, be prepared to do a lot of readings, and REALLY put in the effort. However, he's worth the experience. If you get to know the guy, he has so much knowledge to share. I ended with a B, but I by far took the most away from this class, not only about econ, but just life. You have to experience him once in life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: AMAZING CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lee Bailiff is an awesome teacher, however be ready to not miss a class and read at least a few chapters a week. Average on our first exam was a 49. Probably the most entertaining professor I have ever had and is not afraid to let it out during class, it is awesome! If you are not afraid of the challenge, I highly recommend this class!

TAKE THIS CLASS! I got a 56 on the 1st exam but ended with an A. Hardest A I have ever earned but I loved the class. He helps you understand concepts, and I was excited to go to every class. He is hilarious. Go to office hours it is beneficial. If you read and understand everything, and also listen to lectures and take notes, the tests are easy.

Dr. Bailiff is an outstanding professor, his class should be mandatory for all TCU students, and everything is clearly explained in the syllabus. Grading is very straight forward, and he gives feedback if asked. He clearly wants his students to succeed so my advice is put in the work and take advantage that Dr. Bailiff is at TCU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. There is only 6 tests which are based off lecture and readings. It is reading heavy, but as long as you don't leave it until the night before you should be fine. He is very funny and will use comedy and real world examples to teach. I would take him again.

If you need to fulfill a core requirement, but don't really care if you get a B, take this class. He is funny and makes class entertaining to be in, if a little controversial. If you care alot about getting an A OR you are an Economics major I would avoid. Grading can appear arbitrary at times and he doesn't cover certain concepts as in depth.

Professor Bailiff isn't rated a 5 because his class is easy and the work load is light. Yes, you will have to read and study a lot, but that's why you're in college. Instead, he's rated a 5 because his lectures are very insightful and hilarious. What you learn in this class will help you throughout you're whole life. Everyone should take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lee Bailiff is the epitome of the alpha male. His lectures are a mix of genius economic articulation and pure stand-up comedy. His tests are difficult, but that also may be due to the delusion we college students have of what 'A' quality work is. Take this class if you want an introduction to economics but also an introduction to real life...
Funny teacher and super nice. Lectures are really hard and difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bailiff is awesome! You can tell he loves what he's talking about and knows how to keep his students intrigued. He is super accessible and helpful outside of the classroom and brings lots of character to his lectures. Your grade is based off of 6 tests and you will have to do some reading, but altogether his class is not a disappointment.

Prof. Bailiff cares about his students' success. He is a class professor and a class human being; just from the short time I've spent with him during his classes and chatting with him after class, I've realized how much of a class person he is. He is passionate about his lectures and never hesitates to give everyone a good laugh during class

This is by far the best professor I've had at TCU. His class requires effort and self-discipline as any college class should but the things you will learn will be able to be applied to all aspects of your life. His lectures are informational and funny so make sure you attend. He cares about his students and is a very reasonable person.

Professor Bailiff is a great professor in the sense that you learn so much and are able to apply concepts to real-world situations. However, he grades his tests really hard and all exam questions are free responses so you have to know exactly what you are talking about and be able to explain why your answer is correct. He lectures every class,

He is a good lecturer and makes them entertaining but it is really hard to stay organized in this class because he has no slides and taking lecture notes can be difficult to keep up with. The amount of reading required in this class is absurd and takes up a lot of valuable time. His grading on tests felt biased and unclear at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is really funny and super interesting to listen to. The class consist of 6 exams which includes a midterm that is cumulative. If you do the readings and attend the class then you'll be fine. This class is really informative and opens up new perspectives to Econ. Really liked that he doesn't use a textbook to teach.

Hands down funniest teacher. Prof Bailiff does not care, he will speak his mind. Really tough grader, if your looking for easy A, not the class for you. You will learn a lot if you take his class though.

This course is a test-based class, with no homework, where although attendance isn't mandatory, it can determine your final grade in the class. His lectures are interesting to listen to and he uses lots of examples to explain the topics. There are several books we are required to read but he explains majority of the topics in class to take notes.

For someone who was nervous about taking this class, I found myself always looking forward to coming to this class. He explains macroeconomics in such an easy way to understand. I really enjoyed coming to this class and would definitely take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class is ultra hard, his jokes are not funny, he probably still lives with his mother, and his comebacks to other students on rate my professor are sub-par.

This is my favorite class I have taken thus far at TCU. Bailiff is HILARIOUS. There wasn't one class where I wasn't laughing. Tests are difficult, but if you actually want to learn the material, Bailiff is your man. His class was all lectures with only 6 exams, but he used real world examples to explain concepts in an understandable way.

Do your work, study, and actually learn the material. Tough grader but not difficult to get good grades when you listen to what he says and answer test questions the way he instructs you to. 6 exams make up grade, free response, 6-8 questions, not too bad. Extremely knowledgeable, answers questions, funny, and easy to follow along and understand.

Professor Bailiff has to be one of the greatest Economics professors that TCU has ever witnessed. Economics is a very complicated subject to understand, but Professor Bailiff is so good at applying these concepts to real life scenarios, making it super easy to understand. He is also absolutely hilarious and I look forward to his class every week.

Great Professor. Attendance is not mandatory yet I come to every class. He's hilarious and isn't afraid to say screwed up stuff which keeps the class interesting. He often lets us out early, he understands the life of a college student, knows we're itching to get hammered at 6pm on a thursday and roll TXR. Biggest advice is GO TO CLASS

Professor Bailiff is one of the most profound professors I have ever had. If you are looking to take a class that is taught by someone who is a master of their field, then he is your guy. I can confidently say that every time I walked out of his class, I felt more and more knowledgeable about the subject of Economics. Never a boring lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bailiff is one of the greatest professors I have ever had. His lectures are hilarious and you may get offended by what he says, but he doesn't care. Attendance is not mandatory, but I don't recommend skipping his class. The exams revolve around books and lectures. READ THE BOOKS.

Professor Bailiff successfully keeps every student engaged more so than any professor I've ever had; this is mainly due to his dry humor. Take this class if you like to laugh. If you keep up with the readings, you can easily understand the economic ideas he conveys, even if you have no prior knowledge. He's an genious in his field of economics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I can tell this guy is packing, like packing packing. Like jeez man stop flaunting it everywhere. Dudes basically begging TCU to fire him. The balls on this guy is crazy. Pretty handsome too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I could put this guy in a ball and punt him off a bridge. I could blend this guy in a smoothie and leave him out to bake on a Tuesday afternoon. I could snap this guy like a piece of toasted celery. pretty good overall 7/10

Four assigned books; lectures and tests both use direct examples from readings. He is willing to answer questions and reexplain material, but tests are formatted as open ended questions with no clear grading criteria that is more common in an upper level contending perspectives class rather than an intro level. 6 tests, with lowest one dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bailiff is awesome, hilarious, and cares ab his students. Only grades are 6 exams & theres a lot of reading that you have to do to succeed. Take good notes & take advantage of his office hours. Not an easy A but youll learn so much. Learned the most Ive ever learned from a class here & was overall a really rewarding, informative, funny class.

Bailiff is an awesome, witty, hilarious prof. His teaching style is not what I prefer-- very reading heavy but I have still gotten a lot out of this course: maybe the most concepts I've ever learned in a course. Everyone loves Bailiff. He says what he wants without worrying about being cancelled-- you cant cancel this man.
Really hard class. Learned a lot, but great professor overall. Would not recommend if you want an easy A, it was a lot of hard work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This guy isn't too bad, sometimes he gets political in class and doesn't comply with TCU mask rules, but as a teacher, I actually learned from his class. You gonna read a lot for a Intro Macro class, but it's gonna help you truly study. If you want easy A don't bother taking him but if you want to learn something you should probably do.

Professor Bailiff is one of the best professors I have had. He genuinely cares about his students so much and if you don't understand something he will clarify it up for you until you feel confident. It is a lot of reading, but most of the readings he will lecture about in class so you can connect the dots along the way. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bailiff was the reason that I chose to be an economics major. He is truly passionate about the subject and while he only talks, he narrates it in a way that you can actually understand and in a way that will stick with you. Has to be the funniest man on campus. Would always love to take a class by this man
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: His lectures are more stand-up comedy than anything. I feel like it is a waste of time going to class because he gets off-topic a lot and goes on libertarian tangents. Be ready to read A LOT; I do not mind it and I have learned a lot from the readings, I just think he could more efficiently allocate class time: a scarce resource for college kids.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Bailiff is a great teacher. He is funny and makes learning economics really interesting. Your grade in the class is 6 tests and the lowest test grade is dropped. The only homework you have is to read the books but it's very important that you do read them if you want to do good on the tests.

Prof Bailiff is a fantastic teacher. He teaches economy in its purest form and it's quite interesting. The class is made up of 6 tests and the lowest grade is dropped. The only homework is to read the books and it's essential to do good on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you get over B in his class you are eligible for early graduation. He's funny but his grading is just super tough. Exams are online, at home, but you have to read bunch of books and listen to every single word he said. In general if you like a funny prof but grades dont matter then take him. Otherwise NOPE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Let me tell you - Lee Bailiff is a character. He definitely speaks his mind (sometimes getting off-topic A LOT) and is very brash, but is super funny. There were only 6 exams and I had to work my butt off to get a good grade. You definitely have to read the textbook (it's a decent amount) and pay attention in class. The ave class grade was a C-
Bailiff is a king. I took him for both micro and macro. Lots of readings and you definitely have to work for your test grade, but it is worth it and he is hilarious.

I really enjoyed his Micro class. It was super interesting and I actually learned a lot from it. There is a ton of reading, but I read 1/2 the time and still pulled out an A. If you arent going to read though, you have to pay attention to everything he says. Overall, relatively easy class, and I would take him again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I loved this class! I learned more from Bailiff than any class I've taken. He makes complicated topics easier to understand while being really funny. He calls it like it is and speaks the truth. There is a lot of reading for each exam, so make sure to divide it up. Your only grades are the 6 exams, but just take good notes and thoroughly read!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This class is always entertaining. He knows what hes talking about and if for some reason he doesnt he will get back to you. His grading all depends on how well you answer the questions. Tests are your only grades. Lots of reading but its not bad if you get the hang of things.

Lee is a great professor. He is passionate about what he teaches, hates textbooks, and helps you if you need it. Be prepared to read, because even though he hates textbooks, he does utilize real books written by economists that do a good job detailing what exactly is truth, and what is misconception. Just make sure to answer in a lengthy manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bailiff is by far one of my favorite professors on campus. He assigns a lot of reading but its definitely not impossible. If you have to take micro I highly recommend Bailiff, he makes the lectures interesting and always has a funny story that helps to explain the reading better.

If you have to take econ and you aren't amazing at it, take Bailiff. He made the material easy to learn, and classes were both fun and informative. Overall a super nice guy that wants you to succeed. The only bad thing about this class was how much reading there was, so be prepared for that.

Professor Bailiff deserves a statue on campus. He is one of the best professors at TCU! He really cares about all of his students and is always willing to help. His class does require a lot of reading prior to every class but as long as you do the reading youll be successful!! Take his classes- they are worth it

Professor Bailiff is incredible. If you have no interest in Economics of any sort and are not ready to learn, do not take this class, though if you truly have a passion for learning Economics, this is the guy you want as your professor. Get ready to read as there are multiple readings. If you want to learn Economics and life, this is the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor- really passionate about economics, but it is a hard class. Test heavy. If you do not attend class and read the books, you won't understand the topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: took him for both Macro and Micro my fresh year (I think Macro before micro is easier). FAVORITE classes. Accessible for office hours (go to them) and tests get easier as you learn formatting and what types of answers he's looking for. MAKE SURE to READ. Sometimes does pop questions in class and adds points. Drops lowest test at end (not midterm).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Don't take his class if you are easily offended. He is very blunt but the lectures are hysterical. Lots and lots of reading and only grades are the six tests. A great teacher and truly cares about his students.

You will do most of the learning on your own from the three required books which took me about 8 hours to read for each test, and the 6 tests make up the whole of your grade, with the lowest being dropped. Make sure you start off strong, because most people don't, and you will be sure to learn a lot about the real-world application of economics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Bailiff is the best professor in the whole world and I enjoyed his class immensely. I look forward to every class. He is REAL and says exactly what he thinks so if youre easily offended, hes not for you. You have to read outside of class and go to class but you wont regret taking him. If anything, it will be entertaining!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Bailiff is the most caring professor I have ever had and wants to teach you about everyday life. He knows his stuff and is an entertaining lecturer. Just be prepared to read over 100 pages a week to prepare for the SIX tests. There is a test about every 5 classes. They are all short essay questions, but he drops one test. These are the only grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Bailiff is a SUPER good teacher, but his class is hard and requires a lot of work. He is accessible outside of class and use his office hours to your advantage!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Lee is a great guy. People do not like him because the class is a lot of work so they take out their frustration on him. Read the three books and do the work little by little and you will be fine. Make sure to Show up to class because he will give extra credit on days when attendance is low. Great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are the ONLY grades. Several hours of reading a week. Hard class especially if economics doesnt come naturally to you. He assigns 3 books, but teaches out of one. Dont waste time reading the one he teaches out of bc everything from it on tests was in lecture, read the other too instead. I learned a lot, and Bailiff is a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS! He is an amazing person and teacher. By far the best class I have taken. He is very encouraging and wants his students to succeed. If you go to class and participate you will make a great grade! Going to his office hours before the tests really help as well!

I personally loved Bailiff, but some do not. These people tend to be the ones who don't read or take thorough notes in class. If read the books and take the time to reflect on what the authors are trying to convey, then you will succeed in this class. It may be challenging at times but it is extremely rewarding. If you procrastinate DON'T enroll.

Amid a sea of meaningless academic fluff, Bailiff delivers something of value. There is much to be gained from taking his class and if you want to, you will greatly improve from taking his class. It is difficult to get an A and requires great effort, but if you are interested in bettering yourself take him.

If you not a lazy bum and you understand that your an adult now and have to study tr make a good grade, then this class will not be a problem because he will be there to help guide you through the textbook readings.
Good man, but it was a really hard class. Soooo much to study
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took Macroeconomics. Bailiff is a hilarious man and very interesting to listen to. However, he has nothing online, does not write on the board; everything is verbal. Take him if reading and stress get you off. There are ONLY 6 exams as assignments; each being 6-8 essay questions. Each exam is based on 3-4 chapters of 3 different books. awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lee Bailiff was the best professor I had freshman year. He is so funny and cares about his students succeeding. Yes, it is a lot of studying but if you take good notes you will pass with no problem. Best class ever, 100% take this class!

Professor Bailiff is hilarious and I recommend his class to anyone who has to take macroeconomics. If you are willing to go to every class and see him during study hours it shouldn't be too hard to make at least a B. I always looked forward to his class, take this class!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Well, the only thing I would have to say is that considering Im not an economics major, this was pretty tough for me to grasp. Although I did learn something I definitely wouldnt recommend taking Macroeconomics, especially if it doesnt have anything to do with your major. I would consider Microeconomics if youre in pursuit of a Bachelors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lee Bailiff is the man You should 100% take his class. He is hands down the best economics processor the TCU department has. If you want to learn about economics, you should 100% take his class. He is the best intro level economics teacher this world hs ever seen.

Good professor if you have some Econ background. He doesn't give you any direction for tests, so it's on you to study. Would not recommend for Freshman, however as a Junior I really enjoyed the lectures and class. Interesting lectures with relevant examples, I would take Bailiff again if he taught any advanced economics courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I recommend Mr. Bailiff, however, if you are looking for an easy class or you don't like to read  A LOT, this may not be the class for you. The only grades he gives in the class are tests (6 essay questions). Also, you must read two extra books on top of the textbook. However, I thoroughly enjoyed his lectures- he provides relevant examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Why are people grading this as average? This class is too much. Be prepared for tests with all short answer questions. No other assignment besides these short answer tests.  6 questions over about 150 pages each test. 3 books you have to read. Grades hard. It's maybe doable if you don't work or have tons of other class work to worry about

I really enjoyed his lectures but the only grades in the class are 5 unit exams and the final. The exams are 6-7 essay questions that if you can regurgitate exactly what he says in class, you will make above a B. I had a really hard time with the exams so I ended up pass/failing but I learned a lot! There are easier professors so keep looking...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Incredible teacher. Simply Fantastic. He knows his topic and is so funny, you won't want to ever miss a class. Go to class take notes if you put in effort you will get a good grade.
HARD TEACHER . DO NOT RECCOMEND. I AM DYING STUDYING FOR HIS EXAM. 5-10 QUESTIONS ON EVERY TEST. DO NOT TAKE.

Awesome lectures! Uses real events that allow concepts to be better understood. Instead of hearing about ice cream cones and potatoes to understand a concept, he will give you a historic reference. Funny and engaging lectures, much better comprehension rate than your average Econ class. A must take

Bailiff is an outstanding teacher who cares deeply about the subject he is teaching. His lectures are engaging and very thought provoking. While attendance is not mandatory if you skip class you simply won't pass the class. All his tests are essay only over the lectures he provides in class so make sure you take good notes. Take his class!!!!!!!!

Take him if you get the chance! He is by far the best professor I've had at TCU. His lectures are very clear and as long as you listen and write down what he says you should be good for the tests (which are taken in blue books). He is always willing to help and he is very easy to understand. He loves to teach and he is just amazing. TAKE BAILIFF!

Bailiff is the best teacher I've had at TCU! His lectures are entertaining and he's actually  funny. He gives a ton of specific examples in class. If you basically just recite his lectures on your test - you'll get an A every time! You can email him questions and he answers which makes it easy to get help! 10/10 - would recommend. BEST TEACHER!
Bailiff is the best!  He is one of my favorite professors at TCU.  If you go to class and listen, you will do well.

Bailiff is a great professor and is usually very clear in teaching the concepts in his lectures. If you don't understand something, always go into office hours for help because he will answer questions, especially before the test. The tests(only grades) can be very difficult, but if you read, go to class, study hard, and ask questions, it's doable.

While attendance is not mandatory, if you don't show up, you won't pass. You have to do a lot of reading, but the lectures make it easily understandable. Mr. Bailiff is an engaging lecturer, he gives lots of real-life examples, and he teaches you to think for yourself. Tests are all open-ended questions, but are your only grades for the class.

If you don't attend class, there is no way you will pass. Bailiff is a great teacher who really knows what he is talking about, I did find the weekly tests to still be difficult even though I attended every class and took notes. He is willing to help you an explain concepts to you outside of class which I really appreciated. All in all, he's tough.

Probably the best professor I have had in college so far. Tests every Tuesday that are not that hard as long as you take good notes and read. He gives great lectures on Thursday and gives a lot of real world examples. I really hopes he gets in to Politics later on in his life because the man is a genius. He would definitely have my vote.

Test every Tuesday that are open response. If you go to class and do your readings you will do fine on them. He's good at what he does and overall the class in pretty interesting. He can be funny, but his nerdy jokes fall flat from time to time. Quizzes are open book and take home. At first, class seems very demanding but it isn't.

Very dry sense of humor which I thought was hilarious.  The way this course is set up is awesome because there are tests every Tuesday and you can drop your two lowest ones.  He lectures straight so you must take good notes. I would definitely recommend him

Lee is a very good teacher. We had a test a week but it was only over what we learned the week before. The final was the same way. So we did not have to cram a whole bunch of stuff for a test. Quizzes are take home straight from the book. He is also very funny.
Do not take her. She is unable to explain her reasoning behind certain topics that were presented on the hw and on exams. Her calculations were wrong most of the time, and she is a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grading scheme is awful!!! I would much rather take any other professor and get an easy A+. Do not take her.

Awful, be prepared to self teach yourself all of the material. 
She will not put in any grades until the last day of the semester, so don't expect helpful feedback on anything.

Dr. Kat does not need to be in a classroom. She intentionally works to make her students fail and will not give helpful or direct instructions or assistance. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

Does not give instructions for assignments. Attendance is very important. Class itself is easy A

BEWARE OF DEADLINES, she gives no warnings for when assignments are due, and will NOT take ANY late work. She is a super easy grader, but will take forever to actually grade it. ATTENDANCE IS MANDATORY. She will take an eternity and a half to email you back so beware. Other than her being a generally difficult person, her class is an easy A.

DO NOT TAKE KAT BARGER! She requires participation through pop questions throughout the class. The lectures do not match the weekly homework assignments or the exams. reviews.comment: Stay away she's absolutely horrible. She tries to trick you in all her test and nothing matching the lectures or the textbook. Thinks she's funny and she's not.

Do not take this course unless you want to be mentally drained. Lectures do not match the homework which doesn't match the book. Continuously refers to herself as a "jerk" and "purposely tries to trick us" on exams. Astronomy with her is not an easy core credit, do not waste your time or energy! Half of the class dropped.

she has a very set way of doing things. She has tech rules in class. Lectures are necessary to do well on the hw and the tests which are in class with lock down. Labs are a big part of the grade. She is very smart but not too approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

She is a nice professor, but her tests and homework are very heavy and do not make sense at all. The questions wordings are misleading, and she does not accept her mistakes making the questions.

She uses her opinion in answers. Not Objective like a science class should be. Most questions are select all that apply and she tries to trick you every way she can.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's nice and is always willing to help people out during office hours. However, she does not seem organized as a teacher. Her tests are formatted strangely and she has a weird grading system. The homework is hard too and the lab is what is probably going be the only reason I get a good grade in this class.

I like her as a person, shes just all over the place as a teacher. Shes very patronizing as a teacher and she tries a bit too hard. She never tells you whats going to be on the test because she makes it the day before so I never feel prepared enough.

This class used these in worksheets called lecture tutorials (for credit), which helped me better understand and apply the information in the class. also, the online hw was a great review, as well as she gave explanations at the bottom help when i didnt understand how to get an answer. also, the in class flash card questions were helpful

Dr. Kat was always available during office hours, and maintained flexibility with other students schedules in order to see them during non-office hours time. Conversing with her comes very naturally, and I never got the feeling of being belittled while asking her for help with course materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Didn't hate her as much as everyone else seems to, but beware of her tests cause they are hard and she doesn't really help you review for them. Count on labs, homework, and in class work for to save your grade. Definitely a doable class though.

Typical kind of weird crazy science professor, lots of opportunities to get points in the class but exams are hard - includes lots of questions where you answer it and then have to explain why you chose your answer. Personally found the material boring, labs & online hw are the best ways to get easy points and boost grades but tests are brutal

My god. I had taken physics before so I knew a lot of the stuff, and I definitely wouldn't have done well if I hadn't. Her teaching style is not conducive to learning at all. Three tests, a lab grade, in class worksheets, online homework, and a final make up your grade. Don't take Dr. Kat.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is very scattered and assumes the whole class is on her astrophysicist plane of understanding (which we weren't). I learned nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'm not sure I really learned anything from this class. If you need help with a concept, chances are she's confused by it too. We would spend several minutes discussing something that she would later realize she explained to us wrong. I basically had to teach myself because she didn't know what was going on half the time. I would not recommend.

The worst professor ever. She says one thing, but when it comes to grading she does something completely different. We are always behind and never finish lectures. Online quizzes are a joke. The questions and answers are often written wrong. You never know what you will be tested on and you just have to guess. Do not take this class!!!

Unhelpful during office hrs

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Kat even though some people seemed to hate her. She was really passionate and intelligent if very slightly unorganized. She assigns homework, two papers, and two tests. There are also lecture tutorials in class which were super helpful. She really wants her students to succeed. Overall, I enjoyed archaeoastronomy.
NOT helpful AT ALL. never gives you the answers if you have class questions. Homework is hard. DOESNT MAKE SENSE AT ALL!!! DONT TAKE THIS CLASS

Although this was just for a science credit, it was supposed to be really, really tough. Thank goodness, Dr. Barger makes Physics enjoyable and understandable. She is available to help you out. Extra credit was given out. Homework went well with what we were learning at the time, only 2 tests. Take home quizzes were challenging, but not hard.

Really Great Professor!!!  Only 2 tests, midterm and final. Most of the grade is based on homework due every friday. Take advantage of the physics lab for homework. Quizzes every Monday over reading assignments that aren't that bad 5 easy comprehensive questions.  TAKE HER I SWEAR PHYSICS ISNT THAT BAD. Gives extra credit to those who comet class

Dr. Benner is exactly the type of professor that you want for a night class. He never goes the full time, so you're always out early, and he won't waste your time with nonsense lectures or assignments. He lectures over exactly what you'll need to know and then test you over it. He's also very knowledgeable about real estate and is a good resource.

Benner is easily one of my favorite professors at TCU. He is so knowledgeable regarding real estate and just wants us to learn what is important. No fluff work. Such a respected guy in RE in Fort Worth. The best!

Benner is a great professor. He understands the perspective of his students and doesn't bore us with information we do not need to know. 

He is very respected in the Fort Worth community and an excellent source of wisdom. Wish I could have taken him for other classes.

Benner is an adjunct and very knowledgable and connected especially if you want to go into real estate. All his classes are lectures and the 4 exams are online. Very simple and easy finance elective course.
He is Great and very successful in his field, take him if you are interested in real estate

This guy is awesome. He works full-time so understands how to effectively communicate the lesson's materials. He doesn't waste time, but instead teaches very well and uses his personal experience to break down concepts. The class itself is not difficult he is a must take for Real Estate. Easy A.
I did a premature review and regret my past review. He is a great professor and honestly I would say he is one of the better professors I have had. You should take him :)
The best and easiest Finance elective. Highly recommend. Night class usually lasts an hour max!
Take it. Purvis is 3 days a week, this is once a week night class. Will last an hour max. Great class

By far easiest prof for real estate principles. 3 test online lock down no camera but straight from his PPTs. No homework or projects. Easiest A. Take him!! Also gives extra credit if you join Real Estate Club. He takes attendances but kinda cancels class a lot and never uses the full time. Again take him!

Nice lady but no need to structure the class the way she does. You will do a presentation almost every week where the grading is verrrry tough. That or a guest speaker that is just complete corporate slop. Take someone else if you can. Did the 3 hour night class and usually went the full time.

Overall super nice lady. Just makes the course super hard for no reason. Tests are in person and are very difficult. In order to achieve the grade you want you will have to grind. Stay away from this course

Professor Lillo is super nice. Most of the grades are group projects with very clear rubric. The exam is hard and you have to study but all other assignments are clear and manageable. The lectures are interesting. She have so much experience. I truly enjoyed the class
Take her if she is available. One of the most genuine and caring professors at TCU. Truly is only teaching to help her students. If you show up to class and do the homework you will succeed.
Good Profesor! Cares about students
I loved her lectures and it goes along with tests very well. Assignments are easy and boost your grade.

Took for Intro to Psych (not 30323). Super kind and good at explaining during lecture. Lectures a little slow but easy to understand. Easy weekly assignments on Sage Vantage. If you study Lecture slides and add a little notes you will do well on exams! 4 exams and 1 Final, she drops the lowest out of all so if you did well you can skip final!

Dr. Joseph is an excellent professor. I had her for PSYC 30323; it was my favorite class by FAR this semester. She always makes lectures very easy to pay attention to and understand. The tests are on exactly what she puts on the study guides, and she assigns other exciting assignments. Truly cannot recommend her or this class enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a really sweet lady and will help you when you need it sewing, but everything you sew must be perfect for you to get a good grade on it. This was such a difficult class, definitely the hardest class I have taken at TCU and the lowest grade I have gotten. The tests are impossible, the class average is almost always failing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a nice person in general but not the best professor. Expect to write a heavy paper for every class - took me at least 3 hours. Her instructions may leave you really confused. She doesn't seem super prepared for each class and her teaching is not very comprehensive but she'd expect you to know everything about the period.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you have other classes that require printing, good luck! Professor Bailey creates a tech-free environment in a technology-linked university. Every week two mini research papers are expected to be printed. Grading is inconsistent as some assignments you will receive feedback while others you don't. Unclear instructions leaving students confused.
Hands on class, must go to every class. Ask for lots of help and take good notes. Tests are hard.

Bailey is a very nice person but an awful teacher. She expects you to know everything there is to know about the material she is teaching just after one class. Her exams and quizzes are extremely difficult and half the time they were not viewable to use for studying. Every time me or any of my peers asked for help she gave nothing in return.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took professor Bailey for both Apparel Construction and History of Modern Dress. She is a tough grader in general, but specifically if you are a POC, she tries her hardest to mark you down. In AC, she expects you to know how to sew automatically, and she does not care about effort. In HOMD, a paper is due every class and participation is req.

She expects everyone to be masters at sewing instantly. She is ridiculously harsh at grading, and doesn't care at all if you put in so much effort. She wants every sample to be perfect regardless of how inexperienced you are. Her tests also are awful. I really do not enjoy this class at all and honestly may day was worst when I had this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Bailey lectures most of the class, and gives you 2 seconds to work on samples tbat are due at the end of class. She grades the samples so hard and the test material is something that won't help you in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: she's so sweet and helpful as a professor. If you need help on anything she'll help and she always gives step by step instructions. the only thing I didn't like about this class was how hard the tests were and how hard she grades samples. I work slower than most and she was really accommodating by letting me come in and work outside of class
She is a really good teacher the class is just very challenging especially if youve never sewn before.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I love Mrs Bailey. She is really nice & helpful. Sewing is not bad at all, to do good on the tests you must pay attention to her lectures and take notes. she gives test reviews which are kinda helpful. she will help you through anything you are confused about

This class is hard. Don't be fooled, it is not a blow off class. Actually learning to sew isn't bad, she definitely helps you in that area. If you don't know how to sew, no big deal, you'll learn. The hard part is her tests. I studied for hours on each test and never got above a 78. It is required for fashion majors, so good luck! B's are possible!

Bailey is a fantastic teacher. I had sewn before entering class and Bailey helped me hone my skills. If you need help she is always there. She is willing to come in and open up the sewing lab for you if you need more time. Her instructions are very clear and she will teach you how to sew. Take the class!

Bailey is a nice person, but as a teacher she is useless. I could learn more on my own than by attending her class. She lets us know she isn't sure if she is telling us the correct information all the time and her tests are insane. She doesn't give out slides or a helpful review. She should stick with sewing, thats what shes actually good at.

Attendence is not maditory but if you miss, she will not give you the powerpoints from class. It is alot of material and all at once. All you do is take notes in class. Tests are NOT easy. She is very nice, but expects you to know things immediatly. NOT a blow off class, you must study and go to class.

She is one of the best teachers I have ever had. She is so nice and EXTREMELY helpful. She is such a good seamstress and really knows her stuff. I would definately recommend her to anyone. And next semester she is teaching Textiles. Take her class!
This woman is awesome! It makes me mad to think anyone would say such mean things about her! She is always willing to help and she is very good at what she does. She is one of my favorite teachers!

I hate this lady with a passion. She is honestly the worst teacher I have ever had at this university. For the money we pay to go to this private univ., you would think that they could get decent profs. She is completely unorganized and disrespectful.
SO NICE and a very smart lady!!!
She is very nice and knows exactly what she is doing. the girls who wrote other stuff are just lazy idiots who dont want to work.
She has no idea of the material she is teaching, and he class is boring
She is not clear and has no clue about what she is teaching.  She is demeaning and rude to students, and is unable to answer questions. If at all possible, avoid taking ANY of her classes.

Professor Bhatt is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. He makes me actually want to come to his classes. He was 3 or 4 quizzes, one large group paper, one group project, and one final that he said is supposed to help your grade. If you do what you are told to do you will make a very good grade. Go to his classes, they are great. 100/10
Lectures aren't too bad to listen to. All papers have been group projects.

Great lectures, sometimes can get boring but most of the time they are interesting. A few quizzes, group projects, and a final. Attendance is highly encouraged but it is not a part of your grade. Just take notes about what he talks about and contribute to projects and you will do well.

He is so entertaining to listen to, you can tell he loves his students and teaching. The best part about his class his how relevant his lectures are, he loves relating legal news to class which makes it so much more engaging!

Shams is a great professor and truly cares about his students both as a person and academically. He is willing to work with you outside of class and you can tell he really cares. The tests were hard and accounting is one of the harder business classes but Shams makes it enjoyable and easy to understand.

Shams is great! He worked many years in public accounting and knows what he's talking about. He is very accessible and works with grades if they are too low. Reach out if you feel you can't complete quality work in time and he will extend dates. Not the most exciting lecturer but you can tell he cares and wants students to learn. Would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors I've ever had at TCU. Accounting isn't an easy class but Shams genuinely cares about each and every one of his students and wants you to succeed. 12/10 would take Shams again, can't say enough positive things about this professor. To succeed just do the homework and practice problems and you'll be fine.

One of my favorite professors I've had at TCU. He truly cares for each of his students and really wants you to succeed and understand the material. Accounting is one of the harder business classes and a lot of work no matter who you have but he made his class fun and easy to understand. Take him if you can!!!

I had Mr. Shams this semester, Fall 2021, for fundamentals of accounting. Going into this class I was nervous based off of hearsay of the material. Mr. Shams created an amazing work environment and genuinely cares about his students. He is available whenever you need him if you have questions and will work with you until you understand it.

She makes the class harder than it needs to be. Like, you actually have to study for exams, which is more than any other music survey class. It's interesting, though, and she's a great teacher. Just wish the class was easier since it's kinda supposed to be a sluff-off class

Professor Vergine was wonderful. She uses a textbook to teach, but it isnt required to purchase for success. Attendance is part of your grade and it helps retaining content. She is so sweet and just wants everyone to succeed and not stress! 100/10 recommend!

Dr. Vergine is GREAT - however, this class is by no means the easiest class you can take for the credit you receive, just take another survery class. Attendance is absolutely mandatory, tests are hard to study for: you'll be expected to listen to excerpts and know the title, composer, era, elements, etc from a list of about 20 songs.

She was great for my Fine Arts credit, she wants everyone to succeed. Gave clear expectations, and would extend deadlines/ curve exams if she saw the class struggle. Easy to understand, even if you have no background. Her lectures are clear, posted online, and super helpful. Quizzes/exams are easy if you study, and she's very approachable.

She's so kind and caring, it's a very easy class. I definitely recommend for anyone in need of an easy fine arts credit. She's easy to reach by email, and though there is a textbook, I don't recommend buying it because it's not at all necessary for success.

Lecture heavy, Dr. V goes very in depth and her understanding of the course material is evident. She posts the slideshows online so study material is very accessible for exams. While a lot of the content is less intuitive for people like me who are not musically inclined, she makes exams and assignments very easy and is a very fair grader.
As long as you go to class you'll be fine

To put it simple, this class is probably no one's first choice and most people that take it are doing so just to get their Fine Arts credit. With that being said, Vergine is the best teachers to have for Survey of Western Art. While the topics are difficult to understand, she tries her best to help students get a grasp of the topics. Great Teacher!

Her Survey of Western Music Art class was pretty interesting, and she made it pretty easy to understand. She looks for some participation, but for the most part she explains the concepts well and provides a lot of listening.

Dr. Bittle was an awesome professor and gave great feedback on assignments. She was one of my favorite professors this semester and I would not hesitate to take her again. She is very thorough and detailed. I learned a lot from her.
Great teacher however during her lectures she goes slowly which leads to her going over in time.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She explains slowly but carefully.

I enjoyed Dr. Bittle. She's super nice and helpful. Make sure you go to class. If you miss a class it'll be hard to understand the hw for that week. He's great overall and would take again. Only thing is project rubrics are not the clearest.
Great professor, is clear with what she wants, and gives awesome lectures in which you actually learn a lot of meaningful stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Well respected prof at TCU. TAs are way more accessible outside of class than she is. The exams are pretty easy, and there are little to no quizzes. LOTS of homework, which is very time consuming. If you skip any classes, you'll pretty much have no idea what's going on.

Dr. Bittle is an excellent professor who makes complex concepts easy to understand. There are two lectures per week that are 50 minutes. However, she goes past the time limit a lot. Most lectures end up being 60 minutes or more. She is very caring and willing to help her students. DOES NOT ACCEPT LATE WORK. I found that TA office hours help a lot.
First of all, don't go into engineering. Bittle is a great teacher and knows what she's talking about, but you also need to know your stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Bittle for both Graphics & Design and Statics, and she was an excellent professor for both courses. Dr. Bittle's lectures are informative and she does plenty of examples, so make sure you attend class. Her office hours will help you solidify concepts and will definitely help you get better grades. Overall, I highly recommend Dr. Bittle!

Dr. Bittle is very nice and expectations are clear. Lots of homework and lectures every class. Overall an easy class if you put in the work but can be very boring and tedious. Most exam questions are very similar to homework questions so make sure you know how to do them and use your note sheet on exams.

Take Dr. Bittle if it is the last thing you do. Seriously the best teacher I have ever had. Her course is structured very clearly, she tells you what will be on each test and quiz. Showing up to class is important in order to understand the material and she explains everything very well in class. She sets you up for success. I love Dr. Bittle.

Dr. Bittle is great! She was always very clear with her grading criteria; she also stuck with it, so she was sometimes a hard grader. Her lecture were great though! If you put in all the effort, you will for sure get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I don't have enough characters to express to you how much I love Bittle. She is extremely knowledgeable about ENGR. If it wasn't for her I would have got discouraged and switched out of Engineering. The Bittle/Cote tag-team is phenomenal, I love them both and will sign up for any other class they teach in the following semesters.

Great introductory course for engineering with the perfect professors to teach this course! Interesting material that can be challenging, but Dr. Bittle and professor Cote are there to help. Highly recommend taking this class if you are remotely interested in engineering.

Took her for Intro to Engineering, and she was a pretty clear and good professor. Everything was fairly easy, but you do have to put effort in for weekly homework and three group projects. Group projects can be very easy or absolute condemnation, depending on who ends up being in your group. Overall, good class and will take her again for Solids

Second class I took with Dr. Bittle. She is consistent and clear. Homework will be due every week. She follows the syllabus and there is only one project, which is fun. At this point, the class is very chill with her since most had her for intro to engineering the semester before. She tells you what will be on her exams so they are very easy.

Dr. Bittle is straight-forward when it comes to everything. The projects will be hard if your team doesn't cooperate but other than that, everything is rather easy. Homework does take a while but it isn't too bad after a while. What she says will be on the exam  what will be on the exam. No curve balls. Consistent across the board so that helps.
Good prof but hard class. You have to love it or else you're screwed.
Dr. Bittle is a good prof but the class is a lot of work. You better REALLY love engineering or else it sucks.

I had Dr. Bittle for an intro engineering class that's required for all ENGR majors. "Design and Graphics" was pretty easy, probably one of the easiest ENGR classes you'll ever take. Dr. Bittle is very straightforward and gives a LOT of partial credit. Make sure you talk to her and put effort into your work, she'll help you out a lot more.
Good

Very helpful professor who made intro to engineering enjoyable. The tests were not bad at all, but the homework is graded for correct answers and can be difficult. Overall I liked the class and look forward to taking her for statics next semester!

Dr. Bittle is a great engineering professor. Freshman engineers will experience her back to back in intro and then statics.  Both classes were fairly easy to make a high A in, but had a large amount of homework. Intro to engineering (or engineering design) is a very fun class that non-engineers would enjoy.

Awesome professor. I wish she taught all my classes. She's not very hard but at the same time if you don't put in the work your not gonna get an A. Definitely is an easy grader. We had one hard test in statics and she curved it so that the grades were still high. Overall you learn great from her and get the grade you want, win-win!

Very helpful professor.  Some concepts may be difficult to comprehend during her lectures, but she is willing to help you out during office hours.  Will give you a higher letter grade if she knows you put in a lot of effort. Well, she did for me.
Class 10033: Class was moderately easy, easy to understand with minimal work. Bittle was easy to get in touch with and very clear in her lectures; overall a great teacher to work with.

Professor Bittle was wonderful. I found the class interesting and I'm not even majoring in engineering. She's helpful and she notices when you put forth a lot of effort. Do the homework and you'll be good.

You get points on tests and homework for everything you do, even if it's wrong.  You have to go to class and lab or else the drawings won't make sense.  You work on the lab homework in lab together.  Always bring the book you're working with at that time to class.  Class and lab homework each week helps balance out the two or three tests

Dr. Bittle seems like a fairly good professor. I found her lectures to be hard to understand until she started working the example problems. She tends to keep class late, and her general manner might be irritating to some. She seems to like open-book tests, however, these are not as easy as you might think.
Easy

ENGR 10032 (Statics). Dr. Bittle spells everything out and tells you exactly what is going to be on the tests. She is always willing to answer your questions so if you do the homework you should get at least a B in the class.

Very nice and willing to help. She does move fast in class but she was availible every day before class to go over homework due that day. If you don't understand something just go to her office and ask. If you can't make atleast a B then you're lazy and shouldn't be in college.
very good professor.
She goes really fast.  Doesnt really explain what to do.  But the tests are not that bad. Do your homework!!!  Easy B
No Comments
Amazin  Tests are extremelye easy as she tell you the question before the exam Do the homework seriously and u shd be fine  I recommend this professor to everybody  It is an easy A class
Very nice lady, intro engineering is not hard.  She moves too fast sometimes, but you can figure out work on your own.  Not too much work.
She is the easiest part of your first year in engineering. You learn a lot and get an A or B. If you get less you need to rethink your life. Mrs. Bittle rock, her hubby is a bit harder.
She is a great teacher! If you to go to class, do all your homework, and pay attention it's an easy A. Open book Tests!
Dr. Bittle is great!  Just pay attention and do your work!  She's incredibly helpful and understanding.
Great teacher. Really knows her stuff. Willing to help when needed. Be prepared for lots of homework. Very nice.
Very nice... just go to class and pay attention!
nice person, VERY helpfull, fun class, intresting design problems.
Questions on quizzes and exams are tricky. Final is cumulative, and there's no review for it. If you're absent on the day of a team exercise you get a zero and he doesn't tell you when they are.

Nice guy who is the accounting department chair and teaches like you should know more than you actually will. This class is mostly dependent on the quizzes and exams where he uses a lot of true and false and generally has low averages. He does an okay job of explaining tough material but not great. I would take someone else for this class if youcan

Wempe is a very nice man. But, this class was way too difficult. He would say that he knew we weren't accounting majors and he wouldn't trick us, but (whether intentionally or not) often did on tests. He treated this course as if we were masters of accounting students which we were far from.

Great person, but this class was a pre-req for business majors and was treated like a graduate accounting course. Tests and quizzes are extremely difficult, and there is a cumulative final. Spare yourself.

was a very nice and smart man however though I felt like seeking help outside of class was accessible, it was not helpful. he made the class way too difficult and did not offer any help. no study guides, no new practice problems, homework did not even help for studying. this class is for non-accounting majors and he treated it as though we were.
Great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I had Wempe for graduate managerial accounting. The homework was manageable, but his final was brutal. At 2.5 hours, probably 90% of the class was still taking it. At 3 hours, probably 70% were still taking it. He's very nice, and lectures were interesting, esp with real world application, but I hated the final.

Class was extremely difficult. The averages for the class on the first two tests were 70% and 60.5%. I studied extremely hard for the final and managed to get a 82% on it. My grade should have been a 77% but Professor Wempe rounds everyone grades up at the end and he gave me a B from a C+.

I loved Dr. Wempe! He is very dry though, I would not recommend him for an 8 AM class. He knows his stuff and is very enthusiastic, but he is also very detailed when it comes to testing. I didn't kill myself in this class, but you need to show up, do the homework, and study quite a bit for the A.

He actually teaches you managerial well but you have to go to every class to keep up with his note packet because there is a lot of fill in the blank. Good teacher but the tests were really hard. He does curve your grade about 5 points at the end though to even out his bell curve

Mr. Wempe teaches like every student is an accounting major.  Do not take his tests lightly because you will regret it in the end.  I struggled and had to pull some magic to manage my grade.  I would recommend finding an easier teacher, unless you like the challenge.
IMPOSSIBLE TEACHER!!!!! hard class... do not take it.
Very hard teacher. You study the notes he gives you and then on the test he throws a curveball at you. He will go out of his way to trick you on the test. I would avoid this teacher!!!!

Dr. Wempe is certainly among the best professors at TCU.  He is a ruthless tester, but gives his students every opportunity to practice and learn.  He shows a passion for managerial accounting and I think he's a kind and caring person.  You will earn your grade in this class.  No free rides!

Great Professor! Tests are hard, but if you show up to class and review his notes you will be fine. Don't need to review the textbook much for tests, but the notes he gives you are crucial! Will go the extra mile to help students and what you learn in his class will really help you in the future.

He is extremely nice, but his test are nearly impossible the class average is a 60 and he only curves a point or 2. I would not take him ever again. He expects way too much from students and purposely tries to trick students on test.

This class is not easy even though he is the easier managerial accounting professor. The tests are really confusing so make sure you know the material very well. Don't take his class in the morning if you have a hard time paying attention because it's really easy to get lost.  Cool guy though.

Managerial Accounting 60013:  Hard professor.  He expects a lot out of you in terms of learning outside of class.  His tests are extremely hard.  He makes the class interesting and relevant to real world experiences.
A very practical class. Pay attention and you'll do well. He covers everything you need to know and the message he's trying to convey in each lecture is very clear.

I think he makes what most people say is an easy class pretty dificult. I hope you like accounting because you need to to stay awake in this class. Teaching yourself is critical here and don't sit in the back..all you can here is ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ...

I think the prof must have read these comments, because thus far the professor appears to be very clear about what is expected of you and lets you know EXACTLY whats going to be on the test.  It's definatly not an easy class, but this prof has made this difficult class much easier.
Just know the notes he GIVES to you and you will do fine on the tests...says "anybody" a lot (listen for it).

HARD professor. his exams are so hard that makes you feel like you dont know anything. dont take him unlike that you like to teach yourself and cry in hard exams. almost everyone was failing in my section.
No Comments
Not the best teacher.  Exams are difficult.  Basically copy everything he writes and teach yourself.  I'll give him this, he curved our class significanlty because so many were doing poorly.

In Econometrics, Bista uses formulas to explain concepts, rather than explaining them with words.
