His econ class are interesting and funny. He keeps you awake and interested in the class. Tests a little hard, but fair. Random fact: He loves Elvis.. mention him and you'll be remembered.
He's a really good teacher.

Definitely a difficult class but if you put in the work, you will get the results you want. Make sure you know how to study or learn how too because you will definitely have too. Overall I enjoyed the class, makes you think and topics are interesting but absolutely don't blow this class off or your grade will reflect that.
dont take this class point blank period

Do not take this class unless you have to. She comes off super fun and energetic, but then completely destroys you when it comes to exams and pop quizzes. Make sure to attend every lecture because if you even try to skip, you'll miss everything for the test becasue a lot of the times, the notes don't match with what she's explaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her class is extremely lecture based and boring, but you still have to pay attention because if you zone out for two seconds you'll miss an entire chapter. She is very unhelpful when it comes to questions and explaining how to do assignments outside of class. Would not reccomend taking this class if you don't have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You learn so much in this class. Tests are a lot of application so make sure to take notes in a way that you will understand when you go to study. The lectures are all very interesting so it goes by quickly!
She is awesome! Her exams require studying because they are almost all application, but very doable. She is very knowledgeable and loves questions!

I LOVE Professor Burger.  There were pop quizzes and take-home ones, but lots of extra credit. I really enjoy her lectures, and she is super enthusiastic about her field. A great class that you will learn a lot from if you put the effort in, but definitely not a blow-off class.

Prof Bueno tried all year to micromanage my behavior to an extent that it felt unjustified. I would sometimes draw smiley faces in my notebook and she gave me a lecture after class for it being unacceptable and could distract other students. 
Directions were often unclear for assignments and grammar was not explained well at all.

DO NOT TAKE. She had favorite students all year, and even though I was the favorite, it was glaringly obvious how much harder she was on my friends for no reason. She would discuss the grades of specific students with with me behind their backs and it made me highly uncomfortable. That's not good teacher behavior. The class was unnecessarily hard.

This class was unnecessarily hard. LOTS of presentations and in-class papers. Directions are almost always unclear or confusing. In-class papers and presentations count for pretty much all of the grade. Does give a lot of extra credit (only reason I got an A). Do the extra credit. She speaks ONLY in Spanish and has thick accent (hard to understand)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She spends most of class time doing activities, and I wish she would spend more time explaining the content we took notes over (outside of class) as the notes were often vague. Overall, very nice prefessor but her class is definitely difficult. Just get on her good side and show her you're working hard and you should be fine.

Professor Bueno likes to see effort. Her local to global class is very presentation heavy and you must be comfortable with not reading off of a script for your presentations. She is really kind and makes herself very available. Extra credit possible. Quizzes are for extra credit points on essays. Get ready to write a lot.

She is unclear in a lot of her directions but gets mad if you don't follow exactly what she intended you to (which reflects in your grade). Very nitpicky in your accent and grammar, specifically with accents on words and Spain slang. Is not a very homework-heavy class but doesn't explain nearly enough of the topics to be quizzing the way she does.
This is a great professor. Cares about her students

She is a very nice person but the toughest grader. You have to follow every instruction to get points for assignment; if you miss something, you'll get an automatic 0 -- no in between. Participation really matters so if you take her, try to attend every class

quizzes are kinda rough if you don't study, you have to know the exact names of the icons which is more difficult than it sounds. Spend the $30 for a hard copy of the course manual, it is much easier to flip through than accessing the one online.
Great professor, super nice and carrying, her lessons are very interesting, but the exams make up most of your grade and they are difficult.
She provides really clear study guides so you know exactly what will be evaluated on exams! Engaging lectures, you do not need to buy the book.

Dr. Cox is honestly such a nice person, BUT HER TESTS ARE NOTHING LIKE HER POWER POINTS!!!! I have gone to class every single day and truly tried to do well on them, but they are extremely hard. Her "extra" homework assignment to "help" is complete BS. These are graded extremely hard. Her TA does almost everything for grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Like most psych prof, if you participate in SONA you can receive EC. She is engaging and very authentic in her teaching and communication. She offers great PPT as a baseline, in other words go to class to fill in the blanks. Her schedule is SUPER busy so I'm not sure how much extra time she has for helping students. There was a TA. Recommended!

Wonderful class! Extremely interesting. Writes all notes on the board so important to go to class. Tests are a bit more difficult than you may think based on class material so STUDY! Getting an A is definitely attainable if you go to class and do well on writing assignments

Very fair teacher. Extremely well versed in statistics and breaking them down in an understandable way. Gave handouts and book chapters online. Class was a series of assignments rather than tests. I got a lot out of this course.

I really did not think this class was that difficult. That might be because the information was so applicable and interesting! Dr. Cox is super enthusiastic, funny, and more than willing to help you and answer questions. Her lectures are a little scattered, but she's great at giving examples. If you come to class, you will do fine on the tests.

Loved this class! Dr. Cox kept things interesting and her homework assignments are pretty fun, too! Gives study guides for all of the exams. Exams are a little tricky. Don't need the book unless you like extra reading.

Love her! She's hilarious and keeps the class interesting. Really pay attention to the homework assignments because it can really help your grade in the end if you do well. Tests are a little bit challenging. She's extremely quick at returning emails and is always in her office for you to talk to her. Awesome professor!

Dr. Cox is hillarious! I enjoyed her personality class & would recommend taking it. I learned so much from the class; it is interesting even if you are not a psych major/minor. You do not need to buy the book!
Attendance is mandatory for notes and extra credit points. Interesting material. For tests you MUST study both book and lecture. Interesting class, I enjoyed it. Definitely possible to get an A.

Thought personality psyc would be interesting but she was so elementary. Unorganized, harsh grader on essays. Test questions are extremely vague. You cannot skip class!! Seemed like she was more interested in trying to make funny jokes and be liked than actually teaching.

The questions on the tests were very tricky. Lectures didn't always flow too well, she seemed a little disorganized. All in all she was an OK professor, and relatively harsh grader on the short answer portion of the tests.

This class is not hard but go to class. I failed first exam because I was nervous and unprepared. Rest of exams got a 90 or higher and still ended with a B-. Only grade is based on exmas and final is not cumulative. Pay attention to all his rants in class and read textbook and you should be fine. You just have to do well on the exams.

went to every single class, and he consistently started lectures 10–15 minutes late in a 50-minute class. The material was disorganized, no PowerPoints, just random notes scribbled on the board. Before the exam, he handed out 12 pages of problems with absolutely no explanation. Grades were never updated, and he doesn't respond to emails. DONT TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most unorganized dude ever, but very aware of it. I thought he was funny, feels like you don't learn much though. Doesn't put grades in til the end, but it's not a super hard class.

Butler is a very nice guy, but he is insanely unorganized. He does not post grades at all, ever, and D2L is scattered everywhere. He does not really teach in class and instead goes off on tangents. He also does not respond to emails.

Professor Butler is one of the best professors I have had here at TCU! His lectures are interesting and thorough because of his great sense of humor. His tests are exactly like the study guide, and he is willing to meet with you outside of class if you struggle. Must take MICROECON professor at TCU!
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best prof in life. Take him.

Quirky guy who I really enjoyed having. Class is pretty straightforward if you attend lectures and actually pay attention to what he's saying. Also, be sure to read the assigned chapters from the multiple textbooks he requires (not a lot of reading) because he will put that on his exams. Lastly, keep track of your grade yourself, doesn't use D2L.
Professor Butler's micro lectures can be hit-or-miss, but the class is pretty straightforward. Use unstuck AI and the free textbook to supplement and you'll do well.

His lectures are straight forward however he can go off on tangents that aren't related. He will send out study guides that include things that are actually on the exams. I recommend attending his office hours before an exam because he will basically tell you what's on the exam. He doesn't put grades in D2L till the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'd recommend. He makes the content pretty straight-forward. Some cons are he doesn't grade anything until finals week and most of the grade is based off of 4 exams. So, going into exams week, you won't know where you stand. However, I never really went to class and only studied for the exams the night before and got an A-. Pretty funny guy.

The class overall was easy. We covered way less material than the other micro classes along with some random history. Your entire grade is based upon 4 tests (including the final). He only took attendance and gave us homework twice which also counts for your grade. He doesn't post grades until after the final, which I have no clue what I got on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is chill and has a very light workload, your grade is mostly the 4 exams. As long as you show up everyday and read everything you're supposed to you should get an A. Doug is also super funny/nice and explains the material very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You won't know your grade until the end of the semester. His lectures are boring and are not usually focused on economics. It is a pretty easy class compared to the other professors. If you don't want to learn about econ and have to teach yourself everything butler is fine. Don't buy the other books and find the textbook online.

A very sporadic professor who sometimes lectures all class about random things that won't be on a test, but also the *non-economic* material might also be on the test. The lectures can be quite boring as well. The class is basically graded on only 4 exams with almost no other grades, yet you won't know your grade until the end of the year anyways.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The GOAT; he was my professor for Micro. He's hilarious and tries to make the class laugh. He does talk about his wife a lot, but I thought it was funny. As a teacher, it's not a hard class, but it is one of those classes where you become overconfident, get a test, and bomb it (My Experience)

Professor Butler is one of the most open and charismatic professors I've ever met. He is so understanding of any situation you might have and never takes things too seriously. He may go on tangents here and there while overexplaining simple concepts, but I'd rather have that than the opposite.

Inmd Micro - Did I learn that much about econ? No. But did I learn about myself? Yeah boy. There's no sense in trying to change Doug. Funny dude, showed the Bizarre Foods video again, tests are literally just his lectures, which way overexplain simple content, but I'm not complaining. Be ready for a classic Doug tangent rant, enjoyable time lol

DB is the funniest professor I've ever taken. One day, we learned about tradeoffs & substitution by watching an episode of "Bizarre Foods" where a woman sold fried tarantulas. That was probably the most normal day of class. Tests are easy.

Hilarious professor. Show up to class because his tests are written the way he thinks and that can be really key to understanding what he's asking you to do. If you do the outside work he provides (which is not mandatory or graded), you will do well on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Attendance isn't exactly mandatory but his tests are based heavily on lectures. He is really funny and explains things well.

Butler is hilarious and if you enjoy sarcastic humor you will love him. Attendance isn't mandatory and lectures can get boring as he sometime tends to go on random tangents about nothing, but he rewards those who show up by putting stuff on tests only people who attended class would know. Make sure to read articles he posts online before tests!

Dr. Butler is hysterically funny, usually twisting economic concepts into amusing anecdotes to make his point. He's great at explaining exactly how economics can be seen and applied in real life. He can be a bit scatterbrained at times, but there's nothing on the tests he doesn't go over extensively in class and hardly any homework.
He is great! Very funny! Class is pretty easy just read the articles he posts onilne

Dr Butler is super quirky but hes hilarious. I didnt really pay attention to lectures and he doesnt really take attendance. If you do his study guides, read the book, and go to office hours he'll like you will do well.
He is a character but the class is not exactly a blow off class. Definitely an easier econ teacher though

Butler is a very funny guy, but beware if you do not have a pretty good understanding of economics. I did not.  I struggled in this class even though I attended all classes. DO NOT TAKE THIS AS A BLOW OFF CLASS. I took this class P/NC (as a business major) and passed easily, but still put a lot of effort into studying/learning.

Butler is a character and a half! I took him for intro to Micro and it was a difficult class but he made it interesting. I thought he was really funny and I enjoyed the class even though it was challenging for me. Some people get easy As in his class and others, like me, have some issues. But I would take him again, just make sure to do the rdngs

Butler is a crazy, he puts instant coffee mix in his coffee! He tells a story about a guy who lived in Alabama and used barter as his only means of exchange...we think that was actually him. You read wild articles, and makes witty jokes that are really funny, but only if you get the reference. Ended up with A- in the class

Professor Butler is the best. He's a pretty funny guy, who uses a lot of applicable and easy to understand examples to teach concepts. An awesome choice for Econ. Tests are pretty easy if you do the problems he suggests in the book and show up to class.

Those who know anything about Econ will get through with flying colors. Those who don't should pay a little attention. Although, some of the outside reading occasionally appears on tests, so be careful about that.
Great teacher. Makes the class interesting, will give help outside the class if needed and takes an interest in your success.

Scatterbrained? Yes. Knowledgeable? YES. He may come off as a goofy guy, but my father is an Econ Professor from Cambridge and sat in on one of his classes. After the class he said "Refreshing, he makes even the most mundane information interesting, splendid professor." I agree with my dad.

Haha. Oh Butler. He's an extremely goofy guy. Really smart, but very scatter brained. Lectures are absolutely pointless. I only went so he knew who I was, but I just got on facebook the entire time. I know a lot of people that struggled in his class, but if you do the readings and understand the concepts, it's an easy A.

Hes a very nice guy and he wants you to do well in class but the only grades you have are the tests. He takes alot of questions from lecture and the two shorter books, not the main textbook. Going to office hours wont help and neither will memorizing. you just have to really understand economics bc his questions are analytical.
He is a really nice guy, even if he's scatterbrained at times. His class is very easy though and attendance is pretty much optional. His tests are very straightforward and mostly lecture based.

I actually liked this class because Dr. Butler is quirky yet keeps things relevant (for the most part). The readings and lectures weren't bad, and some stuff from the lectures ended up on the test. I went to every class, tried to keep up with the readings, and studied the study guides he sent out and got a B+ (a few decimal points away from an A)
Funny guy but going to class is pretty pointless. If you do the reading and go to the reviews you should be fine. He seems to talk in circles most of the time but overall not a difficult class.
Awesome teacher, does not cover a lot in class so you don't need to go, but he's really entertaining and funny, easy if you read what he tells you, take him

He's very entertaining and goofy in class, doesnt really teach much, but as long as you do the readings outside of class it's easy to make an A. Plus he's a lot better than all the other teacher for Micro.

He definitely kept my interest! I have taken a micro class before, so it was somewhat painful to sit through his slow pace. Tests were still difficult because of his odd and strangely-worded questions, but he doesn't cover much information. He is very entertaining and wants everyone to do well; I had a great time in his class.

Took him because I heard he is easy-he is in some aspects b/c attendance is not mandatory. He gives extra credit for going to class on fridays. Reading is pretty light and easy-but tests are worded very witty/tricky so you end up making mostly B's-A's if you are lucky. Good class though
He's hilarious. Easy class. Doesn't teach anything in class, but if you read on your own you'll make a high B or A. Take Butler!

Worst teacher ever! Going to class is completely useless. He shows up 10 to 15 minutes late to every class period. He never has his stuff together. When he does teach, its a sea at best. He is completely flaky! He has a habit of sending you 5 to 6 page articles that you'll need to read and memorize 1 hour to 30ins before the test.

I don't understand how you couldn't get an A in this guys class. You would have to seriously not care about school. I got As on all of his tests. All you have to do is the assigned reading (which isn't much) and be awake during class. He made Micro feel like basic college algebra. He also quotes Animal House and The Big Lebowski in class.

He is definitely a character. You never know what you are going to get when you come to class. A lot of people stopped showing up because the lectures usually veer off the topic of economics quickly. It can be helpful to attend class though. The most important thing is to READ.

He is very knowledgable about economics but doesnt have the best teaching method. Class is mainly just listening to him talk. He is a pretty funny guy and makes class entertaining. Tests arent that hard as long as you have read and studied.

Butler is definately an interesting character. His lectures are all over the board and are kind of confusing. Most people don't show up to class except for exams. Exams are meant to trick you, so pay attention in class. He'll send out a review before the exams. You probably have to take him if you're a Business major, so just pay close attention!
he's a cool guy  but his teaching method is not good at all.  his tests are tricky and its not an easy a but you can def. pass with a b

He is so funny. Dry sense of humor but keeps class entertaining. If you get the review from previous people taken the class..you'll pass. I've gotten A's on all my test and have no interest in economics. No quizes or homework. Has taken attendance randomly two times. Great professor!
Funny guy.
He is so funny!

Doug is one of the best professors I have had.  His lectures are a bit off the wall, but if you are patient and stick with it they will make sense and actually clarify his points.  If you don't, you're an idiot.  I learned a lot and still use the books he assigned for references.
VERY EASY A! Go to class and get involved with the lectures. Read the book and you'll do great. I got high B's on the first two test and a 97 and 100 on the last two. Take him!

Easiest econ class at TCU. He's kind of annoying and tells way to many lame jokes which is mainly why i skipped class so much. As long as you read the chapters he assigns and the NUMEROUS articles he e-mails, you'll be fine.

Butler is a good teacher.  Attendance is key if you want to make an A.  There is a decent amount of reading you have to do but its pretty simple stuff and he gives a ton of examples in class to explain the different concepts. Overall is think he was so so. I made a B but thats only because I had a hard time concentrating in class.
I learned somethings, he is really funny and pretty easy going on grades
Go in and care about the class. He really appreciates it and will help you if you want it.
very smart guy that will take the time to help you out whenever you'd like, be focused during class because he'll go crazy sometimes but explains everything extremely well.
Good teacher. Hes a pretty funny guy and makes class enjoyable.

out of all the economic teachers at TCU you need to take Doug Butler.  yes, the material is hard but no other teacher presents it better than him.  uses examples that are easy to remember and very funny.  class attendance is a must if you want to get an A; a B is easy to get if you sometimes go but study a lot.  highly recommend

Funniest guy ever!.. I had him for intermediate micro and got a B in it. Definetely go to class, and study! He is disorganized, always late, never answers e-mails, and loves to ride his bike. He is OK teaching, however his sense of humour makes the class great. Getting an A in this class is veery hard. so if you know your sh*t, take this class.

He's a really, really funny and odd guy.  He cracks me up all the time.  He definitely keeps you entertained and you actually learn economics, which is suprising.  I highly recommend him.  Definitely utilize his office hours!

Funny guy! He should be in comedy central! His classes are interesting and he actually makes you love his class. There are not many readings at all and the exams are based on them. It is pretty easy class and A is relatively easy to get. He likes coffee and saying jokes! If you take this class, choose him

I get so confused from his lectures. All the examples are focused on drugs and alcohol which get confusing. Your entire grade is from tests which sucks! Wouldnt suggest him. Ya he is funny but he never helps you out. I have to email him about 6 times before he responds to me.

Public Finance w/D. Butler = easy!  If you take good lecture notes and half read the books, there's no reason not to get an A.  Everything you learn is pretty valuable information whether or not you are an econ major.  If you're stuck, ask...he's very willing to help and even hold review sessions before tests, if requested.  Highly recommend.

If you read what he tells you to and pay attention to him telling you the same thing over and over in class, then it is an easy A.  He makes it interesting and drills it into your head.  Good about responding to e-mails and funny.  Weird, but open/funny in class.  Offers review sessions before tests.

It's a pretty easy A if you listen to what he has to say.  He takes his outside readings seriously because he will throw a few questions from them.  He is a really nice guy that wants his students to do well, but people think that not going to class and not paying attention is going to get them a good grade when all they are doing is being foolish.
Taking Survey of Theatre was harder than this class. Take it with Butler, and this will be the easiest class you ever took. He is fun, the material is really easy and the book is for idiots.

he doesn't teach well at all, just tends to ramble on during lectures. you can get away w/ skipping a lot of his classes, but just make sure to go through all of the readings to do well on the tests, they can be pretty hard if you dont fully understand the concepts

This is an easy class. The tests are mostly based on the readings, which are short and easy. Sometimes it helps to go to class, but if you miss one every week you could still get an A. I didn't do any reading until a day or two before the test and I got an A on every test after the curve(he curves a lot). Not a bad class at all.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS. He's awful, he's not funny even though the class laughs at him, and he is not a good teacher. The tests come from now where and I so amazingly hard. Don't take it I promise. Even if you read, take notes, go to class, a B Is still as good as I have ever gotten on a test.

Do not take this class!! He doesn't treat it like an intro course, and when the test grades are low he doesn't think that it's even partially because of his teaching methods or the way he writes the tests. He doesn't teach the way he tests at all. The tests are harder than you expect them to be after the lectures he gives.

Don't take him.  Yeah he's kind of entertaining but he falls asleep in his class more than his students do. His tests seem to come out of no where but if you at least do the reading, you'll pass. If you learn visually, good luck, all of his graphs look the same. He did a nice drawing of the Wal-Mart parking lot once though. I didn't learn a thing.

not a great class, but a passible one. he's really boring, has no book, and will put questions on the tests that he didn't teach you just to make sure no one gets 100%. he's a nice guy and all but you can't really prepare a whole lot for the tests

I thought the class was rather easy. He was funny and even wrote on the wall once! You do have to study a little bit, but he has review sessions to go over all the problems he assigned. The tests aren't that hard if you read the readings he e-mails you.

I dont know how anyone could say this class is easy. Butler just rambles incoherently about nothing. His tests are really hard because they call for perfect recollection of readings and movies shown in class. I don't miss class and I am a good student but I still have a C.
No Comments

Hilarious guy! Actually made micro interesting... aside from the 3 weeks it took to get our predominantly hungover class to understand the concept of supply and demand. Easy easy A though for anyone who shows up and does the minimal reading. Very entertaining.

He is an excellent teacher.  He will go out of his way to help you and puts a lot of effort into teaching the class.  You learn a lot and if you work hard and do all of the required readings you have the potential to get an A.  I would take another class by him if I had the opportunity.

I made an A in this class with no problem. He is a very nice guy. I agree with what was said below, if you don't understand micro theory, you need not to be in college. I just loved all the greek people that would walk in talking about how **** they got during the weekend and then act shocked when they failed the tests. It was sooo funny!!!

horrible teacher!!! avoid this class at all costs!! unless you already have taken micro and know everything about it and like study sessions that go like this "any questions?" and that is all that will go on in the study sessions doesn't review you at all!! and there is ALOT of reading!!!!!!!!!!
His ramblings made it hard for me to follow.  If you're a visual learner, it's a nightmare!
Is getting paid to goof off. That's all this class is. Goofing off three hours a week. If you want to have a blow off and not learn, take him. If you want to learn, take someone else.
Really easy and very funny. I recommend him.
Hilarious guy, class is worth it just to hear him talk. do the readings he gives you and read the armchair book.
Funny guy, very random. If you can take structured notes in an unstructured class, go for it, easy if you read.
Very funny and laid back...no homework.

Funny guy makes jokes all the time, even if you don't understand em, Very laid back and likes to talk about current events. No homework, attendance is optional, just do the readings and you'll do fine

What's up with the low ratings?  His class is so awesome because attendance never counts, there isn't any graded homework, and he goes on tirades about government policies.  If you need a teacher to explain micro-economic theory to you then you don't deserve to go to college, perhaps even exist.

funny teacher, but i didn't understand what he weas talking about. i attended class, did the readings, but still did really bad on the tests. unless you're a micro genius and already know what's going on, don't expect to get good explanations.
Very easy, read the stuff he tells you to and you will be fine.
No Comments
very random, not much intellectual stimulation. he does play some cool videos.
he was a very funny guy, the lectures may have been a little random but it made you want to go to class and learn.  Good teacher

Lectures are so off the wall you wonder what the heck any of it has to do with econ. Tests are somewhat hard so just do the Readings and study from the text book and you should be fine. Most lectures consist of him rambling on about beer and his friend who did lsd...he'll make you laugh for sure!!
This is a very easy class if you follow directions.  Simply attend the lectures and DO THE READINGS he assigned and you're on your way to an easy A.  Plus, he's hilarious!
great class, funny guy!!, easy.dont neglect the readings, and listen and you got it made.tests are a bit tricky
easiest micro prof here, go to class read the handouts, easy B, work a little bit harder to get an A

Seriously, what is the deal with people giving Butler low ratings? I think this guy is awesome. The tests aren't bad if you read and he talks about alcohol in all his classes. It really isn't that hard if you go to the review sessions, and his stupid jokes are actually funny.
Funny guy. Pay attention and you will be fine. I liked him.

If you have had ANY economics before, you'll be ok. His lectures are off topic, random, and really make you wonder why you took time out of your day to listen. His test are hard, but if you study an A is possible. DO THE READING-even the random things that hav nothing to do with econ!

Well, the four chapters we actually covered all semester weren't too bad- tests are just very tricky. Lectures are usually random and it's hard to follow him and his messy scribble all over the board.  I defeinitely wasn't impressed with him.

Probably the worst teacher that I've ever had! I never understand what he talks about in class. It feels like coming to class is just a waste of time. He is very wordy and most of the times it's almost impossible to understand what he's trying to say. Don't take him!

His class is really easy if you pay attention and read the stuff he assigns. His lectures are repetitive and occasionally off topic, but it keeps peoples attention long enough to learn something. If you can't pass his class you're a moron...

He is the funniest teacher I have ever had. I am glad I took this class with him. I really am interested almost every day. He teaches more than econ. but also good ideas for life. I think that it is very easy, but I have heard people say otherwise.
he moves very slow and covers only main points of economics, allows you time to understand concepts--he is really funny!
If you go to class and do the readings you will be fine. He gets a little off subject sometimes but a really funny guy. Available outside of class for help. Good class
This class is so.. easy if you actually show and listen.  Do the readings and you are golden.  People who think he is hard either dont go or dont do the readings.
i sit in class wondering why i am there. this class is ridiculous. unless you are some economics freak don't take butler
lectures are pretty much pointless, but hes a pretty funny guy. makes jokes alot but doesnt teach too well. read and study all of the readings he assigns and it should be a pretty easy A.

If you want to learn nothing about econ, this is the teacher for you.  We have only got through 5 chapters and learned just about nothing.  His tests are easy and pointless.  So if you want to leave nothing and get a good grade, you want Butler.
Very funny if you like his style of humor.  Very redundent lectures, but entertaining.  Tests are hilarious and also straight forward, all you have to do is make sure to read what he assigns.

I think this is one of the worst teachers I've had, his lectures make no sense since he spends most of his time talking about his friend Wes Hauf that does lSD and his test are hard and very weird, nothing to do with actual econ!

not the greatest teacher... never went to class and i made A's on all the tests.  watch out for the final, it's nothing like his normal tests... it's a "real" test, not lame questions from his lectures
Funny, and tries to make the subject interesting. Test are somewhat difficult. Can make a B with moderate effort

tests are hard.  (he himself never makes more than 95s in his tests) interesting guy but could be offending to some.  hard to tell when he changes subjects.  other times hard to tell why he changed the subject.
horrible professor, will not help you at all.... he doesn't know how to

Good guy but not very productive, we only got threw five chapters; his tests and be a little hard and confusing so i suggest doing the reading and knowing the graphs. Overall though the rest of the class is a breeze.

I've gotten SO many quotes from him for my website.  Like, "These results end in umm...results."  "I'm serious, also.  I'm also serious."  And, "What do we have here?  That's right, a green line with a bunch of green dots.&quo

Well doug is an intersting person. The class seems almost pointless but you do have to read if you want to do well on his test. You either get the guy or you don't. Try him out and if ur not understanding him in the beggining then i wouldn't stay in it...
enjoyed his lectures...i looked forward to coming to class, if u are looking for microeconomics, this is the guy to take
Gets off task in class, but an entertaining guy.  Read the book and occassionally tune into his lectures and you'll get a solid B or A in the class.
I LOVE THIS GUY!!!  I actually look forward to going to this class.  He is a little weird, but that is what makes him cool.  I learned a lot.

I loved going to this class everyday.  It may not seem like you learn much, but you'd be surprised sometimes.  He makes an otherwise boring subject (Economics) fun.  He can seem a bit weird, but that's what makes him a cool teacher.
terrible!
very smart, wants you to do well, no attendance, but going to class helps.  No homework grades, but to get an A you need to do it.  Just paying some attention in class should gurantee a C
Very Excellent teacher, though he may seem a little querky, you will learn lots. His TA (Wes Hauf) is also amazing

You only have 4 tests all year. Homework consists of lots of reading that will be on the tests.  Great and humorous teacher.  Will give help if you ask for it.  There is a study session the day before every test.
I love this guy! He keeps you laughing all semester and his tests are filled with humor. You rarely have homework and the workload is not that much. It is a really fun class!

cool guy, but we pretty much never do anything in class.  tests are full of his jokes, but can be a little tricky.  never takes attendance, but sometimes gives extra credit to those who actually come to class.
this guy is amazing!

This guy is funny! as far as i can tell so far, he is a good teacher.  he put a quote from Donnie Darko on the board, and immediatly i knew we would get along.  he is kind of a dork, but the whole class likes him because he is so cool.

I took Dr. Carter for Intro to Political Science and he was amazing. His lectures are engaging and he explains things clearly. Be prepared for quizzes, but they're multiple choice and manageable. He's supportive and truly cares, definitely go to office hours!

Best polisci professor you could ever find. He knows his things well and conveys it to us pretty well too. Attendance matters but his lessons are very interesting. Hard quizzes, i mean mad hard quizzes. Easy grading on the three papers. I was ass in his class so I chose to pnc but if study well enough, i could get out with an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly really like professor Carter as a whole, is a nice passionate guy, but beware of his class layout. It can be hard to do well if you arent a great quiz taker. He does not give you any hints as to what is on it, and you will likely be reading through 30 pages of your own notes not knowing how to study.

Super interesting guy honestly. Lecture heavy makes you have to pay attention to content bc he won't repeat it, despite posting slides on d2l. Quizzes are multiple choice and manageable if you study. Essay questions on assignment, midterm, and final require comprehensive knowledge of content. Attendance matters, even tardies, just show up. Enjoyed!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Carter is very kind, enthusiastic, and makes lectures engaging. His quizzes were hard, I would study for many hours and the best grade I ever got was a 91. However, the four quizzes are pretty much the only assesment in the class throughout the semester so I think it is fair that they are hard. There were also two papers, easy grading on those.

This was a really insightful class, and gives you a good understanding of politics in the world today. But, it is just so hard to earn an A in the class. Not many grades are taken and the quizzes are tough! I showed up every day and took notes and really struggled.

This prof is great at giving lectures. Unfortunately, about half of class time is spent on current events, and the quiz questions are rarely about current events; the questions often pull from niche instances in the textbook that aren't mentioned in class or on the PowerPoint slides. Hard to earn an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is amazing. Wrote the textbook he teaches, thus is very accessible and knowledgeable. Makes understanding material super easy. Only got a B because I skipped once a week and attendance is worth nearly as much as the quizzes so just show up.

I thought he was a great teacher overall but just really difficult to do well with so little points to be given. The class is graded out of 382 points: 82 comes from attendance (2 points each time you are present), 100 from final exam, 50 from the midterm 4 25 point quizzes, and 1 book review worth 50 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures do not align with the quizzes whatsoever so you're forced to read a book that he wrote himself. He clearly has a biased, yet cut and dry understanding of international politics or else he wouldn't be teaching college freshman and it's apparent by how lousy the book is. The quizzes require way too much studying for little payoff. Don't take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: IGNORE ALL THE OTHER REVIEWS, THIS GUY IS A GOOD PERSON BUT TERRIBLE PROFESSOR, he is a little biased with his politics and the grading format is bad, dont expect to get an A in this class even with hard studying. Test have essays and he just takes off points without explaining why
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was very interesting and I was engaged, and I did learn a lot. Unfortunately though no matter how much I studied, I always just seemed to get passing grades. I have a B rn but I had to P/NC the class cause I know I'm not gonna do that well on the final. If you're a POLSCI major though, I'm sure this class will be right for you.

I personally would not take Dr Carter again. His lectures are engaging but there are better courses to take if you care about your GPA. The papers and exams are doable, but the quizzes will sink your grade. He grades extremely harshly on papers. There is an overemphasis on current events that don't matter, ie domestic politics/ domestic elections.

Dr. Carter is amazing! His lectures are never boring and he incorporates interesting current events. The quizzes and exams aren't too difficult but you definitely need to study. Attendance is part of your final grade so you have to show up! Also there is a paper that he grades very tough and it's a big part of the grade.

Great lectures, tough quizzes that are hard to get A's on. The quizzes are frustrating because you study a lot and get mediocre grades. He grades very easy on the papers which count for a majority of your grade. Not my favorite polo-sci professor, but not horrible. Midterm and Final are essay based questions, 1 book report, and 4 in-class quizzes.

I highly doubt I'll find a better professor than Dr. Carter for the rest of my time here. He is hilarious, caring, and gives the best lectures. The class is mainly graded off a couple of papers and 5 20-question quizzes. Take notes and read the textbook, it's actually a pretty good read, and you'll kill it. TAKE A CLASS WITH CARTER!

Definitely take Dr. Carter if you get the chance at TCU. He is so nice and knows everything about what he's saying. He lectures and you just need to take good notes to do well on quizzes/midterm & final. He also keeps the class light and funny
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Everyone should take his course. He is so knowledgeable and keeps the class engaged. Has atlas quizzes, 4 quizzes, a book review, written midterm. and written final. He is a nice guy and will help you during office hours. His grading is very clear so try to keep all of your points throughout the semester to get an A. You have to work hard and read.

Dr. Carter's lectures are funny, engaging, and well-paced. Quizzes and tests are hard and require a lot of studying, and he grades papers with a lot of scrutiny. He doesn't assign homework or busywork, just quizzes and papers.

I enjoyed learning from Mr.Carter so much. There were a lot of quizzes, but, they only mattered 20 points so if you did badly on one you could recover. There was one writing assignment that was pretty straightforward. His lectures were very entertaining and he made it worth it to wake up at 8 am. You do have to study, but he is awesome.

Dr. Carter is the best! He is such a great political science professor because he never shows his opinion on anything and lets everyone in the class speak on their opinions and discuss. He moves very quick but it very thorough and makes sure everyone understands. Definitely would recommend Dr. Carter for posc!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed his lectures, because his passion and knowledge are very clear. I wish I did not take this class however, because it is extremely hard to do well. Compared to other Political Science professors at TCU, I feel that Dr. Carter did not care about me doing well in the class nor my understanding of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Carter has been my favorite teacher at TCU so far! He is so kind and caring and truly wants all of his students to succeed and feel heard. He is very relaxed and was very understanding when I had technical issues. His tests aren't hard at all if you take minimal notes and pay attention in class. He is a real gem!

Dr. Carter is one of the best professors I've had at TCU! His passion for the material is clear and he's an excellent lecturer, but he is a tough grader, especially on the research report. Paying attention and taking notes during the lecture is crucial for the exams, especially current events. But I would really recommend him overall.

Dr Carter is a super funny guy that cracks jokes on occasion. One downfall in his class is not only do you have to purchase three books for the class, the tests are all short answer and essay. He also puts questions from the book that weren't in the lecture and also current events talked about in class. It'll be hard to pass if you don't show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The textbook is unreadable and he just lectures and there are not really words on his slides so you get to just frantically try and right everything down. I hate that he does current events it takes up too much class time which means more textbook reading. TCU is full of teachers like this and is not worth your money. I am so bitter I chose TCU.

I absolutely LOVED this profesor. The Intro to political science class was my favorite class of the semester even though it was at 8AM. You have to take notes in class, and read in order to do good on the tests, but if you do that you will be fine. He does a great job of incorporating current events which is what makes the class so fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: RALPH GORDON CARTER III IS THE CHILI DOG KING!!!!!!!!!!!!

Dr. Carter is a great professor, his lectures are interesting and he is knowledgeable about what he is teaching. Tests can be difficult, so I would recommend rewriting/ reviewing your notes before the exam. The only downside about this class is that it is only offered at 8am. Expect to read a lot about current events if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Carter is truly one of the best professors/teachers I have ever had. He is a tough grader, he has high expectations for students, and there are only 3 tests, a book review, and a final, but he is so worth it. He teaches very clearly and fairly and really wants students to learn. He is open to any questions. Professor Carter is passionate!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Carter! Best professor I've had at TCU. His Into to Poly Sci class was really interesting and fun. He is super smart and loves to teach. He takes attendance and you have to take good notes because the tests are hard but he gives extra credit and an A is achievable if you work for it. Take his class for him, not the grade, he is AMAZING

Hands down the best professor I've ever had at TCU, he made the 8 ams worth. Theres a lot of reading involved but the class is really practical and he makes it quite fun. Not an easy A, and you do have to work for a B, but if you do your reading and extra credit, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Seriously the best teacher I've had at TCU! He is so energetic and fun. This is definitely a challenging class--hard to get an A. I am one of those students who is all about getting A's and working hard, but I would definitely take a B for the experience of the class. Awesome guy

Professor Carter wants his students to do well and makes it very possible for you to do so! You have to go to class which sucks, but it's never boring. He's intelligent but never pretentious. Highly reccomend him for international relations.
Best Prof. show up and he'll will interest you.

Very interesting class, but also challenging. One of the best teachers I've had at TCU, inspired me to add a Poli Sci Minor. The reading is mandatory and there is a lot of it. Tests are essay tests, and you HAVE TO attend class; but it you work hard this class is completely manageable. 10% of the class grade also is attendance.

Dr. Carter is absolutely an amazing teacher. He has a unique way in making the lecture entertaining and enjoyable. You get to learn lots of great information from this class. However, tests were not easy and papers definitely needs extreme polishing and revising before hand it before his eyes if you want to get a decent B or above.

Dr. Carter is a great guy and I enjoyed his lectures, but he grades absolutely hard. In this course there were two exams, Midterms and finals. There was a book review, which he grades hard as well. overall good professor but not an easy class.

Does not help you. He presents his information and tests (of which there are only two) and expects you to have it at! Got a C on a paper for messing up ONE citation and having an "awkward sentence." Not kidding. This guy is a good man and would be a great teacher if he set out guidelines for success. Avoid if you care about GPA or like success.

Absolutely amazing. If you want to actually learn something, take this class. I signed up to meet core requirements and found a passion in politics, most likely stemmed from Dr. Carter's enthusiasm and eloquent lectures. I slept through one 8 am class and was devastated. 8 am on MWF has never been so worth it.

I found professor Carter to be very helpful but the course was definitely not a walk in the park. You have to listen to the current events, take great notes, and read the book. He is very knowledgeable and wants you to learn the material.

Even though it's an 8am, I loved this class. So interesting and relevant. Dr. Carter is wonderful and fun. Exams are all short answer (write like a few words), but if you take good notes and read it's definitely do-able. Exams are non-cumulative! Highly recommend :)
Very hard teacher but a good sense of humor and willing to help you if you come to him

He is so helpful and so kind! I didn't do as well as I had hoped on the first test, and he patiently explained concepts to me to help me improve for the final. He genuinely cares for his students. The class IS NOT easy, so STUDY! Be sure you know every concept and know the people! But if you work hard, and pay attention, you will learn a lot.
Very interesting and is unbiased in political views

Hands down one of the best professors at TCU. This class is relevant and genuinely interesting. You MUST pay attention in class, and come! Take about 3 pages of notes a day, but study them and you'll get an A on the tests. I asked him for help and got a 75 on the first test, and a 91 on the 2nd. He loves what he does! Great teacher, awesome class!

Ummm so ya. My major is political science and this is the worst grade I've made in any political science class at TCU. He's hard, nitty picky and just annoying. Don't take unless you have to. Test are FILL in the blank must know everything he lectures on and EVERY line in the textbook. Don't take you will regret. He's just not my type of professor

This class is great. Dr. Carter is very engaged and involved with the class and tries to get everyone talking. Takes all points of view into consideration and never belittles opinions, even if he disagrees with them. Big on current events, so bring a newspaper. No homework, three exams, so study hard because they are tricky.

This class is hard. I'm currently in a junior/sr level class and it is much easier than his intro class. He cares too much about detail and the tests are freaking impossible. Made me almost change my major. Don't take this you will regret it. He sucks and thinks he is the smartest person in the world. Plus its at 8am and attendance is mandatory.

Definitely the best professor I have had at TCU! Professor Carter makes the information exciting and interesting, and is very willing to help. Take good notes, keep up with current events and skim the book and you will be golden. Pay attention in class because the tests are directly from them. Take this class! It is worth getting up early for!

Best professors I've had at TCU yet. Very knowledgable on the subject and makes it very interesting. Tests are too hard, just be sure you know your notes REALLY well, especially the current events discussed in class. And take good notes! I totally recommend this class for anyone with the slightest interest in international politics.

International Politics Honors. Fascinating professor, very very intelligent. I looked forward to that class and continued to think. The book review paper gets graded pretty harshly, and the tests are not easy. Make sure you write down all the current events you discuss in class--they're a big part of the test grade.

20303 honors Great professor. definitely a hard grader and the midterm is pretty rough, but it prepares you for the final. His lectures are engaging and interesting. always makes the material fun to learn. sharp insight on material too. an A is possible, but you have to start strong on the midterm. only complaint is that there are only 3 big grades

Great professor, cares about his students and his subject. Take really good notes most of his test material comes directly from what was discussed in class. He is extremely understanding and helpful. He is willing to hear his students out! Talk to him after class it helps a lot with the material and grade! Take him!!! He is incredible teacher

GREAT professor! One of the best I have had! You have to study a lot to get an A in his honors international politics, but if you go to class (pretty much mandatory) you'll be fine. Dr. Carter knows exactly what he's talking about and makes the class interesting! TAKE HIM!

Very good professor who makes every lecture interesting, however this class is anything but easy. The Tests are difficult, and there are very few grades. Be sure to pay close attention to current events, and go to class because he gives lots of easy pop quizzes (ie, what did you do this weekend). Youll learn a lot from him, but come ready to work.

Good teacher. VERY INTERESTING if you are interested in politics. The text is helps you to understand the different ideologies (liberal vs. classical vs. socialist) I loved the class. Its a good amount of work but definitely not impossible to make an A. Know your text books though and go to class.

DONT take this class! Especially if you are a Republican!!! He will bash Republicans all class. On top of that, he is EXTREMELY hard. Intro? More like ADVANCED political science!!!!Seriously take another class! Must read all books, attend all classes, & take extensive notes. Even then tests are IMPOSSIBLE!!!
Interesting material and some how found a way to make it boring the tests were insainly hard!!!!!!!!!!

I took this class last fall and failed it. I took it again this fall and made a D. I think the important thing to know is that your grade comes from the three tests and nothing else, and if you bomb one of those you don't have a chance of making a good grade.

Great professor and really interesting to learn from. He's extremely charismatic and nice. He wants the best for his students but his tests are extremely hard for a 1000 level course. Take notes! You will not do well without them. Show up every day bec quizzes are random, and that can kill your average. I learned more than I could ever imagine.

Best teacher I've had at TCU.  Hilarious guy, incredibly smart, and able to convey that to his students.  Took him for Middle-East PoliSci, incredible class.  Barely uses the textbook, so going to class is mandatory.  I looked forward to it every Tues/Thurs.  Take this guy for any course, you won't regret it!

Awesome professor!  I had him for honors international politics and I loved his class.  You have to read your textbook and keep up with current events to do well.  There is also only 3 grades in the class, a midterm, final and book reivew. He is an easy grader and wonderful professor, very helpful and just an all around nice guy!

He was an awesome teacher who really knew his stuff about politics and current events.  Coming to class is a must.  Tests are kind of hard, but just pay attention and go to class and you'll do fine.  Would def rec him!
Class is hard if youre not into political science but you learn alot and going to class is definitely not boring! Very smart prof!

I have taken multiple courses with him, and he is my favorite prof. ever!!! All you need to do is come to class and read the books and a b-a is no problem. He is also one of the most hilarious people i have ever met. TAKE HIS CLASS!!! You will learn a lot too!!
He was interesting, but his tests were too hard.
Dr Carter is one of the most helpful and intellgent profs in the polu sci dept
Best class I have had at TCU. Dr Carter knows his stuff and makes class fun and interesting. Hes tough, but take him...its worth it.

Grad school course. Awesome professor, possibly one of the best I've ever had. Very lively and informative. Focus is on facts/current issues, not his views. Best part: you can have your own opinion in class/on papers/tests, but be prepared to back it up with facts. Don't expect favoritism. You will read/write your butt off but will learn a lot.

An awesome professor, really cares about students.  Very interesting class, learn a lot.  Study the book carefully, make sure you read all chapters before the test.  It does take work but you learn a lot and it's really interesting.
Great, animated teacher.  Class is always interesting.  Tests can be difficult.  TAKE NOTES ON CURRENT EVENTS.  Tests are about 40% lecture, 30% notes and 30% current events.
Prof. Carter is great, he makes the class interesting and enjoyable, even the boring aspects.  I would defiantly recommend this class to anyone.

You will understand international politics after his class as well as current events. Class is a mix of talking about events and lecture. he relates lecture to cur events. tests are very hard. STUDY THE BOOK CAREFULLY. 2 books for required reading are good. take this class if you like current events

Best prof. I ever had.  Got mad when I read the 1 negative comment above.  I was in that class. He talked about Sweden cause the Foreign Min. had been murdered.  Clearly written by a vengeful student who didn't get the grade they wanted.  Wrong & foolish.

He is a nice guy, but if you get on his "bad side" the class will be hell.don't be absent if he doesn't like you.All the pop quizes will be on those dates.And he will be harder on you than the rest of the class.don't ****him off and you should d

kept everything interesting, i loved the real world discussions we had at the beginning of class. tests and reading assignments aren't bad, just speak up in class. i'm actually trying to find another class that he teaches right now.
his tests are very hard...study the book
Dr. Carter is a wonderful teacher!
He entergizes politics, connects the dots, and always has time for you. Every class I leave with something to think about.

Carter is my favorite teacher this semester.  I don't study much for his class, but I still have a 96, although  cannot say the same for the rest of the class.  It helps to have a background in world history from 1800.  Bring a newspaper to class everyday

Dr. Carter fosters an environment conducive to open critical discussion of international politics.  I highly recommend him--he explains the complicated world of international politics cogently and concisely without appearing condescending.
No Comments
Among the top 3 professors in my college career.
Great Professor.  Good discussions and learned a lot.
No Comments
Took her last semester and while this class was ok, it definitely challenges you. But she is a good person and was very helpful when needed.

Class was made up of three main solo projects which she gives you great feedback on the rough draft and workshop time to ask questions. In Class Writing Assignments and quizzes are easy ways to boost your grade. The final project is a video group project. Workload is not bad, and she is extremely caring and passionate teach her. Take her 100%!

Hard grader but feedback is often unhelpful. Unclear grading criteria- it's supposed to be an argument class but most of the time I'm confused what the assignments are actually supposed to argue. Professor is sweet but eh- didn't learn a lot honestly and too many group projects where we didn't get to decide our group.
best professor i have had at tcu so far. she cares about her students and gives amazing feedback. overall an amazing person as well as professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Carlson was such a great professor. In this class, we watch documentaries that we end up writing essays about. It is such a cool class and I highly recommend it with Dr. Carlson. She is super friendly and offers corrections on an essay at the end of the semester. There are 2 group projects at the end as well.

Provides an engaging experience through analyzing documentaries rather than walls of text. The largest parts of your grade are the quizzes and the projects she assigns, both of which she allows drops or redos, which is a godsend if you have a bad day. Very firm, but kind and fair professor who I would recommend to anyone taking comp 2
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher!!! She is so incredibly kind and I truly enjoy her class. She really cares about her students, whether it be their grade or well being, and I def reccomend

She is super friendly but you have to be really willing to share your thoughts during class because participation is huge- the projects aren't too hard but they are a good amount of work, but the writing and reading is really interesting. She also gives really clear feedback.

I took Documentary Film themed Composition 2 from her. I strongly recommend, it is extremely thought provoking as it explores themes in today's society. She cares about us and our preferences for how class is run. The class isn't an easy A, however if you put effort into projects which are creative and fun, you will do well. Several group projects!

Easiest class I've taken so far, yet she is such a harsh grader. What she expects is B&W; however, she docs points for things said/unsaid that have no relation to the prompt/rubric. Would recommend someone else for this credit because of her harsh grading for no reason.

Dr. Carlson is supportive and connects you with peers in a larger group. She is accessible and genuinely cares about you as a person. She's a great teacher and grades on improvement. When you upload drafts to the discussion, don't edit your rough draft first! A large part of the grade is how different the drafts are from each other.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Carlson is such a kind professor. This is the second semester I have taken her, and I enjoy her teaching and critiques. She is so willing to sit down and meet with me outside of class. If you want to learn about playwriting from any perspective, take her!

Okay so Dr. Carlson is the worst. She has no attendance policy but if you miss a couple of classes she will fail you. She basically talks the entire class and doesnt teach and then assigns 20 page Scene Assignments. Shes inconsiderate and doesnt care for her students whatsoever.

Carlson is super sweet and will help u if you ask. Don't bother buying the books, you can find all the readings online. There are quizzes every other class on the readings, but if you just read them you'll do fine. Most of the class is based on projects and no tests which is cool. Kinda a hard grader on the projects but if you try you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Love this professor. I've been doing online school for about 3 years now & I've never had an amazing teacher like her. Projects, quizzes, & other grades are so incredibly doable. If you do it and put effort in you will do good. Put time and thought, you will do great. Very nice lady, and SUPER approachable. NOTHING BUT GREAT THINGS TO SAY! TAKE HER

Dr. Carlson was a great professor, 10/10 if you need a HUM/LIt credit. However, do not expect this class to be super easy, an A is definitely achievable, but it doesn't come easy due to her tough grading. If you go to her office hours, she does everything she can to help you do better. Don't buy the book, google the stories instead!

Absolutely adored this class. Dr. Carlson runs the class like a discussion so that all students may participate and contribute their ideas about the content. Generally, the reading is very light, and some of the exams are substituted for group projects. I definitely recommend.

Participation is mandatory, but attendance counts as a big part of your grade. Only a couple of reading quizzes, the rest of your grade depends on your writing projects, in drama, fiction, and poetry. A caring professor, and we have the chance to workshop projects. She makes it easy to care about your writing without feeling like an idiot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Carlson is very caring, and will improve your writing for certain. Very few people had written for the stage/screen before her class, but she was helpful and accommodating. You have to write 3 screenplays (1 in a group) of 10 pages each, and then a longer final project. 3 quizzes as well. Highly recommend her, she's a great professor.
I love Dr. Carlson! I have taken her 3 times, she's amazing! I found real enjoyment in writing for the stage and that's because of her. Highly recommend this class and her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Carlson made my time at TCU truly special! Her class environment is one that feels calm, yet she is passionate about what she teaches. She truly cares about how you are doing in her class, and you will feel that way. Workload is never too much, but there are few pop quizzes. Just come to class prepared and there is no reason you won't succeed.

Avoid Gender Culture Representation at all costs, unless you want a B or C. I was expecting an easy A humanities class, but thats definitely not the case for this class. She makes it way harder than it should be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Carlson is not an easy A, but is willing to give A's out unlike other professors. You only need to write 4 papers throughout the semester and a collaborative project at the end for the final. There is also one presentation and a few quizzes throughout. Overall, very reliable and willing to work with students.

I really enjoyed her class. She cares a lot about her students and wants everyone to get a good grade. She connects good material to real life situations which makes her class very interesting. A lot of discussion in class which makes it easy to stay engaged.

Really interesting class! She is a very helpful professor and wants everyone to do well. Not hard if you put in a little effort towards your writing assignments (only 3) and was a lot of fun. Definitely would take again.
She was a really nice teacher and is an expert in Journalism. Her class is very interesting and I learned a lot from her. Great option for Journalism majors!

Have had her twice-- really nice person and easy grader. Gives you grace periods for late assignments with no penalty and is super flexible about any assignment. Easy to succeed in any of her classes. Would definitely reccommend.

Dr. Hayes is awesome! This is my second semester taking one of her classes, and she is so helpful. Her assignments can be confusing to approach, but she gives workshop days, and she is so helpful during office hours. Class is lecture-heavy with activities sometimes, but nothing crazy. Always make sure to sign in on the paper.

No specific textbook; weekly readings on Perusal. Not many writing assignments, but she covers them in class, has workshop days, and has a 3-day extended deadline policy. Open-note midterm. Lots of concepts, but gives many examples for each. She's passionate about the subject and makes class entertaining, and talks about multiple different sports!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I Took this class thinking it was gonna be a fun elective class focused on sports, turns out it was just a pain. This was Dr. Hayes first year and she was such a picky grader. If you are looking for a fun, easy elective, don't take this class. Their are plenty of other journalism electives you can take.

Professor Hayes was very nice and approachable! Her grading criteria is very confusing and often doesn't make sense. She gives a grace period on assignments. There are weekly quizzes that are sometimes hard, but they online. You definitely have to work for an A in this class. She turned an easy journalism class into a very philosophical class.

He believes that you can learn Calculus by yourself and decided not to do his job of TEACHING. Like I can't teach myself calculus because it is a very difficult subject. Can bro please do his job! He also uses covid era videos, maybe update them, its been 6 years.
I liked how we worked with different people every class. You get to know people and it helps when you're stuck on something.

Lectures made sense and I could follow along most of the time.

Homework is open for a full week which is better than some other math profs who only give you a couple days.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Tests were fair. You always knew what to expect going into.

By the end I understood everything we covered. You can tell he really knows his stuff.
You can tell he actually enjoys teaching. His energy makes a difference. Would take again.

Wasn't sure about the flipped classroom at first but it actually worked well. You work on problems with the prof there to help when you get stuck. Also liked having more smaller tests instead of just a couple big ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Approachable professor. Actually tries to get to know students which you don't always see.
Really clear when he explains things. If you ask for help he'll actually work through it with you until you get it. The group work in class was really helpful.

Had him in Stats.  Very thorough with everything. Good handwriting, always on time, organized notes. He tried to get our class to participate more (we were a quiet group). Office hours are worth going to if you want deeper explanations.
Dr. Carrion really cares about making sure you understand the material. Enthusiastic and will answer any question in class or office hours. One of the better math profs I've had.
Really clear when he explains things. If you ask for help he'll actually work through it with you until you get it.

Prof Carrions dedication to carefully explain concepts and his thorough exercises really helps me excel in this class. In addition to his enthusiatic engagement with the students, prof Carrion always makes sure that all of our questions in class or in office hour are carefully answered. Hes one the best mathematics teachers with his unique pedagogy
Pretty easy, exam questions are just like ones from hw.  Do your work and extra credit and you'll be good.  Funny guy too.

Video lectures you have to watch before coming to work on in class problems in groups.  I found the videos helpful but people that didn't watch (obviously) struggled with the in class problems and then complained about having to watch videos like during COVID.  The math itself isn't easy.
Good extra credit chances, video lectures and lots of in class group work, short exams that you can retake, he cared about me doing well.
Pleasantly surprised.  Very organized class, clear expectations.  Dr Carrion was actually super reasonable and supportive.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Self-study class. Pre-recorded videos didn't help me as much. You should only take him if you have an incredibly strong Math background. Otherwise, this class is a nightmare for you and he would mark you down for any things. But for my prior Math knowledge, I wouldn't have survived this class.

He's an amazing lecturer, and his office hours are great for reviewing material, and homework. He covers all the theory needed for homework in class so don't skip.
There is a lot of homework, and quizzes are mostly theory. Quizzes aren't difficult, but without doing homework, you might feel lost. Take this class only if you have time.

Carrion believes that Calculus 2 shouldn't be taught by the professor. Have a said enough? no? He does not lecture and treats this course as if we are still in COVID, meaning all material will be online and in class he will have you work problems with others... sounds good right? until you find no one else shows up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He carefully explains concepts to make sure everyone understands. Lots of homework (not difficult) after every chapter but it prepares you well for his quizzes and exams. Those who self-study like me may find his lectures a bit slow because he provides examples for almost every new definition or theorem. Textbook is not required but recommended.
Self study class. Show up to class for extra credit.
I didn't think I'd pass this class but he believed in me and pushed me to work hard and I did.  You get out what you put in to his class.

The only teacher that knew my name this semester.  Cares about students.  I actually liked the weird multiple choice quizzes.  Some people complain about him, but most of those just don't come to class.

Loved that you knew exactly what to expect every day.  Clear plan from the beginning.  Video lectures aren't my fav, but I was able to follow between that and online book.  If you put in the work this class was pretty easy.

He used prerecorded lectures which he posted so I didn't attend class unless there was a quiz or exam. His examples in the prerecorded lectures did not help at all with the assigned homework. I typically referred to online lectures on Youtube or other professors in the department. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher. Just don't take him. Even if you think "oh it will be fine"... no, it won't. I am literally a CS and Math Major
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Carrion does not lecture in calculus 2, it is his philosophy or something i guess. Linear Algebra hes good though because he doesn't get lazy and rely on videos he made during covid. Just switch to another professor if you have him for literally any other subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst professor to take for advanced math classes, told you to read the textbook by yourself and hated when you asked questions from the textbook
RUN! Didn't teach a thing the whole semester, literally no slides or notes. Prepare to read the textbook by yourself and be scowled at if you don't know how to do the HW that no one taught you to

I really enjoyed my linear algebra class with Dr. Carrion. While he may seem a little intimidating at first, he cares about his students. His lectures were thorough, clear, and consistent, and I always appreciated his subtle sense of humor. The tests were challenging but not too difficult, especially if you studied the weekly quizzes.

Before school, I heard horror stories about him, so I sat in on two lin algebra lectures with 2 different profs to decide if I wanted to switch, but he was better than the alternative. Lectures are pretty clear. If you take good notes, and take the time to think through them/process/understand the material outside of class, an A or B is achievable.

Took applied calc during the summer session, im bad at math and honestly put in minimal effort and made it out with a C.  Quizzes everyday and tests every Monday but easy to get by even without studying

He goes through things really quickly and doesn't really like give stuff for the class to do- just straight lectures..

Might as well read through the textbook. It explains stuff in more detail and you can do it as many times as you want.

BUt the class itself wasn't *that* hard ??

This is my second class with Dr. Carrión, and he's very consistent with his lectures. He has a lot of availability for office hours, so make use of that! The class is structured around lectures in which he introduces you to the concepts and works through examples with you. Be sure to ask questions if you have any!

Dr. Carrion is unwilling to help out individuals and does not make any effort to make a connection with his students or aid during a time of confusion or error. I have had multiple experiences where I have made technical mistakes due to the new online format of his class, and he is unwilling to offer any help to myself or my peers.

Dr. Carrión's teaching strategy is pretty straightforwardhe goes over examples in class and then assigns homework for each section. The homework is significantly harder than the in-class problems, but the tests are pretty reasonable. He's very willing to help if you come in for office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy
