reviews.comment: Dr. Carrion provides clear and thorough explanations for his Calculus II class. He is also available at many times outside of his classroom times. However, if you are not putting in the work, he will get onto you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: To be honest, and blunt, Dr. Carrion is condescending. Theres no doubt that hes a great mathematician. As a professor, he lacks the passion to teach and that really hinders youre desire to learn. If find that you learn better in a Pink Floyds The Wall classroomthis is the guy for you. If you want my opinion, take Hatcher or Nollet instead.

Do not take Dr. Carrion's class. This guy is horrible. I took him over the summer and he neglected to teach the class and made us teach ourselves. We were not allowed to work together or use calculators, and when I told him he graded one of my test questions wrong he got upset with me and accused me of cheating on a completely separate homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took calc over the summer with Carrion. Might be rougher during the semester, but it wasn't bad at all over the summer. Tests were standard book-type problems. Lecture was fine, relaxed. Funny guy. Lots of HW but it ends up helping your grade.

I love Dr. Carrion. His class was by no means easy, you really have to work for it. He is a very thorough lecturer and solves lots of examples in class. He is also very accessible outside of class and will walk you through problems you are having trouble with. He gives quizzes every Friday, which help you make sure you know the content.

I honestly recommend not taking Carrion. His tests are absolutely insane and refuses to tell you what it will be over. There are quiz's every Friday and again he does not tell you what will be on it. Hw everyday, but you can get it done a day early for some extra credit. I truly advise to avoid this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took for both Real Analysis and Abstract Algebra. Avoid him if you can. Explains the lecture material well, but that's his only positive. Exams are extremely difficult and he is very unhelpful in office hours. Final exam is usually worth > 35%. Offers very little to help your grade. Should be fine for lower level math, but avoid for anything else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you can avoid Carrion, do so. It might be because Abstract Algebra is a high level course, but Carrion made sure to make difficult topics even harder. He taught 2 chapters backwards (literally) and then told us to read the book rather than correct his mistake. He also only has an hour of office hours a week. AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: His tests are extremely difficult and he moves through concepts quickly. However, he really does care about his students, and his lectures are often fun. Additionally, you can get 120% extra credit on the homework if you complete it a day early, and this can save your grade. I learned so much from this class, even though it took a lot of work!

Dr. Carrion is an excellent professor and very articulate in his lectures and will always answer any questions that a student has and go more in depth. He gives homework daily but it is worth 20% of your grade and you get bonus points for completing it early. His exams are very challenging but he is more than willing to help during office hours.
People will complain about Dr Jose, but if you really want to learn he is the one to take.  His exams are tough, so if you want an easy time look elsewhere.
She is a very caring and nice professor, if you take her make sure you don't miss class because some assignments are participation based, her exams and speeches aren't that bad if you prep for them.

She is a really sweet and caring person. I will say she grades pretty hard especially for her basic class (10123). There are in class assignments weekly and nothing gets dropped that I know of. She has 0 tolerance for making up in-class assignments if you have personal excuses or anything, which sucks.

Her class requires a lot of time and focus. If you're not able to dedicate most of your attention to this course, I wouldn't recommend taking it. I've found myself putting my other classes aside all semester just to keep up. There's always something due, so you won't get many nights to relax. If you're okay with a heavy workload.. take her.

Instructor Moore is exceptional. She creates an inclusive, engaging environment that encourages new perspectives. Her thought-provoking questions promote critical thinking and growth. Her teaching style challenges you in the best way. She is also easily accessible and wants her students to succeed. Take her. You won't regret it.

Overall love her, but she's a tad condescending. Definitely doesn't mean it intentionally, more like the type of person that just judges anyone for having creativity or not following the rules perfectly. Kind of gives me anxiety just being in her presence. But great at teaching the material and her class is immensely applicable to the real world.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Moore is a sweetheart. This class is so fun and interesting because she makes sure of it. This is the first class, I have ever had an actual relationship with all of my classmates. She is so caring and kind. Even though attendance is mandatory, it won't feel like it bc you'll want to go. Take this course with her, you won't regret it.

I truly can't put into words how much instructor moore means to me as a professor. Her classes were not only incredible, but she has given me so much confidence and poured so much in to me as a student. She's loving, there to help you always, and overall the greatest professor that I'll never forget. You will learn so much and grow as a person!!!
LOVE HERRR!!! so sweet and this class was fun if you like public speaking. You have to take her!!!!

I P/NC the course, but she was a great teacher. She is caring and wants students to succeed. She does not allow technology, so bring a notepad and take good notes. Do not be afraid to go to office hours and ask for help, it is worth it.

Professor Moore's Advanced Public Speaking class is amazing! This class is so beneficial to learn how to perform a speech. The skills learned in this class range from speaking skills to physical posture &gestures. This class has lots of workshops to actually apply the skills and ask questions. Theres around 8-10 speeches. Practice and youll be set.

Literally so hard and super tough grader when it comes to writing and delivering speeches. Her tests are hard. I would recommend taking another communications teacher because everyone else had a much easier time. Should not spend this much time and effort studying for a core class

Repeat after me: TAKE! INSTRUCTOR! MOORE! She's one of the sweetest profs I've had at TCU. Her nonverbal comm class is so interesting, and the info is very applicable to the real world. Class is seminar/discussion based, so be sure to participate. Very important: read the textbook for tests! Yes it's long, but the info is interesting. Take Moore!!!

As a COMM major, I learned more in Dr. Moore's Advanced Public Speaking course than any other COMM course at TCU. Very engaging lectures, and shows you how this class can be applicable in the real world. Super nice, and creates an awesome classroom environment.

Professor Moore is very kind. She is very light on the lectures, and apologizes for a long day. That's a nice break from my math classes! She was very flexible with remote learning. Beware, she is very picky on speeches. But if you participate in class and show real effort, it won't go unnoticed.
It's not easy, but if you put the work in and follow grading guidelines an A is doable. Lectures really help to understand the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is by far my favorite professor I have ever had at TCU. Her tests are difficult and she expects you to participate but that is every professor in the department. She genuinely wants to see you succeed and cares about your life outside of school. She is one of the kindest people I know and has one of the biggest hearts.

She has amazing energy, so youll always want to go to class. Very graceful towards her students throughout the semester. Any one who takes this class will master outlines for speeches. If you never miss class and turn in all the work, you will definitely pass. Class is politically correct, so keep topics conservative.

Dr. Moore was great for Interpretive Speaking. Preparing for the performances was very hard and you have to practice for them to actually do well. Only one test and if you study and take good notes it's an easy A. Very sweet and gives great feedback.

I currently have Dr. Moore for Interpretive Speaking  is an incredibly nice and helpful teacher. She gives great feedback and really prepares you for all the performances, even though they are hard to prepare for. The book is a pain to read and you have to put in a lot of effort to do well though. Overall one of the best teachers I've had at TCU.

One of my favorite teachers at TCU. I had her for intercultural communication and have learned so much in this class. I would absolutely take her again. That being said, she is a hard teacher and expects college level work and maturity. Some of the topics are controversial and difficult to discuss but she made each class period worth the effort.

i am in her advanced public speaking class and have learned so much about how to give a professional speech. she also gives so much feedback. there's a lot of writing in this class b/c you have to write four speeches plus the outlines and reflections. but she reviews each outline before you give your speech to make sure it's right.

I took Professor Moore in Group Discussion and although I got a C, I would certainly take her class again. She is one of the few teachers that actually makes students apply what they learn in class to real life situations. This was one of the few classes where I actually learned something that I could apply in the real world beyond college.

PLEASE READ THIS! First of all, this is the FIRST time I am rating a teacher on this website. I saw the ratings and saw that she was an easy teacher and the average grade was an A-. THIS IS NOT TRUE. The amount of work required in her class is INSANE, and THIS IS NOT AN EASY A. You work incredibly hard for a B. DO NOT TAKE HER FOR GROUP DISCUSSION

Professor Moore isn't hard if you put in the effort. She really wants you to succeed in her class. She loves socratic discussion, which is much better than boring lectures as in other classes. She's funny and makes class enjoyable. I tell everyone to take her, she's hands down my favorite professor at TCU thus far. Definitely not a waste of time.

Carrie is a fine teacher. Her tests are tough, and she puts things that aren't in the review on them. She does give good feedback on speeches, and I think I improved my public speaking skills. I personally didn't like her as a person, because I thought she was annoying, but if you like public speaking you'll probably like this class

Carrie is an excellent speech teacher if you honestly want to improve your public speaking skills. Have to go to class, fair grader on speeches. Definitely not an easy A, but very doable. Tests are difficult, but not long. After the first test, she gave us a word bank for fill in the blank. SomeEasier professors, but I guarantee you'll learn a lot
Lots of speeches. Willing to help you with anything. Learned a lot to improve my speaking.

I would not recommend this class. Yes it is easy, but the information is worthless. Everything she lectures (more seminar-style) over has been covered in IPC, Org Comm, or Theory... The whole class is learning how to work in a group; if you're a comm major and haven't learned how to work in a group, you should probably reconsider majors.
I love this class and Carrie…we are only 4 weeks into the semester but it is so different and applicable toward real life. She will help you with anything!
this class started off pretty easy but was tough at the end. she expects a lot but i learned so much. very responsive and gives very detailed feedback.
ok

Unless you're really into comm, DON'T take it with her. She's nice and good looking, but grades speeches with the fury of a thousand suns and gives frequent pop quizzes so you have to do the reading every night and show up to class every day. Definitely not a blow off like I had hoped; 10 kids dropped, the rest ended up pass/no crediting her class.

Probably the most spastic person I've ever met. But she's really awesome! She makes a lot of jokes, and sometime they aren't funny. But she is so willing to help you! She definitely takes speech seriously, and it isn't easy to make an A.
took her for intro speech. be warned this is not at all a blow off class and i ended up learning a lot. She is always there for her students and wants to help. Easy B, had to work very hard for an A!
Took her for Advanced Public Speaking, she's now one of my favorite teachers!! She's very helpful and wants you to succeed in class.  Take her any chance you get!!
Top 5 Professors at TCU. Energetic, helpful, very easy on the eyes.
great class...learned a lot.
Professor Moore is great! She is so sweet and is willing to help you if you put in the work! We almost always got out early!
Her advanced public speaking class is the best! Really helpful and super sweet. She is a must take professor!

I've grown up my whole life being horrible at math but with good studying, using my resources, and following along during his lectures, I got an A-. He is so funny and genuinely just wants the best for his students. The course consists of homework on Pearson, 3 exams, and then the final. Gives partial credit, so ask questions! TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice professor, light homework. Exams are easy if you study exactly what he says to in class. Lectures are pretty boring but you get attendance points for coming to class.

He is very caring, understands where you are coming from and wants you to do well. He is very fast paced, like you really have to lock in. He tells you exactly what will be on every test so you will be fine. homework is all online and the "help me solve this" button will save your life. it is challenging but if you actually try you can do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about helping you understand the material. The conecpts he covers stay fairly simple and we didn't get through nearly as much material as the other applied calc classes. Not very many homework assignments and he basically lectures and writes notes the whole time. The tests are short and easy if you know the material.

This was for MATH 10043. Very easy class to get your stats credit as long as you come to class and take notes. The entire class is just note taking (lots of notetaking) but he makes a lot of the information apply to relevant topics and is an overall fun professor to listen to. 
3 exams, 1 cumulative final, weekly ish homework's, graded but easy.

He means well and you can tell he's very passionate about teaching but it's a hard course for someone who is very bad at math. The homework doesn't really help with the tests because you have to fully understand the rules and how to get from point A to point B. This is not a class for a beginner, study study study!

he means well, but his teaching and overall class was extremely unorganized. he rarely posts on D2L and his syllabus has nothing on it except for the exam dates which are tentative. the homework he gives is nothing like the tests and his notes were extremely confusing, especially if you missed a class.

I went to every class, but he still didn't give me a 100 for attendance. I did good on all the homework's and tests, but still didn't get an A. You need to study for exams and get a 100 on all homework. An A is almost impossible, and he doesn't answer questions well. He just copies all the notes straight from the textbook, which is free for you.

Gives you free access to the textbook, but you won't have to use it. Take notes and go in to office hours for homework. No room to bomb any exams b/c of the A- grading scale. Gives seemingly vague study guides, but just study the exact topics that he tells you to, using the notes and homework, and you'll make an A easily. Not a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is ok. He pretty much just writes notes on the screen the entire time so be prepared to take a lot of notes. Topics are fairly simple. Not great at responding to emails though!

I really liked prof Menchaca. You will definitely learn a lot and be challenged in her class but its so worth it! She is a tough grader but she's fair and wants to help you succeed. Lots of reading and participation is important.

Menchaca is nice. However, if you aren't a history major don't expect an A, you have to read whole textbooks and be able to analyze it, or you won't do well. Did I try? Yes. Did it pay off? No. I would suggest another professor because this is known for being an easy course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She makes you participate in class, and often makes you feel stupid for the things that you say. But if you see her one on one to talk about papers, she is very helpful and nice. She assigns a LOT of reading outside of class. Doesn't grade papers/tests too hard. There are quizzes/pop quizzes throughout the semester. Only 2 tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Menchaca is such a great professor. She is super clear on the things she wants. There is A LOT of reading involved, but if you just read through it quick you'll be fine. I did not read at all and I got an A, so it's really not that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Would take again

reviews.comment: She gave us A LOT of reading for homework (after telling us this class would not require a lot of reading) and spent many classes telling us how to do the assignments rather than teaching us. Professor Menchaca was really nice, but I don't feel I learned much about the material as much as I did on how to write an analysis and how to write reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Menchaca is a nice lady, but very hard to keep up with during class. She posts ppts but they have no info on them, she just lectures the whole time. Class: ALL discussion and grades you on participation every class. So much reading to do! Has pop quizzes. Tests: short answer & essay, no MC. Big paper due at end of semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: History Survey: 1877 to present was my favorite class at TCU. Dr. Menchaca is a great teacher and the class itself is really interesting. As long as you participate, take good notes during lecture, and read for the occasional quizzes, you can do really well. You won't regret taking this class especially if you like history.

Professor Menchaca is clearly passionate about history and teaching so that makes the class worthwhile. She also gives you a clear study guide for the midterm and final that has the essay question on it and she also lets you bring a note card into the finals. Super great professor.

Menchaca was the nicest teacher! Her class was very easy so don't listen to what the other comments say! Her quizzes were online and EASY! The tests were made up of questions you already had answers to! Just show up, learn, and get an A. There is a final paper, but it was short and easily graded. If you are just kind and care, you will be great!

Professor Menchaca is one of the worst professors I had in my four years at TCU. She is very biased politically and shows it daily. In addition, there is reading required outside of class every single class - usually 2 to 3 chapters. Pop quizzes and required attendance also present. She made a 1000 level history class extremely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor! Cares deeply about the material. Will do everything she can in order to help you succeed in class. Field work is a bit outside of the box, but a good experience.
The biggest sweetheart. She impacts your life, and makes it known that she is there for you and cares about you and those you are teaching. She is a gem!
Dr. Silva is such a sweetheart. She cares about her students and cares about her subject. Sometimes a but disorganized, but night classes aren't always the funnest. We do love her, though!
She is genuinely one of the sweetest teachers I have ever met. I would definitely recommend taking a class with her if you can.

She is an amazing professor, as she teaches content clearly and is very easy to talk to. The projects assigned take a long time to complete, and she can be picky when grading, but the other assignments and exams are really easy, and you learn a lot in this course. I would definitely take her again

Dr. Robinson is super sweet. I feel like sometimes she forgets that some people in the class are not communication majors. The readings are heavy, but the screenings are fun. The quizzes and tests are graded heavily. Either way, she is lovely, and her class was the only peace I had during my day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: I took her for Women in TV and Film. She was a tough grader on all of my work. Class is very writing and reading heavy. She was nice and her lectures were fun, but this is not a slack off class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I've taken multiple classes with Charity, take her! She's super caring and really wants you to succeed. Her critical classes can have a lot of writing, but she offers a lot of extra credit opportunities!
I love this teacher! She is an amazing person and wants you to succeed in her class. She is a tough grader but not hard to pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Loved this class, it was one of the most helpful classes in the Sports Broadcast program.
My class met once a week, and she gave us no days we could miss. Tons of homework/busy work. Never canceled class or let us out early. I would not take her class again

Professor Stanton was a really good teacher! You do have to work and show up to her class, but she really wants her students to do well. She gives tons of extra credit, and there were only a few assignments and speeches. I could not recommend her more!

Take her! People who say she is hard dont want to work. Very sweet, and has clear expectations. No real tests. A few speeches are a large portion of your grade, but pratice and hard to do well.Take her! Only thing that was hard about the class for me was how it was once a week and 3 hrs. There is weekly journal hw but not bad.

I do not know what the bad reviews are about, Ms. Stanton  is a good teacher and a fairly easy grader. Her speeches are easy and she is clear on what you need to do to receive a 100 on speech(she also offers 10 bonus points for dressing up well). Their is a good amount of assignments but their not hard at all. Overall she's a good teacher.

Not a bad professor. Has 2 impromptu speeches with 1 artifact speech, typically for one minute each. The final is also an impromptu speech. 2 major speeches at the end of the semester. Journals are assigned each week, but they are simple. 3 take home quizzes open note. Some group work in class but they are simple assignments to do.

Beware - this is not a tough class but she is very unpredictable. One of the most common complaints in the class is that she is not consistent with what she expects and how she grades. Overall, she is good at what she teaches.

Mandatory, >1 min improv speeches each class, including the final, with no time to think. Quizzes, homework, and attendance is mandatory. Not like any other communicating effectively class I've heard of. You have to already be an excellent public speaker to do well. I would take anyone else because she is the worst communication professor at TCU.

Literally easiest com class ever, and she was super chill. Once a week. No real quizzes or exams - only 2 big speeches that she gives a clear outline for - so hard to do badly. Threw a pizza party for the last day.

TAKE HER! SO EASY. She is truly a wonderful professor. All she wants is for students to grow as people. She brought in pom-poms, bells, and cookies all the time. Even if you are bad at public speaking, it is VERY HARD to do poorly. Lots of Extra credit (even though it's probably not needed).

I have no idea what these first reviews are about. It's Professor Stanton's first semester at TCU, and she has already become one of the best professors I've had. Even though this is a required course, she made it super fun and engaging. Tests are easy, she sets up the speeches with clear outlines so you know what to do, and gives extra credit.

Professor Stanton is a great professor who cares more about her students becoming better public speakers rather than grades. Even though this was a 2-hour and 40-minute section, she made it bearable by having us do a lot of activities rather than just lectures. It's impossible to get a bad grade with all the extra credit she gave, take her!!!!

I LOVE HER. I have no idea what these other reviews are saying. I think she was incredible. She genuinely cares for her students and told us multiple times not to worry about our grade because she just cares about us getting better. SUPER easy grader if you follow the outline for speeches. Participation was important only because it was once a week
I've straight up told people not to come to tcu because of how awful she is and how bad this class is
just overall awful avoidddddd
Worst professor ever had at this school. Strictest attendance for COMMUNICATING EFFECTIVELY a class that everyone has to take and you can't get out of. Avoid at all costs

Class is a complete waste of time and is meant for 4th graders. You'll feel like a child the whole time and attendance is super strict. If you have no other options, take the class at a different school, take it online at u phoenix, or push it off as long as you can.
avoid at all costs

Dr. Charway is seriously awesome. Prolly one of the coolest professors I've ever had. I wish I could take her class again. She is actually hilarious. Her night class is more than bearable, it's actually entertaining. I wish every class in college was like this. TAKE CHARWAY!
She is super funny and entertaining. Although her tests and how hard she grades the final makes it a harder class to do well in. She is a super tough grader on the final.

Dr. Charway is pretty chill. She's nice and her lectures are interesting. If you go through the slides and chapters you should do fine, although the exams can be tough. There's enough other grades to balance the exams out and you can get lots of extra credit by doing extra SONA (research study) hours.

I had Professor Charway once a week and it was always a treat. In the beginning she can be a little intimidating, but she is the most engaging and dynamic professor I have ever taken a class with. I would recommend either going to the lectures or reading the textbook; I didn't do them both and I was fine. SHe is great though!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She comes off strong, but she's really awesome! In class quizzes are used for attendance but they aren't hard as long as you show up and do the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: really nice, lots of homework, reading heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Ciriza is a wonderfu/caring person which made the class bearable, there was only two easy presentations, a few essays which were a big portion of your grade, quizzes (drops lowest), and books that you read on your own time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This was a pretty good class. This was my first class back into Spanish after a semester off. There were lots of presentations at the start but it slowed down as the class went on. Most of the grades came from in-class essays that took lots of prep to do well on. Takes work but will better you as a Spanish speaker.

Best teacher in the spanish department. She is so caring and understanding. She gives a lot of homework, but it isn't just busy work and it always relates to what you do in class. I feel like my spanish has improved so much in this class, more than any other class at tcu.
simply the best teacher I've had in the Spanish Department at TCU. take her!!

Took service learning with her and it was life-changing! She has an amazing heart and is there to help you as a student and individual. I recommend everyone take a course with her if you get the chance.

Very fair grader and makes sure that are are okay. She values each student as an individual and works with everyone to achieve their best grade. Will definitely be taking another course with her in the future. She is very personable and her course is amazing to learn from not only her but the other students in the course.
Gives great comments on essays. Demanding by fair.
She is a wonderful professor who really cares about her students. Very interesting lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Such a sweet lady who really cares about her students. Expects a lot but very understanding and willing to help. Your Spanish will actually improve in this class. Homework for every class but not too hard. Important to pay attention because participation matters. Grade based on oral exams, homework, participation. Recommend her!

If you take her span 4 heritage class you will feel overwhelmed by the number of papers and assignments she gives out. If you take her, be over organized with your work bc it'll pay off at the end of the year when she assigns the portfolio assign. Other than that, she is a wonderful lady who really cares about her students 100% get on her good side
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Maira is great. She is very helpful if you are struggling and will always work with you. The class is some work but its completely manageable. She is very kind and you can tell she really loves what she's doing. I

There are three pretty straightforward tests and two essays, which she is adamant about while grading. I would not recommend taking this course if your Spanish is not at a really high level. She expects you to know everything regarding grammar, pronunciation, etc. There is a bunch of HW each class. She is a nice lady, but not a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Preface: I ended up dropping this class along with 5 of my friends. We had around 10 activities for homework each night. Instead of teaching things, she expects you to know everything so she will literally skip over a topic but expect you to know it for the class. Yes, she was nice. But I'd rather have a good teacher than a nice one.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Ciriza Lope is wonderful! She is so sweet and caring. She is personable and cares for each student individually. In addition, she is clear with her grading criteria and wants you to succeed!
Great Teacher. I would take any if her classes again. Very easy going. Just talk to her and she can work with you.

Dr. Jones is a very sweet, but hard teacher. The classroom is "flipped" in a very dramatic way, so it can be very tough. He cares a lot for his students, but I feel like he thinks this is the only class we have. Be prepared to put in HOURS of studying for his class. I like micro so I thought it was fun, but definitely NOT easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr.Jones is a great guy and knows a lot about biology, however he doesn't really teach that much. You will have a quiz over two chapters every Thursday even if you had just had a exam on Tuesday. Be ready to make this class your priority because there is usually at least 100 slides to memorize per week on top of weekly assignments.

He is the nicest teacher I have ever met but he assigns way to much slides a week to memorize. For example he will have an exam Tuesday (that mostly everyone fails), assign 50 slides to memorize for lab that Wednesday, Then assign 75 slides to memorize by Thursday and have a quiz on it. Be ready to only focus on this class and have no life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is making me crash out because his classroom is flipped that means YOU have to teach yourself everything he just goes over 4 points and reminds you what is due etc. He is nice but it is a lot of info I would recommend taking this somewhere else if you don't want to be stressed out. His in lecture quizzes are harder than the lecture exams
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He loves biology but not teaching it. He does not teach. I hope you know how to teach yourself everything since it's the most aggressive flipped classroom ever. He constantly criticizes his students for small things, even when he is genuinely barely teaching ever. Be ready to put in 20 hours a week, or to hate seeing him every class period.

You have to be prepared to put in time and effort in this class. He respects all his students and expects the work to be put in which is why he is perceived as being tough. A great teacher to have for this insane class and would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is really difficult but if you put in time and effort you will be fine. I was terrified looking at these reviews before the semester started and I worked really hard and was able to get an A. Go to office hours and know the material before class lectures. Use lectures as strictly review.

The class is inherently challenging, but he goes above and beyond to make sure that you have everything you need to do well in the course. Final is "cumulative" but don't let this scare you - he is very clear about what you need to review and it is high level concepts that have been applied all semester. If you put in the work, you will do well.

I am currently in this class and it is the most hard class I have ever took in my entire life. It almost feels like he wants you to fail and there's nothing you can do about it. I am currently crying so I do not recommend taking this class. He does not care about the student.

Dr. Jones is a great professor, he is very helpful if you just ask for help. The class is the hardest nursing pre-req, so be prepared to spend most of your time studying. His class is set up for you to pass as long as you put in the effort. Final is pretty easy as long as you study, it boosted most people from a D to a C.

Dr. Jones is an amazing professor! He really cares about his students and if you can't go to his office hours he will find a different time that works for you. The only negative is he teaches a flipped classroom so you pretty much have to teach yourself before coming to class. His weekly quizzes are harder than the tests but they are both hard.

He IS amazing, but his quizzes and exams ARE NOT. Get ready to teach yourself before coming to class, because he requires teamworks, so if you come with nothing, you will be left behind. Quizzes are way harder than exam, which means you can get good grades knowing that you did good on the quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Jones is a wonderful teacher. Front-loading is extremely important in this class to be successful. You teach yourself the material beforehand and then use class time to quiz yourself on it, and at the end he lectures about the most missed questions/most difficult topics. This class WILL teach you how to study, but you have to put in the work

This was my first nursing pre-requisite and I absolutely loved this class. Although it was self-taught and I worked really hard for my grade, it definitely paid off and I really enjoyed the content. I also met with one of the TAs weekly which was so helpful! I promise you will be completely fine in this course :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: yes this class is very test heavy and you will have to study A LOT but there are so so many extra credit opportunities to bring up your grade. He's very passionate about bio and his office hours are so helpful. During this class I feel well prepared to be a nurse. He does the backward teaching style so REVIEW BEFORE CLASS and you'll be ok

literally so awesome, he's super nice and make sure to get on his good side lol. He gives a ton of assignments but you will learn so so much so it's worth it. He's a great teacher and is always willing to help, he also provides so many resources if you need extra help and there are many opportunities for extra credit.
How do you know you have the clap???
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The material and tests are hard, but if you study good and work hard you will pass. Very helpful to come prepared to class by going over the powerpoint slides before lecture. Quiz every week and they are hard if you don't study. 3 large exams and comprehensive final. The lab portion is easier than the lecture, only 2 exams.

Dr. Jones is an incredible professor. His class is very hard, but if you do everything that he tells you to do, you will do well. He is very approachable and will always explain something in office hours, it is just up to you to initiate that. Most of the students who would say that he is a bad professor, have not reached out or studied enough.

I LOVE Dr. Jones. He taught from 8:00 am- 7:00 pm and his energy was amazing the entire time. He loves microbio and is so helpful. My roommates all had Curtis and I did better in Jones's class. Be ready to study ALOT, but if you memorize the PowerPoint, you will do amazing on the exams. I did better in this class than anatomy. Don't buy textbook

Dr Jones has an energy level constantly at a 10. He is very passionate and finds what he's talking about very interesting which can be very contagious. There is a lot of studying outside of the class and if you don't keep up with the notes before class, it can be very hard. He has a textbook but you really don't need it. I personally loved him.

if you're chosing betwen curtis and jones, go with jones. he is genuinely so passionate about microbiology and that's really what gets people through this class. It is really hard and it is kind of self-taught, but I seriously couldn't get through it without such an excited and outgoing professor! just stay on top of everything and you'll be fine

you will completely teach yourself as Dr Jones does not actually TEACH in class, says his exam questions are "straight forward" and are the complete opposite and extremely confusing, he will bring up the tiniest details in exams so if you can't teach yourself MICROBIOLOGY then take curtis!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Jones is very passionate about micro. This is a VERY hard class but tests are over power points and videos. Be prepared to STUDY a lot. His office hours can be very helpful if confused on certain topics

Be ready for incredibly long exams. 100 questions each time, with 150 for the final. You can study all you want, but the length of his exams makes it incredibly hard to stay mentally awake. A majority of the class is self-teaching.

Hardest course I have ever taken, but he makes it doable. Reverse classroom so he doesn't lecture and you just come take practice quizzes in class every day. Memorize every slide for PowerPoints and you will be fine. He's so passionate about micro and it rubs off.

Nice guy, very passionate about microbiology! This is a tough class, packed with a ton of topics. Majority of grade is from exams, so be ready to study. This is the only class in my college career I have actually had to study my butt off for.
He makes you do all the work outside of class and then just asks you questions during class. He never actually teaches the material to you.

Microbiology was not an easy class, but the material we learned was interesting and applicable to real life. Lectures are videos, and in class you do group work. A whole lot of memorization, I made a Quizlet for every lecture which was really helpful to learn everything. Put in the effort and you can do well! Dr. Jones is very nice :)

Get ready to teach yourself! Class is entirely flipped, and the vast majority of learning takes place outside the classroom. "Lectures" consist of quiz questions with a short explanation at the end. Jones is an incredibly nice, energetic, and knowledgeable professor, but the time spent in lecture would be more useful studying alone.

Dr. Jones has a very fun personality, and he's a very sweet guy. He loves to teach this topic, but the class is awful. There are never any study guides, you just have to memorize every little detail that gets put on the powerpoints. I would have done much better in this class if it wasn't extremely test heavy (72% of final grade) or had a guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Jones is very passionate about what he does. He definitely should not be teaching an intro microbio course, but should be working in a hospital. I study so much for this class and it doesn't seem to pay off. MEMORIZE THE POWERPOINTS. Every slide matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you are a nutrition/nursing major you have to take this class, and Jones was the only professor for this semester. Participation is mandatory but you can miss 2, however, the lectures don't really help. Tests are pretty hard so don't cram. Grade is mainly based on tests and final exam, then everything else is split up into small percentages.

Dr. Jones is a very knowledgable professor, clearly has mastered microbio, but is an incredibly tough professor! His expectations are super high for his students, requires a TON of hours outside of class studying. Exams are strictly over powerpoint, so you have to memorize every single slide. he is very accessible outside of class and happy to help

Sweet guy, really funny. VERY enthusiastic about micro. He LOVES it. This makes class super fun. Participation is mandatory, but it def helps your grade. Study continuously throughout the semester; don't cram. It's a lot of information. I never read the book and did fine. He is very helpful in office hours and personal emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Overall Microbiology is a difficult course. A lot of the teaching you have to do yourself and he leaves class for questions and practice. Tests are difficult but if you study enough you will do fine. Interesting material and assignments/participation help boost you're grade. If you put in the work you can pass. An A is hard to get but achievable.
He's great. Dr. Jones is a great teacher, but his class is tough.

Microbiology with Jones is TOUGH. Definitely one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. You need to be on point from DAY 1, if you do not want to suffer later. Memorize powerpoints for tests and make sure you know them WORD FOR WORD. Take lab seriously, it can help your grade. This class will take up ALL of your time. Work HARD and you can pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Jones is dedicated and excited about microbiology! He is fun to learn from, but his class is not easy. It was by far my hardest class of the semester & I was also taking A&P II at the same time. I did not love the labs but I did enjoy lecture. Exams cover a ton of topics & you should basically memorize every slide to do well. Get ready to work!

Micro is not an easy class, but if you put in the time and effort, you will do well. The tests are straight from the powerpoints so dont pay too much for the book (you have to buy it for inquizitive but get cheapest option). Dr. Jones cares about his students and is high energy so you won't have a hard time paying attention in class

Dr. Jones is incredibly supportive, and he REALLY seeks to cater to every student's needs. He is brilliant and always willing to help. He really knows how to teach. His class is challenging but not too bad as long as you participate and listen in lectures. There are iClicker questions that are both helpful and count for points, so go to class!

I have mixed feelings about this class. The powerpoint was exactly what was on the test but there were always a few trick questions. The Hot Zone is a fun read and the HZ quizzes can boost your grade early on. I got a low grade on my final and I studied so beware and prep far in advance (like 2-3 weeks). Lab is long but interesting.

The sheer amount of material to learn is what makes the class difficult. Memorize the power points, and work with Dr. Jones if you are struggling. He really cares about his students and will do what he can to help you, but you have to put in a minimum of 2-3 hrs additional time for each lecture. Also, be sure to memorize scientific names.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Microbiology is hella hard just a warning but you have to take it (@nursing). Clark is an enthusiastic teacher and pushes you. MEMORIZE the powerpoints for tests and you will do well. Do not worry about textbook (honestly don't buy it). Google online reading quiz questions, answers are all on various quizlets. Assignments boost grade!
Would not recommend...

I loved Clark Jones with my whole heart. He was by far the best teacher I had for my nursing prerequisites. He is so inspirational and passionate about Microbiology that it made me want to be a better student in his class. The exams are strictly powerpoints and the iClickers are graded but his methods of teaching are SO effective, you will do well!

The novel read is very interesting, but irrelevant. Do not study anything but the power points for the tests but STUDY. I-clicker is graded, so study upcoming material before class. Lab will definitely boost your grade. Know everything inside and out, and how to apply it. You will not have time to study for other classes if you want an A/B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tough class but interesting

Don't get me wrong, this class is TOUGH. However, Dr. Jones is one of the most challenging and and respected professors I have ever had. My one tip to you is to MEMORIZE, MEMORIZE, MEMORIZE the powerpoints. Study for the lab quizzes and lab tests because these have the power to really increase your grade. Work hard & you will be rewarded!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Jones is fantastic, but he is excruciatingly difficult. That being said, the vast majority of those taking this class are nursing majors preparing to start clinicals. The work prepares you for the field and equips you well for what lies ahead. He makes lectures so interesting at 8 am, and he is more than willing to help you when you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Super difficult and unrealistic. Claims the class is a "40 hour work week" so clearly he doesn't take into account the other classes we are taking. His tests are over so much material it's almost impossible to do well. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS IT'S TERRIBLE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Jones for the nursing microbiology class. Honestly, this was the ideal class. Even though it was a large lecture hall, there was lots of class participation. He breaks up lecture with discussion and iClicker questions. The class is challenging, but if you work hard, you'll pass. Way easier than Anatomy.  The lab work is really cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Took Clark Jones for Microbio. He pretends like he is smarter than everyone else. The way the class is organized, it seems more like a high school class than a college class. Doing a bunch of weekly homework, group projects that did not seem like a college atmosphere, and so much busy work. And his tests are so long and ask about very random things

Definitely the hardest class I have ever taken in college. Be ready to spend endless nights in the lib studying for a test that you may not even pass. He designs the class to be hardest in the beginning (then gets "easier" toward the end). I failed all semester and then barely passed the class with a 70... would not recommend if you have the choice

Dr. Jones is an amazing teacher and he really knows microbiology. This class is NOT by any means a walk in the park. You want an A? then you are definitely going to have to work for it! Lab is amazing, you really see some great things in there. I would highly recommended his class but again be prepared to work all semester long!!!!

Dr. Jones is one of THE toughest professor I've ever taken at TCU. He loves microbiology and I mean he loves it. Be ready to work and put in the work for his class if you wish to pass and make a good grade. NOT an easy class but the knowledge you gain at the end is worth it.

Don't get me wrong, this class is A LOT OF WORK. You have to have good study techniques and strong time management. A poor grade in this class is not a reflection of Dr. Jones teaching but of the students lack of work ethic. Jones really does care about the success of his students. He is great. One of my favorite classes at TCU so far.

I dont know what he was like back in 2012 which is when most of the good reviews are from, but now hes awful! Asks you super specific questions in class (both iClicker and asking you to voice a response in front of the 100 or so other students). If you dont know it, he acts like youre dumb. Harder & meaner than he needs to be!

Dr. Jones really loves microbiology but the format of his class is awful. 4 large, dense tests, lots of small lab quizzes, overall a lot of work. He's not very good at answering questions and likes to think this is a student's only class and all time should be dedicated to it. Buck up for a hard semester.

no. just no. on top of 5 tests and a comprehensive final he assigned constant homework, crazy iclicker questions every day, novel readings, big extensive projects, and group projects. while his class is not impossible its definitely too much work for one class. don't take.
I've never felt more uncomfortable around a professor. he'll make you feel stupid for not understanding something he hasn't even taught you. definitely don't take him if you have a choice.

He cares more about his class than your health. He once asked my roommate to reschedule her major surgery because he wanted her to go to a completely useless seminar on that day. I've never met a more self centered professor.

people on this site will say he's a great teacher, and he may be. he really loves microbiology, like has a very creepy obsession with it! while that does make him an interesting teacher to listen to at 8 am, just because he's a passionate teacher doesn't mean you should take this class. run away. he's awful and the other teacher is way easier.

Dr. Jones seems unable to pick a struggle. you can't be a bad teacher, give impossible tests, and A TON of busy work. its a hard science classand he assigns novel readings and long projects that mean nothing to the actual material on the tests.

Dr. Jones has been my favorite professor of all! He is always willing to help and keeps every lecture and lab super enthusiastic!  His tests are hard but definitely manageable, you just have to memorize the PowerPoints verbatim. He gives pop quizzes during lab, but if you study you'll do well! 3 assignments to help boost your grade!Take this class!
Hard class, Ridiculous tests.  One of the best professors out there.  Clearly states what material will be tested over and how to study.  Just listen, take notes and memorize everything!

Microbiology with Dr. Clark is not as hard as people say it is. If you put in the time to study it is definitely do-able. Also there are many other grades that can help boost your overall grade. You will learn a lot of useful information in his class that can be helpful outside of class. Dr. Jones can also be very entertaining.

I love Clark!!! he's a great teacher and is always willing to help out a student. The course material is difficult, but he presents it in the best way. It's a hard class, but he's a great teacher, and it's a mandatory class for nursing so you can't really avoid taking it. I loved this class tho!

He is a really good teacher and teaches the information in a way that helps alot! Definitely try and go to class. Studying for tests is hard but he provides all the information you need and doesn't try and trick you especially in lab practicals

I loved taking this class! It was a pain to study for because of the short answer and free response test questions though. It's difficult, but don't be one of the people that complains about grades constantly. I started off with a D on the very first test. Once I figured out the format, I brought my grade to a B. One grade is not a death sentence.
Very smart guy, but you have to be as smart as he is to pass the tests avoid avoid avoid

He is one bad ass guy. A very cool teacher but his test are hard. There fill in the blank and your spelling must be in the ball park. Overall I loved this class. The book isn't really used. It's all about knowing your notes.

Dr.Jones is one of the best professors on campus, however don't take this class unless you plan on learning something.  Be prepared to know the material not be familiar with it.  You will come out of the class completely satisfied if you apply yourself.  Take this Professor!!!!!

Dr. Jones is a great professor. He will teach you a lot about microbiology and make the subject material very interesting. Funny guy that livens class up for 8:00 in the morning. Although tests can be difficult, they really help you learn the material.
Dr, Jones is awesome! Just go to class and study the powerpoints and whatever extra he says in class and you will do great. He is very nice and always willing to help. Lab is fun and easy.

Easy teaching.  Talks directly off slides and gives a few additional things to know if you attend class.  Lab easy because if you screw up it doesn't effect your grade.  Tests are fairly easy except a random incredibly hard one he gave.  Quirky and fun and helps you stay awake at 8am.
a lot of test questions come directly from power points. go to class for additional info and clarity. good class, learned alot
Everyday is worth going to class.  He brings the world of Microbiology to life.
Amazing, quizzes each week about the readings/movies, but he grades them very easy. One group presentation, one individual, and then one essay. Take him

Professor Dillard is a nice guy but his class is incredibly boring. Exams are easy but only if you read the books (obviously) and there's a lot of writing involved in his class overall. I wish I could've found an easier english elective because this class was just very demanding on top of my already heavy schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is a good professor and really cares about what he teaches. Lectures get confusing or boring sometimes and there is a lot of reading, but the assignments and tests aren't too hard. He is also pretty flexible and easy to communicate with if you have any conflicts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Very passionate about what he teaches! Lectures are a little boring, but the class is very easy overall. Books we read are interesting, and there are only two exams.
Such a great professor. Very passionate about what he teaches and really values class participation. If you show up and apply yourself, you will do very well.

Literally the most boring class I have ever taken. He also is so weird. he is an easy grader but it is impossible to pay attention because he is so boring and all the books we read were also boring. I would've rather taken a slightly harder class that was more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: The man. Really passionate about the work he does. He wants you do to well. I took his comedy english class and really enjoyed it. He is just a great guy who just wants his students to be engaged with the content he shares.

Dillard is one of those teachers that loves the subject so much that you find yourself easily engaged in what he has to say. He doesnt take attendance but does in class writings which count to your grade. He says some repetitive lines and he goes off on a tangent sometimes, but he truly is very caring and smart. Loved his class. High praise.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: tests are a bit hard. but papers he grades nicely. GOAT
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dillard is amazing and is so helpful in and out of class. He truly just wants to see his student succeed. If you put in the work and read what he assigns each day before coming to class, you will do great on all of the writing assignments and midterm and final. Lectures are a little boring but he is a super nice guy!

Very easy. You have to put in some work, but its very easy to get a B or above. 2 textbooks and an exam over each. A research project with a few essays and a project. A pop quiz almost once a week (usually monday). Class work is annoying and IMO insignificant, but its not hard to succeed. Take if you want easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Dr. Dillard is a great professor who wants to see his students succeed and be successful. As long as you read the assigned reading for HW, you are good. Occasional pop writing assignments on homework readings but normally he tells you the class before and they are easy. He does not call on you but wants you to engage in class discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is the GOAT! Hugely entertaining and a very interactive and fun class. He provides a cheat sheet for the exams and is lectures are hilarious.
SO hard, dedicate so much time to this class or be prepared to get a C, he is a really great guy and professor, but the class is so hard

Professor Mackenzie is a very nice professor and his real-world examples are helpful in visualizing concepts, but the class itself is hard. If you struggle with reading comprehension, you will struggle in this class. Tests are a big part of your grade, but there is a small extra credit assignment. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 2013 Lebron, Season 4 Fortnite, 2019 LSU, Prime Kobe, Minecraft on a rainy day... You get the point. Dr. Mackenzie is the goat and his class was really fun. He talks about law from the lectures and shares stories about his career. Cool guy who cares and actually enjoys what he does. GOAT. Best prof at tcu.

Best professor I have had at TCU. Grade is heavily based on exams which kinda sucks but he really helps you understand the material. His lectures are amazing and he tells so many great stories from his own experience. Tests can be challenging but you're allowed a cheat sheet. Take good notes and you'll be fine.

Big Cliff is a great professor who made 8am lectures engaging and interesting. He is a solid dude who's friendly and knows what he's talking about. Tests are somewhat challenging but if you invest in the readings and show up you'll be fine. One knock is that he makes us watch a lot of movies that make up such a small % of our grade. Fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am pretty much a straight-A student; however, it was literally IMPOSSIBLE to get an A in his class. Don't get me wrong, he is a stand-up dude and knows what he is talking about, but don't be fooled by being allowed to have a cheat sheet for his tests. His tests are really hard, and the final exam makes or breaks basically your entire letter grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: MY FAVORITE TEACHER EVER! I will miss going to his class :(  He made every lecture engaging and enjoyable, and truly cares about his students' success. His teaching style is clear, approachable, and he always encourages questions. I learned so much in his class, and he really inspired me to stay passionate about the subject. HIGHLY RECOMMEND
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Mackenzie for BLAW is an amazing professor! I have his 8am MWF class which is usually brutal, but he makes it so engaging and fun to be a part of! I love his real-world experience and the stories that he has for every type of case. I would 100% take this class again and recommend him to everyone!

He is the GOAT. He helps so much in office hours, definitely reach out if you're lost, he is super friendly. He will make time for you. The class is textbook heavy, so make sure to have notes by class. If you're a slow reader, read ahead because lectures may zoom fast. Active recall really helps when studying. Cheat sheet stuff is true
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really interesting class.  Note that the 4 exams are 95% of your grade, so it is important to do well on each one to get an A.  On the last 3 exams, you can use 2 pages of notes.  There are occasional assignments and pop quizzes on the textbook readings.  You definitely have to work for the A, but it is attainable if you study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I love Professor Mackenzie! Amazing lectures but you need to read the textbook before class. If you participate he'll boost your grade at the end of the semester. Super engaging while teaching and test questions are extremely straightforward. He also has an extra credit opportunity for an entire extra point.  Best B-Law professor ever!!

I personally love Mackenzie, he provided valuable information in an interesting way. The reading is very important as he will pick you randomly in class to answer a question. He let us use cheat sheet on the exams and also provided extra credit. Stay on top of the reading and study and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Mackenzie was my favorite last semester. Read the textbook before class, pay attention to lectures, study, and you get an A. Exams are straightforward, not meant to trick you. Fair grader. Doesn't take attendance but I doubt you'll get an A or B if you don't go to class. Overall, highly recommend for B Law.

Overall great professor. He uses a lot of real life examples, which are very helpful. We got an assistance sheet on exams. There were 3 exams and 4 small assignments throughout the semester. We also had a couple pop quizzes, so make sure you do the reading. He did not take attendance.

I took Prof Mackenzie for Business Law and he is a very approachable teacher. Aware of catching students up for missing class. Challenging but the A is not unattainable. He is a lawyer so he has current experience and offers lots of applicable extra credit. A few pop quizzes but if you participate, it is an educational class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took Prof Mackenzie for BLaw and he is a very approachable teacher. Accommodating for missing class. Challenging but the A is not unattainable. He is a lawyer so he has current experience and offers lots of applicable extra credit. A few pop quizzes but if you participate, it is a very fun class!

Professor Mackenzie is a very good professor. He works with you in and outside the class. It's a little hard to reach him out but it's not impossible. He's a lawyer and knows a LOT about the law. He's very passionate about teaching his students. The exams are on lockdown browser but you're supposed to be in class to take them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took Professor Mackenzie Fall 2021 and I think he was a great professor. He is a lawyer and owns his own firm in Fort Worth, so sometimes it's hard to reach him, but he does his best. If I would have studied harder outside of class, I could have gotten a higher grade because he lays things out for you nicely through the lectures and slides.

Mackenzie was a stand-up guy, to say the least. He makes business law enjoyable to a student that may not find law too interesting. You are only graded on 3 tests and the final. His classes only consist of lectures and you will have a short assignment now and then. Attend class and take good notes and you should have no problem passing.

Mackenzie is an outstanding character, to say the least. He is an extremely funny guy who makes lectures interesting and fun. He only grades you on 4 tests with an assignment or two thrown in there. Every class is a lecture and nothing different. Pay attention and take notes off of his lecture and you will be just fine.

Clifford is probably the worst of the bunch to take for ENTRE. His exams are impossible to score well on due to the nature of offering zero study help and very rigid grading on his exams (BTW is 90% of the grade and only has 3 exams). He is a nice guy but his B-LAW class is awful and would not recommend it, even to my worst enemy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Mackenzie is the best B Law professor. He takes attendance. The class is strictly lectures, but he encourages participation to make them more engaging. Reading outside of class is necessary and will make the 4 exams easier. He is also an experienced lawyer and explains everything much better through real-life examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Mackenzie is excellent for Business Law. He does a great job tying real world examples into the material of the class and making you really analyze and think about the material. However, the class is VERY test heavy and not reading the textbook can be detrimental, so really invest your time correctly. He is a great choice if law interests you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Mackenzie is the coolest prof I've had. He cares a lot about what he's teaching and obviously really likes it. It's not the easiest class but this prof is the best of the best. He also has amazing stories since he's a lawyer

Difficult to reach because he's a lawyer so you have to call his office to make an appointment to view your tests, but he's very nice and makes lectures interactive and interesting, which is essential for a night class. Almost your entire grade is based off of 3 tests and a final and he gives occasional pop quizzes, which sucks, but he's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was not too bad, but it was a ton of reading prior to class, then take good notes during the lectures. Only reason I wouldn't recommend taking his Blaw class is that the other teachers are way easier. He has 90% of grade on 4 exams, and they are hard, you need to study a lot. Other teachers have open tests or projects or easier material
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Mackenzie is a great professor just a boring and hard class. The only grades in the grade book is 4 exams, couple 1 point quizzes. Gotta go to class if you want to do good, he is very lecture heavy and doesn't post the slides. Take good notes, study hard and you'll be fine. Trager is definitely the move for BLAW if shes is available tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor. I had him for 8AM, which I originally was dreading, but he makes it bearable to get up that early. Business Law is a tough subject, but he makes sure you know the material before the exam and actually cares. You are only graded by 4 exams, a final, and a pop quiz here and there. Reading the textbook is essential to pass the class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Mackenzie is knowledgeable, caring, and a very interesting professor. He is lecture-heavy/ test-heavy however if you pay attention in class you will be more than fine. There is a textbook however I have friends who got by simply listening to lectures. He is not an easy A however he is an amazing professor and is passionate about his teaching.

Professor Mackenzie really tries his best to make sure you understand what is taught. He gives good examples and makes the lecture interesting. Study the textbook and the notes carefully before exams and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Mackenzie does a good job at making lectures interesting. He grades fair, offers extra credit, and does not assign homework. However, the course is test heavy so studying is important.

Professor Mackenzie is a great teacher. He trys his best to keep it interesting and uses funny examples when teaching. If you want to do well its simple. Read ahead before class, participate in the class discussions and ask questions and study hard before the tests and youll do more then well. Its only 3 tests, a Final and DO THE BONUS.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Though you're only graded on tests (95%) and participation (5%), take this class!! You definitely have to work for an A with lots of reading and studying, Mackenzie makes this class very interesting. He connects concepts to his life experiences, which makes them easier to understand. If you are ready to put in the work, I highly recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mackenzie's class has been my favorite while at TCU. Made me want to be a lawyer even though I'm a Marketing major! He has the best stories to help you understand the concepts and will make you laugh too. His tests are straight forward, but you've still gotta study. I would take his class again and again. And definitely do the extra credit!

Mackenzie made me want to become a lawyer. He is so awesome! He only has 4 grades (3 tests and attendance) and then an opportunity to do extra credit (do it you will regret it if you don't). I always looked forward to attending his class and all the stories he had to tell. Moral of the story, TAKE HIM! You will not regret it, I promise.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is very easy to talk to and approach. He lectures straight from the book, so read before class so you know what he is going to talk about. He gives pop quizzes to make sure you are reading. His exams require time to study, but if you put the work in, you will get the good grade. Also, there's an extra credit assignment I highly recommend you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: LOVED Prof. Clark! One of the sweetest, most caring professors I've had so far. There are many writing assignments, but each aligns perfectly with the course material. There are several in-class quizzes, but they're open-book. She loves what she does, and it shows. I would take her again and again if I had the opportunity to!
Helpful, nice, and great teacher. Really knows her stuff. Tries to make it all interesting and doesn't waste your time.
Knows what she is talking about, excited about the profession. Check all your work for style errors! Nice and friendly.
Ms. Clark is sooooo nice!  Shes the cutest "soccer mom" ever!  She tells us all about her day and real world experiences, which can get old at night, but its helpful too.  Definitely take this class!
Real world examples, pertinent information and portfolio building assignments. GSP quizzes can be confusing but you get used to them. Super friendly and very willing to help.

Professor Clark is a great teacher that actually shows you how to do stuff that you are going to use in the real world. She makes the class fun and interesting. You have to take daily A.P. quizes but they aren't bad.  No exams!!! The final is a portfolio of what you've done over the year, and isn't hard. She is the HOTTEST TEACHER EVER, trust me!
Is it hot in here or is it just...
Michelle Clark is really helpful.  She teaches night class so it is kinda boring because it runs really long.  But she makes it fun.  She is soooooo Hot, so it makes the class go faster!
This class is pretty good.  She is very nice and hands out her presentations every class.  She is also very very hot!

One of the most engaging and humorous professors at TCU. Relates great stories of his own experiences to the content being taught in class. Attendance isn't mandatory, and the class is always full. Everything on the test is on the lecture slides.
Take him! you learn so much but he makes the material very simple and easy to understand. exams are so easy if you look at the slides!

The best professor I have had at TCU!! He is so knowledgeable, and you truly get so much real-world knowledge, not just the course content! He is always sharing his experiences and giving us great advice.

Professor Haggard is awesome! The class itself has 5 tests, but they are very easy so if you read the slides you should pass. He brings in a lot of outside guests, and he has a lot of advice and connections in the outside world! Overall, great teacher, I would recommend him to everyone!

My all time favorite prof at TCU. His lectures were top tier and got me really interested in real estate. He brings in a handful of guest speakers. Did I mention how funny he is? He makes class entertaining with some hilarious comments. He is also a very prominent real estate mogul in the DFW area with a ton of industry knowledge. Take his class.

He's.... something alright. I wouldn't be surprised if his whole life was a lie! 
Anyways, he is really interesting, no real way to describe him....lets just say he had to prove his wife is real!
Reading the textbook is necessary, and I would definitely recommend it. You should take notes, as his tests are open note.

Tests are open note. Almost all classes are lectures, with few assignments. 

Very Random Guy. He tells you lots of weird stories, and says lots of out of pocket things. He's pretty cool though.

I took his Juvenile Justice System course at TCC Northwest during the Fall 2014 semester and would not recommend this professor at all. Very disorganized, doesn't respond in a timely manner to email at all, and goes off topic a lot. I'm a 4.0 student and glad to show my transcript but this professor is a joke and wouldn't recommend him to no one!
Great teacher who actually cares about what he is teaching as well as is involved in what he is teaching. very easy to comprehend what he is lecturing about.
Arrogant and very inconsistent class material. Sometimes will not show up to his own office hours.

Got off topic a lot. He was a cool guy though. For the longest time noone's actual grade was not posted on eCollege. It seemed like he was pretty irresponsible, which made students uneasy. I wouldn't take him unless you had to.
He didn't follow the syllabus at all, attendance was not very important. An easy class but he is a frustratingly unorganized professor.

I had heard he was a great professor for other classes but in this class, his heart was not in it. He didn't consistently come to class and I'm not sure he ever knew what was going on. I'm a pretty good student, I read the book and attended every class but a last minute syllabus change took away the A I had all semester. I would NOT recommend him.
Professor Clark-Miller is one of the best professors at TCU. He is extremely helpful and is able to keep lectures interesting. His classes are a must take!

Such a cool prof with lots of interesting (if at times random) stories. I really enjoyed his class and learned a ton. He is an interesting lecturer and was always able to hold my attention. He is a very fair, if not perhaps an easy grader. He seems like an all around nice guy and I highly recommend him.

Awesome guy and he is very passionate about what he does.  Class is not too difficult because he is very clear and is more than happy to help you out.  He will do whatever is neccessary for you to understand the material, all you have to do is ASK.

Great professor. True... his lectures can drag on a bit, but things could be a lot worse! Just in general, he's a very reasonable, fun guy and a great professor. You may not enjoy every minute of it but you will be glad you took it, its really not that hard!
I recommend his summer Victimology class.  It is writing emphasis, and we only had to do one paper, 5-10 pages, topic of our choice. Easy!
