He was nice enough but his lectures got repetitive at times and classes seemed to drag on forever. The syllabus changed every now and then, but he's a nice guy and his tests are not bad if you study and you get to pick essay questions you want to answer, etc.

I took him for Res. Methods 2. He was not very clear EVER.... we weren't ever sure what our grade would be based on and he kept changing the syllabus... His lack of organization benefits the student b/c as long as he knows you, you get an A. He is passionate about what he teaches and he is a nice guy!

I took him for both Rearch methods 2 & Community Corrections and got As...even though his lectures can get boring, you have to take notes and attend class. He goes off on the topic several times but only b/c he loves what he's teaching. Ask questions b/c he will help you! As long as he knows who you are, you will get an A.

He was absolutely boring in class when he just lectured on and on about literaly NOTHING... He always said he would show us how to break a bike lock but never did. The tests were not graded fairly and he was way to preachy.  Would not recommend him unless you like to write long papers and hear pointless nonesence!
Good guy, not so great of a professor. But still easy A. Take notes in class... reading doesn't really make that much of a difference, just reinforces whats said in class. I recommend him.
Overall, very nice guy. The class is super manageable, and he wants everyone to succeed. The exams are easy if you study the PowerPoint and look at his study guides.
Tests were all based on slides, not too bad if you study. Exam 3 was optional, and class typically ends early

I loved Professor Cole! His lectures are engaging and the material is genuinely interesting. His tests are very manageable if you study the slides he provides. He uses email for everything and sends lots of helpful reminders. He's also very organized and clear about expectations. Definitely take him!

He does not use D2L at all. He doesn't really lecture but he assigns long readings (around 20 pages) and anything in them can be pulled for the exam. Exams are weirdly hard for a class like this where the material isn't very complex. I would not recommend this professor even though he is a nice guy.

Tests are VERY difficult. The class is so chill, but he makes the tests and quizzes unnecessarily hard. He sends everything by email, so it's hard to keep up with. It's definitely doable to get an A in his class but he makes it ore difficult than it needs to be.

Worst teacher ever. Take leader development another semester. Way harder than Dr. Cook. Only communicates by email, and it often contradicts the syllabus. Grading is unclear. Promised no quizzes with participation—lied. Class average was a 76. Gave bonus points to boost grades because too many were failing.

He does not use D2L at all which is frustrating. He sends you everything by email only. His exams are kind of hard. I  later realized he highlights and bolds all the exam questions on his PowerPoints. He assigns weekly readings that are way to long and expects you to read them and you are quizzed on them. But, he gives you EC. Exam 3 optional.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Cole is a good person and a good professor but his course is very heavy on exams and quizzes. With 61% of your grade being exams, it leaves very little room for error. He grades his exams tough, and asks very specific questions on them. For our final paper, he gave us little to no direction until the second to last week. Not the clearest.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His classes are pretty interactive and he never goes over an hour for every class. Reading wasn't too bad, but exams are not easy to get an A, but if you get As from other assignments (which are easy) and put effort into the team project then the class is pretty much easy A-. He cancels class sometimes and left Exam 3 optional for our class.

Sweet guy, funny, and very to-the-point. Most of the grades are from exams (which are manageable if you take notes and do the study guide), a team training project, quizzes, and some easy reflection assignments (100 for turning in). He also gives out bonus points for groups voted the best in the short leadership lesson activities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class used to be a breeze. Not sure what happened, but it's now based primarily on extremely difficult exams. He does not give partial credit and is relatively unwilling to help out. He communicates entirely through email and hardly uses TCUOnline. He's the only professor for the class, so be ready to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A great professor! Very welcoming and open to hearing ideas. Brought pie to class one day. He cares about his students. Work not that hard if you do what you're supposed to.

This class was going smoothly until about the last 3 weeks. Final paper is nearly impossible if you don't start 2 weeks ahead of time - 12-20 pages single spaced. All presentations are with a group and your grades are based on a ranking system. Whatever the class rates you is your grade. Professor has ridiculously high standards. Take someone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Changed my final grade from an A to a C because I turned in one assignment 2 hours late. Very unreasonable. Easy class besides that, but was always unclear as to what he wanted.

Reading quizzes are hard, class is generally interesting and discussion based.  Tests are not bad if you actually fill out the study guide that he gives you, the class involves a lot of writing but that wasn't an issue.  There are a few extra credit opportunities.  Overall, it was a good class that wasn't too painful.

Do not take Cole. Take Youngblood, he's boring but you'll get an A. Cole assigns lots of busy work and grades very tough. Acts cool and is until you take his test and have the group project. My second B ever in college to give you an idea. Low morale was a big problem. Very tough quizzes and boring in class exercises. I warned you.

Take her! She made me feel so good about public speaking, and I actually enjoy going to class because of her. So accessible and wants to help you succeed. 3 speeches, but one of them is a group and a midterm, but pretty simple overall. Seriously wish I could have her again!

Great professor. She got me to feel so much better about public speaking. We had a couple assignments and then the speeches of course, but none of them were "too difficult". She's super nice and is always willing to help her students with their speeches or other assignments. If you still need your COMM credit, take her!!
LOVE HER. super easy class, projects/speeches are actually interesting, and she doesn't care if you're on your laptop. highly recommend this class!!

Worked hard on the major assignments and got perfect scores. A few students in my class who used almost all ai on their projects got points off for bad work. Genuinely a great teacher, and includes us in lessons. The class becomes a group of friends by the end of the semester, as there is so many meaningful and fun activities.
Excellent professor, provides good feedback. Very relatable.
Pretty easy class. Show up and be prepared for your speech. Easy A. Take her.

I really enjoyed professor Kopecky's class this semester. The class was generally easy and she cares about her students! 

You don't really need the textbook - there are "Chapter Checks" on the reading but you can choose a different answer until you get it correct. She goes over all of the important notes that will be on the test.

Such a caring and supportive professor! She genuinely wants you to grow as a speaker and gives super fair feedback. She is always willing to help and gives amazing tips, answers emails within the hour, and makes the class feel super comfortable. Truly one of the sweetest teachers I've had at TCU, highly recommend!
She is such a great professor. There are three speeches (informative, persuasive, and a group one), and she grades pretty fairly. There is little to no busy work, and she is always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: My favorite professor so far in college. They are such a sweet person who genuinely wants to see you succeed in the class. There are only three speeches in total, with one being a group presentation, plus two easy quizzes and a midterm. Overall, the class feels supportive and manageable, and the professor makes the experience even better.

She is one of the nicest and best professors that TCU has. She is very caring for her students and is very easy to reach for help in office hours. Study for the exams and quizzes and you'll do well. An informative, persuasive, and group presentation. Definitely recommend taking if you need a communications credit.

She is the kindest professor I have taken at TCU and she understands that we are all just college students trying to figure it out. With that being said, she still expects full participation and be ready to give your speech on any given day. I loved her as my Comm professor!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best Communicating Effectively teacher. So kind, explains things well, grades fairly, and exams and quizzes are easy 100s if you study. She understands this isn't your most important class and will be super understanding if you can't complete something on time. Take her!!!

Please do yourself a favor, don't take this class or your grade is gonna suffer. Dr.Sanders is quite nice in class but she grades you on ridiculously small details and you can't hardly avoid those pesky technical penalties when you're writing naturally.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very strict grading and frowned upon to use the restroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
doesnt let you use basic words like : to aim
to allow (for)
to desire
to impact, e.g. Enlightenment ideas impacted the French Revolution.
to mention, e.g. In The Social Contract, Rousseau mentions the general will.
to transition
to upgrade
to utilize
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: In my 3.5 years at TCU, I have never encountered a worse professor than Dr. Sanders.  This course is absurdly difficult and completely inappropriate for a Level One core class. The workload and grading standards are far beyond what is reasonable for a course at this level, and they feel deliberately punitive rather than educational.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is no joke - the workload is intense and Dr. Sanders is a tough grader. But if you stay organized, meet with her, and use study tools like unstuck study, you can survive. It's a challenging course, but worth it if you're up for the work.

I joined this class for one day and already she was rude. She is ridiculously hard for no reason and expects you to treat this class as a major despite being a core. I do not know why she has any high ratings.

She is a very great professor. Without a doubt one of the most charismatic professors' I have had. However the class is brutal. Grades really tough, and essays get graded even tougher. I feel like I learned a lot but it might not be worth the stress and pass/no credit, unless you are super history savvy.
major fade on this class; should be a level 5 writing, not a level 1 history. I contemplated multiple times reporting her to the dean of the history department because of the difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanders was an amazing professor. She is so knowledgable and her lectures are super interesting. I will admit the work outside of class is HEAVY.If you are not satisfied with your grade GO SEE HER, it made a drastic change when I knew exactly what she wanted when it came to big essays. She really is an amazing person and is super accommodating!

Her grading is tuff, she is really particular about the formatting of the papers, and there is alot of them. She also sets up D2L in a really odd way where the stuff to due inst there and if it is its for the wrong date, you have to stick to the syllabus, so be ware. Not exaggerating around 50% of the class dropped after the first 3 weeks.
Do not take her on this course!!! I've never done more writing in a class in my life. All of her assignments are so time consuming and I took it for core, but i regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanders is amazing at what she does and very knowledgeable in her field, she provides a lot of constructive and helpful feedback. The course is reading heavy and the bulk of the grade is made up of 3 large papers. There is a lot of room for revision and growth built in. Highly recommend her courses for History or other Lib arts majors.

I took this class for a core requirement, and I wish I did not take it. This was the craziest and hardest class I have taken. This class is more like a level 5 writing class. The directions are all over the place and it is so hard to follow and do well. Majority of the people got C's so pass no credit the class if you have to take it. Try to avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She holds lots of enthusiasm in her lectures and provides many extra credit opportunities. Extra credit is the only way you will pass though. She provides unclear and inconsistent structure regarding the course and instructions about assignments. The class relates to history, but it is a level 4 English class, not level 1 history.

This is the hardest class I have ever taken. She makes you write, then revise multiple times and your revisions even get individual grades. There is always something wrong with what you submit - even if you stuck to the rubric. 2/3 of my class dropped this semester. When I was doing homework - it was for this class. Don't take, my GPA has suffered.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This professor was nice I guess. Toughest grader I have had in my entire life and she is not clear on anything. Very strict deadlines and you wont get above a C on a paper no matter how hard you try. Expects you to know everything before she even says it. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I initially expected this to be a History class, but that really wasn't the case. This class is essentially an English course with a squeeze of history. Sander's is easily the toughest english teacher I've had, let alone history. The amount of work she gives along with how tough she grades things is just nuts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanders is a very passionate history teacher who will push you and make you a better writer. Do not take this class if you cannot afford a hard class that requires a lot of time. She is a very tough and thorough grader but if you follow the instructions and meet with her, what she wants becomes much clearer. PRINT SYLLABUS AND ASSIGNMENTS.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanders is really funny and entertaining in her lectures, BUT she has the strangest due date times that confused literally my entire class. everyone received poor grades on assignments and it was hard to make those grades up. on top of a textbook, we also had to buy several other books and novels plus primary sources - VERY READING HEAVY CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor, with a ton of knowledge about history and a great passion for teaching. Lecutures are extremely intersting. Grades extremely hard tho, brutally critiques essays and papers.

She really is a great teacher, who makes the lectures very interesting and enjoyable. She is passionate about the subject and makes concepts really easy to understand if you pay attention in class. The essays are graded really tough; there are rewrites. Half drop within the first month, and about half the remaining students P/NC. Great teacher tho.

She is really funny and entertaining in her lecture. I literally have never taken a harder class in my life. I tried SO hard on everything and got the worst grades ever. I pass/no credited the class, but did not even pass. If you want to do good on the papers, good luck. She is the toughest grader ever and your GPA will suffer. Nice person though!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is SO HARD. She is great and so knowledgable and friendly, however you will not make above a C on the papers, no matter how many times you meet with her! She's really nice though just insanely hard.

She grades ridiculously hard. Before this class I had never in my life made an F on anything. I made the highest grade in the class for both English Composition classes and C's and F's on the papers in her class. I don't know what her problem is. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Seriously. Save yourself.

Don't take a class with Sanders. Trust me. It will only lower your GPA. No matter how hard you try you will not get above a C on any of the major assigments. Thinks she is very smart and will dock points for just about anything. Caused me a ton of stress. Just don't do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: she is very willing to meet with students and is very sweet but no matter how hard I tried on papers or how much help I got on them from better writers I still could not get over a C. Everyone I know in the class has not been able to get over a C on the papers no matter how good a student. She doesn't do exams which is nice, but tons of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She is a great teacher and you learn a lot through her lectures however her grading on assignments is unreal. She mentions multiple times that she has a law degree and its obvious through her grade rubric and grading style. She grades harder than any English teacher I've ever had. I only recommend to history majors...

One of the hardest teachers I've ever had. However, her class is doable. Do the extra credit (I have about 70 points in extra credit). Take the time to talk to her in office hours, she will help you! The class has 6 quizzes w 2 dropped, 2 papers (3-5pg) and final (7-10pgs). Very tough grader but will allow rough drafts and rewrites! Put in the work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Terrible class. She cares about the material, and there are no tests, but she grades ridiculously on the papers. She asks you to read several books back to back. Her lectures are relatively pointless, since you only need to know the material for the three papers you write. I had a 4.0 and had to P/NC this class. DO NOT take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanders is an amazing professor. Do the assignments, participate in class, and DO THE EXTRA CREDIT. She allows you to turn in a rough draft and rewrite the papers for a higher grade. It's incredibly hard, but you can make an A in this class, just don't expect it to be handed to you. Plus she is hilarious and more than willing to work with you.

while she is passionate about this course, its very hard to please her. no tests but online reading quizzes that she grades very harshly. 2 papers duirng the semester plus a final paper. half the class dropped because of bad grades. only take if you have a PNC left . you know how teachers say there is no dumb questions, well in her class there is
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While Dr. Sanders is passionate, she is unclear about course expectations. WEM class so heavy writing but does not grade clearly or explain why you received the grade. HARD GRADER. No one in this class received over an 85. This is a core credit but should be for HISTORY MAJORS ONLY. Changes her mind on your work- approve one day, fail you the next
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Only take this class if you have a PNC to spare. The class is interesting but she teaches this class like a senior level history major course rather than a freshman level core. Over half the class dropped out after failing every online quiz and assignment. Nice lady but unrealistic expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanders is an amazing professor and even though the class requires A LOT of reading and time, the work is definitely worth it. She lets you do multiple drafts of each essay and provides intensely detailed feedback. She gives lots of chances for extra credit so make sure you do it. Participate in class and do well on the final paper for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I took this class once before and dropped after the very first lecture . However, I take it again this semester as a 3-hour course a week. We did a lot of open-discussion and Dr. Sanders told a lot of interesting stories. A lot of extra credit to back up your quiz. Writing took major points but she allowed drafts and gave really good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The entire class consists of two essays, a large fiction paper, and a few online assignments (Quizzes/Discussion Boards) This class has made me a better writer. Although there are a lot of essays, she allows you to submit a rough draft and a re-write for each essay. Also, there is lots of extra credit available.

I was a freshman at TCU, who loved European History, and was so excited for this class. On the first day, my stomach dropped at the workload I'd have. as the semester progressed, I realized just how amazing she is. Her lectures are engaging, the papers are doable, and she gives ample extra credit options. She truly cares about her students
Dr. Sanders is great and teaches you history in a very entertaining way. The 1879-present class is very tough, if you take it prepare to read a TON and to get a c- in a paper you though was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor, she never updates your grade through the semester, so don't know what your grade until the end. There are 2 papers that are 3-5pages with a final that is 7-10 pages. She does let you rewrite the first two for a better grade and offers extra credit but she tears papers to shreds. If you thought you were a good writer, beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The best professor I've had a TCU. She is a tough grade but only because she wants you to be a better writer. You can rewrite your papers (with her help) basically until you get an A. She expects you to work but also cares so much about you and helping your succeed. Cannot recommend her enough!
Dr. Sanders is one of the best professors that I had at TCU. She really takes the time to talk and connect with each of her students.

One of the best Professors at TCU! She is a tough grader but she gives a lot of Extra Credit and allows for rewrites in order to boost your grade up. She goes above and Beyond for her students. I have a much greater chance to get my dream job because of Dr. Sanders.

I LOVE Dr. Sanders. Yes, she is a hard grader and expects a lot of her students, but she is more than willing to help you succeed as a student. She is a great professor because she respects her students and works with them tirelessly. Take as many classes as you can with her! Expect to work hard, but also expect to become a better writer!

Dr Sanders is a great teacher, but her grading is subjective, and her class consists of three papers so that's what counts. Fortunately there are rewrites so you can correct your mistakes and get points back for corrections
She is a tough grader on papers, however she gives excellent feedback and opportunities for rewrites. To bad she doesn't teach more classes.

Women in European History was an incredible course for me for many reasons. There were 2 analytical papers, 1 research paper, a video project based on the research paper, and a threaded discussion off of the readings every week. It's a small amount of assignments for the amount of reading you do for the course. But Dr. Sanders is incredible.

Her means of grading is overly harsh and subjective. Her reading requirements are an overload and assignments are overly complicated. She is teaching a freshman level class like it is a senior level history major class. No regard for the fact you have other classes and commitments are made. Expect to devote at least 20 hours a week if you want a A.

I love history and looked forward to taking this class. Dr. Sanders crushed my hopes. Don't take this class. She grades unfairly and does not care about whether you learn history (she states this in the class). Do not expect to do well in the class, no matter how hard you work. Please, please do yourself a favor and take another class.

Sanders is an angel. Class is AMAZING if you like history. Lectures on what the textbook doesn't, all the interesting tidbits. You can get 100% in the quiz grade category because she only grades 10-ish of them. The bulk of your grade is 3 papers. She makes you work for these grades but rewards with progress that she helps TONS with. Lot of work tbh

Very tough grader bc she believes writing is important. Papers are big part of the grade, the final is a historical fiction. She's big on extra credit! It's a great deal, actually probably saved me quite a bit. If you take your time to do rough drafts and re-writes you can go from C- to B, easy. Feedback is always helpful. Overall, great professor
There are no exams in this class, but lots of writing assignments. The lectures aren't very clear, so make sure you are following along with reading so you know the information!

She's a great professor.  You get to rewrite everything plus she will look at rough drafts.  the classes were always interesting and there's options for everything.  She's a tough grader but she will also help you and give the option for any rewrites. You only need mindtap getting the textbook too is  waste of money.
This class is lectures with online quizzes following (pretty tough) and 3 huge papers. Attendance is mandatory. Toughest class I've taken at TCU.

This class is incredibly tough (European History 1789 to present). I received a 0 on my paper after taking it to the writing center and working on it for over a week! Its her way or the highway. Would not recommend this class. Very interesting lectures, but not worth it. A lot of people drop or passfail. HARSHEST GRADER EVER. Stay away!

One of the worst classes i have had. She grades papers as hard as i have ever seen a teacher. She is very  energetic and spastic. She tends to go off on tangent a lot and has a hard time focusing. The worst experience i have had at TCU. STAY AWAY FROM HER CLASS!!!

Dr. Sanders is extremely passionate about European history- history in general- & very animated. I could sit & listen to her lecture all day. She is very specific in terms of what is expected on papers and quizzes, but she also wants to see her students take interest in the content. She is very approachable and always provides effective feedback.

I took her honors European history class. There is a LOT of reading and 3 major papers. Quizzes are online. Dr. Sanders gives a lot of extra credit and lets you rewrite your papers. She grades kind of harshly, but class discussions are very interesting. At first it might seem difficult to make an A, but it's possible if you do the extra credit.

Dr. Sanders keeps her history class very interesting. I am not a history major, but  took her Peace or Pause class for my upper level history credit. It was a very challenging class as far as assignments go, but she is always willing to help you if you meet with her! Yes, she is a tough grader, but welcome to college. I loved her class!
Dr. Sanders is an awesome professor, but very difficult. She's a very tough grader when it comes to writing, but she is also very helpful. Lots of reading and lots of writing, so beware.
AVOID!!! Not helpful at all. Very harsh grader.

She is a nice person, but the complements stop there.  This is a freshman level class (Modern History of Europe) and you can expect to spend copious amounts of time writing and rewriting and rewriting and rewriting papers.  For you sanity and your GPA, do not take her class.

Grades papers more on grammar, than on content of paper. Also wants students to site textbook and assigned reading material. Do you really not know where we get the info? Have to read two 250 page novels for a total of maybe 5 quiz questions. Quizes count for almost nothing. Told one student she would fail him due  to stating a bad analogy in class
If you want to hate your life then take Sanders. Overly harsh grader for freshman class, very inconsistent on her grading scale. Going to class is pointless, but mandatory

She threatened to fail a student for stating his opinion in class.  Disorganized, all dates are tentative until she gets good and ready.  She is willing to help you with your writing, but you better be an English or History major to justify the amount of work required. Students that got A's on their research papers had to do 10+ revisions. AVOID!!!

Exciting and fun, though unstructured and inefficient, in-class discussions. GPA destroyer. First and last C+ I made during my time at TCU. Quite disorganized. Syllabus and class schedule were incorrect on day 1. Contradicting class instructions in documents. Inconsistent remarks on graded papers. Inconsistent in accessibility outside of class.
very bad Professor, not professional, not willing to help and will screw you.

Euro history is a challenging class. Extremely hard grader that examines every small detail. Use of passive voice will ruin essay grades. Class based on 2 papers and a 7-10pg historical fiction paper final along with discussion questions and online quizzes. Even if you're a good writer content, know that it takes hard work to succeed in this class

European History 1789 to present isn't an easy A but it's also not death to you GPA. Dr. Sanders is very easy to talk to and every willing to help editing essays and answering questions. There are no tests which is AWESOME! Grades are based on small points with quizzes every other week, 3 DQ's submitted every other week and 3 papers.

Amazing class lectures. She makes history very exciting and alive. Essays are extremely difficult, must perfect format errors. I didn't know there was such thing as passive tense till she brought it up and didn't want it in the essays. I hated skipping class because I knew i was going to miss an interesting lecture. If you can get past the essay writing, it's an easy class. Very rewarding.

Very difficult class with a ton of work.  Sanders however is a very knowledgeable prof willing to help you.  Her grading seems a little unfair, especially on re-writes where she seems to find new things wrong with your paper that were not marked up on the first draft.  If you are interested in history take her course, if not then steer clear.

Hard class... NOT AN easy A... Geared more to hist majors... Dont take it if you don't like writing.. specially if you get a crappy TA... Dr. Sanders is passionate about the class and it I loved the way she taught... but the papers are hard...

This was my honors class and I did NOTHING and got a b+. She says her class is heavy on reading- never did a single one. All quizes are taken online, so you can google your way through them. Otherwise, I am a horrible writer and the class is based off three papers, she lets you do rewrites- so as long as you do those, your golden. Joke of a class.
She's gooooooooood!

Class has basically 3 grades- 2 analytic papers and 1 historical fiction paper. I hate history. I hate writing. I hate writing about history. I would not recommend this class to people who hate writing and hate history.

Dr. Sanders came across as really intimidating at first. She grades really hard on her papers and I got a 75 on my first one!! But if you just go in and talk to her face to face she tells you EXACTLY what she wants if you ask! THEN YOU GET AN A!!!! She is super interesting in class and made me laugh every day! Take Dr. Sanders, she gets a bad rap!!

At first Dr. Sanders can be a little intimidating, but she is actually very nice and helpful. There are several papers, and each of the Analytic ones get a rewrite. Talk to Dr. Sanders about the re-writes- it really helps your grade! Shes great about being available and is always helpful. Really good class- you just have to work for a good grade

You can't please Sanders on papers.  No matter what you say or do she won't be happy.  I prayed that her grading helper (Daniel) would be nicer, but he's just as bad!  He gave me a lower score on my second essay.  Both mark everything up just so you have to rewrite the paper, but don't expect a higher grade!!!

Dr. Sanders is by far the worst teacher i have ever had. I came to the class extremely excited because it was my favorite subject, and left hating it.My papers all recieved C's and on my paper rewrites, after i corrected what she marked wrong, I GOT AN EVEN LOWER GRADE! she offered me no help when i went once a week to her office either.

I would NEVER take one of her classes again! I took the course because I was actually interested in the subject, but it has been such a disappointment. She knows her stuff but sometimes I come out of the class wondering if she even told us anything important. For the first half of the semester I learned more from the readings than her lectures!
She was a pretty good teacher, but she grades like a Nazi on the three analytical papers

She is an great teacher, she loves what she teaches and shows it. A very smart woman. Attendenc is manditory. You have to write two paper and you will not get higher than a B. You can rewrite your papers and you should, your first grade on it will be a 70. You have to be a STRONG writer to get an A or high B in the class.

She is lively and will keep you entertained in class, but SERIOUSLY, watch out for her grading. She is an extremely hard grader. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DON'T PLAN ON GETTING HELP ON PAPERS...because you'll need it. Be prepared to fail papers, and then get help as you rewrite them later.

Dr. Sanders is a very intriguing and charismatic person. The class mainly consists of writing papers. WARNING she is a VERY hard grader. I put a lot of time and effort into my papers and the best I ever made was 75.

Great prof but not an easy class at all.  If you want the easy A don't take it but if you're looking to learn and improve in your writing then she's the one.  I would gladly take her again.  You'll leave her class exhausted but intelligent!!!!

This teacher knows her stuff, but she is not a good teacher. It's impossible to make an A in the class. I was a 4.0 student until I decided to take this course with her. Be aware that Dr. Sanders is an extremely hard on grading, be prepared for F'S, C'S, and D'S. She lets you rewrite the papers but that turns out terrible. Be careful!

Dr Sanders was awesome!  I have never worked so hard for an A in my life!  She is amazing, though, because she teaches you to think deeply about history.  If you want to LEARN history, rather than MEMORIZE history, TAKE DR SANDERS!!!

Big mistake to take this class. I am a history major and I hated it. She does not teach and the whole class is a  waste of time. The papers are super hard. Be prepared for an F on every one. She has unreal expectations. If you are thinking about her, RUN!!
No way would I take Sanders again.... She knew her stuff pretty well but she graded like the devil. I found it difficult to understand her expectations.

Now I might be wrong, but teachers are supposed to teach.  Dr. Sanders gives you huge reading assignments, makes discussion questions due every Sunday afternoon, then puts all impetus on the students to ask questions because she only lectures half the time (the rest devoted to "group discussion" which I found counter-productive).
Papers are not that hard. She gives you the chance to rewrite the papers and that is really cool. The quizzes are easy and they make help you a lot at the end.

Stay away!! Unless you like to write a lot and you like getting Cs on every paper no matter how many people you get to edit it and no matter how much time you spend on it!  She thinks she created English literature or something!! Run..

Claire Sanders is an excellent professor. She is very knowledgable about her material and she is very passionate about what she teaches. But if you are on scholarships that require a decent GPA, steer clear of this class. This woman will jack you up when it comes to the papers..and that is all you do in this class. WRITE PAPERS..it sucks. Run away.

Dr. Sanders likes to feel in control, and does this by making you feel like you're learning things, telling you you'll be fine if you're diligent, and then screwing you over on papers.  If you thought you were a good writer, she'll make you feel differently.  Trying to keep a 4.0? Don't take Dr. Sanders.
Papers are graded too hard, but she is interesting in class. I am not sure how much I have really learned though.
No Comments

I'll admit, Dr. Sanders knows her history. That you cannot contend with. However, what I never got about her are her papers. She says at the beginning of class that this is a hard class that requires alot of effort, but damn, that's an understatement! My paper average was a 74 on and I used help.

Dr. Sanders is a wonderful professor. She made me actually enjoy history. As for her papers, she grades hard but she tells you what she wants. If you listen and pay attention you will do fine. I definitely reccommend her!

the papers are very difficult and she grades very hard b/c she doesn't explain what she wants which is a "perfect paper"...don't take her unless you know how to write papers EXTREMELY well...a C's not too hard to pull off

she is a great professor and a good lady but when a TA grades the papers, you are sure to get c's and d's. Even if the professor says something word for word and you use it in your paper, the TA will count it wrong. Its really frustrating, but im glad its almost over. Very interesting class to take.
great prof.  very hard though.  take it if you love to see ROTC kids get shot down.  its awesome!

Great Professor. She articulates her points very well, and is very clear. However, she does grade papers very strictly. Be ready for C's and D's on the first few papers. I don't know anyone that did better than that for at least the first few papers.

Great information, the way she presents it is not always cronological or topical. Wishes desperately that she was an English professor and a History professor. oh and there is nothing wrong with passive voice.

Her papers are terrible. She asks for your opinion and when you give it, you are wrong.Then if you document other historians they are "wrong." You can do rewrites but you wont get anything high than a C. Her list of do's and dont contradict English rules 33 to be exact. She's a BIG hypocrit as well.
Will teach you to write, think deeply, read. No tests, but have to perfect papers. Knows her stuff.
Take this class if you have a deep desire to hate your life. Her and the assistant loved to bury you under papers. She loves to count off for the most specific and ridiculous things.

This class rocked my socks off because there were no tests. There is A LOT of writing, but you get second chances on all but one of your papers, so you can always improve on a paper if you don't do so well. Dr.Sanders is fun & casual..I loved her!
She insists on good use of the English language.  However, you get many chances to revise and improve your grade. If you can't write, you won't make an A.  Quit complaining!
Wonderful Professor!!  No tests, all Essays.  Is a hard grader but a delightful person. Take all of her classes.

OMG NO TESTS. 9 papers though. make sure to get a good group or you are screwed. MAKE SURE TO WRITE IN ACTIVE VOICE, she will kill any paper in passive, her grades can be skewed depending on the topic you write about.

i had her for honors western civ... the class was hard, but then it was supposed to be.  i learned a tremendous amount, and i loved her class.  she was absolutely phenomenal.  comes highly recommended.

Very nice, funny, and helpful, she will check your papers for you before you turn them in. Only problems: Get stuck with a bad group and you're screwed. And I just hate her insistence on active voice.
All you people complaining about Dr. S need to grow up and learn the English language.  We are not in highschool. Go to the writing center if you can't figure out passive voice. Dr. S rules!
All you do is write papers and aher class discussions have nothing to do with the topics for the papers! Don't take this unless you really like history and really like writing papers!! It sucks!

No tests in this class, but you have to write a zillion papers and go through BORING class discussions.  She pretty much sucks as a teacher, and worries aboutEnglish/Grammar more than history.  Don't take her unless you have a hell of alot of free time.

Biggest **** of a professor....Doesnt grade your papers, has her misinformed and  TA grade them and half the time she doesnt know what the hell she is talking about. Appears to be nice but then is a **** about grading her papers and you will get a C.

I absolutely adore Dr. Sanders! I fought harder for my A's in her classes than in any other class ever.  She's the kind of prof that you curse the entire time you're in the class but absolutely adore afterwards!  TAKE HER!  But expect to work.
Dr. Sanders is a really neat instructor- I recommend her because she is personable AND because she is great at what she does- teaching the material in a fascinating way.
Nice lady, very very very bad class.  If you want to take a history class, do not take this class.  If you want to take an english class, take this class.

very very good teacher, definently knows everything about history you would want to know. the only thing is she is such a hard grader, and her classes should really count for an english credit. group papers also suck. but her vast knowledge is refreshing.
Teacher is very tough in grading.  Wonderful teacher but nearly impossible to get an A.  Grades like a hard English teacher.

if you do not like to write, do not take this class...the discussions are interesting, but the group gets real old and sometimes frustrating...she's very helpful and makes history come alive...you get out of it what you put it
Tons of reading, but you don't have to do it because there are no tests. No real motivation to learn. Class is purely discussion, which can get old. Very picky on papers. Lots of group work.
Should we also get an English credit for this? Oh, make sure you dont use the passive verb tense
She is one of the best at TCU.
A ton of reading in her class, and has extremely high expectations for papers.
Focus is on learning, not grades, test, or stupidity.
Used to like him but he can be very rude and short with students. Easy A but his attitude makes it hard to like the class. I think he a good teacher but just isn't nice to students.
Great proffesor if you have to take Marketing Management take Dr. Corbit. He is highly insperational and focuses heavily on real word applications.

Class is honestly a joke, but he makes a 150-person lecture engaging. As long as you get the tedious assignments done, you will learn a lot and get a free A. Tests are easy, he is just very harsh if you miss deadlines, but on day 1 he says if you do not get an A, it is because you forgot about the class, and that is true.

He makes the class super engaging and never feel long. I feel like I took a lot away from the class besides marketing. Class is not a hard work load WHATSOEVER so idk what those other comments are saying. All you have to do is show up and a study a little bit for the test.

Corbit is very chill... Exams are in-class w/lockdown. "Pop" quizzes every lecture, except they're non lockdown and mainly used to incentivize going to class (iClicker but didn't use it). Big project that if you try and turn in on time will recieve an A. So many "easy points" (go to class!) that if you get an 80 on every exam you'd end with an A.

I am sure Corbit wrote the positive review here. His class is truly easy if you show up, but god forbid you miss a day, even if you email him he will not let you retake or have another chance to make your grade. Luckily a couple misses wont hurt, you'll have 100 assignments all with random points.  He is constantly preaching throughout class.

Easy A. However, Corbit is not a good teacher. He is clearly just a retired preacher. class is a waste of time. Get ready to do meaningless assignments, like interviewing on LinkedIn, as well as talking to chat bots that HE makes on chatGPT. His "passion" someone mentioned, is a mask that covers his ego.

Best professor I've ever met and taken at TCU. Genuine care for students success and comes to class EVERYDAY with contagious energy. He created the best class environment I've ever been part of. You can physically see his passion for what he does shine as he teaches. Best professor but even better human.

The class is easy, you just have to show up and do the random assignment once a week. Sitting through lecture can be boring since you can only listen and not be on technology. Dr. Crawford is a nice guy, but he stresses me out with the way he talks about everything. Like everything is impossibly hard.

Professor Mathew Crawford is not a bad teacher, but he assigns a lot of work for a one-credit pass/no-pass class. Assignments are weekly and due before class, though they're fairly easy and take about 30–60 minutes. He's approachable and very helpful for academic and career advice.

Dr. Crawford is very caring and wants the best for students. He gives great advice one-on-one for anything academic. His lectures are long and a bit tedious at times but the class overall is extremely easy, just show up and do the weekly assignment. Attendance is mandatory and electronics are not allowed for class. Overall an awesome guy!
Easy class and a great professor. He really cares for his students and tries to make the class entertaining.
most boring lectures ever bc u just sit there and listen to him talk without technology. but super easy u just do an assignment every week and ur good

This class was extremely boring and was at such an inconvenient time. Peak study time and the night before all the chem quizzes and exams. The lectures were so contradicting and just made you want to drop more than the tough classes like chem and bio. He also wouldn't respond back to emails and was overall really confusing.

This was a pass/fail class, so pretty easy. Attendance is MANDATORY. He was prepared and laid back, and provided lots of useful information. However, the course can be discouraging if you aren't completely set on pre-med. The required book is a very sad read and slightly disheartening. Very easy, good resources-just prepare for the discouragement.

His lectures are relatively boring. He is sometimes funny, but the class itself is not engaging. Requires phones to be away but is an easy grader and tries to help out. Attendance is very much mandatory and makes you scan a QR code and counts seats. I would avoid this class since it's a waste of time if you know things about the pre-health track.

Pretty boring lectures and attendance is mandatory, but he is a very funny guy who does care about his students. He is very helpful with information about pre-health careers and I would take another class taught by him.
Participation is mandatory, lectures are light and easy. Sometimes, they can have mood swings. CANNOT take jokes. Aside from that, nice guy
Nice guy who gives lots of info regarding pre-health and boring lectures but can be helpful in future endeavors. It's P/NC, and I would take another one of his classes.
Easy class, attendance is mandatory but if someone sends you the attendance you dont have to go. Boring lectures, but nice guy very helpful. One assignment per week, hard to do bad in this class.

Dr. Crawford is amazing. The lectures were fabulous and he truly cares about motivating pre-health students on the right track. Even after switching out of pre-health, these lectures were applicable to so many other courses and majors. Always brought in guest speakers. Little homework. Don't miss more than 4 classes or you will not receive credit.

Dr. Crawford is pretty chill. Lectures can be a bit boring but informational. There's only a few assignments which are easy. Just make sure you have no more than 4 absences or you won't get credit. Good intro to pre-health class.

Took Intro to Pre Health with Professor Crawford and it was very interesting and easy. He gives great advice regarding further advancement in the medical, dental, PA field. Overall, this class is not for a grade but attendance is mandatory. Take him!
The class itself isn't hard and the homework is VERY easy but his lectures are not the best. He is kind of on the negative side and can sound a little discouraging so good luck keeping your major.

Dr. Crawford really inspires his students and prepares them for the future. He gives advice on what to expect as a pre-health student and is very lenient with assignments. He understands that the first years of college are difficult, but motivates everyone to try their best. He is super funny in class and makes his lectures entertaining.
Lectures are confusing and she refuses to slow down for better understanding. If you go to office hours, it is hard to ask her questions as there are many students just chatting there.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please take Dr. Fry instead

She's really great, it's a hard class but she makes it better. Regarding the comment below mine that's a sad situation however and abuse should go through the dean of students not through professors themselves. There are safeguards in space to protect students
She totally ignored my efforts to communicate with her about abuse when I was in a dire situation. Her teaching methods could use a review.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: May the odds be ever in your favor 🫡
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Whatever the person below me said, they're %10000 right.

This class genuinely made me lose all confidence as a student. Drop rate and fail rate was exceptionally high, even for students who studied hard for exams. Professor is condescending and does not provide an adequate amount of time, or preparation for exams and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You need to know chemistry WELL before taking this class. She goes so fast, does not explain super well imo, such hard tests, and the average will be like a 65% and she'll say thats good. My friend stayed in the class and she said drop rate was around 70%. Her office hours are crowded so don't expect to talk to her about anything privately

Dr. Heidi Conrad is a great and approachable professor who truly cares about her students. She may seem rushed after class due to back-to-back lectures, but during office hours she is relaxed, supportive, and very helpful. She encourages questions, gives exam hints, and creates a welcoming learning environment.

Dr. Conrad is so sweet. Gen Chem is so difficult at TCU, but it's definitely manageable if you put the effort in and don't psych yourself out. Dr. Conrad wants you to succeed, so go to her office hours and always attend lecture!

She's very passionate when it comes to chemistry; however, I don't think that her teaching style is the best for me. There's a lot of information to learn and she sometimes over complicates simple topics, which might make it harder to pass quizzes/exams, but if you're a determined learner then I think you'll do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's an amazing professor and wants you to succeed, it isn't her fault the material is hard and there's a lot of it. Super kind and forward, does not have any effs to give. I recommend getting a tutor for the class.

If you're taking pre-med at TCU, get ready. The program is extremely difficult and unwelcoming, largely due to the chemistry + biology programs. As a high achiever who was no stranger to lots of studying, this course was IMPOSSIBLE. Drop rate was over 50%, and most of the class will not pass. Tests/exams every week, and with a strict time limit.

She's nice and cares about her students, but her teaching style does not fit me. She goes super fast during lectures and sometimes overcomplicates simple topics. She also doesn't stop to let students write things. Do not take this class if you have struggled heavily in chemistry before. Office hours are decent but have a lot of students.

The NICEST professor ever! She can be intimidating at first in lectures, but she loosens up after the first couple weeks and then she becomes very approachable. She's very real with her students and doesn't sugarcoat and make you feel dumb. TAKE HER GEN CHEM CLASS
Genuinely everything we were supposed to study for the exam and quizzes, rarely actually popped up on them. Sometimes it feels like she turns the most simplistic topics into complex shot.

Amazing professor for general chemistry, she is extremely caring and approachable during and after class. Tests are straightforward and the textbook is not required, is helpful for practice questions but she posts a ton of practice for outside of class (Not for credit)

Great lectures and lab sessions. It's a lab class, you are all on your own. Accuracy matters a lot, and little can be done since you have one chance for each lab. Helpful inside and outside of class, though her office hours are always full of students from other classes she teaches that you usually have to wait 15 mins before asking anything.
very hard class done by a very straight forward professor. Tests can have many curveballs which are not shown in any example problems

If you're taking chem at all, I'm sure it's required for your major, and you don't have much of a choice. There are not many professor options for Chem here, and she's definitely the nicer, more lenient option, however, the way the class is done here, it's going to be hard regardless of who's teaching it. She talks fast. Test heavy. Drops one exam.

Dr. Conrad is the best!!!!! Gen Chem at TCU sucks regardless of your professor, but if you're willing to put in the work and go to office hours it's manageable. Dr. Conrad is so willing to help you as long as you ask. She has video modules on everything so WATCH THEM! They are lifesaving especially if you miss class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Conrad was a great professor, her class is difficult but she is a better choice than Fry. She tries her best to help you and explain and has helpful TA's, her office hours are not very helpful. You will not use the textbook don't buy it.

Dr. Conrad is very kind and truly cares about her students. The material is a lot, especially if you have never taken AP Chem before, but it is doable to make a good grade with lots of effort and practice.

I truly only got a C in the class (Gen Chem 1) because I bombed the final (was sick). She's funny and explains concepts well. In lecture she talks really fast, but if you can't catch something she says, she has YouTube videos online. The classroom was flipped, but she makes sure to go over those videos' content in class. Finally, GO TO LECTURE!

The best chemistry teacher ever as a freshman. She is super caring and explicitly says what's going to be on exams. Every lecture is online and there is previous quizzes/exams from other years. Go to office hours and she will know you by name and grade your stuff early. Class super hard but she makes it accessible - GO TO OFFICE HOURS.

Dr. Conrad is an amazing teacher! She genuinely cares about all of her students and wants them to succeed. She understands that the course is hard, so if you go to her office hours she is willing to help. The class has quizzes every week, and while they can be annoying, they make studying for the exams a lot easier.

She was sweet but lectures were extremely rushed she would cram a bunch of material into each lecture. She offered a lot of resources with vids and past exams to practice with. There are timed quizzes every week that are hard, rushed, & weigh a lot on your grade. The class started out so full TAs had to sit on the ground to only half of the class.

I took Gen Chem 2 Lecture and lab with Dr. Conrad, she was amazing at teaching everything even a hard concept but that is because she suit my learning style with the flipped classroom style. She has Youtube videos on all her lecture ppwt points which SAVED me so much. Always prepare before class and do lot of practice problems, earn your grade!

Dr. Conrad is very knowledgeable, but this class was a bit of a mess. Lab lecture felt rushed, the quizzes were hard, and office hours are so packed it's hard to get your questions answered. I will say, she is very generous with partial credit and fixing TA's grading mistakes. Lots of extra credit and if you get to know her she will help you out.

Started off the semester with new software and had many issues across the class making you redo many things. Class isn't impossible and can sometimes be easy but some lab reports take 3 hours while others take 1. 10 labs plus a practical (very easy). Pre lab quizzes in class are difficult but aren't worth much. Along with an online final exam.

Dr. Conrad is hilarious and very warm which makes the level of difficulty of the course much more manageable. She has plenty of grace and will reopen assignments because she really does want her students to succeed.

Dr. Conrad is an amazing teacher! She loves her students & wants them to succeed. She will not answer any emails you send! Office hours are crowded beyond belief and takes about an hour to answer any question you may have. She speaks fast but listen to her youtube vids and do as many problems as you can! Do NOT get behind it is hard to catch up!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pay attention during lectures and you will be fine. Always go to her office hours!! She is so nice and will get to know you which makes learning chemistry less intimidating. Lowest test grade is dropped by the final which is very helpful for grades

Dr. Conrad cares about you and your wellbeing as a student, but at the same time, it is very difficult to reach her when you are struggling with her class or something outside of the class that is impacting your work. The class is only quizzes and tests, so make sure you STUDY!

Dr. Conrad is extremely intelligent and a very good professor. Although Chemistry can be hard, she is very helpful for answering any questions you have, and is also very encouraging. The class itself is demanding and challenging, however, if you want to succeed and put in the work you will do well.
I had Dr. Conrad for Chem Lab. She always lets class out early. She uses so much of her time to help us. She never makes you feel stupid. I highly recommend her for Chem Lab

Dr. Conrad is kind, loving, and good at her job. She teaches a HARD chem course, and she knows that. But she will at least try to help you through it as much as possible. I wish I could have her for CHEM II instead of Dr. Fry, but it switches which classes they take from year to year.
She pre-recorded her lectures so you can go back and watch, but since she pre-recorded she doesn't explain much in class anymore. Tough class if you're new to Chemistry.

Dr. Conrad is such an sweet person and she genuinely has so much care for her students. You HAVE to put in lots of time and practice or you will not succeed in this class. Tests are EXTREMELY hard. The point she is trying to test is if you UNDERSTAND chemistry and the procedures not just how to do the problems. Go to office hours, she will help!!

Absolutely killed my dream of being a scientist. She is a very sweet woman but it is impossible to get extra help from her since she is always packed during office hours. You have to take your notes in advance otherwise you will not be able to comprehend anything with the speed that she talks at in class. Only a genius can pass this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Conrad is a precious angel. She has so much time open for office hours and is always accessible. Go to class, participation matters. WATCH ALL OF HER VIDEOS, and especially the additional practice videos to pass the quizzes. TEST are hard, so hard. Chem is hard, so hard. Stay on top of the work and I promise you can pass. U HAVE to study weekly
Great professor for chem and makes the subject as easy for students to understand as possible. Works to make sure students learn and will do her best to get you through the class.

Dr Conrad is definitely one of the best professors. While there are times where the content being taught is difficult she always explains it clearly to make sure you understand it. Her lab lecture is no problem. I highly suggest going to her office hours not just to work on the content. She rewards hard workers with better grades. Take her
Best prof I have ever had, she generally understands her students and does everything possible to help you be successful.

If you got Dr. Conrad you really lucked out, she is the best professor I've had and is hilarious. Not only does she care about your grade she also cares about you as a person. She creates amazing relationships with her students. If you have any choice to take Conrad DEFINITELY DO IT. She is super understanding when extenuating circumstances come up

Only Gen Chem Lab instructor, and honestly that's great. She has a great sense of humor and personality that shines through class. She is the easiest professor to talk to, and going to her hours will really show her you care and she'll like you more honestly. The TAs run each lab, but she (with Fry for lect) gives you the material. 10/10 teacher!!

There is a significant amount of reading required outside of class. Dr. Layne Craig is very kind and approachable, but she is also a strict grader when it comes to assignments. Her classes are heavily lecture-based, and this is not a course where you can simply sit back and breeze through. Expect homework and reading on the regular.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It is a very easy class. You have to do readings but they are not difficult. The only issue with her is that she gives high school teacher vibes and cares soo much about attendance and participation. She doesn't want anyone to be on their computers or phones or leave class early. But the tests and quizzes are straightforward.

Took Literature and Medicine, and all I can say is I am very happy for it to be over. She is a good professor, but a little all over the place and it does not feel like any answer you give is ever good enough. The amount of reading outside of class you have to do is absurd, and there are quizzes every week on it. Only 2 exams, and 2 presentations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Layne is very progressive and the class reflects that, however, she is very engaging and the material that is covered is very interesting. While there is a lot of reading, its not very hard because a lot of it is fiction and is discussed in class. Majority of grade comes from quizzes and one major group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: love Layne, she's a WOKE woman hah. Overall, as a teacher she's great. TBH this class is very heavy on reading; make sure to stay on top of reading due dates & participate in discussions. I will admit, at times, I feel she's biased; she looks for specific answers. I do question the fairness of her grading sometimes. I recommend and I'd take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr Craig is a very nice person that cares about her students and makes it very clear about what she expects in her writing assignments. She is a rather tough grader when it comes to writing assignments and presentations, but she is willing to discuss feedback with you. If you are a good writer and enjoy it I would highly recommend.

She is a lovely professor, however there is a lot of reading and tons of group work- if that's not your thing, don't take the class. Otherwise, I think she is very intelligent and caring. Also flexible about absences and missed work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Craig is a very good professor if you care about literature. I don't enjoy literature classes, so I didn't enjoy the class, but if I had to take it again I would have her as my professor. Utilize her office hours! She is a very tough grader, so study!

Dr Craig made this class awful for no reason. She as a person is very moody and honestly just rude. She makes you feel stupid for asking a question in class and assigns up to 150 pages of reading and then quizzes you on it. If your looking for a easy/straight forward class this isn't it.

She is very moody and pushes her political beliefs on people. With the outcome of the election she has been extra cranky. lots of busy work. Even if you do the reading she will make you feel like you didn't. I would not take this class again just because it was annoying. Relatively easy if you are good at bsing the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's a pretty nice lady, but sometimes she is a bit moody. There were alot of required books for this course (literature and medicine) so be ready to buy quite a few. Overall, good course that provides alot of insight especially for nursing/bio majors, lots of quizzes though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: overall just did not love her as a teacher, she puts a lot of her own political views and pushes them onto you in the class so be prepared to answer based on what SHE thinks NOT what you may think. Any time I would ask a question she would make me feel dumb for even asking in the first place She made this hard for no reason Better options available
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I do like Dr. Layne, I just don't like her class. Seems like a lot of busy work and she rambles for the full class period. She is nice, wants to help, and gives great feedback on assignments. It isn't a terrible or super hard class, I just wouldn't take it if I could go back. If you have to take this class its not THAT bad otherwise avoid it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Craig was very good in my opinion. If you go to class and take notes the whole time you are almost guaranteed a good grade on the quizzes. Only a couple papers assigned. She is very helpful if you go to office hours. I dislike english classes, but Literature and Medicine added a fun twist to reading and I never dreaded going to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I hated going to her class!!! She makes you wear mask and if it's not on right, she will call you out. She's a very unfair grader and you never really know what she's looking for. Don't forget to read the readings before because she is not afraid to call you out and make you answer her questions. Test are open note and lectures are very note heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Craig is a nice lady and the class is very manageable.The grade is mostly quizzes, papers, and 2 tests. Be prepared for a lot of reading though. Attendance isn't required but is helpful for the quizzes and such.Class is mostly discussions with some lecture and participating occasionally will make her like you. Definitely a hard grader on papers.
very pleasant and flexible. lots of readings. people take and post notes. exams are open note and lots of group work but attendance is not mandatory
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is very unfair with her grading and doesn't give feedback on the exams. At least half of each exam is free-response and she is very biased on what students she gives a good grade to. I don't plan on taking another class from her. Beware that you have to teach yourself, she gives readings but doesn't teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: super sweet just a lot of reading and all those readings are on the exams so you are basically teaching yourself that topic by readying the articles she gives. does a couple of lectures but most of them aren't heavy or useful for the articles its just facts. a lot of group work based off the reading articles

She seems like a caring person, but her grading and teaching didn't teach me anything. She has you read 2-3 articles before each class and you discuss in a group, besides that she presented maybe 5 slide shows all semester. She lets you teach yourself with the readings. Also bewared of hard and unfair grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Odenwald is one of my favorite professors! He cares so much about his students - he actually put in the effort to get to know us and asked us for our feedback throughout the semester. He connected all of his lessons to relatable + real life ideas that made it easier to learn. Attendance was mandatory-ish (but you get 7 skips). 10/10 recommend

Professor Odenwald cares about each one of his students. He gives many opportunities to improve grades along with corrections on essays. He knew each one of his students personally and was dedicated to helping each person in the room. I was someone who struggled in English and Professor Odenwald helped me engage and learn throughout the year.

Very easy class with a very nice professor, would definitely recommend having him as a professor. work was always easy with nice feedback for every assignment. Also gave a generous amount of time to complete each assignment.

Odenwald is the goat. He's new to TCU but is a super cool guy who makes class fun. He never said attendance was mandatory but everyone shows up because it's such a fun class. Projects were fun and you can do them on whatever you want. Take his class 100% freshmen. No tests no quizzes. Very lenient with turn in dates as well.

If you are an incoming freshman and are looking for a good English that you are required to take for Neeley. Take Prof Odenwald. Super easy class. There are four projects the last one being the final. He gives you ample time to work on these during class. I have found him to be a super easy grader and a very chill, down to earth Prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: THE BEST. TAKE HER. she was always so helpful, cheerful, and made learning really easy. would always be willing to explain things and quiz you whenever you needed to!

She simply just is too smart and doesn't know where to draw the line on topics when we are literally freshmen nursing majors. She's super nice and I love her as a person but she makes anatomy way too difficult and is not super organized and ends up having to cut content out of literally every unit bcuz she runs behind

I took A&P 1, I did not study or read to the extent I should have. My own choices led me to struggle a lot, so i had to drop the course but what i will say is Crenshaw is such a beautiful person who truly has the heart of an angel. She was so kind and encouraging. She really is the most amazing teacher who is passionate about her work. TAKE HER!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Ms. Crenshaw really loves what she teaches. I was struggling throughout the semester, but I constantly went to her office hours, and she always provided encouragement/advice. Honestly, I think she saw how much I tried in the class and went to see her which she prevented me from failing. A&P is hard regardless which professor so use your resources.

A&P is hard, and sometimes harder than it has to be at TCU. Crenshaw is the best! Literally! She is the sweetest, most welcoming professor I have had on campus. Attendance is mandatory and she tracks it with iClicker. Exams are hard, but quiz and iClicker questions are often reused. Don't count on them - know your content and you will be fine.

She is the most educated professor I have ever had. You can throw any question at her and she'll have an answer. She is very good at explaining tough topics. Her tests are definitely very difficult, but she gives you all of the information needed to do well. As long as you put in the work, you will be okay.

Take her!! She knows her class is hard, so she is always reachable and wants you to succeed. When she sees the class is confused or there is a hard topic, she stops the lecture and takes the time to write it out IN DEPTH. She may rush toward the end of a unit, but just for a class. When she does, the material ends up being removed from the exam.
Had her for lecture, she wants you to succeed! If you are not doing well go into office hours and she will help you, but you have to go in don't show up at the end of the year show her your trying.

Mrs Crenshaw is by far the best professor I have ever had. I had Wallace for AP I and Crenshaw for AP II and with Mrs Crenshaw my grade has boosted so much! She is so caring and is very good about making sure each out her students understand the material. She explains everything in modern terms so it's easier to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: LOVED Mrs. Crenshaw. She is the most caring professor I've ever had and she has such a heart of gold. Yes the class itself is difficult since it's a prereq for nursing but she explains everything thoroughly and answers every question. She usually got behind on lectures but she would take content off the exams which was helpful.

Great Professor; you could tell she was one of those professors who's passionate about what she taught. Her D2L is very well-organized and structured. My only complaint is that she struggles to get through all the slides or material, which leads to her rushing and not learning the material well. However, I can't blame her; there is much to cover.

I REALLY LOVE HER. Her lectures are so easy to follow, but she often rushes at the end so there are several things you have to learn by yourself. Exams are so easy unless you study, they are 100% what is shown on the lecture slides. This class is kinda tough, but if you work hard and figure your learning techniques, it's a manageable A
very lecture heavy and doesn't stay on track at all so you end up teaching yourself everything and end up behind every other teachers sections
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yes, this is a hard class and you will have to dedicate the time to study but that is for all professors teaching this course. She is very passionate about the material and will take the time to ensure that her students understand the concept. She is very caring and understanding and will move material onto the next test if she did not go over it.

I absolutely love Crenshaw. I'm just finishing up her A+P. I'm not going to lie, her class is difficult, but if you put in the work and time then you will succeed. I study a lot and I'm ending with an A. She has amazing lectures and she is one of the nicest professors I've ever had. She wants you to succeed and cares about her students. Take her!

I had Professor Crenshaw for both the lab and lecture, and I loved her. She's very knowledgeable and you can tell she loves what she teaches. She responds to emails quickly. This class was tough though. Tons of memorization, test heavy, lots of reading necessary to pass, and the labs were brutal. Great professor just a tough class overall.

This lab was very difficult. It starts with an overview powerpoint and gets long and boring, though it is helpful. Then, it's mostly self study on the models and asking questions when you need help. The quizzes at the end can be either easy or hard depending on how well you know and which parts you studied (only 5 questions.) Lots of memorization!

Mrs. Crenshaw is an amazing and knowledgable professor. Her lectures are very informative, but are packed full of information and you need to pay attention to do good in the class. Her tests are very similar to the iClicker questions in class and she does a good job preparing for the tests. Fill out the learning outcomes. Go to office hours!

Ms. Crenshaw one of the nicest & most caring TCU professors. She is very thorough in explaining things & goes into great detail for the lab. But her lecture is very disorganized. You have to memorize a lot for exams only for the questions to be completely different from what we focus on in class. It's easy to miss assignments so check D2L everyday!

Absolutely amazing Professor. A lot of people think she's tough but she's just extremely thorough and prepares you very well. She makes the class enjoyable. She has 5 exams, gives you good objectives to complete each week and small online assignments. You do have to study a lot for her exams, they can be challenging but worth it.

I took Professor Crenshaw for lab, and I have to say that she singlehandedly made me want to become a nurse. She is so incredibly helpful and truly wants her students to succeed.
