Fast-paced and lectures the whole class almost every time. No group work. Attendance is not required but necessary. Hard material sometimes. Funny but not everyone thinks so

I took this class for core credit and it was pretty easy as long as you just go to class. If you go to class, he will give you extra credit for participation and you don't need to study for the midterm/final beyond your class notes. Some topics were confusing for me but there are crash course videos that can clarify.

Good professor. Lecture based class and he writes out what he is saying on the board so you can take good notes. It is not an easy A if you don't try, I mean its college you gotta try. He really wants you to learn and is always answering questions you have. For term papers he gives you 3 week's advance notice and helps you with your ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: By all means, do not take this professor. If you don't write word for word what he says for tests he will give you a bad grade. He is extremely smart but likes to show it off. Loves to degrade anything you say and will make you feel dumb. Go to office hours for term papers. Attendance is not mandatory but you won't pass if you skip class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: You can tell that he is passionate about philosophy, but not teaching. Strictly a lecture class and does not give helpful feedback if he even gives any. Everyone is always lost. Papers are vague and an extremely harsh grader. He's a smart guy but not a quality professor. I would avoid taking another class by him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awful professor. He doesn't care about students and gives terrible feedback on reading responses. He lectures the entire class without stopping to ask if there are any questions. The worst professor I have experienced at TCU. Avoid this teacher at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. JP is a good professor. He makes his class lecture and reading heavy, but he provides class notes where he gives you the important points covered in the lecture. A lot of the topics that require reading in his class can easily be learned on Crash Course YouTube. Although he is a pretty tough grader, he is happy to help you after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class taught me a lot and showed me that I like philosophy. Professor Andrew isn't the best philosophy teacher but he does give insightful feedback on how to write a philosophy paper. Take advantage of his extra credit opportunities. Good luck if you are taking this class! You are going to need it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Avoid Professor Andrew at all costs. He has no sympathy if you miss class, his lectures are heavy, his assignments are all writing, he grades difficult, and his exams are written not online which just makes things more difficult. He talks for an hour and 20 min straight and talks as if it were a graduate course when he should use simpler terms.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is only lecture where it is hard to understand the concepts and take notes because he talks so fast and has no powerpoint and only writes one or two word references to what he is saying on the white board. I did better the last half of the semester by not showing up and teaching myself the material based on lecture notes he posted.

Professor Andrews loves what he teaches and you can tell. It made the class and lectures super interesting, even though it wasnt the easiest class. He gives help when you ask for it though, and will you help you with your papers along the way. If you use the resources he provides, youll do fine. Hes happy to help and clarify any confusion
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I dont know what the rest of these reviews are talking about, JP was genuinely one of the best professors Ive ever had. Hes extremely knowledgeable on the topics, passionate about it, has a dry & witty sense of humor (always cracking jokes), a very fair grader, and has a perfect amount of assignments. Just a few papers and 2 exams. Hes great

One word: Awful. This professor does not care about helping his students. The entire class is confused about the topics while he continues to boost his ego of knowledge during the class. He does not stop mid-lecture to ask if we understand, nor does he further explain topics at signs of confusion. DO NOT TAKE. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Easily the worst professor I have ever had. Not only is the course mostly comprised of papers and exams that contain information completely unrelated to the lectures, but Andrew also seems to intentionally make assignments extremely difficult- almost as if he is hoping that his students will fail. Do yourself a favor and avoid this class.

Do not take this class unless you have to. Unless you absolutely love philosophy, the lectures are extremely long and boring. The only assignments/tests are essays and he grades them harshly. Would not recommend.

His class is just lecturing, and he posts the lecture notes online, so attendance isnt mandatory. It does help to go though. Youre only grades are a few short papers, two term papers, and a midterm and final exam. The grading is fair. He assigns reading before every class, but you dont need to do them unless theyre for a paper.

Probably the worst professor I have ever had. Unengaging lectures, and a complete lack of interest in the well-being of his students as he has a TA grade all assignments and seems entirely uninterested in student's confusion surrounding course material. Seems to get off on demonstrating his intellectual superiority on the subjects covered in class.

Professor Andrews is one of the worst professors I have had. He grades super unfairly and just wants to belittle you to make himself feel smarter. He doesn't give good feedback just tells you he disagrees and that you were wrong. Don't take his class unless you have to.

Professor Andrew may possibly be one of the worst professors in the entire country. He lectures by just sitting in front of the camera and talking for over an hour. There is no way to take any notes, as he does not prepare a slide show or slow down at any point. His grading is awful and he does not care about his students what so ever. Don't take!

Worst professor I have ever had. Does not know how to teach, I did not learn a single thing. Way too hard to be considered an intro class. Had a TA grade all papers, she was way too harsh on non major students who have never taken a philosophy class before. Absolutely terrible, 0/10 recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: As a philosophy minor, I found his material to be easy. HOWEVER, near impossible if you have not taken any class in Philosophy. It was his first time teaching, but I felt belittled often and I'm sure those who have never taken Philosophy felt that to a stronger degree. He enjoys showing he is smart - difficult trait for a professor.

Simply do not take this class. He was an unclear and confusing lecturer. He was often all over the place and made it difficult to understand what we needed to know for the tests. Class was only graded by tests and one essay. Unnecessarily difficult for an intro class.

Do not take this class with Andrew unless you have to. It was his first time ever teaching, but he should not stick with it. Lectures are hard to follow and he does not prepare you for his tests, which are all short answer or essay. 0/10 recommend.

THE BEST. Lots of readings every day, but there are never quizzes in class; you just listen to what she says about the reading and sometimes talk about it in small groups. Only one midterm that was very straightforward, so if you study and read, you will easily get an A+! 100% take this class for somwthing chill and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: LOVE HER!! Very easy class and she's also very understanding, attendance is mandatory, but you get two unexcused absences. No actual textbook but you need books, and then a "textbook" you can get printed at the print shop for $25.

I had Dr. Duncan for UNLF and she is genuinely really passionate about her students and cares. Overall a really nice and understanding lady. She also complained a lot about participation in her lectures. Please participate. She loves it.

Passionate about the subject which helps with morning lectures. Lots of work required to get up to that A. Great for a religion credit but would not recommend if you are taking 15+ hours or have lots of obligations outside of academics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very passionate about the teaching but requires a lot of reading and work outside of class to get an A. Great for a religion credit but would not recommend if you are taking 15+ hours or have many obligations outside of academics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She gives you about an hr of reading and 10 mins of writing for homework each class. She's implemented a new method where you'll receive a B in her class for completing all the required work and in order to receive an A, you have to do an additional hour of reading and 10 mins of writing per class as well. So an extra 3.5 hours of work to get an A.

Get ready to annotate documents on Perusall and make sure they're actually good since the only grades are an A, D or F. The paper isn't too bad she gives a pretty clear outline. Overall the lectures require pretty intense participation and you need to read and be prepared. Quizzes were open note for Maymester, Final wasn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Duncan is very sweet, but the lectures are pretty boring. You can tell that she is enthusiastic about the New Testament, but it is difficult to understand at times. There is a decent amount of work, and the midterm and final are difficult. However, to other TCU students, my advice would be to avoid religion here and take it elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Duncan is a really nice person, however, her lectures are very boring. There were no extra credit opportunities for us so make sure to do well on the 2 exams (midterm & final) and the weekly discussion posts. Overall, Dr. Duncan is very passionate about religion, especially the New Testament!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: An absolute GEM for the religion department! I never previously read the Bible nor had any previous knowledge in Christianity, yet she taught so well I understood everything. You do read from the Bible (the gospels and letters), however, just listen to some audio books on YouTube and you are golden. Planning on taking another class of hers!

I have such a soft spot for Dr. Duncan- she's the best. I took her Women in Early Christianity class, and loved it. Her tests are reasonable, and even if you bomb the tests, there are enough other grades to level out. She is so caring, funny, and super understanding. 10/10 would recommend!

Dr. Duncan is a good professor. She is very passionate about what she teaches and shes always happy to answer your questions. There is a lot of writing though. 2 Exams (Midterm and Final), 2 Essays, Preparation worksheets, Participation assignments, and multiple extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Duncan is an Awesome Prof! Class can be dry, basically depends on your eagerness to learn about the New Testament. However, if you have any questions she is definitely willing to help in her office hours (recommended)! 4 Exams, 3 participation assignments, and extra credit opportunity (if you do all, it will add up to 5% to Final grade)!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't take way better English teachers out there. Save yourself the time before you work hard only to get graded extremely unfairly for no reason at all. Not helpful and often confuses you more when you ask for help. Not saying she's super hard just honestly kind of weird person and there's better teachers out there for this class

Profesor Dukes was an amazing teacher. She really cares for her students, and wants you to do well. The hardest part are the essay exams, but if you review a little a day or two before, you will do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very nice and caring and actually have good feedback, the final wasn't hard at all and she's really nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Dukes is great! She is a very tough grader on her in class essays. However, she gives you a quiz once a week, and when added up they can help your grade if you just stay on top of the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Ms. Dukes is awesome. I took her intro to comp course and she is super understanding and nice. There are 4 projects and 3 RAP's that make up most of your grade. She also lets you re-do projects as many times as you need within a certain period of time(usually around a week or two). You can also argue for a higher grade on your projects.

I took her for Intro to WGST and she was great. Attendance is taken via in class work. She is a super easy grader and there are no tests. Readings due before class are not hard at all. If you try in her class you will do amazing.

Professor Dukes was great. I took her Intro to Women and Gender Studies course. Attendance was mandatory (and contributed to grade a lot), but her lectures always ended early and were interesting. The assignments were quick and she graded easy as long as you put in effort. Easy A course.

I took WGST - women and gender studies class with her. She is so understanding and caring! Her classes are mostly fun/learning activities. No mandatory attendance but she sometimes gives pop quizzes(based on reading). No exam for her final - you have to submit a presentation. Overall I would recommend this class to anyone!

I loved professor dukes, she was very kind and understanding. I took her WGST class and it was really enlightening. There were 5 unit project things and I thought each was very well put together and I had fun doing them. Definitely take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took WGST 20003 with Dukes, but it wasn't listed. I absolutely loved this class, there were quizzes once a week over readings, one assignment at the end of each unit, and our final was just walking around the room looking at everyone's zine. She is so nice and does an amazing job explaining things to her students. A favorite of mine for sure.

I took the intro to fiction narrative medicine class, and I thought it was super easy. Although that being said, I read the reading she assigned, it would take me 45-1 hour before each class of reading. If you do that and study for like 2 hours before each of the 3 tests, you should be chilling. The books were fun, not bad reads. Would recommend

This class has no homework other than reading. Each class is the same by taking a quiz on the required reading and doing a short writing exercise. Ms. Dukes is super nice and is understanding if you are sick or are not feeling well. There are a few books that are required but are fairly easy. Overall, I would take this class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took ENGL20803 Argument and Adaptation. The class was very straightforward and not very difficult. 2 essays over the semester along with weekly reading quizzes. Prof Dukes was really kind and understanding, and she was always very flexible with due dates and attendance. Definitely take this class if you want a fun lit credit!

I am a nursing major. I wanted to take her Introduction to Fiction: Narrative Medicine class because I thought it would be relevant down the line. It was a great class. A lot of time was spent on narrative reflection. I enjoyed the Reflective Writing Responses (RWRs) because they made me connect with the books on a personal level.

I am in her intro to literature class (the theme is magic). I am a business major and I still find the class interesting. It had been a while since I had read literature but she walks you through the process.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was one of my favorites I've taken at TCU. Professor Dukes incorporated a lot of different relevant texts and movies, so it wasn't boring at all. It was an enjoyable class, while still making me a better writer.

Miss Dukes was a lot of fun. She tried to tie in current music to help make the class less boring. She was a little scatterbrained, but in a funny way. Show up to class and participate. It's easy to get an A, but you do have to put in some effort. She also gives good feedback; she want's you to use the feedback, so don't blow it off.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class was challenging but in a good way!
His grades did not make sense. It looked like he graded with AI. Boring class and final was really long for a class about video
Not a good professor. Makes it seem like he cares about teaching and his students but in reality doesn't

This class is extremely demanding and hard to balance with other courses. The live sports show assignment is unclear and rushed, and the expectations feel unrealistic. Think carefully before taking this class.
Great guy! Had him for video production for sports. A tough grader sometimes, and nitpicks a little bit on projects, but his critiques are insightful and I learned a lot from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is an awesome guy. His class was not easy by any means, but he gives great lectures and if you study, his tests are not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Took for a Maymester and really enjoyed this class. You have to read the book and participate in class as well as there being 2 exams as well as a show analysis. But as long as you read the textbook and participate in class you can do well in this class
Taking this class is hard in general but he is helpful with explaining how to do homework assignments. You need to go to class every time because there are a lot of in class projects.

Dr. Hahn is an amazing professor who really cares about his class and every one of his students. He isn't the best lecturer, though. He tends to go on of-topic tangents that don't have anything to do with the power points. Lab attendance is mandatory but after the first few, the labs become more tolerable. Exams are easy enough but you HAVE to read
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are straight out of the textbook, 2 big video projects where one is individual and one is a group project. Not sure if I would take him again - very specific quotes/terms on tests and not the most helpful for those who haven't had video experience before, decent choice but the class itself is pretty boring
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Overall, Professor Hahn is pretty solid for history of broadcasting - one big project but as long as you complete the requirements it's easy to get an A. Each class is spent either presenting or him talking about the chapter. MUST READ THE TEXTBOOK though because he has fill in the blanks with exact words and quotes from the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Hahn made this class boring and hard when it didn't have to be. The labs are incredibly boring and if he sees you using your phone he will take off points for participation. The tests had tons of oddly specific fill in the blank questions. At the beginning of the semester he said there would be reviews for tests but never gave any.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took basic vid with him and I really enjoyed it. He's very interested in his students and helping them succeed. Class overall was pretty easy. It started out with really basic stuff, but  by the end I think I learned a lot. The textbook is easy to read and the reading quizzes are easy as well. No tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Greenhill is a very enthusiastic and fun professor. All of his lectures are things or knowledge you would use in the real world. Super successful guy, great person to learn from

I LOVE GREENHILL. Such an awesome professor and doesn't waste our time or his time with boring lectures. He makes class fun, and the class I took (diversity) was group project-based. He gives great feedback and ensures that everyone succeeds. would take again

Super useful group projects, briefs, audience personas, and a couple of (very easy) exams. He loves using real world examples and his feedback is beyond useful. He knows/loves everything about the industry and is nit picky with each project. As long as you take his feedback and participate you will do well. He is the best and made class so fun!

Take this class! You learn a lot and he has so much real world experience, which makes the lectures interesting. We only had a few tests and they're online. He reviews before them and answers any questions you have.
Great class. Lots of group projects and hands-on work.

LOVED HIM. The assignments that we did were very real world things you would do in the advertising industry. group projects, briefs, audience personas, and a couple of exams. All the assignments you do can all be used in your portfolio so that's super good. He's a clear grader and gives amazing and useful feedback.

Duke is very knowledgeable in what he does and shares his experiences that he has had working for big name brands. The class is a little disorganized with due dates always being changed and assignments given last minute/ no direction. But, I love that he teaches things you will need to know for the real work world.

He is super knowledgeable about advertising and has worked with a lot of big brands. There are quite a few group pitches. I enjoyed the lectures and learned a lot. How he graded things was really confusing and some of the tests in my opinion were not necessary but I ended with an A- regardless.

Duke was one of the best teachers I have had. I took advertising with him and while it isn't an easy A you learn a lot. He's a real professional with lots of experience. His lectures are informative but fun.

Duke is great and super nice, but is rarely there in class. Due dates are always moved around and there isn't a lot of direction or clarity when it comes to projects. All you really do is a few group projects, most of the class is getting you to present well and pitch to clients.

Duke has a ton of experience in marketing, advertising, and PR. One of the most interesting backgrounds I think a professor could have. He is a great guy that is very easy to reach out to. Since I took a senior course he would dedicate some days to just discussing job hunting and how to get your foot in the door. One of the best professors
I loved this class so much and Professor Dunn really made the class. The class was so interesting and totally stress-free. Definitely take this class with her if you need this for credit

I just had professor Dunn for Critical Investigations to Teaching and Learning. She was one of the best teachers I've had my entire life and does a great job creating a sense of community among her students and keeping lectures fun and interesting so that students look forward to class every week. Literally so much fun cannot recommend her enough!

Professor Dunn is easily one of my favorite professors. She is so kind and funny and ensures that the classes are interesting and engaging. The class consists of a few easy assignments, quizzes, two exams, and school observations. She really wants her students to succeed and will work with you. I would 100% recommend you take her class.

If you're just taking this class to fulfill a core requirement... don't. There are much easier FAR courses. There are 4 out-of-class assignments and 3 tests with MC and essays. There is a textbook with assigned reading, but if you don't do it, it won't hurt your grade. Dunn is nice and knowledgeable, but the class is a little dry.
Does not know how to teach. Lectures are awful and only contain photos. Hard grader, I worked super hard in this class and deserved way better than what I received.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Dunn is a really caring teacher. The class is harder than it appears, and she is a tough grader. However, she is very helpful and will meet with you outside of class to help you. Office hours are great. Rubrics are clear. Lectures are long, and skipping class is not a good idea. I would take her again, she is a very caring person.

At this beginning/middle of this course I had a very good grade (low A or high B) and my grade has been significantly dropping ever since. She is a very hard and picky grader with any type of written responses. She lectures very heavy during class and tries to cram a lot into one class section. I take thorough notes but she talks veryyy fast.

I loved professor Dunn! I was a little worried going into the class because of all the bad reviews from the class, but she is honestly the sweetest teacher and has made a lot of significant improvements from the reviews in previous years. All of the tests and quizzes are based word for word on lecture so its essential to take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I loved Lindsey Dunn! You definitely have to study for the tests but if you listen to her lectures and take notes you'll be fine. There are a few reflection papers that are really easy. Great class and I would take it again!

Art history is never an easy class, but at the very least Dr. Dunn makes it really straight forward and doable. Theres a lot of memorization for each test, but thats really the hardest part as long as you take good notes and go to each class. Her class is lecture heavy, but luckily she doesn't have an annoying or monotone voice.

This class is the hardest class I've ever taken. I went to every test and took good notes and had to study for hours for each test. She makes you memorize 60 pieces of art for each test and counts off for small details. If you want an A on the homeworks you better spend hours on them.

Do not take this class for a fine art credit. Probably the hardest class I've ever taken. Requires you to memorize over 70 pieces of art for the final and go on 3 different field trips. She reads her lectures and talks very fast so it's hard to take notes.

This class is real hard. If you're taking it for fine art credit, take something else. There are plenty of different options that are easier, even if they seem stupid.?This is a waste of class time. She requires about 4 field trips to museums towards the end of the semester. I warn you!

Professor Drenner was an excellent teacher. I had him for Contemporary Issues in Biology, and his lectures were very clear and interesting. He is very caring and is passionate about the subject. He is also very easy to approach. I would take him again 100%. 10/10 an excellent teacher and man!

Last semester I had a bad experience with my natural science professor, but this semester was different. Drenner is a great guy who is passionate about teaching and his lectures are amazing. As long as you understand the lecture slides, you will do well in the class. Drenner is also always available to help you in office hours. Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Drenner is great! His lectures are fun and you can tell that he really enjoys what he does. The exams are not hard as long as you pay attention in class and review the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He uses iCliker for participation and in-class questions. It's only 4% of the grade and he drops some questions. He's a good lecturer and the materials flow well. His questions are all multiple choices but are still tricky because all questions have multiple options.

Dr. Drenner taught the first section of Ecology. He's a solid professor, not my favorite, but certainly not bad. The class itself is difficult to get an A in because of some confusing questions on tests, but it's easy to get a B in. Participation counts towards your grade and their are 6 exams total, but the final isn't cumulative which is nice

Drenner is such a precious professor. Go into office hours and he will help you better prepare for exams in general. The lectures were all on powerpoints you could look back to and he had clicker questions that help your grade. The lab is easy and helps too. I did bad on tests but still ended up with a good grade. The info was mostly interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The class is very lecture heavy, but Drenner is a very good lecturer. He keeps you engaged for the most part. The only advice I would give is make sure you know all the material for the tests because the tests are the most difficult part of the class because of the way they are formatted and there is a lot of material.
Interesting course content and very helpful, but his tests are hard!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lectures are very random and boring, but not terrible. He makes the test all "which of the following are false?" and makes you know the smallest, most dumb things from the keynotes.. If you can take any of the other professors, DO IT!

Dr. Drenner taught the first section of Ecology. Ecology is so much easier than intro bio and Dr. Drenner is funny and cute! I liked having him as my professor. Don't think Ecology is a blow off though - relisten to the recorded lectures and the tests cover the extra material the professors put on the powerpoint slides.

The class is pretty interesting. The lab is in the computer lab and just busy work. There are clicker questions at the beginning over readings and at the end over the lecture, so you will have to go to class. The tests are pretty hard, "Which one is false", but  if you study the lectures where you can say them yourself then they are pretty easy.

Not a blowoff class but definitely would recommend for a nat science credit. Lectures can be interesting, attendance is necessary b/c of clicker questions. Tests are HARD but if you study for several hours you should do fine. A definitely possible with effort and Drenner is a very helpful, nice guy.

Great teacher! I highly recommend this class. The power points are pretty self explanatory. He makes the class enjoyable. Curves test grades. Tests are a little tricky but study for about 4 hours the colored notes and take notes on those and you will be fine! Show up for clicker questions. Lab was tedious and boring but good guy.

Comtemp issues is a good class for non science majors! pretty easy class, no real homework except reading short news articles. Class based on lectures and quizzes in class, so attendance is necessary to do well. Topics are interesting enough and explained well. Basically a big picture bio class. Tests can be tricky but an A is possible with effort!

Contemporary Issues in Biology was a pleasant class. Lectures were (for the most part) engaging. Drenner is a good lecturer, although not particularly helpful to struggling students. The coursework is pretty easy, but the tests are tricky ("Which of these statements is false?"). Watch out for the lab, as it's mind-numbing busywork on the computer.

His Contemporary Issues class has been very interesting. I learned a lot of new information that was all somewhat relevant to the real world. Lab is literally in a computer lab, which is a breeze. The tests can be sneaky challenging, but if you study the Powerpoints beforehand, they're feasible.

With absolutely no interest in the field of science, this class is highly interesting and even captivating. He is vague on what material will be on the test but very sufficient studying for the exams, coupled with class attendance (for the daily quizzes) and extra-credit opportunities make this course very bearable.

Okay teacher, tells good stories. though he is very vague when going over the slideshows and what's important information.He gives out a quiz every morning if you are late its a zero. You have to print out articles for homework every night. he does offer extra credit that equals one test grade. test are difficult and he's not very helpful

Great teacher, very easy class. There are articles that you must read before class, and there are  short quizzes that he gives everyday, but they are very easy. For tests there are three statements per question and you must choose the "false" statement, and the tests are very easy. overall good class and professor definitely recommend!!!
Contemporary issues in biology was fun with him. quiz every day 5 minutes into class so show up! Lectures from powerpoints and makes it easy and fun to learn. great prof
great class!im not a huge science fan but drenner has an easy class with interesting material.Kinda liberal but nice guy.Take it!

I hate science & was not looking forward to taking a sci class. However, this has probably been the MOST interesting class I've taken at TCU. Dr. Drennar is very nice & helpful. He is accessible outside of class. Daily readings b4 class, followed by quizzes. Tests are difficult "Which of the following is false?" LAB is harder.

Nice guy. Currently enrolled in summer course. He has changed questions to be easier (thats what he told us on the first day) and it has held true.  Fun material, or at least material we should learn more about as a culture anyways.

Cont. issues in bio which is very interesting but he acts like he knows a lot more than he does, all tests and daily quizzes are pretty tricky because he gives 4 statements and you have to choose the most false. Doesn't provide study guide either.

Contemporary Issues: This class is so liberal it's not even funny. I hated his teaching style and he doesn't seem to know as much as he thinks. Tests were horrible and purpose of format seemed to be to trick you and nothing else. Not that hard though.

He's a great teacher, class is pretty interesting. He's really smart so he can answer most of your questions. Be at class because of the quizzes before each lecture, they really help your grade. His tests are 50 questions which statement is false, so they're pretty hard. Go see him if you have probs. He's really nice & funnny.

Great guy with great sense of humor.  Very knowledgeable & helpful outside of class.  2 question quiz at beginning of every lecture, but easy if you read short article & review last lecture right before.  Tests are somewhat difficult - several questions taken from quizzes, but others can be tricky.  Great class - very interesting & worth it!!

studyy 30 mins before each class and about 4 hours before each test and you'll get an A.  daily quizes that aren't hard if you just read.  easy class and very intestesting.  he is also a really nice guy that wants to help you.  and do the extra credit as soon as you can.
Very helpful and nice professor. Very recommendable. I found his tests to be the easiest of the 5 professors. Great guy, always available in his office.
Dr. Drenner is a great teacher. He knows and loves the material he teaches. The tests are kinda hard, but all the Contemperary Issues classes have the same type of tests.
Weird kind of tests (which one is most false), but he makes class fun and interesting. A very funny guy.
Dr. Drenner is very interesting and quite comical.  He makes class fun!
Great teacher.  He gets a little long winded about fishing.  Study the slides and you are golden!

great guy, knows his stuff, willing to help and while the subject is tough he makes it pretty interesting. Tests are tough(which 1 of 5 is true kinda tests) but if you study the info in every slide he gives you it's easy(sounds harder than it really is)
He is pretty funny and makes a hard subj. interesting and not so bad.  The discussions are helpful b/c they are about current topics that affect our lives.  His tests are hard.

This guy is hilarious. All lectures are on PowerPoint presentations, and he gives a handout of the presentation to everyone, so there is minimal note-taking but make sure you follow along and pay attention. I thought the labs were pretty boring and hard.
well versed in his course, has great office hours if u need help, offers extra credit, has interesting lectures, tests are difficult, study the details
He is a great teacher and always has a story about someone he knows to relate to the topic.  His tests are multiple choice but very difficult.  Study the details of the slide shows.  But great guy!

So funny!  I typed up all of the important things from the slideshow handout to study from and made an A.  Read for details-he loves to take questions from insignificant facts.  Know the material well and you will be fine on the tests.

I had Dr. Drenner for contemporary issues and absolutely loved that class.  Everybody who said his tests are tricky is right on the money--I'm a TCU grad, and his class was my only B in all of college.  But I loved him and loved the class--no regrets.
Very enjoyable class.  Dr. Drenner is an excellent teacher.  Read the handouts and you'll get at least a B.
Class is interesting! but the tests are horrible!! extremely tricky!!!
Awesome class and awesome professor, but the tests are very tricky.  Beware of disturbing slide show depicting the miracle of child birth (close up shot, very gross, needed therapy).
Intro to Contemporary issues is a cool and interesting class. Beware of the tests, the multiple choice he gives are killer. Cool guy otherwise.

He's a very funny man who is always ready to be there to make sure you understand everything.  His tests are harder than you expect.  Definately fought hard for an A, it's an easy B/C if that's what you want.  Labs are all on the computer.
No Comments

Really nice, good sense of humor.  Contemp. issues in Biology was interesting, but the multiple choice tests can be tricky.  I couldn't make an A, but I wound up with an easy B.  The labs are super-easy, too.
No Comments

If you don't want an extremely hard writing class he is the perfect professor. Honestly he gives you a lot of time to write essays and definetly taking him again. Believe me, he is suuuuuuper chill you'll thank me later
For a requires class I think he doesn't do a very good job, and treats his students like middle schoolers
Makes you work but extremely good teacher. Very helpful and flexible in deadlines. Will extend deadlines if you have legitimate reasons. Very helpful

If you work hard and talk to him outside of class time, you will do well. He wants everyone to succeed but won't just give you an A. Take the time to work with him on your papers and you will be rewarded. Go to class. Make sure you cite correctly, because that is one of his biggest focuses. He's a good guy.

He is a great teacher! He will help you out with anything! Even if you need extended time for a paper, he is very understanding! Lots of writing, and he is kind of a tough grader. But you just have to do all of your assignments. He does give opportunity to re-do assignments too!

Awesome professor explains everything and is the only professor for excel that lets you make up certain HW assignments. Makes class fun and again very helpful when it comes to assignments that no OTHER professor for excel does.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Excel is hard to understand but he explains what to do pretty well. Class is pretty boring but I find it useful to hear the lecture. Test are just like assignments without the detailed instructions.
Professor Eaton did an excellent job at sharing real business examples that covered all the course material.

Just looking at her makes you want to go to class, but it is very hard because she gives you the slides and that is all you really need for the lecture. The labs are pointless but the quizzes will screw you if you don't do them. The MC on the test are easy, but she grades the SA and essays more difficult. Offers some extra credit, A is possible.

Gave us a quiz that just asked for your lab teachers name, your name and lab time. Hardly anyone was there and it actually hurt a lot of ppl's grades. Alot of ppl said it was a really easy course, but I heard that department heads heard about the classes being easy A's...so now its pretty hard. I had 3.635 gpa and got a C in here. Tests= vague.

She's really hot. Class isnt too interesting. Didnt want to go often even though she's hot. Labs are boring but I made a 98 in it. She doesnt round grades though, or else my C+ would have been a B. She has a cool +/- System. Gives you a + GPA if you get the +, but doesnt do the - (if you get a B-, she still gives a 3.0, but a 3.3 if you get a B+)

HOT HOT HOT!!! worth taking just to look at her. aside from that, its still not a bad class. i hate science and am really bad at it and made an a. the lab is painfully boring, but they are with a TA. Prof eady does a good job discussing controversial topics without ever being offensive or condescending, and really cares about her students learning.
She only has a good rating bc shes hot. Beware...

If only she knew how to write tests...Lectures kinda helped. I felt like I was on my own in here bc it was so confusing! Good Luck...You will hate this class by the end of the semester. Final is cumulative. Lab also blows!!!
great teacher.  test arent bad and labs arent bad either.  she used to go to tcu and is very underestanding of students and very cool.  take this class.

contemp issues was all right with her. she's a little intense. studying will get you an A or B. She did one pop quiz that really hurt a lot of peoples grades because people usually don't go to class. And there's no place on the syllabus for quizes. Kind of a sneaky move.

Contemp. Issues - I learned a lot in this class! Interesting subject matter. Tests are hard and sometimes worded strangely. Hard A, sorta easy B. She's hot in the lecture hall, and even hotter close up so sit in front :) Lab's easy. Take notes during class --particular questions on exams. If you need a Lab class, just take Nutrition instead.

Eady is a really great prof, not to mention she is a fox. hands down, hottest professor at TCU. Not a very hard class either, i hardly ever went and i still did pretty well. but seriously, global warming is not real.
I LOVE steph!!! Shes the best!!

she is a great professor. not to mention she is young and good looking. she just started teaching but you wouldnt know it. very nice and helpful outside of class. powerpoints are online and she sends out a study guide before every test. she makes lectures interesting and has a sense of humor. one of the best profs i have had so far. GREAT prof!

She was incredibly useful outside of class. Always checks her e-mails. She does study guides before every exam. The only bad thing is there is a cumulative final. Loved the class though! TA's were kinda hard to understand but, the professor was awesome!

At first I was not interested in the class, but it turned out to be very fun. We hardly used the book, beacause she would post lecture notes online. Even if things didn't seem clear in class, her do is always open and is extremely helpful one on one with test (go to her office...trust me). I got an A and we still talk.
she is hot. but she is married :( . her lectures are funny and so is her jokes but be sure to read everything or else you will fail her tests. the lab is fun so show up.

Very cool teacher and accessible outside of class. Tests were somewhat hard, but it is college, a good amount of trick questions. Lab is easy enough, I do enjoy environmental science but professor Eady really made this class easy to attend. Would highly recommend if you're looking to expand or enhance your knowledge environmental science.

She is pretty good. She is young so she tries to make jokes and tries to keep it interesting. All of her power points are on ecollege. Attendance is not mandatory, but it helps for test,but she doesn't take attendance. The Lab is easy, as long as you do well on the quizzes. Just read the manual.

Her tests are hard & tricky, she lectures WAY TOO FAST & doesn't leave enough time for students to ask questions. I would choose another class for NSC or another professor. I fell asleep or got close to it nearly every class and it was at 11am! She is friendly though.

She's new, I'm assuming. Very upbeat and loves the subject. The lectures are nearly identical to the book. Print out lectures before class and take notes on them. It helps! Tests were surprisingly hard, with a few trick questions so read the whole question. Study guides are helpful. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll fail if you don't show up.

Funny guy, and lectures made sense; however, you CANNOT miss a lecture. This class is very difficult, make sure you have plenty of time to study and get extra help. Gives some credit even if you get entire quiz wrong. Thankfully, tests are open-note and computer- but don't think that means automatic A. Ended class with a 41% and got a C.

Ochem is difficult, there is no getting around that, but Dr. Dzyuba makes it bearable. He is very funny and is always in his office if you have a question, literally like 24/7. He gives lots of partial credit when grading and the class has a massive curve, everyone is guaranteed to pass. I would not take ochem lecture with anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very passionate professor, very patient with students. He answers questions outside of office hour and even hosts review sessions before each exam. Class content, i think, is easier than some other professors, though its still pretty standard. The textbook he refers to, mcmurry, kinda sucks though, i personally use klein.
The absolute goat.

I have my MD now, and I am taking the time to write this- so enuff said.  Bad teacher + unreasonable passion for organic chemistry => confused & defeated pre-med student with dreams to be a physician.  Had to retake the class at a different school with a Good teacher + harder workload than Dzyuba, & got an A + found myself liking the subject.

Probably one of the best professors I have had. The amount of time he is willing to take out of his day to help students learn concepts is incredible. When confused I would ask questions over email and he would always give detailed explanations. Insanely hard class but with I professor who will help you succeed if youre willing to put in the work.

By far my favorite professor at TCU. By far the hardest class I have taken in my life. Come to lectures prepared knowing the material already, if not, you will be extremely confused and lost. Dr. Dzyuba loves what he does and truly takes time to help students in office hours, very caring, and very nice. Was very welcoming in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Dzyuba was really helpful outside of class and was always really nice. I felt like I could ask him for help whenever. Don't fear Qual. Lab as much, and make sure you study for the quizzes. Overall, a hard class, but a solid one. Some people find his lecturing isn't their style, but finding online resources helps with that.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a brilliant, super funny, and caring guy but really isn't great at lectures. He loves Ochem and knows it very well, but is super disorganized in lectures. He doesn't cover the lab at all during the lecture period and confuses you when he does. He's very accessible outside of class and is very quick at replying to the discussion board.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: OK he is very sweet, extremely funny, really loves o-chem and wants you to learn BUT he is just terrible at explaining things. His lectures are all over the place, he doesn't go over the actual labs, he doesn't explain how things relate or what he's talking about. I often left his office hours more confused than when I went in. study old materials!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Sergei is the best teacher Ive ever had in my life. He is exceptionally thorough, articulate, and clear. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and goes above and beyond to be available outside of class. He is prompt to reply to the discussion board and email and is a true gem. Take his class over all others you wont regret it.

I want to bless this man. He is hilarious, nice, and tries his hardest to make sure you understand concepts, but is not a good lecturer, particularly for lab. He is very disorganized, skips important steps, and goes on tangents. Go to his office hours! He will take time there to explain things throughly. His jokes are low-key really funny too.
Might be the worst professor at TCU.

Had him for Fall and Spring sems. His Finals are killer! Should practice past exams and quizzes. Don't have to read his lectures/textbooks. Instead re-write his notes. MUST GO TO LECTURES!!!!!! He's a gem if you love Chemistry as a science. But would hate him if memorize -- will for sure fail his class. If you work hard 1st sem, Ochem will be FUN!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I had Dzyuba for lecture last semester and this semester for lab. He is definitely better as a lecture professor. I really didn't feel like I got much out of his powerpoints and usually ended up teaching myself most things. However, he is very kind and very willing to meet outside of class to answer questions (his answers may or may not make sense)
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Hottest prof in the department! Dzyuba rocks every Ochem class!! His exam questions are the hardest, but he gives reasonable partial credits. A thing worth concerning - disorganized lectures: he never writes down title of what he's going to teach and jumps quickly from 1 topic to another so you gotta pay attention always or else you won't catch up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Dzyuba is very smart and really tries when teaching us ochem. The class is hard, but he does an alright job of making it bearable. My main complaint is that he isn't very organized and clear titles would significantly benefit his lectures. However, on reviewing your notes, you can figure out the intent of what he said/drew.

The class is super hard; the material is challenging. You can't get by with memorizing, you have to learn to think. However, Sergei is a great teacher. He cares about his students, gives many practice problems & review sessions before tests (no one else does). He has lots of office hours and is available outside office hours if you just ask.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Dzyuba is a great guy and an enjoyable presence in class. His lectures can be hard to follow because he often skips basic material, but overall is fairly well done. A LOT of outside studying is required to get an A or a B, but he is extremely helpful, understanding, and respectful in office hours. Tests and quizzes are tough, so study always.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Definitely the hardest class I've ever taken, but for how tough the class is, Sergei is a great teacher and really connects well with his students. You without a doubt will need to go to every lecture because that's what he puts on his tests and quizzes. The textbook will give you a good intro to each topic but use your lecture notes 2 study 4 test

Compared to Dr. Minter, Dr. Dzyuba has a more open-minded grading system where he will give you credit for WHATEVER MAKE SENSE AND EXPLAINABLE you put on your exam. TIPS: Don't be panic at all  the rings and branches, show him what you are taught. If you felt behind, go to his office and ask for practice questions (some may be similar in exams)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Dzyuba is awesome. He is sassy at times and definitely the funniest professor I have ever had. Overall he is very helpful, and wants the best for his students. The class is tough, and sometimes his lectures become scattered. Study everything and don't be afraid to ask him for help.

Organic chemistry is a very difficult subject, but Dr. Dzyuba is a great professor. He is clear during lectures, and all of the material that appears on his tests and quizzes is from the notes. Of course, he finds ways to make questions much more difficult than the examples in the notes. If you study hard, it is definitely possible to get an A.

Sergei is pretty awesome! He was always willing to helpclarify during office hours. The class overall is pretty difficult: quizzes are tough, exams are super hard. However, Sergei is a wonderful professor with a great sense of humor once you get to know him. I can tell he really cares about his students!

sergei is SUCH a kind person. you can't meet a professor more patient than him. he will stay extra hours just for you to make sure you understand. he's challenging but he makes you think and doesn't just hand you the answers. but he's a very hard professor. lectures are very difficult to understand sometimes.

He is the most helpful professor I ever had. He gives a lot of partial credit. However, his final grading scale is confusing. Very few As, lots of B's. I got a B and even if I skipped the final I'd still be able to keep my B. Crazy. Only very top students get As (this year 5% of the class!)
Awesome lab professor, very helpful with lab reports and reviving very ugly compounds. The lab final is a beast though.
Dzyubanator is an excellent teacher. He is so helpful in the lab and gets grading done quickly and fairly. For the lab reports he is very lenient.
Sergei is so helpful in the lab, much more than Minter. He doesn't just care about crystal quality or raquetball skills but wants us to learn something. He's also very lenient on grading.
best teacher ever
OChem is ridiculously hard, but he is very good about  working with students outside of class. He has been my favorite Chemistry teacher at TCU!
Dont take this class with anyone but Sergei. He's so helpful, will meet with you anytime, does whatever he can to help. Best teacher in the deparment by far.

Sergei is one of the best teachers I've ever had at TCU. He is the most helpful teacher in the chem department. He'll do whatever he can to help you. Tough class but but he doesn't try to make you fail. He's funny and one of the nicest teachers I've ever had. Def nicest of the three organic profs. Highly recommend.
No Comments

Course material was super interesting, and Neil made it so cool to talk about. He knows everything about Science Fiction to the art of it. If you just like the movies but don't know anything about the art of it, this class isn't for you. Expects you to know the vocab and the meaning of everything. Your writing and journals should be top tier.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class isn't as hard as people make it seem. We are expected to watch/read a movie/book each week. The quizzes are super easy and filled with a lot of extra credit points. There is a journal that isn't bad if you keep up with it. There is a midterm and final but you know every prompt that could be on it. This class isn't hard if you keep up

Crime Fiction. You are expected to be able to read a novel or watch a movie every week. You will be quizzed on every reading/viewing. A lot of trick questions in the quizzes. He does not use TCU online, email only. He grades weird and you have to ask him for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Easterbrook is the definition of a teacher with tenure and says whatever he wants. I made an A even after taking a 0% on the final. I was able to do this because he offers insane amounts of extra credit on the weekly quizzes. Be prepared to watch a few bad movies but there isn't a lot of work associated with the class. He grades the midterm hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is the hardest class I have ever taken, and I took molecular biology. He does not use TCU online so you have to calculate your grade using his crazy system of grading. The classes are helpful, but don't try to give your own interpretation because he will count it wrong. This class gave me 7 panic attacks during finals week. 0/10

This professor SCARRED my college career. I have never met a teacher so absurdly sarcastic, and petty with their grading ever before in my LIFE. Easily one of the worst classes I have ever taken. No... just no.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The discussions helped a lot in understanding the required readings and books. He does grade hard though and was often sarcastic, making the class not as enjoyable. He grades harshly on the final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: In regards to his Science Fiction Lit class, Easterbrooks a likeable guy, Funny,lots of jokes, & strange in a good way. Lots of reading, prepare to read at least 5 hours a week. Quizzes are easy. Tests are medium difficulty essay questions. Big paper due towards the end & he grades tough. If you enjoy SF you wont have a problem getting an A!!!

Professor Easterbrook is most likely one of the most intelligent people I've ever met and he makes class interesting but if you are not interested in science fiction it makes it VERY hard to be motivated. You are required to read about 9 books so you'll have to read a LOT. If you are struggling though he is very helpful in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Funny guy who likes to make cheesy, sometimes stupid jokes. Other than that, he talks for a long time during class and is an extremely tough grader on papers and essays. Not often clear with what he is looking for when revising or grading papers. Wouldn't recommend him unless you are very interested in science fiction or crime fiction as a course
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Other than being by far the most entertaining professor ever, he is by far the hardest grader I've come across ever in college so far. The quizzes are awesomely easy as long as you read the books. They carry great weight to assist your grade however, midterm, paper, and final are essay form and are graded extremely tough. Find another HUM

Lots of reading and have quizzes but the quizzes help your grade out. tests are essay-based and he grades super hard. Funny, nice, kind of weird guy. Makes a lot of jokes and is liberal. Gotta work hard for this class - I would personally take something else for a literary tradition credit
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: took this as a LT and HUM and not sure i'd recommend for someone not genuinely interested in the material. A LOT of reading if you want to do well. quizzes are very easy and gives lots of bonus questions but tough grader on tests and essay. Spent a lot more time stressing about this class than expected. Friendly guy though..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The quizzes are supposed to be based off of (9!) books read over the semester, but they're so easy that you can google a summary and still get a 100 on them. Also, he gives a lot of bonus points. His grading policies are more than fair. There is one really lengthy essay that he grades tough, but the quizzes bring up the average so much that it's ok

I took American Lit from 1960s to the Present (we read 8 books!) with Neil and he's great. He grades hard, but not unfairly, and his feedback really helped me grow throughout the semester. He is head of the graduate program (or will be in fall of 2014) and is a really valuable resource as both a professor and a mentor!

I thought I had already taken the worst class of my college career, I was wrong. This takes the cake. Not only is the material difficult, it is like swimming thru quicksand, with Easterbrook throwing sandbags at you instead of life savers. He makes it 100x harder. it's hell!!

Neil is a really good professor who is interested in what he's teaching. You have to be prepared to work - you read 8 books in the semester and one of them is about 600 pages, but he's willing to work with you on ANYTHING and all the exams are open-book. Just stay on top of the reading and you'll make at least a B. Plus, you can rewrite your essay.

This professor is the smartest person I have ever met.  He goes out of his way to help his students, meeting them as many times as they desire.  He lets you revise papers as many times as you want to earn a better grade and can make Lit Theory bearable.  He actually is extremely hard but worth it.

Do not recommend! He is pretty entertaining (if you are easily entertained). He never takes class attendance, but will fail you for missing more than 3 times. I had a family emergency that forced me to leave for a week and a half, and he failed me, saying: "I just got divorced, and I made it here." Lots of reading. Doesn't follow his own guidelines

Fables and Fantasy: Ok, here's the scoop on Neil.  His class's all over the place. You read 6 difficult novels throughout the semester. The essay he'll let you turn it in early and let you correct it. I went to him 3 times for the essay and every time, I got the same, unguided help and suggestions, which apparently didn't help me grade. Avoid Neil!
He's a pretty funny guy. he made me become more interested in the SF genre. You have to read 8 novels in 16 weeks, but you can easily find some torrents for audiobooks online. or you could buy them.

Neil is a good professor, but be prepared to do A LOT of work, like reading a 400 page book in only a week. I had to drop the class at the last minute because my GPA was suffering. I think Neil cares about your grade, as long as you show him YOU care. You must pay attention in class. I didn't do that well and had to drop as a result.

Ok, he's tough. But he's an awesome professor! Yes, he expects you to write well, but he also lets you turn in as many drafts as you want before the final product. He gives amazing advice on what to fix. It's really not that bad, but students, especially at TCU, don't like putting in any effort. Take his Science Fiction class. It's amazing.

This class is very difficult. At times it is just about impossible to wrap your head around this philosophy stuff. If you weren't able to take AP English in high school, beware! Neil thinks he's funny and entertaining. At first, you will agree, but he gets annoying fast. He does let you revise papers but he's a tough, picky grader. Not recommended.

i don't understand why everyone is giving him bad marks. these people probably didn't do any of the work. if you show up to class and read what you are supposed to, you will get a good grade. he is willing to help you with any of your writing. he's awesome.

DO NOT take any of his writing classes!  NOBODY in the class received an A on any of the assignments.  There were a few F's and D's, but most people received either a C or a B.  I was in the C crowd.  He also has a nasty habit of teaching us things that would have been useful LAST week.

Very smart and funny guy.  Learned a lot in his class, but extremely difficult.  This is by far the hardest English class I have taken.  Honestly its more of a Philosophy class than English, so heads up.  He lets you revise your papers, which is nice, but they have to be incredible to get an A.
Smartest English professor at TCU.

He is super boring, hard, rather uncaring, and not funy even though he tries to be. I would not take this class, even though there were no tests it was still alot of other work to keep up with. You had to read a huge novel like every week.

yeah, he's cooky and he'll scare you at times, but it's better than having a boring teacher. just go to class and take notes (he practically gives you answers for the test). just write long answers and think outside the box and you'll be fine.

Really enthusiastic, but rambles A LOT.  Entertaining classes.  Funny at first, but after awhile you realize he makes a lot of jokes and you didn't really learn anything.  Good books, but a little weird.  If you like english, you might like him, but I can see how math or science major might hate him.  Overall, a really nice guy.  Mixed feelings.

Had him for Theory. Very funny professor. Although he is an extremely hard grader, he is fair enough and will let you revise your papers as many times as you need to in order to boost your grade. Class is mandatory and participation is strongly encouraged. Definitely not an easy A class, but managable if you put the work into it.

He's like a large hobbit. Very entertaining. He will challenge you. Make an effort to get to know him, especially if you are an English Major. If not, be aware he is difficult, but worth the time and effort. He will reward you if he knows you care. Excellent teacher. I have had him for Joyce and Fable & Fantasy.

If you love to spend hours writing papers and reading random books, you will probably like this class.  If not, I would advise against it.  He lets you revise papers and says if you try to fix problems he will give you credit, but don't count on that.  Lets his liberal, anti-religious bias slip a little too often for my taste, as well.
Do not take this class unless u really like sci-fi.. he's a little out there and doesn't make alot of sense.

Neil is a wonderful man.  Probably the most brilliant instructor I've had (not necessarily the most brilliant I've ever met), his lectures are genuinely a treat to hear.  Hilarious, out-of-fashion, and thoughtful, he's certainly worth  tackling someone else in the Registrar's office if there's only one space left in his class.
Very difficult class...made some students feel like idiots.  Not very helpful, not very clear and hard to learn from.

This was by far the best class I've ever taken in either college or highschool, the guy is really funny and the books he chose were interesting. The papers were not really that much work, and he is always willing to help, couple essays for tests and a quiz every now and then, but if you read the book you should do fine.
No Comments
Neal is the hardest teacher at TCU.  I busted my tail and made a C.  Very smart guy, crappy jokes.  Avoid him at all costs.

I absolutely loved this class, but if you are narrow-minded, judgemental and/or unwilling to learn, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!  My critical thinking and writing skills were definitely improved by Easterbrook. I made an A. Definitely one of the funniest profs at TCU!! A refreshing change of pace for me.
Just a "big" waste of time!!!
This guy is the worst professor I have ever had.  I worked my ass off in his class and made a C.  Any professor trying to fail his students in a UCR is messed up in the head.
Great teacher, dry sense of humor, not easy.

Neil is an interesting guy. He is remarkably smart in diverse fields and makes the class fun and interesting The class is also interesting if you can manage to read all the novels. The class is not Star wars oriented, but the people in the class are (except for me)

He is always willing to help and bends to your schedule.  If you work hard and put in the effort then he will help you with your grades...  Don't take the class unless you enjoy the type of literature!  I made that mistake!

This was a very difficult class, but worth it.  If you are actually willing to put some effort in (gasp!), you will learn alot.  Some people may find him unhelpful, but that's because he treats his students like adults, not little children who need theh

You'd better be darned good at writing essays in PERFECT MLA format. Very difficult teacher, who gets off the subject frequently. Unless you are an English major you will not make an A, regardless of how much you study. This class will ruin your GPA.
This was without question the most difficult class I ever had.... but I learned more in this class than I did in just about all my other classes combined.  It's tough but absolutely worth it.

Easterbrook is not a non-major's teacher. This guy knows english like a text book (only better b/c he comes with those great bad jokes we all love.) But he doesn't teach a class that you can take and pass without effort. If you actually care, take him.

DO NOT EVER EVER EVER TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!! Although a nice guy, he is the worst professor I have had in my life. The work load is enormous and his teaching style is wack. Do anything you can NOT TO TAKE HIM.
This is a great class, but he is a tough teacher.  His grading is hard but his knowledge and enthusiasm for the subject is excellent.

Great teacher who will teach you excellent critical thinking skills if you actually let him. Yet, I realize in our theraputic, post-Kantian culture actually being held accountable for quality scholarship is a social sin.  Ugh.

NEVER take this class unless you're an English major. He is very absent-minded, and doesn't seem to know how to explain things in simple English terms. Nice hippie guy, and passionate about his work, but just don't take this class!

This is the worst teacher I have ever had.  If you want a literature class, do not take from him.  On the other hand, if you want a philosophy class, then he's the perfect teacher.  He goes on tangents all the time and never clarifies his statements.

he's incomprehensible when he is teaching b/c he goes off into random subjects and never actually makes the point that he was trying to make. the class involves way too much crappy poetry which he somehow seems to enjoy... basically my worst class ever.
No Comments

Awesome professor.  Funny New Yorker with weird hair growth.  Sort of a hippie, extremely intelligent.  Grades harsh as hell, but it's worth it.  One of the most enjoyable classes I've ever had, despite the amount of work and the stress involved.
The papers are killer...he grades so hard, and class has a tendency to drag.

Great teacher.  Knows what he's talking about, and really knows how to improve your saxophone playing.  Is patient to a point, but your grade will suffer if you don't do what you're supposed to before each lesson.  One of the many reasons there are so many aspiring saxophonists at TCU.
Very clear, concise, detailed in his instruction. Challenges you to the point of perfection. Also very friendly.
Take lessons from this guy.
Lectures are pointless. If you want to be successful in this class, read the book and TCU online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Lectures do not pertain to his tests. If attendance wasn't necessary, I would say to just read the book and material he puts online. Grading does not make sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Although he is not a good professor, McMahon really does try his best. I studied probably 30 hours per test, using only the text book and online materials. His lectures are pointless. He is willing to help you on tests though,  if you ask. Cool dude, not great at teaching. A difficult A, but not impossible. Definitely ask for help on tests.

He is so hard. His class is the hardest class I have taken. Class is pointless. He spends the entire class talking about irrelevant information and the tests are impossible. He is very hard to connect with and skips around at all lectures. I definitely recommend getting out of this class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Horrible class, his lectures are worthless. His test are extremely hard. Had to put in a lot of work just to get a B. An A is almost impossible. Textbook is an absolute must!!!
VERY boring class! Lectures are confusing  and hard to see where test questions will come from yet somehow I did okay in the class.  Hard to pay attention because lectures were all over the place.

This class isn't too hard, but the problem with him is that his lectures are very difficult to follow. You don't understand anything until you teach yourself the content the day before the test. Like right now I'm in his class typing this, so as you can tell, there really is no need to listen to the lectures
He tends to go on tangents and doesn't really match up with what he expects you to know. Really pay attention to the study guide because otherwise you might get lost listening to him.

Do not take this class for World Religions! I took this class as a requirement for the core and thought it would be easy. His lectures are long, boring, and very hard to keep up with. Nothing he says makes sense. There are two essays that are easy and three tests that are hard. He gives you a study guide but they are VERY HARD. Must read textbook.

I really like Mr. McMahon. Ignore these last few comments, they are old and outdated. He is a sweet man who gives only 3 tests and two easy papers. The papers are double spaced and only 3 pages. He helped me out by explaining the material to me after class. His class was hard for me but by doing the readings and paying attention, I received a B!

His lectures are completely useless. Even reading the book won't help you on the tests because he pulls the most random things and there is no possible way you can memorize everything because it is SOOO much information! This teacher is awful. DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!!!
lectures are useless and impossible to follow. only way to pull of an A is to know the readings.

His lectures literally make no sense and are extremely hard to follow. His reviews are unclear and extremely hard to understand. If you are unfortunate enough to take this class READ because his lectures are useless

By far, the worst professor I have ever had. His lectures make no sense and are of no help in the exams. The only learning will come from reading the text book. I think the reason he doesn't have many reviews is because almost all students drop his class as soon as possible. Waste of time and damage to your GPA no matter how hard you work.

He has the WORST lectures ever. i did not understand anything because he talks about the most random stuff and jumps around every 5 seconds. the whole class is completely confused. dont take him for world religions.

Survey since 1877: I dont know what happened but i read the comments on here then i took the class... nothing like it. His tests were hard and he was always lost in his teaching. We never got our grades until very late in the semester. I would never take him again. I got a low b and im an A student. I heard he left after my class. Great.
Surv to 1877: great teacher, simple tests, easy to listen to lectures. you have to come to class & if you do he says the "grade fairy" will be on your side. so nice & helpful & gets to know everyone.

History 1877-present.  Liked the class, but not very exciting.  Lecture intensive, but easy.  4 short tests make up the grade, so don't screw one up!  Go to class and pay attention and get a B easily.  Not too much work to get the A either.
Take him! He is my favorite teacher so far. He is really funny and extremely nice. He does take attendance so you need to be there. He gives reviews for the tests if you know those you will make an A

Very easy course, made a B+ but only because I messed up on one test, could've worked harder for an A. Tests were only 20 multiple choice and a few short answer. He sometimes gets lost in his thoughts when he's lecturing but he's a cool professor, likes to open with a joke. I lost a decent amount of points for attendance so that is pretty important
This class was very easy. There is no need for the book at all. Take notes and you will do great. he tends to wonder off topic a lot which helps if you don't like history!

He is a really great teacher. You don't have to memorize any date nor do you have to read the book. In fact, I wouldn't even bother buying it. Just go to class and take decent notes. Study the review he gives a few nights before the test and you should be good!

The man knows his stuff. He wanders off into different topics sometimes but he keeps the class interesting. He's always more than willing to answer any questions and as long as you take sufficient notes the tests are cake. Take the class, it will make your life a lot easier.                        P.S. You don't need to read the book.

I took him for post CW American History and at the beginning of the semester he was really slow, covering the same material over and over but he picked up after the first test.  He def knows his stuff and his class is really easy, if you pay attention in class then you'll ace the tests, he doesn't care for you to memorize dates! very helpful guy!

Mr. Sutton is such a fun professor! His lectures are interesting, and he is passionate about his job. The assignments are essentially just graded by completion. He also canceled class pretty often and let us out at least 30 minutes early every class. Overall, this was an enjoyable and relaxed class that I would definitely recommend.
