Awful teacher, lectures make no sense. She purposely makes her lectures difficult to understand only to make herself seem intellectual. Took macro summer school at a community college this summer, and had a phenomenal teacher compared to Elliot
Her lectures were almost impossible to follow. Attendance was required, but if you get on her bad side it's impossible to do good in that class. Tests are difficult. Not a fun class.

Hard, and difficult to understand. I took honors micro with her, she didn't make much sense and her grading was erratic. Get on her good side in the beginning. She is difficult to get a hold of, and I had class during her one hour of office hours a week. For intro micro, just take Butler.
Not an easy class, but she is willing to explain concepts if you ask. The text book will help. On tests, it was sometimes difficult to tell exactly what she was looking for on the short answers.

I took her microeconomics class the first semester of my freshman year and it was a class I dreaded going to. Her lectures are almost completely understandable and she writes on the board without looking. I stopped going to class after a while but make sure if you take her class you go in the beginning so that you can find your small group

She is very difficult to understand.  She contradicts herself multiple times within a class.  attendance is mandatory if you want a good grade.  thought i understood micro going in, but ended up pass/failing class.  very hard, tests are extremely hard!

She is a good professor. Very helpful and grades farily; she is also flexible in grading. Very helpful,go to class, and takes notes you will do fine. If your lazy you better take a different class, you can do well you just have to do the work.
Has an inability to teach college students refrains from using anything other than elevated diction, told our class that she did not enjoy teaching us and that we were boring
she completely does her own thing and it does not go along with the book at all. SO CONFUSING! Do not take this class!

One of the best! Take this class if you enjoy a challenge. The people that complain about how she is "hard to get ahold of" obviously never went to her office. I suggest taking contending perspectives otherwise you will be lost. Ask lots of questions, READ, and goto her office hours. One of the most rewarding/challenging classes I took at TCU.

She's great, I love her. Yes, she's really hard, but she'll help you - everything you need to do well, she gives you. But you HAVE to do the work, she will not do it for you. If you're lazy, don't take her class - in fact, don't even be an econ major. I do more work than anybody I know, but I love what I do.
WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD. RUDE. MEAN. DOESNT KNOW HOW TO TEACH. WORK YOUR ASS OFF FOR ABSOLUTELY NOTHING. DO NOT TAKE UNLESS YOU WANT TO KILL YOURSELF.

Hard teacher.  Willing to help if you have questions.  DO ASK QUESTIONS IN CLASS.  She doesn't care if she has to explain something again, she wants you to understand it.  Her accent is entertaining but it does not hinder your understanding her.  Read the book, study hard for the tests, do the homework and you can make a B.  Really work for an A.

She is truly a genius.  Unfortunately, she talks in the language of economics.  Considering it is an INTRO class, it makes it kind of hard.  You will really have to work hard in this class but she is willing to help you.  USE HER OFFICE HOURS/EMAIL HER!  Know the concepts for her tests.  HAVE TO READ THE BOOK!!!
This teaacher is way too difficult and is not able to teach the subject, though she is very smart, she just cant teach it

Brilliant, most definitely. She is a genius. However, that doesn't mean she is a good teacher. She is very unclear in her teaching and her handwriting is very hard to read, yet she refuses to correct it. When I emailed her questions or wanted to set up appointments, she never got back to me until the third time I emailed her. Avoid.

This is not a teacher you should take if you are not willing to work. If you are willing to work and you have a thirst for knowledge of economics then this might be the best teacher you will every have. Absolutely brilliant teacher.
she is from jamaica, her english is jst fine...she goes extremely fast...and if she knows your name she will call you out during class!!!

Dont take a class with Dr. Elliot unless you enjoy working your ass off for a B. You cant understand half of the stuff she says and her examples are terrible. She seems to go out of her way to teach you the hard way to do things rather than the most efficient. I hated this class
She is very hard to get a hold of. If you email her wait about 3 days for her to email you back. Overall the class wasn't that hard, but it can be challenging at times.
Great Class. You will learn a lot, but expect to work. This class is not for slackers.
shes horrible
HARD CLASS. Came in with prior understanding to economics so I was able to bear it. Most class struggled. Never there for office hours. Very Complicated and very dry. Wouldn't recommend it.

SHe is the hardest teacher i have ever taken. This class ruined my GPA, I got a C only because the final was a paper...i failed every test and quiz because i understood nothing she said...Do NOt take her especially if you are a freshman it will ruin your semester!

IntroMacroIf you are going to take this class, I'd recommend that you already have an understanding of macro. She's a grad-level teacher and she teaches this intro class like it's a review. She's very smart, just not a great teacher.

Don't take any class with this professor!  Her lectures make no sense & her ideas are very scatter brained.  She's a super hard grader and the book is no help.  Tests are based mostly on lecture, though reading will help you understand.  I advise against her unless youre up for a major challenge - I'm an A/B student, and I almost failed this class.

She is an awesome person, and SO intelligent! However, she told me that I had a good grasp of the test material, and I made a C in the class. Definitely ruined my 4.0 this year! 9 A's and 1 C! Take a different Professor - try Lovett. Heard his class was MUCH easier, and my friends made an A with minimal effort. I made a C with 6 hour study groups!

Okay, this woman is a genius! However, teaching is far from a gift she has. She explains complicated examples with even more complicated examples. She talks the whole time. I had to teach myself the material. Good luck if you take it. I would advise you to take someone else - especially if you want to make at least B

If your not an econ major do not take anything with theory in the description!! She really knows what she is talking about, making it somewhat intimidating to ask questions.  'HW' is not heavy, just the usual 5-8 pages... She tries to be nice but fails, this is a hard class.

Intro microeconomics - hard class.  She lectures a lot and takes tests and quizzes from lectures and the text, so make sure to go to every class.  If you do the extra credit assignments, she will grade a little easier come finals time.  She is not the best but will help you out if you take the time to go meet her.
Who the heck gave those high ratings? They must be her (the professor). This class is impossible and not easy or fair by any means.

Go to every class.  Do the bonus questions, and start early with the outside readings.  Read the textbook because the lectures move fast and can be confusing.  Learn to take shorthand (but thorough) notes.  Ask for help, get tutoring.  Study like hell to make a B.  If you're not a brilliant econ major, lose all delusions of an A.

Loved Her!  You must go to every single class to do well in the class.  I got an A, so it is very possible to do well in her class.  Do the bonus questions, its a lot of work but worth the extra points.  Don't  take this course if you aren't willing to go to class.  She is a awesome prof though!
BEST Teacher ever!!
No Comments

For those undergrads taking her micro class: good luck. She is a genius who will move at an accelerated pace, talk about material not in the book, and has possibly the worst handwritting on this earth. She also can be rude if you don't understand what she is saying. Her final is HELL.
Worst teacher I have ever had. Made my semester twice as hard.

Very diffiult class. No textbook, only articles. If everyone earns a D in the class she has no problem giving eveyrone a D. Attendance not mandatory, but recommended bec the articles are confusing. 2 tests and 2 hw assignments, that's it. if you can get around this class, do it
She is the hardest teacher at TCU! If you want to make better than an C then dont take this class! Nice lady when she wants to be!
No Comments

I think personally very nice lady..but i SUCK at math and she does use alot of math...so i dont recommend her unless you like and are good at it.  lots of application..if you just came out of butlers class your in for a shock ;) *cough* actual work ;)
She is not as hard as everyone says she is.  I think she has been an excellent prof.  She uses a lot of math, so if you're not a math person you might have some trouble.

She can't write, you can't understand what she says, and for this class half of the material wasn't even in the textbook.  She expects that half of the class will be failing come finals time, so she gives the option of a "one-shot" 4.5 hr. final

This lady is a horrible teacher.  She is very inaccessible so she can never help you outside of class.  She does not return e-mails.  Her handwriting is atrocious, she knows it and refuses to correct it.  She is very hard to understand because of her acce
No Comments
NEVER EVER TAKE THIS COURSE IF SHE IS TEACHING IT.  IT IS NOT EASY AND IT IS NOT FUN.  YOU WILL NOT LEARN IF SHE IS TEACHING.
She is very difficult but you learn the material.  Only several students will make an A in the class.
Easily one of the deadly classes at TCU. I recommed that you be well prepared for this class, especially tests. The exams are quiet scary for the weak hearted.
Amazingly difficult teacher.  Had to teach myself everything.  Can never read her writing on board, she knows and refuses to improve writing.

Extremely hard to understand and the words she writes on the board is her only little style of shorthand so its impossible to understand. Tests are unbearable. 2 People made an A on the first test out of 45+ Most people made C's or less
She is a great teacher, but it takes a while to get used to her  conceptual  teaching methods and testing.  provides an interesting perspective on material and i also learned A LOT.
She is very tough and very smart. A challenging class, but I enjoyed it because I felt like I learned so much.
Intense, Intersesting, Worthwhile, but Challenging.

Social problems was an easy class. No tests/quizzes but lots of writing, which was easy. Graded on participation and attendance, so go to class. Gives a lot of extra credit. Participating in this class was a little nerve-racking. I ended with a 102, so take this class if you need the credit! GPA booster

ok, she seems super nice and everything but she grades like her class is super important, I get that it's important for students to submit work with quality, but c'mon I needed a 0.01 to get an A and there was "nothing I could do about it!"
She is enthusiastic about her class, I wouldn't mind taking her again. Group projects and participation matter. Overall, good, not best for me.

Dr. Simanek is the greatest professor I have ever had in my life. His class truly changed my perspective on life. I have learned so much from him and he is the best. I recommended his class to all my friends and everyone should take his class.
A disorganized disaster. I don't have a single good thing to say.
Poor conduct towards students. People don't actually like him, they like taking a class on whiskey. He showed up unprepared every day, often left the room, and did not explain things well.

I had Professor Yorkston at a graduate level marketing class. This class was awful that I wanted money back immediately. Heavy article readings that you don't discuss in class. Read Marketing Myopia and you will be fine. No grades. At the end I got a B, with no explanation. BOOOOOO.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible. I wish I could have these days back in my life but I cant unfortunately.

The professor and the entire class itself are extremely vague and confusing. At no point in the semester was I fully confident in my understanding of what we were doing. He takes FOREVER to grade things and assignments that were turned in two months before the final weren't graded until the semester ended, so you never really know how you are doing

Yorkston is by far one of my favorite professors. He knows so much about marketing and makes it interesting where you're learning without even realizing it. Theres not a textbook for the class only 2 books you have to read but are very interesting. HIGHLY RECOMMEND taking, even if your major doesn't require it.

One of my favorite professors at TCU. You'll find that if you actually listen, he's a great professor with a wealth of knowledge. If you don't read the texts closely, there's a strong chance you won't do too well on quizzes. During my class, however, it was all quizzes and projects, no tests! I found him to be fair and wise, and fun to get to know!
He must have tenure.  How else could he get away with putting so little effort into his classes?

Frustratingly inconsistent instructor.  He his lectures are meandering, unfocused and often unrelated to the assigned texts.  He gives very little guidance on assignments then grades very strictly.  Also, his quizzes are poorly and confusingly written.

I've had two courses with Yorkston and he is very disorganized and seems to put in very little effort to prepare for class.  His courses are extremely unstructured and rarely stay on topic.  You'll think it is a blow-off class until it comes time for final exams and assignments.  Then he becomes an extremely harsh, demanding and unfair grader.

Customer Insights. Be prepared to take notes. He doesn't really plan the lectures so whatever comes up is what he teaches. His tests are weird and you really need to know the material. Put your ALL into the film you get a 95 on the final if your film is the best. Come to class because there are lots of opportunities for extra credit!
Definitely not a professor type.be aware

Had him for Insights. SUPER laid back and very scattered presentations. You learn very interesting stuff though. The tests are like 10 MC and 6 short answer, and usually from one of the THREE 250+ page books required to read over the semester. A LOT OF READING. Project deliverables boost grade though :-)
Impossible teacher. Multiple choice off the wall and essays are impossible. uses no book which sucks. attendance is mandatory or ur docked like crazy. may be nice guy but bad teacher.

Yorkston is my favorite professor at TCU. He's not hard at all and he's cool as hell. Easy A if you go to class. So much fun. Plus he's hot in that unconventional sweet shy kind of way. Take him! I wish I could take more of his classes. love him!
You will learn but you'll have to work extra hard to follow his train of thought.  Very scattered presentation. Little organization of the material. Multiple choice questions are off-the-wall.
Do not ake him, he is laid back but a super hard grader with a feeling that no one is a s smart as he is.  His tests are ridiculous
Tests are impossible, grades super hard on research paper. Do yourself a favor and wait until Thompson teaches it if you can.

Cares about her students and is always willing to listen. Easy class and she is pretty fair on grading but like all English teachers she looks for specific things in the essays, but even so it's not hard to at the minimum pass her class.

I loved this professor. The only reason I got a B was because I did not ask for feed back on the first essays. As long as you communicate with her she will help you do good in this class. One of my fav english professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She made that class so much easier... Ill definitely take her class again next semester

Very good professor. she is supportive and caring! however, get ready for writing 3 pages long essays that makes up most of the % of your grade. she gives good reviews and helps you in all ways to write paper. replies quick to emails but not much extra credits. would definitely take her again
I think she's a good teacher
shes fine
I love her! She is so cool and so nice! She will help you with anything, and is really easy to talk to!

Great teacher, very helpful in and outside of class. Can't expect class to be to exciting afterall what could she possibly do. I had C throughout the course but my final grade was B, must have done something right.
If you just put in a little effort in writing your papers, you will make a good grade.  EASY class!
She's a very nice teacher. She is willing to help her students.
She is a lot more helpful outside of class than she is inside of class. Pretty boring class, but then again, its required comp, its not going to get too exciting.
She's really helpful if you go in on your own time.  The class wasn't that interesting but required for most people and not too difficult.

I've taken Espo for three classes and I always search out his classes. He can be a little intimidating at first, but once you get to know him you love him. He's hysterical and truly cares about students that are passionate and want to succeed!

Don't get me wrong—this class is hard. It's very lecture- and test-heavy, but the content is fantastic, and Espo's teaching methods make it easy to understand. Very few assignments. To succeed, don't cram the night before, and make sure you not only know the material but are able to apply it. I highly recommend this class if tests are your thing.
Professor Esposito is the funniest professor I've ever had lol. I've had him twice, and both classes went very well. There was very little work, mostly only tests. But they were easy if you study.

Espo was great to have for Intro to Kinesiology. I was told he was very scary, but that wasn't the case at all. He was very engaging. There were only a couple of assignments and tests throughout the semester, so every grade mattered. Both in-class and online lectures are required to do well. I would take any course with him as the professor.

For a 1 credit class, this professor takes his stuff too seriously. Emailed him a question and gives the most aggressive feedback. I don't know about the other classes but bro doing too much for a 1 credit class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. E wants the best for you. His exams are difficult so study at least 5 days prior. His grading is very fair. For this class, find a study group- discussion helps a ton and going over the information with other people makes it bearable! Take notes from his examples and show up to class- it'll benefit your studying and success in the class.
Hand's down the best professor in the kinesiology department. His lectures keep you engaged and he actually cares about how his students are doing in the class.
Literally the most fun/best professor you will take at TCU

I have had him for Motor D and Intro KINE. He is a total goofball but he really cares about what he is teaching. In Motor D he would look up extra information on topics that we found interesting (Did not test us on this too!). His tests were not terribly hard, it is important that you study the notes and the textbook.
I loved this class and Dr. Espo
I think he is an excellent instructor. He is nice and a good instructor. I thought he was funny too.
Dr. E is the best.  Take him!!

Awesome professor. Very helpful if you go visit him during office hours. Go to class and take notes. Attendance isnt mandatory, but necessary. Only one exam and a few projects. Do not procrastinate on projects.. they do take time. He is very reasonable when grading. You get what you earn. Study what he tells you for the exam and you'll do fine!

Wasn't entirely clear on some assignments. Make sure you know APA format, because he takes off points for any mistakes! Overall the class was enjoyable, I should have gotten a higher grade but getting points off for formatting brought it down
She is an enthusiastic professor; classes are based on conversation and participation. Show up for classes and participate and you should do great.

I LOVE TEIXEIRA! Everyone loved her she's just the sweetest dynamic woman ever and made the whole class feel like a community. She's organized with the schedule and homework was not very time consuming. You can always bring notes into the compositions and have to do a few oral assignments. Pretty easy to get an A but I didn't learn much.
She's very nice, but there is a lot of homework and I truly don't think I improved my spanish in this class. I'd take someone else

Dr. Teixiera is one of my favorite professors that I've had at TCU. She is extremely passionate, especially about her students becoming proficient Spanish speakers.
Workload wise, there are sometimes 3 assignments a week. Your grade in this class is definitely earned. However, I will say she is very understanding when it comes to late work/grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Culture of Brazil - I really really enjoyed this class. It is very discussion based (which means its not exam heavy- we didn't have any exams) and you have to be willing to put yourself out of your comfort zone and speak in class. You definitely have to put work into this class but she makes it very interesting and worth it. I would recommend.

Teixera is by far one of my favorite professors that I have had at TCU. She is so kind, caring, and hilarious and does a great job of keeping class interesting. She is also a fair grader and realistic expectations. I would 110% take a class with her again.

Teixeira is the sweetest, most caring professor I've ever had. She is super understanding and willing to help wherever and whenever you need it. She is always willing to give you an extension or extra time and makes herself super accessible. Be ready to SPEAK!! Lots of homework and lots of papers, but she is a pretty lenient grader!!

I have taken her for 2 Spanish classes and she is by far my favorite. She is the best professor in the Spanish department and hey class is easy to get a A- in with pretty much no effort, an A is easily achievable with a little bit of effort. Shes a pretty easy grader and is very sweet, understanding, and willing to work with you.

Do NOT take this teacher if you are not nearly fluent in Spanish. Its mainly a literature class. So much reading with words even native speakers had never seen before. If you arent 100% active she will fail your participation grade. Unbelievable amount of work. The tests are all big full essays (4+ paragraphs for one question). Do not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Incredibly nice and caring woman but the hardest grader I've ever had. She expects your grammar to be perfect even though it is an oral comm class. If you are only okay at Spanish and not proficient I would not recommend. She is so nice though and feels like a professor that would actually go out of their way for you. It was just so hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I don't fault the professor at all. The TCU Span. Department is in shambles. She is probably the best professor in the department (which says a lot) but still can't seem to figure out how to be a fair grader or put grades in the grade book in a timely manner. By far my worst grade this semester. If you aren't a native speaker, avoid this class.
Paik is well educated and she makes her lectures engaging. The tests aren't super hard because she posts a study guide. Definitely not a bad class to take.

Dr. Paik is great and her deception class is interesting and easy. Lectures are not the most interesting but if you pay attention and just listen, it makes studying easier and you'll pass the exams. Very chill Comm elective.
Paik is such a kind lady. This class was not easy or hard it was just kind of there. The final wasnt hard at all it was a group project on a movie and made the end of the year less chaotic.

Dr. Paik is a very sweet lady and makes an effort to get to know her students by name. You are allowed 3 unexcused absences, and she made sure to let us know that we can use our own judgement to miss class when we need to. Her exams are all multiple choice and she gives a study guide with everything you should know. I really enjoyed this class.
Love this professor, but sometimes was hard to understand and speaks fast. You dont need textbook as i never used it.

Professor Paik was one of the kindest professors at TCU. You can truly know that she cares about each one of her students and knows you on a first name basis. I was not doing well in the beginning and basically bombed the first two exams and met with her during office hours and she went through every question in depth until I understood. TAKE HER.

Professor Paid is one of the greatest professors at TCU. I have never had a professor care about me succeeding like she does. Tests are easy as long as you study. She is very willing to help you. When the average for the first test was 85 she gave us all a worksheet that gave her ideas on how to improve. Super easy grader and just a great person.

Professor Paik is kind hearted and an amazing professor. I enjoyed sitting through lectures because she gave great examples. She is very helpful and approachable. She cares for her students. I would recommend taking her course. Such a sweet lady.

I gave Dr. G a 3 to balance out his caring, patient, helpful attitude (4 or 5 stars!) with his monotonous lecture style (2). The class is him reading off the powerpoints that repeat the textbook verbatim. The labs are a little more interesting but the lecture is not at all engaging. It's not a difficult class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. G is kind, but the lectures all look the same and he struggles to keep the class engaged. It's not a difficult course, but some of the assignments could use more explanation. I'd take him again but he wouldn't be my first choice.

One of the worst professors I've had at TCU! Dr. G is not sure of what he is teaching, uses outdated materials and software. He expects you to find solutions to problems but does not teach you how to or provide any guidance, counts wrong if it doesn't match his. Will lecture while you having you work on the outdated workbook.

This class was taken for ModelUN, but Dr. Cox is such a great professor. He is a relatively easy grader and is super accessible for help on assignments. He basically tells you what you need to add to a rough draft for an A on the assignment. This class is lots of writing, but it was straightforward and he was extremely helpful. Take his classes!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Cox makes this hard class doable. The content is hard to understand but he is good to  break it down and go slow. The paper is written over the course of the whole semester making if feel lighter to get done. You will need to be in class to understand the material because the book alone is hard to understand how to solve problems

Dr. Cox is a great guy with an incredible sense of humor. He cares about his students and is happy to help anyone who asks for it. The class itself is pretty challenging. Two exams that are essentially pure math (game theory) and a paper that takes an entire semester to write. Pretty challenging class overall, but worth it.

Dr. Cox really wants the students to do well.  His lectures can get boring but does post the powerpoints online.  Main part of your grade is tests, and they can be difficult so definitely study hard for those!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cox is one of the best professors I've had at TCU. Extremely knowledgeable in the field and has interactive lectures. Big Texas Rangers fan & big into cycling. Content can be tough, but Dr. Cox has review sessions and provides study guides to help students succeed. Highly recommend.

Dr. Cox is a pretty average professor. He rambles during class a lot, about things that do not matter and are not going to be on the exam. He recently changed his exam to in person, on paper exams. This class is a 2000 level class, and he made it a lot harder than it needed to be. The exams are based on memorization, which does not help me learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There's a learning curve to this class but once you get in the hang of it, it's really not that bad. The best advice is to really pay attention to his lectures because that's where most of the content on the exams come from. If you can take good notes during the two lectures a week and dedicate yourself to studying for the 3 exams, you'll get an A.

I LOVED Dr. Cox! His other review is correct because you WILL leave his International Politics class a smarter person. He is so knowledgeable and his class was so interesting. I enjoyed learning about all of the material and the tests aren't bad at all if you study the study guide he gives you. I looked forward to taking another one of his classes!

Definitely go to class and pay attention to take notes. His slides have some information, but the majority of the information on the test is from his lecture. He is very good at being engaging and not just spitting out facts. The tests are open note, but definitely still study for them or you won't have enough knowledge to do well.

Really great professor and I loved his class. His lectures were always very interesting and we often would discuss current events even if they weren't always connected to that day's lecture. A lot of information is covered throughout the class but if you keep good notes then it'll be easy. Would definitely recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It is not an easy class but he is a great professor, he is always willing to help the students and his lectures are informative but he includes the students and he makes the class very interesting

Dr. Cox was an incredibly insightful lecturer that was able to get an engineering major like myself more actively interested in the intellectual field of international conflict and negotiation. There is a good amount of writing as coursework but he was always there for helpful feedback and guidance every step of the way and set clear expectations

This class was different than what Ive ever taken and was very interesting. Professor Cox was amazing he was funny and caring and will be flexible on deadlines. He also always answered my emails when I had questions fast and very thoroughly. I really enjoyed his class even though it was a little tough learning a new skill!

Took him for an honors course and he is amazing. I enjoyed the class even it was an 8 am class and although this class is lecture heavy, his lectures make it interesting. Study the study guides he gives and you're grade will look pretty good. Take him if you can - I've not seen anyone who doesn't like him.

Dr. Cox is VERY knowledgeable! His international politics class is one of the best classes you can take! Take note of everything in the lectures as he likes to see his specific examples on the test. He is always willing to help you. A little bit insecure for a man but super funny!

Dr. Cox is so caring and genuinely wants everyone to learn something in this class. I was honestly dreading taking this class but he made it so enjoyable. There is a simulation that is fun, but does take some time outside of class. Do all of your memos and turns in the simulation and you will do well.

Dr. Cox is so knowledgeable. You WILL leave POSC20303 smarter than you entered. A lot of time outside of class is devoted to a Statecraft simulation, which is fun but also time consuming. His lectures are awesome and the tests are a piece of cake. Honestly, a pretty easy A if you're willing to do the bare minimum of work.

His class is super easy but it is the Model UN trip semester so all you do is prepare for the confrence. This whole class is built to learn about the conference and how to engage once there. Amazing class and you will get really close to all your classmates.

I love Dr. Cox! He is a great speaker, can drone on a little bit and gets off on tangents, but I genuinely think he is the smartest professor I have had at TCU. This class is pretty interesting if you care about political science, economics, humanitarian issues, or even war. It has a little bit of everything. I think the hard part for me was tests.

Dr. Cox is a great professor that truly does try to imprint his knowledge on his students. He does drift off during lectures, but they really are awesome and enjoyable for the most part. This class is a writing emphasis class, so the majority of your grade comes from essays, but they are easy if you enjoy the topics and care about the class.

Dr. Cox was great very easy to follow through his lectures, but beware of his rants. He does tend to deviate from class topics, but its good as it gives a break from the material and you know you won't be tested on it. Overall he truly cares about his students and is more then willing to help you succeed and make sure you take very good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Cox is one of my favorite professors at TCU. He is very intelligent and knows how to relate to everyone. He knows his stuff and makes it interesting. He will really work with you if you try.

Cox does a great job of making the subject come alive. He also gets on tangents real quickly, but they often draw you back into the lecture if you were zoning out or uninterested. Also, he is very chill when it comes to deadlines as all three papers I had this year got pushed back at least 3 days and same with tests. Take Cox! I love him!

Dr. Cox is one of my favorite professors at TCU, because he's really intelligent, knows how to relate to people, and uses funny stories and anecdotes to drive his points home. The material is in-depth, and can be tricky to comprehend. But he'll do whatever he can to explain concepts to help you understand. I'd recommend his Game Theory to anybody.

I Have taken Dr. Cox for 3 classes now and he is by far the best professor in the POSC department. He makes class interesting goes on funny rants and has a great sense of humor usually making fun of himself or other people. You do have to do work such as article readings but goes over in class. I made an A without too much effort.

Dr. Cox is awesome. His work isn't too bad I took him for game theory and the class was fun and he tells a lot of jokes and lets you out early especially toward the second half of the semester. Easy A as long as you study and do a well thought out paper.

Dr. Cox is incredibly smart and worth taking! You feel like you are getting your tuition money worth when you take his class. His lectures aren't always clear and organized, you will type until your fingers fall off. He is head of the Poli Sci department and a great person to know. He is great at running the Model UN program!

Great professor! He has a really dry sense of humor, but I thought he was funny and his commentary kept me awake. He also ties the theories into current events and history. You have to do an online simulator called Statecraft. Its an easy way to boost your grade by writing updates on how your country is doing each week.

Best professor I've had at TCU, always accesible and always willing to do whatever it takes so that you have everything you need to do well. Also a great sense of humor, classes are relaxed but engaging!

This class is way harder than it needs to be. He makes a review for tests but then asks questions over things not on the review. I practically fell asleep in every class. Statecraft was the best part of the class and he really liked you if you got into the game. I wouldn't recommend for an easy A but the information is interesting.

Great class. Cox really knows his subject and is good at teaching it (Pearson pays him to make the study guides he uses) Uses an online teaching game Statecraft. If you read and understand what the heck your supposed to do it is really fun. Tests follow powerpoints and are not that bad. If you actually go to class and care is the easiest A ever.
GREAT,GREAT professor!He is extremely acquainted with what he does. Exciting lectures and care about his students.Wise and pleasant to answer your questions. You do not want to miss his class.

Cool professor. He knows a lot about the topic and is a great resource. He does like to go off on tangents during lectures but all around a nice guy that cares about his students and MUN..visit in office ours.

GREAT TEACHER! He really knows what he is talking about and does not take himself too seriously. Read the book and study for the test and you can get an A. He is very straightforward and does not try to trick you.

Incredible prof. engaging early in the morning (always a plus). read the book, study for the test, you get a B. Also has fun Current events discussion almost every class. Definitely recommended for core.

Great class! Dr. Cox is light-hearted and does not take himself too seriously like other professors. He teaches you valuable information every citizen should know. Tests are hard but not too bad if you study. A's are def possible. Doesn't really follow the book that closely and is very practical. Keeps class entertaining and willing to always help.

Good-natured, pleasant professor. Can keep a class engaged even in the mornings (be sure the smile at his jokes). Missing class won't kill you - he will eventually post the powerpoint online and besides they are just outlines of the chapters. I'd recommend reading the book also because it's really not that bad (but not necessary for a decent grade)
friendly and chill in class. puts all his powerpoint lectures on the net.  i was able to visit with him in his office easily. challenging but fun prof.

Dr. Cox is an amazing professor! He is really smart and knows his stuff. His tests are pretty difficult but if you study for them you should be OK. He is a really nice guy and his tests are pretty fair.

BEST poli sci teacher at TCU! (trust me we had 2 poli sci subs who SUCKED compared to him!) Read the book to clarify some points, go to him for help if need be, don't be afraid to ask for help on a test. Really interesting, especially for an early morning class. Very intelligent and witty. I def recommend taking his class!!

Great teacher and extremely helpful! I was in his Honors International Politics class and i pulled a B with minimal effort, just hard studying when it came test time (all essay questions).Talk a lot in class, he loves it.Go to him for help on papers too, it could help ur grade on it.Very personable and nice.

I've learned more from him than any other Prof. in the Poli Sci department.  He's helpful, hilarious and brilliant. He's pretty liberal but tries to be moderate in class.  Go talk to him outside of class.  Only take Model UN if you're going to put in the effort..but it pays off if you do.
Fantastic guy, really fueled my interest in the department. 'Must reccomend.
Awesome teacher! More relatable then the rest of the political science department. Take him definitely

Participating in this program was a great experience. Not only for poli sci majors but for anyone who likes talking about world politics. He is a very smart, young guy so you should be able to get along with him great. Can be a tough grader at times, but he is understanding. Highly recommend. The best in the department!!

He is a brand new professor so he is very understanding unlike much older profs. His expectations are a little unclear but go in and see him. It's kind of hard to make an A on anything for this reason and also because he is demanding (but no too much). Very interesting class if you're into politics.

His class is fun. I am not a big international politics person and I enjoyed it. It is very informative and not really hard. He has 2 papers and 2 tests and the second paper was made optional. I liked his class.

Dr. Cox is one of the more demanding of the political science profs, but his class is worth it.  he will get the class involved in the discussion which is great and pretty much seems to know anything and everything you talk to him about.  VERY smart guy.  Nice prof too.  HIGHLY reccomended.

lectures cover main topics but hw is more difficult / not what she goes over. exams are heavily based on the reviews, but she prioritizes rushing over them rather than ensuring you understand the question. quizzes are easy, exams are fine if you study the review, hw is probs the worst. not understanding or pleasant to talk to, mid course.

This class is extremely un useful. Every single class is her just writing on the board and speaking. No explaining, no TEACHING, just rushing. She does not clearly and efficiently go over any of the material. She also is an extremely hard grader, she takes off points or gives no credit for the tiniest of errors. I do not recommend. Horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lots of homework per week, but very smart teacher. Go to class, it helps a LOT. Honestly did bad on all my quizzes but do good on exams and youll do good. Gives lots of extra credit. Quizzes after tests are automatic 100s. Gave us 15 extra points on an exam if we went to a math talk. Take her if u plan on taking calc 2 so you truly understand.

The course was harder than I expected. The online homework assignments can be a lot and/or pretty difficult, but I think that the extra credit balances this out nicely. Dr. Lee is consistent with grading, transparent about upcoming assignments and grading.  She's a really good teacher, I like her teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She understands what she is teaching very well. I would take this class if you are a math major. However, this class has a TONNN of work. 5 things per week. There are definitely easier professors with less workload. Gives xtra credit (every quiz after exam is free 100, attend a math talk and get 15 points on test). OH are right after class.

Do yourself a favor and don't take her. She explains very little and just gives notes. Even if she doesn't have enough time to cover all topics, she'll rush it and make the exam hard. Hard to understand. The two times I took a class with her, I dropped it. Later scored an A with other professors. Will never repeat that mistake.

Be ready to self teach the majority of content in this course. Goes over main ideas in the lecture but assigns extremely complex homework. Feedback on homework is basically nonexistent unless you go to office hours. This class is about prioritizing studying what will be worth the most points and conceding the rest. Some content is unlearnable solo.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DON'T DO IT!  Quizzes and written homeworks weekly, including exam and post-exam weeks.  Quizzes over material not covered in lecture.  3-4 Pearson assignments weekly on material not always covered. Written homework is due on test days over material on exam. Review for exam given without answers. Lectures are hard to understand. Self taught course.

She is very nice but difficult to understand during lectures. Homework is done online and only given 5 attempts to get the correct answer. I had to put in lots of extra work to get an A in the class. A quiz is given every Monday, even after spring break.

Very hard professor, I liked to believe I was good at calculus but she made me think otherwise. She tests over useless information and makes her test incredibly hard. I would completely avoid this teacher.

She was a very nice lady but very hard to understand and not very helpful. I had to learn essentially everything online after class. Homeworks are very long and very hard and have little to do with tests. that said, her grading scale is very light, I finished with a 68 and got a c plus

Lecture heavy, not much course material online. The textbook is pretty barren too. Very nice prof, but doesn't allow calculators at all which definitely isn't for me. If you're going for a BA/BS in math, she would be a good choice because she emphasizes memorization of formulas and trig identities. Also very good abt explaining theories/formulas.

Kwon was a great professor! I learned so much, she is definitely tough but if you pay attention in class and take good notes you can get an A no doubt. She is always willing to help students out as well!
Didn't believe that my dad had cancer had to get my mom to send proof to her when he was in surgery. hope that explains enough
Petty grader, no grace given. Tests on specific details from book and lecture. The study guides barely help
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Try to take someone else for advertising. She is a very tough teacher. Her tests had everyone in the class freaking out because there was so much content on it. Her lectures are long. She is also a very tough grader. She is a nice lady though but the class itself, you need to work hard in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dont skip this class. The quizzes are online so they're manageable but the tests are super difficult and the projects are graded pretty harshly. I am usually an A or high B student and I am struggling just to pass. While Dr. Kwon is not the best teacher, she has made adjustments based on feedback and is kind and cares about her students.
Take someone else
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE KWON. YOU WILL HAVE BETTER LUCK GETTIG A GOOD EDUCATION DROPPING OUT OF SCHOOL AND GOOGLING YOUR MAJOR.

Probably one of the worst professors at TCU. Not only is she hard during lectures and go too fast, but you won't understand her either because of her horrific accent. Shes caused too much stress and tears, and is not lenient on ANYTHING. She formats her class in a way that is harder and faster than other professors for this class. Trust me on this
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Does not care about her students or their education. The lectures are all over the place and make no sense. She rushes through the notes and never asks to see if the class understands what she is saying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: DO NOT take Professor Kwon! Not only is her class harder than the other Advertising classes but she has no sympathy for anything... anything. Try not to get sick during the semester or have a family emergency because you will fail the class due to her lack of understanding. Take any teacher but her, other class is on Chapter 8 and we are on 13.
He is funny and engaging in class but grades unnecessarily hard. The class is a lot of work, I wouldn't take it as an elective if it is not required for your major.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Evans is the best!!! if you get the chance take him. Genuinely hilarious and engaging in class.

Take. This. Class. 
Professor Evans is my favorite teacher I have had at TCU. The daily lectures start as the material and end up morphing into discussions about our lives. I learned so much, and I have been able to use him as a resource outside of class as well. He is so invested in the success of his students!

My favorite professor ever! He is so funny, nice and HOT hehe. Daily reading quizzes are open book and only like 2 questions. The tests are multiple choice, take home and no lockdown. The test review is word for word the test. He can be a little picky on your new venture papers but not bad. get ready to present in front of class.

He is a nice guy who cares about his students, but often seems very confused and gives no clear instructions. Exams are very challenging, and I felt unprepared, as you have to teach the concepts to yourself. Class never goes the full time, but overall, it's very confusing.
Ewbanks gave us the topics to study for exams. Attendance was not mandatory. He did not undertsand the supply chain simulation therefore none of us did.

Ewbanks has been one of my favorite profs so far at TCU. With that being said, he is not the best teacher. His grading criteria for group projects is never clear. He taught the simulation for the first time and it didn't go well. The tests also included simulation content which nobody knew because its irrelevant. I would recommend for next sem.

This is his first time teaching the simulation, which has been disorganized, but he is a professor who really cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. Very nice and takes student feedback to better the course. Offers xtra credit so students can succeed. Overall great guy and is getting better each week.

I am currently taking this class this semester. He used to go off of his own criteria, which was much more relaxed. Exams are very difficult and directions and feedback are so vague. This class is extremely difficult for a Business Core Requirement.

This professor used to make his own course, but had to use the simulation this semester. It is extremely difficult for a core or non-major class. Doesn't give too much feedback regarding exams and homework. It is just very time cosuming and confusing directions make it harder. For sure my hardest class.

Currently taking this guy and had to change my whole schedule to be able to take him. He only has good reviews because the year before he went off of his own curriculum. This year, he was forced to do the Simulation just like most teachers and assignments are Professor Layton's who has awful reviews. Spent 3 days on an assignment and didnt complete

Cannot say enough great things about Ewbanks. I am not very interested in supply chain but I really enjoy going to his class. He is very passionate and caring. There are 2 assignments typically weekly and tests are online. He is a very easy grader and just wants you to understand the content. Take him!

Prof. Ewbanks is awesome. This semester was his first time teaching + he is killing it. Lectures are informative but engaging. He is more than understanding if you need to miss class + provides you with a make up assignment that is very straight forward. Supply chain is a difficult class, but he makes it enjoyable. Take him!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, really cares about his students learning and just a great person overall. No test, just weekly mini projects and short quizzes that aren't bad as long as you get them done and pay attention in class. He works pretty fast but you'll learn so much in this class and it'll make your other classes seem so much easier. Highly recommend!

Weekly quizzes and "mini-projects" but the workload really isn't that crazy. If you don't pay attention in class, there's a good chance you'll just bomb a mini-project, but he always drops videos and helpful information to help us out. Really valuable stuff that you learn in here if you want to be in quantitative fiannce. Awesome guy too.

It is extremely difficult to get a decent grade in this elective class. Yes, he does give you a very generous curve to your overall grade, but the weekly projects and quizzes that few do well in outweigh it. Just take a different finance elective!

Great professor, incredibly smart - just understand you will have to do a lot to get an A- or A in the course. Really in-depth statistical modeling - don't go in with the idea that you will be modeling FCFF, FCFE or LBOs. Monte carlo simulation, probability distributions, and matrix algebra.

Grant is a good dude and he means well. Problem is, this course is extremely deceptive. Description indicates that this course seeks to teach "real-world" financial modeling tools. This is factually inaccurate - the course is theoretical and academic. I advise you to avoid this course - just swag WACC at 10-15% and call it a day. Thank me later.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I was excited to take financial modeling however its turned out to be a statistics class. I understand that the models are backed by statistics but its to the point where only the geniuses in the class are doing well. Prof Farnsworth is the best and its a great class to learn how to use excel shortcuts. Just be prepared to not know whats goin on...

Class title is a little misleading but still great stuff nonetheless. It is more of an advanced statistics class than "financial modeling". Not doing LBOs or DCFs so forget about that lmao. Definitely good for learning some Excel shortcuts and touching up on your linear algebra/advanced math.

Prof farnsworth is the best professor I've taken at TCU. DONT take him if you don't go to class/dont care about actually learning the material. No tests but there are quizzes every class that are very difficult (avg can be between a 40-80) I only got a 100 like 3 times. He curves it tho. I learned more in this class then any other class so I reccom
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Farnsworth is the best professor I have had at TCU. The financial modeling class is difficult, but it is definitely doable. There is little to no work out of class and as long as you are engaged you learn a ton about finance and Excel tools. Also, he provides great recaps before quizzes.
BEWARE!!! Do not take his financial modeling class. The worst class I've ever taken at TCU for sure. Don't do it to yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The financial modeling class is the hardest, craziest finance class I have ever taken. And it's an elective!! There's a quiz/project every single class. They are tough and he does not prepare you well for them. He is very fast-paced and does not slow down. I have approx. 50% in the class which translates to a B-. Insane. Haven't learned anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIS FINANCIAL MODELING CLASS. It was the hardest and worst class I have ever taken at TCU. He expects all this prior knowledge it is not a good elective. I genuinely learned nothing because the class is so confusing and difficult. If you want to stress over an elective take it. You will spend all your time on this class it is horrible!!

Farnsworth is an amazing professor. You will have to work hard to get an A, but he is available for help and his lectures are very informative. My only complaint is he speaks very fast so lectures can be hard to keep up with. He is a super goofy guy and wants his students to succeed.

He's super goofy and you learn a lot. I wouldn't say it's an easy A, but if you show up to lectures you'll do fine. He explains things really well and answers all the questions you could have. Don't buy the book; I literally never opened it and got over 100% on an exam. I would take a class with him again.

This course was not what I was expecting, but the skills and techniques we learned were exactly what one would expect at this level. Dr. Farnsworth had high expectation for the knowledge level of the class and taught based on that, but was also very willing to go back and supplement areas where individuals were weak. Can't recommend enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Farnsworth is incredibly knowledgable. No textbook needed, but you have to go to class to understand the powerpoints. He has pop quizzes but nothing you cant study during the 5 minutes prior to class starting. The WEM assignments are short and good prompts. He is always willing to help and clarify whenever you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: This was his first year at TCU, and he killed it. Lots of quizzes but helps your grade and is good preparation for exam. Exams are mostly short answer and some multiple choice, but this allows you to get partial credit. Curves class majorly depending on grades. Super friendly and nice. Always willing to help with anything! Will take again if I can!

She was one one of the easiest classes I have taken.  Attendance is mandatory and it's a pretty boring class but she really sympathizes with the students.   The class almost always goes the whole time but its a easy class to get out of the way and shes an easy grader.
Best professor I've ever had!

Amazing professor. She cares about you so much and will help you anytime you need it. Just make sure you read the books! She knows when you don't in your essays and you will not do well at all. Really good professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Saffyre is super understanding in every aspect of the class whether its a personal matter or a class matter. Get 6 skips for attendance. We have like 3 books I think and the essays are really well outlined and straight forward. There is a late work policy and have time to submit the paper a week late. Easy grader for the most part
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Falkenberg is really respectful and understanding to her students. There's a lot of group work and reading but as long as you do your part there's nothing to fret. She is very approachable and willing to help you. She is not bias about opinions when grading either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Falkenberg is one of the most laid-back teachers you will ever have if you decide to take her course. I took her for Intro to Women's Writing and I actually never went to class. The assignments are the same every class and I would just do them ahead of the due date, it's basically the same lesson plan every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: TAKE HER!!! She is very liberal but honestly it doesn't matter because she is so sweet. This whole class is a big book club and it is so fun if your class makes it fun. Mostly women (it is women's lit after all) but everyone was so down to chit chat every class. It is a lot of discussion but it's chill don't worry. She really cares abt you. Easy A!

One of my favorite professors I've had! The class is discussion based and there is a reading due before every class, but they're always interesting and the discussions are very engaging. She is very flexible and understanding when it comes to extensions, but the assigned projects are actually fun to work on. Absolutely take her classes.
Great teacher- really cares about her students. The entire class is drafting, revising, and editing your papers, but she gives lots of feedbacks and helps a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: I love this woman. She is amazing. I am not an English person but I had so much fun in this class. The only grades were a few papers and some peer responses. They were tricky and she is a tough grader but she wants you to do well. She responds very quickly to emails and she is so nice. Made me work for the A but I would take this class over again!!

She is such a kind woman and she co-taught this class with Dr. Lowry. I learned so much from her and felt very cared for and appreciated. That being said, the class is super paper-heavy so get ready to write and occasionally the grading can be a bit tough. Work hard though and you will love the class and Ms. Falkenberg!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The section I took of this class was 3 hours long which sounds awful but Professor Faris made it a lot easier. Something I really loved was the fact that she gave us a dinner break every class period. Final is a group project which could be annoying with a bad group, but easy project. Tests do require studying but super straightforward.

Dr. Faris is amazing! She is really sweet and always keeps her lectures engaging. I would definitely recommend her class whether you are a child dev major or not. This class covers lots of important information that everyone should know! Overall, the class is worth taking!

Loved Dr. Faris! This class is def lecture-heavy, so if you want to pass the 4 exams you might want to pay attention. Along with the exams, you have a graphic organizer that is very easy to do, as well as a group project at the end where you apply what you've learned to the real world. This class was fairly easy, especially if you are a CHDV major
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Faris is amazing at what she does. She really knows the subject material and although there are a lot of lectures, they aren't boring. Tests and quizzes are easy if you study and pay attention. This class requires work, but an A is very achievable. She also offers extra credit that helps a lot! I learned a lot from her and this class!
Easy class, Faris is very caring and passionate about the subject

Dr. Faris is a very understanding professor whose assignments are worthwhile and engaging. Lectures are relevant, current, and never boring. She incorporated group projects, a variety of activities, and reading material that got me excited about each course topic. I highly recommend taking Dr. Faris' courses!

I love Dr. Faris!!!! This is the second class I've taken of hers, and I'd pick her for any class she teaches. She is seriously amazing, and I'd recommend her for any class you can have her. She is so caring and sweet and makes the information so interesting. This class is really fun and really not that hard. She is my favorite professor at TCU!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. However, I still learned a lot. I didn't pay much attention in class yet still learned a lot from the tests and projects. She is very caring and understanding and makes the material very easy to learn. I would recommend her for an easy A. She also gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit.

One of my favorite classes. I would highly recommend it to anyone. Mrs. Faris was caring, easygoing, and was always wiling to help. Lecture slides covered all the material being tested on, 2 unexcused absences were given, and all projects and assignments were very straightforward. She also was very prompt in responding to emails.

This class was probably one of the best classes I have had at TCU! You learn a lot and with a minuscule amount of work. She keeps the class interesting and provides a test review for every test. The final was open book and open note! to do well, pay a little bit of attention in class and follow what her test review says. Great Class!

Faggella-Luby is great! You can tell that he really cares about his students and wants us to do well. His lectures are amazing and he is very engaging. There is one group project and a few major quizzes throughout the semester, but if you prepare they are not bad. I feel way more prepared for being a teacher after taking him!
He's awesome!

Dr. FL is the most caring professor I've ever had. I would put this man in charge of the Dept. of Ed because he could change it, seriously. His grading is clear and he never tries to trick you. He wants what is best for every student, and he cares about his students as people. This class is eye-opening and incredibly helpful for future teachers

This man is the absolute best professor I have ever had. He is also just a wonderful human being who cares deeply about each of his students and wants you to do well. His class is a requirement for Education majors, but I would take this class even if it wasn't. He prepares you very well for exams and is always available to help you!

MFL is a great teacher! He is outgoing and energetic, which makes his class entertaining. If you do your best on all assignments, you will pass. He does not give exams- instead he gives quizzes and papers. He treats all his students as individuals and cares about every single one of them.

Her World In News class was pretty easy overall. A lot of assigned readings, but no tests with one final at the end. Project in between that is fun because you get to write letters to international students. It is all discussion based and talks about interesting topics that are relevant today.

I had her for my first honors class and she was incredibly sweet and caring. She genuinely wants her students to succeed. The class is reading-heavy, but she adjusts the pace based on how the class is doing and makes expectations clear. You can tell she's truly engaged and passionate. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very sweet and caring professor who genuinely wants her students to succeed. The class is reading-heavy, but she adjusts the pace based on how the class is doing and makes expectations clear. You can tell she's truly engaged in her work and passionate about the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would prepare yourself for lots of reading, it's about 30-50 pages of annotations every other day (NO SHE DOES NOT PROVIDE THEM), everything is printed on your own. Do not buy frog prints; you have a $30 limit on your library card, use that instead. Overall, her feedback is rude and passive-aggressive. Take someone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took "The World in the News" HCOL. Read & annotate a few articles in preparation for every class. Discussion-based class format. No tests. The way she speaks can be difficult to listen to, but she has a lot of interesting points to contribute and is unique in her perspective, particularly at TCU.

I took Professor Ferebee's Era of Environmental class and it was very easy, but also very boring at times. Only grades are nightly annotated readings that are turned in everyday, project and paper, and final reflection. Super easy A if you do the work. It's just extremely boring most days because you sit there, and don't take notes.
Class is easy but she is a terrible teacher

Dr. Ferebee picks extreme favorites. If you aren't a typical "honors" kid (if you know what i mean) she wont like you and the way she grades you will be reflective of this. She picked on me and discriminated against me all semester and was extremely rude. DONT TAKE HER.

I took Dr. Ferebee's Environmental Crisis class and had an amazing experience. Reading is required outside of class, but she provides all the resources and it is 10 pages a night max. Quizzes are very straightforward and easy, and all assignments are completed during class. 50% of grade is a presentation at end of course but she is an easy grader

I took the honors class Era of Environmental Crisis, and it was both informative and easy. There are assigned readings but you can get away with not reading them. Quizzes are easy as long as you study. Dr. Ferebee was funny and knowledgeable in the content. Final project was easy and she is helpful as long as you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ferebee is a very easy professor to get honors credit out of the way. She has a clear grading style; although the material isn't always interesting, you can avoid paying attention. In-class worksheets go toward your grade but are easy, so attendance is recommended. Quizzes are exactly like the study guides, and the final project was very easy

Dr. Ferebee is the perfect person to teach the War on Terror. She cares a lot about the information. She cares a lot about her students and has been super helpful. All you have are discussion posts, quizzes, process writings (short essays), and the final exam. You have to keep up, but it is super doable and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Took The War on Terror. The class involves quizzes but you are given essentially every question that will be on the test. The biggest grades are 3 big essays, which you NEED to be very knowledgeable about the material in order to get a good grade. There is reading that you need to do for class everyday, but it isn't technically required.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I was so excited to take Narratives of Climate Change, but this professor was terrible. Grading was all over the place and not consistent. I got grades anywhere from a 70 to a 100 for the same type of assignment; there was no difference in the quality of my work. Her lectures are boring and lack diversity in perspective. Don't take her class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This professor was absolutely terrible. I would have to drag my feet to class every other morning not only because she was sooooo boring, but attendance was mandatory (if you skipped more than 3 classes your grade would drop a letter grade). Her grading is rough and she is so unhelpful. AVOID her honors class at all cost!!!

Undoubtedly hardest course taken at TCU. Daily lectures & assigned readings. Her grading is often far too strict. She was hardly available to meet with outside of class & was extremely impersonable. Way too difficult for a core credit and although the content itself is interesting she made class unbearably boring. Don't take if not a strong writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's a good professor. Gives extra credit and goes out of her way to make sure you don't fall behind for a bad grade. The reason she didn't get a 5 from me is that she doesn't stand out. She can also come off as insensitive and rude at times, but I think that's just a cultural thing. For the class, Hard Tests and death by PowerPoint lectures.

Tests are tough, they only make up half of your grade though. The homework and quizzes are very easy. Getting an A is tough, but not impossible. Study the slides + everything you hear in class THOROUGHLY; test questions are specific. Prof is great and genuinely wants you to succeed. She might come off as mean, but it's clearly not her intention to.

Prof Falcone is one of the kindest professors at TCU. She cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. The class consists of two exams and one cumulative final. The tests can be somewhat difficult, so it's important to study. Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are in-class questions that count toward your grade. Best SCM professor!

Professor Falcone is a great SCM professor who truly cares about her students. The class has three tough MC exams (last one is cumulative), a group project, and light homework. No cheat sheets on the first two exams, so study the slides. Attendance isn't required, but in-class questions help. She's fair, offers extra credit, and is very supportive.

Falcone is the best prof to take for SCM! She cares about her students and wants you to succeed. Three exams, group project, and minimal amount of hw. Exams are MC but kinda hard so pay attention to lecture slides. Attendance isn't mandatory but in-class question points can impact grade so GO. She makes class fun and offers extra credit.

Ellie is an amazing teacher that truly does want her students to do well. The class content is difficult in nature so not an easy class, but if you review slides before hand, pay attention, and take notes you will succeed.

Professor Falcone was a phenomenal teacher who really cares about her students. Exams are overall difficult due to it being information heavy, but she gives plenty of other assignments to make up for it. She is a very genuine person who cares about her students. Would recommend taking her!

Dr. Falcone is an amazing supply chain professor. Make sure to review the slides for the three exams, supply chain is an extremely hard subject that takes time to understand. No homework but be willing to put in the time to study.

One of the engaging lecture classes I've ever taken. Professor Falcone has a gift for teaching and truly wants to watch her students grow. She is so supportive (especially if you attend her office hours!). The tests can be moderately challenging, but she gives you everything you need to succeed, and she's always there to help you! TAKE HER CLASS!

Let me start by saying I wish she taught more courses! She is a great professor who has very engaging lectures and activities. She truly cares about her students and wants to watch them grow. Her course is moderately challenging, but she encourages you and gives you everything you need to succeed (and even more if you go to her office hours!).

Amazing professor you can tell she genuinely cares about what she is teaching and how her students do. Taught me a lot about supply chain and made it an interesting class that I looked forward to going to. It is a hard class no matter what, but she makes taking it interesting with her lectures and teaching.

I enjoyed her class—she's really kind and wants you to learn. The first test might seem like common sense, but make sure to study for it. If you pay attention in class, you'll be fine. She has office hours and makes the class funny, which helps you remember stuff. Also, no simulations, which is great! Take her for supply chain.

Prof. Falcone really cares for her students and their success in her class. The class is lecture heavy and done through TopHat rather than D2L. Her exams are quite difficult, but by doing A LOT of studying, they are manageable. The other assignments in the class make up for the difficulty of exams. You will definitely learn a lot with her.

I do not know where the hate comes from, Professor Falcone is a very understanding professor who wants to see her students excel and helps them in all ways possible. She is very accessible and open to all questions to help all student's needs. She is very engaging in class too with many simulations, games, and group activities. She is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's nice and clearly wants students to succeed. Grading on assignments and group projects are fair. That being said, the exams are no joke. 50 MCQs on all 3 of them, and the last one is cumulative. No cheat sheet on the first 2, so you need to be very good at memorization. I took the exams seriously, but I still barely ended with an A.

Professor Falcone is a very caring teacher that truly cares about her students. She responds to emails very quick outside of the class. The tests are difficult but if you are actually studying it will be manageable. Overall, great teacher and learned a lot.

I'm not sure where the positive reviews are coming from. Trust me - do NOT take her class. She rushes through the material, overwhelming you with too much information at once. I would strongly recommend avoiding this course if you want a clear and manageable learning experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take Professor Falcone! She's the best supply chain professor for sure. No textbook, everything's done through an online platform. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you get points for quizzes that cover the previous class's material so you probably won't do well if you don't go. She's so nice and willing to work with you if you ever need anything!

Professor Falcone is a very caring individual who values her students a lot. While the class is an introductory class you learn a great deal of material in a short period of time. It may seem daunting at first, but it gets easier as the semester goes on. I have enjoyed her class and will miss her once I am done.

Advise for Future Students:

Read the slides before class since it helps a lot. Stay organized and don't leave assignments for the last minute. Elie is one of the best professors. She is welcoming, helpful, and wants you to succeed. Go to office hours and don't skip class; lectures are key to doing well on exams.

Supply chain is a tough subject, but Professor Falcone makes it manageable with clear guidance, helpful tips like reading slides beforehand, and engaging in-class activities. She truly cares about her students' success and emphasizes real understanding. Put in consistent effort, study a little each day, be an active participant, and you'll succeed.

She truly cares about her students and supports their success. She explains concepts clearly and makes the material engaging - office hours too. Skim slides and take notes before class so you can pay attention to the teachings. Don't cram—repetition and understanding the big picture are key. Study with peers to test and deepen your understanding.

Do not take this professor. At the beginning she seemed kind. However, the class quickly took a turn. 3 exams and a group project, but no final. Her exams do not cover any of the content from class. They are super specific. Average on each exam has been around a 75. Also, no simulation or opportunities for extra credit. Every other class can.
Tests are hard!!! She makes them sound way easier than they will be. Also, attendance is technically optional but 50 points are based on your quiz scores which are done at the beginning each class.

Would not recommend. She talks too much and presents very little useful info. Exams are super specific and barely cover what's discussed in class. Exam reviews are pointless. Worst part—she roasts students if they answer wrong. Not a supportive environment at all.

Avoid at all costs. Tests are all application based where studying barely helps. Average test score was a 73% on exams. Super degrading when students try to answer her questions. Lectures the whole class and makes you pay for homework assignments and top hat where its super unnecessary. Her quiz questions are nothing like her test questions.
