She is not understanding at all & is very passive aggressive. Claims attendance is not mandatory but is unwilling to help with assignments if you do miss class. 2/10 do not recommend

Prof. Gailey is super kind and knowledgeable. This class was definitely interesting but also one of the harder sociology classes I've taken. Assignments aren't too hard, there is just a good amount of reading and in my opinion, some of the readings can be dense so for someone who doesn't know much about gender in society it can be hard to take in.

Professor Gailey classes are mainly discussion based. Be prepared to participate and give personal opinions on controversial and difficult conversations. There are a couple papers, a group project, and 10 other check in assignments. The class work isn't too difficult or time consuming and attendance isn't really enforced.

Highly recommend taking any class Dr. Gailey teaches! This is the second class I have taken with her and she is a phenomenal lecturer. She makes sure to explain concepts and topics thoroughly, goes in-depth during class, and the course super organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Gailey is very straightforward and wants you to succeed. I didn't think I was going to do well in the class, but her midterm and final were extremely straightforward. She provided the essay questions far in advance, so you had plenty of time to go back through the readings. Key statements weren't very fun, but they prepared you for the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is literally such an easy A. Would recommend. Gailey is such a nice professor.

Professor Gailey was a great professor! Really passionate about sociology!  Pretty easy exams as long as you study her study guide! Takes notes during her lectures, fill out the study guide and then you will do fine on the exams. Not an easy A but definitely attainable. There is reading for pretty much every class, but its very interesting material
The bottom line is that if you show interest in the class he will like you and it will guarantee an A. His humor is raw and he can be blunt at times but you will enjoy going to his class everyday.

Going to class where either Dr. Galvin or Dr. Hestir explain the text is essential to understanding what each philosopher is saying, so make sure to attend class and take detailed notes. They really care about their students, try to make class engaging, and are eager to help you! The TA is also very helpful when it comes to writing your papers.

This class was ALL about reading before each class and just sitting there listening to Galvin rant about random things - super hard to follow and most of the time not even related to the readings. If you participate, he will like you, if not your essay grades will probably will not be as good. Also he can be pretty offensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Philosophy classes are usually graded with large subjectivity, however, papers graded in this class were disproportionately subjective.  Papers of similar quality graded +/- 15%. The professors care very little, one skipping most classes.  Lectures do not relate to pertinent material needed for the papers.  Most students do poorly.  Avoid the class

I was personally confused by his lectures and did not understand what he was trying to get across to the students for us to put in our essays. There are no tests or quizzes, but it is reliant on all writing, so if you have issues with big writing class, it may not be the best to take. If you do, strongly suggest using writing center to help you.

Dr. Galvin truly cares for his students and really tries to push us as students to fully understand the material. There was never a class where he didn't make me laugh. Definitely take Dr. Galvin if you have the opportunity to!

This class is all lecture and papers. I didn't have a single test, even the final was a paper. However, I wouldn't say that's a bad thing. This was the first class I took in college that made me really think, and I loved it. He's really engaging, and even the discussions are fun. He will go off syllabus if he (or the class) feels like it.

Philosophy of Law, AMAZING TEACHER AND PERSON. No quizzes. Tests are short essays. (final is a 5 page essay) you have to buy the packet from the print shop. I would read to help you understand but its not necessary as he explains very well in class - even when you dont read you understand it through his teaching. Downside - does not use D2l

Alright here's the low down on Galvin. He likes to make beer jokes and leaves no sacred ground untouched with his biting and offensive humor. If you want an easy time, look elsewhere. If you want someone to teach you (and have an open mind) he's your man! If you get offended easily, run away! If you can take the heat, I deeply suggest this class.

I had Dr. Galvin for Intro to Philosophy. His lectures are pretty clear-cut and he knows what he's talking about. He has a sense of humor that some may find a bit crude but I enjoyed it and he always made me laugh at least once during lectures. He is a pretty nice guy and can answer pretty much any question you may have

Hardest phil professor of the four in my class. Didn't like him. All he did was yell the things he said and curse. He was very rude and his comments were unnecessary. He doesn't make sense. The class itself is already super hard.
Galvin is an amazing professor. Those who criticize his style do not really understand Philosophy. He cracks jokes to make the concepts he teaches easier to grasp and remember.

This guy will put you too sleep. Grades way too hard on the midterm papers, and thinks its cool to curse as much as he can. Its okay to have a little fun but sometimes he just gets annoying. Don't take Advanced Philosophy of Law, won't do anything except bore the life out of you all semester. I'm an econ major and its also titled Law & Econ. 3 prof

Galvin is a great teacher, but to do well in his class, you have to have the skill of taking good notes straight from the lecture without powerpoint or the board being used. MMM is a very difficult class but he does a great job making sure everyone understands everything.

Galvin does an amazing job of keeping a class captivated. He talks about the ideas he has such obvious zeal for with such enthusiasm it is hard to not get caught up in them. Yes he is sarcastic. Yes he is cynical. But, the rude comments on here do not truly capture the meaning behind what they see as rudeness for the sake of being rude. Brilliant!

Probably one of the most ridiculous classes I've taken. The entire class was always lost; ideas were never fully explained. The TA was more help than the profs; review sessions saved my grade. Profs basically say you won't make an A in the class and that remains true. They assign a philosophy paper and expect it written in a style they never teach.

He's passionate about his stuff, but he often didnt finish his lectures and we were expected to know what we didnt make it to. If you cant take your beliefs being challenged, dont take him, because he will.
He is a very good proffesor, but you will have to keep an open mind when he teaches or else when he lectures, some of the things he says may offend you.

One of the more eloquent and intelligent teachers I've had so far. If you are evangelical, it is not recommended that you take his classes, since he will effectively challenge you. If you can't take that, don't take the course. That said, if you enjoy thinking about problems of ethics, his section is the best in the intro class.

Most of the negative comments regarding Galvin come from whiney evangelical Christians who don't know how to challenge their beliefs. Galvin is hilarious and extremely intelligent. Take this class if you're willing to check your dogma at the door, you won't regret it.

Galvin's lectures were full of crude examples and cussing... they were sometimes hilarious and sometimes just plain distracting. I would come out of the class saying "what was the point of that?" and to this day probably couldn't tell you anything about philosophy. However, he is really nice on one-to-one encounters! Overall wouldn't recommend him.

I can see why some people may be ticked off by Galvin, but I had very different beliefs than him and wasn't offended at all!  He is SO passionate about what he's teaching, and his lectures are always very interesting.  He's very helpful and nice outside of class.  I recommend him - if you take him, you'll learn a lot!

intro to philosophy is a horrible class! 3 professors stand and lecture about things; when it comes to the test you have no idea what to do! the term papers were ridiculous, you tons of quizzes and response papers, it is impossible to do well on anything because they expect you to know the exact phrases to put on the paper and if not you get a C

Intro Philosophy was an ok class, but the sessions with Galvin made me want to jump out the window.  I personally don't care about his belief system, but the fact that he just spouts obnoxious derogatory comments about anyone who's not a lonely old man who's mother didn't hold him enough. I also don't like when he sits there and stares at you.

I don't know where the negative comments are coming from, but these folks are surely not putting themselves into the material. Galvin is EXTREMELY BRIGHT and remarkably generous with his time. Granted, the material is not easy, but nothing worthwhile is. And he does all he can to make it digestible for his students. A jewel at TCU.

Extremely unprofessional and lazy.  I agree with most of his personal beliefs but he is tacky and tactless in his comments during class.  He is one of the worst profs I have had at TCU and I am a senior.

If you think you're going to law school, you should definitely check both of the law classes out. Of course Galvin's awesome and so much nicer than he seems. If you're conservative, just keep your head down and everything will be alright. The grade will be tough if you make it tough.

Sure, he might get his point across, but Galvin does so as obnoxiously as possible.  He sits in the calss every day, even when he's not teaching, and just stares at the students.  His points and lectures are incredibly slanted and his humor is derogatory, unecessary, and directed toward whatever views he considers false.

This guy is hilarious. He really knows his stuff and he's extremely enthusiastic about the material. He could make anything interesting - keeps everyone captivated. I love how at least once every session he mentions getting **** on Guinness.
Easy to understand and actually interesting!  Tells lots of stories.  Not easy, but works with students to ensure their success.

He constantly challenges one to not only be able to construct his own philosophically sound opinions on various complex topics, but also how to cut through the crap in flimsy or fallacious arguments. I took more classes from him than any other single professor. If you are really interested in learning something, take one of his classes.
Know your three stooges, Woody Allen, and Kant. 'Nuff said.

okay, Galvin is a very cynical person.  "I'm in a bad mood and I am taking it out on each and every one of you until further notice."  Yuck.  He is very smart, though.  The most entertaining of the four.

Galvin is an extraordinary professor, if not in the most obvious fashions. He is unbelievably dedicated to sheparding his students and leading them toward a genuine understanding of complex ideas. One would be a fool to not take his classes while at TCU.
Incredibly brilliant prof.  Interesting lectures.  Best of the team that teaches intro.
I had him for IntroPhil, which is team-taught by all of the faculty. Go to the review sessions.
Galvin's style is intense and impassioned. If you're having trouble go and talk to him, he's always eager to help.
Galvin is a great guy.  Once you get use to his teaching style the class should be cake.
No Comments

Professor Gaul is so sweet! She really is passionate about what she talks about which keeps class interesting. There were only 3 writing exams which were all pretty easy. There are multiple readings that sometimes she quiz you on, but its very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I would Professor Gaul is a typical Women and Genders studies professor. Even during Covina-19, she didnt let off the gas and was persistent the students performed at a high level. Learned some things but nothing useful that Ill need down the road.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lots of reading quizzes that are super specific, also after 3 absences your grade goes down SIGNIFCIANTLY, if you participate she will love you
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lots of work to be done in this class, but it gives you a solid direction on how to analyze literature for future classes.  This is a class that is a round table discussion, so it's basically like going to a book club all semester.  Her directions are very clear and is willing to work with students with disabilities.  Wonderful class and enjoyed it
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Other people have mentioned she's pro white .. I would tend to agree. Not much else to say. Good luck.

Dr. Gaul is a great woman, but a very egotistical teacher. She assumes students taking her class have no other classes, homework, or other extra curriculum activities. TONS of reading, reflecting and SO MUCH WRITING. I do not recommend anyone taking this class unless you enjoy your time being taken up by countless hours of writing and reflecting.

Terrible professor...not very personable, conservatives were told to keep an open mind and opinions to yourself...overload on readings...missing class resulted in lower grade...horrid...do not take...
She's a great teacher but very challenging. If you meet with her throughout the process of writing major papers her guidance is very helpful. Not an easy A but definitely worth the time.
Dr. Gaul is fabulous--a knowledgeable and witty professor.  Her courses always are a joy to attend, for they are enticing and intellectually stimulating.   A must-take for any literature aficionado!

Very nice.  This is the second semester I've taken her.  Lots of reading, but it's Literature, so...  Inconsistent grader, I think (not over the course of both semesters, but from week to week).  Sometimes she seems like a fair grader and other times she goes harder on you.  Be prepared for either way.

Great professor.  She is encouraging and if you read you will be prepared.  Take notes and you will have no problems with the exams or quizzes.  She is tough on grading but fair.  I learned a lot in her class.

Dr. Gaul is a great professor! The classes are discussion based, so if you just read your assignments and chat a little about it in class. You'll be completely prepared for her exams. The final in Intro to Drama, wasn't essay, but rather a fun play you put on as a group project.

An A has to be earned-you have to read the stuff but if you do, the quizzes are easy.  She is very accessible outside of class and very willing to work with you.  The class itself was discussion oriented and interesting.
A decent professor...she can be tough sometimes, but maybe that was because the class I took was online.  The class structure was interesting, and it made it more fun to be involved in discussions!

Regardless of other rating - Great prof! Likes class discussions and likes those who speak up. Make sure you elaborate on every answer you write about and think creatively-it will help you greatly! I got an A in the class easily, and if you genuinely try, she will notice. Overall I really enjoyed her class - highly recommended! =)
Ugh!  Boring class, teacher isn't confident.  She is a TWA, teacher with attitude.  Students she don't like get the attitude.  Think twice and then another.

This class is a good if you need a literature credit and it will not cause you to be up all night studying. Just come to class, do the readings and act interested in the class. Dr. Gaul is a decent professor and you will get a lot out of the class.

Dr. Gaul is a wonderful professor, but she is a tough grader. If you want a good grade, you must go into elaborate detail on anything you write for her. Plays are okay and the quizzes help your grade if you read. Tests are completely essay, but instead of a final, you get to do a fun group project.

She's a very nice professor but grades a little tough. Tests are pure essay and she doesn't take bs. Most of the plays are pretty boring even though she tries to make them interesting. Not a bad class - there's no final, just a group dramatization.

The person who thinks she is pro-white is an idiot; did you pay no attention to the things she said and the way she acted all semester long?  Did it ever occur to you that maybe you took the overheard conversation out of context?  She is a champion for those groups who have been oppressed by whites.

Very intersting class. Many quizzes which help your grade only if you read the plays. Tests are straighforward, but the online 'discussion' board postings seem to just be boring busywork. A group dramatization occurs at the end of the semester, but no final.

If you are non-WHITE...STAY AWAY!!!  Very critical of people who don't look like her!  I overheard her in her office speaking poorly about a student to the chair of the eng. dept. She wasn't trying to keep her voice down either. Stay away....PLEASE!!!!

Very unfair in grading.  I think the best grade anyone had on a paper was a B, and that was what she considered to be "very good".  She doesn't explain what she wants and is j/a horrible person in general.  She may send you mail if you're not a GREAT student and bein from the south is an auto F
No Comments

The trick to this class is to rent the books on tape from the Ft Worth lib. It is the only way to keep up with the reading. And if you fall behind on the listening, just read pinkmonkey. The tests are easy though. Take this class, it really is no bad.
She's really intense and very prompt.  Overall a great prof!

Okay, so yeah she starts class on time and you have to read a lot--but this is COLLEGE!  And she teaches ENGLISH!  As an English  major, I think she's awesome.  I want to take more of her classes.  She's  really nice and fair, and she knows her stuff. She
Umm all yall need to stop trippin.  dont read the books! read summaries from pinkmonkey notes or spark notes... EASY A! go to class, pay attention, be able to do intepreting well and BAM easy A =)

Dr. Gaul is extremely intense. She starts class at 10:59 for her 11am class, so if you're a late person beware! There's a lot of reading so if you don't like to read literature watch out.  She's not very personable though.

Unless you like alot of reading do not take this class... It is almost impossible to keep up with the readings.. You start a new book before you even take a test on the last.. other than that she is nice and if you read it is pretty much a guarenteed B

She's a nice lady, but the class is damn annoying. If you can't keep up with EXTREMELY HEAVY READING don't even look twice at this class. Her in class writings are a **** and the tests take longer than the actual class. Overall... take something else

Professor Garcia provides unclear instructions & will minimize a students who asks for clarification/help, is a harsh grader, is unapproachable, and is honestly just rude. I personally would never recommend taking his course.

Loved this class, he is a great guy cares for his students and tries to make lectures fun and interactive. YES he does give a lot of papers but was very lenient and pushed deadlines for students. He is a little hard headed and feels strong about his opinions but was never rude. If you listen and respect him they he will respect you as well. NO TEST
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. It's his way or the highway. He is extremely disrespectful and is not afraid to put down a student or single one out for privilege. Couple that with nonstop reading and busy work (always due on Saturday nights) and you have a horrible class on your hands. Thank god I figured out how to cheat my way through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Don't take this guy. Listen to the reviews. Never had such a joyless experience in any class in my entire life. I worked so hard, clearly hard enough to earn an A, but he repeatedly gave me poor grades according to my own opinions. Even failed me on my final where I went above and beyond the prompt and did all the possible work. POS. DON'T TAKE HIM
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The most unorganized professor.Assignment directions are unclear & due dates change constantly (once a discussion topic changed the day it was due) Doing work before the last minute is impossible because he doesn't open things up until the day of.Doesn't respect students & gets combative in discussions.Class is easy but isn't worth the headache

Dr. Garcia has absolutely no idea how to run a college class. His inability to use D2L makes it so that you are responsible for doing the quizzes the day that they are due, without any reminder in class. He will simply assign a 3-hour video to watch or a 40-page essay to read every week and get mad if you don't extensively cite it. DO NOT TAKE!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Pro: funny, wants you to succeed, content applicable to life, plenty of chances to get a good grade
Cons; lots of reading, frequent essays, must participate, must be able to apply knowledge but this isn't hard
I learned a lot and am thankful for the class. If you can fit a little extra work I do think this class will benefit your life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His class comes with a bit of work but nothing unmanageable. Mostly 3-page essays, a weekly discussion post, and a take-home quiz. There will be weeks without work, but he does expect you to read the reading assignments he gives. Some days his way of giving participation points is by open dialogue of the assignment. He always takes attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: LISTEN TO THE REVIEWS. I didn't. Don't make the same mistake I did. Do not take him for an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The first month was great and I actually learned a lot of important material, but then it went downhill from there. Professor Garcia would be rude and disrespectful towards students. He spent entire class times complaining about how students turned in assignments incorrectly. Asked him a question and he then chewed me out over email.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: No tests.  If you participate and show up that is a huge part of your grade.  Lots of papers but not a tough grader on them.  Get things turned in, completed and on time and you will get a good grade.  Lots of extra credit opportunities, nice guy if you make an effort and wants to give you an A.

Participating in his class can be very difficult to do as his lecture goes on for the entire class time. You need to be attentive of the syllabus as he will not send any reminders for when assignments are due. You must pay very close attention to his lectures. Will not remind you when class is canceled or what he calls "library days".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Cant work technology forgets everything, is not organized

DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER! Every week you have a three+ page paper that is due about some wack topic that makes no sense at all. You have to choose among three choices that he then chooses from, and you can't have a single option that any other classmate picked. One of the worst teachers I have ever had the displeasure of having. Multiple 3+ papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Jerry Garcia will give you multiple readings a week that he claims you should read, but they will take you like 3 hours and will add no value to the class. He will also assign many papers which although are not graded hard, he gives weird timelines for doing them and is not clear on instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was something I dreaded to come too. He takes attendance everyday even though he says he won't. He also assigns so much work each week with 3+ assignments due each week. He expects so much from you and doesn't take into consideration any other classes that are on your plate. You will need to read, write, present, and take many quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Garner is awesome! very passionate and engaging professor! He cares about you and TCU. His exam are not hard if you pay attention! he gives good details and examples that make it easy to remember things. He loves jokes and participation! I recommend him! Not a lot of homework either

This class is not hard by any means but I just did not agree with some of the things that were being taught. I had to sit through and listen to things that I and a lot of my classmates did not believe in that were played on videos about political views. I just think it caused some issues for me personally so I would not take again.

Professor Garner is a great professor. His first 2 exams are hard but the final is much easier. There's 4 case studies that help boost your gpa but you have to work for them. There's a final paper and presentation that is to be done with your assigned group throughout the semester for the end. He cares about his students and want them to succeed.
Nice guy, with great lectures. The final project is not too boring. However, somewhat of a tough grader and grades depends too much on exams.

Garner is a nice guy, but he has a fair amount of issues as a professor. For one, he takes a lifetime to grade the handful of assignments we receive. When he does grade them, he leaves little to no feedback, and is extremely inconsistent with his criteria. I got an A on one Case Study and practically replicated the same format just to get a B-.

Dr. Garner is a good professor. However, the bulk of your grade WILL be determined by how well you perform on the tests, which are 25-30 multiple choice questions and 1/2 essays. The essays dont count for anything though, which I find very strange/poorly calculated. This is Schieffer why is my grade being determined by a scantron? Makes no sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Garner is great! His lectures are clear, he provides study guides for his exams, and he genuinely cares about his students. The workload isn't as much as other upper-level COMM classes I have taken but it's not a blow-off class either. Make sure you take notes during lectures, he blocks out certain things in his D2L ppts after lectures.

He is such a caring teacher and wants everyone to succeed. You get 4 unexcused absences which is nice, but every absence after will cost you a letter grade, so make sure you go to class! The class is only 50 minutes long, so it's not hard to show up. The tests are hard if you don't study, but he gives you a review of everything that will be on it
One of the best professors I've ever had.
Great professor, probably the greatest in the communication building! Recommend taking all of his course!
Love this class! I am learning a lot from Dr. Garner. He is great and is very passionate about teaching organizational communication. I love coming to his class!

Of all the Org Comm classes in all the universities in all the world, Dr. Garner's is the best. His humor allows for lively discussions on thought-provoking and rigorous topics. I highly recommend that you take this class.

Came into it feeling indifferent, but ended up loving the course by the end of the semester. Garner is a great professor that knows how to facilitate really good discussions. His reading were interesting and made me see organizational communication in a new light. Would definitely recommend this class. Awesome sense of humor, take him!
Knows his stuff, keep up w readings.
Dr. Garner is approachable and knowledgeable! His class is great!
Dr. Garner is a god.

Prof is enthusiastic, knowledgable, organized, and has high expectations. To perform well, read all articles each week and take notes, then in class take notes from his questions and the collaborative answers. Easy to get behind if you don't do the readings and take notes.
Awesome!
Johny is the greatest professor. He holds great class discussion, and he makes the content very interesting.

Took him for Org. Comm. & got a B but had to work for it. 1 huge group project mid-way through semester w/ presentation & paper due at the end of it. Talk to him about outline for essay or any ?'s over it. Tests came out of book & were application questions & some basic matching & definition questions. Study the reviews & you'll be fine.

Funny professor who is easy to relate to. Attendance is mandatory and he is kind of a hard grader. His powerpoints are straight from the book, so if you read you should do fine on the tests. There is a huge group project with a big paper due at the end of the semester.
He is so nice! He is extremely helpful. Class is mandatory and unfortunately really dull. There are never any quizzes. His tests are difficult and there is a huge semester project.

He is very hard! Attendence is mandatory! You cannot miss more than four times or else he takes off a letter grade. Lectures are great but his tests are hard and it is based on how you can apply what you learn. Be sure to tape record his lectures. Also, there is a group project and be sure to take your paper to writing center. It helps!

Professor Germain was a wonderful teacher who made sure her students understood the subject material and how it could be used to benefit us in the future.  She was extremely kind and engaging to all her students, and made the class much more interesting.

Felt like 95% of the stuff she taught me would not help me become a better engineer. Her code constantly had errors in it and she would spend the next 5 minutes trying to figure out why. Her class was very easy until an absurdly hard end of year project that she gave us during finals week. She at least is a very nice lady and very passionate

She's a wonderful and passionate teacher who loves her job. Accessible outside of class and provides many helpful resources. Makes class enjoyable, offers plenty of extra credit, and gives useful tools for other classes. As long as you attend class or keep up with the material and do your homework, you'll do well on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you don't want to tank your GPA. You are graded on 3 tests and pop quizzes that are only 5 questions, so 1 wrong and you're at an 80. His lectures are hard to follow and he doesn't post them or use D2L, so there's no way to catch up.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Im not good at history and I did fine. There are pop quizzes so keep up with the readings. The exams are easy but the essays are a little difficult so make sure you are prepared. You don't really need the textbook but it is helpful if you are struggling. Do not blow off this class because if you do not study you will not do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Most challenging class I have ever taken in my life. Do not even try to study for the exams because you will not do well. If you are not a History major DO NOT TAKE. I had to drop in November because of how hard I tried and never saw the results.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While he's a nice person, his class is very difficult. Unless you are obsessed with history and can remember every little detail do not take this class. His pop quizzes are very difficult and he doesn't use d2l so you don't know what your grade is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is very interesting; however you need to come to class and listen to the lectures, because powerpoints are only pictures, which could stand for a thousand words, and keep in mind there is not D2L for this course. There are only a total of 3 exams, and unannounced pop quizzes which hurt your grade for one bad grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very hard class - I do NOT recommend. Very hard to take notes during class, he talks nonstop and goes through topics rapidly. You only have three tests and pop quizzes(5 questions each) so rly easy to have a bad grade. the pop quizzes are why I had to drop the class. I also never knew what my grade was because he never updated D2L.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hardest class i have taken at TCU. If you are trying to satisfy your history credit, DO NOT take this class. If you a history major, I would recommend. He teaches class by lecturing the entire class time and only has pictures on the screen. There are no visuals with words because he believes "a picture can stand for 10000 words". Pop quizzes weekly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith lectures really fast with just pictures, so take notes! Although he only "assigns" 20 pages/night, he expects you to read the entire chapter and know every detail in it before the first class of the week. He can also be patronizing at times. I will say though that this is the history class I have learned the most from in my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is super nice and caring, but the class is not easy. he talks super super fast so can to take good notes because he moves from topic to topic so quick. the pop quizzes are 5 questions so are SUPER easy to fail. there is reading every night and a lot of pop quizzes. he does not use TCU online so you do not know what your grade is.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He doesn't provide lecture outlines, he speaks insanely fast, and he jumps from thought to thought so it's next to impossible to get clear, comprehensive notes. He also doesn't use TCU Online. If history is not your major, I would recommend looking for a different teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gene Smith is very passionate about History, but expects students to share his passion and knowledge and spends class yelling his lectures too fast to take notes, with only photos on his slides. His arrogance is apparent, and his teaching style is not effective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I have never had a teacher who didn't genuinely care about students success until I had Gene. He doesn't help you at all. You are required to attend office hours after the first exams when he "helps" you. He told me to take notes while I read (which I was doing) and then made fun of me for not going to a college far enough away from home.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His US History class is a prime example of natural selection. Class started with about 45 people and ended with maybe high 20s. Painful class

I have never struggled more than I have in this class. Dr. Smith's class is only verbal lecture based and the only thing he uses the screen for is pictures. This makes it difficult to take notes as he goes entirely too fast and there is no powerpoint to follow along. His tests and quizzes require you to know literally everything and are impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He goes really fast in his lectures and jumps around a lot with the dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Definitely have to work for your grade but Dr. Smith is very passionate about history and makes the lectures seem like big epic stories. I found the class very interesting. Few tests (multiple choice and essay) and pop reading quizzes make up grade so be prepared. He will help you out if he sees that you have made progress each test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Smith was very helpful in office hours and passionate about the material. My issues with the class were that his quizzes/tests related completely to his lectures and not with the book he assigned us to read for homework. Also only having three tests and pop quizzes made it to where one test will make or break your grade in this class.

This class isn't too bad. You only have three tests and pop quizzes and those are the only grades you have. He is a good teacher and doesn't read directly off of the powerpoint so it makes the class bearable.  You definitely need to go to class and do the readings or you will NOT do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Let's just say that there is a reason the rest of the History dept. refers to him as 'the devil downstairs'. Difficult man and even worse professor, takes joy in mocking his students. Unclear grading system, and class is pretty much just him yelling for an hour and a half. Good luck with this guy!

His classes are geared toward history majors like my self. His lectures are incredibly in depth, but you'll learn that you dont have to write down every word he says, just the stuff pretaining to the list of words he gives you at the start of class. Do your readings, talk to him if you need help and again, do your readings and youll get an A.

this guy is completely full of himself and shouldn't be because he is not that good at his job.  preaches more than he teaches, but his message is self serving.  don't take any classes with him and this opinion is coming from someone who got an A in his class so you know i'm telling the truth!

I am a history major, and I can easily tell you not to take this class unless you want to study your butt off for a B at best. You will learn a lot from this class, but it is SO much reading and work that unless you must take this class, dont! At least not with Smith. There are so many other teachers that give easy As for this class.

I have never met a man so full of himself. History is fun, exciting, and should make you critically think about issue, but not in this class. Made an A by regurgitating the text and learned nothing that my fantastic AP teacher has not already taught me. If you want an intellectually challanging class, look elsewhere...
I'm sorry, but he isn't very good at his job.  He thinks he is a far better professor than what I know he is.

If you don't like reading, don't take this class. you have to read the entire text. random pop quizzes, but he drops the lowest 3 grades so go to class. constant note taking w/ no sigh of relief time, av. of 3 pgs of notes per class. he gives you essay topics in advance but is a tough grader and multiple choice ?s r very tricky at times, no easy a

As a history major i learned alot from him. He give lots of info and really seems to like what he does. Its easy to speak with him out of class and if you get to know him he can be a nice guy. If you dont like reading or taking notes i wouldent suggest this course.

Not a good class to take if you are looking for an easy A. He talks too fast for you to write and his tests are things you never learned. The books are ridiculous and there is no way you can read 100 pages in a night. Dont take him. He is unfair and not worth your time.

Dr. Smith is a good professor but his class is very difficult. You will take a minimum of 3 to 4 pages of notes a class and have a ton of reading to do. He's very good at what he does, but if you're looking for an easy class, I definitely don't reccomend him.
Great prof. Really nice and helpful. I have enjoyed this class and have learned a lot. Thanks!

The class can be very difficult if you cannot keep up with the readings. He gives 3 excused abscences, and then drops your grade for each one afterwards. Gets to know you outside of class and is much nicer in his office environment. Very knowledgeable about history in general, but doesn't always lecture very well. So take GOOD notes and READ!

Do NOT take this professor. You will be reading about 80 pages every two days out of the books, aside from taking 3 pages of notes if you try to get down what he is saying. His tests are very unfair and he grades your essays unfair as well. Difficult guy, hopefully he is gone soon.

He's a great guy. He makes time to meet with each student after the first test to get to know you. He knows his stuff, and class is interesting. Tests not too hard, but have essays and they can be tough.

No doubt the man has great knowledge of the subject and is a decent teacher. Classes were interesting and almost fun but he is a terrible human being who will look you in the eye, smile at you and be your best buddy. Then when you turn away will stab you in the back and twist the knife. Sad but true

He's the DEVIL! My computer caught on fire the night before my paper was due. He gave my 2 more hours, I got a C and busted my butt all semester. The other teachers referred to him to me as, "THE DEVIL Downstairs bc where his office is when i asked them where I could find him. Doesnt suprise me!

Puts completely usless facts into his lecture which causes him to get behind so he's forced to rush through the rest of the material too quickly. I told him my plans for after college and he basically told me I couldn't do it. Worst experience I've ever had. No help at all.
Lots of material in so little time; good teaching, good clarity. There's just soo much history to go over. If you like history, this is the class for you. If not, it's your loss.
My history class in high school was more informative and challenging.  This guy has a fetish for sexual history.
hate this course more than hell itself
Lot's of material...very hard...but makes class very interesting

Long Lectures and always behind.  Great teacher but gets carried away too easy.  Tests aren't bad just cover a lot of material.  Lots of reading throughout semester but spread out nicely.If taking as UCR be ready for some studying. Good experience overall
Get with the program, or get out of the big guy's way.  I've had four history classes and Smith's was the best, aside from all the Jefferson.

Not a hard class but just an awful teacher. She is very confusing, doesn't make things clear, doesn't post grades until randomly at the end, bunch of random assignments that equal one grade. Just a very terrible class to take.

Professor George is absolutely the worst. She I the toughest grader. I would receive feedback on my papers that said "extremely well done" and still receive a low b on the assignment. It is impossible to get an A in this class. She is rude, not understand, and not a nice person. She should not be able to teach at this highly respectable university
She is very nice but is an extremely tough grader. Get ready to write and read over difficult material. Felt like a 3 level class instead of a 1. one of the harder "intro" classes at TCU.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This was the hardest class I've taken at TCU and it shouldn't have been. The lectures were a waste of time, the instructions were unclear almost every time, and she is very critical about the writing. The whole class was a waste of time. It sucked the life out of everyone having to go to class and listen to her talk 3 times a week. Not helpful.

Dr. George is extremely difficult and very controlling in the way she wants things done. If you ask her a question she tends to turn the question on you and embarrass you. Least favorite class in my college career

No textbooks or exams. Doesn't have attendance policy outside of English policy. I'm unsure if she cares if you show up or not. Very easy to talk to and discuss things. A lot depends on your ability to write the various things she asks for. If you have a strong voice you'll be okay. If you don't you may need to get extra help to do what she wants.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: You need to be an english major with hard core interpretation skills to take George (Writing major here). I had to interpret her paper rubric and convert that to a paper. Some papers I didn't know why I got the grade. You will learn material in her class and she is amiable, but if you are not willing to "mine" your grade out of her don't take her.
Dr. George is super helpfull if you are struggling, and is really nice. I learned alot and if you need to take intro to comp. take her, your writing skills will improve SO much.
Very interesting class, the writing assignments can be difficult at times, but she is always willing to help students. A nice lady with a great attitude. I would recommend this teacher.

Took Intro to Comp and the class was alllllll about Dracula.  Im a really bad writer but she is really helpful outside of classand basically writes your paper for you when you go to her office hours.  She is super sweet and you should def take her class.  But there is a TON of writing.  I had to write a 4-6 page paper about once every two weeks.

Very nice lady. She assigns interesting readings. I am not great at writing and this class didn't contain any. She makes the class fun by assigning cool projects, short stories, and novels. Take it! Easy class and is very helpful. Easy A if you read and study for quizzes and tests.
Was a pretty easy class. Always had a paper to write but she was a fair grader and was really specific with what she wanted. I got a B+ and I generally hate writing.
One of my fave Engl classes.  George's attitude is excellant and teaching style is engaging.  Fun writing exercises.  Wants you to be a better writer.  Highly recommend.

She is the sweetest lady ever, she would make a great kindergarten teacher! The class is really interesting if you like fiction, and I highly recommend it! She is SO sweet! The class is an easy A if you pay attention and study for the exams!

Going to the class itself is pointless, but sometime interesting. Class is based around class discussion, so you have to participate. Grade bases on papers and attendence. Papers not difficult. She is a very fair grader. And she is a realy nice lady and has interesting points of view.

i did okay on all the papers but i had most my homework in on time so she gave me an A. as long as you put in a decent effort and show some interest in the class you will do very well. if i can get an A in writing in her class, anyone can

LOVED THIS CLASS! Fewer papers to write than other comp classes and more time. Very leniant if you have a good excuse. Downside: she takes attendance seriously.And sometimes she's a little unclear in her paper feedback, and sets weird due dates.But she's really willing to help, too. Interesting topic! I'd highly recommend.

took this last year. sometimes class is boring and unorganized, but assignments are interesting and she'll love you if you visit her after class with your papers. going to her office is the only way to get an A!
Borathon.

I hate this class..and I dislike her teaching a lot.  She seems to never have a plan, and the class is very disorganized.  Her paper assignments are okay--in general one of the worst English classes I've taken.
A tough class but good.
good teacher. i enjoy class. she grades pretty harshly, but a 'B' shouldn't be too hard.

This subject takes awhile to get through, so be sure to give yourself some study time.  She's helpful and doesn't rush through things, but this class can be dull if you understand the philosophers and rhetoricians fairly well.
Geogre was quite helpfull and nuturing- I had her for rhetoric of modern war, which was an interesting class and I learned alot about college-level paper writing. She's very accessable and helpful
Not a very nice person, she would not help me or adjust at all to my time schedule.
neat topic (rhetoric of modern war)/not Hard/several papers/ VERY helpful & nice

Dr. Gilmore is easily one of the best professors I have ever had. She is funny, relatable, and brilliant. Her classes are even enjoyable and I never had an issue showing up. There is the occasional in class assignment. Prepare for group work. Really can't recommend Dr. Gilmore more she is the best and you won't regret taking any class of hers!
She cool. She nice. She funny. Easy clah.

She requires high class participation and is very strict in grading. Although TCU's music department doesn't have many worthwhile courses, don't choose a course that is troublesome and gives low grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For her discussion posts she expected us to write very detailed and long responses without giving us anytime to write it. Not only would she do it right before class ended, she would never give full points even if you wrote a detailed response. She even gives you half points ondiscussion posts that are for checking in with the students mentalstate

I took a musical theater colloquia with her. Really interesting class - loved the material. All musical lovers will enjoy. Do average amount of readings before class, watch a musical every 2ish weeks. Participate in class, do discussion posts every week. One group project and one individual presentation. Should be an easy A if you do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Lecture and material is great, but the projects don't pertain to HistoryIII/are graded harshly. IS HARD
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Makes the class as if you are a music major. Seems like it should be easy but tests are rather hard if you don't memorize every song completely given in class & there are A LOT. Participation grade is given every day and you have to talk more than once to get a good grade for the day.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is so personable and friendly; class is always fun! She's very knowledgeable and fair. Grades are not just test and quiz based, it's also based on 2 essays and 2 projects. Sometimes, the projects are tedious but they're totally doable. Watkins, is the other prof for MH 1 whom is apparently a hardass, so definitely take Gina if you can!

Dr. Bombola has been serving as an interim professor for the past year, but has recently been hired on full time. She is a very friendly, kind person and pretty pleasant to be around. However, the two classes that I have taken with her (History II and World Music) have been a little disorganized. Not bad, but just be aware of some disorganization.

MUST memorize whole continents weekly with a quiz each week. Excruciatingly monotone and boring lectures. She bragged on the first day of class that she's only ever given out 3 A's in her whole career before.

don't take geography with her unless you absolutely need to. I took this as an elective and it's going to be my worst grade. Tests are absolutely impossible to really be prepared for as we are told to study pages of information and tons of book reading. Cumulative final - insanely hard. An unnecessarily hard class that will ruin your GPA.

reviews.comment: very monotone voice. not clear about what to study for. if you care about your GPA do not take this class unless you wanna waste a PNC.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Monotone voice. Ridiculously impossible tests. Weekly map quizzes. Lecture heavy. Doesn't post the slide shows. Says attendance is mandatory but doesn't know who anybody is. Just don't take her.
Does not care about students. Quiz heavy. DO not take unless you need for major.

Don't take this class. My worst grade so far. She is boring, not helpful, rude, and makes the class so much more difficult than it needs to be by overloading her material to the point where it's hardly even retainable. It is next to impossible to get an A even if you put in the effort and are studying every day for a week straight before the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Geffert is an ok lecturer, but the class is made so much harder than it should be. The map tests aren't too hard, but you have to memorize entire continents practically week by week. Tests are EXTREMELY thorough, you have to study months beforehand. Only take if you're majoring in geography, save yourself the stress.
She is terrible! Monotone voice and mean. I barely passed. Any other teacher is amazing but not her. test are miserable. She does bad review
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Geffert makes this class more difficult than it should be. The three exams are very hard and you need to study everything the study guide says. She doesn't take attendance, but she lectures (boring) everyday and doesn't post the slides so you need attend if you want to know what to study. Be prepared to work if you want a good grade.

super monotoned and lecture heavy. maybe its just cause Im not interested in geography but it really just went in one ear and out the other. Didnt even touch the textbook and still made a decent grade. If I had put more effort in I probably wouldve done better it was just so hard to pay attention because it was so boring

Professor Giffert has the most monotone and boring voice I have ever heard. Seriously, I am on zoom and other people walk in and ask why I am listening to something so boring. Otherwise, tests are a LOT of material. I got an A, but studied 50 hours for each test. Everything comes from lecture and she is not accommodating what so ever.

Unnecessarily difficult and stressful for an entry level class. My entire class spent weeks studying for her tests--50 page study guides-- and most still didn't pass. Would not recommend unless you love geography!

The lectures have a lot of information but have all the info you need. Monotoned voice in lecture but worth it to attend class. She gives a study guide for the tests and if you fill it out and study that you will do well. Also, there are weekly map quizzes. If you study and know it, they are easy 100's. She doesn't try to stump you.

Weekly map assignments and quizzes which are not too hard if you do well on the map assignment. She gives you study guides for the exams with everything that might be on it; these were helpful but were always very content heavy. She does not post lecture notes online, so take good notes. Not a class I enjoyed too much but it was doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Weekly map quizzes that aren't hard, but are time consuming. Tests are verbatim from lecture slides and she provides a study guide with every possible thing that could be on the test. If you study, it is doable. Definitely not an easy A but could happen if you really try. She does not post lecture material online
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: insensitive and tough on things going on in personal life. tough on hw and tests too
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great class! Caring professor. Available. As time offered was inconvenient
Really enjoyed her class! There are weekly map quizzes and map assignments but nothing crazy. One group project but very simple!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is passionate about the field of geography and tries to do her best in class with her lectures. She just makes this class harder than it should be especially for a GE. Get ready to study for her tests and weekly map quizzes that you will have to put a lot of time and effort into. Not an easy A or B class.

Detailed map quiz EVERY week. Long, very boring lectures and she doesn't post powerpoints online so if you don't go, then you won't have the test material. Test reviews are SO long. I ended with a B, but I had to work really hard for it, she recommended that we pass/no credit. Do not take her if your looking for a fairly easy core!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: not the most exciting professor. 10 map quizzes and 2 tests that have nothing to do with the quizzes. Very easy to make A's on everything except the tests, but she gives out study guides with everything you need to know.
Overall a great class experience. Although the class was long she kept it moving pretty well.

She may just be new, but this teacher needs to work on lecturing. Monotone reading of powerpoints and busywork homework, plus mandatory attendance make for an unpleasant combo. It's hard to pay attention to lecture when you could just be reading the ppts yourself. Quizzes are manageable, but she's a very specific nitpicky grader. Easyish class.

Tons of map quizzes/assignments (but they are not that hard, I would study for them the morning of). She gives you study guides for the test that are super long but everything on the test is somewhere on the guide, so just start working on them early. Lectures are long and kind of boring but relatively an easy class as long as you put in some work
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: 10 map quizzes, 2 tests, and a final. Lecture heavy class and she doesn't post notes so you better be there. Long study guides but exams are easy. Overall not terrible but not the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She gives weekly map quizzes which are tough at first, but you get use to them.  Tests cover a lot of material, but she gives a study guide so you know everything that could be on the test. Expect studying, but if you put in the effort, you can get a good grade. It's certainly not a blow off class, but I enjoyed it.

Personally, I thought this class was tough. The lectures were extremely long and you'll only get out a few minutes early, despite Geffert running through the power points. You had to complete a series of maps and turn in for a map quiz every week which were pretty time consuming. The tests were challenging and the study guides were lengthy. I PF .

Professor Geffert is a wonderfully straight-forward professor. She knows that this class is a core requirement, so she does all she can to help you pass. It is easy to do well on tests because she gives you the information ahead of time on a review. The maps and quizzes every class are a pain in the butt, but you'll get used to them.

Go to class because her tests are mostly over the lectures. She's very helpful if you need anything. Her lectures can get a little boring, but she tries to get through them quickly. Also, she does give a weekly map quiz, it's not a huge percent of the grade, but you do have to study for them. And her tests are pretty easy if you study the review.

Dr. Geffert is a very nice person who is willing to help  you  if you make an effort. She genuinely wants her students to succeed, and her class is straight forward. She gives you study guides with everything you need to know. The maps and quizzes are time-consuming so you have to try, but you can get a good grade if you are willing to try!

Geffert is a kind and fair professor. If you need help she is willing to meet up with you and answer all of your questions. The only thing is she goes through powerpoints fast. The tests are fair (if you study) though. What she says will be on the test is on the test.
Some homework but easy and quick. I really love this course and learned a lot. Extremely easy literary traditions credit.

I loved Ms. Gill she is a great English teacher and makes it very easy to get an A. She gives extensions if you need all you have to do is ask. Very good at giving feedback and makes it easy to be interested in what you are writing. Pretty easy grader just have to do the work.
The class was not overly difficult, but the lectures were very tedious and boring. It almost seemed as if Professor Gill attempted to take simple concepts and over analyze them in a technical way.

Kelli Gill is one of my favorite professors. She is so nice, and you can tell she really cares about the students. She makes her class fun, often showing her dogs on the zoom call. She is the best writing as inquiry prof, and I highly recommend.

Definitely take his musical theatre class for an easy honors colloquia! Even if you are not a theatre person, the class is enjoyable and understandable for the most part. Half your grade is participation and weekly reflections. There are 2 easy projects. Gibbons truly cares about his students and wants everyone to get an A.

I took a musical theater colloquia with him. LOVE HIM. Really interesting class - All musical lovers will enjoy. Do average amount of readings before class, watch a musical every 2ish weeks. Participate in class, do discussion posts every week. One group project and one individual presentation. Should be an easy A if you do the work.

I expected a lot more from an honors music class. We covered a small handful of topics tangentially and that was the course. Gibbons is a nice guy and also a complete pushover; I found myself annoyed every moment in his class because he tries to push his liberal/sjw agenda into every single topic. Discussions are boring, no work and easy A though.

Professor Gibbons is awesome. I highly recommend taking his colloquia classes. Not only was it an easy A, but it was also really interesting material and we had a lot of engaging conversations in class. Wish he taught more classes!

Highly recommend taking this course. Dr. Gibbons is very knowledgeable and entertaining so class flies by. If you somewhat pay attention to lectures tests will not be a challenge. Very few assignments or work outside of class. Material may not be the most exciting but is made understandable and you will definitely get something out of the class.

Gibbons is a downright beauty. He's super passionate about what he does, and he wants to make sure you learn the content. Only three tests, and they're all easy. Lots of lecturing and discussion, but there's no wrong answers in discussion.

awesome class. learned alot from music and politics. would defenantly take him again. readings before class but easy to handle. treats you like honors students and doesnt baby you to do your HW or readings. 2 presentations but straightfoward. might seem alot but as long you put it in, your gonna get rewarded.

Professor Gibbon's is AWESOME!!! Loved his Honors class and would 100% take him again. The majority of the class is discussion-based and our conversations were very interesting. He really creates an inclusive atmosphere.

Love Dr. Gibbons. Very progressive music prof. Encourages you to read about composers on wikipedia(!!). Does a great job finding overall historical themes and presenting them. Promotes great class discussions and brings in really cool guests. Big advocate of living composers. Wrote books on video game music. Some work, but not hard and graded fair.

Dr. Gibbons is fantastic and probably my favorite professor that I've had at TCU. There is no required textbook for his history III class, and he lets you use wikipedia articles to find info in class. He does a great job at approaching music from various genres in a number of academic and social ways. Highly recommend, you'll get a lot out of him.
One of the rarest and most incredible teachers in all of TCU. Def take his classes.
Dr. Gibbons is one of the coolest professors I have met. His class was a highlight in my busy semester. He is extremely knowledge in his area of focus. He is very helpful in and out of class.

Gibbons is a great guy. Loves video games. Young, nerdy, and awesome. Honors Survey with him is easier than regular Survey. Lectures are chill, interesting, and easy. Only tests were an online midterm and final. Gives a bit of extra credit. All he asks is to show up to class and participate. Very understanding and really easy to talk to.
He's a great teacher and will help you out

I LOVED Gibbons! He's hilarious and adorably geeky. Tests are easy enough if you review the night before, easy ten point assignments throughout. Spent whole classes listening to music, doesn't get better! Highly recommend for fine arts credit or for fun :)

Really great guy. Funny and very knowledgeable on music. He makes lectures feel like conversation. Very laid back, very helpful if you ask. Lenient grader - accepts a lot of reasonable guesses. Tests require minimum studying if you regularly attend class and pay attention. Kind of slow to get grades out. SUPER nice guy

His Film Music class is really interesting & VERY easy. His lectures are well organized. His tests are multiple choice, matching, true/false, & an essay. There are also 2 papers & a group project. This class is an easy A. He's a very likeable professor & he's HILARIOUS! If you want an easy FIne Arts credit, take Intro to Film Music!

He is a really good guy and is very passionate about music.  He is funny but lectures can get monotonous after a while. Tests consist of a listening section which is not too bad if you simply study some of the follow up questions can be a bit difficult.  If you study just the slightest you should get a B or so.

Mr. Gilbert was the worst teacher I ever had. I have never struggled in a class as much as I did in this class. He was a replacement teacher for my pre cal class and was the most confusing guy. He is very nice, but too smart for his own good. He tries to answer questions, but only offers a more confusing answer. Do not recommend at all.
Just don't take him
Don't take him cause you will drop eventually. The more he talks, the more confused you will be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Gilbert seems to be a very kind man but is way too smart for his own good. I have always been a math wiz and finished AP Calculus my senior year with a 95 yet what Dr. Gilbert was speaking was a foreign language. He starts nowhere near the basics and this class left me with my jaw dropped. Don't take it.

Dr. Gilbert is very nice and tries to help answer questions but his explanations often complicate things even further. He teaches everything at a very fast pace and it is hard to keep up with. He often skips steps in his explanations that leave you wondering how he did the math. Had to go back and teach myself everything before exams.

Dr. Gilbert is the worst teacher I have ever had. The man is too smart for his own good and is unable to teach us a thing during his lectures. Calc 2 is hard enough as it is, and with his teaching it is unbearable. If you can take ANY other teacher DO IT. Every single lesson I retaught myself using online videos.

The guy is too smart for his own good. He talks in circles and doesn't really explain anything clearly. He's basically a walking textbook and teaches like it too. He moves incredibly fast in his lectures and seems to automatically assume that we retain and understand everything he mentions.
His not clear in the class, even if you ask him a question will confuse you more and more.
AWFUL! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH GILBERT
Took him for Calc1. He became the department chair the semester after my class. He is super smart and expects you to understand things right away. Take someone else if possible!!!

Take the class from a different teacher. He teaches like a textbook so it is very hard to understand anything he says. He goes too fast & doesnt explain it thoroughly. His teaching style is so difficult to understand most of the people dont even show up for class. He is kind, but is not a good calculus teacher for the first time calculus student.

Worst professor ive ever had. cant teach to save his life. you go into every class knowing for sure you are not about to learn anything. and finally theres nothing worse than a terrible professor who grades hard. on the final paper he takes off 2/20 points each for PUNCTUATION AND CAPITALIZATION! has no mercy while grading tests either. HE SUCKS!!!

its not so much him, its the class. its a really hard class and there should be way more prereq classes than calc 1. that is probably why probability and statistics is a 30000 level class instead of 2. I would not recommend this class unless it is required for your major. if you do have to take it, i would take Discrete 1 and maybe discrete 2 first
George Gilbert is pretty much the most adorable professor ever! And he's a great teacher. I HATE math, I mean it's my nemesis and I really love his class. great teacher. Take him for Topics!
George Gilbert is pretty much the most adorable professor ever! And he's a great teacher. I HATE math, I mean it's my nemesis and I really love his class. great teacher. Take him for Topics!

Took 2 classes with Gilbert. First one was well taught. Statistics was horrible. Getting passing grades was difficult. I spent roughly 10 hours studying to get a C on an exam. Asking questions in class does not help because he gets off topic easily. Don't take Prob and Stat if you don't have to.

I took him for Topics in the Summer semester and he was wonderful!  I had anxiety about taking math and he was willing to explain everything multiple times and had drop in office hours if you were still having problems.
I agree with the other ratings, he is not a very good teacher and is terrible about explaining things. He really isn't much help one on one either. He is a nice guy though.

Dr. Gilbert is not a very good teacher but he's a lot better one on one.  He only gives general examples and cannot seem to explain things more than one way.  Curve was sooo high a 39 was a "C" on a 100 pt. scale.  Confusing as hell!!!!  Nice guy though.

He is a really nice prof. His tests aren't too bad if you pay attention in class, do the HW, and study his old tests, (he gives you copies of them in class).  Just watch out for the final.  They are harder than the rest of his tests.

Had him in differential equations and linear algebra.  If you read the book before the lecture, his lectures are good, but if you don't it can be really confusing.  He will answer any question you want, but sometimes his answer is hard to understand.  His

Intro to Health Disparities in African Americans is such an easy class for a CA core credit. There are no exams, final, quizzes, or homework. Four assignments the entire year with three of them being group projects. No textbook but you will need to get a copy of a book assigned to you for a project but you only end up reading a section.

So, Adult I is def a difficult course. What made it a bit harder was the fact that the course is taught by 2 completely different teachers. One is very detailed oriented and the other rushes through slides. If your having a hard time do not wait to meet with them outside of class they do give great feedback. I personally never used the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you're taking Daniels for Adult Nursing, you MUST READ EVERY CHAPTER! I swear if you only read the power points you will not make more than a B in her class! Her test questions are ridiculous, you can study forever and still struggle to make an A....
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I never opened the textbook and did not really study all that hard and got an A. She will sometimes give extra credit and she always curves the tests sometimes significantly so that's a plus. It can seem kinda tedious to go to class but I would recommend going because she often times goes over exactly what she wants you to know.
Can be confusing at times but will help you and is very kind

Love Dr. Daniels!! Didn't have her for clinical, but I heard she was great there too. Study power points and go to class and you can get an A. She is always available for questions or to talk. Very sweet!!

Love her!! You must attend class to pick up on extra notes that will be on the test. Her powerpoint notes are great, but if you attend class and read then its very achievable to get an A. She also gives quizzes between tests to help boost your grade

Dr. Daniels is fantastic! Very kind & always available for to help students. Get to know her, she's really awesome. Tests are PPT based, the book is excellent. Tests can be tricky but she lets you review and sometimes argue your point as well. Love her!

Dr. Kroh is a hidden gem at TCU. The material in this class is really interesting. The tests are pretty much all memorization based, but I found 1-2 days was plenty in advance to study and get an A. Showing up to class is paramount, but I really enjoyed attending his class so it wasn't a problem! Strongly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Kroh is the best! Grades are based around nerve-wrackingly few items, and tests cover a LOT of material, but he goes far out of his way to help you understand the material and have your best chance to succeed on the tests. Lectures are a little PowerPoint dependent, but fun nonetheless.

Kroh is an amazing man but his classes are brutallllll. Reads straight from the slides, tests on tiny details that dont really matter. His lectures are very very dated too. He cares a lot about the students but would not take him again simply b/c his lectures are brutal and exams over dumb details.

Such a sweet man! His natural history was genuinely one of my favorites, and I took it for core credit. The tests are hard, but you learn a lot, so it's worth it. He really wants to help his students learn and is very helpful. Labs are a great grade booster- show up and watch the videos, and you'll do well.
He was a tough teacher, made you work hard and pay attention to the tiniest details.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lewis means well, but he is not that helpful with critique and is really out of touch with design aesthetics of today.  ALL of the projects in Type III are useless, and I never want to see them again.  Be prepared to get little to no portfolio pieces from his classes. He prides himself on having an easier class than Jan's, which is true. (not good)
Lewis is amazing! If you think he's the worst teacher you've had a TCU you must have had some pretty out of this world professors. He's very helpful.
This is the worst professor I had at TCU.
Quirky, but a good professor. Gives many good design references.
Survey of music is so boring. If you don't like classical music, then it is really hard to stay awake. The class is really easy though
This is the most boring class at TCU. She is really hard to understand. The textbook cost $150, and you rarely use it. I would NOT recommend this class.

SUPER EASY. Go to class and take notes directly from her power point or get someone to do it for you. I just looked at failblog all through class and iChatted with my friends. Grades super easy. Tests can be a little tricky but nothing an hour of studying can't ace. Definitely a good and easy fine arts credit

Survey of Music, Dr. Lin is a great teacher who is also a great piano player. Class sometimes drags on, but she really knows what she's talking about, and we even got to watch the movie Amadeus during class! Honors students, I recommend taking her Honors class, it is very similar to the non-honors version.

Everything you need to know for the exam is on the powerpoint, just come to class and copy it. Very nice teacher who is willing to repeat things when necessary. If you need a fine arts credit, I highly recommend this class.
Chill class. Pay attention! There is lots of EC. Just study and pay attention in class. I really enjoyed the class.
Although I know nothing about music, I felt although I lerned somthing. I was very pleased with the A I reseaved. Although some of the classes were a bit boaring.

This was one of the most boring classes I have ever taken. But, if you're looking for an easy A...sign up. If for whatever reason you can't manage to make an A on the tests, she gives about 20 points of extra credit.
if you do not make an A in this class then you did not work hard enough.. you can add about 15 points to your average in extra credit.

Class is pretty boring, but you would be surprised to what you learn. She's very sweet and very knowledgable. GREAT PIANIST. Just take notes and look at the terms in the book. Test is straightforward and pretty easy. Gives TONS of extra credit. EASY EASY A.

Class is pretty boring, but you would be surprised to what you learn. She's very sweet and very knowledgable. GREAT PIANIST. Just take notes and look at the terms in the book. Test is straightforward and pretty easy. Gives TONS of extra credit. EASY EASY A.

Dr. Lin is a very nice lady, and she's a great musician who really knows her stuff. It's a pretty easy class, an easy A... But I've studied music since I was 8 and I really don't know how people who had never had music before understood her at all... lectures are a little disorganized and the accent can throw you off a little...
Really great teacher, sometimes hard to understand in class, but she gives tons of extra credit, if you do the extra credit and pay attention then it will not be hard to earn an A in this class.

I knew nothing about music going in and got an A.  She offers so much extra credit--do it ALL!!.  I had a C average without extra credit and got an A because of the extra work.  She is a bit sperratic and confusing.  Be sure to get help if you are confused, cuz the material builds on itself.
