Everybody here was right. He is terrible at teaching. But even if you self-study, the tests are very difficult. It's all a form of short-answer. 10 points per problem. You never really know what to expect since he doesn't tell you

Worst professor I have taken at TCU, does not know how to teach. He only explains simple problems in class and then assigns hard problems on the exams. he makes the final impossible... do not take him... should not be teaching at TCU
Whatever you do, do NOT take this professor. He is incomprehensible, unclear, confusing, and just abo****ely awful. Save yourself and take someone else.

The worst teacher I have had in my 4 years at TCU.  His first two exams are relatively easy and his final is impossible on purpose.  He cuts off his office hours 2 weeks before the final. You will learn nothing by going to class but have to go for attendance grade.  However, he may be easier than Cobb for Int II so pick your poison.

One of the WORST professors I have ever had. Lectures are very boring painful, has a thick accent, and he dumbs down his lectures in an attempt to make them easier to understand, but in the end just ends up confusing everyone. Known as the smiling assasin - gives "easy" tests for good reviews then fails everyone on the final! AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!

you cannot understand his english. do not take him.  my sister had to teach me the class and i made all A's because of her help until the final. the final was nothing like he described and the class average on it was 35 and that was with a partial curve.  which gave me a B in the class when i had an A on everything else. don't take him! can't teach

Accounting is a pretty important subject for any business majors...and if you want to learn it, don't take Lim. You won't understand a word he says, end up teaching yourself, and end up wondering why a school charging their students 12 grand a semester would even consider hiring someone who you can barely understand. Seriously, do not take him.

Pretty easy class. Study old exams b/c they are very similar to the questions he will ask on the new exams. The final is really hard. He grades homework on completion only. Very personable, but a little hard to understand.

Lim is great - the topic is pretty basic, but non-biz people struggle. He does a great job of simplifying things-he uses good examples. The tests are extremely easy-if you study the old exams that he gives you, it is hard not to get an A. He tricked up the final a little, but if you understand the old exams, you will be okay.  Great class and prof.
Very poor ingrish.  Tests are hard, grading is almost random.  Be very mindful of your grade in his class.

This is the worst teacher on earth. Take anyone but him. Seriously, he has no idea how to teach undergrad students. And his English sucks. Don't let his smile fool you. He will make you think you're doing alright, and then BAM!!! He will make the next test twice as hard, and the next test even harder. And the final will KILL YOU!!! Students BEWARE!
All over the place, very hard to follow

I do not know why Dr. Liu is rated low on here, because she is one of the best professors in the economics department. As long as you pay attention and take good notes, you will be well prepared for tests/quizzes and an A is super attainable. Homework is completion with posted answers. Could not recommend more, especially for econometrics.

Liu is actually a good professor, as long as you pay attention in glass and do the homework you should be fine. There are weekly quizzes and homework. If you study those then you should get a decent B on each test. The final is a project and not overly hard, I would start it extra soon as they style is unique.

Not a horrible teacher just talks really fast and can be hard to understand at times. Pretty test heavy but homework's are just completion and there is a fair amount of quizzes. Econometrics is very hard and it's even harder if you get behind. Final is a project but it takes forever and it is a lot. Overall not horrible but recommend another prof

Dr. Liu is fantastic, i have never written a review but i felt inclined to because i was so surprised of her low rating. It wasn't as difficult as people made it seem. She had assignments graded by the next class. Her english is not bad at all. Spends the time to make sure the class understands difficult topics.Take her class and ignore the hate.

Really don't understand the hate for her on here. Pretty easy. Go to class, take mid notes and ur chilling. Homework is overly easy. Make sure you have general knowledge of the topic/unit before each quiz and youll do fine. Always an easy grader in my experience. Lectures and scribbles on the board a lot but the slideshows have good info

Lots of negative reviews but I have taken her for Resource and Energy and Env Eco and Policy and she's a sweet woman. No exams, graded on 4 quizzes, homework, a group presentation and a final. Probably not an easy A as far as econ electives go but the material is interesting. She's happy to help if you ask for it and she usually responds fast.

Weiwei gets a bad rep on here, but she is truly a fantastic person and professor. Be ready to laugh at her corky jokes and comments as the class size are usually small. Quick teacher, and it can be hard to follow, but if you make a friend in the class or use chat, y'all should be fine.

My least favorite professor I've ever had. I've never done so badly in a class and it wasn't because I wasn't trying. I had an excused absence and she took off for my participation. She blamed us when the WHOLE class failed a test when it was really just her lack of sufficient teaching. Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just rambles and scribbles things on the board

Professor Liu's class for Econometrics might be difficult, but Resource and Energy Econ was a breeze. Easily one of the least labor-intensive econ classes I've taken and she posts all the slides so the quizzes really aren't that difficult. Very lax with attendance on non-presentation days. Overall, I would highly recommend for energy econ.

She's probably not qualified for this job, all around in every category just awful. Not a single good thing to say. She also has an accent and terrible sentence structure on all her written assignments.

just avoid AT ALL COSTS, she gets frustrated at students asking her questions, even though the class is extremely hard and her grading makes it even harder, honestly one of the worse mistakes i made was taking this class with her in my last semester.

She talks way too fast and expects you to be following along at her pace. When people don't understand her rapid fire tangents, she acts like it is the students fault for not studying enough rather than her teaching method not working for the students. I suggest getting a tutor if you have this professor.

Do not take. Studied 24/7 and still managed to not pass. She does not care about helping students, grades ridiculously. Previous reviews have to be written by her or colleagues. Do not waste your time and take any of her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly this is one of the hardest classes in Econ and she makes it ten times worse. She doesn't speak English very well and makes it very hard to understand. She also writes like a preschooler and you can't read anything on the board if you are not in the front row. If there is another Econometrics professor take them. She sucks

Dr. Weiwei is a fantastic professor and a true gem of the econ department. Going in to the course I was very nervous as I heard that econometrics was extremely difficult. Honestly, just make sure to do the homework and understand the concepts on the homework as they help you to do well on the quizzes and tests. Make sure to attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Liu is awesome, I took her for Econometrics and was worried it would be really tough, but she makes sure students understand and she breaks everything down into manageable topics. She's always open to helping students and really cares about their success. Quizzes and exams are just like homework so you can be sure you can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Liu is a fantastic professor. This was my first class with her and I loved it. If I wasn't graduating this semester, I would definitely take her again. She sometimes talks fast in lectures, but she is not hard to understand. She is very helpful and knowledgeable, and really cares about every student succeeding.

Dr Saleh is so kind and really cares about her students. She is super personable and funny when she teaches. If you just do the work in class and on time you will do well in this class! Quizzes are online and open note and this class group project heavy but the rubrics are straightforward.

sweet teacher who cares about each student and their well being! She will give grace and as long as you turn stuff in on time she is  a easy grader and is happy to answer as many questions and look over projects before turning in. Quizzes are impossible for this class but they are weighted super low and you can easily get a on all other assignments

Professor Saleh is such a kind and caring professor. However, she will not give you a 100 on your midwife journal solely for the fact that your APA citations will never be good enough. Her stories are awesome during lectures and the class seems pretty easy until you get to the exams which are difficult. Doesn't give resources to help with exams.

She was my teacher for role 1. I used her resources for APA format and she took off points. when I emailed her to ask for help, she sent me back the same resource she had posted, told me to use it, and gave me examples. I used the examples she gave me and she said it was wrong. On tests every choice is the same, its just what she thinks is best.

This class has 2 group presentations which are 20% of your grade. Textbook is not required but recommended to clarify any confusion in the slides. Participation matters there are graded class activities. Exam is horrible because it's not about memorization. She talked a lot during lecture but it sometimes goes off topic. Take other profs if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She's my nightmare for Role I. She will deduct point out of your journal if she didn't like you. The prompt journal isn't clear. She also didn't prepare you well for the exam. She just lectured random things and repeated her examples which aren't related to the slides. She seemed nice at first but deep inside is rude. Good luck with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is really not hard at all. I just don't think ppl are used to studying for psych classes. I went to class, took notes, and did all the hw and extra credit, and easily got an A. I studied for everything the night before and was able to get an 80 or above. If you do all the extra credit, a raw 85 will get you an A. Just take detailed notes

He puts in so many extra hours into his job, because he cares about the subject and students. His exams are challenging, but one exam gets dropped if you do the study guides. People often complain this class is hard, but as long as you spend time with the material you'll be fine.

Dr. Leising is an amazing professor and he is so passionate about what he teaches. The material is more difficult than your typical psych class but if you put actual effort into studying IT IS NOT THAT HARD. Most people saying this class is hard/impossible is not actually trying. Leising is great.

This is the most frustrating, difficult class I've ever taken. I would never take it again. Exams are brutal, and the “study guides” are extra credit but unclear, then graded harshly. You have to reteach yourself daily to pass. Lectures are confusing and too fast to take notes. I hope I get hit crossing university, so I don't have to go to class.
would not recomend taking this course it is so hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Definitely the worst class I have ever taken. He should be teaching honor students or upper division classes. The tests were extremely difficult unless you studied for hours, which is unnecessary for an intro class. The lectures were fine for what they were, but I would have appreciated more application during the class.

Dr. Leising is super nice and cares about his students but his lectures can be dry, boring, and confusing. His tests are also super hard and he tends to grade the short answer questions pretty hard. If you participate and go to office hours he will help you though. He also offers SONA and other extra credit opportunities.

I loved this class so much. Leising makes lectures very interesting. Missing a class is not an option. He does not take attendance, but there is so much information in every class and you will miss a lot on the exam. There is an extra credit option, but it is very time-consuming. In my opinion- the course was worth it, and I learned so much.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take him if you can. He is a really nice guy but he makes this class so much harder than it should be. The lectures are interesting and all but his exams are impossible, they are all in person and on paper. I don't even know if I will pass the class.

This class is definitely hard but it is not impossible. The content is challenging and requires work to understand, but it really is fascinating. He is super passionate about the content and he wants you to succeed! He started recording his lectures and that has helped so much! Reading the textbook is not required, but it helps for studying!

This class was too difficult for an intro class. I was excited because everyone typically loves psych their freshman year but boy this class was ridiculous. I paid attention and went every day, but that wasn't enough. The tests were what did it for me.He's an ok guy but wants you to care about psych the way he does.
I loved Dr. Leising. I won't lie this class wasn't the easy option for the course, but I'd recommend it anyways. Dr. Leising is dedicated to his job and truly puts in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: My absolute favorite professor at TCU. Dr. Leising is passionate, brilliant and dedicated to his work. If you put in the effort you can get an A, this was one of my hardest psych classes at TCU, but easily the most rewarding. This course laid the foundation for so many of my graduate school classes and is very applicable in everyday life. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are very confusing. Better to read the textbook than pay attention in class. Expectations for students are through the roof. I struggled to get an A, and barely made it! Hard exams, know the implications of EVERY study. Go to all review sessions and office hours regularly for an A. But he is a good person, and he loves chatting with us

By far the hardest class I've taken at TCU. The professor requires intense memorization for tests with an abundance of information. He has claimed to try to "trick" students on exams instead of being straightforward and teaching material we need to know. The information presented is so dense and dull that it makes studying nearly impossible.

I did not love Leising at the beginning. His lectures are dense, and the quizzes can seem like busy work. He definitely grew on me throughout the semester. He goes out of his way to be engaging in lecture and gives lots of participation incentives. You MUST read to do well on quizzes, which can be overwhelming. DO THE STUDY GUIDES to drop low exam!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: LOVED HIM!! Such a sweet professor and super intelligent. These reviews are not it, this class is no harder than AP Psych. Just look over the notes before the quizzes, and make a study guide for the exams (both of which offer bonus points) to be exempt from the final. Definitely recommend.

leising is very difficult and requires a lot of your time. if you want to pass you need to go to office hours multiple times and put in the work yourself. although he doesn't give much homework, the lectures and tests are very material heavy.

Professor Leising treats his class like an upper-division course. There are quizzes every other week and multiple exams during the semester. You get to drop the lowest one. There are lots of opportunities for extra credit. It's hard if you have never taken psych before. Study well for the exams and you will be good.

This is not a course you can blow off or hope that Google will carry you through. You need to be prepared to understand concepts instead of just memorizing things. Extra credit is generous here. This class felt like how a challenging yet rewarding course should be. Would not recommend with a heavy course load or no passion for psychology. Great guy

I really like Professor Leising as a person. He's a nice guy, and he's extremely intelligent... Probably the smartest professor I've had. But he's also a tough grader, and this course was often overwhelming. He sometimes doesn't realize the difficulty of the material (it's pretty easy to him) & his lectures often drag on. Beware of the lab papers!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Overall, I liked him as a professor and person. However, DONT TAKE THIS CLASS FOR CORE CREDIT. Hardest course I have taken in my life. I had to pass no credit. The study guides you have to make to get a test dropped takes a total of around 8-10 hours every test and in the end aren't worth it.

Prof Leising is a good professor. I enjoyed his lectures. The activities are easy, but you need to attend class to understand the material and complete the assignments. Do the study guides to be exempt from the final and help you do well on the exams. The class is not an easy A, but he offers plenty of resources and extra credit to make it doable.

Do not take this class if you're looking for an achievable A or even B. He picks his favorites, and made sure to cancel the one review session before the final exam. Oh and good luck getting help outside of class, he won't respond to his emails :)

Absolute no. For an intro course, he expects us to know an absurd amount of info. You can prepare for the exams but wording of the questions makes it 10x harder. This class made me question my major. Be sure to do every SONA extra credit and lecture outcomes. You're better off with another professor or holding off taking this class.

He is very passionate about psychology and can be engaging but he also tends to rush through lectures and expects you to do a lot of reading/learning on your own. It is possible to do well in this class but if you are looking for an easy A other professors would be a much better option.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: not the best, not the worst. exams are worth a lot, quizzes every week, and activities in class. iclicker is used randomly for attendance. he doesn't respond to emails a lot he will make time to meet with you if needed.  research hours as extra credit on top of the required and if you make study guides for each exam, one exam grade is dropped.

I really enjoyed this class! I am no where near being a Psych major, but Professor Leising is a great lecturer. He keeps you entertained and interested in what he's teaching. If you are looking for a complete blow-off class, this is not it, but I think the class was easy. There is almost no homework, and there are only 3 tests. I would take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very funny professor but he covers a lot of material so unless you are a psych major do not take this class. his tests cover several lectures and some aspects of the book so unless you are willing to do the work and actually set aside time to study and go to office hours I wont recommend this class.

He's one of the few intro professors who doesn't allow you to use your notes on tests and exams. Don't take this class, it's unnecessarily hard and there's far better psychology professors. Tests are an abundance of information that he lectures on in class.

By far the worst professor I have had all my years at TCU. I have never written one of these reviews before but felt a moral obligation to WARN those who are thinking of taking his class. He is arrogant, disorganized, and makes fun of students not understanding his content. So discouraging and unhelpful and does not make himself accessible at all.
Only take if a psychology major!!! Ph.D. in Psych and a very good lecturer, but incredibly hard quizzes and tests, and lots of them. If taking for a core TCU credit, there are much easier professors

Professor Leising is the only intro to psych professor at TCU that gives exams that arent open note. However, if you do a study guide for all 3 exams you get to drop your lowest test score, which means you dont have to take the final. He does weekly quizzes and a few homework assignments here and there. Its very important to go to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. Dr. Leising gives great lectures and has a lot of opportunity for extra credit. If you pay attention in class, you will do well on quizzes and exams. Make sure to read the textbook for exams. He always likes to tell jokes and you can tell that he really enjoys teaching.
Discouraging professor if you did not show high amounts of interest in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Leising is a good professor. His tests are easy if you pay attention in lecture and take notes. He says to read the book, but his lectures cover the material in the book. His tests are open note which makes the test questions a little harder, but not unbearable. There isn't much homework, but the homework that is assigned is not hard.

Dr Leising is a great teacher. This class was not super easy, but he offers tons of office hours, review sessions, and study guides that really prepare you for the test. You can tell he is super passionate about this stuff and that he truly wants his students to do well. He also curves and offers extra credit and his grading is fair.

- 10-15% of all information tested is from the book, the books mildly expensive. - Lectures are quick and if taken at the 9:30 am the course you're likely to get groggy and tired. - Quizzes harder than tests. (6Quizzes,3Exams,1final) - Nice optional grading possibility for tests, and easy extra-credit. - Inherently have to work harder for grade

This class is the hardest class that I took in all of my 4 years at TCU. He expects you to be an expert in this field and does not do a good job of going in depth and slowing down in class. There is way too much information in the lectures to be able to understand the information in the depth he wants. You couldn't pay me to take this class again.
This class is great for a gen. psych. It is really easy if you go to class and read over the notes before the quizzes and tests. Easy A for sure and lots of extra credit!!!

Psych with Dr. Leising was great! His lectures are so clear and so entertaining. As long as you read the textbook and listen in class you will make an A. If you go to him outside of class for study tips it will really help! Also major key to an A: while studying, write test questions and examples that you think he will put on the test.

Dr. Leising is a decent professor and is definitely willing to help but makes his class harder than other professors at TCU. If you're looking for an easy A then I'd choose someone else but if you're truly interested and willing to work then I'd take Leising. I did not LOVE him but I did get a lot out of this class and I respect him as a professor.

Dr. Leising is probably the best professor I have had at TCU. I had him for Experimental Psyc: Learning. He lectures well and is more than happy to answer all your questions and meet with you outside of class. One of the most challenging classes but so worth it. I learned a lot and it is totally achievable to get an A if you put in the work
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is very challenging, but worth it. He grades the writing assignments very hard, but they are only worth 10% of your grade. He makes lectures fun and interesting, although it may get confusing at times. He is very helpful if you go to office hours. The tests are very hard and you need to be able to apply the concepts to real life examples
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Leising is a great choice for general psychology. As long as you go to lectures and take good notes, you'll do well. The tests and quizzes are not that hard just make sure to study. Also, he offers a lot of extra credit. Dr. Leising is a great professor and I thoroughly enjoyed his class! Study and you'll get an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best professor I have ever had. He is so nice and will explain anything you don't understand. Go to office hours, he is so helpful. He gives extra credit questions on each test and also extra credit for in class participation activities. If you turn in a handwritten study guide for each test you can opt out of final. Easy A if you go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Had Leising for Memory & Cognition, he is a great choice for a professor! He gave us reviews for the exams which is a huge help. It is a very concept based class, so you need to understand the material. Not a blow off class, but he makes his expectations for the class attainable. Really helps is you ready the book and take notes in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Leising expects you to understand everything at a PhD level. His lectures are unorganized and do not make sense. When you attend reviews he is disappointed if you dont understand the material. Expect to teach yourself before every test. Most of the material carries over which makes it difficult to study for the nest test.

Makes his learning classes very difficult. Even after going to many office hours my grades were terrible. Hes a nice guy and is willing to help you, but the content of the course is overwhelming in the first place and his tough grading does not help. A challenge is always nice, but his class is absurdly hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'll just say this - Our class average on every test was an F - he did not curve. Utterly speechless at the way Prof Leising teaches Fundamentals of Learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Leising was very hard. Fundamentals of Learning is not what I expected. He lectures the whole class and expects you to understand hard material. We had to ask him for extra worksheets in order to understand the material. I would not recommend taking this class or this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Given the level of info. that is needed to be taught, summer session was not best choice. If you can do the extra credit you can get 10 pts extra. He wasn't always prepared and spent time searching for videos that didn't always work. He was funny and straightforward about his requirements. Show up to class powerpoints have info that may be on test.

He's a super cool professor. Explains things really well, and is clear about his expectations. You'll need to study, though, and don't be one of those people shopping/on facebook during class, because you have to show up and pay attention to know the information that will be on tests. His notes are clear, though, and if you study, you'll get an A.

Fantastic teacher. Lightens the mood with a bad joke of the day at the beginning of class, and the material was interesting and easy to follow. I never opened the textbook and my grades were good enough to be exempt from the final.

AWESOME choice for General Psychology. Professor Leising is hilarious and always willing to help. If you show up and pay attention, this class is an EASY 4.0. He has lots of extra credit opportunity and make sure to do good on the quizzes every week (which are VERY easy) because you can get exempt from the final exam which is nice. TAKE HIM!!!

I enjoyed Prof. Leising's lectures and jokes; however, his class was very difficult. Not only would he ask so many trick questions, but also, he was teaching us about topics that some of my upperclassmen psych major/minor friends had barely started learning about. I don't recommend him unless you want to work hard and potentially end up with a B.

Dr. Leising provides you with sufficient information that you really don't need to read the book because it has way more information than he teaches. I feel like he is kinda all over the place and I just didn't really like that, so I wouldn't take  him again. Only good thing is you have extra credit opportunity to have a 5% grade increase, it helps
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Leising is the best Psyc teacher at TCU. This class was fairly easy, pay attention, study for quizzes, and do well on test. There are only 2 test, and if you have  a 90 quiz average you are exempt from final. Extra credit offered with all quizzes and test. 5 Sona hours required, can do up to 15 hours for extra credit points. MUST TAKE!!!

I loved this class and Professor Leising! He was extremely helpful when reviewing for exams. I would definitely take advantage of his office hours before a test! He's very nice and wants his students to really understand the information. There's some effort that needs to be put into this class, so don't expect it to be a blow off.

Love this guy. If dad jokes are your thing, you've found your perfect class. He's funny, keeps you entertained throughout lecture, and is super helpful. He also gives amazing extra credit opportunities. Take this class! Show up and do the readings and you'll be fine. If you ever have questions, he's the friendliest dude ever so go ask him.

Leising is funny and interesting! I'm interested in Psych to the point where I may get a minor but I didn't try hard in the class. Drops final if you do well on quizzes, and quizzes are frequent and easy. Exams can be tricky. Read one chapter before I realized I didn't have to read at all. Go to lecture and you'll be fine.
Hard class. Hard to approach

A lot of professors use turn it in for papers but he considers any two word combination as plagiarism which makes it impossible to write an acceptable paper. He began the semester with "Most students make C's or D's on my exams". 25 question tests over 100+ pages of material. Would not recommend taking him.
Great techer, i didnt make an A in the class but i have little interest in Psychology, quizez every monday 5 questions easy. tests are about 30 questions also easy, great fun teacher.

Awesome Prof. Drops lowest quiz score. If you get average of 90% or higher on quizzes you are exempt from the final.. They are really easy too. Great lectures and slides. I would def. recommend him for psych. You actually learn some interesting stuff in his class AND he's entertaining.

He is a GREAT professor. If you go to class everyday and pay attention, you will get an A. Study for the quizzes because you don't have to take the final if your quiz average is an 90% or higher. The tests are semi difficult but if you study you should be fine. Do they extra credit SONA hours, they are worth a lot. All around great teacher.

This class is good if you GO TO CLASS EVERY TIME. If you don't go to class you're screwed because of weekly quizzes, etc. I wish I would have taken Broom instead, because not so much of the grade is weighted on participation. This is like 50% participation, which sucks if you miss an early class!

This class is super easy!! He is a really nice teacher, who loves to give extra credit. there are 9 quizes that are 5 easy qustions with extra credit chances. If you have an A average you do not have to take the final.

Dr. Leising is an AWESOME prof. He's understanding, super funny, and makes psychology a lot of fun. He makes his class easy by really explaining everything,  and giving you opportunities for extra credit. GO TO CLASS. pay attention, and you have an A. :)

Really great guy. I took this class since it's a requirement and it literally has made me consider switching my major to psychology. You learn a ton but he is more than happy to help you achieve the grade you desire. I never wanted to skip class because the lectures were actually really interesting. Definitely TAKE him, best prof at TCU!!!
Awesome dude! Take him!!! Best professor at TCU! Easy A, I promise. He is way better than the other classes (more interesting, less boring). Take him or you will be missing out!

The lectures are organized well and clear to read. He incorporates youtube videos which were always fun. It was a class I looked forward to every week. I loved the guest lectures by the student worker and his wife. They presented amazingly!I am very glad that I have had the opportunity to have Leising as a professor. Take him. :D
Super super SUPER nice guy, but if you have to take general psychology, he is NOT the guy to take. Quizzes once a week.  Midterm was impossible.  Definitely wish that I took Broom. But, he's nice!
He is an amazing professor. He makes class super fun and gives tons of extra credit opportunities. TAKE HIM!

Very animated about his lectures.He makes lectures fun by incorporating youtube videos and movie clips.He is very knowledgeable about his subject and will help you understand anything you have a question about. He really cares about his students! Quizzes are very basic--over lectues and exams are fine. Oh and he is fun to look at ;)
the best teacher ive ever had here i literally changed my major to CJ. a queen

Ms. Lopez is THEE best professor ever. She explains everything well, makes the lectures fun and interesting rather than boring, has a great sense of humor, and tells you exactly what to expect in tests; like she really wants no one to fail! She made me love criminal justice when I was mildly interested in it.
If I could I would 100% take her again

Ms. Lopez is a great teacher! She is a current FWPD officer and has an amazing understanding of the material she teaches. Attendance is not required for your grade, but missing a lecture can put you behind, and she does not post slides on D2L. Before tests, she will go over the material and give you hints about what will be on the exam.

Her lectures were very interesting and easy to follow. She taught fully based on her experiences as a FWPD officer and 2 books which were very cheap and easy to read. Her exams were very manageable (I only ever had to study maybe a day before and got high B's and A's), and there were only a few papers that were opinion based and only a page long.

She is the best professor ever! She literally give you the questions and exams, so its really easy to study. She is very engaged with the class. The exams and quizzes are on paper, but if you record the lectures, you can make flash cards to study. She also brought donuts at the end of the semester for the class lol. AMAZING PROFESSOR!!! TAKE HER!!!

She made the lectures engaging and the coursework manageable—only three tests (including the final) and three one-page, mostly opinion-based essays. Before tests, there's a review day to ask questions, and she tells you exactly what will be on the test. LOVE her!! There's also no textbook. We read "American Prisons" and "New Centurions" instead.

I took her class as a first semester freshman and I genuinely looked forward to class. Professor Lopez is very kind and makes efforts to get to know all of her students. She gives out only 3 exams throughout the semester, all with very clear study guides that aren't excessive and well prepare you for her exam. 3 papers, take this core class!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was her first year teaching at TCU and she ROCKED it! She's an active-duty cop in Fort Worth and is passionate about CRJU. The class is incredibly engaging and interesting. She bought our whole class donuts and learned everyone's names. She wants you to exceed and feel inspired. She creates a safe space for every opinion to be shared. TAKE HER

He's very caring and a good teacher, but he likes to go ahead on new lessons before you take quizzes and tests on the current lesson so it's really easy to get behind and get confused. I ended up having to use the videos he uploads to fully learn the material. The class overall is not bad but there's definitely easier teachers to take stats with.

Awesome! Take him! You need to pay attention but honestly he makes the class easy. Homework counts for extra credit and it helps A LOT with quizzes and tests. You won't regret taking this class with him.

Lause is a GREAT professor. He actually made us understand the material and made it super easy, he gave us extra credit in exams if we had less than 10 absences and got 10/10 in every homework (honestly he doesn't check it, just do the hw and you're good) 
You need to pay attention and do the homework, but it is very easy. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Dr. Lause is the best professor at TCU by far. He is absolutely amazing and makes statistics easy to understand and learn even if you aren't good at math. There is homework but he gives you extra credit on exams if you complete it on time and the quizzes are based off of the homework problems and class work.

AMAZING!! He's very passionate about stats and knows what he's doing. Very funny and super helpful. It is a hard class but as long as you go to class and pay attention you'll be fine. Lots of homework but it actually helps for quizzes and tests- homework also counts as extra credit!

I love Professor Louse! He definitely knows his Elementary Stats, and is really good at lecturing for it. He is also pretty funny. I recommend going to class because he covers everything that will be on the test, in the lectures. Great extra credit opportunities, and overall good class. Just be prepared to do your homework and study.

Take Pat!! 
Great professor. Funny and caring guy. Lecture heavy class but there are online videos if you miss. I got a lower grade than I had wanted due to outside circumstances but he really sets you up for success. Email him and communicate!! He is very helpful.

Patrick Louse is the funniest math teacher I've come across. He does a great job explaining things in class and doesn't move on until you understand it. There is homework, but it's due every Thursday. He is available during office hours for help and smiles when he sees you around campus. Highly recommend taking his class.
He definitely made such a boring topic an entertaining class. He is very kind and engaging with students and truly wants the class to learn.

Really caring professor! He is really interested in the material and tries to make classes as interesting as possible with demonstrations, a game day and guest speakers (which you can write about for extra credit). You just have at home quizzes every week, 3 tests, and a final project which is not too hard at all! He does go the whole 2 hrs though.
Professor Lubrano is SO nice! He really wants his students to do well and brings in guest speakers sometimes that are very interesting.

Professor Lubrano is a great professor! He is caring and very passionate and knowledgeable about the supply chain that not only impacts the USA but also international countries. He also does a perfect job at teaching such a complex subject!
Professor Lubrano was a great teacher and I learned a lot. This class wasn't to difficult if you went and paid attention in class. I highly suggest taking his supply chain management class.
He lectures well and is big on participation. Has a semester long group project that he grades pretty easy on. Tests were hard though, one midterm and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He grades the group project very easy. Tests are hard but if you participate in class and do the homeworks its a manageable class.

Kind, caring, entertaining, grandfather-type professor. I took his night class: 1-2 textbook chapters a week with a journal entry due (long readings). His tests are hard but he tells you what will be on them. Participate in class and do well on the group project. He does not respond to emails quickly
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: go to class and do the handful of papers due and you will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: no exams only essays. attendence matters. very interesting topics
I really enjoyed Professor Diel's class, but I will say she was a tough grader on the essays, and participation does matter. The material can get interesting, and overall it was not a horrible class.
the topic and lectures were interesting. Graded by super long writing assignments and attendance only.

Lori Diel is good at getting material across but I would only suggest taking her if it is a class for your major. There are only 2 tests which are 3 essays 1,000 words each but are so specific that you always write more to get at least an 88 on them. 6 quizzes that are confusing. If you miss class you won't pass the questions that were covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great prof! Cares about her students and is accessible/understanding. Lecture heavy, but it's always very interesting. Tests are take home papers you have a week to complete. I would most certainly take her class again, it was a wonderful time. If you put in a bit of effort you'll do fine!
Aztec art is a hard course, but she's passionate about the material
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Diel is such an amazing professor! She's very accessible outside of class and always answers your questions. I was super nervous to take the class since I've never taken an art class, but I got an A with an average amount of studying. Her lectures are super interesting and engaging, but be ready to take a lot of notes. Dr. Diel is the best!

LOVE this class (but I also love art history) She lectures A LOT, but it is interesting stuff. She has great stories and concepts about each piece of art and is very knowledgeable. Only grades are tests, participation, and one paper. Get ready to study, memorize, and learn about amazing art!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took this class by mistake but i love it! Very fascinating. She is helpful and easy to reach.

Take detailed notes during class. With her lectures alone, you don't need the textbook. Regurgitate all the info on tests and you'll be fine. Papers and test essays compose most of your grade, and she is picky with writing, so be sure to take her feedback on your writing seriously. Long lectures, but overall a kind professor and interesting course
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is probably one of the hardest fine arts classes at TCU, so if it's not for your major don't take it. Diel grades both essays and essay questions insanely hard. The lectures are boring and are easy to fall asleep during since the room is dark for slide shows. Final is cumulative, has 80 art pieces, and is worth a quarter of your grade.

This is the hardest class I have ever taken. I studied harder for this class than I did any of my other classes this past semester and I BARELY passed with credit. Would not take again. Unreasonably difficult for an undergraduate course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is very knowledgeable about the subject. Tests are mostly writing, but are manageable. All the information you'll need to know for the tests is discussed in class. Participation is encouraged and this helps lectures to be more interesting. With this prof, this class is not as bad as people say art history classes normally are.

One of hardest classes I've ever taken. Professor is demanding and sticks to the syllabus. Attendance is necessary to know anything that is happens during classes, as the pictures she chooses mostly don't have any evaluation online. It's a tough class. Definitely not for people not interested in Art history and Mexico itself.

Great teacher! I am not a good test taker and although I felt like I never had time to answer all of the essays, I still ended up with a B in that class. She really knows what she is talking about and loves art. You don't need a textbook because she will give you all the information you need in class.

I took intro to art history and loved it! However, there is a ton of pieces you need to memorize and the final is cumulative. Tests are long and involve essays and multiple choice questions. I learned so much though and I'm glad I took it.

You should take any art history class from this teacher. She is very informed of the information she is teaching. She is very willing to give her analyzation of artworks to aid you in your interpretation. I am not an art history major, but I had no problem in her Art of Mexico class.

Wonderful class that has information that will honestly help with future classes in unexpected ways. Study diligenlty for tests (flashcards are key) and try your best on the essay assignments, which she grades incredibly hard. Enthusiastic professor and interesting class. Take if you can!

With the writing assignments, she could have been more clear with what content she wanted because she kept changing her mind. Her tests are somewhat easy but she is a hard grader with writing and can be contradicting with what she tells you to do.

GREAT PROFESSOR! She makes it very clear whats going to be on the tests. Must go to class to have everything make sense. must study!! lots of memorization. She makes the class really interesting and a lot of fun.

unbelievably inconsistent in what she wants in your papers, i had two professors edit my paper and they said that it was quality however she seemed to disagree. Her tests are long and she is often unclear about what information she wants you to know for the tests themselves (which of the 80 pieces you'll look at for the three tests).

This class is very interesting, but it does require a lot of work. I did not have a problem doing so, with Art History being my major, but if you are taking it for fun, keep that in mind. Lectures are pertinent. Also, the papers are graded pretty hard, so keep them clear and concise and never make assumptions about the piece you are writing on.

Honestly, this course was challenging.  I was not expecting to learn so much about art.  Tests were mostly essay and about a few pieces of art out of 40-50 pieces.  There is one paper you have to do.  Final consists of a 5 page essay.  Not bad...actually became a much better writer after taking this course.  She is nice and helpful.

tough teacher. inconsistent in what she wants.  sometimes unsure of information about the pieces she teaches and expects you to know it for the test.  very picky grader for essays and paper.  as an english major, she had a problem with my wording which was not grammatically incorrect.  my eng. prof. thought it was well written, which she didnt.

I dreaded the class but ended up loving it. She is very nice and makes it clear what will be on the tests. The class itself requires a lot of memorization, but it's definitely possible to get an A. There is a lot of emphasis on writing, so it will be easier for you if you're a good writer.

she is really nice and pretty laid back. that class itself was kinda borring, not because of her, but just the nature of the class. try not to take it early in the morning, because you sit in the dark looking at slides the whole time. perfect to fall asleep. she makes it very clear the info that you will need for the test, but its alot of studying.

The chick thinks she is an English teacher, she grades papers extremely hard.  Tests are fair, if you study your notes, and memorize...memorize...memorize you will do well.  I recommend placing the artwork on notecards to study.
very knowledgable.  nice lady, smart, knows what shes talking about, and is a good teacher.

She was very helpful if you were confused or had a question about a piece you were to be tested on.  She updates the slides after every class so stay up with those.  This class is a lot of memorization and you may freak out b/c you think it's a lot but when you get to the test you realize it wasn't that bad.  Very fun class.

She was hard and the class was boring. It an hr and a half of lecture about paintings geez shoot me.I explained to her I had missed some classes due to my busy work schedule and needed some help and she said tough you pick work over school uh no it's paying bills. dont get on her bad side ****
She is really nice and makes the class very interesting. The tests are hard but if you go to class and study hard it is definitly possible to make an A.

She is really funny and interesting.  She is always helpful and very intelligent.  The class is not easy with all the memorizing but if you study like you should, then you'll make a good grade.  Easy B if you study.
If you actually listen in class and dont fall asleep you will do FINE. She is easy to listen to if your interested, and if you study at IHOP the night before you could probably pull a high B.

Tough class, would not advise it for incoming freshman. ALOT of memorizing, its stressful. I learned alot, but I was happy it was over. good class, you just have to work really hard to even get a C or a B.

Diel makes snap judgements about students, and refuses to apologize when she is proven wrong about someone. She mostly knows Aztec art, so if you want to learn about Mayans or Incans, take a class from Guderjan and buy an art book at the Kimbell.

Diel is a good professor. If you ever are unsure about a slide she is talking about in class she'll willingly answer your questions. The tests are difficult but who says college is easy?She's always on top of things and knows the information very well

Tough stuff.  She enjoys the material but expects so much out of people in an into class.  Very hard to do well in, also dark room makes you sleepy.  I would have dropped but I'm a moron.  P.S. the art building is far away
This is not an easy class, but she is a good professor. I never figured out how to take her essay tests and the amount of slides you have to memorize date, author, and other stuff on is ridiculous.
I could not stand her. she picked her favorites and was very unhelpful!!!

If you're a good writer, her all-essay tests aren't too bad. You do have to memorize a lot of slides, but it's not tough if you make flashcards.  Don't buy the book, I didn't touch mine.  Be prepared to take a lot of notes.

She's one of the easier in the art history department.  Does make you learn tons of slides, but all of them do.  And 10-12 slides is the norm for art history tests so no big thing.  She will try to help you if you need it.
cool class, but get ready to memorize a TON of slides and then be dissapointed when there is like 10 on the test
very interesting class, must study a lot- must know 50-60 slides, only 10-12 on tests

Dr. Lucas is a cool, funny man, and a great professor. He taught us how to use Word efficiently and apply it to my our own projects. Be prepared to write. You have several big writing projects and small weekly assignments. Very clear grading criteria. He gives you the opportunity to clear up your mistakes through several drafts. Great experience.

Dr. Lucas is great and very helpful. Coding in the humanities is an easy course with minimal homework and one project (group or solo) at the end of the semester. You have full creative freedom for the project and are given all the material needed to complete it. This is a great course for fulfilling a humanities credit!

3 big group projects. They are a lot of work but are doable if you split it up. Tough grader, but is willing to help you. He lets you do revisions, but by the time he grades it you dont want to do it anymore. I took this as a core and would not recommend it. But it isn't terrible, just annoying amount of work and too hard for a core class.

A tough course but if you put time into it you WILL succeed. Dr. Lucas is extremely caring and will do everything he can to help you outside of class. Asking questions will be super important, and be ready for a project-based classroom.

He is incredibly detailed with the assignments he gives you, so you know what to expect. He will cancel class occasionally, but he'll always notify you beforehand. Don't expect to get a good grade on the first project, but take his notes in the revisions and you'll get a much better grade. Showing up is part of the grade, but you'll learn a lot.
The class was mostly group projects which could be difficult but he gave the opportunity to redo them for a higher grade. Attendance was mandatory for activities but he offered many days off.

Dr. Lucas is a super nice guy but his projects are nearly impossible. Grading criteria was always unclear and hard to do well on projects the 1st time around. He lets you do revisions for full credit and is great if you meet him outside class, but I wouldn't recommend taking this class. He's a super critical grader and the content itself is boring.

Trust me, do not take this professor. The projects are extremely detail oriented - he does not help students step by step like he should and students rely on each other to figure things out. He nearly fails most students for projects but offers revisions. Take this class if you want to waste your time and deal with a lazy teacher.

Professor Lucas is a great teacher but his projects are extremely hard and if you do not have a basis of Technical Writing it will be difficult. I suggest meeting with him and he is very kind and lets anyone do revisions for each of his projects.

Had this class last semester and learned a lot about tech writing, even though I don't like it but it is useful. Group projects were a pain, and some students complained nonstop about every little thing. A lot of work, but option to revise for higher grades was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Projects are so hard/long and grades extremely hard. Does not give clear instructions, feedback or examples. Nothing makes sense and you have to rely on people in your class for information and instructions because he wont help.

Great professor, heavy workload though. two group projects and two on your own. He gives opportunities to revise projects with lots of helpful feedback, so if you don't do well the first time you can bring your grade up. As long as you do all your work and go to class you should get a good grade.

Professor doesn't explain the projects and refuses to give examples of anything. He is really boring and assigns so much homework that he doesn't mention in class and doesn't post it in TCU online until like a day before. Very hard grader but when you ask him questions about project he says it looks fine then proceeds to take off points for it.

Literally the worst class I have ever taken at TCU. His lectures are painfully boring and he gives so much busy work. The lectures are a waste of time and the projects are awful. Take literally anyone else. Using my last pass no credit on this class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I could not think of a more useless class then Tech Writing and he somehow makes it even less interesting with his horrific lectures. Every project is absolutely idiotic--> do not take him

I thought Power & Protest would be one of those easy electives. I was wrong. Although I got an A, there were so many homework assignments and so much reading on top of that. Make sure you participate because thats most of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Lucas is a very passionate professor, but gives a TON of homework, class assignments and projects. 5 projects total for the course and its all crammed in with lots of homework and readings on top of that. Hard grader, but does give you a chance to fix it. I wouldn't take him again because its all busywork. He's a cool dude though.

MEMORIZE EVERYTHING! Best tip: PRINT CHAPTER OUTLINE on afirstlook .com BEFORE the lecture. During class write lecture notes. Then after class highlight everything yall discussed. At the end of his lecture he says "look for this in the book," which is ALWAYS in the chapter outline. Nice professor, but hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He requires a lot of reading for the course but outlines exactly what he wants you to get out of the readings. It is an interesting course and one that he brings a genuine excitement to each and every class period.

POWER & PROTEST: Easiest A. Read one chapter a week and if you scan it for the key concepts he gives you, that's all you need. Made a 100% on the midterm. Group project at the end. Super nice prof, easy A and core credit.

Dr. Lucas is one of my favorite professors so far. I have taken him twice and will take him again next semester. Always keeps class very interesting and never afraid to let class out early! Gives you a good amount of time for projects but expects you to put in the work, allows revisions so his harsh grading is not too bad. Very nice and funny guy!

30223. Don't know why he's English Dept. head. It's gotten progressively worse throughout the semester. Really unclear on when things are due and how to do things. Busywork. Pointless projects. No room for creativity in the least. If you email him, he may never answer. And if he does, he'll beat around the bush and tell you to ask another student.
Awesome documentary class!
Senior seminar, easiest ever. No stress, lovely class. I enjoyed it.

This class (Professional Writing & Editing) is almost like business writing - do NOT take it if you are not required to, or unless you are interested in business writing. This is not creative writing! Dr. Lucas is nice and helpful, but the work required for the class is difficult. Dr. Lucas doesn't actually teach a whole lot.

Dr. Lucas is amazing. I have taken a lot of classes at TCU and found his to be one of the most rewarding. He does require excellence in work, but I have never seen a professor more willing to help you. He will make you a better writer and more coherent communicator if you take the knowledge he offers. He is also an excellent leader/great resource!!

He is a pompous man who likes to talk down to his class, because--afterall--he is much smarter than you. There is SO much work in his Technical Writing and Document Design class. I would recommend that you not take it, but if you are looking, that probably means you are required to take it. If that is the case, I feel sorry for you.
great professor! does lots of multimedia writing and bestseller books but doesn't lecture enough
cool class, lot of computer work. not typical stuf
One of the worst classes ever taken at TCU. So much random busy work. Always working on projects, really boring class. If taking for degree find another class cause its not worth it.
Took him for summer school class on Documentary. Not bad for a summer class, got some good things from him about argument and movies.
great class, knows hi s stuff.. useful but a lot of work. fair grader w revisions
Very nice professor. Always willing to help you with anything. Although it seems like you're always working on something
really fun professor. seems like you're always working on a paper though, not much down time. he does allow to revise every paper as many time as you want after the due date which is nice.
fun class at first, then alot of work at the end, overall worth it

Assigns a lot of projects.  Be prepared to work.  I learned a lot from his class.  He helps prepare you for the real world.  Overall nice guy, don't be afraid to go to his office hours and tell him your issues.
okay class
Lucas rocks!
Was a pretty easy A for me.
Deals well with airhead Education majors.

THIS GUY SUCKS!!!! He is biased, unfair, inconsiderate, and he grades on some imaginary scale based on his like of dislike for you. I made 100's on every test and quiz he gave, but he showed a strong dislike for me in class and in return I received a B in the class. Any assignment that was not graded based on questions missed I received low grades
Rude. Unfiar.

He has some issues, yes, but he devotes everything into his job.  He grades your papers rather strict and dedicated a lot of time to grading.  He just wants you to learn and get something out of the class.  Be prepared to work hard, and start projects waayyy early.  Then it's a def. A!!

He is the worst teacher I have ever had.  I took him in the fall but I still feel the need to warn you.  He has person issues, and takes it out severely on the students.  He is an unfair grader, and is biased towards students.  BEWARE
Obviously has problems with his life and wants to take them out on you... WORST TEACHER I've ever had in my life... WORST GRADER... It's like he's out to get you.  I agree... he NEEDS to be FIRED!
DO NOT TAKE HIM! He can be very misleading. Big mistake if you want to take freshman comp with him. He loves to hear himself talk rubbish. I agree that he really needs to be fired!!

He's fake --seems like he cares and likes you, but really he's one of the most disrespectful, rude, noncaring teachers at TCU. He critisizes your work, rather than help you out.  He's out to make you feel like an ass.  DO NOT TAKE HIM!! HE SHOULD BE FIRED!
rude and didnt care about feelings or you as a person.  never had such an inconsiderate professor.
Nice professor. I didn't find his teaching hard. He grades fairly but tough. He's a well read person.
Hard and is not the nicest person!! Grade papers hard also...dont  want to take
Very helpful; there is a lot of writing so be prepared!! Overall I enjoyed going to class.
This was my favorite class last semester.  It was a freshman seminar in globalization.  I learned lots and always wanted to talk in class.
No Comments

Picked this professor for Calculus 2, and I don't think any calculus professor can be as caring and understanding as this professor. Super compassionate and makes the course a breeze. One homework a week, 3 exams, a final, and extra credit. Very streamlined and if you turn in all the work, it's impossible to fail.

Professor Wiggins is the best! His lectures are very straightforward and he is super helpful in office hours if something is confusing. He gives so many points on quizzes, homework, and tests just for knowing the f

He is a good professor however I had friends that had wayyyy easier stats professors at TCU. He definitely doesn't give you anything for free and you need to attend lecture if you want to understand everything. He's honestly a good teacher and I learned the information however I love math and it comes pretty easily to me. I know some struggled.
Best math teacher. He teaches to his tests and does a ton of examples to make sure you know it. Love him!

My favorite professor! He is straightforward about what is expected and lectures really well. I felt that this class was easy but then again I love math. It is a STATS class so you do need to work. It's not easy for everyone but he helps you when you go to him.

Wiggins is great. Lectures are straightforward, he offers extra credit (with a tutorial how to do the entire thing), and will always help you if you seek him out. I'm not a math person but stats with him was easy and I enjoyed coming to class.

He made stats easy! I would definitely recommend this class. He was very helpful and clear to understand. His lectures were straight forward and entertaining. Even if you miss class, he posts everything online, but still go!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is a very nice and caring teacher. He always is available for extra help after class and does review sessions before exams. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Attendance is not mandatory but it helps to take notes in class.

Professor Wiggins was incredible, and one of the best teachers I've ever had. Calculus is a difficult subject regardless of the professor, yet he cares beyond the course and about each student. He will stay after class and help you for however long you need. Great teacher, calculus sucks but he makes it slightly more enjoyable.

Mr. Wiggins expectations are that you are to be as genius as him.  He teaches you so much material that is above and beyond what a normal Applied Calc class is expected.  He teaches so quickly that you can't keep up and then gets mad if you ask him to slow.  He appears to be interested in showing how smart he is, then getting us to understand.

Mr. Wiggins is the best applied calculus teacher at TCU. If you take his class, you will genuinely learn a lot. He is extremely caring, and you can tell he really wants his students to succeed. The class has homework, quizzes which are done at home, and 3 exams plus a final exam, as well as extra credit projects. Highly recommend taking his class!
Dr. Wiggins was great! He was very accommodating and always gave extra credit. He took the time to get to know his students and prepared us well for our exams.

Professor Wiggins made learning about stats bearable/enjoyable coming from somebody who isn't great at math. He wants you to succeed and will help you get there IF you seek out the help. He has office hours and offers a good amount of extra credit. Not the easiest math class but you feel fulfilled when you complete it.
thoughtful, truly cares about students success. lots of extra credit. makes concepts easy to understand

Prof Wiggins wants to help you succeed, and you can help him help you. Take him for Applied Calc and PLEASE GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS!! Even if you want to sit and solve questions. He is always seeking to make student's experience better. He is an attention to detail math teacher so you might find that annoying. Start strong so you won't strugle later

Honestly Im bad at math and got a B+, he was so amazing and whenever I needed help with the HW he was always available. He also gives a TON of extra credit. He listens to what his students need and provides them a solution. definitely take him you wont regret it!!

Professor Wiggins is an incredible instructor, you can tell that he genuinely cares about his students learning the material and always goes the extra step to help prepare you for homework, quizzes, and exams. Would definitely recommend!

Professor Wiggins is by far one of the best professors at TCU. He cares so much for his students, and even holds extra review sessions on the weekends before exams. If you have to take Applied Calc, take it with Wiggins!

He is a great professor! He explains everything very clearly and always answers questions. He has lots of office hours and is always willing to help his students. He gives extra credit on all of his test and drops your lowest quiz. The only thing is you cant use calculators.
He is an amazing professor. Clearly explains every concept in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Wiggins is a great professor. Highly recommend. If you don't understand a concept, just ask him and he will try to explain it in another way that you'll understand. Although he does not give test curves, tests and homework often have extra credit questions that add 5-10 points. He will make time to meet with you outside of class if you need it.

Prof. Wiggins is the best!! He is super kind & loves talking to his students. He's very good at explaining how to work out problems & will stop at anytime if anyone has questions. He likes to make sure everyone participates so he will randomly call your name asking you how to work out a problem. I'm bad at math, but he helped me out a ton!

3 Test (including final), Hw every or every other week, occasional in-class problems for attendance. She explains things super well, but can move fast. I went to her office hr and she was super helpful and willing to work with me for however long it took. Can't ever seem to get a good grade on her exams though.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Morgan was sweet as a person. Is willing to help you and wants you to succeed. However, to be in her class you MUST buy $300 D2L replacement. The exams are also nearly impossible. The homework is super easy but NOTHING like the exams and does not prepare you. Lots of math and word problems, personally that was difficult. Syllabus makes no sense

Not sure why she has such bad ratings on here. I loved her for intro micro! The content is boring, but she made her lectures interactive and informative. You will have to work for an A as the tests are difficult, but she wants her students to do well and will help a lot outside of class. She rounds grades if you have good attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: She gives somewhat interesting lectures but the content is pretty boring. Tests are very difficult and require a lot of studying if you hope to get anything higher than a n a B. Overall not an easy class, don't miss a lecture or you will find yourself very far behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super nice teacher and really cares about her students learning the material. Goes through the notes thoroughly. The majority of your grade is from the tests and final, although there are some homework assignments and a group project. A somewhat tough class, but she makes it doable.

Econ is not easy but Bergeland breaks it down and explains concepts well using examples. Lectures are engaging and she cares about her students. Textbook is used for reading outside of class and is helpful. Grade is mostly based on 3 multiple choice exams. Limited homework. Will succeed if u take good notes and put in time before tests. Recommend!

Professor Bergeland is really nice and fun to talk to if you enjoy Economics, but her class is an absolute beating. The tests are so long and difficult that barely anyone can finish it in the time allowed. The lectures cover the basics but you're never trained for the much more advanced application questions she asks on the exam. Would not suggest

My biggest issue with this class was the lack of practice problems given. There are problems in the textbook, but to check your answers you have to email your answers to her a week before the test, which is pretty unrealistic for a student to have time for in my opinion. Tests are hard and take a really long time. Definitely must study.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Overall, she's alright. She has a great personality, but her teaching style is vague, and thus you pretty much have to read the book and teach the class to yourself. Group presentation isn't tough at all (unless you're a business student with six other presentations). Overall, wouldn't recommend, but if you need this class in a pinch, go for it.

Read the book for any clarifications. She is math-heavy so do the problems in the book. She uses some of those exact ones for the exams. Her lectures aren't super clear but if you write down everything and then refer back to the book, you should at least get a B. Don't be afraid to ask for clarification in class, but you need to put in work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dont let the good looks fool you. Drop the class after the first week because the material is not covered clearly. You have to take notes over what she says because the material on the board during lectures is meaningless. Very harsh grader and does not extend a hand for help.
Tough class, quizzes extremely difficult. Can be very hard to know what to study for test. There is so much material and she does not give us a great idea of what will be on test.

Ms. Bergeland is very challenging. Half of my class of 45 people dropped the class after the second test. There are about 12 quizzes, and they can KILL your grade. The book is a little confusing and does not have practice problems. I really enjoyed Ms. Bergeland's teaching style, you can tell she spends a lot of time preparing for her lectures.

No homework. Do not buy the textbook. I didn't realize how large of a part of your grade the exams are and that kind of screwed me but as long as you study for like an hour you will do well on it. 10 take home quizzes open note. 2 exams and 1 presentation. I really liked this class it was interesting and easy class for core.

The G.O.A.T. Dr. Montgomery is a great, empathetic resource during this course and beyond. Take him! Experimental Methods can be difficult; it is a semester-long project that requires dedication, but it can be fun if you choose a project you are passionate about. Dr. Montgomery will make sure that you are prepared and on the right track.
You get 3 skips and textbook is optional! Loved this class, learned so much and he gives you a study guide of whats on exam and amazing professor. You do one presentation that is graded soooo easy.

Dr. Montgomery is pretty great. He tries to make the class fun even though it's Intro so it covers a lot of stuff. The class is basically two big tests and then the weekly quizzes. The tests can be hard though so actually study for them. I do wish I could take him again but I do not need any more political science classes.

Montgomery is a great guy and pretty funny. His classes are all lectures, have to complete a quiz after every chapter (online) and a presentation that you can record online as well. He posts the study guide for each exam and even reviews them beforehand. You really do not need to go to class to succeed, though do not know how he counts off for that
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Montgomery is amazing!! Take him! He truly cares about his students and the content he is teaching us and his class was really easy. There are only two tests so it is important to do well on those otherwise, making an A would be difficult.

He is my favorite professor. I took his class as core and it's awesome. Take him, he's the best. He's so nice and he grades very fairly. The tests are based on the study guides which is very helpful. Make sure to do the weekly quizzes, which are easy if you go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Montgomery is great. I'm in his Experimental Methods class and while the first half of the semester was a bit dry (he knows this) content wise, the second half is all working on your paper and you do a lot of it in class which is nice. I've gone to his office asking questions a number of times and he has always been super cool to me.
Simply just a great professor and person. Not much else to add.
Matthew Montgomery. mAtthew mOnTGomery. Scramble the capital letters (AOTG). GOAT. Greatest of All Time.
Dr. Montgomery is an amazing professor. His class was fun and engaging. Take him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Montgomery is a good professor. Attendance is not mandatory. Exams only include information on the study guides he provides before each exam. He does require one 5-7 minute presentation, however, grading is super lenient. Good professor to take for Political Science course.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Truly a great professor. Caring and passionate about the content and wants students to succeed. Provides reviews before exams full of all potential test questions. Highly recommend.

Dr. Montgomery is the ABSOLUTE BEST! There were 2 reflection papers that were a maximum of two pages double-spaced, so super easy. We had three tests and Dr. Montgomery always gave us a study guide that he would go over the answers to before the test. AMAZING class and FANTASTIC professor! I will definitely be taking Dr. Montgomery again!

Every exam has a study guide in which all test questions are directly from the study guide. This study guide is then gone over during class in which Dr. Montgomery explains all the answers, making it an easy A. At the same time it's an interesting class where Dr. Montgomery truly cares about your success.

professor Montgomery was great, I would take him 10 times if I could. He has two tests worth 65% of your grade. so, be ready to study for those. If you put in roughly 4 hours of studying for these tests each you WILL get an a in this class. he gives a study guide which is very related to the test. the presentation is 7-10 minutes alone. grades easy

Very easy class. His exams are copy and paste from the study guide he gives you and goes over the answers class before exam. One presentation that is also not hard. He is a nice guy that wants his students to do well.

He wants all of his students to succeed and it is so clear in the way that he teaches. Literally the best professor I have ever had and I would take a third class from him if I could, he slays. If you have the opportunity to take a class from him you must!! You learn a lot and you will most likely get a good grade in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Such a fun teacher. Understanding in terms of deadlines. 2 tests and 2 presentations which are free choice. very easy grader
