Dr. Montgomery is the best professor I have had at TCU. He's super understanding of your circumstances and makes an effort to engage all of his students. He focuses on the right things and gets the most out of his students. If you ever have the pleasure of taking him I would highly recommend it.
This class was awesome and I would definitely recommend it! He gives very clear study guides for the rest and is not trying to trick you on any of the tests.
Very easy and interesting class. You have 2 exams and one presentation (you get to pick your topic). Lectures are kind of long but if you go and take notes the exams are super easy.

Dr. Montgomery is one of the best professors at TCU! He is super chill, has interesting lectures, and a super-easy class. Only two exams, one at the beginning and a final. Super easy homework once a week that is impossible not to get a 100% on. Would recommend to everyone, including non-poly-sci majors for an easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Highly recommend professor Montgomery for intro to American politics. Tests are exactly like the reviews and one weekly quiz that you answer through the book, super easy. Also one easy presentation but no other assignments. He is super nice and funny, and very easy to reach outside of class. Interesting class too, would definitely take again!

Super clear grading criteria (study guide is literally the test) and also a fairly easy grader. Lectures were really clear and concise, he never rambled or went on tangents about random things. Really personable and wants to help his students succeed, willing to work with you if you just ask. One of my favorite professors I've taken at TCU!

Dr. Montgomery was amazing! The homework load was not hard at all and is a grade booster at the end of the semester when he puts it in. He has clear and to the point lectures and tries to get participation to make it fun. He has 2 exams with study guides put out before that tells you exactly what is on the test. I really enjoyed the class!

Dr. Montgomery was the GOAT. Everything was very straight forward. No surprises on the exams. Gives clear study guides and goes over them before the test. I needed him outside of class and he was always available and happy to help.

Great professor. His class had a ton of discussion, he fostered it in really fun and interesting ways. He does not take a long time to lecture, his points are concise, he encourages everyone to participate (but never forces people), and has a good sense of humor that makes the class much less dry. Lowish workload, all the assignments have purpose.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Lynn Jackson's grading system is blatantly inconsistent. She arbitrarily deducts points and provides varying feedback and grades for the same work among different students. I STRONGLY advise against taking her class. She is the most frustrating professor and class I have ever had.

She is a great teacher and teaches the class well, but you can't slip up or stop paying attention for a second, especially for the stuff outside of class. I missed my mentor meetings, and I might fail the class because of it. :(

I really enjoyed having Dr. Jackson for UNLF. She is very sweet and easy to talk to. Very few assignments. The assignments we did have were always easy and she always said that we should never be pulling an all nighter over them. Make sure to stay off your phone and engage in the class!

DON'T overlook the negative reviews: she has most removed. This is my second review of Lynn Hampton.
DO. NOT. TAKE . HER.
Her lectures are pretty much the "Lynn Hampton show." It's miserable. Your views are ignored and unwelcome if they aren't hers-not even in like a political sense, she just HAS to be right all the time. 
Don't do it. Trust me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hampton really cares about the material being taught, there is a lot of reading but all of it is interesting, assessments are all papers or presentations.

I would recommend not taking this professor. My biggest problem with this class is that she gives instructions for assignments a week or less before they're due, so I would sometimes have only a week to write major papers. The content of this class is also very biased towards a certain narrative, and you're graded by only a few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Easy class because most people got A's, but it was just unbearable. She plays favorites, encourages discussion but doesn't want to hear opinions different than hers, grade is based off of a few things, end of semester workload was so heavy for no reason. Not a great prof, not an enjoyable class. Most negative reviews are accurate here.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: End of the semester she floods you with work (two semi big projects)... like within the last week. Your views are not quite welcome if they do not align with the teachings here.

Dr. Hampton is my favorite professor & this course is the best one I've taken at TCU! She is accessible outside of class and incredibly knowledgeable. I've learned so much from this class and the readings. Lectures are honest and engaging. Participation is graded, but the class is discussion-based and provides many opportunities to participate.

This is a Black feminisms class. I enjoyed the class, but the overall structure of the course was a bit monotonous at times. Know that there is a lengthy group research paper/presentation at the end, but it is not graded harshly provided that you put effort into doing it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Hampton was one of my favorite professors I have had at TCU! She is very passionate about course material and encourages student discussion. Participation matters in this class, so be sure to speak during class discussions. There is a lot of reading, but you can usually get away with skimming most of it. Take her if you can!

This class is supposed to be focused on how the US education system is affected by gender, race, and socioeconomic status, but the vast majority of the class was focused on the issues between blacks and whites in society. Grading in the class was also very weird, with poorly organized rubrics and subpar feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Hampton is more interested in making you align with her own political beliefs than teaching you anything. Any time you agree, the conversation stretched the entire class. If you disagree, well the conversation has to move on and you cant speak anymore. I wish she could separate politics from education, but unfortunately, she couldn't.

Professor Hampton herself is a decent person. Be very prepared to discuss racial inequalities in the school system over the entirety of sociology in the school system. Take notes in class, as there is a book review where you have to compare it to the articles. A lot of big assignments at the end, the final being a (group) Research Project.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Hampton is a great professor. While the class may be boring at times, she genuinely cares about the topic and her students. She is willing to have honest conversations about school culture and call people out if she needs to. Great honors class.

Dr Hampton is an amazing woman and professor who prides her class being a discussion based setting. There will be a multiple presentations and a few essays here and there but a majority are in groups so its not as exhausting as it sounds. She gives an emphasis on participation and the more you speak your mind, the more rewarding the class will be.

Dr. Hampton is just a great human-being. There is a lot of reading to do outside of class, but it isn't super necessary to do. No formal exams, just projects or presentations that typically involve pretty long papers. There were a ton of projects back to back at the end of the year. To get a good grade, just get your work done.

An overall okay class. The material was less about the school system and more about racial inequality. There's a lot of reading assignments but by the end of the semester no one was actually doing them. She's a pretty easy grader and most of the class is discussion based. Be prepared for very liberal material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed class. Quizzes kinda hard but good amount of opportunities to boost grade. Lots of reading but no textbook

Social Problems was a super cool class but the quizzes were impossible. There was so much reading and the quizzes were so detail oriented. It was heavily based on discussion and group projects which, for me, sucked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Hamptons Cultural Visions Class was amazing. The class was heavily discussion based and once a week people gave presentations and facilitated class discussion. There's a lot of readings and you have to read two books but they are all interesting! Highly recommend this class for people who want to learn more about the education system.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: The class itself is not too bad. It is a points class out of 500 points, the final is 200 points and the other two exams are 100 points each. There is a short answer section on the exams where she gives you full or no credit. The other 100 points come from participation and group projects. She gives extra credit, but it doesn't help much.

TONS OF GROUP PROJECTS! Personally didn't have the bet experience in her class.  I don't feel like I got that much out of it and she isn't always clear on expectations.  Show up to class because attendance counts, 3 tests including non cumulative final.

Professor Hampton was overall a great professor. There are only 2 tests, 3 group projects, and the final (not comprehensive). The group projects are easy 100s if you simply do the work, but the tests can be a little tricky if you don't know the material super well. They are also worth a lot of your grade, so you have to read the book and study.

The class is overall very easy. Do not spend much time preparing for discussions or group projects, she gives out easy A's. There are 2 exams and a final. I recommend reading the textbook a few days before the exam and highlighting vocab. Be familiar with different perspectives. Sometimes she also throws on a few dates and key people.

Social Problems was one of my favorite classes that I have taken. Dr. Hampton was awesome... her lectures went the whole class time but they were very interesting. I would recommend to do the homework readings because there are quizzes, but they aren't hard if you read. No tests, but there are projects.

I thought this class was interesting, and pretty easy.  Her lectures are basically the same as the textbook, so if you just show up, pay attention, and skim the textbook before the test you should be able to get an A. The projects and tests are super easy, and overall I'd definitely recommend her.

Professor Hampton is a nice women and is pretty chill about sleeping in class. Her lectures are really long and she just reads out of the text book word for word. So skipping class wouldn't hurt. Plus its extra credit to come to class. She is not the best teacher but her class is pretty easy. Just cram read the textbook for the tests.

Professor Hampton's class wasn't too bad. You get credit for coming to class, but I sometimes dreaded the class personally. The test are straightfoward, but you have to read the book if you want to pass the test. Overall, if you want to do well in this class, and put in the work, you will.

Professor Mackay is a great teacher. She gave one homework per week and there are three big essays throughout the semester. There is also a final essay and a presentation. You also have three campus events that you have to attend and then make a video about that experience

I took Stage Movement I. She was very easy going and everyone loves her including me. The only reason it was not a 5/5 for me is because time management was a big issue. In most classes, we didn't get to participate and get feedback. But what a loving character!
Lydia is my favorite professor Ive ever had. She is an amazing role model and I am so grateful to have had the opportunity to take her class.

Dr Mackay is the easiest to take for fine arts core. Just show up, all the info on the quiz are from lecture slides. You have to go to one play on campus and write a critique over it and perform a play in front of the class with a group. She gives many extra credit chances too. Only reason I got a B+ is because I never showed up yet still passed!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Super easy class overall but Lydia makes it very fun. I hate getting up in front of people and she created a welcoming environment where I felt comfortable. 10/10 would take

Ms. Mackay's Survey to Theatre is fun, easy, and inspirational. No tests, just quizzes (mc), she gives study guide. Final is open book (not very easy). The projects (telling a story, putting up a theatre show) are great, a lot of memories. Also, do the Extra Credit (going to watch a show) is easy and interesting way to enrich yourself in culture.

Best FAR credit to take at TCU. The class requires very little work and Mackay is caring, funny, and an easy grader as long as you come to class and participate. Do not take this class if you plan on skipping more than 3 days.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Best fine arts credit to take at TCU! She is super caring and fun as long as you show up and participate. Do not skip more than 3 classes as she will take off points. Quizzes and final are very easy. You will not have to spend any time outside of class studying. Highly recommend her for survey of theatre. One of my favorite TCU professors!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She is by far one of my favorite professors at TCU. We only have one day of learning a week and the others are designated to each person telling one story about themselves. The tests are come right out of the review she gives us and right out of the lectures in class.

Loved taking this class for core. She is so engaging and makes it fun. You get to use your book for the final exam and survey to theatre is said to be much easier compared to survey of musical theatre. Very easy A as long as you show up and study about an hour for tests. The worst part is telling a 5 min story in front of class.

I love her. She is such a good professor and keeps the class engaged. Very lenient and it is easy to get extra credit. Her quizzes are MC and are easy if you pay attention in class. Experienced teacher :)

Lydia is such a great professor and this is such an easy class. you need the book in class and she suggests that you read the chapters before hand, but you really don't need to because she goes through it all during the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Take Survey of Theater for a FA credit its so easy and enjoyable! Lydia is an awesome teacher very friendly and engaging. Tests are easy especially if you fill out study guides. You will have to tell a personal story in front of class, but it's not scary you can ready from paper. Lectures can get boring but not bad
Easiest class ever but make sure you go to classes becsuse after the third absense it will start affecting your grade.

Easiest class that I have taken so far. Lydia is great, very loud and enthusiastic. Have to attend a play or 2 on campus and do a group project. She doesn't like phones in class and takes attendance. As long as you turn in the few assignments that there are you'll get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Lydia is such a lively and nice professor. As long as you study maybe 1 hour for each test, this is a guaranteed A. She has two extra credit opportunities and many points to boost your grade throughout the semester. If you are looking for an easy fine arts elective, take this one.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT--Would take again

reviews.comment: Lydia really knows how to keep class interesting. She's an actress so she has experience in theatre which makes it fun. The tests are so easy and straight off the review. If you pay attention and show up its very easy to get an A. If you need a fine arts credit, take this class instead of survey of musical theatre!!!!

Professor Mackay is a great theater teacher. She keeps the lectures interesting and the expectations for the course very clear cut. She also gives many opportunities for extra credit, which is very helpful. Textbook readings are encouraged, but there is not much homework outside of class which is great. Overall very good professor.

She is an amazing professor, super engaging, encourages participation, and LOVES to hear from students during class. Her tests are incredibly easy and it's harder to not get an A than it is to get an A. Her final is open book and only 25 questions, and the two tests during the semester and very straightforward and multiple choice. Highly recommend.

One of the best theatre teachers I have ever had. She has an amazing way of helping you grow and learn. She is an amazing person and if you can take a class from her DO IT! Do not miss taking a class from this awesome human if you want to become an amazing performer or if you just want to be happy and learn.

Took her survey of theater class and it was an easy A. Test are super easy and straight forward. She grades super lenient and seemed like it was more of a completion grade more than anything. You don't really need to read the book, but she expects you to have it. Bottom line:  shes's super nice and chill, definitely recommend.

Take Lydia for Survey of Theatre! She is a really fun teacher and works hard to learn all your names. She makes you feel like a real person, not just a number in a big class. Go to the plays and write thorough reports, have fun with it!

Reading is optional, she'll go over it in class. You have to go see plays and critique them. Open book final. Requires you to go in front of 140+ classmates and tell them a story. Beware of class participation. 3 absences allowed before they affect your name. She makes sure to know everyone by name. Super fun.

Probably the easiest A if you're looking to get fine arts credit. Tests are easy if you study for maybe two hours. Gives a lot of extra credit and has an open book final. The "My Story" assignment is kind of nerve-wracking but it's definitely entertaining to listen to other peoples stories. I would definitely recommend taking this class.

Awesome prof! She really cares about her students and wants everyone to do well. Probably the easiest class I have taken at TCU but I still learned a lot. Highly recommend taking Survey of theatre with her, she's the best!
Easiest class ever. She really cares about her students and wants you to get an A, she's great. I liked her a lot, she makes the class interesting for sure.

Super nice and funny. Be careful of sitting in the front row, because on a whim she might just pull you up on stage for an impromptu scene. Easy, short tests and not too much out of class work. We had to see one TCU play for a grade, but could see an additional play for extra credit. Easy A!

Easy A for fine art, but at the same time you learn a lot. Six 25 question MC tests. Offered 200 points extra credit, and friends and I went to Dallas for a play, and became a lil more cultured. If you're lazy, you only need to read Bug, sparknote rest. She managed to keep a majority of 140 students engaged. High energy, fun, and a bit quirky.

Ms. Yarbrough is so so sweet and made my UNLF class something to look forward to. She always has a funny story or happy moment of her week to tell the class, and brings such a positive energy to her students. The class itself does require some work in the papers/homework articles, but if you work hard and put in the time, you will do well!

I absolutely LOVE Ms. Yarbrough!She is such a sweet lady and is never too busy to say hi and catch up with her students.  She is always in a good mood and it's obvious that she really enjoys what she does.Her tests can be tricky, but if you go to class, pay attention, and study a normal amount you will do extremely well.Bonus points for attendance!
Her tests are tough, but if you do the work, you'll do fine. She relates her lectures back to clinical experience, so that keeps the lectures interesting. I liked her a lot!

I really enjoyed Survey of Communication Disorders! 99.9% of her test questions come from her lecture, so although attendace isn't mandatory, if you don't go you miss out! DO ALL of the extra credit opportunities. they boost your grade A LOT! Very interesting class!!

very difficult class. her tests are compiled with whatever she feels like putting on them. no review for tests with loads of material. easy to talk with outside of class and seems like she wants to help with no idea how. be prepared to work.

In all honesty, she seems to be a great advocate for children needing services, but not an advocate for her college students. Be prepared to have to memorize everything for her exams, determine for yourself what is most important to learn, and to get rude/condescending responses to your emails if you ask questions.

don't email her without expecting a really rude response and oh yeah don't bother trying to make a good grade in her class the entire semester because she just will screw you over in the end.  She has no heart, and shows no sign of human emotion.  She takes pleasure in making others lives a living hell.  literally.

Comp 2. Centered around the 1960s in the US. Dr. Davis knows a lot about the time period. She lectures a lot and rambles on but sometimes they are interesting. Will help students in class and office hours. Only 3 papers all semester. She takes a while to grade papers which can be frustrating. Not an awful class but you will have to work for A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took her for comp 1, it was the most pointless class I've ever taken. Lectures are boring and could be communicated in an email but it takes her the full hour and 20 minutes.  She gets distracted easily and takes FOREVER to grade papers. She is caring and will help outside of class but expect to write 9 papers throughout the semester.

Lynda is a really awesome professor, she is always there to help you and answer any questions that you may have. Having said that, there are lots of essays on par with the standard and her lectures are pretty boring. Still, very nice and respectful.

The class was interesting and fun. We learned about the hero and his journey in the western. We had to write two papers, and do daily quizzes, but they were pretty easy if you did the readings. Readings were heavy, but if you read and attend class, you'll be fine.  Drops two lowest quiz grades.

Her grading and assignments are unorganized. You must do all the readings because she gives pop quizzes. Lots of reading in this class, quizzes definitely lower your grade. Interesting material. Would not recommend this if you just want it for CORE

Intro to Fiction with her isn't too bad. I pass/failed the class and easily made the grade. Not an easy A, but for sure an easy B. She's a little crazy and sometimes monotonous, but in some strange way I liked this class. You watch a lot of movies and her corkiness makes this class not as boring as other lit classes.

I had her my first semester, and I thought the class was hard, but now I see that it is just college that is hard.  Ms. Davis meet with me--even if it was her office hours.  She always answered my e-mails and smiled every day she walked in class.  I would recommend her.  Attend all class, and don't talk while she's talking.  You can revise papers.
No Comments

At first, I didn't like her, but she grew on me. She knows what she's talking about most of the time and it can be beneficial to listen to her. There's some reading for her class, but nothing too unbearable. It is very possible to get an A if you put the effort into it. Overall, pretty good teacher.

This class was by far the easiest I've had so far. NO TESTS. A lot of papers but they're very easy. We literally just went on field trips every day. awesome. she is kinda controlling but take this class!!!
Too controlling. take someone else

Not the best lab teacher. Treats you like a kindergartener. (i.e. tells you how to turn on your computer and sit down EVERY class). Very Controlling and Anal. Take one of the others. Pretty easy but probably still the hardest lab grader.
SHe is very nice and helpfull, the class isn't really hard if you just make sure you make the deadlines

if you keep up with printing off the powerpoint notes that she emails to the class and study the night before your tests.... you're fine. I made an A and probably missed the class about 10 times. The projects sound harder than they are. She's a little off the wall, but very helpful and understanding.
Very laid back class. you learn alot of practical stuff. Assignments aren't bad, but she grades grammar harder than my english teacher!
Easy class but lots of busy work.
Sometimes a little off the wall, but she creates a fun learning environment.
Had her for Basic Speech. Very nice and understanding professor. Grading is straightforward. Some group skits in class. 3 speeches total. Exams were tougher than expected though. Great class!

Definitely one of the easiest courses I've had so far. Very nice professor. Had a great time in her class all semester. A lot of in class activities and skits, and you have 3 presentations to do towards the end. Don't underestimate the exams though.

Def the easiest speech teacher at TCU, i highly recommend her over taking a class with a TA and a hundred other students. Not always the more organized, but a nice lady. Will prob go down as the least intellectual class you will ever take in college- you play lots of games, take personality quizzes, and give group speeches. not challenging.

Easiest class at TCU with an excellent teacher. You know exactly what she expects from you. She is also very accommodating and made class fun to sit through. My grade was so high I took a 0 on the final and still made an A
Advanced public speaking with armstead is the easiest class ive taken in college.

Amazing professor! Passionate about what he teaches and wants students to succeed. All exams are multiple choice/ true or false. Only assignment the entire semester is a 3 page musical review. Take this class!
I literally never went and got an A. You can use your phone..

Tests dont go along with study guide. Make sure to actually study the musicals he tells you to watch. Great professor though you just dont do well unless you pay attention to everything he says in class
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very passionate about musical theatre. However, his lectures contain a lot of information and he is not clear on what will be on the tests. Despite that, his class is easy and requires minimal effort. Listening and watching musical scenes is enjoyable and he uploads the PowerPoints shared in class. I would definitely take him.

94 for an A in this class, had to P/NC because I had a 93.7. Lectures so much so you can't know what's going on the test. Studied so much and got B's. You have the opportunity to replace one of the tests with extra credit (attending additional musical), but even with this I couldn't get a solid A. Kind of ridiculous given it was a core arts credit

TAKE HIM! He's very passionate about what he teaches and is hilarious. Your only grades are 3 tests+final+written production review and you get an extra credit option which can replace your lowest test grade. If you study and go to half of the classes you can easily pass your tests. Definitely recommend it's easy and he's a good professor.
100% would take again, he's so funny and his class is very easy if you study for the tests

TAKE THIS FOR ART CREDIT! All exams are lockdown browser but you take them in the lecture hall. Lectures are super entertaining. You have to go to one musical and write a paper on it. There is an option to go to another musical and write a report to replace your lowest exam grade. You get out early every day. Take this class.

He lectures the whole class and is not very clear on what will be on the test. Most of the test questions are things we have never gone over. Overall, he is very passionate about Musical Theater but is not the best at teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: my icon, i love this man. im not passionate abt musical theatre, but this mad made me passsionate.

THEA 11003 Survey of Theatre

It is very very easy and he is a nice dude. Just go to class and listen

He is a great professor. He lectures heavily but makes it super interesting by using relevant videos and stories about the topic, making it easy to engage. Tests are a bit difficult, but if you study and pay attention, all the tests are on the content covered. He is super nice and gives extra credit, so I definitely recommend taking this course.

He is really nice and funny! Definitely recommend taking his survey of theatre class. Easy A- as long as you try to study for the tests. 0 Homework. The whole grade is 4 tests and 1 play review but you can do an extra review to drop the lowest test grade. An A is a 94 so that's a little harder to get just because it's so high.

Easy class if you go to every class and study for the 4 tests you have. The final is not cumulative and is basically just test #4. He's a nice guy. Take a different teacher if possible because its just a bit too much work for a "core arts" credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mcquillen is very kind, funny, and engaging. However, his survey of theatre class had a lot more outside work than I was expecting. Also, his quizzes and exams are somewhat difficult. The lectures can be boring sometimes but overall I enjoyed the class. We had to write 3 short essays but they were graded easily.

love him as a professor but the class is definitely a lot of work for a fine art credit. he has a lot of knowledge and knows what he is talking about, but it is difficult and a lot of information if you dont have a fine arts background. there is a midterm, final, 3 papers, and 4 quizzes.
She goes super fast, so you kinda have to learn alot outside class, but shes super helpful and nice if you make an effort to know her. SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT!

Dr. B is a great instructor. I only wish I took her on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The material covered within a 50 minute class did not allow for digestion of the material. A longer class would help as we wouldn't feel so rushed in lecture. Great instructor, but harder course due to class length and rushed lectures.
The class is pretty hard but I am so glad that she was my professor. She was always willing to help you out and her lectures made the topics easier to learn. Great professor!!!

Dr. Barnard is very kind, and truly cares about a student's wellbeing outside of class. Her classes are very lecture centered and activity centered during lab days. She makes it very clear what is expected of the students and makes it very possible to get a good grade in the class, she is just very picky about tiny details on things like lab report
DO NOT take her. She does not respond to emails and she is very passive aggressive. She sneak disses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She was really nice but for me it was confusing what she wanted us to do for major projects, when she first sends instructions it isn't very clear and when I sent my final project she told me that two things were wrong and I couldn't even find the rubric at first due to the canvas being unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanford is absolutely hilarious. She is one of those professors that is really easy to engage with during class. If you are not a huge fan of reading, I would recommend staying away from her class as it is very reading heavy. She does do random quizzes based on the readings but they are easy. If you show up and engage, her class isn't difficult

She's a super nice and understanding professor. But, if you do not like reading, stay away. We read five chapter books in the semester, plus short stories, and the class is basically a book club. So, if you are into that, take the class! If not, don't do it. Personally, I had fun with it, but I know it's not for everybody.

She's honestly really nice and funny but if you're not obsessed with reading don't take her. Attendance is mandatory and she spends the whole class talking about the reading you had to do outside of class and the reading load is A LOT. Overall she's a good teacher but the amount of reading makes it a really difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanford is incredible; her classes feel like a book club, full of engaging discussions. She gives very engaging and funny lectures, but most of the time the classes are purely discussion-based. I took both ENGL 20643 and ENGL 20803, and they were both amazing. Be prepared for a lot of reading. Definitely take her—you won't regret it!

Dr. Sanford was really good. She's not a harsh grader and is much more lenient than other profs about assignments being on time. She's incredibly understanding, and her classes are pretty funny. I would recommend her class for an easy grade + a fun class where your writing does actually improve.

I am so confused why this awful person and awful professor has a good rating. A rating above one star would actually surprise me. I cannot say enough bad things about her, but unfortunately can't use profanity or say she has favorites otherwise I would touch more on that. She gives many time consuming assignments just to fail them. Don't take her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I really like Mrs. Sanford. I took her Intro to Lit (Vampire Fiction) class. The class is not hard as long as you do the work. There are reading assignments in every class that are either a short story or around 50 pages of a book. You can get away without reading, but there is a large paper at the end based on a book. Overall easy if you try.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: I love Susannah. I am taking her for the second time, and she is one of my favorite professors and is so cheery, intelligent (SO intelligent), and I genuinely enjoy going to her class and her sense of humor. Just engage and the class is a lot easier. Lots of reading but if you decide to not be lazy you'll keep up.

She is a very nice teacher who is a great choice for Comp 2. There are multiple books to read, but she goes over the material and makes them easy to understand. She gives great feedback and help with ideas on the essays. She is really nice and great teacher.

I enjoyed Professor Sanford so much. She makes class so enjoyable and wants to get to know her students. She wants to build a relationship with the class to make everyone feel comfortable with sharing and class discussions. Attendance does matter because you can earn easy extra credit points for being in class. Three big projects but all different.

She is a pretty easygoing professor. Discussions take up most of class but you don't have to participate. If you have a lot of talkers in the class it is pretty enjoyable. Sometimes there will be a pop quiz...2 per book so you can sometimes guess when they will be. Very straightforward. Takes a long time to put in grades.
Super funny and entertaining. 10 Reading responses and 3 projects. Some pop quizzes but not too bad. She kept class interesting and I would definitely take her if you need this credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Shes super funny and nice and I would say her English class is pretty easy! There is a lot of discussion but you don't have to participate. There is a reading before each class, 10 reading responses, 3 projects, and a final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Comp 2 English class is all based on Pride and Prejudice. We are reading the book, watching the movie, and then reading different versions and watching different movies. Super nice and has a sense of humor. Write a personal letter, research paper, and 10 reading responses. Good class for comp 2 and its interesting since based on P&P
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
RELI 10043 
Dr. McDonald is the most chill professor. He cares about his students and is passionate about their understanding of the material. There are weekly quizzes in the class based on the daily homework readings, though the homework isn't graded. I ended up P/NC the class, but if you need a religion credit, Dr. McDonald is the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McDonald was a very caring and personable teacher. You can tell he genuinely wants to teach the class and for them to do well. Very accessible and will help you with your needs. I had to reschedule my midterm and he was so understanding about it. Genuinely values your opinions and feedback during class.

Homework readings every day, not graded but the material is on a 10 question multiple choice quiz every Friday. Super easy if you actually do the readings. Tons of extra credit opportunities. McDonald is a cool guy, his lectures can be a little boring but compared to what I've heard about TCU religion classes, this is one of the easiest ones.

Professor McDonald is such a great professor! His religion class definitely included frequent reading but it wasn't bad as long as you stayed on top of the reading. You can tell he is passionate about what he teaches so lectures are interesting and he's pretty chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: It is very clear that over his time of teaching, he is still interested and cares about what he teaches. He is a very kind and understanding professor who cares for his students. He is easy to reach over email and gives great feedback on work. Weekly quizzes are not bad if you pay attention. For a religion credit I definitely recommend him!!

Dr. McDonald was a very nice and respectful teacher. He truly cares for his students and he is passionate about religion. His class leaned towards the boring side. There are weekly quizzes and make sure you read. The course work is also very boring. But overall Dr. McDonald is a great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: There are a lot of complaints about religion classes being hard but this class was fairly easy. Read the section of the book that's on the syllabus and Bible verses before class to get a better understanding of the lecture. There is a quiz every week fairly easy if you pay attention with 3 exams. There are 2 minor reflections and 1 essay.

I love Professor McDonald! Yes, his class is a bit challenging but if you do the reading and pay attention in class, you should do well. He cares so much for his students and WANTS you to succeed! If you need help with anything in his class, he is more than willing to help you and reason with you. I recommend this class :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McDonald is a very respectful and caring professor. He is more old school when it comes to technology but he is willing to grow to help accommodate students as best as possible. If you take his class and you are struggling, email him! He is willing to help in any way and is super kind and helpful when it comes to everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr. McDonald for Hebrew and it was a great experience. As long as you pay attention and read the textbook before quizzes you will do well. He is very willing to help outside of class and really cares about your education. I highly recommend taking his class because youll learn a lot and enjoy doing it.
One of my favorite professors. Do the readings, follow the reading guides, ask questions. His lectures are enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Overall pretty good teacher, very knowledgable and he gives feedback on every test and quizzes. Quizzes every week but as long as you pay attention in class they aren't bad. Also had a few minor papers but nothing super time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She was a fantastic and caring professor. She really wants you to succeed, and all you need to do is read and do the practice quizzes to do well on tests!

She is actually a very caring and thoughtful professor that does want you to succeed. If you give this class at least a little bit of your attention you will be fine. She goes over the test questions the class before to get you prepared and lets you have a cheat sheet. As long as you show up every once a while and do your work, you will do well.

Everyone is overreacting. Her tests are difficult but just study and you'll be fine. She is a nice professor who seems mostly informed on the subject matter. Her lectures are hard to sit through but not brutal. If you need to take comm theory, which is already a hard class, you'll be fine with Schroeder. You just might not enjoy this class much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were limited in material, it was hard to receive feedback on assignments (speeches were not graded till last week of the semester) we did not know how we did to improve. Only two exams, the mid term and the final, for chapter quizzes we could not retake them, you had to take the grade you were given on first try. Overall, a nice person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Schroeder is a great person but ultimately not a strong professor. Her tests are wordy and hard to understand. You can attend every class lecture and still make a C. Her lectures are very unorganized leaving students without a clear understanding of the subjects.

Schroeder is a very slow grader, and her exams are tougher than most, but she curves generously which is great. DO NOT expect an easy A, but it can be done. She is willing to work with you to schedule a meeting outside of class. She's an amazing person, and cares genuinely about her students. Weigh the pros/cons on whether or not to take her.

Do not take Dr. Schroeder. Don't get me wrong, she is a super nice lady, but her class is incredibly disorganized. There are no study guides, it's a lecture heavy class. You won't know what to expect on the exams. The exams are 3 essay questions and the questions are overtly loaded and detail-oriented.

1. Slowest grader, you won't know your grade even 2 months into the semester
2. Mainly just rambles
3. Impossible exams no matter how much you read
4. When she does grade, she is incredibly tough
5. Good luck getting ahold of her outside of class


She's a SUPER sweet human, just too busy to be a good/intentional professor.

Professor Schroeder is nearly impossible to reach outside of class. She often never responds to emails, and you have to ask in class. She also is an extremely tough grader for no reason. She verbatim told us that it is "nearly impossible to get full points." I'm a straight A student who did all of the work, and her tests dropped me to my first B.

Do not take this course. I thought it wouldn't be as bad of a class considering she is the Chair of Comm Studies but it was horrible. The class itself isn't that hard but she makes it as hard as it can be. Avoid at all costs.

Probs one of the worst communication teachers I've had at TCU. She is super nice, but her teach style is really bad. She gets very side tracked and off topic during class to where its hard to realize what we are actually talking about in class.

I took her for conflict, and it was definitely harder than I anticipated. If you want an A in the class, you need to read the book; her power points only give you a fraction of what is going to be on the exam. You write two big papers during the course, both of which she grades pretty easily. She wants you to succeed and is willing to help

I don't even know where to begin.. her class was a joke! Her tests combined lecture and readings from the book that you HAVE TO DO or you'll fail the tests completely. Her powerpoints were not at all helpful. The speeches are graded ridiculously tough and will destroy your self esteem. There is a CUMULATIVE FINAL.. do NOT take her if you want an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Such a nice teacher! Power and influence was kind of hard, but she keeps it interesting and is very willing to help. Tests are pretty hard, even with a ton of studying I made C's. There is a research paper due at the end of the semester though that can help raise your grade. I highly recommend Schroeder!

I took Deception and it's pretty advanced. Expect a lot of reading and be prepared to learn on your own. You MUST read each book thoroughly in order to be successful in this class, but an A is not unattainable. Dr. Schroeder is VERY willing to help you if you ask. It's worth the intensity, she's one of the best professors in the department!

Dr. Meyn is one of my favorite professors in the SOM. He is very good at clearly explaining basic theory, and pretty much everyone that does the homework gets a good grade. There's daily homework, but that is standard in every theory class here. Overall though, a great teacher and a lovely person.

I want to start out by saying that Dr. Meyn is a lovely person. However, he is not a good teacher. His ear training class is excessively hard, and the sight readings he expects you to just know are simply ridiculous. He pretends to care for his students, but every time my classmates have asked for help they have felt unwelcome by him.

Dr. Meyn is a genius, and a really nice guy. But some of the stuff we get as homework is flat out ridiculous. The last transcription nearly killed me. He doesn't grade tough on his homework but does on the tests... How am I supposed to know I was messing up. Also if you're an instrumentalist, get ready to sing, a lot.

Dr. Meyn's class is a great time. He covers a good amount of material within the class period, but still manages to keep it relaxed and fun. Homework will be assigned after every class (but it isn't too difficult). Don't slack on the homework because it'll affect your final grade more than you may realize. Super sweet man!!

Dr. Meyn is one of the nicest professors on campus. The course is tough if you aren't a vocalist. The problem is that it's expected that everyone has been trained to know ear training before starting the course. Hands down the hardest class I took this semester. Tests are graded hard and sight singing is challenging. Very willing to work with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Overall this guy's personality is charismatic and optimistic for 8:00 in the morning. My flaws, however, begin with his ability to teach ear training. He goes in with the expectation that everyone is a vocalist and has been singing their entire life. The vocalists will succeed in this class but if you are an instrumentalist, you won't do well.

Dr. Meyn is an amazing theory professor. Hilarious guy who makes theory enjoyable and easy. Even those who are less knowledgeable in theory from the start do extremely well as he is great at explaining the topic. He is very clear about what the tests will contain.

I LOVE TILL. :) Theory 1 wasn't super challenging for me because I took AP Theory in HS. That being said, he is an excellent teacher whom is also super funny and entertaining. He is very clear on what is expected and provides plenty of practice in class. Homework usually takes about 20 minutes, 30-45 at most. Tests are very doable and clear.
Great teacher!
he should not teach in a university

I had him for 4 semesters of theory and he was wonderful. In counterpoint though, he shows his bad side...he blatantly doesn't care about the class and hardly grades homework, so i never have any idea how I'm doing in the class until an exam comes along and kicks my ass. He also grades exams way harder than homework...so there's that.

Hilarious teacher and great class. Pretty regular homework assignments, but they aren't TOO long. The worst is the composition assignment, but I got an A- on it although I can't compose to save my life. Definitely recommend him though. Great teacher and a really cool guy.

I did not like getting A's homework and then all of a sudden not doing so hot on tests when I gave the same sort of answers. That tells me that he does not actually grade homework which is rediculous because the work load is insane. You might really try hard on long assignments but end up sunk because he won't give you feedback until its too late.

Dr. Meyn is awesome and so friendly! I was worried going in to the class because a lot of older students told me he was rather tough, but after taking his class I completely disagree! There is a worksheet due for each class, but they aren't difficult or time consuming at all. Overall, Dr. Meyn obviously LOVES music and loves teaching theory.

Meyn is a goofy guy, and loves music. He cares about what he teaches, and he tries to make his students care. He wants you to understand, and encourages questions and practice. Homework for every class, but if you pay attention it's way easy. Definitely take him, you'll love it!

Great guy and wonderful professor.  He knows his stuff and really loves what he does.  Gives his students alot of homework, but he has toned it down alot from when he first got here.  I would recommend him!
Professor Stanley is a great teacher, but the class is quite difficult. He really cares about his students and gets you ready for the workplace. He's very accessible and knowledgeable.

Truly one of the best professors I have had so far. He truly cares about his students understanding the topics and wants you to succeed. The class is just a hard class but he teaches the material very well and applies it to real world application. TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN!!

This is just a tough class, but Mr. Stanley is one of the best professors I have had at TCU. He is so passionate about the subject and if you show interest he will help you. Class is 4 homework sets you do with a group, 3 exams, and then a case study project. Hard, but he teaches so well. Would absolutely recommend.

Best professor I've had at TCU. Super passionate about what he's teaching and cares about his students. If you show up to class and listen you will succeed. Most of your grade is made up of 3 tests and a project but the tests are very manageable and if you don't get the grade you want he works with you.
Great teacher for stats.

Dr. Meitl is fabulous and I recommend taking her for crim law. She explains difficult concepts well, and will guide you through any questions you have have questions on as much as you need. Her course is not easy, but if you show up to class and pay attention you will do well.

Dr. Meitl = 10/10
Love love love her I wish she taught every class.
100% take her criminal law for CRJU Req.
I love her. That's all I have to say. Take her class.

Loved her class. Quizzes open-note, online at home, and no class that day. Two papers. But she prepares you for everything that you need. In class assignments, so go to class. Just be present and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Love love love her. A genuine professor who cares about her students. Will always be glad to talk to you in or out of class. Clear syllabus and interesting lectures. I wish she taught every CRJU class. I would take them all with her.

Mock Trial Class: Fun, engaging, relaxed. If you are considering law or have an interesting in mock trial this is a MUST. Fair amount of work in the front half of the semester, however it all builds up to doing mock trial with teams. Some weekly quizzes, otherwise just assignments.

Dr. Meitl is an awesome professor. Her lectures are great and she plays videos and movies that relate to class which are super interesting. Mostly graded off of papers and a few in class assignments. Attendance not mandatory but if you go to class and put in work you will do well.

I learned a lot about criminal law during my time in Mrs. Meitl's course. I never really formed a relationship with her, and that is partially my fault, but I know she is very accessible if needed. Grades are based off several quizzes, in-class assignments, and two papers. I would be interested in taking a course with her again

I had the worst semester by far in regard to things going on in my personal life so I really slacked and turned everything in late. She was super understanding, patient, and graded me more than fairly for the quality of work I was turning in. Not my proudest moments but she is such a great professor and I couldnt have been more thankful for her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Meitl is so kind and accommodating and was especially helpful to me because it felt like she genuinely cared to help us with whatever life threw at us.
I liked this summer class. Works with you when you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She likes teaching about the law you can tell. In class assignments that are not announced. I would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Con law with her was difficult. Her quizzes had trick questions, her lectures were not thorough enough to understand material in the fullest. She goes fast in lecture, slides are not detailed. You learn a lot by reading the book, but you have to put a lot of work in. Attending lectures and writing what she says is very important. 94 is an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teacher. I would take her class again.

Dr. Meitl is one of the nicest CJ professors at TCU. She genuinely cares about all of her students and gives informative lectures. She loves having students join her for office hours and gives great feedback on papers.
Great summer class.
Challenging course but doable. Prof Meitl is available outside of class and encouraged us. Make sure to read.

2 tests and a paper are all of the grades and she hardly even teaches the information. I was not prepared for anything. Would recommend a teacher that is more interesting and actually teachers in lecture. We watched like 5 movies.

Dr. Meitl is one of my favorite professors ive had so far. she is very sweet and really wants everyone to succeed. Her style of teaching involves asking the class questions which i like because it helps you know if you are on track. She is also very accessible and willing to work with you if there is something you dont understand.

A wonderful lady and professor. Is very knowledgable because she is a lawyer, but then can sometimes be confusing when trying to explain concepts. But, overall great and super accessible outside of class!
Mrs. Meitl is incredibly nice and grades very fairly. I will def take her for any class I can!

Dr. Rahdar clearly cares and he wants to help people do better in his class. It's not a class that's going to kill you work-wise, and he does let you have some notes with you for exams. That said, the presentations are a disaster because he doesn't know what he's looking for and the grade you get in the class is way too dependent on other people.

great teacher, really caring for students. attendance is not mandatory but a lot of the class still goes anyways. you have to do a supply chain simulation in a group the whole semester which is great if you have a good group but sucks if they dont care. tests have 2 pages front and back of open notes but are still challenging so be prepared

LOVE HIM and one of my favorite professors at TCU. So kind and funny and cares a lot about his students and helping them do well. Offered extra credit in my class and helped so much when I went to office hours for the simulation, that it ended up helping me do really well on the final simulation exam. 100% take him for supply chain he made it fun!

The sweetest guy in the world. Lectures were boring and the simulation was difficult but he will always give help if you go to his office hours. Get 3 pages front and back for exams which makes them super easy. Presentations also have clear grading criteria. If you have a group that is willing to go the extra mile and ask for help, you will succeed

He's so sweet and funny. His lectures can be a little boring sometimes, but he's a really good guy. If you're struggling with the simulation go to office hours and he will really help you it makes a huge difference. One of my favorite professors at TCU!

This was Rahdar's first semester at TCU. He is pretty quirky but so nice and he genuinely cares about you and your success in the class. The tests are not too bad & most of your work is rooted in the simulation. Also fret not, he does not randomly call on anyone. I was scared for supply chain but this class turned out better than expected

I sobbed after my first lab with Dr.Montchamp because him and a TA gaslit me and going into lab felt like war. In Orgo, you want a professor that is accessible and wants to help you, yet when I went to office hours he told me he's is not going to answer anymore of my questions...mind you it's his job. Not worth the irritation and sleepless nights.

Lectures are snooze fests. I was in the first lab section, and his instructions/procedures were very unclear until he fixed them AFTER our section. He was very condescending when we messed up, too. Lab reports graded DIFFERENTLY every time. His quizzes were super random and I felt as if there was no way to study for them. Same with the final exam

In a class as difficult as OChem, you want a professor that you feel comfortable with to ask for help/guide you. Montchamp is not this. Very intimidating and when you're told concepts "should be obvious" in lec, makes you feel dumb. Unless you can follow fast lectures + diagrams, and have time for lots of studying out of class, would not recommend.

To succeed, always be on top of your game. Study the content in class as soon as possible. Make sure you're comfortable with the new information. Go to office hours to clarify whatever parts you're not certain about. Study, and then ask questions that show you've studied the material, because this professor really doesn't like dumb questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Scary and not open to questions during labs. He expects everyone to know the lab perfectly before coming and will scream at you if you make a little mistake.

Dr. Montchamp teaches one tough Organic Chemistry I course. He uses the chance of pop quizzes to keep you studying the content everyday, which is required to do well in this course. His handouts are very useful and compliment his lecture content. Once all is said and done Dr. Montchamp is a super nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very condescending. Probably the worst professor at TCU.

STAY AWAT FROM THIS PROFESSOR!! (from someone with As in Ochem 1&2 at TCU) Either wait a whole year to take OCHEM with minter or dzyuba (but youll still have montchamp for some lab or lecture) with TCUs strange ochem rotation. or take it at another school (best option). This man without fairness will ruin your transcript you worked so hard for.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I hated O. Chem. a lot, but that wasn't the professor's fault. Montchamp comes off really scary and intimidating at first, but he really does want you to succeed. If you go to office hours, he will take the time to explain everything to you from lecture and really help you figure out the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very dry lectures and never seemed approachable for any questions because always answered rudely. Never seemed like his best interest was of the students and when quiz averages were low blamed it on the lack of effort of the students rather than his poor teaching. Good luck.

The final for 2nd semester was literally the hardest test I've taken in my life, but in the end he gave most of the class an A or a B! The first 2 exams and quizzes are mostly from old exams/quizzes. He actually does care about students even though he has a funny way of showing it at times (can be rude and impatient) but he's funny and so smart.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. M is an amazing professor. He is very accessible and responsive on the discussion board. He can come off strong, but if you take the time to understand, and you admire how amazing organic chemistry really is, then you will have a great semester. The codes are just for own privacy when we pick up quizzes. He is so supportive! Best professor!!

Montchamp is one of the worst professors at TCU. Not friendly at all and makes students feel like they are not welcome to speak with him. In OChem 2 we arer required to put a specific number ID on each assignment, and he takes points off(up to 25% of the total grade) for merely just writing your name on the paper. Wouldn't reccomend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's a nice person if you prove yourself hard enough that you are a good student. He loves it when you have difficulties and try figuring it out on your own before having him answer the problems. The lab is always hard, but he makes it seem easy because he is very responsive on the Discussion Board and he seems to care about your study outcome.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Montchamp is awful. I had him for ochem lab this past semester. He was always dry and boring during the lectures and extremely rude during the lab. He often yells at people over very minor things and is never helpful in answering questions. You don't really have a choice on whether or not he is your prof, but... fair warning.

Dr. Montchamp is a great professor. I had him for Organic Qualitative Analysis, which is a tough lab in itself. Dr. M was super helpful when I went to office hours to ask for help and really wants to see his students succeed. He is a super fast grader and typically was easy going as long as you followed the lab report format.

He may seem hard and intimidating, but talking to him will really improve ur understanding. Unlike other professors he wants you to learn. Once you learn how to do the reports everything gets easier, tough the final is very hard (and some very detailed questions can show up). However, if you understand (not just memorize) u can definitely do well.

Organic lab is hard, but fun and the best class to prepare for med school, by far. Dr. M is the best teacher to take it from because he's the only one in the department that keeps you updated about your grades the whole semester. He is very generous grade wise and promptly returns your grades and quickly answers questions on the discussion board.

People are too quick to judge Dr. M based on what prior students have told them. Conversely, Dr. M taught me how to think and how to learn. He is incredibly helpful and highly knowledgeable. If you show you care he will do anything to help you. Obviously, organic is very tough but Dr. M will return your effort with fast and very generous grading.

Dr. M is an excellent professor.  He is always willing to help his students and office hours are flexible.  Not only is he willing to talk about hw, but he also gives helpful real-world advice.  He really does care about his students.  All he wants is a little effort.  If a student puts forth that effort, then he/she will get the grade they want.

Dr. M is a great teacher and a great help if you utilize him.  He is always willing to help you if you have problems and is very dedicated to his dedicated students.  All you have to do is stay on top of things and ask for help when you need it.  Anyone who bags on Dr. M didn't put enough effort into the course and is simply angry at the subject
He is a very helpful and understanding (outside class). The only problem with him is that he jumps around topic and so very hard to follow. His exams and quizes are extremely hard.

Dr. M is a great professor. He cares about his students and has the best intentions for his class. The material is difficult by nature and he does a great job helping you understand it. The class is curved, he has a fair distribution of grades, and you almost always know where you stand in the class. INCREDIBLY FAST GRADING- never seen it this fast

It's a hard class, but it's organic chem, what do you expect?  Dr. M can be a little condescending sometimes if you ask a question that he has already answered, but he does a good job at getting the material across.  Anyone complaining didn’t put forth enough effort.

Dr. Montchamp is a great big softy once you get to know him.  He's also hilarious if you appreciate his kind of humor. In my opinion, the tests and quizzes are easy.  It's just a matter of whether you studied or not.  If you slack off, the pop quizzes will start to hurt.

He jumps around a lot, even though he seems like a jerk he is pretty nice if you go talk to him.  He is very sarcastic but quite funny at times.  Quizzes are not so bad if you study some.   he sends lots of useful stuff in email

Dr. Montchamp's class may seem hard, but is is  worth it. He is very dedicated to his students-even when he gets mad around finals time. I graduated in 2002 and am currently in a Kaplan course. I am, without a doubt, the most stellar organic student in class! I have even corrected the teachers.

Organic lab is going to be difficult to begin with. However, Dr. Montchamp is very helpful which makes the class more interesting and bearable. He gives the students fair warning many times and ample material for the student to be prepared. He is a great teacher who does all he can for the students.

I have never met a professor more dedicated to his students. Who else would stay up til 2 am to answer our questions on the Discussion Board? He even helped out in O. Lab 1, not even his class. He is bluntly honest but you've got to respect that. He really does have a big heart.

Dr. Montchamp is one of those professors who appreciates students who work hard and are willing to learn and is VERY intolerant of students who do not work hard and do not want to learn. The trick is being one of those students that wants to learn! :)

Dr. Montchamp may come off gruff and uncaring, but he truly wants his students to do well. He is always available to talk with students and try to lead them in the right direction. He puts in a great deal of time outlining procedures and reactions and is always present in the lab to offer assistance

Dr. Montchamp cares about his students' learning experience very much. He was willing to stay past his office hours to help answering my numerous questions about a particular lab. He has not ignored any of my emails. I have to say that he's a very honest person, & some may like that, others may not.

Dr. Montchamp is BY FAR the best professor at TCU. If you put effort forth, he will double it.  No matter what sequence of the organic courses your taking, he always helps and even gives advice on career and life questions. He truly believes that every student is intelligent and can earn an A.

Dr. M was extremely willing to help students, whether in his office or via the online discussion board, which he responded to frequently and at all hours.  The class is difficult by nature, so that should not be held against him. His grading was very fair.

The most helpful O Chem prof we have. He's always trying to make sure that the class "gets it". O Chem isn't super easy, but Dr. M definatley makes content & expectations clear. Try hard, study and you can def. get an A.

Dr. Montchamp made organic (get this) fun!  I was always told you would die in this class; however, I will always tell everyone that my second semester lab for organic was the best.  Dr. Montchamp was always helpful when I needed it and always had (and still does have) time to just chat.  Thank you!
Very sarcastic so don't be offended.  Pay attention in class and you will do fine.  It isn't as hard as it sounds.

Regardless, organic is going to be a challenging course.  Dr. Montchamp does a good job of emphasizing what's important to learn.  He is always responsive when answering questions and clarifying concepts.  Some sarcasm, but it is with the intention of building a repoire with the students.
He can be a really nice guy.  If his comments seem harsh sometimes, don't take it too seriously.  He knows his stuff -- get his help when you need it.
Has a gigantic temper.  Be prepared to be belittled.  I think it is a French thing.
Dr. Montchamp can be your best friend or your worst enemy.  Do your work and plan ahead to get an A.  Definitely a rough course though.
She is one of the nicest professor I have ever had. She is caring and dedicated. Study the slides and pay some attention, you can get an A

She is very flexible, which is great especially during a COVID pandemic. She's really into social work and you can tell she cares about the people she works with. Be ready to talk about homelessness and aging. If you do your best, she'll do whatever she can to help you. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly, really easy A. It is all really interesting to learn about, but the class is graded by one presentation, one paper, and a few tests, which you'll need to pay attention for.

Professor Murray is a great guy, kind and welcoming to everyone, but he is just not a good teacher. His grading requirements are vague and hard to understand. You can edit many times, but you won't always have time. It's an easy class, but extremely frustrating. He doesn't teach; he has students read and then present content themselves.

Easily one of my least professors at the school. Extremely rude and condescending when looking at work, and is vague in what he look for in an assignment. Do not take him if you want to maintain a piece of your sanity.

Professor Murray is one of the best and nicest professors at TCU. He lets you revise every essay as many times as you would like until the end of the semester and gives good feedback on every essay. If you do the revisions, it should be easy to get a good grade in this class.

Joddy is a nice guy but he's extremely condescending, tough grader, and very unclear. You do nothing in class except threaded discussions and "discussing readings". He gives you super harsh criticism on your papers that would have helped you write it if he had told you beforehand and the prompts make no sense. Papers are very long and take forever.

DO NOT TAKE HIM. He is an incredibly picky grader, essay prompts are not clear at all, it feels like not even he knows what he is asking for. You have to write perfect essays to get a grade higher than a B+ on them. The final is preparing a TED Talk to present to the class. You do not have to go to class, and he is nice, but still, TOUGH GRADER.
He criticizes your paper, but not in a helpful way. He believes he knows it all.

Joddy is definitely a great professor. If you're a sub-par writer going in, you might have a hard time, but if you've got a good hangle on the english language it should be a fairly easy A. Book readings are assigned for each class, but there isn't any penalty for not reading. You will be required to submit your work to the class for peer review.
Loved this class, really great guy.  Just let him know you want to do well and he will help you! Take HIS CLASS for all your English requirements!

This class is an analysis of new media class disguised as an English class! A knowledge of new media software such as photo editing is pretty much required. Also, you have to know how to make fun of something. The textbooks must be read, although you don't have to go to every class. Dr. Murray is okay, although he gets pickier when grading.

Seems like a nice person, but HORRIBLE professor. Barely lets her students view old tests to study. Will not give you a review at all for her exams. Weekly quizzes over information that hasnt been taught yet. Definitely the most boring 3 hour class Ive taken. Good thing it was online. Stay away if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: VERY unclear of whats on exams, weekly quiz over untaught material (weird time frame, available midnight and due 2 hours before class), 3 hour unengaging lecture. Gave extra credit which was nice cus class had 74 test average. Cumulative final and can only see what you got wrong on past tests for 1 hour period. Shes nice but wack class set up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: you have quizzes each week before she even goes over the material, so you better pay close attention to the reading. hard to focus in class since you have already been quizzed on the material. she seems like a nice person, but just can't teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The literal best professor I have and will ever take. He is so genuine and cares way more about you as a person than as a student, in a good way. I had him first semester last year, and I still see and talk to him regularly. Wants to know about your life and story and help you succeed.

Dr. Musoma is truly one of the most genuine and caring people that I have ever met. He lectures daily about taking care of yourself above anything else. Someone who clearly loves his job and has shifted how I view thinking. If you have the chance, please take one of his classes. It's been one of the greatest experiences that I have ever had.
By far the best professor I have had at TCU. I 100% would recommend taking his class.

I had Professor Musoma during the switch to online classes. He was not a great transfer to online but I really enjoyed going to his class. He was super friendly and supportive and connected concepts to bigger pictures. He fell short with communication during online classes and didnt grade everything but who knows what he could have had going on.

I don't mean to brag, but to gain credibility; I have received straight A's since sixth grade, and I believe this class is unorganized. He says his examples are not A's, his instructions and feedback are unclear, and it takes weeks for grades to be returned. I kept making recurring mistakes because of the late feedback. I found it extremely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Musoma is likely one of the most interesting people I've met in my life. He has a way of speaking to his students that is unmatched by any prof at TCU. Like everyone else says, his grading is on the tougher side, but it's certainly manageable. Incredible person and mentor.

Great professor. He has a great story and doesn't really lecture. You show up to class and it is a conversation. He begins telling stories and then relates it to business in society. No midterm test or final--just papers. A decent amount of work but he is by far the best business in society professor. Go to breakfast with him!
LOVE HIM!!! Best professor ever! He teaches life lessons and really cares about his students. You will have to work in this class, but he makes it worth it.

Dr. Musoma is probably the best professor I've ever had. As long as you put in some honest effort into your work, you should have no problem getting an A. He is a great speaker and encourages productive conversation. His lectures may not always seem relevant, but seeing how business involves building relationships, they are very useful.

Dr. Musoma is a great professor. His liberal views on politics are strong but he encourages and respects alternative points of view. He has a genuine care for his students and possesses an uncanny ability to bring people together through honesty and respect. Any student that misses his class is missing a unique and deep learning experience.

He is literally the FUNNIEST TEACHER IN THE WORLD. If you want roll on the floor in laughter every class then take him. He tells so many stories that are not always business-related but are so interesting nontheless. He made my latest class my favorite by far!

Out of all of the BUSI professors, I would take Musoma again. He has high expectations for grading but they aren't unattainable. He wants you to show you know the material and that you're thinking outside the box. Every section of the class has a lot of work, but he just cares that you put effort into it. He cares about his students!

Dr. Munson is very knowledgeable and kind, but her Intro to Art History class is crazy hard. She is willing to work with you if you reach out to her and ask questions in class, but do not assume her class is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Munson will take your lack of knowledge in art and make you an avid museum goer by the end of the semester. She's extremely nice, knowledgeable, and a great teacher.
