funny funny prof lectures always entertaining this was my secnd class with dr t and i think i liked it more than theory and i loved theory no doubt the short papers were actually fun she makes the topics apply to stuff happening in life and society i got skills to understand conflict and weirdos one of the most useful classes at tcu

Animals and Society class   was way better than I thought it would b. There is a zoo project where you watch the people at the zoo. a reversal it is cool makes you think and see the world different. films and assignments were great. Super nice prof not too hard if u just go to class and keep up. lectures are high energy keeps your attention.
Took a class of us to London in the summer--that class changed my life--she gave us leadership lessons you can never learn in a classroom.

She is so knowledgble & very fun & energetic- you won't fall asleep. It may be difficult to comprehend, but is always available in person or by email if you have questions. You must take her before you graduate! You will certainly learn alot!

Fantastic woman. She knows so much about sociology but sometimes she gets so excited about it that she gets off on tangents and it may be hard to follow. She really cares about the success of her students at any rate. Take her class. You'll learn a lot if you apply yourself.
Carol Thompson changed my life. Shes the most passionate professor I have ever had. She makes it easy to come to class, THIS CLASS MAKES YOU THINK.

Dr. Thompson is an unbelievable woman and professor.  Her intelligence, compassion, and commitment to students is practically unmatched at TCU.  Enrolling in one of courses will prove to be an edifying college experience - this is what we came here for people.  Read the textbook carefully and pay attention to due dates.

wow, im liberal, but unless you like having liberal ideology crammed forcefully down your throat dont take this course.  Shes very unorganized and the class is pretty boring.  she is a cool person, however.

Do not graduate without taking this professor!  Must read what she assigns or you will be lost for the tests.  Papers are fairly easy.  She is crazy and so much fun.  I also previously had her for Sociological Theory.  Both were hard classes, but easy Bs.  A must take teacher!!

Dr. Thompson is the craziest prof. ever. INSANE. Loved every second of the class. Not too difficult just go to class and read some of the readings. Papers aren't too bad either. Tests are written, so you have to know the theories. Wouldn't suggest taking this class if you're not a soc. major or minor, you'll be lost
No Comments
She was amazing!!!

I had her for Psych of Crime, too. Both classes were challenging- you'll work for your A. However, if you graduate without taking her, you will be missing out for sure. She is a definite asset to TCU and humanity. It's difficult to make the world a better place. She does. Open your mind while having fun- take a class with Carol Thompson.

This prof is the best TCU has to offer. Wonderful, talented, opinionated and vocal. She'll challenge you mentally both in class and beliefs.  Very enthusiastic about her work; intellegent lectures that bring dead theorist to life.  Worth the work, will work with you, open to a lot of ideas. Great.

She really loves what she teaches and makes these dead sociologists fun! She will work with you and is there to talk after class. Class is not hard, just read. She explains everything very well. Take at least one class from her, she is such a fun person!
The best Profesor at TCU. Class is tough if you don't remember psychology, a lot of info.  Her lecutres are the best, willing to work with you.

She is so fun and makes the class fun and interesting.  however, she is very tough - she grades hard but fair.  there is ALOT of writing, it should be a writing emphasis class - stressful and very hard class but she is a great prof

Theory can be brutal, but she makes you care about insane dead guys.  Very funny & can get a bit off track, but it's a blast.  You do have to read quite a bit & the tests can be grueling (essay), but just keep up.  She'll tell ya how it is!
She's a kind, caring individual who is always willing to help you. Expect to work in her class though. 5 Stars! TCU should give her a raise imo.

I took ideas of Leadership, a mix of Philosophy and Sociology. If you'd like to get a highly liberal worldview, this class offers a different perspective. Prof. Thompson is intense and fun.  Ask about irritable bowel.

hardest class in college. I love her anti humanistic nature-and maybe trees need hugs too!if you are smart and open minded Take a class w this woman. though the course was hard, iliked it ALOT. silly republicans(;
This class is hard only because there are quizzes over 5 chapters of the book and are very picky - class is really interesting though! The tests and quizzes are just tricky!
republicans beware! this chick is a freak! stay away! will try to brainwash you with her eco/tree-hugger attitude!

Amazing woman. Intelligent and hilarious in class. Very personable and easy to get to know outside of class. The work is tough, but it's definitely worth it. You are never bored because she does a great job of mixing outside elements into her lectures
You have to work in this class, but Dr. Thompson is an amazing teacher, and she is also entertaining.  I always have fun in her class but still feel that I have learned alot.

She is an amazing woman. Class is fun, but you actually have to read and study. This is not an easy A, but is definitely a worthwhile class. I would highly recommend at least taking one class from her.
Dr. Thompson has a magnetic personality and is incredibly intelligent. I learned a lot from her class.

I would avoid taking her for Communicating Effectively at all costs. Her class is overkill and so much more work than all the other ones. She does not correctly post assignment due dates, is a stickler when grading, and is very unorganizedl
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A semester-long group paper is absolutely horrific; she isn't super helpful with feedback either. Lectures are fine, and the notes pages she gives you are helpful (only if the words line up with the textbook - usually they don't). Tests aren't terrible, but the way she phrases questions can be confusing. I personally would not take this again.

She talks so unnecessarily loud—literally yelling as she speaks. You have to write three papers with a group, and it was much harder than I expected because she gives really difficult feedback. At the end of the semester, you also have to present in front of the campaign you chose. This is the one class where I've had a constant 60 all semester.

Fully textbook taught, you can tell slides are years old, and gives terrible feedback. Exam questions are way too difficult for an elective class and you will have 10-20 page essays due (all while having busy work assignments due the same week).  Just no.  I really love the content, but the class could be so much better.

for a comm elective, this course is way too complicated. wording of test questions is purposefully trying to trick the student. Extremely difficult to score above a C on exams and tests and the class itself is not interesting. Highly recommend not taking this course

Some of these reviews are harsher than they should be. Professor Mindt cares about her students and wants them to get better at public speaking. Unlike a TA, this is definitely a class that is graded a little more tough — but for the better. I still recommend it b/c it really is a skill that is critical to life, and I have seen major improvements.

reviews.comment: Communicating Effectively changed from previous semester to where the professor has to follow the departments course. reviews.comment: She is very laid back and makes a class that seems pointless actually interesting. It is very easy to get a good grade in her class. Homework doesn't take more than 30 minutes at maximum. Good GPA booster.

Dr Mindt has made this course exceptionally challenging for just about everyone enrolled; the expectations for papers and exams are downplayed by her, which results in the class doing poorly. The class is interesting, but its unfortantley taught by the textbook... not the teacher. This class would be better suited taught bt someone with enthusiasm.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mindt has a great personality and is nice. However, she makes this class more difficult than what is necessary. You will have quizzes over chapters and they are ridiculously hard and complicated. No in-between. She offers guided notes but goes over the chapter after the quiz. Take this class with a TA or another teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Mindt is awesome. She really cares about her students and her class is never boring. She can be a tough grader and the weekly quizzes are SO hard (at least for me) I always do poorly on them and they really bring my grade down.
terrible teacher... don't even try to email her. Her quizzes are very hard even if you study and she grades speeches very harshly for an intro speech class. She is awful.
Nice person, with somewhat interesting content. Very hard exams and quizzes. Tough grader when it comes to the final group project.

This course is writing intensive despite not receiving WEM credit for it. The professor is a harsh grader and struggles to articulate their expectations to students. During lectures, examples are outdated and create a disconnect between herself and students. Old powerpoints come across as her being poorly prepared and not updating her content.

Professor mindt is a super sweet person and fun to listen to. She makes her class engaging and comfortable for those who are new to and scared of public speaking. She is a hard grader tho, and the quizzes are very difficult. If you study you should be ok, but its not something you can just wing.

reviews.comment: She sucks. I fell short in her class because of a damn peer review. I am writing this to worn people not to take her because of how bad of a professor she is. I hope that people read and learn from this review. She cried on the last day of class acting like she actually cared about her students but she never even learned my name.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was very sweet and understanding. It's important to complete the powerpoints before quizzes, because that is what they are based off of. She is a relatively hard grader on speeches, but if you follow the outlines she gives and go to her for feedback then you will be fine.

The quizzes were unnecessarily difficult, weighing in as much of our grades, as it is department-wide. Prof Mindt takes the time to get to know students and genuinely has passion for what she does which makes class enjoyable.

If you would like to get an A in the class, she will make you work for it. Tests play a major factor in your grade as they weigh 50% of your average. She is a kind teacher, but a very tough grader. Personally getting a B in the class was tough, so do with that as you will.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I also want to add she does not respond to her emails. 'Communication' between professor and student is terrible.

If you don't want to destroy your gpa stay away from her. This professor absolutely sucks. The book is terrible. She is a nice person, but not a good professor. There are nine quizzes in total. There are four speeches. She makes students write a speech in the hallway under a few minutes and then present it in front of the class. Dooooo not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Communicating Effectively was a lot harder than I thought it would be. There are many notes and you are only graded on a few quizzes and 4 major speeches. It is overall a stressful class, however, professor Mindt made my experience enjoyable and manageable. This class is required for TCU but I think Mindt is one of the best professors for it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The actual material of this class is super interesting, but Mindt was not my favorite. the group project (three harshly graded essays) was awful, especially because the class was online. The tests were actually super easy, so where I suffered with the group project, I made up for with the other assignments/tests.
Her project for p&i is the worst. That alone made the class horrible
One of the best I've had at TCU. She rewards effort and provides great feedback on the papers. The class does have a large group project component but that didn't bother me at all.

Mindt's tests are extremely fair. If you study what she tells you it is very possible to get an A not them. Make sure you chose a good group at the beginning because you will write several essays with them. Take the essays very seriously and double check APA. She's tough on essays but super helpful if you send in a rough draft. Lectures are great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Mindt's class was my favorite of last year. All of her presentations are engaging and she really helps you understand the information. The group project is the hardest and is graded the hardest. However, I felt our group grade was due to our bad communication and lack of cohesive work. I wish I could take more classes from Mindt.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great class, not as great of a professor. She acts like her Power and Influence class is WEM, but it's not. Had a huge semester long group project, to which we worked very hard on, and got a C average for that grade. She grades the group papers like we are graduate students. Made A's on everything else, including tests, but still ended up with a B.

Be careful with this class. An A is doable, but don't expect an "Easy A." Mindt makes you work for it with harsh grading critiques on speeches and assignments. Exams are easy, but there's only 3. Be prepared to work in groups because you will be graded on how you and your partner(s) perform. Be specific on everything and study up!

Nice lady, tough grader. Would not recommend if you want to get an A. Requires too much hard work for a core class. Grades assignments and speeches very harshly, tests aren't that bad. Lectures are good, she's a decent speaker. Doesn't respond to emails very quickly. Will help you when necessary, but it is awkward. Overall, meh.

The information she teaches is very interesting and so applicable to daily life. Plus, she is very helpful. She was more than willing to correct our group papers for us as many times as we wanted before the due date. I think it has really helped me become a better writer. She is so upbeat and happy!
Cool teacher, likes pop culture, no plus minus, optional final, interesting class. would definitely take it
like it
nice guy but expects so much of you. wasn't too bad online but the few major assignments were a concern
He has lots of knowledge about his material. However, the lecture may seem heavy and his oral exam can be a concern. Try your best and you may succeed.
Very tough grader, his exam was hard and he does not allow mistakes so if you are not ready to do public speaking class, please do not take him at all cost. Very harsh grader and condescending.

Betts is one of the best professors I've had at TCU. He's someone who cares about his students and is very passionate about what he teaches, which shows in lectures. Oral exams were a concern, but as long as you know the information, you'll be just fine. Classes are long, but everything learned is impactful. I'd take Betts again in a heartbeat.

BY FAR the worst professor I have taken. He pushes his opinions, shuts down disagreement, and goes out of his way to make students feel small. Totally disorganized, harsh grader, no empathy. Felt like he enjoyed causing stress. Most frustrating class I've ever taken at tcu. AVOID AT ALL COSTS unless you enjoy putting yourself through misery.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst class format I've ever taken. I don't know where he get the lectures from but I was lost 90% of the time. Don't know for god's sake what he's talking about. Exams are insanely hard. Avoid at all cost.
Horrible. Avoid at all costs. Worst class experience I've had at TCU

One of the best professors to have for comm theory. His class is mostly just busy work but easy.he gives great feedback and cares about his students If you have any questions or want him to look over an assignment before you turn it. His exams can be a bit hard but nothing you need to study for.
One of the worst experiences I have ever had in a class. Hardest professor I have ever had and worst formatted class I have ever seen. Absolutely brutal grader.
Timothy is a great prof and super helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Not sure why so many people think he is a tough grader- if you follow the DETAILED instructions he provides on the syllabus, ask him for help, not use AI or do things last minute, he is really great. Timothy is usper caring and he tries to make his lectures as enjoyable for us as possible- I took him for Comm Theory & Org Comm- fav times!

We had barely any assignments, and the ones we did he graded them insanely hard. He graded and taught like we were seniors or even grad students when in fact we were freshmen or sophomores. overall this class is the WOAT. First C I have ever made. It wasn't like it was just me either I had 5 of my friends in my class and they all made C's.
Nice guy, with enjoyable lectures.  But a very very tough grader!

Timothy is absolutely great! Take him for Comm theory without a single doubt. The class is so intelligently structured with a theory days and practice days were students lead. When it is your day to lead, you'll have an essay to write later. You will lead a min of 2 and max of 3 times in the semester.  Take him! Very accessible and understanding.
Tons of reading with very hard test
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: SUCH A HARD GRADER!!! not understanding when it comes to being sick or having to miss class for any reason.

I took Prof. Betts at USF, but I'll leave a review here because he's amazing and turned my semester around! I struggled in a new city and used to have an awful job. He saw I was struggling but willing to do the work. Told me to do my best and the late turn-ins would be accepted. Kind, compassionate, and funny. He made all the difference. 11/10.
Most reliable and understanding teacher I've had at this school. He teaches his content in a fun and interesting way. Also he is very technology friendly.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He explains the concepts and techniques really well. If you put any effort into this class at all you will definitely be a better public speaker by the time you're finished. The class is pretty homework heavy but not that difficult overall.

Amazing professor, she is so sweet and truly cares about everyone. Her lectures are actulaly engaging, and if you study her exams are relatively easy. One of my favorite classes at TCU, I could not recomend enough

I could not recommend a professor more. She is extremely caring for all of her students. She gets everyone engaged with her lectures and they are super interesting. She gives out a review before each exam and it has everything you need to know.

BEST professor I've had at TCU! So smart and genuinely cares about her students. Lectures are very engaging, and she encouraged discussion. 3 exams, all very easy if you study. Don't take anyone else.

Dr Ton is THE GREATEST marketing professor I've ever taken. She cares so much about her students and is always willing to help. Her exams are multiple choice with 3 open ended questions, and are fairly easy. She geninuenly know what she's talking about, and demonstrates so much passion on her teaching. Don't take any other professor for this class.

Love her. Her tests are very straight forward if you study the review decks. She cares about her students and is the cutest teacher ever. group projects are super easy. Show up and study for the tests and you will get an A. Shes the best!!!

Dr. Ton is amazing professor!! She is very kind and you can tell she really cares about the students. The class overall is very easy and the assignments are not hard at all. She also gives out review slides for the tests and she also has a full day dedicated to prepare students for the tests. The lectures are very interesting and informative!

She is an awesome professor who cares about the success of her students. For exams, she does not try to trick you or make the exams really hard. She does reviews before the exams, and her PowerPoints for the exams have all the information on them. Participation matters in the class, and the lectures will make more sense if you participate.

She is one of the best professors at TCU. Extremely kind and tries to help and make the class as easy as possible. There are 3 group projects that she grades easily and three exams where she gives you review slides that are exactly the content that is on the exam. Definitely take her for customer insights!

I loved this professor. She is caring, kind, and truly wants the best for her students. I started the class unsure and even tried to switch, but I'm so glad I stayed. If you try and put in effort, the material isn't hard, and building a connection with her makes the class even better.

3 group projects, 2 tests. The class is a lecture with in-class activities. Very easy to follow along. She does track participation, but it's super easy to participate, and she gives a lot of opportunities. Truly wants her students to do well. Gives extra credit. If you pay somewhat attention, you will do well!!

Professor TS was my favorite professor I have ever had. She deeply cares for her students, and wants everyone to get good grades. Test can be a little lengthy, but she CURVES the heck out of them. TAKE HER SHES AWESOME!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Professor TS was by far the best professor I have had at TCU. She was so willing to help and wanted everyone in her class to succeed. She would answer late night emails before exams when I had questions and genuinely cared about how our class was feeling before the exam, or project. Her feedback was so kind, and she knew what she was teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is nice but I would NOT recommend taking her. Impossible to get an A no matter how much work you put in.

She is nice but the last two exams were randomly graded based off how she feels about you. She doesn't provide clear criteria for her open response exams and encourages bullet points but then grades extremely unfairly. Test and participation heavy course. Docs participation/ professionalism points if you use your computer for notes.
She is literally the nicest, sweetest prof ever. I love her and would definitely take her again. She really cares about her students and us having good grades. 100% take her

Do not recommend. 3 tests worth 15% of grade each with a failing average before curve. Exams confusing and more difficult than the course should require. About 500-700 pages of required reading throughout the semester. Graded projects harshly/gave very little opportunity to bring grades up. Kind woman with very little skill  in being a professor.

Ridiuolous class, don't take her for org man. There are 4 tests and 3 group projects and she grades everything ridiculously hard. The class average on the test was a 40% and even if you studied a lot it was hard. Also - an A in the class is a 95 which is impossible

The actual WORST teacher at TCU. The hardest org man teacher my far, it is nearly impossible to get an A and she is ironically the least organized teacher I have had. The average on all of the tests was an F before we forced her to curve it. If the average is an F, its the teacher not the students.
Again, DO NOT TAKE her. The needs to be fired.

Tough grader with little sympathy for students. Makes the class harder than it should be in comparison to other professors. Kind professor who cares about her students, but I would recommend most other teachers for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof T cares SO much about her students. The tests are very lengthy but she does curve them. She is VERY strict on participation and if you are clearly not paying attention/on your phone she will knock points off participation. Her class is very collaborative and fun however there's 4 tests and 3 group projects....

While tonmar's class is an easy A, it's not necessarily easy to sit and listen to everything he has to say. It is understandable that the topics discussed in this field can be controversial. However, Tonmar had some out right unacceptable comments, such as “No one works harder than the Mexicans in a field”.

This was such a great class. He stands and talks for most of it, but it is more of a flowing conversation than a lecture. He said you dont have to come if you dont want, but then your test grade is on you. The two tests we had were both take at home multiple choice (all on quizlet), and a few easy homework assignments. Would def recommend

Professor Johnson was late to class almost every day, and when other students were late, he would take them out in the hall to reprimand them for being late. He was also never at his designated office hours, never gave rubrics for assignments, and wouldn't allow you to turn in an assignment even a minute late.

Tonmar Johnson is, to this day, my best TCU professor. He is intelligent, kind, easily approachable in and out of class, teaches subjects with zero bias, and engages the class in conversations that are extremely important. Tonmar is one of the greatest out there and really truly cares about his role.

Professor Tonmar's class was not hard at all, it is an easy A. Make sure to read the textbook because, in each class session, you have to provide your own feedback, which counts as your participation grade! Exams were online and there was one group presentation. He is open-minded and very funny.

Go to class and participate.  Class and entertaining and usually the first part is discussion based.  Sometimes he acts like he knows better than everyone else, but overall is a nice, respectful guy that you will be able to learn a lot from.
Very boring

Her class is very confusing and she seems to be pretty unorganized. She explains the concept in a very convoluted way that complicates simple things. Her expectation is unclear for most assignments. Her grading isn't hard as long as you work a little bit, even just before the exam. She's not a bad person, but do not take her class.
She might

Twish is a great professor. I was actually excited to go to her class and learn every day and I took her for a 9:30 Tuesday/Thursday class. She explains everything she's looking for very clearly and if you put in the work and go to class, guaranteed A.
I took Twisha for both Intro Micro and Intro Macro and she was amazing for both courses. I love this professor. I'm actually sad that I won't have her for anymore classes.

Goes over things very fast in class but if you ask for clarification she is willing to explain topics in depth and genuinely wants you to understand the material. Multiplication practice sets are given in class, if you understand how to solve these you will have no problem on exams. No homework other than take home exams. Curves exam if too long.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Chatterjee is an amazing professor. She relates to students very well and gives you plenty of chances to do well. Study her practice sets and multiple choice and you should be fine! You also get two take home tests so thats very helpful. Must take for Intermediate Macro (:
Go to class and be a good student. If you can do that, easy A guarantee!

Twisha was an AWESOME professor for MacroEcon. She offers a ton of office hours and truly cares about her students succeeding. We had one take home test, two tests in class and our final was a one page paper. The tests were super easy if you DO THE PRACTICE SETS she gives in class! 10/10, I love this prof!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: She was probably one of my favorite professors this semester. She really wants her students to do well and has more office hours than any other professor I've had. She has one take home test and two multiple choice tests which all the answers come straight from the practice sets she gives you. I put in the effort and got an A+. Take her for Macro!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Requires explanations for full credit on "multiple choice" tests. Which alone isn't terrible, but there are no scantrons (only blue books), and not even close to enough time. And they are your entire grade. If you are interested in learning economics and maintaining your sanity, skip this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Very very demanding and course heavy

3 complaints: 
1. Very difficult grader. Prof had to curve all quizzes and tests; strong indicator of difficulty level.  
2. Inflexible. During winter storm the university shut down (no classes) except Browning. Created hardship situations for students. 
3. Pace of course was unrealistic given the amount of material and the 8 week course length.

Lots of reading every class and be prepared for being cold-called. Tests are very tough. However, his classes are always well-structured and he organized everything wisely. Be ready to work hard during his class.

Dr. Browning class was tough to pass. Primarily test expectations were confusing and way harder than most other professors of the subject. You think you got an A then fail a test for inexplicable reasons. No do overs, No curves withwithout a Drs note. Other than that he is about the best teacherperson I knew briefly.
This professor makes things more complicated than necessary.  Avoid his classes if at all possible.

MBA student, had him in Spring 2010 for INSC 60023.  For those who will have him in the future, know that while he expects a lot from you, you'll be happy he did.  Easily in my Top 10 professors including undergrad.  His final was the 2nd hardest exam I ever took next to a Physics one at A&M, so be prepared.  That said, he cares & is very helpful!

An incredibly intelligent individual who knew he needed to ensure the students stayed focused on a core class. A lot of work, long hours, and frustration, but definitely one of the best classes and professors at TCU. I highly recommend any class Dr. Browning teaches even if it is not in your core field.

Tyson's Operations Management class was good in my opinion.  At times I felt that his pop quiz timing was a bit cruel (i.e. on the day of another classes midterm that he completely knew about), but if you work hard, the class is totally doable.  Tests are tough and at some things seems almost impossible, but I really felt like I learned a lot.

I hated Browning while I was taking his class. It was hard, we had to work, and he actually cared enough to make us learn. Definitely one of the most useful classes I had in my MBA program. That said, be prepared for major frustration as you wade through all the material. Talking w/ other MBA's, though, this is a right of passage.

This professor understood that his classes were meant to cover a considerable amount of important material. He instructed well and was consistently fair. His exams were difficult, but not surprising. He did his best to prepare his students for his exams.
no clarity as to what is tryly importatn in this class.

Great prof!  I took him for Operations Mgmt (MBA).  He is a very brilliant man, but not arrogant.  His course is very challenging, but worth the effort.  Be prepared to spend significant time outside of class.  I would definitely take him again.  I have used a great deal of what he taught me at work and it has paid off!

Browning was a good prof, took his time explaining each subject and encouraged participation.  Grading was fair.  I would take this class again and found it to be relevant to application in the real world.  I would have liked a little more teaching of some of the "tools" for the test, but the curve reflected the class's knowledge, so no harm done.

He is an extremely bright and very personable professor.  He is very knowledgeable in his field and understands how to transfer that knowledge to a class. He does not toss softballs, expects good effort and is fair.  The workload is not overly arduous and develops a good foundation in project and program management for the serious student.

The exams were very difficult.  I didn't feel the homework assignments adequately prepared you for performing well on this exam.  Dr. Browning is approachable.  I would have liked the group project to not be as paper-oriented as it was.  Perhaps a PM simulation would have provided a better and more experiential learning opportunity.
Great class.  You will read a lot and need to workout the assigned problems to do well in the exam.  Helpful no matter your major or graduate concentration.  Highly recommendable.
Extremely hard, but he is very knowledgable and willing to help.
Very good professor whose style forces learning.  Project management became incredibly applicable to business environment.  Dr Browning's courses should be sought out.

Dr. Browning is a very good instructor with a good grasp of the subject matter.  He is very easy going and very helpful even after class (willing to work with yours schedule).  He is not easy by any means.

Dr. Browning is a tough but super-smart professor.  He has a wealth of knowledge to share with his students and access to a group of excellent guest speakers. In typical Dr. Browning fashion, the exams are pretty challenging but the grading/curve/scale is very fair...highly recommend all of his classes...
He wants class participation, but if he does not like you he will be very condescending towards you when you participate.  Beware!
This class was tough but fair.  Lots of outside work.  Hard to argue with the curve.

A great continuation to Professor Browning's project management course. A great quality professor and by far one of the most impressive on staff. I'd have no hesitation recommending him for consultive work with my company.
A great professor with a clearly demonstrated knowledge of the topic. If you're looking for a great education, this is the professor for you. Always approachable and a great sense of humor.

The class is tough and there is a fair amount of outside work.  I went into the class thinking that it would not apply to anything that I would EVER do in the 'real world.'  As it turns out, it is one of the most useful classes in the MBA curriculum.  Dr. Browning is, without a doubt, one of the smartest Profs that I have ever had...also very fair.
Explains well, teaches the great work ethics, and makes sure you learn in the class. In my view, a good balance between lectures, cases and other assignemnts.
Amazingly smart individual. This guy should be recruited by the top business schools. Very clear on his expectations. Classes are very useful for the "real world".
Tough class- but very helpful.  Changes the way you think about all types of management- people, financial, operations.  Browning is tough, but fair.

Tough class with a TON of reading.  The exams were very hard & emphasised materials barely discussed in class.  However, Tyson is very approachable and was willing to meet one on one.  He is very knowledgable and creates interesting class discussions.

Dr. Browning is an extremely intelligent person who comprehensively covers all material needed to succeed in his classes.  The material may be dry at times, but there's no real exciting way to cover it.  There is a lot of work involved, and you must pay attention at all time.  But the effort put forth should pay off well in your future.
While Tyson’s classes are difficult, he is also one of the most helpful professors I have ever had. You will get out of his classes whatever you put in.

I was fortunate enought to have taken a class from Dr. Browning, a very highly qualified professor at both an academic and interpersonal level. Graduation from TCU should be something that speaks volumes about the individual; Dr. Browning is TCU's investment to that end. Taking a class from him means being be well equipped.
As a project manager I found this class to be a useless exercise in feeding the inflated ego of a statistician with limited instruction skills.

Boy genius! Browning is an extremely smart man.  Class takes a major amount of outside work.  Standard rule of 3 hours a week translates into 15-20 hours.  Make sure that you work problem sets! (ALL OF THEM)  Hard class!

TOO MUCH WORK!!! Requires 6 hours of reading for each class, plus homework and projects.  He is the most monotone man I have ever heard.  Prepare to fight sleep in each class period.  The class was taught only for engineers, although it was meant for managers.

This class is hard, but in spite of that I found the material interesting and loved the class. Extra credit and curves in exams are very generous, and he is super nice and accommodating. Definitely one of my favorite professors at Neeley.

TAKE HIM!!! I could not recommend a professor more. He truly wants his students to understand the concepts and enjoy tax. He gives practice tests that are VERY similar to the actual exams. He was super accessible outside of the classroom and was always willing to help. I believe he only teaches in the spring so I promise it is worth the wait!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Super clear and engaging professor. Tax is a hard subject in general but he makes it as understandable as possible. If he is an option I would 100% recommend.

TAKE HIM! His lectures are so clear and engaging. Also, he gives great preparation for the tests. I will say our second test was IMPOSSIBLE but he gives SO MUCH extra credit (like more than I've ever gotten in any class ever) because he cares about his students. I'm still waiting for my grade but its hard to imagine I don't get an A.

Caring dude. He clearly wants his students to do well. His tests are a bit difficult, however he does offer extra credit to improve the grade, outside of other extra credit stuff. Sweet professor, usually ends class early, lectures can be boring, but what can you expect from a tax class.

For a tax class, he teaches it very well. He encourages questions, is available outside of class, and provides useful practice exams. Weekly HW/Smartbooks. Does not allow exam retakes but provides opportunities to get points back. His class is slightly boring, but he tries his best to make it entertaining. Great guy, would take again.

This was his first semester at TCU but he's really good. explains everything in detail in class. Tests have practice exams that you can take as many times as you want to prepare and they are just like the actual exam! Opportunity to get 1/2 of your points back on exams too. 2 exams, 1 final. weekly smartbooks and hws but they're easy. def take him!
Great professor, one of my favorites so far.  Super down to earth guy that was very helpful.  You can tell he loves what he teaches which is awesome in a professor.

He is a really tough teacher!!! You really have to work hard reading and writing everyday in order for your efforts to pay off in the end. But it's worth it!  (I am not a "humanities" major, and I survived the course). Just come into the class expecting to bring it and you will do fine. I don't  necessarily recommend taking it in the summer though.

He just doesn't explains things well, at all. Even when he tries, it still doesn't make sense. He is only available for help for an hour before class (no help at all). He only asks questions when he looks at your paper, which doesn't help. The book (The Curious Writer) stinks. It's pointless and doesn't help. Not to mention boring. Don't take him.
he says he wants to help and he wants everubody to suceed but he wouldnt give above a c+ even if u went to the writing center and him multipule times to make sure it was perfect

Dr. Kerstetter truly cares about his students and was my nicest professor of the semester. Although his class involves a lot of reading( Three books and a weekly textbook chapter) I would take him again in a heartbeat.

He's exceptionally kind, caring and helpful. If you need accommodations or extra help, reach out and he'll likely be more than willing to help you. I would 100% take him again. My only qualm is that there's lots of reading. Besides that, great course, requires little effort outside of class and he's accessible and easy to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a really really nice teacher. He assigns a lot of reading for every class, but as long as you do it and participate in class you will get a good grade. He cares a lot about the subject and wants students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is such a sweetheart and really cares for his students, but be prepared for a quiz every Monday on textbook readings that are very long, and worksheets with lots of writing that are graded strictly on Wednesdays and Fridays. his TA is also really scary not a fan.
DO NOT TAKE HIM !! His class is impossible and SO much work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is such an amazing teacher and you can tell he truly cares about his job. Regarding work, we do have a worksheet every class, but overall it's not super difficult if you listen. We take a quiz over this book every week and it's a little difficult at first, but you get the hang of it. He also takes the time to check up on his students well-being

He is such a sweetheart. I would recommend attending his office hours at least once. We have a quiz on the chapter for our reading from our textbook every week, and we have an assignment every single day of class. The assignments and quizzes are not hard. If you took 7th-grade history, you'll be good. Just go to class and do the assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Such a nice amazing guy but there is so much reading and he is an extremely tough grader. You can do well in his class but you have to put a lot of time and effort in. Reach out to him for help because he truly does care. But again so so so much reading.

While I don't think Dr. Kersetter is a bad professor, be prepared to have a quiz every week and basically be learning from the books. You will read A LOT. This class is based heavily on interpretations, and he focuses heavily on effective writing. I had more reading and writing for this class than I did for my lit class this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very nice guy, though grader and a lot of reading but once you get into the grove of things structure becomes very clear. Attendance is mandatory because there is a grade for something everyday.  Really cares and lectures are interesting just A LOT of reading everyday before class. (Most major grades are essays based on books)

Dr. Kerstetter is so nice, and he obviously cares a lot about what he is teaching and a lot about the kids he is teaching! The class is very informational and I really did learn a lot and thought it was fun. The reading and writing assignments each week can be long and a lot of work, so just be prepared to work hard if you want a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Such a great teacher. You can tell he really cares about what he teaches and his students. Class size was perfect and made it easy to have deep ad thoughtful discussion. Very interesting course with great sources and readings. I loved this class and would recommend it to anyone who is interested in history and Fort Worth.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Although this class was one of my hardest this semester, Professor Kerstetter made it interesting and manageable. You need to be prepared to read a lot, write tons of papers, and participate in each class, BUT he is a passionate, caring professor that is willing to help you. This class is very structured so you know what to expect. Would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerstetter is a great professor who cares about what he does and tries to get the best out of every student. The classes are structured and you know what to expect.  An assignment is due every week which is a decent amount of reading and writing. I would recommend taking one of his classes because it is interesting and I have learned a lot.

He is super passionate about history and making sure that students understand why history matters. There is a ton of homework with a quiz each week on lengthy readings but I understand history much more than I did going into the class. There are lots of different assignments so grades are spread evenly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I loved having Professor Kerstetter this semester.. and that says a lot from someone who has no interest in (and has never been good at) History! He is an AMAZING professor who is super accessible and very willing to help. He makes history actually seem interesting. You do however need to be prepared to read lots and study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I read some of the texts over break, because I expected a lot of reading. However, after one week I dropped. He didn't seem willing to work with my accomadations and appeared very close-minded. The first week we were given a quiz and essay to do. He didn't give clear study guides and graded the quiz harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I was in class the first week then dropped. I had read some of the texts over break, because I expected lots of reading. However, after the quiz and essay the first week I dropped. He doesn't give clear directions or study guides then asks particular questions on quizes. He doesn't understand that most take the class to for the core requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: US History since 1877 was the best class i've taken at TCU so far. This professor is super interesting and if you put the time in, you'll do well. It's a lot of reading but I learned so much and was truly interested in the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Does a point system that makes it pretty much impossible to get an A as you get little points off every single week. This should be considered a writing class by the amount of essays and thesis's he makes you write. Grades based on writing quality. Barely learn anything on history and even said he was not worried about teaching content in his class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His class requires a lot of writing and reading, but it's definitely doable. He's super nice and has interesting lectures about the West. Would totally take him again!

Dr. Kerstetter is hands down one of my favorite professors I have had. His class is definitely not a walk in the park, however, his reading quizzes are fairly easy as are in the class assignments. He is a tough grader but I feel like the in class experience makes it all worth it. He truly made learning enjoyable again for me.

Knows his stuff, as any professor should, but is way too full of himself, and overall is pretty darn petty. In all frankness he should focus more on teaching, and less on trying to score points on his students.

This guy expects his students to read absurd amounts of material each week, with a homework assignment/essay usually due every Wednesday and a quiz every Friday. He expected us to read about 5 novels and he is the most difficultand ridiculous grader Ive ever encountered. DO NOT take this guy, his attitude also is very prideful. Not a serious class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Kerstetter is a really nice professor, but difficult. This class is not an easy A by any means. You have to read, you have to write numerous essays, and there is a video project. If you are not good at writing, I do NOT suggest taking this course. It requires a lot of time, but ultimately is enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He means well but does not understand students have other classes to study for or do assignments for. I know I sound like a lazy student who was looking for an easy A but thats not the case. He assigned a paper to be 3000 words (10ish pages) as our final and only gives you the prompt the week of finals so ur torn between other test and the paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very difficult grader. It is hard to understand his feedback. So much reading and a lot of essays. Participation matters, so read and speak up. I did enjoy class discussion, as he was knowledgeable and funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Had Dr. Kerstetter for American West to 1900. He is very passionate about the subject and it makes the lectures very interesting. Be prepared to work for your grade. 4 novels with quizzes, and lots of papers over many different sources of history. Helps to develop your analytical thinking. I learned more in this class than any other this semester.
A great professor, one of the best I have had at TCU. There's a lot of reading involved, but the class is interesting and Kerstetter does his best to change things up.

Hard, but not impossible. The book quizzes stressed me out but he's such a personable professor that I can't say anything bad about him. He is very passionate about the West and it makes things enjoyable.

BEYOND HORRIBLE CLASS AND PROFESSOR!!!! He is degrading to students and has a very pompous attitude throughout the entire semester. He honestly believes his class is the ONLY class students have! AVOID!!!

WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD! He is the most arrogant teacher at TCU. You have 40 hrs of reading & writing EVERY week! If you are not a history major you will NOT do well. There is no point in participating in class. He makes you feel and look stupid if you voice your opinion. He does NOT care about students at all. DO NOT TAKE THIS KERSTETTER!

I really didn't like this guy at first. His lectures were kind of unclear and his style didn't fit my style of learning. After struggling on my first exam, I went in to talk to him. He was more than helpful and cleared up a lot of questions I had. I ended up meeting with him on a semi-regular basis and got better grades.

Don't take this class if you are not willing to work hard for your grade...this is not the easiest class, and if you don't do the reading, don't expect a good grade! He is a terrific teacher and more than willing to help you when you struggle, just go speak to him during office hours. Lot's of reading/writing!

He wasn't the best or the worst. I thought honestly he was kind of a lazy teacher. He just assigned a bunch of books and then we had to write about them. Many classes were watching pointless videos. He could be interesting sometimes in class, but more often he would just talk about how challenging he was. Stop talking and start teaching!
When I look back on my classes at TCU, he stands out as one of the worst professors.  Very full of himself for no good reason.

Dr. Kerstetter is demanding but fair. The entire grade in this course was from take-home essays and half-hour readings quizes. You do have to do all the reading, or you will get a really terrible grade. I enjoyed taking his class.
Nice guy, willing to help you out.  I took histroy survey since 1877 and it was all essays, i'm not much of an essay writer but I still did fine.  Overall a decent class and nice prof.
Extremely difficult, extremely hard grading on everything. quite arbitrary.
A moody teacher.  Not a difficult teacher, but requires you to do exactly as he pleases in terms of writing style.  Grades essays almost as if flipping a coin.

The guy is so self-indulgent it makes me sick. We learned absolutly nothing all semester. Half the time he has no idea what is going on. Way to much stuff was crammed in late in the semester. Always, always writing something and no matter how much you do, he always wants more. Don't ever expect to be right with the man, but only ever somewhat close

Were we suppposed to learn something in this class? Because I didn't.  If I wanted to take a class on continually discussing the validity of sources, I would have done so. He's so self-important it's ridiculous.

I expected it to be more political history than cultural, he really like cultural history so I found myself rather bored. Attendance is a must, I hate essay based tests so that didn't help. If your looking for an EASY EASY B or A don't take him. He's one of thosem, my class is the only one that you all are all taking so there is a lot a lot of WORk

This class is a ton of work and requires a good effort. However, Todd is an awesome guy with such a passion for history that you cannot feel anything except interest. He is also funny and very helpful for students. Getting a B isn't too hard, an A is extremely hard.

Great class and prof. Be ready to work extremely hard, but go see him and get to know him, I think it helps when he's grading essays. Tests and quizzes all essay, you read a lot but you'll learn so much, I enjoyed going to class and was willing to do the work for this guy.
Not a class for slack offs, but for those who are truly passionate about history.
Have learned a lot from him, but have worked my butt off for it.  Would recommend it to anyone who likes readings, not to people who want to slack off.

awesome teacher. never boring. pay attention in class and read what you learned about in the book for the tests. lot of reading tho, read 3 novels, but quizzes on these weren't too hard. just basically read the book and breifly do study quest. he gives. easy B if you go to class and read the books.

Great guy, wants you to learn, but his class has you reading TONS of books and tons of papers. He wants your opinion, and most books he gives has a worksheet with it. Write whats on the worksheet and you'll get an A on those. Test are TAKE HOME ESSAY, you have a week and are 3 essays.
Be prepared to read and write A LOT. Write down EVERYTHING you know on the exams if you want to get an A. Nice guy and all, but he needs to ease up a bit in his UCR history class.

Definitely not the class you want to take for blow off history, but if you want to learn and work hard, take him. You learn so much and in the end, you'll come out with more history knowledge than ever before. Make sure to keep up with the reading and be thorough on the quizzes/exams.

This class is difficult and there is a lot of reading, but it was still my favorite class last semester.  He cares about his subject which makes the lectures more enjoyable.  He is also willing to work with students.  If you put in the effort you will probably like this class

k-stunna is the best prof i have had so far at tcu. he makes history interesting and is hilarious. all his tests and quizzes on books are essays--be thorough: answer WHO WHAT WHEN WHERE and WHY on EVERYTHING. multiple choice quizzes help.

Again awesome teacher! Actually made history interesting with his unique approach! A lot of reading, 3 essay quizzes over novels, and essay exams, but, nevertheless, a fun teacher who taught me a LOT! Just read everything!
Kerstetter is an awesome teacher and uses awesome visuals to help you understand. However, he is very hard and his exams are pretty difficult. But study the book and read through EVERYTHING
Good teacher, but very hard.  I would only recomend him if your major has to do with history.  All tests are essays, so be prepared to write, and a lot of reading, 3 books along with the textbooks.
very hard, lots of books to read

He is great! Very interesting the way he approaches a subject that can be booring. I had to re-take this class cause I had a bad prof before. I loved his class. It was well worth waking up for, especially since I never fell asleep. Very animated and makes class enjoyable.

Mr. Kerstetter is freaking awesome! I loved his class and i usually don't like history. He mostly covers domestic issues which i loved. His class is hard and time consuming, but it's interesting and he's such a nice guy that it's fun. i recommend it, you actually can get something out of this class!
Makes an odd subject really interesting. Can speak Lakota language. Very insightful. Have to read and write a lot, but that's history.
By far my favorite professor throughout my college career. A thoroughly inspired teacher, who easily passes on his love of learning to his students. I would recommend any of his classes to anyone.

One of the few great professors at TCU. He knows a lot of stuff and makes his class as fun as possible! I was proud of the work I did in this class and actually learned more than just how to memorize stuff. It made me want to take him for everything!

Very nice guy. There was a LOT of reading to do, and it was esp. hard to finish b/c the book was TERRIBLE (This Land). A pretty good class; I would definitely suggest taking it Pass/No Credit. He likes to focus on minute, seemingly insignificant, details.
Intersting class, leaves you wanting to go back if you can believe that.  You WILL learn something in this class.

Amazing professor, so incredibly knowledgeable, awesomely understanding and fair in everything he does. Interacive class discussion keeps you intuned and involved in class. Alot of reading though, need to keep up with it. Fabulous teacher!!
Great professor! Loves what he teaches and is very involved around campus. Wonderful discussion class too!
Great prof, good lectures, informative and interesting. Incorporates great outside sources.
I took the basic history since 1865 and Dr. Kerstetter was a great lecturer and made me excited about history. He is always available through office hours.

His classes are very thought provoking and I find myself talking about the issues outside of class with friends. He give interesting lectures and incoroporates really good outside material including books, music and movies.
He is a great teacher! He is very interesting and relatively easy. He is not that difficult but be prepared to do some reading. He has an innovative style of teaching!

Very easy teacher, passionate about her topic and wants you to do well. She talks with an accent, but it's more funny than an inconvenience. Ask questions on her tests and she literally will circle the right one. I sit in class doing nothing but playing on my computer and I have an A. Get  someone to sign u in & study PP for test and your set!

Dr. Verma is an excellent teacher and she is very passionate in teaching. She explains very well and if you pay attention in her class she gives you cues as to what will come on the exam. You will get 3 tests and 1 paper, she will also give you extra credit in class for group discussions. Pay attention in her class and you will do great.

Prof. Verma is fairly straight forward. She has a strong accent which makes it a bit difficult to understand her, but overall she sends you the powerpoints just in case you dont understand. You basically only have 3 tests and 1 paper. So make sure you study for those tests and the paper is fairly easy. She does not offer extra credit.
This is my mom

Dr. Vela is great!  Sometimes you forget she is a teacher, she seems like another student.  She is very helpful and there will be many times in this class where class is cancelled for comferences.  She is funny and keeps things interesting and class is almost always out at least 30 minutes early.
she is tough, rude and a bore!
She is a great teacher. Some of the books we used were kind of boring but she is nice and if you do the work then you will get an A in the class
Very good teacher. She does seem tough at first, but she isn't. I would recommend her.
Dr. Vela is amazing! Intimidating at first but very nice! She will work with you on everything if you just talk to her. Easy A!

She seems like a mean bitter woman at first, but as the semester progresses she gets easier and so does the class.  She is not afriad to make fun of you in class, and all remarks are tolerated, have fun, interact, EASY A
Good class. Very easy grader.

I agree with the 12/18/14 rating. He's a great guy, but not so great a professor. He does not seem able to get his message across. He'll constantly use the term "above and beyond the book" and usually ends that portion of the discussion with "why am I seeing a lot of blank faces". It's best to record his lectures because it's difficult to keep up.

Very nice guy with good intentions but not meant to be a professor. Class is straight lecture and incredibly boring, languag barrier is evident in both lecture and test questions. Projectsassignments are extemely vague and there is no clear guidelines or instructions, really have to figure it out yourself. Tests aren't that hard if you study well.

His class was super boring, and he has an accent so it is really hard to understand him. His test only have 25 questions so it is easy not to do well on a test. The project he does not help or even talk about it at all. It is ver unclear what he wants or what he is looking for.

She's the best professor ever. I am not a theatre major, but a Computer Sciences, and I think her class is one of the most exiting ones I've take at TCU, Great Professor !!!! she doesn't spoon feed you to get an A, but given that you put the minimum required effort in the class, its an easy A

class is not bad at all. takes attendance so you have to go to class, but all you need to do is read the chapters assigned before the tests and you'll be fine.  tests get harder throughout the semester but there not bad if you just read. A is not hard to get if you just read

I really enjoyed my Survey Class with Connie. Although I am a theatre major myself, I did learn a lot from this class. Connie has a wide knowledge of the theatre and is very willing to help. She is strict about her rules, but if you study, you should be fine. Her office door is always opened and she is very funny. Class is light hearted and fun.

soo i made an A but only because I had some theatre background. its a lot of information really fast so i wouldnt take it if you are looking for an easy A fine art credit. she's really funny, and she constantly says, "do ya dig?" it was one of those classes you dont mind going to because its funny. just use her study guide.. its pretty legit.

Connie de Veer is absolutely amazing. She is so helpful and knowledgable about the Theatre. Initially, I was a little skeptical because she is so 'out there', but you come to realize that she is one of the most amazing professors ever. Explains the material in depth. Accesible outside of class. All around amazing professor and person. TAKE HER !

i think deVeer must have put these on here herself cuz these ratings are completely wrong...this lady is the hardest theatre teacher...cant work the technology...acts like everyone in the class as a theatre major...gives a study guide then doesn't use it on the test...absolutely insane...DO NOT take her unless your a theatre major...awful

Easy A. I didn't read the book except for the first test, and that was only because I did not know what to expect. Lecture notes are online, and the tests pretty much come from that. Final is not cumulative, which is great. Watch movies in class every so often. If anyone tells you this class is hard, their existence at TCU is questionable!

The nicest professor I have ever met. The class is so easy and everything is based on the book. Her lecture notes can be found online. This professor is very approachable and helpful. Very nice class, great professor, easy A.

For Survey, I got an A without taking many notes at all, or really ever listening. She puts the notes and she gives you a study guide before every test. All I did was define every term on the study guide in a word document and printed it, then studied that the  for a couple hours. The test are straight from the book, it's very easy. She's nice too.
She is such a nice lady and is not difficult at all. If you want to do very well read and take the notes. She emails all notes to you and is very helpful.

She's a little crazy/ weird, but very nice and helpful. Her mind is sometimes all over the place and she does not always think about the easiest way to do things. If you read the book (inluding the "spotlights") and look over her reviews the tests are fairly simple, if you dont do good on a test, GO TALK TO HER!!
Loves tech theatre. He is such a funny guy, who makes tons of corny, lame jokes. He has a great time teaching it and it makes the class fun. His test are all memorized so take notes!

A lot harder than you think. The tests are strictly memorization and if you don't study...you're screwed. No bookwork or homework and the labs only last 30-45 minutes. Can only miss a few times and grade is based mostly on the tests you take.
hilarious, funny, awesome

Awesome professor- makes lots of corny jokes and knows more about the subject than anyone I have ever met.  Make sure to go to class- much of the info on the tests comes from notes.  Labs are really fun too!

Nice guy.  Know's what he's talking about.  Worst thing is that class is at 9 am and he takes attendance, but if you at least go to class it'll be  a lot easier.  The text books I hardly used.  Tests can a little tricky sometimes.
Makes cheesy jokes you can't help but laugh at.  A fun and helpful teacher who knows his stuff.  Just make sure to study and memorize for the tests, because you're pretty screwed if you don't.

class is pretty easy, his tests can be pretty detailed, so they're hard if you didn't listen, Judd is really funny and likes to draw pictures on the board which can be entertaining, just go to class and listen and you'll do good, cool guy :)

Mr. Boschini's class was like no other. He's a very easy person to talk to and genuinely wants everyone in his class to get an A. There was a good amount of reading but he made learning very easy with how engaging his lectures were. Seriously take any of his classes if given the opportunity to, no doubt.
If you have the opportunity to, take his class. I was excited to wake up at 8am every day. There was always food, the format of the class was unique, and he always keeps you on your toes.

I would take this class. It's a good connection but the class is pretty bad. You have to read 2 books and they were the most boring books ever. A quiz every class. Hes a good guy and fun. He gives you a lot of gifts. Final is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's definitely the coolest professor I've had so far. The class is structured to be fun. You learn about TCU's history and about other colleges. We got to go on a tour to the museum, listen to inspirational speakers, and know the chancellor up close. He genuinely wants to know everyone in the class. Take the class if you have the opportunity to.

Vbo is awesome.  An upperclassmen advised me to take his class and it was one of the biggest blessings I had at TCU. Just a quality man, and while many say he's a politician, to some aspect I'd agree (I mean you have to be to gain the ground he has at TCU) but, and if you take his class you will learn, he is an incredibly genuine individual.

This is THE COOLEST professor at TCU, and it's not just because he is the Chancellor. I learned so much useful information in this class that really helped begin my freshman year. Do whatever it takes to be in this class. I promise you wont regret it.
Boschini's class is the best class at TCU. If you are a freshman and get the opportunity to take it, DO IT!! He is awesome and the class is so much fun.

V-Bo is the man.  If you're a freshman, take this class.  Do anything to get in!  The class is an easy A, and you get to know the coolest faculty member at TCU (not to mention the fact that he's the chancellor!)  Dr. Boschini is a great guy, and you'll learn a lot in this class!!
Great guy--absolutely the coolest professor at TCU.  He cares about the students and TCU, and this is very apparent in all aspects of his class.  Get to know this guy--he's awesome.
Very much a politician.

I thought he was a good guy until the fourth time I saw him within two weeks when I had to remind him of my name AGAIN. Pretty typical chancellor: says and does what he needs to do in order to get money from alumni and organizations, even if he doesn't believe in a lot of what he says.
Very interesting
very smart but I little bit of a politician.  He seems to tell you what you want to hear at the time whether he believes it or not

I don't know what he is like as a professor, but I can tell you as a Chancellor he is very genuine and down to earth. I sat at his table for dinner during senior conference and it was a true honor. He loves his job and it shows.

This guy is the smartest, most admirable person I know. He is sharp as a tack for his age and his class was a joy to take. Since he is the Chancellor, every person working for TCU kissed his ass when we visited different sites, it was fun to watch. Take this class no matter what it takes to get in.

I rly liked Bennett's Wildlife Ecology & Management course.Come to lecture because she grades participation & because the slides only have some of the exam material, most of the material are her lectures. Lab was rly fun, though excel could get confusing rly fast. Overall she's a rly funny, passionate, and down-to-earth person, would recommend.

Dr. B makes this class incredibly interesting, but the tests do not necessarily reflect the main points that we learn in class (like a previous review said, it's more about memorizing species than their adaptations). Would recommend taking a class with her, but be aware that this one will require time dedicated to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bennett seemed nervous and inexperienced. The class was structured weird. It was just a list of animals and their characteristics. The tests didn't match the content in lecture and seemed more like quizzing you on random details rather than larger themes in the field. She seemed more into finding pics for her ppts than teaching

Dr. Bennett is easily my favorite teacher on campus. She's funny, engaging, passionate and truly wants you to do well in her course. Tests are tough, you DEFINITELY need to study, but if you talk to her out of class, she will help you get the grade you want. Very witty and great lectures. I've taken her for multiple classes. Awesome professor.

Dr. Hodges class was a very enjoyable class with few assignments. We read children novels (easy reads) and had group discussions during class. She showed us several children's books and directs the class on how you can use it for your future. She is inspiring and has interesting stories about where she has worked before.

Professor Hodges' class is so nice and easy. We read several novels adapted for young adult literature, and there's no need to take notes. She gives us cool, engaging assignments to respond to literature meaningfully. Her stories are amazing, and she inspires a passion for reading—whether we're teachers, parents, or just working with children.

Dr. Hodges is very understanding and caring! She deeply wants you to succeed and make an A in her class! The content is very straight forward with small assignments and projects but overall, the class is very and super easy.

The sweetest woman and professor I've ever come across. Took her for children's literature. She told us from the get go that she wants every single student to have an A in the class, and that she would help us get there. She doesn't care for MLA/APA format, she doesn't give us any crazy work to do, she always tells us to write "informal". TAKE HER!

Ignore the online part of this review it wouldn't let me put the class number its EDMS 50153. BUT I LOVE HER!!! Please take her for adolescent literature literally the best class EVER. she is amazing and although attendance is not mandatory, you genuinely want to go because it is so much fun and super easy.

Vigeland is a nice guy and all, but I would never take one of his classes again. He tests us over material that we've never learned and the material we do know on the test he asks it in a completely different way where everyone is confused and has no idea what they're doing.

One of the best professors teaching!!! He is very knowledgeable and is always available to help you out. Homework problems were difficult, but the tests were very basic and much easier than assigned problems.

Dr. Vigeland teaches probably the hardest undergrad class for accounting majors in Intermediate 2.  Having said that, he is also an extremely knowledgeable and helpful professor.  Go see him in his office whenever you are confused, do the homework, and go to class.  Tests are very difficult.  Study far in advance and get with partners to study.

Dr Vigs is super nice! However, the class is also super hard... well at least the first exam was.. Find a good study group for the exams and start well in advance for that killer first one. Focus more attn on his chapter handouts and assignments.
Difficult class, but he is GREAT!!  Very approachable and willing to meet at any time.  Really cares about his students!

One word: Awesome!  Very nice prof, ALWAYS in his office willing to help anyone whenever they need it.  The class material is difficult, but Dr. Vigeland does his best to make the material easier to grasp.

Her class is HARD because the tests require you to know a lot from the book and from lectures. Sometimes she gives you assignments at the end of class and barely explains them. She is easy to reach out to and will help you before tests. She will round any grade from an 89.5% to an A despite what the syllabus says. I had an 89.99 at the end
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her tests are hard and they are 80% of your grade.
Prof Vogel has great content in the class, as boring as Blaw always is. There are very few assignments throughout the semester so make sure youre ready for the four exams she has.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not a bad professor, but the exams are not easy. Questions are worded weirdly and there are a lot of typos. It's hard to take a test on lockdown browser with 25 matching vocab words when you can't cross any letters off and have to continually scroll up and down. Exams have essay questions too. Based off of 4 exams and a few easy assignments.

I really enjoyed Professor Vogel's class. Business law can be tough but she makes it easy and approachable. Also, she is laid back and understanding. The one downside is that her tests can be worded badly. Besides that, I would recommend.

Professor Vogel is great, she is pretty straight forward about what she expects but makes the class really interesting with her real-world examples. The tests aren't bad if you study for them and there is no other homework besides 2 or 3 small assignments.

Professor Vogel is great. Expectations are laid out for you and if you are willing to study her powerpoints and study guides you can do well in her class. Its not an easy A but she is a great teacher and her class is very fair. Perhaps most of all she made class very enjoyable to attend and tried to bring in some real life stories that made it cool

Really enjoyed this class! Professor Vogel creates a really nurturing learning environment. I never really felt stressed out because of this class so I enjoyed going every Tuesday and Thursday. The tests and material are pretty straight forward. The only thing I would ask her to improve would be in adding a little more context to test questions.

I enjoyed this class way more than I thought I would. Professor Vogel made the class more relevant to us and i like how she would go over the court cases with us. the assignments were also not difficult, and as long as u go to class, you can do good on the tests, which count for a lot of our grade. Take her!

Mrs. Vogel is a decent lecturer and her tests are very straightforward. With any law class, you learn as much as you read. If you read and take notes or pay attention to her PowerPoint slides, you'll do fine. She takes forever to upload grades though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Vogel is fabulous, she relates the subject to her everyday stories.  Her lectures are long but interesting.  She is a bit scattered and does not post grades until the very end, however, her syllabus is clear so if you read it you will know what to expect and how to calculate your grade.  Learned a lot and would highly recommend her.

Professor Vogel was really nice, her lectures were pretty clear but a little to long. My biggest problem with her was that she took way too long to give grades back, you never know your test grades. Also she is the only one not giving extra credit this year and that is making a big difference for me.
easiest teacher i've ever had. lots of extra credit

Professor Vogel is a fantastic teacher! She is very relaxed and knowledgeable about her subject. Tests are not too difficult, but a lot of studying is required if you want to get an A. She makes Business Law very practical, and I would definitely recommend her!
