MUST TAKE FOR B-LAW. Easiest teacher by far and she is nice and interesting. Don't buy the book!! I didn't read it once and got an A in the class. She prints out her powerpoints for you and everything on the test is in the notes.

Very easy class, as long as you go to class, study the slides she gives you and at least skim the book. Offers an optional final, extra credit opportunities, and is a very nice lady who wants you to get a good grade. Very laid back overall.
Easy teacher for Business Law.  I love law, but only two people took the optional final.  Go to class...tests are from slides.  Doesn't use the book.  I recommend!

You have to take Prof. Vogel! Very nice lady. Class is really easy. Don't buy the book. Teaches off  PowerPoint, hands you a copy of it that you fill in the blanks during class, and if you know the slides, you're ready for the tests. Gives option of watching a trial and writing a paper on it--worth up to 5 points to final average! Easy, easy A!

Do anything possible to get Dr. Vogel for Busines Law.  A great teacher, and a very funn and down to earth lady.  Textbook helps but is not mandatory to do well.. use her slides and know them well.. one of the few teachers I have had who really gives you an opportunity to excel.. extra credit is a huge boost on your grade, reasonable A, or easy B

OMG Easy street with this one! She requires NO reading, don't even bother buying the book. Memorize the slides and you are golden for the exams. However, the course is only 3 tests, so don't screw up. She also offers extra credit for 5 points. Its easy to pull off a B, and with a good memory you can nail an A. You can also argue your grade up ;)
She is a great lady. I enjoyed her class although it was very boring. She uses a lot of great examples while instructing. She is a bit unorganized but she means well.

she was a great teacher- used lots of examples to teach... seemed like a lot of notes at first but just pay attention and ask questions and it will sink in.. also read the chapters before class or right before the test.
There is a lot to memorize, but her tests are easy
take this class. there is a lot to memorize, but she gives you powerpoints of everything she says and tests right off them. she definitly makes a boring class more fun.

She's actually a conservative prof which is rare. She tells it like it is and she gives out her powerpoint in packets but you have to go to class to fill in the blank spots unless you sit with about six of your friends and then yall can rotate attending class...works great! FRAT FRAT FRAT

The class is not very hard, if you can stay awake in class. Vogel I bet is a great lawyer, but she is a lawyer who happens to teach, not a teacher who happens to be a lawyer. Every class is the same thing, going over power point notes. You will have killed a forest in a paper quantity by the end of

I really like her, there is a lot to memorize, but that's sort of what law is. You really need the book because she talks about the examples but she doesn't put them in the handout. Then the tests are all examples, so the book at least has them in print. TAKE THIS CLASS. Highly recomend it.

A lot to memorize but fortunately thats all it is. Because there is so much required of you to know I would advise reading the textbook, it's great reinforcement of the material. Vogel is so laid back and really sweet, from what I've heard about the other B-Law profs Vogel is top-notch!
have to memorize a lot but everything is from the packets that she gives out.  don't bother buying the book. at first looked like we needed it but you'd do just fine without it

Dr. Vuic is an amazing professor. The class is easy if you do the readings, make discussion questions (HW) and have input throughout the in-class discussions. No quizzes or test. The big major grade was a podcast with a partner which is easy if you stay on top of it and get help from her when needed. No textbooks are needed either.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The most personable yet professional professors This class (TCU War & Society) is a discussion based class from weekly readings (not hard). No exams or quizzes and no lectures. In this course, you work on progress for a large research assignment. She is a tough grader but gives great feedback. Offers generous office hours. You will write a lot!

Class- war and gender- extremely interesting. Thats the only think good about this class. She is an extremely hard grader, even if youre in every class and work hard. 100+ pages of reading for every class and discussion questions for reading due. Which she grades hard. 25 page essay, book report, film review, Vietnam paper etc. Dont take this.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I am very glad I took Dr. Volcansek's public law class. I don't think I have ever learned more in a single class. There is a lot of reading, and the tests (essay and short answer) can be daunting, but if you put in the time and effort, it is doable. I made an A in the class and would definitely take it again if I had the choice. SUPER smart lady.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Intro to Public Law was an awesome class, definitely recommend if you are remotely interested in law school. She restructured the class this semester to make it  a lot easier. You have to read pretty much every night but it's interesting stuff! Volcansek is a great professor and you will learn a lot! Gives essay prompts in advance.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Incredible professor, so helpful, emails back almost instantly, and is dedicated to teaching. Her tests are somewhat hard to study for, but it's definitely not impossible, and if you email her a question she'll give you a very thorough answer.

Greatest professor I've ever had. Have had her for 4 classes. Go to class and pay attn. Always do reading. I have gotten an A in all her classes. You learn SO much from her. Very helpful outside of class too. If considering law school, she is a MUST. She is reason I declared a POSC major. A is entirely possible. Encourage everyone to take her.

Great prof. The class was difficult. But, if you do the work and go to class, A/B is possible. Ask for help. She loves emailing students back, and is always thorough with her answers. Tests are essay based, and require attention to detail. Highly recommend.

Easily one of the greatest professors I've had at TCU. HIGHLY RECOMMEND. Has made me so passionate for POSC. If you want the A, do the work. Read what is assigned. Test are pretty straight forward definitions & an essay options she gives in advance. She uses TCU id# to prevent bias. Curves individual grades at end of semester. She's brilliant.
BEWARE! If you disagree she will penalize you. Cheated out of good grade. New the stuff well. Didn't matter. Wish I'd checked this first.

Public Law is a VERY difficult class. Very knowledgeable, kind personality, but gives a great amount of work--very heavy reading and extensive exam reviews. DIFFICULT essay exams. However, what I do like is she is always willing to help and will round your grade up if she sees that you are consistently working hard.

Very kind. Extremely difficult for an intro class (public law). You learn more from reviewing for tests than from what she teaches.  I would stay away from this if I were you. I am not bitter, I got an okay grade - it was just a LOT of work. She is a very very tough grader and there are only 4 grades a semester. Beware!

Dr. V is absolutely brilliant. Easily my favorite class this semester. She is pleasant and very knowledgeable on the subject. If you are considering Law, go talk to her. She is a Pre-Law advisor making her extremely helpful outside of class. You'll learn a ton in her class. If you want an A, attend lectures and do all the reading. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

One of the most intelligent and thought-provoking professors I've had at TCU. Don't take her if you are looking for an easy A or a blowoff class. She makes you think about law from a philosophical point of view and wants to challenge you. I didn't think I would love a law class, but she made learning about the judicial system very insightful.

Dr. Volcansek really knows her stuff. You won't do well if you don't try, but it's nice to get a good grade you worked hard for. Take her because you want to learn something and you'll love her class. Don't take her to get a class out of the way. Lecture-based with two essays, two tests and a research design for Judicial Politics. Very nice lady.

I dropped this class after 6 weeks of failure. (Im a straight A student). The reading was the actual writings of Plato, Aristotle etc, and she would quiz over the material BEFORE she lectured about it. The quizzes pulled out tiny details. I do not recommend taking this class unless you have to. It's semi-interesting but the way its set up....
Interesting topics but she made class horrible. The only grades were written essays and there was no rubric. You are graded subjectively and only receive an A if you agree with her.
Really nice, helpful, and knowledgeable. She makes you think, and put in some effort, but I would most definitely recommend taking a class taught by her- you will learn a lot!

She's like one of those Warhead candies-- Sweet on the outside... Well, go eat a Warhead and you'll figure the rest out on your own. I dropped her class after seeing how ridiculous her grading regiment was. Studied a lot, didn't matter. Her class is not for the faint of heart, especially if you don't like being told what to believe.
I hope she's better at being a dean than she is in the classroom.  She should be ashamed of the lousy job she did.  DO NOT RECOMMEND

one of the worst teachers ever, bashes law school and lawyers non-stop. unclear in what she is looking for and  doesnt explain her grading. should stick to being the dean cause shes not helping students
I never knew it was possible for one person to be so contemptuous and so incompetent.  All I can say in her favor is that she has good photocopying skills.
She will kick your butt but you will really learn your stiff. Not for the timid, but worth the effort.  A good prep for law school.
she seems to think that it's alright to be condescending if you use a sweet voice.  she'll tell you one thing, then stab you in the back

I've never had anyone grade me the way she did. No Dean should be allowed to teach for the principal reason that she cannot dedicate as much time as other professors can. She also is not as easily available. It was just a bad experience. Grading is real unfair and you only have two tests. Thats your grade for the whole semester.
She graded me on my handwriting for crying out loud! DO NOT RECOMMEND!

She is the best teacher I have had at TCU.  She makes the class interesting and worth going to, even if you are not a hardcore law lover.  This is not an easy class by any means, but she will reward you effort.  A's are possible.  Great teacher.

She doesn't really teach as much as simply hand out material for you to do. I've never been in a class that thinned out this quickly. She knows we have trouble understanding, as she noticed how we "all look confused" during class but then she doesn't do anything about it. Unless you're a little pre-law/political science nerd. I DO NOT RECOMMEND!

Amazing class!! One of the most interesting courses ever taken. Awesome professor. I wish Dean Mary would quit her job and teach full time...there are not enough prof like her out there. Highly recommend!!!

I only recommend this class if you're hardcore about law. Many dropped throughout the semester. She is sweet, but because she is Dean she can't dedicate as much time to you. She also doesn't seem to want to help you as she remarks how we look confused & ask her questions yet she says "well maybe I shouldn't put it on the test."

I took every class of hers that I could because she is so good. She was a major reason I added political science as a major. I suggest taking her any chance you have. Also she's the Dean of AddRan, who is a good person to know in the future as well.
She is an amazing professor!  She tells you everything you will have to do and pushes you to your limit, but is always there for you ready to help.  Would take her no matter what the class is!

She gives you everything up front that you will need to do for the semester. Very understanding with deadlines. This woman is amazing. She knows when there is a lull in the lecture and she will change it to where it is relevant to you.
Texts are fairly easy.  She gives a really good review.  Study and you will make a B.  Amazing professor!  Makes things relevant to today.  Convinced me poli sci was right for me!

I absolutely love Dr.Wallace, I truly do not have enough good things to say about her. She keeps lecture lighthearted with jokes and details about her life, but also covers all the information that could be on the test. You do need to read the textbook though, it is so important to come to class and be aware of what you are going to be learning.

Lots of work and lots of exams and very content dense. Hard class regardless of professor, but there are lots of points to be earned unlike other professors have. This class is truly a part time job, but it is possible to do well if you have the time to dedicate it to this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Wallace is very difficult and challenging, however, by having 6 exams that means you can fail one or two and still do decent in the class. She also gives out study guides to fill out which were extremely helpful for me along with posting all the lectures and slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Wallace for lab and lecture. She's a nice lady, and you can tell she loves Anatomy. However, her exams are extremely hard, and pack so much information. Also, she's unnecessarily hard for compared to the other professors.

Do not listen to anyone that says you get what you put in. I put in so much time and effort this semester and got nothing out of it. I went to office hours just to be told that I am doing everything right, but still not passing tests. Tests are 25-31 questions which leaves no room for error and does not even reflect half of the material covered.

Her tests are extremely hard and are only 33 questions out of SO MUCH information. However, all anatomy is going to be hard, but she does not drop your lowest test grade like Professor Crenshaw does which really helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wallace was a pretty great professor for A&P. Her lectures are interesting and she makes them pretty entertatining. Lots of drawings which can be helpful and she reuses quiz questions on her exams. The tests are difficult as per most A&P classes but her learning outcomes help a lot. Overall you get out what you put in.

Great professor with clear, engaging lectures and funny comments that keep things interesting. Her D2L is well-organized, and assignments and quizzes really test your understanding. Success depends on the time you put in outside of class to study and review.

Prof. Wallace is just an okay professor for A&P. She is very kind and always willing to answer questions in class or in office hours. Her lectures are just a little hard to follow, and sometimes the explanations don't make sense. But if you study the textbook and her lectures hard, it's possible to get an A.

Professor Wallace is very caring and always accessible outside of class to answer questions or concerns. She is a little unorganized with TCU online which was often frustrating. There isn't a big cumulative final since she has exams that are 15% of cumulative material. She is a pretty good professor but she goes pretty fast with lecture.

I really liked Professor Wallace she was very caring and straight forward when you have questions. I had her for both lecture and lab and she was very devoted to making sure we did well in the class. It is possible to get a good grade if you just follow/study what she tells you. A lot of her exams have questions from the quizes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's very knowledgeable on the content and is good at explaining but she would be better at teaching a smaller class. She would skip around during lecture and would usually only explain 30-40/100 slides. Everything counted for credit and there are 6 mc exams that are partly cumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I LOVE Professor Wallace. I had her for A&P I and II and she taught me so well. All of her assignments are very intentional and they help you learn and study. Quiz questions are also on exams. She also explains the material so well. She is so caring, records all of her lectures, and is the best anatomy professor ever!!

Wallace is super nice and kind. She cares about her students if you make the effort to know her. Her lectures are boring and she jumps around 100 slide ppts. Her tests are doable if you study a lot, but know that you will have to study all the time (tests every 2 weeks). You can do well, but I did not learn very much tbh.

Wallace's tests are super easy and in class assignments are rare and also easy. However, she doesn't prepare the class well for her tests. She will frequently skip slides and assume you know things. She is kind and makes class interesting, but is not a great professor.

any anatomy class you take is going to be difficult but i think professor wallace is very intelligent and truly cares about how her students are doing in her class. she is easily accessible outside of class and responds to emails quickly. you do have to study for her tests but she provides a lengthy study guide

Wallace was made to teach. There is soo much to learn in anatomy and it gets so overwhelming, but she actually goes through concepts in great detail. 6 exams, pre- and post hw, and 30% of the grade is lab portion. I have Crenshaw for lab (also great) Consider yourself lucky if you get W. You won't get by cramming. You need to study well in advance.

Take her!!! Had Crenshaw for anatomy 1 and didn't learn a thing.

Wallace: emphasizes learning and concepts. exams are fair and straightforward. lectures will prep u for exam

Crenshaw: emphasizes memorization of terms. exams are tricky and random. makes you read textbook end-end and memorize

This is a very difficult and time consuming class. I took her in the fall and ended up taking the course again online in the wintermester. She genuinely cares about how well we do in class and is approachable and easy to reach. She answers questions very quick. The course in general is a ton of information to cover in such a short time.

I've heard Wallace is a great professor for lecture, but try to avoid taking her for lab. She either lectures for way too long or she lectures for way too little. Either way, she barely walks you through the content and barely covers what is needed to be taken away from the lab information. She's nice but, in my opinion very unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved professor Wallace. She truly cares about you succeeding if you show that you care. While her test are hard if you go to her office hours she is always willing to help you understand the topic better.

She's decent, there are a lot of times I feel I am having to teach myself the content that we don't discuss in class. If you like that teaching style then she's definitely for you. She is very open and responsive to students' questions and is crazy smart. Her tests are decently easy and you have a chance for more points after tests

Wallace is a very good teacher! I enjoyed going to the lectures as she is very smart and explains the topics in depth. This class is not easy but with her lengthy study guides, HW quizzes, and other assignments it is not that bad. She usually has tests every 2 weeks with 30-35 questions. She is understanding and helpful I highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I actually liked Wallace for the anatomy lecture. We had a test every 2 weeks but they were only 30 Q's and were taken outside of class and you had the whole weekend to take it. She gives you a long study guide but I think it made studying easier because you just needed to know what was on the study guide, which was still a lot of info.

Out of all the anatomy professors, I would highly recommend Wallaces lecture! Anatomy is definitely not an easy class, but with Professor Wallaces lectures it made it very do-able. Her tests are 30-35 questions, and she accepts late work without any penalty. I followed the learning outcomes and took the HW quizzes, and have made high B's

Wallace is a queen! She lectures from pictures which is sometimes confusing but she is very accessible outside of class and very willing to answer questions. She gives a lot of homework quizzes but those quiz questions are questions on the test. I recommend her over the other two professors because her tests are 28-30 questions and easier.
anatomy is obviously a tough class no matter what professor; I loved Wallace, her tests are very clear of what your gonna be testes on. Cares about the students and is passionate

I really loved having Professor Wallace for lecture. She knows exactly what she is talking about and wants her students to do well. I recommend taking notes before class based on the learning outcomes and then listening and adding notes during lecture. Professor Wallace is so kind and I 100% recommend her for anatomy lecture!

I loved Professor Wallace. Anatomy with any professor is difficult, but Wallace knew her stuff. She was accessible outside of class and wanted her students to do well. It's definitely a grind, but I would take her again if I had the chance.

I loved Mrs. Wallace, and would recommend her for lecture. Anatomy is a difficult course, but she definitely wants you to succeed. I bombarded her with emails every week, and she was always super helpful and responds within a day or two. All lectures are recorded. This class is very fast paced, so just read the textbook and keep up with work.

I personally really liked professor Wallace. I had her for both lab and lecture for A&P 1 and I have her again for lecture for A&P 2. The tests are hard but she really tries to teach you the material in class and will try to answer your questions in class. I ended with an 89.9 in AP1 and right now i have I think a 95 in AP2 but she doesn't round.

Anatomy is a difficult class no matter what professor you have. I was scared to have wallace at first based on the reviews here, but if you read the textbook, memorize the learning outcomes, and stay up with the work, you will get a good grade. She makes it very clear what you need to know and is very helpful anytime you need it!

I took this class because I was a biology major, but then I changed majors and didn't apply myself as much in this course. I wouldn't go to class at all but still managed to pass. Whenever I was in need of help, Professor Wallace would answer emails pretty quickly and was really understanding. I recommend her if you need this course for credit.

I loved Professor Wallace! She gets a bad rep but shes actually a really good teacher. Anatomy is hard but she gives you lecture outcomes and homework quizzes that tell you exactly what the test is on. Her lectures explain the concepts really well. I really enjoyed her class.

Anatomy is a hard class no matter what professor you have . Professor Wallace makes it clear through the learning outcomes what you need to know for the exams. Lectures are hard to pay attention to but if you do the notes before class the lecture will reinforce the notes. Use the learning outcomes and homework quizzes to study and you'll be fine.

Great prof, her lectures are helpful, but a lot of slides to cover in one class. She skips around when lecturing so as long as you read the section of the textbook you will be fine. If you put in the work you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had Wallace for lecture. This class definitely is a lot of work but if you keep up with the readings and work hard you will be fine. Wallace is good about providing lots of resources to help you succeed: her office hours are really helpful, she provides learning objectives for each chapter, case-studies and hw quizzes help as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I had her for lecture. The class is definitely not easy and it is so important to keep up with reading the textbook. She is lecture heavy but also has in class and out of class activities that help apply your knowledge so you better understand it. Attendance is not mandatory but it will definitely help if you go in person
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Anatomy is never going to be an easy class no matter who you take. Professor Wallace really cares about how you do at the end of the day, and she is willing to explain something to you at a moments notice. She also can be pretty funny at times. There's a lot of material to cover, but I do suggest her as a good Anatomy teacher!

Homework is through the textbook but she highlights what you need to read/know. Lectures are mainly her reading off of her powerpoint presentations but she answers all questions thoroughly. Attendance isn't mandatory but sometimes that are class assignments that she takes for a participation grade: case studies, group assignments, etc.

There is a reason why her classes do not fill up quickly when enrollment comes around so please take this as a hint. A&P is already hard as it is but Prof. Wallace makes it 10x harder. Her teachingreading off slides on her powerpoint along with tricking students on what's going to be on the exam.

I had heard some bad things about Professor Wallace but ended up having her for my lab professor (before COVID sent us online) and really enjoyed it! She was much more helpful in lab than the professor I had in A&P 1. She was always right there when you needed help and never made you feel stupid for asking a question.

Take Garcia or Crenshaw if you want to have engaging lectures. She reads off her power-points and doesnt give you enough time to take notes. If you need to take A&P 1 or A&P 2 your best option is a different professor if you want to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had Crenshaw first semester, & everyone told me not to switch into Wallace saying that she wasn't the best lecturer. Best switch! No more in class quizzes anymore, just ones on TCU Online with unlimited attempts. She was really engaging in class and she's funny. I didn't go to every class, just listened to the lectures & it didn't affect my grade

I took Crenshaw's first semester and really struggled. Although her lectures aren't as engaging she is a really good teacher and really cares. Everyone says Crenshaw is the teacher to take but I actually liked Wallaces class a lot more due to how structured she is and gives your quizzes that are very similar to test questions. Very accessible!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took her for A&P II. She was so funny and made lectures interesting and fun! She genuinely seemed to care about the well being of her students and that we actually learned instead of just stressing about our grades. Because of COVID-19, we had to move to online but she has made it as good as possible so that we still learn and can do well!

Amazing lectures. Incredibly engaging and interesting to listen to. She provides very clear outlines for what is test material and plenty of additional resources whether that be through the text or supplemental audio and visual content. Open office hours and great human overall.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Anatomy is a must for Nursing and Wallace is not the greatest or sweetest but she does know what she is talking about. She is difficult as heck but she's really just trying to make students better which I can see. She doesn't sugarcoat anything but that is how she's preparing you for upper level nursing classes. Suffer now, soar later lol
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Wallace was great for Anatomy Lab and I enjoyed learning from her. She cares about her students from a Lab perspective. There are differing opinions on her lecture class. I recommend taking Crenshaw for lecture at TCU. Lab doesn't really matter because you teach yourself for the most part.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: A&P is the hardest class I have ever taken (so far) #nursiglife. With this being said, Wallace didn't make it any easier on me. She is "nice" but enjoys tricking you on exams and makes things even more difficult. I studied weeks in advance and still failed exams! So be ready to live in the library for a semester and still might not even pass :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: this professor reads from a powerpoint and is not very accessible outside of class. She does not give you very valuable information when you go to her office hours anyways. During lecture, she can elaborate on important things but it does not really help because her tests are worded overly difficult. Get used to doing this entire class by yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hardest class I have ever taken. HIGHLY recommend going to her office hours and reviewing your tests. She doesn't test the understanding of the material, she tries to see if you can connect things together. Tests are wordy and can take 5 min just to figure out what she is asking. Get a tutor early and be ready to study at least 20 hrs/test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You have to go to class as there are quizzes everyday. Professor Wallace just reads off the powerpoints, so you have to teach yourself all the material. Her test questions are not straight forward at all, she tries to trick you. She is very accessible outside of class though and always willing to answer any questions / re-explain anything.

Obviously, A&P is a very difficult class. But professor Wallace knows exactly what she's talking about and is always available/willing to answer questions. She does word a lot of the test questions in a tricky way, so make sure you really know your stuff. There is a ton of work that goes into this class no matter what.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: A&P is just one of those classes that is crazy hard because it's a weed out class. That being said, if you memorize literally every powerpoint and have a solid understanding of the concepts taught each week in class you should be fine for Wallace. You really do have to teach yourself the lectures because she just reads off the Ppt in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: For such hard concepts that are taught in A&PI, Mrs. Wallace does a very poor job at explaining them. Her tests purposely try to trick you - she said so herself. Expect to teach yourself the lectures and work your butt off for just a B. Take Crenshaw (had her for lab) - who explains stuff SO well and is very clear on explanations and exams.

I had her for lab. The practicals were weird because sometimes she'd point to stuff and I literally had to ask the TAs what she was even pointing to. She didn't explain anything because I think she expected all of us to know everything coming into class. Wish she would've worked with us more, she's smart and explains well (you just have to ask!)

Mrs. Wallace is a cool professor, but not sympathetic in the slightest. You have to work for your grade, and nothing is handed to you. That said, the class is definitely doable. Memorize the powerpoints and be willing to put in the time into the class, and you will pass. I made an A first semester and B second (89.5 which she would not round)

Mrs. Wallace read off of the PowerPoint and rarely added anything besides what was on the slides. If anyone asked a question she would respond with "I'll get back to you on that" . Her tests were way too hard for how unhelpful she was. I went to her office hours to get help and she never seemed to care. Crenshaw is the way to go (had her for lab)

My number 1 tip for this class is to rewrite the PowerPoint notes every day after class in your own words. That way you aren't completely under water for weekly quizzes and especially the tests. I believe this improved my grade 2 letters second semester. For lab use the white boards in the library to practice spelling and visualizing.

Although a bit unorganized and always 5 minutes late to class, Mrs. Wallace is a good teacher. Her lectures are audio recorded and put online after class so if you missed class that day or something important was said and you didn't get it down, you can go back and listen. Her test questions are straight from the powerpoint and lecture. Memorize.

A&P is just straight up a hard class.  You HAVE to start out strong and finish strong, i spent endless hours studying for this class, at one point it became my life.  Wallace is VERY willing to help thought!  Definitely go to her office hours.  The class is difficult but I found it very interesting and informative!

One of the most difficult classes I've ever taken. I lived in the library studying for this class. I found the class extremely interesting & learned a lot of valuable material, but it was tough, no doubt. Wallace will help, but she's not even close to sympathetic. You have to work for your grade. Study from day 1!

A and P is a hard class regardless. Wallace is notorious for having really hard tests, but she is very clear cut on what is considered "fair game". A lot of material is covered in this class and it moves incredibly quickly. Wallace can help if you ask for it, but her office hours are definitely limited.

Wallace is a fine teacher. She makes it very clear what you need to do well in the class. She basically tests straight from her powerpoints but her tests are definitely VERY HARD anyway. She will help you if you reach out to her during office hours, but she words things to be harder than they could be. If I had to do it over, I'd take Crenshaw.

I took Wallace for A&P and she takes a little while to warm up to. It's not that she is a bad teacher, it is that A&P is A LOT of material. Want a good grade? Study every single night, don't cram, do all the online homework, and memorize her power points. It's not an easy A, but if your a health major, it definitely prepares you for the future.

Class is not mandatory but YOU SHOULD GO TO CLASS EVERY SINGLE DAY AND ON TIME or YOU WILL PROBABLY FAIL. Be prepared to work your butt off. Tests are mainly from lecture. She is funny and an enjoyable teacher but it is the material that gets to you. Study before labs. Just study everyday, the only way to make an A unless you're a genius :)
He is super funny and the class is not hard if you study what he tells you to!

Weekly quizzes & three exams (one being the final). Exams are fairly difficult and multiple choice + written, if you do not study lots you will do poorly. His class lectures are pretty disorganized & he never posts slides. Nice guy but would not recommend taking if you can avoid it.

He was such a funny professor and class never felt as long as it actually was. Class was unorganized at times, but his quizzes always had extra credit on them so that was a major plus. The few assignments he had were an easy grade boost, overall would take again.
Literally my favorite class ever, I wish i could re take it over and over again. Study, pay attention, and respect him and you will do good.
Great professor! Inspired me to learn more about America's history and become more involved in world events and politics

Watters is the best! I find his class clear and engaging. Unlike other history professors, Watters doesn't play tricks. He truly cares about his students and wants them to learn and thrive in the class. I love the way class is structured with weekly quizzes, it keeps me studying. Study hard and you'll be fine:) Also he is so funny!!!

Watters is genuinely the sweetest guy. You have a quiz every week based on soley what comes out of his mouth, he doesn't provide notes and his lectures are all over the place. You have 3 exams that are 75% written. Pay attention, engage, and study your butt off and he will help you. He really is hilarious and nice when you get to know him.

Dr. Watters is super kind and really cares about his students. I never dreaded going to his class. I found the weekly quizzes to be manageable if you study the day before but the exams are difficult. The two exams are heavily weighted so even though I did good on all the quizzes the exams weighed my grade down. He gives extra points for attendance.

I like Dr. Watters and he made his lectures pretty interesting. Exams are kind of difficult and they are spaced out between two days. Attendance is mandatory and he gives 10 extra points for those with perfect attendance. Gives weekly quizzes but they are relatively easy if you study.

He's pretty lecture heavy, but it's interesting topics and he doesn't just read off the slides. A lot of the lectures are what he says in class and not so much what's on the board. There's quizzes every week which are really helpful because it keeps you studying. But overall he's really funny, cares about his students, and is a good professor

Professor Watters makes his class engaging and enjoyable. Frequent quizzes effectively prepare students for the challenging tests, which he outlines clearly. Success requires paying attention, as the material is demanding, but missing a class or two won't significantly impact your grade if you stay on top of the content.
If you're a lambda you'll be good.

One of the best classes I've ever taken. If you go to class, take notes, and study your notes, you'll make an A in this class. 11 quizzes (drop 1) with extra credit on each. 2 homework assignments that are easy. 2 exams, the higher grade counts twice. Final WASN'T comprehensive. Attendance is extra credit. Prof Watters is a personable and nice guy.

Such a nice professor and really funny. Lectures are pretty interesting but you have to go to class because he does not post the notes, or anything on D2L. Everything is paper and handed out in class. Weekly quizzes and I believe 3 exams throughout the year. Gives a lot of extra credit on quizzes. Love this professor as a person, but hardish class

He is a great guy but hardest class I have ever taken. Unless you have photographic memory, have hours (and I mean 10+) to study, and are great at tests or quizzes, I would not take his class. Wish it was easier to pass because could have been more enjoyable. Truly awful.

Watters is super funny and a really chill professor. He is super easy to talk to and really wants to help in and outside of class. The course content isn't difficult there is just a lot of it. I would say the tests are difficult but if you actually study there is no way you get below a B. You can get over 100 on his quizzes. Highly recommend.

Wes Watters is a great professor who cares about what he teaches. He made it very interesting. If you dont miss a class you get 10 points added to your final. He helps a lot throughout the semester by adding bonus questions and he drops your lowest quiz score. It is a difficult class that requires a lot of studying but it is maintainable.

I took this course and it was relatively easy. He does go through notes pretty fast and doesn't have an exact powerpoint to follow, so you have to take notes as he goes. He gives a quiz every Wednesday, but if you go to class and pay attention, the quizzes are pretty easy. He gives many opportunities for extra credit, so take advantage of that.

Wes is the man. If you are interested in history he is really knowledgable and you will like this class. Quizes every week sucks and tests can be hard. This class is not easy but at the end of the day if Wes likes you he will take care of you.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Let me preface by saying, I like Dr. Watters as a person. The notes he gives in class are the worst I have ever experienced in my time as a student. You will be teaching yourself this class and you better know everything down to the time stamp. There are better and easier history classes to take. Again I like Watters I just cant recommend his class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy but his notes are very confusing, hard to follow, and messy. Quiz every week some are easier than others but overall difficult. Exams were very difficult and very detailed. Grades hard for short answers. Gives extra for not missing class. Puts nothing on D2L. 3 homework assignments over the semester. Kinda have to teach yourself

History is my favorite, so I am really upset about this class. He is a very nice and caring guy but notes are horrible and messy. Does NOT go in depth with lecture - leaves us hanging to teach ourselves. Material we "learned" was not on tests.Everyone in my class is struggling.Class average is a 70 right now. only take if you can teach yourself.

Pros:
- WW is funny and lectures are entertaining


Cons:
- his notes are a scrambled mess they lack the info you'll need for the exam
- good luck finding the notes (doesn't use D2L) 
- 3 exams for each you memorize 30+ cases and specifics about them
- rarely releases any study guide, you're on your own 
- Exams only on paper 
- Time constaint

OMG i love Dr Watters! He is the most caring professor I have had at TCU. His tests are pretty tricky but if you study and put in effort you will be just fine. He loves questions and answers emails super fast too. Weekly quizzes but not bad if you pay attention in class

Lectures don't go in depth enough and slides offer minimal information, ensuring student understanding is a the bare minimum and that students are really left to teach themselves. It's a poor reflection of his ability to teach and all around disappointing since he clearly knows the content and seems like a nice person. Sadly wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Watters is a stand up guy who wants the best for his students. The night class can be long with a lot of notes that all gather up on the test, but it is doable with studying and rereading notes. He will help whenever you need it and wants the best for his students.

Do yourself a favor and don't take this class unless you HAVE to. It is so hard and you are tested on about 25 supreme court cases each quiz. So much memorizing and he isn't very good at explaining. It is a senior level class offered as a CORE but DONT take it! His lectures don't help and you will be learning everything yourself. This class aint it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Watters is a great teacher, just make sure to actually do your readings and be prepared for the quizzes. You'll have to spend a decent amount of time studying for the test as well. Make sure you take good notes as well, they make up a lot of the information.

Watters in this class senior level course or not doesn't matter, he does not help you at all, he sets you up to fail he gives you an obscene amount of information to study and never helps you review for anything, doesn't help you prepare for anything. Legitimately give you absolutely no help at all even if you reach out to him and seek his help
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was my second time taking a class with Dr. Watters. This class was harder than the first one I took but I still really enjoyed it. The class is mostly lectures but they are very entertaining. There aren't many grades (there are a few quizzes, a case study, and the final). This class does require a good amount of studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very old school style of teaching; I did not use D2L a single time in the class. However, as long as you attend the lectures and take decent notes, you should have no problem getting a B at the very worst. Dr. Watters is a very caring and knowledgeable professor who interacts with his students. Would definitely recommend.

I took this class for a core credit- wish I wouldve taken another. Class consists of weekly quizzes on paper, 6 question sets (questions about topics you havent covered), and 2 tests on paper. Watters is super nice and approachable and does try to help his many failing students. A lot of easier core classes than this. Do not recommend.

Dr. Watters was a great professor but as a side note, I am biased because I love U.S. history in the first place. He provides his great knowledge of the subject along with funny jokes to keep you engaged. But, t is crucial that you pay attention and study well for all quizzes and tests to do good in class. I would take another class with him.
really try not taking him!!!! his class is all tests and quizzes and they suck so much. it is awful and boring
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Watters' class was very hard to succeed in. He "lectures" by putting a few words on the screen. He then tests you on these "notes" the next class. Quiz or test every class. I am a great student and am hardly passing. The class will be on pass/no credit. He is extremely old school and nothing, including grades are posted on D2L. Don't take
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was my favorite class and professor this semester. The lectures were very interesting and did not just contain all the usual/basic things we learned in US History in high school. EVERYTHING is done on paper in class. There are many quizzes, but he always gave us notice. There is some extra credit. He is willing to work with students a lot.

Dr. Watters is a great guy, gives extra credit, but he's old school and doesn't post anything online. Everything is done by paper and handed in at the beginning of class. For lectures, he projects words on a screen and lectures on the words. There are quizzes every class on the previous lecture & 3 exams the whole semester. I had to study ALOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Watters is honestly my favorite professor. I was sick the first month of class an the gave me so much time and grace to make it up. He is funny but old school. Nothing is online and everything on paper. Honestly he is awesome and I love his lectures! He even includes fun facts about history like scandals of presidents.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Watters teaches in a lecture format and is very old school when it comes to technology. All of the material on the exams comes from his lectures, so be sure not to miss class as he doesn't post them. There are 3 exams, along with quizzes for every non-exam class so it is imperative to pay attention. Overall he is a nice and caring person.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy

heres my story. so i was chilling in class during after my test and then someone texted me something so i laughed. And then he got mad at me. Ig the expectation is to cry in class. Man whoever said learning is fun lied. This is horse bs. I also recieved an unforrtunate grade on my quiz which i recieved no feedback for
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He tells you to buy all these textbooks that you don't use. He also uses a projector to project words which are considered notes even though they have no detail. I do not recommend. I am pass/failing the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He uses a projector of notes that aren't very helpful or descriptive. These notes turn into weekly quizzes that are very hard. The tests are also extremely long and difficult. Nice man, but a bad teacher. He knows what he is talking about but just doesn't explain anything well and does everything way too quickly. I'm a good student too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Watters is a genuinely caring individual. If you show up and take notes then you should be fine. The tests are rather long and he does have pop quizzes every class but he is funny and very thorough when it comes to his notes. He doesn't use TCU online, but regardless is accessible when you need him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Watters is an absolute animal. His lectures are great. Awesome semester.
Gives the entire lecture without a powerpoint & it's pretty boring & incredibly hard, but he's funny

Long, boring lectures. Doesn't use powerpoint, instead one of those image projectors he puts papers under. you take notes on what he says the entire class and that is what is on the exams. very funny, nice guy but the material is very difficult and the tests are too. I would take him if he taught a different class, but not this one. dr watters a g
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He does not lecture the first week so it was too late to drop when I realized how awful this class is. Does not use PowerPoints or TCU online. He lectures the ENTIRE time and moves ridiculously fast. You will be studying 100+ terms per exam (3). 50 MC, 15 FIB w/o word bank, and 7 short answer. Quiz every week. Tries to trick you on MC. I P/NCed it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Love my man, Wes!

He is a great professor, his lectures are HILARIOUS and really makes history interesting. The class is long, but he gives you a break in the middle and frequently lets class out 20-30min early.  Be prepared to take notes - LOTS of notes. There are 3 exams and quizzes every week but are easy if you take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I am an intelligent student, but this class was SOOOOO hard.  I struggled through it.  You have to pay attention to the lectures and literally write down every word that comes out of his mouth in order to well on the exams.  His quizzes are hard and everyhting about this class is just hard.  I had to pass fail it and it was hard to even pass that
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wes Watters is a really funny prof. I took a night class which was probably a mistake because it's hard to sit through 3 hours of lectured history, but I'm glad I did because he is a great teacher and class was easy. He gives tons of extra credit that improved my grade by a letter. Quizzes every class, so reread your notes before to get good grades

Take notes every class and show up to every class. If you show up to every class he will give you 10 EC points. Go to office hours if you have any questions regarding the material. He will let you look over your tests in office hours, which helps before the final, and provide what you needed to include in your short answer to get full points

SUPER RUDE. Don't even bother going to him for help! He doesn't use ECollege and there is no official way to know what your grade is. Only 2 tests and a final. Lots of information to grasps for just one night class. I would not take again and I do not recommend taking this unorganized, pompous teacher. Oh and don't waste your money buying the book

The class is easy if you show up and take notes.  Wes Watters is very passionate about the class and throws a bunch of interesting stories and funny facts about the information he is lecturing about.   Class is usually cut short and goes by quickly while he is teaching.

Only taking this class once a week on Monday nights. Quizzes before every lecture. Lectures are long but he teaches in a story-like descriptive way so it makes it easier to understand. The textbook is confusing. If you miss even a few minutes of what he says or a class, it's really hard to know what's going on. Nice guy though, and helpful.

His class is one of the more enjoyable classes I've had at TCU.  Lectures are long (because it's a night class) and can be boring at times.  Sit in the front, focus on the lecture and write down what he says.  He doesn't go to fast and will repeat a point if you ask.  He also provides you with a good review sheet and what to expect on the test.

doesn't use ecollege, never responds to emails when asking for grades even though he tells you to email him if you want to know. only two tests. doesn't use powerpoints, just talks with key vocab words on the board. not very organized. entertaining for a long night class but not a good teacher
Extremely rude when you go to him for help. His lectures are boring and disorganized. He gives a quiz every class that you will not do will on unless you study.

take his night class!!! i actually kinda looked forward to it. he is hilarious and a great lecturer, he makes history really interesting. weekly quizzes and the tests are pretty hard, but I passed/failed the class and didn't really study at all and still got a B-. night class usually doesn't take the whole time and he gives you a 15 min break

My favorite professor this semester. I actually looked forward to this class. It is a lecture class though, so if you aren't the type of person who can sit and take notes for 2+ hours, then don't take this class. But he makes the time go by really fast and almost always lets us out early.

Watters is very helpful when you're having questions about tests. The class is not bad as long as you read what he tells you to and actually study. His tests are a combo of multiple choice and fill in the blank. Also, he tries to make the class interesting and you can tell that he genuinely loves what he's teaching.

Really good teacher. I took him for a night class and even though it is 3 hours long, he keeps it interesting and is really funny. If you show up to every class you get 10 extra credit points which is huge. The material is not hard, just a lot of memorization. EASY B, tough A but definitely doable. I highly recommend taking him for US history

He's a great guy, provides a lot of extra credit opportunities. He's funny but his class can become a little dull. I took his night class, and a three hour lecture can be very...long. But it is easy if you study. I was never a history person and this class is probably my favorite this semester.

Anyone who is saying that his class is "impossible" simply isn't trying. He's a great teacher, best history teacher I've ever had. He's funny and has some really cool stuff that he shares with the class. If you know how to take notes and study then you'll be fine. Definitely take him.
great guy. his class is long but he makes it very interesting. it's history so not the best stuff in the world. really nice guy. talk with him

He lectured for a straight 2:15 hrs.  We were given barely any text to look from that we actually used.  I recorded each lecture and typed out my notes twice after every class, but still managed with a C.  I am a nursing student and do know how to study for hard classes.  His office hours were VERY limited as he is a high school teacher as well.
great teacher, really funny. makes class interesting. talks pretty fast, and tests are tricky, but well worth it

Quizzes are based on lecture notes, gives you a review for your test, which you fill out based off your notes and some reading from the books. Kinda funny, and nice guy. Get extra credit for making every class

If you have a chance to take Dr. Watters it is well worth your time! He is the best professor I have EVER had. He is extremely helpful, and does not make you waste your time reading the book. Rather, he actually TEACHES. Go figure. He is funny and keeps your attention through the entire class. He is nice and is extremely helpful.BEST PROFESSOR EVER

1877 to present:  IMPOSSIBLE. I had to take this pass fail.  Doesn't use the book. All from lectures. I am taking WAY harder classes....but somehow this is my worst grade. DO NOT TAKE if you want a blow off class

1877 to Present...Mr. Watters is an amazing and funny professor.  He cares and tries his best to help out your grade.  Quizes are from lecture, so are test, but a little book thrown in.  It is an easy B, but A is not at all out of reach if you try.  Make yourself known.  Mr. Watters is my favorite teacher so far at TCU!
he rocks
He is an awesome teacher, and A MUST TAKE!  I got an easy A, just take the quizes(study), he will help you, and the test are easy, as long as you study, and he is funny and caring!

Though I did make a D+, that was because I failed to attend class the first two weeks of school.  He made EVERY attempt to help me excel! He is an excellent professor who gets to know you personally.  He knows everyone's name and makes the class fun and entertaining.  This is a must-take class for everyone...he's one of the good ones here at TCU.

Take notes, read your reading assignments, you will pass.  There are weekly quizzes that you won't pass if you don't study.  Dr. Watters is always helpful and will repeat something if you ask him during lecture.  He keeps things light and fun.  I highly recommend.
He is a pretty hilarious guy. Just take notes and study for the quizes very week and you will be fine. If I needed another history credit I would take his class again!

Pretty nice guy, if you talk to him he will basically do anything to help you.  Tests are pretty hard and require you to memorize a bunch of stuff.  Overall i would say he is an easy B and a somewhat challenging A.  Definetely recommend taking him.

Not an easy A, but an easy B. Go to class.  Quizes every night and takes attendance. Remembers faces and names, so he will notice if you are not there. Males the night class interesting and go by quickly. If you attend every class, 10 bonus points. If not interested in Histor, but must take it for UCR, and don't mind a night class, take him.

Go to class because he offers lots of extra credit. study for the quizzes. he gives a good review sheet for the tests. he's an awesome guy so get to know him, he knows lots about history just be ready to take over 2 and a half hours of notes with one break

One hell of a teacher. I would take him again if I could. Study for the quizzes and the tests will be easy. Very funny and keeps you focused on what he has to say. Easy A If you go to class and read the assignments.

Wild Wild Wess is one of the coolest teachers in TCU. Every night class he says: Don't worry will be done by 12. Nice guy. Not an easy but also not a difficult A. For all the tests I studied the night before and I got A at the end of the class. Quizzes - very helpful. take good notes

he is funny, very entertaining!! you have quizzes every (night) class - they are easy though. be prepared to dedicate a significant amount of time for an A, it is not an "easy A." You need to take notes like crazy. Average class over all. He will remember 50 people's names in 1 class, seriously, I am not joking.

If you don't mind night classes his is definitely the one to take. The class goes fast (lots of notes); however, if you pay attention an A is definitely possible. There is a daily quiz but it will only help your grade (they are very easy). He is very funny and makes class interesting.

He talks REALLY fast as if we knew everything. You have to write at least 6 pages of notes every class. He is not helpful since he doesn't reply emails. Easy C! Quizzes all weeks. DO NOT recommend to take this class!
I had him in high school, he is one of my all time favorite teachers. He is funny, and interesting. I highly suggest him he is engaging and will make whatever he is teaching interesting.
This is definitely the person to take if you don't mind having a night class.  He makes the material interesting.

Seriously, this is the guy you wanna take. Very funny and nice, looks and acts exactly like conan obrien. Loves to teach and does as much as he can to help your grade with extra credit, but it's an easy class anyways. Very fair and understanding too.
Interesting, knows a lot of little things here and there to add to the coursework. Bunches of chances to keep a good grade. Good lecturer. Likes kids, likes to teach.

The class was ok. He's a funny guy, very nice and friendly. He gives the worst notes though...you have to be able to write fast to keep up! The tests were ridiculous...the quizzes were what saved me. Prepare to take insane amounts of notes!

I had this guy in Highschool , he one of the best teachers I have had in my life. Funny Guy, really smart, and cuts out the BS work. ( loves teaching so much, that he has a Ph.D and still teaches highschool kids, also reason why he teaches at night.)

Tells good jokes. Really likes history and makes it clear what is going on. Be ready to take notes like your life depends on it, because your grade does. I thought the tests were pretty hard, but maybe thats just me.

VERY nice guy, clear and always ready to help, makes you want to learn! Many quizes, but not very hard, just study the notes with the small details. Gives good study gides. Many extra credits. You can easily make an A if you study. rally fun class.
Really enjoyed his class, just read and study for the tests and they aren't too bad.  He gives extra credit!  Study for weekly quizzes.  Very Funny.

He definitely makes this night class worth taking! I would recommend this class. He makes the class fairly entertaining for History. There is a quiz each class, but they count as a third test grade which helps you out. He talks fast, so be ready to write!
He is so awesome! I love him! His tests are very straight forward and he offers extra credit!
Is a very interesting teacher who makes you want to learn
Great teacher. Very easy class. I think that's how he wants it to be. Take as a night to pad your GPA.
GREAT CLASS!! I LOVE HIM!!!

He is such a funny guy! Always is making jokes about college kids drinking and such. Quiz for each class (once a week/night class) but they are not hard if you look over the notes before. He will help your grade out if he knows you tried! TAKE HIM!!
Very funny-makes night class worth taking.  You take notes all class, and have a quiz each class.  Study the notes for insignificant details and you will make an A!

The material for world music is amazing, and the lectures and passion Dr Watkins has is amazing to have in the som. That being said, this class is seen as a rite of passage due to how difficult some students find it, and the amount of work it takes to get through.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: A significant portion of your grade is determined by attendance. He accepts virtually no excused absences, and being tardy will earn you a 50% grade for the day. He's very passionate about what he teaches, which makes lectures interesting, but you're expected to study at least 6 hrs a week, and as if music history is your major.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The amount of hours I spent filling out all the scoresheets for the listening is insane. He gives way too much homework, tests are super hard, and the final is cumulative. Do the extra credit! Worst professor I have ever had, I don't like his teaching style. I thought I hated math so much, scratch that, this was even worse.
Dr watkins is straight the most evil professor in the music programs at tcu.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer, people complain about having to read textbooks. If you read and participate in class you'll most likely retain what you need to pass the tests. I never studied much for tests and passed with a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is easily the worst thing about the TCU school of music. Hardest class I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Agree with the other reviews of him being a poor professor. I think he is one of the worst things about TCU, and the School of Music.

Don't take Survey of World Music w/ Watkins unless you have some musical knowledge.  He expects you to read everyday, grades on participation daily, and the tests require a lot of studying.  Impossible to have phone out or even relax in class, you've gotta be on your toes the whole class or he will get mad at you or you will not do well in the clas
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Didn't have enough room to mention that he said I could make up the 0 I got for staying home (because I couldn't eat without throwing up from the Flu) by getting a 150 for outstanding participation. Unless you literally FIGHT to ask questions during class, getting that 150 is very difficult - just like every other aspect of his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I tested positive for Flu one day & had a doctor's note to stay home. He takes daily grades for participation & gave me a 0 despite me emailing him my note & asking for a virtual attendance option. There are NO excused absences in his class. If you take him, get a hardcover textbook. You'll need a copy, & he doesn't like people taking online notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Watkins can be entertaining, but you will not do well unless you have a music background even though he thinks it's very accessible. His tests are very music-theory based, and he is one of the most condescending professors I've ever had. Talks a lot about his own talents and repeatedly says that he expects students to study 9+ hours for class.

This professor seems to take pride in the fact that most students fail his class. The amount of homework is completely unreasonable (3+ hours every night). Thinks his class is God's gift to mankind. Honestly, I can't say anything bad enough to fully describe the hell that is Watkins' class. Avoid this professor at all costs

A Timothy Watkins survival guide: 1) Read the book. His lectures repeat the content, but his pop quizzes are from the reading you were supposed to do. 2) Write essays as plainly as possible. He dislikes superfluous words. 3) Build a rapport with him by speaking in class. He appreciates participation, and it boosts your grade by a lot over time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Watkins is an enthusiastic and dedicated teacher, but in order to be successful you must reciprocate this enthusiasm. Participate in class, pay attention, and occasionally go the extra mile! I found the class to be more interesting when I arrived prepared and read into the material beyond just the textbook. HIGHLY RECOMMEND TAKING THIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Spent more time in his class than my other 4 combined, still got a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't let the most recent rating fool you. This man is terrible. He seems to enjoy watching his students struggle and fail. He finds things to criticize and mark down for.  I know of numerous people that have had to retake his class 2 or even 3 times. That is ridiculous!  He belittles people to coax his own ego. Must be a very unhappy person.

One of my favorite classes of the semester. All you have to do is read and listen. You should DEFINITELY get the CD set that goes with the course. You're going to be lost if you don't have it. Be engaged in class and show some interest, and Dr. Watkins will have your back.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Watkins class was easily that hardest class I've ever taken. He is really passionate, but doesn't really cater to the needs of the student. In one semester, I had 6 papers, 2 tests, and a final. If you are not good with music, beware - this class will kill you. He gives pop quizzes and takes daily participation which makes getting an A hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: If he isn't considered to be the worst person within the TCU School of Music Faculty, he is certainly trying to be that person. This guy is really passionate and learned about Music History but is also a complete self-centered tool. Oh yeah, and he's a pretty terrible teacher at that. If only there was a bigger character limit for this.

Would never take this professor's class again. He does not care about student learning. Even though he claims to not care about grades, he takes the opportunity to deduct points anywhere and everywhere he can, regardless of whether it is within the scope of the class.  He takes pride in having the hardest class in our degree plan and offers no help

Do not take this class. Avoid at all cost. This teacher is cynical, sarcastic, condescending and self-absorbed. He does play favorites and he will belittle you in every way possible if he doesn't like you. He will make you suffer through the course because he feels righteous to do so. His rating at TCU and back in Rhodes college says a lot...
Don't take him.  He always tells his students to study the key concepts, but his tests cover the most random, unimportant facts found in the book.  Good luck if you take him because you'll need it.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. If you enjoy music at all, don't bother taking this class. Watkins is not a nice person nor is he a good teacher. His tests are hard, and even for an honors class his essays are impossible to do well on. If you go in to see him for feedback he is condescending and rude, not to mention he won't let you get a word in edge wise

He's a nice guy, very funny. The subject requires a lot of study, but he gives out good study guides. READ THE ASSIGNMENTS, he makes pop quizzes on them and they help you know what's going on during the lecture.
Very broad in explaining things, final was difficult, just not the class to take if you need a fine arts

Honestly he's "OKAY" I had him for World Music and after not doing so well on my second exam he talked with me and helped me with what I needed to work on. He's a little picky on papers but he doesn't grade very hard. Overall he's AIGHT!

Incredibly difficult essays for his Honors class, particularly at the beginning. Also, get ready to be responsible, because the due dates are nowhere except on the syllabus. If you need an Honors class, avoid this one if you can. Two thumbs down.

Interesting Professor, but the class is either a hit or miss in understanding what he is talking about. I would suggest a taking a different class if possible. The tests are VERY HARD, and he does not give out easy grades. You better have a great understanding of the world and of cultures around the world to do well in this class. Good luck!

This guy is complete trash. He expects you to know everything and does not cut anyone slack. Tons of reading and every class mandatory. He even took off points for me missing class because I had a funeral to go to, and those six points made the difference for my grade. DO NOT TAKE HIM, HE IS TERRIBLE

Watkins takes this way too seriously and has no sympathy. for one of his assignments my computers internet crashed and i couldn't submit it to e-college. I told him my situation and he basically told me to there was nothing he could do.
stay away, class is to hard for a fine arts class. way to into himself in his opinions about the music. not that hard to get a B but its miserable

I actually really really liked this class! It is a tough class but if you study regularly and keep up with the material you can definitly get a high B if not an A. The class is very interesting, especially if you love listing to differnt kinds of music. Watkins is VERY helpful outside of class if you ever feel lost. Don't be afraid to ask for help.

I loved Dr. Watkins. He's funny and entertaining and knows what he's talking about. Plus, he reminds me of the little short guy on Princess Bride. The class is not easy, even though I have an extensive music background. You have to work if you want to make a good grade, but it is definitely attainable. Having a music background is a great help.

He teaches over interesting subject material, but can at times be illogical and fixed in his views. The class was more difficult than I expected from a class that exists primarily to fulfill a core requirement, and was the hardest class I've taken outside my major.
ive never taken music before and i loved this class. it was really interesting and super easy to get an A. just talk to watkins a lot and show interest in the things he does and he'll love you.

If music isn't your thing, BY NO MEANS will you sail through. If you dont spend at least 2 hours preparing for each class, you'll have no idea whats going on, and the notes on the slides he puts up are close to useless. He's not very easy to talk to...I felt like he would judge if  I asked for help. Just find another class that covers this category

simply the worst. this class has been the least favorite part of my day for the past semester. watkins doesn't know what he's talking about (he teaches STRAIGHT out of the book) and revels in making his students feel like idiots for asking questions. i wouldn't wish this class on my worst enemy.

This was by far the worst Professor I've ever had. I have played music for 18 years of my life. The tests were way too thorough over all the information in the book. He taught the freshman level class as if we we were seniors. Didn't reply to any emails! Doesn't let you turn in work early. Doesn't accept late work "unless your dead" Worst Professor

Dr. Watkins is actually my least favorite teacher I've ever had. He's super full of himself and loves to obsess over tiny, insignificant details that make him seem smart. He's nice enough, but he's just ridiculous. Such a ding bat.

Lots of info to know.  It's really interesting, but it's so much to remember.  The tests are really hard and attendance is mandatory for your class participation grade.  Basically, if you have a lot of time, it's okay to take the class.

class is hard if you aren't musically inclined. you have to listen to songs on your tests and be able to identify elements and instruments and composures. test include way too much information and too detailed. he requires you to draw conclusion that he thinks are logical but really are far reaching and stretched. hated this class!

He puts plenty of information on his tests. He teaches as though it is junior or senior level course when it is and entry level freshman. He uses paragraphs on his slides instead of short sentences which makes it difficult to take notes.
Really fun class. Good for core, musical backgrounds help a lot. Online quizzes are really good review for his tests. His test cover everything in lecture. You should take this class.
Good guy, alright class too. Having some music in your background helps a lot. Easy B, will make you work for an A. But not too hard. Do the online assignments and you will do well.

Mrs. Walder has to be the best professor I've taken. She I would throw in personal details from her career at the FBI and CIA into the lectures and made the class so much fun. It was one of the few classes I really looked forward to each week. She is amazing and I couldn't reccomend her more. 3 tests and a final with a few easy assignments.

Most interesting professor I've had. Absolutely loved her class and she makes class super interesting and fun. Not sure why people say she is rude; she is one of the most caring professors I've had. Can't recommend enough.

Great person and great lecturer, made the class interesting. Test are web cam which for a non criminal justice major sucked. Final exam was web cam as well and 1 page open note, but she gave no info on what to put down or what was even going to be on the test, so I struggled studying for it. Wouldn't recommend for someone doing the intro class.

She really cares about all her students and does her very best to get to know every person by name. She loves questions, as she used to work as a CIA agent and an FBI agent, so she loves it when people are actually curious about that. No question is a dumb question! Also, she like a very caring figure, which is special as a teacher, I think.

One of the best professors I have had. She has an interesting background and provides unique perspectives about past and current events. Lectures are engaging, exams are mostly lecture-based, but read the textbook too. There are multiple minor assignments, which are interesting and will help your grade.

Very interesting class that is not too difficult at all. She talks about current events a good amount which keeps the class engaging. She also has incredible experience being in the FBI and CIA. Would definitely recommend for CSV credit.

I heard such good things about her before, and she is a super interesting lecturer bc of her experience, but she can be rude at times. The class is pretty easy but she's a bit disorganized bc she has other jobs besides teaching. Maybe take someone else if you can, but if not it's not a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not sure about Professor Walder, I had heard great things prior to taking her class. She as a unique background which makes for interesting stories, but she was often disrespectful to students during class. Class is straightforward and not difficult. I would look for better professor.
