Tests are T/F, MC, and short answer and cover a lot of material. Tests are out of the textbook primarily but she has never read it. She should not teach intro courses.

Channel Planning with Macias was great! She's very helpful and likes to interact with students. Her tests are not hard and an A is definitely attainable if you stick with the HW, attend class, and stay on top of the group project. I'd take her over Bright.

You have the ability to learn a lot in this class, especially if you really are going to go into the advertising or public relations field. Keep up with attendance, the readings, and homework because they help your grade. Get started on the group project early in the semester or else you will regret it!
Hes the GOAT.

For AIS, he's a really nice teacher and is always willing to help students with questions or concerns. The exams are quite challenging, as the class averages are typically around 75 with a curve. Definitely need to put in a good chunk of time.

This guy hates his job. Had him for FR2. He is so unorganized and was never prepared for class. You do practice problems the whole class. The material isn't that difficult, he just doesn't explain anything because he is too lazy to. He also did not respond to any of my emails when I tried to get in contact with him.

What Professor Wills teaches wasn't hard, but he'd test things that he never taught. He didn't seem to enjoy his job much or think what he taught was very useful. He often told us not to spend too much time on his course, but if you didn't, you'd freak out at the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy to talk to, but he barely explained concepts and mostly went through practice questions during classes, which can be confusing for people with no accounting basics. The quizzes and exams were way harder than the practice questions in class, so getting fluent with all practice questions won't do any help. Avoid at all cost!
Great guy, manageable class! Everything was covered in class for exams and you can practice as much as needed to do well. Would recommend him for AIS.

Genuinely cares about students and funny. Took him for AIS. Show up to class to learn the applications. He adjusts the class based on everyone's progress. Written portions of the test are more difficult but the application part is worth more and gives you practice exams. I believe he is less vocab heavy than Olvera. An A is definitely achievable.

If you have any other option, avoid him. He is a genuinely nice guy, but his class was extremely confusing and unorganized. I have gotten A's in all other accounting courses, but his tests were so hard I got D's and C's. He did round our final grades, with him giving me a B instead of a C, but I know I would've done better in another class.

By far the best choice for FR1. The material and exams are hard, but he does not want to fail anyone. He truly cares about all of his students, so as long as you go to his office hours and show you are putting in effort, you will most likely get a good grade. One of my favorite professors

He is a nice person but a bad professor. He is impossible to reach outside of class. Class is not organized or engaging which makes it hard to focus. Exams are very challenging, but he ends up heavily curving because the whole class does poorly. Despite little mastery of concepts, you may end up with an A or B if that's what you want.

Professor Wills' class is not easy. He test hard and his lectures can be confusing, but he is one of the most caring teachers I've had TCU. He worked very hard to accommodate all students, especially due to COVID. He was very generous in giving points back on exams and quizzes. You will be challenged, but Wills is worth it.

This class is hard regardless of the professor that teaches it. Having said that Dr. Wills is by far the better professor to teach this class out of his peers. The test are very hard and I would suggest running through the work though problems very thoroughly before the tests. He makes it to where you will make a B in the class at minium.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: nice guy but extremely hard tests, you cant find on google either Questions are from Gleim CPA test prep questions that are expensive to buy. Use his office hours for best chance and even can help on a curve. Hard to follow along during LEC and goes off in a tangent. Class is made to average a B. so take it on your final year. can affect GPA
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Wills is one of the most loved accounting professors at tcu. He is hilarious and very accommodating. If he likes you, he will definitely help you out a ton. His classes are usually very exam heavy and he pretty much lectures the entire time. Not the easiest teacher to understand but he is responsive to emails and will chat after class. awesome prof

Really nice dude and means well. He never actually taught anything as class consisted of him running through practice problems, with maybe 5 minutes per class spent on overview. Test questions were way harder than the questions we went over in class. Wouldn't suggest taking his class unless you feel like you already understand accounting well.

Really nice person. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He will always try to challenge you, and his test is tough. But he will try his best not to fail you, finding a best way working for everyone.

Super chill guy, wants to challenge you but nothing you haven't learned. He doesn't teach from the book, he just gives you a bunch of example packets and you go through those in class while he teaches the material. This can be frustrating sometimes but when content got harder he gave us step-by-step handouts. Only tested on in- class material
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Wills was the most laid back, common sensical professor I've ever had. He wants you to succeed. Very calm and relaxed class, would rather you come late than not come at all. Absolutely would take this guy again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He was nice and definitely cares for his students. BUT you have to read a ton of books and watch really long movies (on your own time). You also have to do a presentation. It is very discussion based. He does care if you don't go to class/are late. Tests where super hard to study for and you don't get much info on what will be on it.

There is so much homework in this class (Honors: The Afterlife of the Greek Tradition). There were times where we read and wrote a precis over a novel every week. Tests were vague and difficult to study for. No assignments were graded until the last week of school.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Look, he's really nice and you can tell he really cares about his students, but only take if you want to do a ton of reading and projects and write ups and so much stuff. There was a point where writhing two weeks I had a presentation, two books to read, and two write ups on each book. It's just a lot, and a lot more German focused than you'd think
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I absolutely love Dr. Williams. He's so kind and cares so much about his students. You can always come to him for help.
Scott is the boss! Take him its not hard and you learn a lot of material. Writing is easy because the essays are based on the readings.

Very interesting class about German lit. Would recommend to anyone looking for a lit or Hum. credit. There is a good bit of writing but its not difficult because the prompts give you a lot of freedom. lectures are interesting and make sure to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: While Dr. Williams is nice and cares about his students, his grading style and utter lack of any organization when it comes to following his syllabus and returning grades to students make this class unbearable for anyone who is not a native speaker or actually cares about their grade. Grades are subjective and won't be entered til after the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Overall really awesome teacher. Loves to speak in German and about Rome. Super passionate about the subject so everything he says in class is important. Only 2 tests but you just have to basically write what you know and if you take notes and study you can easily do well in this class. Have to read a good amount.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a great guy, but his lectures do not match up with his powerpoints. He gets point for kindness, but as far as a teacher, he is not the best. I would not recommend taking his Greek traditions class. AT ALL.

At least 7 novels and 5 films are read and watched respectively. You MUST read them and watch them to get a good grade. There are assignments associated with each one and there's a midterm and a final. 1 paper. He's a great guy who will work with you on any situation. I hated this class at first, and now it's my favorite and Williams is the best.

Pretty challenging class with tons of reading. Pulled some all-nighters. However, you'll learn lots, and he's a good teacher. Take notes, of course, but I managed to skim most of the books. STUDY for the tests. I got Bs on everything, but the As on the tests pulled my grade up to an A overall. Definitely doesn't hurt to be interested in the topic.

Williams is the best!! I've had him in German classes and Greek Traditions and he's absolutely great. All of his classes are a lot of work (reading & assignments) but worth it because class is so much fun. You learn a lot too and the tests aren't actually that bad, if you have been paying attention. I highly recommend him!

Herr Williams is super sweet and understanding. At first, it's hard to feel him out, because he wants to care about you but he has to get to know you first (read: you don't know if he likes you or not for a while, kinda awkward in a lang class). DO THE WORK and DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE HOW LONG IT TAKES!!

Best teacher I've had at TCU, and I mean that.  Great guy.  Sure he's not easy, but he teaches you a ton of stuff, even if you didn't have any prior interest.  Guy's a genius, and he really wants to help you learn.  Because he cares about you.  Not your typical history teacher.  Uses Germany to teach history across the ages.  TAKE THIS CLASS

Dr. Williams is a great professor, and I learned a lot from him in Roman Tradition.  His class has made me very interested in antiquity, and I really want to learn German now! He is willing to help and move due dates around to help the class.  I enjoyed all of the class readings and films, because they are ALL worth it!

Great guy.  Once I needed help with a book, and he took me and another student out to coffee.  Really smart, but also hard.  Had him for Roman history. Gave us, literally, the worst book I have ever read, "Across."  REALLY hard readings, but complements that with a lot of required, awesome videos.  It'll be a lot easier taking him the second time.

Great guy! He means well and will talk with you for however long you need if you are ever confused. Lectures are often drawn out (and about German culture/history!) but it is really not too hard of a class. I really enjoyed the creativity he lets us have on the papers.

This class is overwhelming at first. There are several novels and epic length movies to watch outside of class. Just about each novel has a specific summary with it. There are only 2 tests-midterm and final. Hard A (I worked for mine), easy B. Nice guy. Long, often boring, classes. I needed it for my Honors class, and I ended up not hating it.

Prof. Williams is an incredibly sweet person, he means well and tries to help you in any way he can. If you are not trying to learn the information it can feel like a VERY long class. He relates EVERYTHING back to German. And I mean EVERYTHING. His honors Roman Trad. class has a TON of reading and movies. You have to have patience w/him

Dr. Boyd is awesome. A great class to take for an honors class. You grade yourself on participation, and there are 5 self-reflections along with one presentation that you do with a partner. This class requires a lot of dialogue on tough topics. Loved this class!

Boyd does a great job talking about touchy topics. There are readings before class, journal entries, and video. You grade YOURSELF on participation but to do that you have to show up and talk at least once. There is a community project the last month so in class lectures end early. There is extra credit and def recommend for an CV honors class!

Dr. Boyd is kind of a tough grader and you need to really participate in her class to get an A. However, she is genuinely interested in making her students better people. College Life & Identity is an amazing class, and I recommend Dr. Boyd if you are going to take it.

As someone who worked with APD, Prof. White is knowledgeable on the subject. Lectures are heavy with information, but she tries to let you know the key facts. She used Cengage to make following course material outside of class easy, and it was efficient for studying. Tests are not the easiest but run on learning/memorizing the material.

I really like Jennifer White as a person, but I could do without this class. Most criminal justice classes are an easy A and it is possible in this class, but not the easiest. I ended up pass/no crediting this since 1 bad test sinks your grade. Overall, I wouldn't say don't take this class (it isn't bad at all), there are just way easier options.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor White is amazing. Her class is very doable. Gives many test hints during lecture, so attend class. If you don't attend, you will still do good in the class. Very minimal homework. The class is usually very late at night 6:30 to 9, but she makes lecture interesting.

Dr. White is a good teacher, and super understanding with her students. She gives test hints and questions in class, so wouldn't recommend skipping. Barely any homework and its easy points for your grade. She is super engaging, but definitely study for the tests and they're easy. Theres only 4 tests, multiple choice and some fill in the blanks.

Dr. White is a super understanding teacher. My method of studying for the class (exams were MC w some fill in the blanks) was using flashcards for terms which worked great. She will give hints about what will be on the exam and the class before the exam, she will give a handful of questions out. Easy homework points if you do chapter reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor White is the nicest lady ever. Criminal Justice with her is fun and she has experience in the field so she tells her stories. Her tests can be challenging but if you study the power points and study guides you will do good. Overall great professor and super nice. Would take her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall a very good professor. Go to class and listen closely. She gives a lot of direct test questions during lectures. It can get boring, but she does her best to make things interesting. Four exams and a discussion and short video assignment every week. Not a blow off. A lot of facts and dates to memorize but not impossible to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor White is SUPER sweet and caring. Despite this, her class is still really hard. She makes you work for an A, and I did not finish with a good grade. Tests are pretty hard. She's an ex cop so she's really engaging and interesting, but if you want an easier option, I would recommend taking one of the other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor White's class was very interesting and engaging. Some of the material is very boring but she knows it and makes those classes more fun. She encourages class discussions which makes the lectures less boring. The tests are not bad if you pay attention in class because she gives out hints of what is going to be on the test. Highly recommend

Perfection in a teacher and a class. actively engages you and challenges you to challenge her on anything and everything from lectures to tests. Defend you position well, and you may see yourself rewarded. The absolute best guest speaker of all time from Arlington Police. The hardest part is knowing case details. She loves her legal cases.

Taking a Thursday night class is not ideal, but White makes it so worth it! She is super caring and hilarious. Tests are not easy, but the information is right out of the lectures and textbook. As long as you go to class and read the book, you'll get an A. I'm not a criminal justice major but highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Passionate, intelligent, and caring. Tests are based on the textbook readings, so definitely keep up with readings. Her lectures are clear and precise and go over the main ideas of each chapter. Super approachable and wants you to pass. I loved all the examples she gave from when she was a police officer.

My favorite professor at TCU so far! She is an ex cop and very knowledgeable. The class is lecture heavy, but she makes it interesting and interactive. Expect to study the lectures and textbook a lot for the tests as they are very specific, but she often tells you what is important to know. Final is not cumulative. You are guaranteed 100% on hw.

Professor White is the best! Total of 4 exams and one police ride out short essay. Show up to take notes, and you'll def get a good grade. Her reviews are VERY INFORMATIONAL. Def would take her for any class!

First of all, this class is an easy A unless you are super lazy. All you have to do is to show up in class and take notes when she says important things that will appear in the test. The homework is online, easy and helpful for studying and a grade of 100 is certain. The lectures are very interesting and informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's a wonderful professor. Her class was a little tough but she made it interesting. I got sick during the semester and she was incredibly caring, understanding, and accommodating. She's an ex-cop and really knows her stuff.
Super interesting class about crime and justice. Knows what she's talking about, ex cop, very cool person. Memorization for tests, usually multiple choice, but interesting material so its not hard.

A very kind person and is very interested in what she does. Helpful when I emailed her with questions. However, this was the most rigorous child development course I've taken. Put in the work and make the changes she recommends in the papers, and you will do well. Interesting class! The TA was awful. The papers she graded were graded intensely.

This class is unbelievably hard for no reason. I have never had so many papers in my life & they are graded SO hard. This class consists of speaking in class, discussion posts, discussion reflection papers, group projects, presentations, observatory hours, & more. The information taught is useful to your future if you are wanting to work with kids.
Worst teacher at TCU. Do not recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! She requires insane amount of papers and no matter how good it is you will receive a C. The grading is extremely inconsistent and the feedback is super unhelpful. Worst class I have taken a TCU. Sounds easy, but not at all!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The course content is fascinating, but the atmosphere of class and the amount of homework soon knocked the enthusiasm out of me. Papers week after week and the expectations are unrealistically high--only way to get a good score is to do way more than she asks for. Lectures are long and slow, not much variety. My least favorite class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor White was my favorite teacher in Oswego.  She has a clear grading criteria that is organized and lenient.  White is extremely compassionate and I leave her class feeling refreshed and exited about the world. Definitely take her class if you are interested in PR!!!!!! There is not a bad thing I could say about her.
Great teacher! Very helpful and patient person. She would do everything in her power to help you succeed. Attendance is important and quizzes aren't that bad. Makes pediatrics fun.
As a lecture instructor she was great! I have really enjoyed this class. Exams aren't bad. Getting a "B" or an "A" with effort is very do-able. I loved her class!
Knows his stuff and students are very engaged.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Knows his stuff!  Hard but fair.

Evolution of the Blues was fun and interesting. Whillock knows his stuff and knows students have other classes besides his. We could turn stuff in days later and still receive full credit. Also, graded papers easy. Test were all essay, but he was pretty leaninent on the answers. Take him if you can.

History of Film was way too hard to be a 1000-level course. The grade is made up of 4-5 exams and 5 papers, so not much opportunity to do well unless you study a lot for the exams. You have to read the textbook to do well on exams and pay attention in class. Long notes and lectures. Interesting class and good professor though.

He is very difficult as a professor. He is a great individual and a good teacher. If it's possible I think he may be just too passionate about his subject. He will go on random rants about other things, and then come back to the topic at hand. His tests are way out of left field and questions very often just seem random.

This professor is extremely nice and an incredible person. However, his tests are amazingly difficult, and contacting this professor outside of class besides e-mail is more difficult than just dropping by. I love film and I loved going to this class, and learning the material. I still however made a D.

Whillock is a haus.  His lectures are interesting and humorous and he has great stories and film clips interspersed throughout the class to keep you entertained.  From what I've heard, he's way better than the other Intro to Film teacher.  The labs are worthwhile and he's very understanding about grades and accessible.

I really enjoyed his class (loved the labs too) and thought he was a fun professor, but his lectures were rather disjointed and all over the place, making it very hard to determine what will be on the test. Make certain you read and study the textbook, take good notes, and you should be okay.

Dr. Whillock loves to talk, about anything, even it if isn't going to be on the test. I got hardly anything out of his lectures and only memerized the information for the test and then forgot it. We got to watch some good movies in lab but that is about it. Don't take this class if you don't have to
He was a lot of fun in London! Many stories.

He is very passionate about what he teaches, albeit sometimes a little scattered. He knows his stuff, and he often assumes that we are just as coherant on the material. He is a good professor, though, and has a wierd attraction. I liked the class. READ!
Dr. Whillock is my idol! He's the real deal and has alot of fun teaching the class. Come to class and get all the notes and reviews and you'll be fine.
Dr. Whillock is the real thing...you want to learn film, he'll teach you that and more.

He gives out a list of names before each exam. Your grade is based solely on the 4 exams, no quizzes or papers. I had to take the class twice, but managed to get a B. Some extra credit is offered. Fun guy.

I'm not good at history, so the class was hard for me.  But Whillock was fun and I like the way he talks about the things he knows a lot about.  His handouts help A TON!  But you DO need to read from the book.
I don't care what anybody says this guy is the man!  He has so much excitment and knowlegdge when it comes to film.  He is unclear at times but he gives you a guide for his notes.  I loved the class!
He is a nice guy, and he tries to work with you. But, it is kinda a hard class overall. He is the best of the 3 into RTVF class teachers!
No Comments

Whillock is nice and all, but his lectures are hard to absorb, unless you're a hyper-fast writer. The only visual aides that he gives us are a typed outline of the day's lecture that has names on it and that's it- no powerpoints or anything.

Williams is the BEST. Super interesting class and not that hard. She also does a great job of connecting with the students. Classes are discussion based so participation and attendance are mandatory. I would definitely recommend taking Williams for any class!

One of the nicest, sweetest professors you will ever meet. She is so caring and very laidback, all you have to do is try in her class. Very participation focused, hardly any assignments, until the end which are mainly group projects.

Professor Williams is a kind and engaging instructor. The class relies heavily on participation and group work, but the manageable workload and interesting material make it a great experience. I found unstuck AI helpful for study prep.

Be prepared to discuss! Everyday is a discussion led by other classmates where participation is required for credit. There are papers at the end of the semester, but most of the work involves the weekly readings and huge presentation where you lead the class for a week. It wasn't my favorite, but Dr. Williams was very nice and understanding.

Taking Dr. Williams for Cultural, Literature, and Adaptations and it is one of my favorite honors courses! Dr. Williams is very kind and accommodating and the class is easy, use SparkNotes if you don't have time to read the novels. There are two major projects, a Discussion Facilitation and Research project, and a final. Easy A!
Dr. Williams is an incredible professor. She is kind and fair, always willing to accommodate her students. Take her if you can!
would recommend taking this class! loved it! it was fun/interesting, and I learned a lot

Wendy is amazing!!! I have taken her classes twice and she is my favorite professor at TCU. Her classes do require a lot of outside reading, which is annoying, but the books are good. Participation is very important in her class, and you do really have to read and contribute to the conversation using examples from the texts.
Dr. Williams is so kind and amazing. this is the best class I have ever taken. it changed my life
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Great professor.

Wendy Williams is the best. The class is usually discussion based and there are about two group projects that are not difficult. I have taken her twice and would be taking her again if I had the chance. She is a fair grader and loves her students. Attendance is mandatory, so if you want to skip a bunch this might not be the best class.

She is known for her exceptional teaching style and ability to convey material clearly. She employs a dynamic and engaging approach in the classroom, making complex topics more accessible and interesting. Her lectures are well-structured, which aids in providing a clear understanding of the subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Willams wants you to succeed. The class is reading heavy, as you read a 900 page novel, but you spend all semester reading it. I have learned so much and would take another one of her classes if I ever got the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Although the title of this course did not sound interesting to me in the slightest, this has been my favorite honors course I have taken by far. The book can sound daunting however split up over the course of the semester it is not bad at alI. I never dreaded going to this class; Wendy is an awesome professor. Take any class you can get with her!

The syllabus makes this class seem like a hard class because 30% was participation but trust me, just show you pay attention and participate in the discussion, you will get an A. It's not hard to discuss because we just read a book and talk about it. The book's great and she's also a easy grader. Totally love her. Would definitely take her again!
Dr. Williams, by far, is the best Professor of Gender&History I have ever had. She is great!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Williams is one of the best professors I have ever had at TCU. From day 1, she makes it her goal to make each student feel accepted and like their opinion matters. Her discussions are so interesting and made a class I thought was going to be boring and long a class that was engaging and exciting. There are 2 big projects, but she grades easy.

100% recommend the class. class was easy, it was very relaxing, and nice to have an easy class. class was never too stressful. 2 big project grades, but they are easy, she grades easy, and grading criteria is very Clear. participation is easy. allowed to miss 2 classes with no penalty.

Professor Williams is one of the best teachers I have taken here at TCU. She offers amazing feedback and is always willing to listen to your feedback, no matter the issue. She is super reasonable and this can be seen as super easy for many!

Dr. Williams is a great professor! She genuinely takes interest in her students and cares for them. I feel like half the class was taught by her, and the other half was learning by group projects, so if you like group projects, then you would enjoy this class. Participation is important as well too! I would definitely recommend Dr. Williams!

Dr. Williams is a great teacher of mindfulness to college students! I learned so much about mindfulness and its effect on our lives and how to implement it! I loved this class and found it very interesting and Dr. Williams was an excellent teacher. not to mention an easy grader and the work load was not bad at all for an honors class.
Dr. Williams is an amazing professor. She grades very fairly and gives good feedback on all your assignments. She makes everything easy to follow and makes the class fun at the same time.

Mindfulness with Williams is the best!! If you have the chance to take her, do it- you will not regret it!
She is amazing at creating a safe class environment where students feel comfortable being vulnerable and discussing hard things. I was always excited to come to her class despite being in 18 hours this semester, and that says a lot!

Professor Williams is one of my favorite professors! I was wary going into her mindfulness class, but ended up learning a ton. The course load is extremely manageable (not a ton of hw, mainly a chapter or so of reading). The class is heavily discussion based, but Wendy creates a comfortable atmosphere that makes speaking up easy to achieve.

Dr. Williams is a super knowledgeable and caring professor that will foster a respectful and caring environment. The class is largely discussion based (duh, its an honors class) with a couple of group projects and individual assignments and readings. Participation is key, show up everyday and contribute and you will be fine.
She's amazing. Take her if you can. She's one of the kindest professors at TCU and is just beyond understanding. I promise you won't regret taking her!

Professor Williams is great! I had Mindfulness with her and learned a lot. The class was really easy. If you show up, participate in lectures, and do the reading, you'll be able to fly through it easily. Honestly, it didn't feel like much of an honors class besides the quality of the other student's work. The class is mostly student taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor who cares about her students and creates a very warm and welcoming class environment. Very understanding- She will always be there if you need anything

Dr. Williams is one of the best professors I've had at TCU. Classes are so engaging and there is barely homework- just a few small readings. One group presentation and small research project, but really not that much and they are graded so fairly. She is such a kind and inspirational individual as well that going to class is super enjoyable

Dr. Williams was such a great professor! Mindfulness wasn't a difficult course, but I definitely learned a lot and I am really glad I took the class. It is not difficult to get an A but you do need to come to class and participate!

I love Dr. Williams! She is an amazing professor and person! You will not regret taking her class. The topics discussed in class were so interesting and relevant. Enjoyed going to class and learning something new. Highly recommend.

Wendy is a fantastic educator and a caring person who makes an effort to connect with each of her students individually. This is a class that I already knew I would enjoy, but she really did everything she could to make the class as stress-free and conducive to real discussion and learning as possible.

I took this class because I had no other options for the credit I needed and was very worried going in. However, the class ended up being the best honors class I had taken. Class is very interesting and is discussion based so if you participate, you will have a good grade.

Dr. Williams is one of the best professors at TCU. She is so welcoming and made class so fun. Class consists of 2 easy presentations and participation in class (but it is super easy to get). She is a pretty easy grader and it is very doable to get an A in this class. Come to class prepared knowing what happened in the book. Take this class!!!!!

Being scared to speak in socratic seminars, I became more comfortable to talk because of Wendy. She made class so fun and was an easy grader. She answers quickly on emails and cares more about your mental health compared to your grade. I absolutely loved Wendy and I totally recommend taking this class.

Dr. Williams is a very caring professor! She is always happy to help you with any problem you have. She wants to make sure you are not feeling too stressed in her class. There is reading- we read Middlemarch, which w so it is a bit of a hard read if you are not an avid reader. However, the discussions in class made it a fun read.

reviews.comment: Wendy is the most passionate and encouraging teacher ever

reviews.comment: Absolutely the best of the best if I can find another class to take with Dr. Williams I will. The only thing is for this class it's fairly large reading requirement.

reviews.comment: She is truly passionate about what she is teaching and her students. Never worried about my grade because she will work with you to make sure you succeed. Listens to her students and adapts. Highly highly recommend!
Best professor. Very intentional with her students. She is very flexible with each individual. Participation is graded but over the semester you will become more comfortable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is the best!! Most caring and empathic person. She wants you to suceed!

Great professor!! So understanding!!! The class required quite a lot of reading (entire book over 12-14 weeks) plus presentations, and research papers. Amazing student-led class, that gives quick feedback! Easy to improve your grade!! Best professor at TCU!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: She was amazing! Easy to access outside of the classroom! Great time and would definitely take again!

Dr. Williams' Mindfulness should 1000% become a core class. She helps you learn many techniques for all aspects of life and encourages you to use them when possible. There are a few group projects and the reading can be a bit dense, but overall the class is not super difficult. She also encourages you to reach out if you have questions or concerns.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Wendy is the best professor I have ever had! I took her class "Mindfulness for College Students." She is honestly the most caring and positive person I have every met. I wish she could teach every single class I take because she is so awesome. This class was mentally challenging but not super hard. It challenged me to better myself! LOVE HER!!!!

One of the most caring, empathetic professors I've ever had at TCU. Highly recommend taking any of Dr. Williams' classes. Her mindfulness course was super engaging and interesting. Good balance of group and individual projects.
If you take a class with her, it is an honor to learn from the best! She is so kind and her smile lights up a room. I can not get over how much her class has transformed me.

Dr. Williams is by far the best professor I've had at TCU, and her Culture, Literature, and Adaptations course was one of my favorites that I've taken. The final grade is based entirely on class participation and 2 projects, which keeps you engaged without feeling suffocated by work. It is a lot of reading to keep up with, but worth it!

I loved Wendy!!! So kind and caring for all her students! She is so passionate about her class and is willing to help anyone who needs anything. Gives great feedback and really wants you to succeed in class. She makes her classes super fun and engaging and it is always fun going to class.

Dr. Williams is a great professor! This class requires hard work but she makes it interesting and enjoyable. In this class, you read three books, give three presentations, and write a final research paper.

Dr. Williams is a great professor. She really cares about her students and is very accessible in and out of class. There is a lot of reading for this class, but the class is completely discussion-based with a few projects/papers. Expect to put work into the class, but if you do the work you will be fine. Highly recommend!!
This class was great. I never thought coming in to this class that I would be interested in a class about the Victorian era of England, but Dr. Williams helped change my mind.

I wasn't interested in the Victorian period before, but thanks to Dr. Williams' teaching on this period, I have gained so much interest in it. Dr. Williams is so supportive, so if you take everything seriously in this class and work for it, you'll achieve the grade you want easily.

Dr. Williams is a gem, best professor I've had at TCU. She cares a lot about her students and doesn't try and push any sort of agenda or bias. I took CLA, 5 total papers, a group project, and participation are all that is required. You can make an A without reading any of the books using sparknotes. Would definitely take another one of her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: The best professor at TCU by far. She is caring and so sweet. I will definitely be taking one of her classes again. There was a substantial amount of reading outside of class, but as long as you participate, you will get the grade you want. She is an amazing woman who I will stay in contact with even after graduation.
Dr. Williams is incredible! She creates a wonderful environment in the classroom that truly brings out the best in each student. She is kind and approachable. Wish I could take her again!
Absolutely fantastic and flexible!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very caring person, don't stress about grades, as long as you do the work she will take care of you. Assignments and grading are extremely flexible if y'all ask her. Be prepared to write. Would highly recommend

She is the best prof at TCU. She is so incredibly kind. Empathy has been the best class I have taken at TCU, I wish I had the chance to take more of Wendy William's classes. You learn so much and she challenges you in a way that is beneficial. Also, don't stress about your grade, you just need to try your best.

Dr. Williams is EASILY my favorite professor at TCU. I've take n 2 classes with her, and both have been my favorites at TCU. She gives great feedback to her students, and she genuinely cares about her students and wants them to be the best they can be. Some assignments were due back to back, but they are do-able! BEST professor- I adore her!

Dr. Williams is awesome! She is so friendly, truly cares about her students, and is very approachable. Classes are discussion-based so attendance and participation are important. There are about 5-6 assignments; however, they are thought provoking and you get an A on them if you try.

She is extremely nice and wants the best for everyone! This class makes you learn a lot and so much more rewarding than the usual class at TCU. This is one of my favorite teachers I have had thus far and I highly recommend.
Great professor, cares about your learning and the subject. Awesome Honors class. Pretty stress-free also
Cares a lot about her students. Group projects are a major part. Must participate to get a good grade. A lot of outside of the class work Overall would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is extremely easy. You watch a lot of ted talks and talk about them together. It's really about learning and not about performance or grades. Dr. Williams cares about her students and is super flexible. Recommended if you need something not very time consuming but that will make you think.

Dr. Williams is such an awesome professor - she listens to what you want to get out of the class and you can change the syllabus depending on needs of the class. She truly cares about the class and what you will get out of it!

Dr. Williams is great, she really cares about her students. I took her Nature of Value- Empathy course and I learned a lot and actually really enjoyed the class. Make sure to prepare before class and participate during the discussion. Highly recommend!

Definitely cares about her students and their growth. Class covers relevant topics and the classroom environment is engaging. Lots of reading for homework but it's fairly interesting. Few small presentations, but grades are mostly based on daily, self-graded participation. Fairly easy, but interesting cultural visions class. Would recommend.

She is a true gem. She cares about her students both in and out of the classroom and wants them to succeed. Classes are a lot of work, yes, but if you take them seriously you will get a lot out of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I absolutely adored this class! It is a lot of outside work, but the in-class work is rather light. There are 12 hours of required service learning and approximately 10 hours of other assignments (where you have to go to events). Other than that, you just need to be able to contribute to discussion in class. 70% of the course is completion.

Wendy Williams is one of the kindest professors I have ever had. And she is very knowledgeable about all things empathy-related. There is a fair amount of work outside of class, so you need to be committed to the class, but she is not a tough grader, and the work is definitely doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took her Nature of Values: Empathy class, and while there is reading for class and outside projects, her class helps you grow as a person and go beyond an ordinary class for a grade. If you do all the readings and the outside activities, an A is virtually guaranteed. 100% would take her class again.

Really powerful class. The class structure is heavy on outside of class work which makes it somewhat time consuming. Class engagement and participation in discussions was very important. Most of the grading is if you do it, you receive 100% so nearly impossible to get a bad grade

Wendy Williams is one of my favorite professors I have ever had at TCU. She cares deeply about her students and is there for you if you need anything, whether its class related or not. Her classes require a lot of outside work but aren't necessarily HARD.

Wendy Williams is truly one of the best people I've met at TCU and am so glad I could have her before I graduated. She is so nice and caring, just wants the best for all of the students. There is a decent amount of work outside of class but it is worth it in the end. Do the work and you'll learn a lot. Highly recommend!

While this is an Honors class and there is often a fair amount of homework/off campus assignments, the content of the class and how Dr. Williams conducts it makes up for that. She establishes a mutual respect during the very first day of class, and the class discussions are sometimes life-changing (in a good way).
Wendy was awesome! She's super sweet and genuinely cares about all her students well being. There's a lot of reading but manageable. Overall amazing human!
One of the best professors at TCU.

I took Cultural Literature and Adaptations with Dr. Williams and it was a great class! I really enjoyed the class. The novels we read and the discussion were really interesting and I'm glad I took it. Make sure you have a good group for the discussion facilitation and participate in class discussion and you'll do great!
I really loved Dr. Williams! She is engaging and accessible outside of class, and the course is a very fair level of difficulty. Would gladly take another class with her!

Dr. Williams is an amazing professor. She really cares about her students and the class and makes the course enjoyable. The class is very discussion based and she allows the students to lead the discussions. You must read 4 novels in the class however they are pretty good stories that are easy to follow along with. I would 100% recommend this class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Take Dr. Williams!!! She's the best :)

She wants you to succeed in class and will give you as much help as you need. She is always available and runs her class well. She is clear on her grading criteria. The books we read were interesting and we also got to watch the film adaptations and compare them. You definitely need to go to class, but she makes it worth it.

reviews.comment: Highly recommend Professor Williams, she is very kind and lets you create a large part of the class for yourself.

honestly wendy is amazing. very respected, encouraging, and supportive as a professor. would not want to take an honors class with anyone else. make sure that you read the material and are ready to participate, because that's a big part of your grade. attend class, read, participate, and you'll do fine.

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! Caring and designs class for the students. Participation is necessary for a good grade-come prepared to share. I appreciate the class because she will never let you do busy work. This meant all the work was meaningful. If you are a self-motivated learner with initiative, you will appreciate Dr. Williams and her courses.

This class is very beneficial for anyone in any department considering departmental honors. This class is self-graded and you really get out what you put in! There are 5 major assignments, but they can be adjusted to fit your major or research needs. Dr. Williams is a great mentor and keeps you accountable in pursuing honors research.

She cares about students but not enough to lead the classroom. We kind of teach ourselves with her guidance. Too many guest speakers and service learning projects and I don't get the sense that she understands the community she is sending us to or the leaders she wants us to work with. People like her because she is nice. But I wanted to be taught
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I took empathy with Wendy and had a great experience. Grades consisted of self graded participation, a service learning project, a group presentation, attending outside events, and a research paper. Mostly completion grades. Wendy is an inspiration, and I would take her class for no other reason than to build a relationship with her.

Honors Empathy Colloquial- Service learning based class. Very interesting way of learning by reaching out to the community in Fort Worth. No tests or quizzes. Research project on anything related to empathy (ideally, as it relates to your future career goals) and a service learning paper and group project.

Honors Gender Colloquia: This class has by far been one of my favorite classes at TCU! Class meets once a week for 2 hours, and class is only discussion/project based so you don't have to worry about tests. Dr. Williams is also really understanding and is always available for office hours to talk about your grade or even just about life.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honors Gender Colloquial- Wendy is amazing. The course will broaden your view and understanding of all things related to gender. Touches on femininity as well as masculinity- aka does not ignore the male aspects of gender issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is very informative and makes you think about topics. Each week some articles or videos are assigned to be prepared for class, and they are helpful and not "busy work."
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honors Colloquia- Gender. LOVED taking her gender class. I was very hesitant to take this honors gender class especially since I had no background in gender at all. I can now say that this class has made challenge the way I and how to be a more emphatic and accepting person. Open discussion every class and very conversational in class.

I took Williams Honors Gender Colloquia class. Williams is so inclusive and accessible. She is genuinely a truly kind woman. The class was participation heavy and there was a service learning project, like her other colloquia classes. The workload is not overwhelming and the assignments are interesting.

She is one of the most inspirational teachers. She truly cares about your learning experience. I definitely would take her again. I took her Honors Gender at I learned so much. There is a lot of class discussion on interesting topics.
Dr. Williams is the best. She is sweet, intelligent, and the class is by far the most interesting class I had this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Tests? Not many--Would take again

reviews.comment: Took Dr. Williams for an Honors Thesis Prep class. She is an AMAZING person. Take her classes if you get a chance. She will be an advocate for you throughout your college career and beyond.

Helpful teacher. You don't have to agree with her to get a good grade, just have an open mind, understand why you believe what you believe, and be respectful. This class is all about perspectives, and accepting that the world is a complicated place. If you want an A, then show up to every class and follow the rubrics closely when writing papers.

She is super flexible and happy to work with you. She's passionate about her subject and makes the class enjoyable for all of the students. She truly made me excited to come to class today even though it was almost entirely discussion based, and I don't normally like those classes.  I had the opportunity to do a creative project that she helped.

1st half of the semester was focused on group presentations- your group does 2, you participate in discussion when you're not presenting. 2nd half is all writing workshops for the final paper. I loved the presentation portion of the class and learned a lot from our discussions. She kinda sits back, but she'll definitely help you if you want her to.

WW is an interesting teacher. If you would even call her a teacher. She makes students and guests do most of the teaching. She expects a lot of pointless reading assignments to be done and you don't really learn much. You learn how to write a paper to her liking. Good luck, I do not recommend taking if you want to learn about English/ writing.

She assigns group at the beginning of the year, 3 hours of every period, we have to sit listening to poor-quality highly-googled presentation whereas she just sits at the back and sometimes swoops in when the discussion gets stuck. Easiest A, learn zero. Shes a professor but teaches nothing. Even has TA grade paper.

DO NOT TAKE DR. WILLIAM'S EMPATHY CLASS. I could list at least 20 reasons why not to take this class. She requires 25 service learning hours outside of class, chooses favorites, and has a TA do all of her work for her. If you disagree with her views she will punish you for it. The worst class and professor I have ever takehad at TCU.

There are no tests in this class--just 2 big group presentations.  They aren't bad though, even coming from someone who dislikes group projects, and presentations in general! The books are interesting though, and the discussions are great.  I recommend this class, but stay on top of your reading! Final is a 6-page paper.

Dr. Williams is an awesome professor. For people who said that if you don't agree with her then she'll destroy you, that's incorrect. I've had her for 3 semesters &she is a fair teacher. However, if you say something offensive or ignorant, she will correct you just as any responsible & educated honors professor would. Love her as a person & teacher

If you read, go to class, and participate you should do pretty well. There's a presentation you have to make and 6 page paper at the end, but no final. This class was pretty fun, and discussions during class were pretty thoughtful and sometimes lively. Dr. Williams was helpful and a really good teacher.

Dr. Williams has been my favorite professor at TCU. The course promoted copious amounts of thought-provoking discussion and plenty of civil discourse. Dr. Williams took as much of a passive role as possible, allowing the students to openly debate amongst themselves. She is incredibly kind, caring, empathetic, intelligent, and an absolute delight.

Wendy is ridiculously biased and says she wants people to debate their opinions and play devils advocate but really she is looking for people to agree with her raging liberal views. Take this class if you want an easy A and absolutely nothing else. Not thought provoking in the slightest and don't share your views, you will get destroyed.

STRONGLY RECOMMEND THIS CLASS. Easiest A ever while still learning a lot. You read and article before every class and discuss the article in class. No final. Attendance is mandatory, but class is discussion based, so it goes by quickly. Dr. Williams is extremely helpful and wants her students to do well.

Very easy honors class. You need to read the material before going into class (she will call on you). If you do the online discussion questions you should be fine.  Class is mandatory and participation is a big part of your grade as well as the online discussions.  No final. Main grading points come from a presentation during class and a paper.

Worst professor ever. Please do not take. He does not know anything. Don't know how he got the job. If someone from the department heard him talk for 5 minutes, he would no longer be at TCU. Pissed that I have to pay $200 extra for Neeley classes when this is the type of professor you get. STOP TAKING DOWN MY REVIEWS!!!
Take any other supply chain professor. He's a nice guy but has NO IDEA what he is doing. Don't do it to yourself.

Supply Chain is already the most poorly developed class at TCU, this teacher makes it impossible to listen, study, or ask questions. I still have yet to hear a fully formed sentence from his mouth. Not kidding at all. He knows 0 of the material. If a higher-up listened to just 5 minutes of his class, he would no longer work at TCU.
Just a very low intelligence individual. Does not understand the material whatsoever, not sure how he even graduated high school.
Absolute worst professor I've ever had in my life. Completely unprofessional, does not know material, and in the most respectful way I have no idea how we he has a doctorate. DO NOT TAKE!
Clueless and unqualified professor that has no idea what's going on. Simply there to collect a paycheck. "University" of Phoenix alum haha. QUIT TAKING DOWN MY REVIEWS!!

Worst professor I have ever had. SO unorganized its insane. Grading criteria is not explained. Tests are made by ai, in class lockdown browser (we learned nothing that was on the tests) impossible to do well, forced to do extra credit. Highly do NOT recommend!! 1 wk left in the semester and only half of things are graded. DONT TAKE.

James Woods doesn't know what is going on. He doesn't write the tests or understand the new curriculum and therefore is pretty useless as a professor. Class average on in class lockdown exam was D. Literally take anybody else. His reviews from years ago are misleading because he has changed. It is very frustrating and we haven't learned anything.
Has no clue whats going on. Does not write his own tests. Cant answer questions. Lockdown browser tests. Class average was a 60. No curve. Nice dude just cant teach

Dr Woods is a nice guy and always willing to talk and try and help but I would not take him again. The class and material was very poorly organized. There seemed to be a big disconnect between what was being taught and what was on the quizzes and exams. He would say one thing wouldn't be on a test and then it was.
Horrible teacher but easy A. Also doesn't take attendance so you don't really have to go to class.

One of the absolute worst professors I have ever had at TCU. He completely lacked knowledge of the subject material, lectures were mind numbing, and the course structure was a complete mess. His inability to stay on top of things and communicate effectively to the class led to more than a few stressful situations. Avoid unless you have no choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I loved her. I had to take a night class and was lowkey dreading it, but she is really amazing. Yes, her class is very lecture-heavy, but she's entertaining, and her work is very light. She's willing to help you if you need it. Her exams were easy to an extent, and the homework wasn't overloaded. It's just the long class period, but she's amazing.
Not a hard class as long as you are willing to sit through the equivalent of watching 3 hours of The View or CNN

Overall easy but way too bias and hard of a grader. I worked so hard on all my assignments, and she gave me lots of negative feedback. BIG LIBERAL! So if you don't say or write stuff that she agrees with your grade will be effected. She makes her students feel dumb because she shuts them down if she disagrees. She screams. I don't like her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wood is very intelligent and knowledgeable.  We had lots of papers to write but she gave lots of feedback.  She is nice, but can sometimes come across as stand offish because she is so smart, so if your ideas differ from hers that sometimes can be awkward.  A nice lady and gives lots of extra credit opportunities and chances to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Wood is an excellent teacher who knows what she is talking about. Her tests are online and not super complicated. There are writing assignments, but they arent too hard. I overall enjoyed the lectures and would recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Woods is an outstanding teacher and knows a wealth of information about the material. She is eager to answer questions and provides in depth answers that display unbiased knowledge about the content. Lectures are engaging and you can learn a lot if you pay attention. The assignments are manageable and she provides great feedback on them

Wood really knows what she is talking about. Ask her questions and you can learn a lot. Tests are super long but not too difficult. Assignments tend to be time consuming. Pop quizzes are incredibly hard. Not a very caring teacher overall.

I loved Professor Wood. She only teaches one class at TCU and the rest at TCC. She is a die hard TCU football fan and really cares about her students. She is very knowledgeable and might know every current event since the day she was born. She is a fair grader and really nice. Highly recommend!

If you need a history credit, take Woodworth! Attendance isn't mandatory and every class attended is extra credit. Exams and quizzes are online, take-home, with a lockdown browser. He uses a book but goes more off of his lectures, which are not recorded with no notes posted. Don't miss too many classes or you will have no clue what's going on.

Woodworth is an excellent choice for fulfilling a history core credit. He's incredibly intelligent and delivers his lectures entirely from memory, which makes his classes both impressive and engaging. Attendance is rewarded with extra credit, so if you show up and pay attention, it's very manageable to succeed.

Class is all lectures. Genius in Civil War history and has written books on several topics. Lectures can be a bit dry, but he incorporates jokes and football analogies to lighten things up. Clear expectations. Would recommend. Online exams & quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take this class!!!! One of the easiest history professors. Textbook chapters are short and super easy to follow. Tests and quizzes aren't bad. Each class you go to is a bonus point. Going to class is helpful because the lecture slides don't have words on them. Would definitely recommend this class.

Probably one of the easiest classes I've taken at TCU. Professor Woodworth is passionate about history and the lectures are entertaining, however attendance is extra credit so really all you need to do is read the textbook which he wrote and it is super short and you will be fine. Highly recommend!

His lectures are very detailed and clear although they are long. Quizzes are multiple choice and tests are multiple choice/ essay. But, the textbook is easy to follow and corresponds directly with exams.

Professor Woodworth is an amazing professor. He is super caring and his lectures are very intriguing and genuinely interesting to listen to. This class has caused me no stress and I have actually learned more about history without feeling like I have been pressured to learn because of tests.

Professor Woodworth is one of the best and most methodical lecturers on the Civil War. If you love military history, take this course. Very structured. Class consists of 2 Book Reports (easy), 3 Primary Source Reviews (easy), 3 Quizzes(multiple choice) and 3 Exams(essay). Do the weekly readings and take time to write good papers and its an easy A.
Avoid him if you can! He wasn't understanding at all...and doesn't really put in the efforts to help students...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Woodworth knows what he is talking about, but stands in front & lectures the entire class. Must take your own notes as his slides have no words, only pictures. He is always behind on lectures - the tests will have questions on material he has not covered. Strict and unclear when grading essays & will not change your grade even if you visit

I would not take this class again. Dr. Woodworth lectures straight from memory and didnt understand I had accommodations for teachers notes and would not allow me to have them. He is very lecture heavy. He also cant tell what chapters the exam is over because he just looks at the syllabus and says exams cover certain chapter when its inaccurate.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would not take Prof. Woodworth again! He stands in front and lectures the entire class with no participation from students and you take your own notes. He makes you buy his textbook and is always behind on lectures. He expects you to know material on tests that he hasn't gone over and is super strict and unclear when grading essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Read the textbook content before class. Lectures will review and add more detail to course material. Essay portions of tests are graded rather harshly because he wants specificity. Very upbeat and energetic, kept lectures interesting even though he often goes on irrelevant tangents.

Don't take class online. Gives more work because its online. His tests are ridiculous, 15 mc q's each worth 4pts and a 40pt essay with lockdown browser/camera & no notes. Impossible to please him. Essay assignments are graded hard too and his feedback makes no sense/not specific. Lectures at camera entire time, no slide notes. Wrote his own book.

Nice guy and always in a good mood but sometimes his jokes go a little too far. Only grades by 6 tests: 4 in-class and 2 take-home. TH are easy prompts based on 2 books but IC are really hard multiple choice. He tends to ramble in lectures and it gets boring. Pay attention in class and buy/read the online textbook or else you're not passing
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Does not care. Takes forever to respond to emails. Lectures are so boring and hard to pay attention to, he's monotone and rambles. You sit there wondering "is this going to be on the test?" People say you can just read the textbook- to be honest unless you already know a lot about history, you cant get by with just reading the book
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He does not care. Takes forever to respond to emails. Very difficult to follow during lectures as he rambles, says you can just read the book and pass. False- if you aren't in class even halfway listening you aren't gonna pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great teacher! Hoping to have one of his classes again!

Read the textbook and listen to his lectures and it is an easy A. Grade based on 4 tests that are straight forward. Multiple choice format with a basic essay. Nice, humorous professor. Lectures can be long but he has good stories to enhance the material. Textbook chapters only have like 3-5 pages and are easy to understand. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Wonderful and encouraging professor who cares about the students. The texts were extremely helpful and he helps as you write the final paper by guiding the students through valuable feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He lectures straight from his mind; there was no writing notes on the board or powerpoint to follow. He doesn't really engage the class or ask anyone to participate ever. The lectures are pretty boring and hard to follow. There are two papers and 4 multiple choice tests. The papers are pretty ambiguously graded and the tests come from the textbook.

1877-Now: 4 tests- 2 are multiple choice and 2 are questions about the books you read (don't really need to read); lecture is so boring and attendance isn't mandatory. If you have a basic knowledge of US history you'll be fine. use the ?s at the end of his book to study. One of the easier history classes for sure

Total nerd. likes to make political jokes and sometimes he goes a little too far. I definitely didn't like him in the beginning because of all of his political comments and opinions. he is very biased and take what he says with a grain of salt. 4 tests, 2 rare take home and two are normal in class multiple choice tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: survey from 1877 is a super easy class. attendance isn't mandatory. 4 tests and 2 homework assignments make up your grade. the book he suggests (the one he wrote) has questions you need to know at the end of the chapter; know them and you'll do fine on the tests.

Outstanding Professor and author! As a student of American history who has read countless books, his are among the best I've read. He cares and gives positive feedback. I learned a lot and would highly recommend taking a class from him!

I feel everybody rates him based on how nice he is. He's extremely intelligent, but a HORRENDOUS teacher. He talks AT you, not TO you. Lectures are very boring, uninforming, & non-inspirational. While he has a bit of notoriety based on his intelligence & experience, unfortunately, he severely lacks in connecting w/ students. Avoid his class.

2 short homework worksheets, 4 exams (including final). Easy history class that is also really interesting. He only lectures, so that can get a little long sometimes. You don't ever have to read the book- just take good notes from his lectures. I really liked him and thought he was funny in a sorta dorky way. Would definitely take again!

Don't bother buying the book, unless you're really bad at history. If  you just go to class and take good notes, you'll be fine. He gives you 2 homework assignments that are super easy and his exams (4) are too. Exams are composed of 60 MC and an essay. The MC are super easy and he'll even review with the class before he hands out the test.

Great professor! If you go to class, you'll be able to answer the study guides. His study guides are straight-forward and contain relevant information for his exams. Only 2 homework assignments and none of his exams are cumulative, including the final. Highly recommend.

Had him during the summer. He is one of the top teachers I've taken. He is vary fair and teaches vary good. There are hardly any professors like him in fairness and knowledge of the subject as well. I would definitely recommend him to anyone. Test  come directly from lectures.

Epitomizes the derailment of higher education. Clearly highly knowledgeable and writes very well. Good for tenure bad for teaching. Neither understands how to engage the student in the learning process nor how to participate to the advantage of the student. Grading is subjective, soft and arbitrary. Horrible teacher – great historian.

VERY VERY VERY VERY GREAT TEACHER! He is very clear about what is on the test and his reviews are straight up test questions. I loved going to his class, he always made jokes and made class fun/ I did not read the book and I got through the class very easily. LOVE LOVE LOVE Dr. Woodworth!!!!!!

Very fair professor. The exams come straight from his lectures so it is important to go to class. If you study and listen in class it's an easy A! He is my favorite professor at TCU! He is a very energetic speaker and makes class fun!

I really like Woodworth as a person, but I was really not interested in the material we learned in this class. He is super knowledgable of the material, so he literally just stands at the front of the room and talks without power points or anything. As much as I tried to focus I always got bored in that class.
He was really personable and easy to listen to each class.  If his U.S. history class wasn't full I would have taken him again
Outstanding. Incredibly helpful. Pushed me to do more than what I thought I ever could. Kind, demanding, a true scholar.

Best history class I've ever taken. Sticks to the facts. Everything comes from the lecture, so no need to get the book. No papers or homework, 4 exams and attendance quizzes. Go to the class, reread the notes prior to the next class, and the quizzes aren't a problem. Super helpful if you go to office hours. Great professor, great class.

I'm actually taking a class online through Liberty University, where he's also a professor.  He is probably the one of the three best history professors I've had, and I have certainly taken my fair share of history classes.  I highly recommend him.  He's incredibly knowledgeable and very clear in what he is teaching. A++
If you go to class you don't need to read the book. Loved Woodworth, still hate history and I barley studied and got a high B.

Absolutely the best. I have had two courses with Dr. Woodworth and of all the courses I have taken (B.A. M. S. partial Ph.D.), he is the finest professor I have had. He is a recognized expert in his field. Being in his courses was an honor.
Great professor. If you don't pay attention the lectures are boring, if you do pay attention their exciting. Tests are easy, just read the book.

Absolutely amazing professor. I was not a big History fan coming into this class but he made me really enjoy it. Makes History feel like a story that is easily understandable. Tests are multiple choice and essay and are challenging but fair. Uses slideshows but most of his notes come from him talking so you have to be attentive in class. Loved it!

Awesome class! He's very animated and engaging in his lectures. He goes without a notebook or powerpoint, so you gotta keep writing. Great office hours policy and helpful if you see him. Takes a conservative approach to history, which is rare in the university setting. All quizzes and tests are from lectures. No homework!

Absolutely awesome professor! My favorite at TCU, even though I'm not a history major. His lectures are very interesting and keep you listening... He tells funny jokes and makes a lot of football references. Great guy and even better professor! Take him for sure!!! Not an easy A, but read through your notes and you will be successful. Love him!
Very conservative professor, nice and helpful. Tells a lot of jokes and most are funny. An easy B push harder and a nice A. no homework or busy work, you don't need the book.

Took 2 classes w/him & the reviews are pretty accurate (smart, funny, conservative, sexy). I abhorred history before taking his class, but he makes it interesting & relates well to students w/jokes and analogies. Attendance is crucial, exams are straightforward. He?s a true storyteller & has a talent for drawing you in?even w/the Illinois accent ;)

If you like football, you'll love this class. Woodworth constantly makes references comparing historical politics with different NCAA conferences. If you pay attention you'll remember a lot of what he says. Can be an easy A if you put some effort into it.

Dr. Woodworth is brilliant and the best professor I have had at TCU.  He is an expert in the Civil War and can tell you everything you ever wanted to know.  Be forewarned, he will get up and lecture w/o notes for the entire class.  Notetaking and attendance are a must.  Plus read all the books.  I highly recommend him for anyone interested in the C
MY FAVORITE TEACHER! He actually kept history interesting, which is something that I was never able to achieve. Great guy and willing to work with you if you need the help. TAKE HIM!

A very conservative professor.  He actually graded me down for taking a liberal perspective on a topic.  He is superb for knowledge but in an online MA course on Civil War he isn't particularly active with comments.

Woodworth's class is pretty straightforward. The lectures aren't very interesting, but if you pay attention and take notes you will easily get an A. He's actually kind of funny. Don't miss class often. I wish I hadn't because I missed out on an easy A.

This class had me worried!  I thought I was getting a B, but ended up with an A!  He knows his Civil War History, so don't try to play around, he will catch you on it!  Great teacher and learned a lot!

Survey of U.S. History Since 1877. Take him for your history! His class is easy but interesting! 3 tests and a final. He gives you study guides for all the tests and if you follow them you'll do well. You do need to go to class even though he doesn't take attendance because tests are straight from his lecture. He has conservative opinions.

I had prof. woodworth for 3 classes. He is extremely smart and knowledgeable. However, he will not have much structure, just lectures, so make sure you take notes and pay attention. You dont want to miss much class either. But a nice prof and knows what he is talking about and you will learn a lot of cool things about history.

Survey of US History after 1877, Dr. Woodworth is a smart guy with rather strong conservative opinions. Which is refreshing! I liked him a lot. He was pretty funny while lecturing at times, and he does it all from memory. His tests are pretty easy, though attending class helps. If you want a cool, easy history class, take Woodworth! PS he is sexy.

He is a terrible lecturer.  There is absolutely no class interaction, he just stands in front of the class and talks in a monotone drawl.  The only grades for the class are reading quizzes and essay tests(which don't have reviews).  Oh yeah, and there are three books to read for the class; two of which he wrote.

go to class, take notes and listen a little...he gives you a review with all the terms you need to know for the test.  really not a bad history class at all.  only tricky part is the one essay on the tests, but as long as you read through your notes once or twice before the test, on top of studying the terms, you will be fine.
Great professor.  My favorite since coming to college. Very helpful and tests come from lectures.  Go to class and you will make a B without any effort, an A with little effort.
greatest prof ever! tests are easy classes are interesting. talks about college football and just great

Doesn't teach so much as reward people for agreeing with him, and it will only cost you $2400. Incredibly right wing opinions with a hint of facts sprinkled here and there.   Easy class if you don't care about learning anything.

The guy is really knowledgeable, he knows what he's talking about. He makes corny jokes and I don't advise anyone to take it as an 8am cause it's kinda boring. Take notes, his lecture tests are easy. Reading tests are hard especially if you don't read. Take the class it's an easy A.
good teacher, easy tests. reading tests are hard, especially when you have to read his books. makes lots of football analogies, very easy to follow along.
